Bioinspired Multi-metallic Relay Catalyst for Efficient Nitrate Reduction and Zn-NO3– Battery Performance
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (e-NO3– RR) to ammonia offers an effective pathway for environmental remediation and clean energy production. However, its efficiency is often constrained by sluggish multi-electron/proton transfer and mismatched intermediate adsorption. Herein, we report a bioinspired multi-metallic cobalt copper molybdate (CCM) catalyst that overcomes these limitations through a relay-type catalytic mechanism enabled by spatially distinct metal centers. In this architecture, Cu, Co, and Mo sites cooperatively orchestrate intermediate stabilization and proton activation in successive reaction steps, thereby facilitating an efficient cascade conversion of nitrate to ammonia. As a result, the optimized CCM catalyst achieves an ammonia yield rate of 2.6 mmol h–1 cm–2 and a Faradaic efficiency up to 92%. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses identify the synergistic interplay among the multiple metal active centers as the mechanistic basis for the enhanced nitrate-to-ammonia performance. Beyond half-cell evaluation, integration of the CCM catalyst into a Zn-NO3– battery delivers an output voltage of 1.34 V and a power density of 4.1 mW cm–2, demonstrating its viability for coupled ammonia synthesis and energy generation. This study identifies multi-metallic relay catalysis as an effective strategy for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate-to-ammonia conversion.

articles.title: Conformationally Locked Yttrium Indanosalan Complexes for Fast Isoselective Ring-Opening Polymerization of β-Butyrolactone at Elevated Temperatures
articles.abstract: We report rigid yttrium indanosalan complexes for the high-temperature ring-opening polymerization of β-butyrolactone. Some of the complexes (isolated or obtained in situ) developed were able to polymerize β-butyrolactone with high isoselectivity (Pm = 0.88) and very high activity (TOF up to 135,000 h–1) at a polymerization temperature of 100 °C, at which the polymer remains in solution, facilitating its further processing. Polymerization at 30–60 °C yielded the poly(3-hydroxybutyrate)s with Pm up to 0.94. The roles of active site configuration and non-covalent interactions were studied experimentally and by DFT, which reproduced the enantiomorphic-site control and showed that the monomer was oriented by C–H···π and C–H···O contacts, rather than by N–H···O hydrogen bonding.

articles.title: Iron-Catalyzed Decarboxylative Phosphonylation of Aliphatic Carboxylic Acids with Succinimidyl Phosphites as Bifunctional Reagents
articles.abstract: Aliphatic carboxylic acids are abundant, stable, and cost-effective, rendering them ideal substrates for site-specific C(sp3)–P bond formation via decarboxylative pathways. However, the direct catalytic decarboxylative phosphonylation of these acids remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report that the use of dialkyl succinimidyl phosphites as bifunctional reagents enables the iron-catalyzed decarboxylative phosphonylation of aliphatic carboxylic acids to proceed smoothly at room temperature under visible light irradiation. The transformation accommodates primary, secondary, and tertiary alkyl acids, delivering the corresponding alkylphosphonates in satisfactory yields with broad functional group tolerance. A reaction mechanism involving photoinduced ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) of ferric carboxylates, β-scission of phosphoranyl radical intermediates leading to N–O bond cleavage, and single-electron oxidation of ferrous ions by succinimidyl radicals, is proposed.

articles.title: Temporally Distinguishing Photocatalytic Dynamics
articles.abstract: Light can induce both photothermal and nonthermal catalytic activity in plasmonic nanoparticles, but the extent, timescale, and efficacy of these two mechanisms remain unresolved. Here, we introduce pump–pump photocatalysis, an adaptation of ultrafast excitation correlation spectroscopy in which incident laser pulses are split into two spatially and energetically equivalent pulses separated by a variable time delay. For a given reaction and catalyst, time-sensitive nonlinear enhancements in photocatalytic activity may be distinguished from time-insensitive responses as a function of time delay, pulse power, excitation wavelength, applied temperature, reactant pressure, and pulse asymmetry. In this way, the timescales of photothermal and nonthermal activity of any photocatalyst may be monitored on sub-picosecond to nanosecond timescales, and the conditions for optimal chemical reactivity may be discovered. To illustrate this technique, we perform ultrafast measurements of the ammonia decomposition reaction using a Cu–Ru antenna-reactor photocatalyst. Photothermal contributions exhibit little sensitivity to pulse delay, while nonthermal contributions are most apparent at low excitation intensity, moderate temperatures, and sub-nanosecond timescales. Here, nonlinear, nonthermal mechanisms enhance H2 production by a factor of up to eleven compared to when pulses overlap. This technique may be used to provide insightful in operando diagnostics and control of any photocatalyst for any chemical reaction while revealing the optimal distribution of light to maximize photocatalytic activity.

articles.title: Donor–Acceptor Tuning Regulates Viologen Redox Behavior for Selective H2O2 Photosynthesis
articles.abstract: Regulating redox-active electron acceptors offers a strategy for directing multielectron photocatalysis beyond conventional charge-separation engineering. Here, we demonstrate substituent-controlled viologen redox regulation in pyrene–viologen porous organic polymers (PyVio-X) for selective H2O2 photosynthesis. Carbonyl functionalization (PyVio-CO) enhances donor–acceptor interactions and charge separation, while facilitating photoinduced viologen radical (V-N+•) formation. PyVio-CO achieves an H2O2 production rate of 1786 μmol g–1 h–1 in pure water under visible light and ambient air, with a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 0.25% and an apparent quantum yield of 4.95%. Mechanistic investigations support sequential O2 reduction involving ·O2– and *OOH intermediates, mediated by reversible V-N2+/V-N+• redox cycling. Enhanced two-electron O2 reduction selectivity and suppressed H2O2 decomposition further promote H2O2 accumulation. This work establishes substituent-controlled redox mediation as a molecular design principle for selective multielectron photocatalysis.

articles.title: Transition from Dehydration to Rehydration of Chloride Salts near the Melting Point: Thermodynamic Origin and Implications for High-Temperature Corrosion
articles.abstract: Molten chloride salts are promising functional media for high-temperature energy systems; however, trace water can accelerate corrosion of structural materials. We investigated changes in water concentration in six chloride salts—LiCl, NaCl, MgCl2, KCl, CaCl2, and ZnCl2—during heating across their solid-to-liquid phase transitions under a nominally inert Ar atmosphere. During solid-state heating, water concentration generally decreased, indicating dehydration. With further heating toward and through melting, however, this trend unexpectedly reversed in five salts except ZnCl2. As these salts entered the liquid phase, their water concentrations increased, marking a transition from dehydration to rehydration. Thermodynamic analysis showed that melting shifts the free energy balance toward water incorporation through enthalpic and entropic contributions. By comparing molten MgCl2 under conditions allowing or restricting entry of Ar gas, we identified trace water in the Ar atmosphere as the source of rehydration. Corrosion tests further showed rehydration substantially increased 316H stainless steel corrosion.

articles.title: Tuning Mass Transport through Pressure Modulation for Lithium-Mediated Nitrogen Reduction
articles.abstract: Lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction (LiNRR) produces ammonia at ambient pressure and temperature, and gas diffusion electrodes (GDEs) have advanced its production rate by intensifying nitrogen availability. However, the mass transport of lithium, nitrogen, and proton donor within the GDE and how the balance of their fluxes governs LiNRR performance remain underexplored. Here, we spatiotemporally varied the balance of species fluxes in a LiNRR GDE by dynamically modulating the pressure difference across the electrode, which altered the position of the gas/electrolyte interface. We found that decoupling the pressures applied during the plating and resting steps of pulsed electrolysis leads to higher ammonia production rates compared to the corresponding static pressure conditions. Decoupled pressure modulation enables even lithium plating during electrolysis and fast transport of nitrogen and proton donor during subsequent ammonia formation steps. This strategy may unlock a new design space for LiNRR by dynamically optimizing the reaction interface.

articles.title: Correlating Defects and Surface Contaminants: Toward Clean Graphene with Improved Mechanical Performance
articles.abstract: The mechanical performance of large-area chemical vapor deposition (CVD) graphene membranes is often compromised by coexisting lattice defects and surface contamination. However, the underlying synergistic mechanisms remain elusive, particularly regarding how defects mediate contaminant nucleation and how their coupling degrades the mechanical properties of graphene. Here, combining in situ spherical aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy with controlled contaminant removal and redeposition experiments, we provide atomic-scale experimental validation for the causal correlation between graphene point defects and amorphous carbon contamination on CVD-grown graphene. We further achieve real-time, site-resolved visualization of active carbon species migration and defect-trapping dynamics. Multiscale simulations uncover a defect-mediated kinetic-trapping mechanism: active carbon species migrate rapidly over intact graphene yet become captured and immobilized at defects, with the calculated diffusion coefficient dropping from ∼14.4 to 1.65 nm2 ns–1. Moreover, nanoindentation tests confirm that clean graphene exhibits superior mechanical properties (stiffness: ∼305 N m–1 and fracture force: ∼1900 nN) compared to the contaminated counterpart (stiffness: ∼224 N m–1 and fracture force: ∼1077 nN). Continuum finite-element analysis indicates that the reduced stiffness of unclean graphene cannot be explained by surface contamination alone, supporting the presence of defect-induced softening beneath the contamination. Atomically resolved simulations further reveal that the mechanical response is jointly governed by defect type, contamination, and interfacial bonding. In particular, chemically bonded contamination can redistribute local stress and mitigate defect-induced stress concentration, thereby altering the failure process of defective graphene. Our study identifies point defects as both contamination traps and mechanical weak links, offering a unified strategy for high-performance graphene membrane design.

articles.title: Covalent Interface-Engineered Bone-Targeting Piezoelectric Heterojunction Reprograms Tumor Stress Adaptation and Reverses the Immunosuppressive Microenvironment
articles.abstract: Breast cancer bone metastasis remains a major therapeutic challenge due to endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS)-associated stress adaptation and an immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Herein, we report a zoledronic acid (ZOL)-loaded bone-targeted covalent piezoelectric heterojunction nanoplatform (Z@BT-P) for sonopiezo-dynamic therapy (SPDT) and immune remodeling. In this platform, barium titanate (BTO) was covalently integrated with a porphyrinic porous coordination network to form a stable BT-P heterointerface, while ZOL enhanced bone-metastatic lesion enrichment. Compared with physically assembled BT@P, Z@BT-P promoted interfacial charge utilization and strengthened ultrasound (US)-triggered piezoelectric catalysis. Under US irradiation, enhanced charge utilization and Piezo1-associated mechanosensitive Ca2+ signaling jointly amplified reactive oxygen species accumulation and Ca2+ dysregulation, causing dual oxidative/Ca2+ stress. This stress cascade promoted ERS associated with glucose-regulated protein 78 and C/EBP homologous protein, leading to apoptosis and immunogenic cell death. Consequent damage-associated molecular patterns release and ZOL-containing treatment enhanced dendritic cell maturation, drove M1-like macrophage remodeling, and activated antitumor immunity. In a 4T1-luc tibial bone metastasis model, Z@BT-P + US achieved 89.4% ± 4.9% tumor growth inhibition, alleviated osteolytic bone destruction, suppressed distant metastasis, and promoted immune memory. This study establishes a covalent interface-engineered piezoelectric nanoplatform for bone metastasis therapy.

articles.title: Decoupling Laser Intensity and Laser Heating Effects in Plasmonic Photocatalysis Reveals the Temperature Rise Plays a Dominant Yet Nonexclusive Role
articles.abstract: Separating thermal and laser intensity effects in plasmonic photocatalysis has proven challenging because the two are frequently intertwined. Higher laser intensities will increase any laser-induced heating, making it difficult to isolate the influence of laser intensity and complicating efforts to disentangle thermal versus nonthermal contributions to plasmonic photocatalysis. Here, we decouple laser intensity and laser heating effects by fabricating plasmonic nanostructures with nearly identical optical properties but divergent thermal properties, allowing us to modulate and even eliminate laser heating while applying the same range of laser intensities. We simultaneously perform upconverting nanoparticle (UCNP)-based microscale thermometry and monitor the photocatalyzed dimerization of 4-nitrothiophenol (4-NTP) to 4,4′-dimercaptoazobenzene (DMAB) with Raman spectroscopy. We show that larger temperature rises enhance the reaction and, even more importantly, the temperature rise alone dictates the degree of 4-NTP to DMAB conversion, independent of the applied laser intensity. These results are consistent across two different plasmonic nanostructures. External heating combined with a threshold laser intensity can also drive the reaction, with the degree of conversion again determined solely by the temperature rise. However, despite the critical influence of the temperature rise, external heating alone fails to catalyze the reaction. Leveraging ultrahigh thermal conductivity diamond substrates, which let us increase the laser intensity without inducing heating, we further demonstrate that higher laser intensities increase the reaction rate yet have no effect on the degree of conversion. Thus, although temperature plays an outsize role, the plasmonic photocatalysis process nonetheless cannot be explained by a purely thermal mechanism.

articles.title: Electron-Modulated Pt–Co Dual-Atom Sites with Hydrogen Spillover for Robust Acidic Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Pt single-atom catalysts (Pt-SACs) are regarded as one of the most promising electrocatalysts for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) owing to the maximal atom utilization and distinctive coordination structure. However, their reaction kinetics and stability at large current density are severely limited by the linear scaling relations and metal sites agglomeration. Herein, we present an “electronic anchoring strategy” to construct Pt–Co dual-atom sites (PtCo-DASs) on onion-like carbon nanospheres with carbon vacancies (OLCv) (denoted PtCo-DAS@OLCv) as a structurally integrated electrode for highly efficient and stable HER. Experimental and theoretical calculations demonstrate that Pt atoms achieve electron capture through d–π orbital coupling with Co, C, and O, subsequently guarantee superior structural stability, and establish a localized electric field. The electric field is further amplified by the confinement effect from the high-curvature of nanosized OLCv, which facilitates proton enrichment, lowers the Volmer barrier, and accelerates hydrogen spillover from Pt sites to Co sites, ultimately decoupling hydrogen adsorption and desorption at the atom scale. Consequently, PtCo-DAS@OLCv with an ultralow Pt loading of 6.16 μg cm–2 exhibits a high HER activity with a low overpotential of 14.1 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and high turnover frequency of 83.2 H2 s–1 at 100 mV, which are superior to those of commercial Pt/C and the most reported Pt-based catalysts. Interestingly, a practical proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) assembled by PtCo-DAS@OLCv achieves a large current density of 1000 mA cm–2 at an ultralow cell voltage of 1.78 V and operates stably for over 2300 h with negligible degradation.

articles.title: Ferroelectric Neuromorphic Devices Enable Nonphotosensitive Neurons to Achieve Event-Driven Photosensitive Artificial Neural Interfaces
articles.abstract: Neuromorphic devices integrated with biological neurons hold significant potential for rehabilitation and human-machine interfaces, thereby attracting extensive research interest. However, the effort to connect them through light stimulation is still in its very initial stages. Here, ferroelectric neuromorphic devices based on α-In2Se3 and P(VDF-TrFE) are proposed to construct hybrid neural interfaces. In contrast to neuromorphic devices employing other working principles, ferroelectricity plays a crucial role in connecting biological neurons, which enables nonphotosensitive neurons to respond to light stimuli. Various optoelectronic synaptic behaviors have been achieved. Under light pulses, the ferroelectric neuromorphic device induced a significant increase of up to 200% in the calcium ion signal of artificial neural interfaces. Patch-clamp was applied for further verification, revealing the influence of different light wavelengths and pulse frequencies on neuronal excitation signals, which is analogous to the human retina. Simulations demonstrate that the ferroelectric neural interface improves dynamic gesture recognition accuracy from 51% to 99%. Our approach offers a strategy to connect neuromorphic devices with neurons through light, which may offer a platform to investigate the fundamental principles of synaptic plasticity and learning in a hybrid setting for future remote therapy and human–machine interfaces.

articles.title: Interphase-Adaptive Chloride Solid Electrolyte Enables High-Performance All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
articles.abstract: Halide solid electrolytes offer a compelling combination of wide electrochemical stability and high safety for all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs), yet their practical application is severely hindered by interfacial degradation, mechanical contact loss, and low active-material utilization when paired with Ni-rich layered oxide cathodes. Here we synthesize a monoclinic Li2.4Yb0.4Zr0.6Cl6 (LYZC) with a high ionic conductivity of 2.1 × 10–3 S·cm–1 at 30 °C, and then coat it with an ultrathin amorphous organic interphase (LYZC@CH) through an organic-solvent-assisted low-temperature strategy. The adaptive organic interphase transforms the intrinsically rigid chloride electrolyte into a chemo-mechanically compliant ion conductor that accommodates cathode volume variation while preserving rapid lithium–ion transport. Consequently, the engineered electrolyte stabilizes the cathode/electrolyte interface, suppresses parasitic interfacial reactions and structural degradation, and enables composite cathodes with a high active-material content of 90%. The resulting LiNi0.83Co0.12Mn0.05O2 composite cathode delivers an electrode-level energy density of 402.22 Wh kg–1 and retains nearly 100% of its capacity after 2000 cycles at 5 C in 30 MPa. This work establishes an electrolyte-centered interfacial engineering strategy for practical high-energy all-solid-state lithium batteries.

articles.title: Microalgae-Macrophage Hybrid Exosome-like Nanovesicles for Mitophagy Restoration and Wound Regeneration in Aging
articles.abstract: The wound healing capacity in the elderly is significantly impaired, leading to increased susceptibility to inflammation and infection, and potentially contributing to reduced lifespan. In aged wounds, dysfunctional mitophagy in senescent cells (SnCs) results in the persistent release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, fostering a chronic inflammatory microenvironment that further delays tissue repair. To address this challenge, we developed a thermosensitive hydrogel loaded with hybrid exosome-like nanovesicles to enhance wound healing in aging. These hybrid nanovesicles (termed SP-M2-ENs) were generated by extrusion-mediated fusion of spirulina-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (SP-ENs) with M2 macrophage-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (M2-ENs). SP-ENs are rich in phycocyanin and exhibit strong antioxidant activity, whereas M2-ENs carry multiple anti-inflammatory cytokines and growth factors. This synergistic combination endows the hybrid system with enhanced anti-inflammatory and regenerative capabilities. To ensure sustained release and conformability to irregular wound topographies, the hybrid nanovesicles were encapsulated within a thermosensitive hydrogel (PF-127 gel), forming the final therapeutic construct, designated SP-M2-ENs@Gel. Comprehensive in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that SP-M2-ENs@Gel effectively scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS), promotes tissue regeneration, stimulates angiogenesis, modulates macrophage polarization toward a reparative phenotype, and enables prolonged delivery of therapeutic agents. Specifically, SP-M2-ENs@Gel accelerates healing in aged wounds by restoring mitophagy function in senescent cells, thereby alleviating chronic inflammation. Collectively, this platform represents a promising strategy for overcoming senescence-impaired wound repair, highlighting the clinical translatability of engineered exosome-based therapies in regenerative medicine.

articles.title: Nondestructive Piezoelectric Nanocomposite Sonodynamic Toothbrush for Synergistic Dental Disinfection and Whitening
articles.abstract: Over 3.47 billion people worldwide suffer from dental health and aesthetic issues, however, existing commercial toothbrushes lack synergistic antibacterial and whitening functions and fail to prevent biofilm accumulation and progressive staining. Here, we develop novel sonodynamic bifunctional piezoelectric nanocomposites by integrating piezoelectric Au@BTO nanoparticles into a porous elastomer matrix, enabling synergistic disinfection and whitening in a biosafe and efficient manner during daily toothbrushing. These nanocomposites exhibit superior mechanical and piezoelectric stability under continuous ultrasound stimulation for 30,000 s, along with robust andcontrollable generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) based on a piezocatalytic mechanism. Under physiological conditions, the piezoelectric nanocomposites demonstrate highly efficient and durable antibacterial activity against Gram-positive S. aureus and S. mutans as well as Gram-negative E. coli and P. gingivalis (>99% efficacy), while preserving >95% oral cell viability. When integrated into an innovative Piezo-brush, the system maintains structural integrity for ∼5 months under daily toothbrushing and achieves 96% biofilm reduction and nondestructive whitening (CIELab color difference = 70.3, 0.6% Vickers hardness reduction), significantly outperforming existing functional toothbrushes and commercial products. This work develops a piezoelectric sonodynamic toothbrush for daily dental care, offering avenues for advanced biodevices in cosmetics, wound healing, and medical implants.

articles.title: Plasmonic Hot Carrier-Driven Chemistry Revealed by Dual Raman Thermometry
articles.abstract: Plasmonic nanoparticles (NPs) have been employed as nanocatalysts in a myriad of photochemical reactions with the underlying mechanisms divided into two categories: thermal and nonthermal pathways. Differentiating these two pathways is the key to optimizing plasmon-mediated chemistry; however, the challenge of measuring temperature down to the nanoscale hinders the advancement and causes the ongoing debate in the field. Herein, we report an in situ spectroscopic approach that leverages two Raman thermometries─the background of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (plasmonic thermometry) and molecular vibrational fingerprints (molecular thermometry) are used independently to probe the local temperature of NP/molecule hybrid systems. Using gold NP/4-nitrothiophenol as a prototype system, we demonstrate the agreement between the two thermometries and prove the nonthermal pathways for the dimerization of 4-nitrothiophenol. Since the temperatures of both metal NPs and adsorbed molecules are probed simultaneously, the dual Raman thermometry enables a detailed mechanistic understanding of plasmon-mediated chemistry.

articles.title: Quantifying Viscoelastic Alterations in Virus-Infected Cells by Optical Tweezers
articles.abstract: The viscoelasticity of cells is closely related to their physiological functions, influencing processes such as differentiation, proliferation, and migration. Viruses replicate by infecting host cells and can affect the cells’ viscoelastic properties. However, current research mainly focuses on changes in the overall cellular viscoelasticity, while intracellular viscoelastic properties remain difficult to measure. Optical tweezers, due to their noncontact nature, offer a promising tool for measuring intracellular viscoelasticity. In this study, the viscoelastic moduli of host cells infected with three different viruses (H9N2, PRV, and HSV) were measured using the active-passive calibration method and microrheological techniques. The changes in viscoelastic moduli across different frequency ranges were systematically analyzed. The results showed that viral infection altered the viscoelastic properties of cells, with the extent of changes varying by virus type. We conclude that viral infection leads to an increase in viscous modulus and a decrease in elastic modulus of the host cell, and this is attributed to virus-induced depolymerization of the cytoskeleton, which reduces cellular elasticity and increases viscosity. These findings provide insights into the mechanisms of virus-induced alterations in cellular viscoelasticity and offer a theoretical foundation for further studies on the cellular mechanisms of viral infections.

articles.title: Regime of Geometrical Mismatch in the Phase Separation-Regulated Endocytosis of Nanoparticles
articles.abstract: The biological responses related to microdomains formed by phase separation in cell membranes bear long-standing controversies, and, in particular, how this lateral heterogeneity impacts the cellular uptake of nanoparticles remains poorly understood. By combining theoretical models, computer simulations, and experimental discussions, we report on an unconventionally constrained regime of nanoparticle endocytosis on the membrane microdomain, emerging within the intermediate scale of the domains. This regime leads to the nonmonotonic dependence of nanoparticle endocytosis on domain size, in stark contrast to its counterparts in the homogeneous membrane and endocytosis without nanoparticles. Theoretical analysis evaluates the regime boundary and reveals that the regime arises from the geometrical mismatch between nanoparticles and microdomains governed by various energetic contributions, which capture and explain some experimental observations. The findings suggest an appealing way and useful guidelines to control cellular uptake and might be of immediate interest to the desired biomedical applications.

articles.title: Retraction of “Bottom-Up Engineering of Peptide Cell Translocators Based on Environmentally Modulated Quadrupole Switches”
Sulfur Doping-Induced Surface Reconstruction of High-Entropy Composites Boosts Bifunctional Oxygen Electrocatalysis for Zinc-Air Batteries
articles.abstract: The development of high-efficiency and durable bifunctional electrocatalysts for both the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is essential for the widespread application of rechargeable zinc-air batteries (RZABs). Rational screening of ORR/OER components and precise regulation of their electronic structures to achieve synergistic effects currently stand as an effective solution. Here, we report a composite catalyst prepared through the high-temperature decomposition of molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), synthesizing sulfur (S)-doped high-entropy alloy (HEA) nanoparticles on carbon nanotube (S-FeCoNiMnMo@CNT) with metallic single atoms. High-valent Mo can precisely modulate the local electronic domains of HEAs. S doping not only triggers surface reconstruction of HEAs during the OER to deliver outstanding OER catalytic activity but also immobilizes metal single atoms to boost ORR: an overpotential as low as 247 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and an ORR half-wave potential of 0.746 V are achieved. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the S-doping-induced surface reconstruction promotes the adsorption of *OOH intermediates and reduces the Gibbs free energy barrier during the OER process. RZAB based on S-FeCoNiMnMo@CNT exhibits a peak power density of 229.8 mW cm–2, along with a low voltage gap of 0.716 V at 10 mA cm–2 and a cycle life exceeding 800 h. Furthermore, this work extends its applications to flexible ZABs.

articles.title: Voltage-Gated Ionic Conductivity in Ultranarrow Confinement
articles.abstract: Voltage-controlled ion transport in subnanometer pores underpins the operation of emerging filtration, energy-storage, and iontronic technologies, yet its microscopic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using classical molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate ionic transport in ultranarrow (≤1 nm) quasi-two-dimensional nanopores in MXene electrodes filled with an ionic liquid. We reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of linear-response conductivity on electrode potential, with a pronounced asymmetry between positive and negative electrode polarizations. These behaviors originate from a competition between confinement-induced ionic ordering and charging-induced ion crowding within the pore. The resulting transition from a structure-limited to an ion-crowding-limited transport regime provides a general framework for understanding voltage-gated ionic conduction under extreme confinement, which facilitates the formulation of design principles for MXene-based nanofluidic, electrochemical, and iontronic devices.

articles.title: Wheat Spike Topology-Inspired Dynamic “Pearl Necklace” Nanoarchitectures for Topological Interlocking Adhesion and Precision Agrochemical Delivery
articles.abstract: Fusarium head blight (FHB) is one of the most devastating diseases of wheat, threatening global food security through yield losses and mycotoxin contamination. Although fungicides remain essential for FHB control, their field efficacy is often restricted by poor deposition and rapid removal from wheat spike surfaces. Inspired by the hierarchical topology of wheat spikes, we transform these inherent surface features into functional anchoring sites by developing a supramolecular “pearl necklace” nanoarchitecture for enhanced pesticide retention. The nanochains are constructed through cooperative electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions between poly-l-lysine (PLL) and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), where SDS nanodomains are periodically organized along PLL nanowires. Isothermal titration calorimetry, molecular dynamics simulations, and physicochemical analyses reveal the noncovalent interactions governing the hierarchical assembly. After deposition onto wheat spikes, the flexible nanochains adapt to surface microstructures through topological interlocking, while PLL amino groups form hydrogen bonds with oxygen-containing groups of fatty acids and esters on the wheat spike surface, collectively enhancing adhesion and rainfall-resistant retention. Compared with commercial prochloraz suspension concentrate, the SDS-PLL-Pro system retained 162% more model-tracer after simulated rainfall. Moreover, PLL-mediated membrane disruption synergizes with prochloraz-induced metabolic inhibition, reducing the EC50 against Fusarium graminearum to 0.37-fold that of the commercial formulation. The system also exhibits favorable biosafety and wheat growth-promoting effects. This work provides a topology-guided supramolecular strategy that converts crop surface characteristics into functional advantages for advanced agrochemical delivery.

The Watchful Many: Platelets at the Intersection of Hemostasis, Immunity, and Cancer
articles.abstract: Platelets are anucleate megakaryocyte-derived cytoplastic fragments best known for their roles in hemostasis and thrombosis, but they also play roles in systemic immune surveillance, vascular integrity, and tissue homeostasis. In cancer, this versatility is co-opted through communication between the tumor, bone marrow, and platelets. Tumor-derived cytokines, extracellular vesicles, and inflammatory cues can rewire thrombopoiesis and platelet activation, lifespan, and cargo, giving rise to tumor-educated platelets. Platelets support multiple stages of cancer progression by promoting metastatic traits in the tumor, cancer cell survival in the circulation, immune evasion, and vascular adhesion. Clinically, platelets are key drivers of coagulopathies in cancer patients, including venous and arterial thromboembolism, thrombotic microangiopathy, and disseminated intravascular coagulation. Here, we review platelet biology at the intersection of hemostasis, inflammation, and cancer.

articles.title: The Linguistic Behavior of Third Culture Kids
articles.abstract: Third culture kids (TCKs) grow up as temporary migrants in a host country with an expectation of repatriation to the home country. Ideologies of being international and interstitial, rather than part of the home or host country cultures, lead to complex identity formation. The continual mobility of community members in expatriate communities results in a superdiverse linguistic feature pool for young TCKs to draw from in their own speech development. Studies have shown TCKs are agentive in their individualized combinations of these features, and they have an advantage over non-TCKs in their perceptual skills across multiple linguistic varieties. During repatriation, TCKs typically acquire the dialect of their home country more quickly and completely than second dialect acquisition studies predict, due to their perceptual exposure to the home country variety from their parents, or due to their previous use of the variety prior to moving to the host country.

articles.title: Rethinking Meningioma Biology: Integrating Molecular and Microenvironmental Insights for Mechanism-Guided Therapy
articles.abstract: Meningiomas are the most common primary intracranial tumors, accounting for 42.6% of all central nervous system tumors. Although many meningiomas are indolent, clinical behavior is highly heterogeneous, with recurrence occurring in a minority of low-risk tumors but in more than half of clinically high-risk cases despite standard therapy. During the past decade, significant advancements in molecular profiling have provided insights into meningioma biology and have begun to influence clinical practice. Genomic sequencing, DNA methylation profiling, and gene expression analyses have revealed distinct molecular subgroups with prognostic and therapeutic implications. These advancements, coupled with a growing understanding of the meningioma immune microenvironment, have expanded therapeutic possibilities beyond traditional surgery and radiation approaches. Here, we review how molecular profiling is refining patient stratification and treatment selection, examine the evidence supporting various therapeutic approaches, and explore ongoing clinical trials. Finally, we highlight the critical challenges in advancing personalized medicine for meningioma patients. This comprehensive review provides an integrated overview of current diagnostic and treatment paradigms while offering perspectives on future directions in meningioma therapy.

articles.title: Beyond the Squeeze: Nanodomain Control of Smooth Muscle Mechanotransduction in the Gut
articles.abstract: Gastrointestinal smooth muscle cells (SMCs) generate the forces that drive digestion while continuously sensing and adapting to mechanical deformation. How SMCs detect force and convert it into localized chemical and electrical signals remains poorly understood. We propose that mechanosensory output depends on the spatial organization of the nanodomain a channel occupies, and not on the intrinsic properties of that channel alone. Within these environments, mechanosensitive channels integrate opposing depolarizing and hyperpolarizing currents, translating mechanical load into contraction, relaxation, mechanical compliance, or adaptive remodeling. This junction does not appear to be a permanent structure, because it is assembled during development, maintained under load, and eventually lost with age. Which of those elements fails may then determine the clinical phenotype that results. Two questions remain unresolved within this framework: whether stretch reorganizes the nanodomain itself and whether force is also sensed at organelle membranes rather than at the cell surface alone. Emerging tools may finally resolve these dynamics within the active syncytium, uncovering targets for treating dysmotility.

articles.title: Participatory Budgeting in Public Health: Promise, Evidence, Challenges, and Opportunities
articles.abstract: Participatory budgeting (PB) is a deliberative decision-making process that invites community participation to direct spending for a defined portion of public budgets. Originating in Brazil in the 1980s, PB has since diffused across the globe, including several hundred cases in the United States and Canada alone. PB programs vary but are generally characterized by five core principles: voice, vote, social inclusion, social justice, and oversight. Research on PB shows promising though moderate associations with improved population health outcomes, including infant mortality reductions and health and sanitation spending increases. Despite PB's conceptual alignment with many public health values, adoption of PB by US public health agencies remains limited, constrained by categorical funding requirements, small discretionary budgets, and a polarized sociopolitical environment. This article reviews PB's conceptual foundations, evidence base, and real-world applications before examining structural and political challenges and opportunities for PB as a means to improve the public's health.

This work establishes supramolecular packing as a molecular design strategy for exciton management and solar-to-chemical energy conversion.

articles.title: Transition-Metal-Catalyzed Multicomponent Cycloadditions
articles.abstract: Transition-metal-catalyzed multicomponent cycloadditions provide a powerful strategy for constructing complex cyclic frameworks from simple unsaturated building blocks with high atom and step efficiencies. This Review highlights the progress made in transition-metal-catalyzed multicomponent cycloadditions based on the size of the cyclic products formed. First, reactions that construct five-membered rings, including [2 + 2 + 1], [3 + 1 + 1], and [2 + 1 + 1 + 1] cycloadditions, are discussed with an emphasis on key reactive intermediates, such as carbon monoxide, vinylidenes, carbenoids, and nitrenes. Next, six-membered-ring-forming processes, particularly [2 + 2 + 2], [3 + 2 + 1], [4 + 1 + 1], and [2 + 1 + 2 + 1] cycloadditions, are described, highlighting combinations of alkynes, alkenes, and heteroatom-containing components. The Review then covers strategies for constructing seven-membered rings via [3 + 2 + 2] and [4 + 2 + 1] cycloadditions. Finally, emerging methods that enable the formation of eight- and nine-membered rings through higher-order multicomponent cycloadditions are described. This Review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the conceptual framework, mechanistic principles, and synthetic possibilities of transition-metal-catalyzed multicomponent cycloadditions by organizing them according to ring size and cycloaddition components.

articles.title: Electronic and Thermal Properties of Crystalline and Polycrystalline Ni3S2: A Metal with Weak Grain Boundaries Contribution
articles.abstract: Ni3S2 is a metallic nickel sulfide with promising catalytic properties, yet its transport behavior remains poorly investigated. In this work, we synthesize single-crystalline (via CVT) and densified (via SPS) polycrystalline Ni3S2 samples and characterize their electronic and thermal properties over a broad temperature range, extending up to 700 K for the polycrystalline material. Both samples exhibit metallic conductivity with electron-like carriers, as indicated by a negative Seebeck coefficient (−2.5 μV·K−1 at 320 K) and Hall effect measurements, which yield an apparent carrier density of 4.0 × 1022 cm−3 within a single-band approximation. Polycrystals show a substantially higher residual resistivity ratio (RRR ∼50) than that of single crystals (RRR ∼14). Moreover, the polycrystalline material exhibits a higher thermal conductivity peak at 50 K, indicating that grain boundaries do not strongly limit thermal transport in the highly densified polycrystalline sample and that additional growth-induced structural disorder in the CVT-grown single crystals contributes to phonon scattering. Magnetoresistance reaches +20% at 9 T and 12 K for single crystals, decreasing to +2% at 100 K, with the polycrystalline sample exhibiting even stronger low-temperature responses, further highlighting the limited influence of grain boundaries on charge transport in the highly densified materials. High-temperature measurements confirm the persistence of metallic transport, with ρ reaching 50 μΩ.cm at 700 K. By comparing single-crystalline and polycrystalline Ni3S2, this work establishes a reference for its intrinsic transport behavior and provides insights relevant to researchers seeking to understand and tailor the role of grain boundaries and other forms of disorder in catalytic applications.

articles.title: Investigating the Role of Silica Coating toward Artificial Solid Electrolyte Interphase Formation for Na-Ion Anodes
articles.abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIB) are a promising cost-effective energy storage solution. However, many anode materials developed for SIB suffer from limited cycle life due to interfacial degradation processes. These lead to the formation of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), a heterogeneous nanolayer resulting from electrolyte decomposition. The SEI is essential for stable long-term cycling; however, its continuous growth progressively decreases performance and may eventually lead to failure of the battery cell. In this work, we examine the effect of an artificial SEI made of thin SiO2 layers on Li4Ti5O12 (LTO) nanoparticles used as a SIB anode. The silica coating results in a 24% improvement in cycling stability after 150 cycles, with minimal effect on rate performance. Detailed characterization by solid-state NMR spectroscopy and electron microscopy shows that the silica layer suppresses the growth and alters the composition of the SEI, reducing the formation of inorganic species, particularly NaF and NaF-rich components. Using dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP)-enhanced NMR, a technique that greatly boosts NMR sensitivity, we show how the coating alters the SEI structure, from a layered inorganic core with an organic shell on uncoated LTO to a mixed mosaic-like SEI. Furthermore, we find SEI formation beneath the SiO2 layer, providing molecular-level insights into the interfacial processes. This study provides routes for the design of improved SEI layers, paving the way for the development of more durable and high-performance SIB cells for future energy storage applications.

articles.title: A comprehensive benchmark and dual-encoder baseline for terraced field extraction in complex mountainous regions
articles.abstract: Terraces play a vital role in mitigating runoff and intercepting sediment. Large-scale, high-precision extraction of terraces from remote sensing imagery is essential for environmental monitoring and soil erosion control. However, accurate spatial identification of terraces still presents significant challenges, including scale variability, shadow interference, and complex geometric configurations. To address these issues, we propose DETS-Net, a dual-encoder network that integrates CNN and Transformer architectures. The network employs ResNet-34 as the CNN encoder for local feature detail extraction, utilizes a Transformer encoder to strengthen long-range dependency modeling, and incorporates an adaptive feature fusion (AFF) module for the dynamic integration of the two feature branches. We develop the THDIR dataset, which covers four typical terrain types, namely, plateau mountains, hills, and mountain-basin transition zones, and contains 9,336 standardized 256 × 256 pixel images. We conduct systematic comparisons with eight representative deep learning models. Experimental results demonstrate that DETS-Net achieves an overall accuracy (OA) of 89.91%, a mean intersection over union (MIoU) of 81.28%, and an F1-score of 87.99% on the THDIR dataset, outperforming current mainstream methods in segmentation precision. We apply the optimized model to 2023 remote sensing imagery of Luotian County in the Dabie Mountains, Hubei Province, and generate a high-precision county-level terrace spatial distribution map. This framework supports the assessment of soil and water conservation benefits through area statistics, slope distribution data, and high-precision boundary extraction and provides a reproducible technical pathway for automated terrace mapping using high-resolution remote sensing imagery in complex mountainous regions.

articles.title: Contrasting local responses but similar regional turnover in phytoplankton and rotifer assemblages in saline–alkaline wetlands, Northeast China
articles.abstract: Freshwater salinization and alkalization are emerging threats to global biodiversity, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions. Although ecological impacts of freshwater salinization and alkalization on local biodiversity have received increasing attention, it remains unclear how diversity patterns of organisms in different trophic levels respond at a regional scale. Here, we investigated rotifer and phytoplankton assemblages across 61 wetlands spanning a broad saline–alkaline gradient in the Songnen Plain, Northeast China. We quantified local (alpha) diversity, partitioned beta diversity into turnover and nestedness components, and evaluated how saline–alkaline conditions are associated with assemblage and diversity. Our results showed salinization in wetlands was often associated with high pH, nutrient enrichment, shallower surface water and lower macrophyte coverage, association with a significant decline in local phytoplankton diversity but no significant effect on rotifer diversity. Rotifer assemblages were mainly shaped by water depth, and macrophyte coverage, while phytoplankton assemblages were more influenced by TOC, NH4+-N, water temperature, and macrophyte coverage. Phytoplankton diversity in local wetlands was negatively associated with pH and inorganic nitrogen concentrations, whereas rotifer diversity was associated with water temperature, water depth, and nutrient concentrations. Despite these contrasting local responses, both groups exhibited high spatial compositional dissimilarity among investigated wetlands. Mean total beta diversity reached 0.89 for rotifers and 0.91 for phytoplankton, with turnover accounting for 74.16% and 67.03% of the assemblage dissimilarities, respectively. These findings reveal the profound impacts of freshwater salinization and alkalization on wetland organisms. We highlight the importance of integrating both alpha and beta diversity dimensions in monitoring biodiversity response to these emerging threats in freshwater ecosystems under global environmental change.

articles.title: Coupled MaxEnt-InVEST modelling identifies habitat suitability, quality and conservation gaps of Garrulax maximus
articles.abstract: IntroductionHabitat degradation and conservation gaps severely threaten China's endemic montane birds, yet few studies have integrated habitat suitability with quality assessment.MethodsUsing the nationally protected Giant Laughingthrush (Garrulax maximus) across five provinces in western China and the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, we coupled optimized MaxEnt, InVEST, and GIS approaches to quantify potential distribution, habitat quality, conservation gaps, and environmental drivers. ResultsThe MaxEnt model performed robustly (mean AUC = 0.946). Climate dominated distribution (69.3% cumulative contribution), with annual precipitation (bio12, 35.7%) as the core limiting factor. The species occupied a cold-humid niche: annual precipitation 631.60–794.65 mm, driest-quarter temperature −7.12–2.75 °C, and elevation 2496.79–4012.78 m. High-suitability areas centered on the western Sichuan Basin rim, decreasing outward. Notably, a spatial mismatch emerged between habitat quality and suitability: Yunnan held the largest high-quality habitat (17.28 × 104 km2) but limited priority conservation areas, whereas Sichuan, with less high-quality habitat (13.63 × 104 km2), contained the largest priority zones (6.95 × 104 km2), indicating complementarity rather than substitution. Conservation gaps were extensive (54.26%–75.98%), mainly along reserve boundaries and buffers, revealing structural deficiencies from overemphasizing core zones while neglecting corridors. DiscussionThese findings underscore the urgency of reassessing and expanding protected area networks to cover priority zones. Our integrated framework offers a scientific reference for conserving the Giant Laughingthrush and managing montane birds within the Hengduan Mountains biodiversity hotspot, with implications for broader conservation planning in ecologically sensitive regions.

articles.title: Leaf water status and contrasting physiological response profiles of urban Echinacea purpurea in Budapest
articles.abstract: We examined whether leaf water status, stomatal traits, and biochemical markers followed a common site ranking or formed contrasting response profiles in three public-space stands of Echinacea purpurea ‘Prairie Splendor’ in Budapest, Hungary. The stands occupied a roadside bed at the edge of Vérmező Park, the paved transport hub at Baross Square, and a bed within Pope John Paul II Square park. Microclimate was recorded on 24–26 July 2025, and leaves were sampled on 26 July. Vapour pressure deficit (VPD) and relative water content (RWC) were interpreted alongside stomatal traits, antioxidant-enzyme activities, proline, pigments, and extractable protein. One composite soil sample per site characterised soil chemistry, enzyme activities, and microbiological profiles. At Baross Square, lower mean VPD (1.89 kPa) accompanied a mean RWC of 98.36%. Mean RWC was 97.29% at Attila Street under greater atmospheric drying demand and 84.64% at Pope John Paul II Square, although the latter two sites had nearly identical maximum VPD. The Attila Street profile included shorter, denser stomata, the highest class III peroxidase (POD) and catalase (CAT) activities, and the highest mean proline content. Pope John Paul II Square had the highest mean pigment and extractable-protein contents on a fresh-weight basis. Total superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity and the air pollution tolerance index (APTI) showed no significant site differences, while individual APTI components varied. The descriptive soil profiles distinguished Attila Street, where higher relative organic-matter and phosphorus fractions, microbial respiration, fungal abundance, and functional microbial groups accompanied high RWC. Leaf water status, stomatal traits, and biochemical markers did not share a common site ranking. Their contrasting combinations indicate that leaf hydration alone only partly characterises the physiological state of these urban stands.
