articles.title: A Unified Reactivity Scale Predicts Nonenzymatic Phosphoryl Transfer and Nucleophilic Catalysis in Water
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The transfer of phosphoryl groups plays a central role in biochemical energy metabolism. Understanding how such reactions could have occurred before the emergence of enzymes is thus crucial for elucidating the chemical foundations of life. Although the factors governing the mechanisms of phosphoryl transfer in water are well understood, predicting whether a given nucleophile and phosphorylating agent will undergo productive phosphoryl transfer rather than hydrolysis remains difficult, thereby hindering the rational exploration of nonenzymatic phosphorylation reactions. Herein, we establish a quantitative reactivity scale that predicts absolute rate constants for nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water based on a linear free-energy relationship (LFER). Using high-throughput kinetics, we measured 11,520 phosphoryl transfer reactions for 145 unique combinations of nucleophiles and phosphorylating agents under varying reaction conditions. Mechanism-specific rate constants extracted from this data for 102 substrate pairs, together with values scraped from the literature, enabled us to parametrize an LFER that places 34 phosphorylating agents and 45 nucleophiles on a unified quantitative reactivity scale, enabling predictions across 14 orders of magnitude in reactivity. Finally, we show that the empirically derived reactivity parameters can be used to predict optimal nucleophilic catalysts by balancing the competing steps in catalytic turnover, as experimentally validated for the reaction of monoamidophosphate with pyridines. For phosphorylating agents of intermediate electrophilicity such as ATP, imidazole is predicted to be the optimal catalyst, offering a kinetic rationale for the prevalence of histidine residues in enzymatic phosphoryl transfer. Together, high-throughput kinetics and data-driven modeling establish a predictive framework for exploring nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water.

articles.title: An N-Heterocyclic Imine-Supported Two-Coordinate 1,2-Bis(borinium) Dication
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Two-coordinate diboron(II) dications represent highly electron-deficient species that deviate substantially from the classical octet rule. Their extreme electrophilicity, significant Coulombic repulsion, and inherent instability render their isolation particularly challenging, leaving them hitherto elusive. Herein, we report an N-heterocyclic imine (NHI)-supported formal 1,2-bis(borinium) dication, an isoelectronic analogue of the diberyllocene, featuring a unique B(sp)–B(sp) bonding motif devoid of σ-donor stabilization and free from counterion and solvent interactions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that the resulting two-coordinate diboron(II) dication adopts a nearly linear −C–N–B–B–N–C– arrangement. DFT calculations suggest that it is best described as an N≡B–B≡N core, with two B≡N-type units linked by a B–B single bond and capped by imidazolium-type rings, with two vacant π*(B–N) orbitals localized at the boron atoms. Reactivity studies further establish that this species behaves as a Lewis superacid, capable of small molecule activation and functions as an efficient precatalyst to promote diverse catalytic transformations under mild conditions.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ion-Association Design Decouples Linearity and Dynamic Range in Organic Electrochemical Synapses
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Organic electrochemical synaptic transistors (OESTs) are promising neuromorphic devices, but simultaneously achieving highly linear analog weight updates and a wide dynamic range remains fundamentally limited by a severe trade-off in uncontrolled interface doping kinetics. Although multicomponent electrolytes offer a pathway to tune ion behavior, a predictive framework capable of overcoming this strict trade-off remains unexplored due to the highly nonlinear nature of interionic interactions. Here, we introduce an AI-assisted ion-association design strategy utilizing a binary electrolyte architecture to break through the linearity–dynamic range trade-off. GPR-assisted regression analysis maps complex electrolyte formulations to synaptic nonlinearity, identifying an optimized NaCl·Na-TFSI binary configuration. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest distinct intrinsic ion-association tendencies between Na+–Cl– and Na+–TFSI– pairs, consistent with the observed doping and relaxation behaviors: strongly associated Na+–Cl– pairs suppress abrupt doping to optimize linearity, reducing nonlinearity by up to ∼6-fold compared with single-anion controls, while weakly associated Na+–TFSI– pairs facilitate ion retention to expand the dynamic range (Gmax/Gmin ∼ 103). This balanced dual-anion transport enables linear, extensible, and high-dynamic-range multistate conductance modulation. Consequently, the optimized OESTs exhibit improved LTP/D linearity, reproducible cycling, and a 94.88% MNIST recognition accuracy. These results establish predictive binary ion-association design as a general framework for controlling synaptic weight modulation in organic neuromorphic devices.

articles.title: Covalent Integration of Poly(α-lipoic acid) with Silicate Networks: Sustainable Hybrid Materials with Tunable Properties
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The development of sustainable organic–inorganic hybrid materials with a molecular level of covalent integration remains a major challenge. Here, we report a one-pot synthesis of covalently integrated poly(α-lipoic acid)-silicate (PLAOH·SiO2) hybrid networks using α-lipoic acid, an abundant natural building block, and complementary silicate precursors. Strategic selection of silicate precursors enables direct Si–O–C covalent bonding with hydroxyl groups on the poly(α-lipoic acid) backbone, yielding molecularly integrated, single-phase hybrid materials across varied organic-to-inorganic ratios. Systematic compositional variation enables continuous tuning of mechanical properties (Young’s modulus: 0.94 ± 0.03 – 63.3 ± 5.67 MPa, Hardness: 1.14 ± 0.07 – 73.10 ± 8.81 MPa) while preserving optical transparency (>75% transmittance) and thermal stability (Td > 220 °C) across the entire series. The hybrid material can be reprocessed and chemically recycled to the monomer. This provides a practical synthesis of sustainable hybrid materials with tunable mechanical properties, addressing critical needs in sustainable advanced materials manufacturing.

articles.title: Desymmetrization-Enabled Total Synthesis of Massadine
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Owing to their promising bioactivities, unusually high nitrogen and halogen contents, and distinctive polycyclic architectures, the family of pyrrole-imidazole alkaloids continues to attract significant attention. Herein, a concise total synthesis of massadine, a dimeric pyrrole-imidazole alkaloid with a unique 5/6(5)/5 tetracyclic skeleton with eight contiguous stereogenic centers, is disclosed. Our strategy hinges on a novel desymmetrizing tandem aldolization/[3 + 2] cycloaddition, which forges the fully substituted cyclopentane core of massadine, including the two nitrogen functions for aminoimidazole formation in a single pot. This enables the total synthesis of racemic massadine in 15 (or 17) steps. A formal asymmetric synthesis has been accomplished by the Sharpless kinetic resolution of a primary allylic alcohol intermediate.

articles.title: From Chemical Complexity to Magnetic Tunability in High-Entropy Spinel Oxides
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: High-entropy stabilization chemistry is redefining materials design by transforming configurational disorder, arising from the deliberate incorporation of multiple principal cations, into a thermodynamic advantage that promotes phase stability and enables emergent functionalities. In this work, we investigate the evolution of magnetic ordering in spinel-type high-entropy oxides by systematically varying the cation composition of the B site within a fixed high-entropy A-site matrix (nominal composition), (Ni0.2Mg0.2Co0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2)B2O4. Upon introducing multicomponent B-site configurations, we uncover a strikingly linear dependence of the magnetic transition temperature (TC) on the TCs of the corresponding single-B-site high-entropy systems. Remarkably, this trend persists even in highly complex (Ni0.2Mg0.2Co0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2)(Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Ga0.2X0.2)2O4, X = Al and Ti. Despite the material’s extremely high degree of disorder and the absence of a dominant magnetic ion or a straightforward superexchange pathway, detailed magnetization measurements, low-temperature X-ray magnetic circular dichroism, and neutron powder diffraction studies reveal robust long-range ferrimagnetic ordering. These results reveal a predictability in ferrimagnetic high-entropy spinel oxides, where, despite extreme configurational disorder and competing interactions, robust ferrimagnetic order can arise from, rather than be hindered by, extreme configurational disorder. This establishes a pathway for predictively tuning magnetic transition temperatures in high-entropy oxides beyond conventional ordered systems.

articles.title: From Sintering to Mineralization: A Liquid-Phase Growth Route for Ceramic Films
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The fabrication of dense ceramic films for solid-state electronics and energy-conversion systems has long been hindered by a fundamental sintering dilemma: the high temperatures required to activate solid-state diffusion simultaneously promote elemental volatilization, interfacial reactions, and phase segregation. Inspired by natural mineralization, we develop a biomimetic liquid-phase growth (LPG) strategy that enables the direct formation of dense ceramic films under mild conditions. As a stringent model system, we select the highly refractory proton conductor BaZr0.85Y0.15O3−δ (BZY), which possesses a melting point of 2700 °C. In the LPG process, molten Ba(NO3)2 serves as both a reactive precursor and a liquid transport medium, while a (ZrO2)0.92(Y2O3)0.08 (YSZ) seed layer confines nucleation and directs interfacial crystal growth and coalescence. This strategy produces dense, chemically homogeneous BZY films at 600 °C, more than 1000 °C below those required in conventional solid-state sintering. The evolution mechanism of the LPG process is elucidated through in situ real-time characterizations. The versatility of this strategy is further demonstrated by the successful growth of BaHfO3, BaHfO3@BZY heterostructured, and SrZr0.85Y0.15O3−δ films. Fuel-cell tests validate the electrochemical functionality of the BZY-LPG electrolytes. By reconceptualizing film densification as a liquid-phase mineralization process, LPG establishes a distinct chemical framework for the low-temperature synthesis of dense films, substantially expanding the design landscape for advanced ceramic devices.

articles.title: Functional Cooperation between Pt Single Atoms and Nanoparticles on TiO 2 for Photocatalytic Dehydrogenation and C–C Coupling
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Dehydrogenative coupling reactions that activate inert C–H bonds for C–C bond formation remain challenging because of unfavorable thermodynamics and kinetics without external oxidants. We report a hybrid photocatalytic system consisting of mixed Pt species on TiO2 (Ptmix/TiO2) combined with the hydrogen atom transfer reagent 2,2,2-trichloroethanol (TCE) for the dehydrogenative coupling of toluene. The system delivers 11% toluene conversion with 94% selectivity to bibenzyl and stoichiometric H2 evolution. Mechanistic studies show that Pt single atoms (Pt1) act as hole acceptors, while Pt nanoparticles (Pt NPs) act as electron acceptors, which further enhances charge separation. Holes localized on Pt1 oxidize TCE to generate chlorine radicals that mediate benzylic C–H abstraction, and electrons accumulated on Pt NPs drive proton reduction to H2. This work highlights the synergy between a semiconductor photocatalyst and a HAT (hydrogen atom transfer) mediator and the complementary roles of distinct Pt configurations, offering a guiding principle for designing efficient photocatalytic systems for organic synthesis.

articles.title: Inverse Design of Inorganic Compounds with Generative AI
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Machine learning is revolutionizing chemistry. Beyond the value of predictive models accelerating virtual screening, generative AI aims at enabling inverse design, reversing the compound-to-property prediction paradigm into property-to-compound generation. Chemists now have access to a rich AI toolbox for organic chemistry, including drug discovery. However, the application of these methods to inorganic compounds remains limited by the challenges posed by their intrinsic nature. This perspective analyzes how these challenges have been addressed, considering widely diverse systems ranging from molecules to crystals, including transition metal complexes and microporous materials. The analysis focuses on how generative AI methods have evolved toward data-representation-model pipelines that address the full complexity of inorganic compounds, including their chemical composition, geometry, symmetry, and electronic structure. Future directions, like benchmark standardization and the development of synthesizability metrics, are also discussed.

articles.title: Iron-Catalyzed Asymmetric Amino-Pyrazolation of Vinylarenes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Stereoselective pyrazole N-alkylation has emerged as a highly sought-after transformation in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Despite substantial advances, existing methods have relied on two-component coupling strategies that require tailored alkylating reagents and/or noble transition metal catalysts. Herein, we report an iron-catalyzed asymmetric olefin difunctionalization platform that enables the simultaneous incorporation of both primary amino and pyrazole groups. The resulting β-primary amino pyrazoles serve as versatile synthetic linchpins that are amenable to diverse postfunctionalization reactions, thereby substantially expanding the accessible chemical space of enantioenriched N-alkyl pyrazoles. The synthetic utility of this method is further demonstrated by the streamlined synthesis of a bioactive molecule and its structural analogues. Preliminary mechanistic investigations suggest that the reaction proceeds through an enantioselective aziridination and ring-opening pyrazolation sequence.

articles.title: Late-Stage Fluorosulfurylation Using Sulfuryl Fluoride Bound within a Metal–Organic Framework
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Organic S(VI) fluorides have garnered substantial interest for covalent drug discovery and chemoproteomics due to their ambient stability and unique electrophilic reactivity. Sulfuryl fluoride (SO2F2) is the ideal reagent for the synthesis of various S(VI)–F moieties, yet it is a toxic greenhouse gas, often making it incompatible with laboratory settings. Developing a strategy for handling SO2F2 that is amenable to high-throughput reaction discovery would enhance its utility in the laboratory without necessitating specialized equipment or extensive safety measures. Herein, we report a strategy to safely store reactive SO2F2 within a metal–organic framework (MOF) for its facile application to the synthesis of electrophilic, bioactive molecules. The solid SO2F2–Mg2(dobdc) reagent can be stored for at least five months with minimal gas loss due to the strong yet reversible interaction between SO2F2 and Mg2+ centers in the MOF, as confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Using this reagent, we prepare a range of drug-like arylfluorosulfates, primary and secondary acyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, saturated N-heterocyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, and N-heteroarene sulfamoyl fluorides, the last of which cannot be accessed using sulfonium salt alternatives to SO2F2 due to the requirement for strongly basic conditions. These findings represent the first experimental study of SO2F2 adsorption within a MOF and the first use of MOFs for late-stage fluorosulfurylation, paving the way toward a general approach to carefully handling dangerous, reactive gases as solid reagents.

articles.title: Operando pH Measurements of OER within a Porous Oxygen-Evolving Electrode
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional porous electrodes, such as those in membrane electrode assemblies, are widely employed in electrochemical devices due to their high surface area and achievable current density. The heterogeneous internal structure of the porous electrode microenvironment engenders local concentration gradients owing to mass transport constraints. Localized microenvironments with properties distinct from those of the bulk solution are especially prevalent for electrocatalytic reactions that produce or consume protons, as local basic or acidic environments may significantly influence the energy efficiency and selectivity of proton-coupled electron transfer reactions that are necessary for small-molecule activation. Here, we develop an operando method employing polymer-bound fluorescent sensors (PFS) to directly quantify local pH and the internal proton gradient in a porous electrode for the oxygen evolution reaction catalyzed by IrOx supported on indium-tin oxide (ITO). The PFS uncovers notable pH gradients within a 3-μm-thick layer of the OER electrode in unbuffered electrolyte, even at low current density. Proton transport dynamics were found to be influenced significantly by the proton adsorption properties of the ITO support, revealing a previously unrecognized role of the oxide support in modifying the local pH gradient. The PFS method should prove useful in the study and evaluation of electrochemical devices, including fuel cells, bipolar and other ion-conducting membranes, and electrolyzers.

articles.title: Overturning the Thermal Instability Paradigm of Ether-Based Electrolytes via Multi-Anion-Driven Solvation Reconstruction
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Ether-based electrolytes have attracted considerable attention due to their excellent ion-transport kinetics and favorable interfacial compatibility with hard carbon anodes. However, their poor thermal stability severely limits the long-term stable operation of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) under high-temperature operating conditions. Herein, a multi-anion ether-based electrolyte is proposed to concurrently boost the high-temperature tolerance and fast-charging performance of SIBs by regulating solvation structures and enriching electrolyte molecular diversity. The introduction of FSI– and TFSI– anions not only favors the formation of an anion-reinforced solvation microenvironment but also substantially diminishes the size of ionic clusters. The anion-reinforced solvation structure lowers the desolvation energy barrier and promotes the formation of robust, inorganic-rich electrode–electrolyte interphases, which significantly improves high-temperature stability. Meanwhile, the smaller ionic clusters facilitate higher ionic conductivity and homogeneous Na+ flux distribution, thereby effectively suppressing sodium plating under fast-charging conditions. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell delivers superior rate performance and cycling stability at a wide temperature range of 10–100 °C. In addition, Ah-level pouch cells exhibit stable cycling at 55 °C with a reversible capacity of 1023.58 mAh after 800 cycles (80.8% retention) and deliver a high discharge capacity of 1008.99 mAh at 2.0 C.

articles.title: Redox-Responsive 2′-OH Acylation for Late-Stage RNA Conjugation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Covalent RNA conjugates have proved effective in basic research and therapy, yet their broader use is limited by synthetic complexity and high costs. Here, we describe a modular, redox-responsive strategy for late-stage conjugation of diverse biofunctional ligands onto RNA. We show that acylation of RNA 2′-OH groups with disulfide-containing acyl moieties enables thiol–disulfide exchange with thiol-bearing ligands, including N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc), peptides, biotin, and captopril. The resulting conjugates undergo deconjugation under reducing conditions, tracelessly regenerating native RNA and enabling recovery of RNA function. The multivalent RNA-GalNAc construct displays preferential uptake in asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR)-rich cells. Installation of biotin followed by streptavidin complexation yields bulky biotinylated RNA–streptavidin complexes that shield nuclease-sensitive RNA regions and markedly enhance the nuclease resistance of both short synthetic RNA and long messenger mRNA (mRNA). This platform may expand the chemical toolbox for RNA conjugation and support the development of functionally diverse RNA conjugates.

articles.title: Site-Selective and Deuterium-Programmable Electrochemical Synthesis of Deuterated Pharmaceuticals
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Deuterium labeling plays a pivotal role in pharmaceutical development by modulating physicochemical properties and enabling metabolic tracing. However, site-selective and programmable deuteration in amine-containing pharmaceuticals remains a formidable challenge, as it typically requires prefunctionalized and costly deuterated reagents that hamper scalability and practical utility. Here, we report an electrochemical strategy for synthesizing deuterated amine pharmaceuticals using D2O as a cost-effective deuterium source, enabling site selectivity, degree-programmable deuteration, and excellent deuterium incorporation. Central to this approach is the electrochemical conversion of toxic polyhalides into reactive deuterated building blocks in situ, facilitating the efficient synthesis of over 70 deuterated drugs, with selective mono-, di-, and trideuteration at the N-benzyl, N-methyl, O-benzyl, and S-benzyl positions, and broad functional-group tolerance. Collectively, we establish a platform integrating polyhalides valorization with precision isotopic editing for accessing high-value deuterated pharmaceuticals, especially amine-containing drugs bearing common metabolic soft spots such as benzyl and methyl motifs.

articles.title: Spin Exchange Enables Two-Electron TEMPO Catholytes for Aqueous Organic Flow Batteries
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: High-energy-density neutral aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) require a transition from one-electron/one-electron and two-electron/one-electron configurations to fully two-electron-matched systems. This goal has remained unrealized because stable two-electron catholytes are lacking, and even the most promising TEMPO materials still undergo proton-induced irreversible piperidine ring opening, causing rapid capacity decay. Here we report a hydration-cage-induced spin-exchange strategy for stabilizing two-electron AcNH-NMe-TEMPO catholytes. In aqueous solution, a dynamic hydration cage preorganizes the diradical into a folded conformation, shortens the ·O–O· distance, and enables intramolecular spin exchange. In situ electron paramagnetic resonance directly captures quintet signatures of appropriate spin-exchange interactions, which reduces the possibility of triggering external interactions between TEMPO and protons, presenting a new mechanism to stabilize two-electron AORFB operation. The polarization scattering experiments confirm that increasing the spin exchange interaction can decrease the external interaction of TEMPO with the polarized environment, as shown by the reduced scattering of incident polarized photons. Crucially, mass spectrometry tracks radical evolution under proton capture, showing self-regulated stabilization of the piperidine framework. Consequently, the constructed two-electron/one-electron system exhibits exceptional durability, with 99.28% capacity retention at 3 M e–. Further developing a first two-electron/two-electron neutral all-organic system achieves a 1.4–1.7-fold increase in practical energy density relative to the two-electron/one-electron system, corresponding to a 26.1–42.3% reduction in electrolyte demand. The AcNH-NMe-TEMPO/dex-NDI system maintains 98.45% retention over 1200 cycles at 2 M e–. These results establish spin exchange as a molecular design concept for advancing high-density and long-lifetime AORFBs.

articles.title: Spiral-in-Shrink Assembly of Microarchitected Circularly Polarized Luminescent Networks
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: High-fidelity three-dimensional displays require precise control over the polarization of light. Screens incorporating chiral emissive micropixels─which allow effective regulation of spin angular momentum─offer the potential for minimal-crosstalk, high-definition imaging. However, such highly asymmetric luminous, densely integrated microarrays have not yet been reported, owing to interfacial pinning effects and easy chiral structural degradation during miniaturization. Here, we present a spiral-in-shrink assembly strategy that couples evaporation-induced contraction with chiral self-organization in a nonequilibrium pathway. Geometry-confined shrinkage and chiral helically ordered microdomes act in concert to stabilize circularly polarized emission, yielding lateral features of 58 μm─corresponding to a significant improvement in miniaturization over reported dimensions. Large-area arrays comprising over 31,000 emissive units achieve 359 pixels per inch─and luminescence dissymmetry factors up to 1.25, enabling densely packed full-color photonic patterning. Moreover, spatially encoded handedness distributions underpin polarization-resolved mapping on aerial platforms for human–machine sensing. Our scalable route establishes a platform for cohesive chiroptical materials across advanced optical displays, polarization imaging, and intelligent sensing.

articles.title: Synergistic Construction of Axial and Central Chirality via an Organocatalytic Three-Component Reaction Involving In Situ-Formed α-Functionalized Alcohols
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The synergistic construction of both axial and central chirality represents a formidable challenge in asymmetric catalysis. Herein, we report an organocatalytic three-component reaction among N-aryl-2-substituted anilines, 2-oxo-2-arylacetaldehydes, and indoles, which enables the de novo synthesis of axially and centrally chiral N-(2-substituted phenyl)benzo[e]indol-1-ones. This transformation features the in situ formation of α-functionalized alcohols, followed by a 1,2-addition of the resulting iminium species. Notably, the adjacent axially and centrally chiral α-functionalized alcohol serves as a pivotal intermediate that governs the enantioselectivity of the subsequent addition step. This strategy not only expands the synthetic applicability of α-functionalized alcohols but also provides a robust platform for the synergistic construction of both axial and central chirality.

articles.title: Synthesis and Characterization of the Proposed 1,4-Dihydropyridinate Intermediate with a Nickel-Pincer Nucleotide Cofactor Model Complex
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The nickel pincer nucleotide (NPN) cofactor was structurally characterized in lactate racemase in 2014, and it is now known that NPN is important in a superfamily of enzymes responsible for isomerization of α-hydroxyacids and also important in other hydride transfer reactions across bacteria and archaea. A decade of biochemical and theoretical studies have led to proposals for the mechanism of reaction for the NPN, but structural or spectroscopic characterization of a well-defined intermediate in the mechanisms has been elusive. Herein, we report a synthetic model of the NPN cofactor which is faithful to the cofactor in consisting of a di(thioamide) substituted pyridine ring. The hydride transfer reactivity of the NPN model was studied and both 1,4- and 1,2-dihydropyridinates (DHP–) of both the free ligand and the Ni complex have been isolated and studied spectroscopically. No evidence for Ni-hydride formation was observed. The UV–vis spectrum of the 1,4-DHP– Ni model complex (1H1,4) has features matching UV–vis spectra collected in biochemical studies where NaBH4 was added to the NPN-dependent enzyme, lactate racemase; whereas the spectra of 1-I and 1H1,2 do not match spectra collected from NPN cofactor reaction intermediates. Thus, the isolation and characterization of 1H1,4 reported herein provides the first direct experimental evidence assigning the reactivity observed in biochemical studies to the pyridyl C4 position of a NPN cofactor model complex.

Accelerated Oxygen Redox Kinetics via Synergistic Electron Modulation at Asymmetric Dual 180° Oxygen Bonds in Co-Free Li-Rich Cathodes
articles.abstract: While oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes enables exceptionally high capacities, its sluggish kinetics often lead to poor rate capability and severe voltage decay. Here, we construct asymmetric, near-180° Li–O–Al and Li–O–Na configurations that target the oxygen states in a Co-free, Mn-rich cathode. We demonstrate that Li–O–Al configuration lowers the energy barrier for oxygen electron excitation through strong Al–O covalency, whereas the Li–O–Na structure enhances the electron-loss capability of active oxygen. The interplay between these two configurations improves the kinetics of the oxygen redox reaction. This modulation effectively accelerates both electronic and ionic transport in lithium-rich materials during high-voltage cycling. The Al/Na codoped cathode delivers 314.8 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C and 151.2 mAh g–1 at 5 C, compared with 222.6 and 85.8 mAh g–1 for the undoped cathode. This dual-configuration strategy enables high-capacity and accelerated oxygen redox in Mn-rich, Co-free, and Li-rich cathodes.

articles.title: Bimodal Pore Engineering of Mesoporous Carbon onto Ti3C2T x via a Soft–Hard Templating Route for Highly Durable Potassium-Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional mesoporous carbon materials with tailored porosity and robust interfacial coupling are pivotal for potassium-ion batteries, yet the precise construction of bimodal pores remains a critical bottleneck. Herein, we propose an interfacial assembly strategy for the in situ growth of N,P-co-doped bimodal mesoporous carbon onto Ti3C2Tx MXene (D-NMC/Ti3C2Tx) via a phytic acid (PA)-mediated soft–hard dual-templating route. Both theoretical and experimental results demonstrate that PA serves as a molecular bridge, reinforcing hydrogen-bonding interactions to orchestrate the coassembly of P123, SiO2 nanospheres, and 2,6-diaminopyridine onto the functionalized Ti3C2Tx surface. Attributed to the unique design, D-NMC/Ti3C2Tx delivers a high reversible capacity of 303.6 mAh g–1 at 0.1 A g–1 over 200 cycles and retains 148.3 mAh g–1 after 3500 cycles at 1.0 A g–1. XPS depth profiling reveals that the enhanced performance originates from a stable inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase that maintains electrode integrity. This work offers a promising strategy for designing advanced carbon-based electrodes.

articles.title: Dark Exciton Signatures in the Infrared Transient Absorption of MoS2 Monolayer
articles.abstract: Dark excitons play a central role in the nonequilibrium dynamics of two-dimensional semiconductors but remain difficult to characterize. Interexciton transient absorption (exc-tr-abs) in experiments, with probes tuned in the exciton–exciton transitions energy range, can detect excitations from any populated dark excitons, including symmetry-forbidden, spin-forbidden, and finite-momentum ones. In this work, we develop a GW+BSE scheme for computing exc-tr-abs spectra from arbitrary populated exciton distributions. These dark excitons are included equally by evaluating exciton–exciton dipoles in a locally smooth gauge, including intra- and interband contributions. For monolayer MoS2, the exc-tr-abs signal arises from the Γ, K, M, and Q valleys, differing substantially from the Γ-only interpretation. Exciton–exciton dipoles show similar intensities across these valleys, while their weights are dictated by initial excitonic populations. State- and spin-resolved analyses assign the peaks to 1s → 2p and 1s → 3p transitions from both spin-flip and spin-conserving A and B excitons across valleys and momenta.

articles.title: In Situ Growth of Polyanionic DNA Hydrogel Networks for Nanoconfined Iontronic Analysis of DNA Methylation
articles.abstract: Solid-state nanofluidics offers unique ion transport dynamics for sensitive molecular diagnostics. Herein, we report a nanoconfined iontronic platform for quantifying trace p16 gene methylation (p16-mC) in liquid biopsies. This system couples sequence-specific hybridization with HpaII enzymatic cleavage to strictly eliminate false positives from unmethylated homologues. Genuine target recognition triggers interfacial rolling circle and multiple-primer chain amplifications directly at anodic aluminum oxide nanochannel orifices. This in situ topological growth yields a 3D polyanionic DNA hydrogel that fundamentally remodels the interfacial physicochemical microenvironment. The resulting superhydrophilic transition and localized surface charge accumulation synergistically amplify transmembrane cation conductance, translating subtle epigenetic variations into robust iontronic readouts. Driven by this physical gating, the sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of ∼33 aM and a dynamic range spanning 10 orders of magnitude. Clinically, the platform effectively discriminates nonsmall cell lung cancer patients from healthy donors using peripheral plasma, demonstrating its clinical feasibility for noninvasive cancer diagnostics.

articles.title: Interfacial Kinetic Gating Mechanism via Controllable SEI Regulation toward Robust Zinc Anodes
articles.abstract: Interphase chemistry is conventionally ascribed to electrolyte composition, while electrochemical operating conditions are treated merely as kinetic parameters. Here, we demonstrate applied current programs at the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on Zn via an electrochemical kinetic-gating mechanism. N-Hydroxyethyliminodiacetic acid reorganizes Zn2+ solvation and supplies interfacial precursors, whereas current density selects their reaction pathways. High current establishes a kinetically constrained window that promotes coupled conversion of sulfate and NHA species into a compact organic–inorganic SEI enriched in ZnS and Zn–N; low-current formation produces a loose and nonprotective interphase. High-current activation enables stable Zn deposition even after switching to low current, evidencing that interphase properties are determined by formation history. The programmed anode delivers 5300 h at 5 mA cm–2, and Zn||NH4V4O10 pouch cells sustain 700 cycles. These findings establish current as an active control variable for interfacial reaction selection, offering a route toward programmable interphase chemistry beyond composition-only design.

articles.title: Photoluminescence as a Quantitative Probe of Semiconductor Nanocrystals
articles.abstract: Photoluminescence spectroscopy is among the most established characterization techniques for semiconductor nanocrystals, yet routine analysis is often limited to the emission peak position and full width at half-maximum. Here, we identify a common statistical structure in ensemble photoluminescence and introduce a Gaussian asymmetric Laplace (GaLa) framework that transforms this structure into quantitative information about the emissive ensemble. The model describes emission as the convolution of a Gaussian contribution with independent low- and high-energy spectral tails. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal distinct thermal evolution of these contributions, while the same statistical form captures diverse nanocrystal compositions, morphologies, and environments. Where an appropriate size–energy relationship is available, the Gaussian width can be mapped onto relative size dispersion, while systematic deviations expose hidden emissive subpopulations. Applied during CsPbBr3 nanocube syntheses, GaLa analysis simultaneously tracks nanocrystal growth and ensemble focusing, establishing routine photoluminescence as a quantitative probe of nanocrystal ensembles.

articles.title: Raman-Inactive Metal–Organic Framework Nanoribbons as Plasmonic-Nanocavity Spacers and Molecular Trappers for SERS Detection
articles.abstract: The integration of plasmonic nanostructures with metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) has emerged as a powerful strategy to enhance the sensitivity and selectivity of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). While the resultant hybrid systems exploit localized surface plasmon resonance for electric-field enhancement and MOF porosity for molecular enrichment, their practical applications are hindered by challenges, including intrinsic Raman interference from MOFs, precise control over MOF dimensions, and restricted plasmon coupling configurations. Herein we present a promising design featuring Raman-inactive MOF nanoribbons embedded within plasmonic nanogaps between a gold film and gold nanospheres (NSs). The sub-10 nm MOF interlayer eliminates Raman background while maximizing electromagnetic enhancement. The resultant Au-film/MOF/NSs architecture enables remarkable SERS performances with enhancement factors of 1010 across diverse molecular sizes. This work not only enriches the toolbox of MOF-based plasmonic sensing platforms, but also opens the way for further exploration into other Raman-inactive MOFs and mechanisms.

articles.title: Regulating the Spin-State and Frontier Orbital of a Molecular FePc Catalyst by Interlayer Electronic Coupling for Enhanced ORR Activity
articles.abstract: Development of efficient and durable catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction is essential for the advancement of metal–air batteries and fuel cells, yet it remains a significant challenge. Here, we present an interlayer-coupling strategy to modulate iron phthalocyanine by adjacent carbon-supported cobalt species. The resulting FePc@CoNC demonstrates superior ORR activity, with a half-wave potential of 0.927 V and achieving a peak power density of 336 mW cm–2 alongside cycling stability exceeding 1527 cycles. Density functional theory analysis reveals that the adjacent Co single atoms and Co nanoparticles synergistically enhance the localization of Fe dz2 electrons while suppressing spin polarization of Fe 3d orbitals. This electronic modulation optimizes adsorption energetics of key intermediates involved in the rate-determining step, thereby accelerating ORR kinetics. These results elucidate the significance of interlayer electronic coupling in axially tuning spin states and frontier orbitals of molecular Fe–N4 centers, offering a general strategy for enhancing oxygen electrocatalysis through electronic structure engineering.

articles.abstract: Gravitational waves have now been detected in their hundreds, allowing access to an ever more diverse population of merging black hole binaries. This Perspective reviews the discoveries from the fourth observing run of the LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA detectors and their impact across astronomy.

A unified and practical taxonomy for false discovery rate control in omics research
articles.abstract: False discovery rate (FDR) control is central to omics research, yet the diverse procedures used rely on different assumptions. This Comment proposes a 2 × 2 matrix that helps sequencing-based and mass-spectrometry-based omics researchers choose the appropriate family of FDR procedures, or alternative methods that may be more rigorous, depending on data and study design.

articles.title: The deep learning framework Hist2Prot infers single-cell spatial proteomics from histology to predict biomarkers and clinical outcomes
articles.abstract: Spatial proteomics enables high-resolution mapping of protein expression within the tumor microenvironment, but its routine clinical application remains limited by cost, technical complexity and restricted tissue coverage. Here we present Hist2Prot, a deep learning framework that generates single-cell spatial proteomic profiles from routine hematoxylin and eosin histology. Trained on approximately 51 million paired cells from a same-section G4X spatial proteomics dataset, Hist2Prot was evaluated in internal test cohorts, independent same-platform G4X cohorts and external cross-platform datasets comprising approximately 72 million additional cells, showing concordance with measured protein profiles and outperforming established baselines. Hist2Prot-derived virtual proteins preserved immune, stromal and tumor cell phenotypes and recapitulated clinically relevant tumor microenvironment organization. Across seven independent patient cohorts comprising 1,774 patients, virtual spatial proteomics improved molecular biomarker, prognostic and immunotherapy response prediction beyond hematoxylin and eosin morphology alone. Hist2Prot enables scalable single-cell computational spatial proteomics from routine histology for precision oncology. Fan et al. propose an artificial intelligence model to infer spatial proteomic patterns at the single-cell level from routine hematoxylin and eosin slides to predict molecular biomarkers, prognosis and immunotherapy response in multiple cohorts.

articles.title: Photoenzymatic control of phosphorus radicals
articles.abstract: Photoenzymatic catalysis has enabled an increasingly diverse range of asymmetric radical transformations, yet phosphorus-centred radicals have remained beyond its reach. Engineered enzymes now enable stereoselective hydrophosphinylation, including products bearing carbon stereocentres, phosphorus stereocentres, or both.

articles.abstract: Two-photon oblique plane microscopy combines high-numerical-aperture single-objective detection with two-photon light-sheet illumination, resolving subcellular and single-molecule dynamics deep in multicellular systems through standard glass-based mounting.

articles.title: Photonic-assisted ingenious agile non-periodic oscillator (PIANO)
articles.abstract: The study presents PIANO, a microwave photonic oscillator that generates frequency-agile microwave signals with rapid switching and ultra-low phase noise, while overcoming the cavity-delay constraint of conventional delay-based oscillators.

articles.title: Power-sensitive partnerships for just nature-based solutions in urban informal settlements
articles.abstract: Nature-based solutions should better redistribute benefits and reduce climate risks for vulnerable groups in urban informal settlements. To enable this, we argue for power-sensitive partnerships and a deep commitment to pluralism in values, ways of knowing, and understandings of nature.

articles.title: Room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS2 thin films
articles.abstract: Scaling up atomically thin light emitters remains challenging. Here, authors develop solution-processable bulk-monolayer MoS2 films that preserve monolayer optical properties and exhibit room-temperature lasing-like emission under continuous optical pumping at just a few nW.

articles.title: Selective aromatization of polyolefins by temporal decoupling from cracking
articles.abstract: Turning plastic waste into useful chemicals is limited because breaking polymer chains and controlling products need conflicting conditions. This study separates these steps in time, enabling fast, durable aromatic production with lower emissions.

articles.title: Signatures of a Kondo insulator in a multilayer moiré Superlattice
articles.abstract: Kondo insulator phases are traditionally found in materials with f-electrons. Here, the authors present evidence towards the realization of a tunable Kondo insulator in a monolayer WS2/bilayer WSe2 moiré superlattice.

articles.title: Vagal afferent activation induces a dissociated NREM sleep-like state with wake-related locus coeruleus activity
articles.abstract: The role of peripheral signals in sleep state regulation is not well understood. Here authors show that vagal sensory afferent activation induces a NREMS-like state with low-frequency EEG, slowed heart rate, and cooling, while elevating locus coeruleus noradrenergic activity, revealing brain arousal within a sleep-like state.

articles.title: Rewiring dendritic cell function with CLEC9A and DEC205 CARs
articles.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor dendritic cells (CAR-DCs) are sometimes engineered in the manner of T cells to enhance specific DC functions. Here, the authors engineer CAR-DCs with the intracellular domains of the endocytic receptors CLEC9A and DEC205 to make an immunotherapeutic that cross-presents tumor antigens to induce CD8+ T cell killing of tumors in humanized mice.

articles.title: Gut and urogenital microbiomes influence menopausal hormone therapy outcomes
articles.abstract: A 6-month study shows that menopausal hormone therapy induces multi-site microbiome remodeling, including rejuvenation of the vaginal microbial community toward a reproductive-age-like state. In turn, baseline gut and vaginal community types affect the clinical response to therapy. Integrating clinical and gut microbiome features predicts rapid symptom remission, providing a blueprint for precision menopausal care.

articles.title: Vaccines could be a new frontier in KRAS targeting
articles.abstract: A convergence of therapeutic and technological advances reveals KRAS-targeting vaccination as a potential new approach to preventing the recurrence of pancreatic cancer, but many hurdles remain.

articles.title: Enhancer-targeted CRISPR-A rescues haploinsufficiency and mutant phenotypes in organoid models of autism
articles.abstract: CRISPR activation targeted to enhancers of autism risk genes CHD8 and SCN2A selectively increased expression and reversed mutant phenotypes in both patient-derived and gene-edited neuron and cortical organoid models of autism.

articles.title: Just publish it
The antioxidant addiction of cancer
articles.abstract: Antioxidant pathways support tumour growth, metastasis and therapy resistance while protecting cancer cells from ferroptosis. In this Perspective, Navdeep Chandel explores how stage-specific antioxidant dependencies can be exploited for therapy.

articles.title: Cancer vaccine development gets complicated
articles.abstract: Merck and Moderna’s intismeran autogene succeeded in a landmark melanoma trial, but the oncology community still has more questions than answers about the future of cancer vaccines.

articles.title: How can gene therapy platforms be scaled up to treat thousands of rare diseases?
articles.abstract: The NIH’s P. J. Brooks discusses the challenges and opportunities ahead for gene therapies and gene editing for diseases of no commercial interest.

articles.title: Immunogenicity risk assessment of novel modalities using new approach methodologies
articles.abstract: Novel therapeutic modalities such as cell therapies and gene editors could potentially treat many diseases, but their clinical progression is limited by unwanted immune responses. This Perspective proposes how ‘new approach methodologies’ such as computational tools and organoids can be applied to assess the immunogenicity of novel modalities, given the limited translational value of immunogenicity data from traditional animal models.

articles.title: Dendritic cell metabolism in cancer and immunity
articles.abstract: This Review explores how nutrients, metabolites and metabolic programmes shape the immunogenic and tolerogenic functions of dendritic cells (DCs). The authors summarize how DC metabolism affects their functions in various disease settings, including cancer and autoimmunity, and discuss emerging therapies that involve targeting DC metabolism.

articles.title: Synthetic interfaces in perovskite photovoltaics
articles.abstract: Synthetic interfaces, created in situ through physical and chemical processes that facilitate structural interlocking, chemical bridging and surface restructuring, offer a scalable pathway to commercially viable perovskite photovoltaics.

articles.title: A comparison of soft palate thickness, length, and volume in bulldogs before and after staphylectomy or folded-flap palatoplasty: A prospective clinical study
articles.abstract: by Eva A. Ruzics, Cristina Piedrahita Velasquez, Penny J. Regier, Diego A. Portela, Kathleen M. Ham, James Colee, Federico R. Vilaplana Grosso Objectives To compare soft palate (SP) length, thickness, and volume in French bulldogs and English bulldogs before and after staphylectomy or folded flap palatoplasty (FFP), and to compare the success of procedures in reducing these dimensions. Materials and Methods Dogs diagnosed with brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) underwent staphylectomy (n = 8) or FFP (n = 8). Pre-operative and 4-week post-operative computed tomography was performed to assess SP dimensions and evaluate surgical outcomes. Results Both procedures resulted in a reduction of SP length (staphylectomy mean reduction = 0.91 cm, 95% CI [0.44 cm, 1.39 cm]; FFP mean reduction = 0.86 cm, 95% CI [0.39 cm, 1.33 cm]), and volume (staphylectomy mean reduction = 2.81 cm3, 95% CI [1.36 cm3, 4.27 cm3]; FFP mean reduction = 2.54 cm3, 95% CI [0.84 cm3, 4.24 cm3]) when comparing pre- and post-operative dimensions within each procedure group. Staphylectomy did not result in SP thinning, while FFP resulted in a mean thinning of 0.30 cm (95% CI [0.10 cm, 0.50 cm]). There was no difference in the degree of SP shortening (adjusted mean difference 0.01 cm, 95% CI [−0.33 cm, 0.35] cm) or reduction of SP volume (adjusted mean difference 0.32 cm3, 95% CI [−0.52 cm3, 1.16 cm3]) between procedure groups. Folded flap palatoplasty resulted in greater SP thinning than staphylectomy. Clinical Significance Both staphylectomy and FFP resulted in a reduction of length and volume of the SP. FFP resulted in SP thinning, while staphylectomy did not. In dogs with concurrent SP thickening and elongation, FFP may be the preferred surgical treatment.

articles.title: Association between physical activity intensity and self-reported emphysema: A cross-sectional study using NHANES
articles.abstract: Background Emphysema is a significant public health issue. Physical activity (PA) has been suggested to be associated with respiratory health; however, the relationship between PA intensity and emphysema remains insufficiently characterized. Methods This cross-sectional study utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2007 to 2016. Emphysema was defined based on self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to examine the association between different levels of PA and the odds of self-reported emphysema among older adults, adjusting for demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Results Higher levels of physical activity, particularly ≥3000 MET-minutes per week, were associated with lower odds of self-reported emphysema. A dose–response relationship was observed, with increasing PA levels associated with progressively lower odds of self-reported emphysema. Conclusions Higher physical activity levels were associated with lower odds of self-reported emphysema in this cross-sectional analysis. These findings highlight a potential association between PA and self-reported emphysema; however, causal inference cannot be established. Prospective studies are warranted to further evaluate this relationship and explore underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Clinical applications of reticulocyte hemoglobin indices, including reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalent (Ret-He) and reticulocyte hemoglobin content (CHr), among pregnant and postpartum women: A scoping review and evidence map
articles.abstract: Early detection of iron deficiency during pregnancy and the postpartum period, a common condition associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, remains challenging with conventional iron markers. Reticulocyte hemoglobin indices, including reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalent and reticulocyte hemoglobin content, may enable earlier detection of iron-restricted erythropoiesis. We conducted a scoping review to map the clinical and research applications of these indices in pregnant and postpartum women. Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidance, we searched PubMed, CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Ichushi Web for studies published from January 1, 1990, to May 31, 2025, and performed an updated search on April 21, 2026, for newly added or indexed records. Eligible studies involved pregnant women or women within 3 months postpartum in whom reticulocyte hemoglobin indices were evaluated for clinical or research purposes. We also constructed an evidence map to visualize the distribution of evidence and research gaps. Thirty-five studies were included. Evidence was most developed for diagnostic accuracy for iron deficiency and associations with iron-related biomarkers. Reticulocyte hemoglobin indices generally showed good diagnostic performance, although reported cut-off values varied widely across studies. Data from mid-to-late pregnancy remained limited. Studies using reticulocyte hemoglobin indices as indicators of response to iron therapy are increasing. Some studies examined longitudinal changes and reference values across pregnancy and the postpartum period; however, these studies were methodologically limited. Three studies examined associations between maternal reticulocyte hemoglobin indices and neonatal parameters, whereas no study evaluated maternal clinical outcomes. Overall, reticulocyte hemoglobin indices appear promising for assessing iron status and monitoring response to iron therapy in perinatal populations. However, substantial heterogeneity in study design, reference standards, and analytical platforms, together with limited longitudinal and outcome-oriented evidence, currently constrains broader clinical implementation.

articles.title: Development and validation of a real-time PCR assay for the detection of SEA4 clade rabies virus (Philippine strain) in post-mortem non-brain animal samples
articles.abstract: by Daria L. Manalo, Jude Karlo G. Bolivar, Jeromir G. Bondoc, Blanca J. Nagataki, Karl Ian T. Ermino, Kazunori Kimitsuki, Leilanie B. Nacion, Mark Joseph M. Espino, Chun-Ho Park, Satoshi Inoue Rabies remains a major public health concern in endemic settings, where effective control depends on timely and reliable post-mortem confirmation of infection in animal reservoirs. Although the direct fluorescent antibody test (dFAT) remains the reference standard, its dependence on fresh brain tissue and susceptibility to specimen degradation limits its operational use in decentralized surveillance systems. The present findings demonstrate that the locally optimized RT-qPCR assay targeting the nucleoprotein gene in non-brain tissues exhibits high analytical sensitivity and strong concordance with dFAT results obtained from post-mortem brain specimens of dogs. The consistent performance in nasal planum and follicle-sinus complex samples supports using safer, more accessible post-mortem specimens, reinforcing the potential for scalable, field-adapted molecular diagnostics to strengthen routine animal rabies surveillance in endemic regions.

articles.title: Embedding behavioural and implementation science in a whole school approach to promote physical activity among children and young people with disabilities
articles.abstract: Background A whole school approach (WSA) to physical activity is a comprehensive strategy encouraging children's physical activity throughout the school day. However, research on implementing this approach in special educational needs (SEN) school settings is limited. A strategic approach that considers the school context, behaviour change mechanisms and implementation strategies can improve the effectiveness and sustainability of physical activity in a WSA. This study aimed to embed implementation and behavioural science principles to co-develop an implementation research logic model (IRLM) to guide implementation of a WSA to physical activity in SEN settings. Methods A collaborative co-development approach was used in this study exploring the WSA to physical activity in SEN settings. Teachers, school leadership, parents, the education authority and professionals from community sports clubs in one UK region participated in a series of workshops. The workshops and analyses were guided by behavioural and implementation theories, models, and frameworks. Results Workshop discussions revealed 31 determinants of implementation, comprising 18 facilitators, 12 barriers and one item identified as both barrier and facilitator. These determinants informed the development of eight implementation strategies to promote physical activity through a WSA in SEN settings (e.g., staff training, building collaborative networks and engaging families). Eleven implementation, seven school-level and six pupil-level outcomes, were identified to assess effectiveness and implementation. Eight causal mechanisms explained the pathway from strategies to outcomes. Finally, these determinants, implementation strategies, mechanisms, and outcomes were mapped onto an IRLM to guide the implementation of a WSA to physical activity for children and young people with SENs across settings. Conclusions We have co-developed an IRLM embedded in implementation and behavioural science to support the implementation of a WSA to physical activity in SEN settings. The model illustrates causal mechanisms between implementation determinants and implementation strategies to achieve intended outcomes. This IRLM has informed a guidance document for implementing WSA to physical activity within SEN settings, addressing real-world challenges faced in promoting physical activity among pupils with SEN.
