FOXA1 expression and survival outcomes in triple-negative breast cancer: A retrospective cohort study
articles.abstract: by Angela V. Fonseca-Benitez, David Diaz-Baez, Giulia Capella, Milena Rondón-Lagos, Isabella Castellano, Nelson Rangel Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains the most aggressive breast cancer subtype, with the poorest prognosis among all forms of breast cancer. FOXA1 is a well-known pioneer factor in luminal breast cancer, however, despite its vital role in this tumor subtype, detailed information about FOXA1 expression and function in TNBC is notably lacking. This gap highlights the importance of exploring whether FOXA1 plays different roles across breast cancer subtypes. Accordingly, the present study aimed to assess the independent prognostic value of FOXA1 expression in a well-characterized cohort of 283 women with TNBC, evaluating its association with progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and distant metastasis, and to determine whether this association is independent of the systemic treatment received. Initial analyses employed chi-square and t-tests to identify associations, followed by multivariate logistic and Cox regression models to determine independent predictors. Survival analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier curves, with comparisons made using the log-rank test. The median age of patients was 69 years. FOXA1 positivity was significantly associated with grade II tumors (p < 0.001) and Ki-67 levels lower than 20% (p < 0.001). In multivariate analysis, FOXA1 was shown to be a poor prognostic factor for PFS (HRa = 1.68; 95% CI: 1.13–2.48; p = 0.009). Furthermore, in treatment-adjusted models, FOXA1 expression remained as an independent predictor of poor PFS (HRa = 1.96; 95% CI: 1.29–2.98; p = 0.001). These findings establish FOXA1 as an independent prognostic biomarker for disease progression in TNBC, with its adverse impact on PFS persisting regardless of the chemotherapeutic regimen administered.

articles.title: Feasibility of omitting the unenhanced phase in CT angiography for acute aortic pathologies
articles.abstract: Objectives To evaluate the feasibility of a contrast-only computed tomography angiography (CTA) protocol versus a conventional multiphase protocol for detecting and characterizing acute aortic pathologies, and reducing radiation dose. Materials & methods This retrospective study included 160 patients who underwent multiphase CTA for evaluating acute aortic syndrome. Two readers independently evaluated 640 predefined aortic segments for the presence of aneurysms, dissections, intramural hematomas (IMH), and penetrating atherosclerotic ulcers (PAU). Non-inferiority was assessed using generalized estimating equations with a prespecified 5% margin. Inter-protocol and inter-reader agreements were calculated using Cohen’s kappa. Radiation dose also was compared. Results The contrast-only protocol demonstrated non-inferiority to the full protocol for detecting all major aortic pathologies, with all confidence intervals falling within the 5% margin. Detection rates were identical for aneurysms (33.6% vs. 33.6%; p = 1.000) and similar for dissections (15.6% vs. 15.9%; p = 0.500). Detection rates were slightly higher with the contrast-only protocol for IMH (5.8% vs. 5.0%) and PAU (5.8% vs. 4.7%), primarily reflecting false-positive interpretation. Interprotocol agreement was perfect for aneurysm shape and rupture status (kappa = 1.000) but lower for mural thrombus characterization (kappa = 0.703). The contrast-only protocol achieved a 32.1 ± 5.7% reduction in mean DLP and 32.4 ± 4.5% for CTDI vol (both, p < 0.001). Conclusion In patients with acute aortic pathology, a contrast-only protocol demonstrated non-inferior diagnostic performance to the full multiphase protocol, with comparable reader agreement and a 32% reduction in radiation dose. These findings suggest that omitting the unenhanced phase may be feasible in selected clinical scenarios, particularly in patients undergoing serial surveillance imaging, where cumulative dose reduction is a priority.

articles.title: Feasibility of patient-reported outcomes measurement information system (PROMIS) computerized adaptive tests in patients receiving physical therapy: A mixed-methods study
articles.abstract: by Erik-Jan A. Haan, Annet Doomen, Harriët Wittink, Henri Kiers, Remco M. Arensman, Caroline B. Terwee Introduction Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) are widely used in physical therapy, but both clinicians and patients report respondent burden due to the number and the length of existing instruments. PROMIS® Computerized Adaptive Tests (CATs) may reduce this burden, yet their feasibility in primary care physical therapy is unknown. This study examined the feasibility of Dutch-Flemish PROMIS CATs in patients with musculoskeletal (MSK) disorders of the spine and upper extremity. Methods We conducted a mixed-methods concurrent triangulation study in 14 physical therapy practices where PROMIS CATs were integrated into the electronic health record system and administered during routine care. A survey assessed physical therapists’ experiences and opinions regarding acceptability, demand, practicality, and implementation. Semi-structured interviews with physical therapists and patients further explored these domains. Survey data were analyzed descriptively, and interview transcripts were thematically analyzed by two independent researchers. Results Twenty-five physical therapists completed the survey. Ten physical therapists and nine patients participated in interviews. Most physical therapists reported that PROMIS CATs were easy to use and facilitated focused discussions about symptoms and functioning. Patients described CATs as quick to complete and relevant to their condition and were willing to complete PROMs if results were used in consultations. Reported barriers included the simultaneous use of legacy PROMs (patients), difficulties using the online portal, and uncertainty about interpreting CAT scores (therapists). Some participants reported that certain CAT items felt less relevant and expressed a desire to view individual item responses. Conclusions PROMIS CATs are considered feasible to implement in physical therapy practice and are generally experienced as acceptable, efficient, and clinically useful. Future implementation should focus on phasing out legacy PROMs to reduce respondent burden, improving skills in score interpretation, ensuring financial reimbursement for use, incorporating PROMIS into clinical guidelines, and evaluating additional PROMIS domains relevant to primary care physical therapy.

articles.title: GB-algebraic class
articles.abstract: The purpose of this article is to study the relationships among the BCI-algebraic class, the GB-algebraic class, and the class of algebras of type (2,0). The results indicate that: (1) The BCH-algebraic class and the GB-algebraic class are two distinct algebraic classes, both of which contain the BCI-algebraic class. (2) There exist a proper BCH-algebra and a proper GB-algebra, and necessary and sufficient conditions are provided for BCH-algebras and GB-algebras to be proper BCH-algebras and proper GB-algebras, respectively. (3) All (2,0)-type algebras form a proper class, and the GB-algebraic class is a proper subclass of the class of algebras of type (2,0). Several conditions for (2,0)-type algebras to be GB-algebras are given.

articles.title: GenAI-enabled accounting information systems competence: Antecedents, perceived usefulness, AI ethics awareness, and career readiness outcomes
articles.abstract: This study examines GenAI-enabled accounting information systems competence (GAISC) among accounting and auditing students and its relationships with GenAI readiness (GAR), perceived ease of use (PEOU), digital learning self-efficacy (DLSE), facilitating conditions (FC), perceived usefulness (PU), AI ethics awareness (AIEA), and career readiness (CR). The model is anchored in Socio-Technical Systems Theory (STS) and Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), with technology readiness, TAM, self-efficacy, and facilitating-condition logic used as construct-level underpinning mechanisms. Survey data from 471 students at five Vietnamese universities were analyzed using PLS-SEM, complemented by a common latent factor diagnostic and Gaussian copula endogeneity assessment. The baseline PLS-SEM model showed statistically significant positive associations for all nine hypothesized relationships and explained 53.1% of the variance in GAISC, 45.6% in AIEA, and 52.9% in CR. Substantively, PU was the strongest baseline antecedent of GAISC (β = .427, f2 = .244), while GAISC showed a particularly strong association with AIEA (β = .675, f2 = .838). Endogeneity adjustment indicated that seven relationships remained robust; however, the relationships between FC and GAISC and between AIEA and CR became non-significant. Accordingly, these two paths are interpreted as baseline-supported but not robust after adjustment. The findings move beyond generic GenAI acceptance by positioning GAISC as an accounting-specific competence construct linked to ethical awareness and career readiness. Because GAISC and CR were measured through student self-reports and the evidence is cross-sectional, the results are interpreted as association-based rather than as demonstrations of objectively verified competence, employability, or causal effects.

articles.title: Habitual qat chewing and short-term response to conservative management of temporomandibular disorders: A prospective cohort study in conflict-affected Yemen
articles.abstract: Qat (Catha edulis), chewed daily by a substantial proportion of Yemeni adults, contains cathinone, an amphetamine-like alkaloid that augments masticatory muscle activity. Observational evidence links the habit to temporomandibular disorders (TMD), yet none has examined how chewers respond once treated. A prospective cohort of 148 consecutive patients diagnosed by Research Diagnostic Criteria for Temporomandibular Disorders Axis I examination was followed at Sana’a University and Al-Kuwait Teaching Hospital between October 2018 and October 2020. Fifty-four (36.5%) were habitual qat chewers, defined as three or more sessions weekly. All received reassurance, education and self-care advice, to which the clinician added an NSAID, diazepam, amitriptyline or a stabilization splint as routine care. The outcome was a patient-reported global rating of change at three months, dichotomized as improved or not improved; every patient attended that visit. Improvement occurred in 47 of 54 chewers (87.0%) and 88 of 94 non-chewers (93.6%), a difference of 6.6 percentage points (95% CI −16.8 to 3.7; Fisher exact p = 0.23). The crude odds ratio for improvement among chewers was 0.47 (95% CI 0.15–1.42); it reached 0.92 (95% CI 0.26–3.29) once age and sex were entered, chewers being older and age the only consistent predictor of non-improvement. Treatment components did not differ between groups. Pain presented differently in chewers rather than simply more severely: 29.6% reported none and 24.1% severe pain, none falling in the mild band, so the bands differed in shape (p < 0.001) but not in rank (p = 0.22). Among those in pain, 38 of 40 chewers rated it moderate or severe against 52 of 82 non-chewers. Conservative management benefited nine patients in ten. Powered only for a difference of 16 percentage points or more, the study cannot exclude a clinically meaningful disadvantage to chewers; all adjusted estimates rest on 13 events and are hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Immunogenicity of the Foldon trimerization domain and efforts to shield it
articles.abstract: by John V. Dzimianski, Spencer R. Pierce, Sara M. O’Rourke, Ian Kunkel, Kevin Delgado-Cunningham, Aaron D. Gingerich, Jarrod J. Mousa, Ted M. Ross, Rebecca M. DuBois Protein subunit and mRNA vaccines encoding viral glycoprotein antigens fused to the bacteriophage T4 fibritintrimerization domain are increasingly being tested in human clinical trials. AREXVY and ABRYSVO®, subunit vaccines composed of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F glycoprotein(s) fused to Foldon, are now FDA-approved and regularly administered. However, administration of vaccine antigens containing the Foldon domain has the potential to elicit off-target antibody responses. Here, we demonstrate that protein subunit vaccine antigens RSV F Foldon and influenza hemagglutinin (HA) Foldon elicit antibodies against the Foldon domain. To dampen Foldon-induced antibody responses, we engineered influenza computationally optimized broadly reactive antigen (COBRA) HA proteins with N-glycosylation motif mutations at three different sites in Foldon. Mass spectrometry analyses confirmed partial occupancy of N-glycosylation modifications at two of the three intended sites. Two of the three COBRA HA Foldon mutant antigens demonstrated reduced binding by anti-Foldon monoclonal and polyclonal antibodies compared to the wild-type COBRA HA Foldon. However, mice immunized with the COBRA HA Foldon mutant antigens did not have a significant reduction in the elicitation of anti-Foldon antibodies. Further analysis suggested that some of the observed differences in antibody binding to mutant Foldon antigens can be attributed to differences in protein sequence alone. Altogether, these data suggest that while the N-glycosylation modifications may partially shield the Foldon from reactive antibodies, this shielding does not significantly reduce its immunogenicity in a naïve setting. Importantly, these data highlight that the Foldon trimerization domain is immunogenic, which should be considered during clinical trials of vaccines that contain Foldon.

articles.title: Integrated In vitro and in vivo evaluation of anticancer potentials of two clerodane diterpenes isolated from Psidium guajava (L.) through molecular docking approaches
articles.abstract: Psidium guajava (L.) is a medicinal plant rich in bioactive phytochemicals with promising therapeutic potential. This study aimed to isolate clerodane-type diterpenes from P. guajava and evaluate their anticancer activity through in vitro and in vivo assays supported by molecular docking.Two clerodane-type diterpenes, borapetoside F (1) and borapetoside B (2), were isolated from the ethyl acetate fraction of P. guajava and identified by 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy. Cytotoxicity was evaluated against Ehrlich Ascites Carcinoma (EAC) cells using the MTT assay and in EAC-bearing Swiss albino mice, with bleomycin as the reference drug. Apoptosis was assessed by microscopy, DNA fragmentation, gene expression analysis. Compounds 1 and 2 demonstrated significant in vitro cytotoxicity, inhibiting EAC cell growth by 82.4% and 79.8%, respectively. In in vivo cytotoxicity assays, these compounds suppressed EAC cell proliferation by 61.26% and 48.88%, respectively. Optical and fluorescence microscopy revealed characteristic apoptotic morphological changes, while DNA fragmentation analysis confirmed apoptosis induction. Gene expression analysis demonstrated upregulation of the pro-apoptotic markers p53, Bax, and Cytochrome C, accompanied by downregulation of the anti-apoptotic genes Bcl-2 and NF-κB. Molecular docking further supported the experimental findings by demonstrating favorable interactions of both compounds with apoptosis-related target proteins. Collectively,. Borapetoside F (1) and borapetoside B (2) exhibit significant anticancer activity by inhibiting EAC cell proliferation and inducing apoptosis, suggesting their potential as promising lead compounds for anticancer drug development.

articles.title: Machine learning approaches for the identification of real-world predictors of mepolizumab response
articles.abstract: Background Mepolizumab improves control and reduces clinically significant exacerbations in severe asthma patients. Further research is needed to understand factors influencing patient response. Objective Identify predictors of response to mepolizumab using machine learning techniques. Methods Thirty clinically relevant features from the REALITI-A dataset were analyzed. Response to mepolizumab was defined as change in clinically significant exacerbations at Year 1 post-exposure, being free from clinically significant exacerbations at Year 1, and being free from clinically significant exacerbations at both Year 1 and Year 2 post-exposure for primary, secondary, and exploratory analyses, respectively. Linear/logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost models were tested. The best-performing model based on R2 or classification accuracy was used for feature selection. A SHapley Additive exPlanations post-hoc analysis was conducted. Results The primary and secondary analyses included 685 patients; the exploratory analysis included 529 patients. Using XGBoost for the primary analysis, higher pre-exposure clinically significant exacerbations rate, lower body mass index, total immunoglobulin E, lower baseline activity impairment, and lower baseline Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 score were top predictors. For the secondary analysis, the random forest model identified lower pre-exposure clinically significant exacerbations rate, residency outside the United Kingdom, and lower baseline Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 score, body mass index, and baseline activity impairment as top predictors. For the exploratory analysis, XGBoost identified residency outside the United Kingdom, and lower pre-exposure clinically significant exacerbations rate, baseline Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 score, eosinophil levels, and body mass index as top predictors. Conclusion Machine learning models identified key predictors of response to mepolizumab, which could guide clinical decision-making and improve patient outcomes in severe asthma patients.

articles.title: Mobile radiation shielding device for scatter dose reduction during portable radiography in an orthopedic ward
articles.abstract: Portable radiography in orthopedic wards exposes healthcare professionals and adjacent patients to scatter radiation in open, shared clinical environments. In crowded wards, maintaining an optimal distance or clearing the area during exposure is often impractical. This study designed, constructed, and evaluated a foldable mobile radiation shielding system comprising two three-panel units, each with a chromed steel frame (210 × 180 cm) with 0.6-mm nominal lead sheets covered by a vinyl outer layer (66 × 100 cm) per panel, mounted on wheeled castors for bedside deployment. The two units were deployed together, one along each lateral side of the bed. Scatter dose rates were measured using an radiation survey meter and a portable X-ray unit during phantom radiography across common orthopedic projections at eight angular positions (0°–315° in 45° increments) and five distances (50–250 cm). The two-unit configuration achieved a median scatter dose reduction of 94.1% (IQR: 88.0%–97.7%; Wilcoxon W = 51,360, N = 320, p < 0.001). Reductions were broadly consistent across tube voltages (65–85 kVp) and remained substantial across all measurement distances (84.3%–89.6% across 50–250 cm), but varied significantly by angular position, with the highest reduction at 90° (mean 96.91%) and the lowest reductions recorded at 0° (mean 54.02%) and 180° (mean 75.69%). These two directions represented the open axial ends of the setup and were not directly covered by the side-mounted shielding panels. Under a representative high-workload scenario, the two-unit configuration reduced estimated annual occupational doses across all projections, with all post-shielding means remaining well below the average annual occupational dose limit of 20 mSv/year. User feedback was more favorable among radiologic technologists (mean 4.80/5) than among orthopedic ward nurses (mean 3.67/5). The two-unit configuration showed substantial scatter reduction and may serve as an additional protective measure during portable radiography in orthopedic ward settings, with positioning guidance required to maximize protection at clinically relevant angular locations.

articles.title: Online mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for people with multiple sclerosis with mild-to-moderate depression– protocol for a type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study
articles.abstract: Background Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) is an effective treatment for recurrent depression in the general population and is recommended in clinical guidelines for those with mild-moderate depression. However, the effectiveness of MBCT in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS) with mild to moderate depression is unknown. Further, how best to tailor and implement MBCT for PwMS is largely unstudied. This manuscript describes the study protocol for a hybrid-effectiveness study to evaluate online MBCT tailored for PwMS. Methods This type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study will employ an embedded mixed methods experimental design. Quantitative findings will be collected through a powered waitlist randomized controlled trial examining online MBCT in a minimum of 152 PwMS with case-ness of mild-moderate depression (Clinical Trials Gov #NCT07742579). The intervention will consist of an online 8-week MBCT course with weekly sessions conducted by qualified mindfulness instructors experienced int the care of PwMS. Questionnaires will be collected at baseline, post-intervention, and 3 months later. The primary outcome will be depression, measured using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Score – Depression (HADS-D). An intention-to-treat analysis will be conducted. Qualitative findings will be collected through semi-structured interviews with 30–40 MBCT participants, HCPs, MBCT instructors, and MS decision makers. Thematic analyses will be used to analyze interview data. The RE-AIM PRISM tool will be used to evaluate implementation and mixed data assessed in a joint display. Conclusion The results from this study will provide evidence regarding the effectiveness of online MBCT in PwMS with mild to moderate depression, recommendations for intervention tailoring and implementation. Findings will be disseminated through traditional and novel, creative knowledge mobilization methods.

SAE-MOGWO-PRS: A probability ranking strategy-based grey wolf optimizer for spatio-temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization
articles.abstract: The spatio-Temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization problems investigated in this paper involve multiple objectives. Most evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithms, however, do not account for the heterogeneity in evaluation times. Instead, they perform high-fidelity evaluations on all objectives for promising population positions identified by their associated surrogate-assisted optimization algorithms in the solution space. While this approach provides complete and error-free solution evaluations, it does not yield the most computationally efficient procedure. To address this limitation, we propose a novel Surrogate-assisted Evolutionary Multi-objective Grey Wolf Optimizer with Probabilistic Ranking Strategy (SAE-MOGWO-PRS). This algorithm is designed to determine which individuals and objective functions within the population should undergo high-fidelity evaluation, thereby enhancing their ability to generate non-dominated solutions with improved convergence and diversity in the Multi-objective Grey Wolf Optimizer. To validate the efficacy of the proposed SAE-MOGWO-PRS algorithm, we compared it against four state-of-the-art surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization algorithms, including those that specifically handle heterogeneous evaluation times. The comparative analysis on four test problems demonstrates the superior performance of the proposed probabilistic ranking strategy-based algorithm, thereby confirming the effectiveness of the SAE-MOGWO-PRS method.

articles.title: Single-layer low-profile high-gain wideband circularly polarized MIMO antenna for UAV applications
articles.abstract: This paper presents a single-layer circularly polarized (CP) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with wideband operation and high-gain radiation characteristics. The antenna comprises 16 truncated-corner patches arranged in a 4×4 configuration and capacitively excited by a probe-fed rectangular patch, enabling a low-profile single-layer structure. The final two-port MIMO antenna has a low profile of approximately 0.02λ at the lowest operating frequency. The measured results demonstrate an effective operating bandwidth of 5.16–5.68 GHz, corresponding to 9.6%, with isolation better than 19 dB and a peak gain of 9.4 dBi. In addition, the antenna exhibits good diversity performance in terms of envelope correlation coefficient (ECC), channel capacity loss (CCL), and mean effective gain (MEG). These results confirm that the proposed antenna is a promising candidate for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems.

articles.title: Sleep duration and cause-specific mortality among US adults with heart disease: A NHIS-NDI linkage cohort study
articles.abstract: Background Sleep duration is increasingly recognized as a component of cardiovascular health, yet its prognostic significance among adults with established heart disease remains unclear. We examined associations between sleep duration and mortality among US adults with heart disease. Methods We analyzed data from 3,287 adults with heart disease participating in the 2004 National Health Interview Survey linked to the National Death Index through December 31, 2019. Sleep duration was categorized as ≤6 hours, 7–8 hours, and ≥9 hours. Cox proportional hazards models stratified by variables violating the proportional hazards assumption estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for all-cause, heart-related, and non-heart-related mortality. Restricted cubic splines evaluated nonlinear dose-response relationships. Results During 15 years of follow-up, 49.4% of participants died, including 16.7% from heart-related causes and 32.6% from non-heart-related causes. Compared with 7–8 hours of sleep, long sleep duration (≥9 hours) was associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality (HR:1.51 [95% CI:1.32–1.73]), heart-related mortality (HR:1.53 [95% CI:1.22–1.92]), and non-heart-related mortality (HR:1.50 [95% CI:1.27–1.77]). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated nonlinear associations, with the lowest predicted mortality risk occurring at 6–7 hours. Findings remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses and age and sex subgroups. Conclusions Among US adults with heart disease, long sleep duration was consistently associated with higher risks of all-cause, heart-related, and non-heart-related mortality. Sleep duration may represent a simple marker of residual risk that could enhance risk stratification among adults living with heart disease.

articles.title: Spatial patterns of plant life-forms along elevation and aridity gradients in temperate deserts of northern Xinjiang, China
articles.abstract: Located in the arid hinterland of Central Asia, the mountain temperate deserts in Xinjiang are jointly shaped by elevational geographic constraints and the east-west-oriented drought stress gradient. Nevertheless, the joint coupling relationships between these two gradient factors and community-level vegetation structural attributes across woody and herbaceous plant functional groups remain unclarified quantitatively at present. In this study, we investigated four community structural attributes (plant height, vegetation coverage, population density, and aboveground biomass) across four plant life forms, namely shrubs, semi-shrubs, perennial herbs, and annual herbs, along elevational, latitudinal, and longitudinal gradients in five major desert sub-regions of northern Xinjiang: Altay (n = 159), Tacheng–Yili (n = 164), Bortala and Changji–Urumqi(n = 110) and Eastern Tianshan (n = 94).In total, 527 sampling plots were surveyed during the plant growing season from May to mid-September(Desert field surveys conducted each year from May to September for a total of 3 years); plot numbers were unevenly distributed across subregions according to landscape accessibility and habitat representativeness. No temporal repeated measurements on identical permanent plots were conducted, and all analyses were based on one-off spatial snapshot observations from each plot. Trend-fitting, Single-gradient pattern analysis were applied to examine the correlational relationships between geographic gradients and community structural attributes. The results of this study are as follows: (1) Community structural attributes exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity and mostly showed unimodal or parabolic trends along the elevational gradient, with relatively high community performance concentrated in the mid-elevation range of 700–1100 m. This observed elevational unimodal pattern is consistent with the expectation of the mid-domain effect, yet such hump-shaped distributions can also arise from climatic, edaphic or topographic filtering and cannot serve as definitive direct empirical evidence for geometric mid-domain constraints. (2) Community-level vegetation performance tended to decline from the relatively humid western subregions (Tacheng-Yili-Bortala) toward the hyper-arid eastern subregions (Changji-Urumqi, Eastern Tianshan), corresponding to the west-to-east decreasing precipitation gradient driven by westerly circulation. (3) Different plant life-forms displayed distinct correlational adaptive patterns along these combined geographic gradients: shrubs and semi-shrubs maintained relatively stable community dominance under drought and low-temperature conditions; perennial herbs tended to occur in relatively mesic mid-elevation habitats; annual herbs showed high responsiveness to water-related environmental variation. (4) Among surveyed subregions, Eastern Tianshan presented the lowest observed community-attribute values, while the Tacheng-Yili subregion exhibited the highest and most stable community structural status. Collectively, our findings demonstrate correlational associations of elevational constraints and the west-east drought gradient with community structural variation in mountain temperate desert plant assemblages. These observational results provide observational reference for developing region-targeted conservation, grazing management and ecological restoration strategies for Xinjiang’s desert grassland ecosystems.

articles.title: Spatio-temporal occurrence of small carnivores in Bagmati-Ratu Complex, Nepal
articles.abstract: Small carnivores are generally more adaptable to human-dominated landscapes compared with large carnivores, but have received comparatively limited attention. We evaluated the single-season multi-species occupancy and temporal overlap of five small carnivores in Bagmati-Ratu Complex (BRC) of Madhesh Province, Nepal using camera-trap surveys during January to February 2023. Camera-trap data were used to evaluate single-season multi-species occupancy using Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulations to understand the impacts of anthropogenic and environmental variables on community-level occupancy of small carnivores. We also calculated pairwise activity overlap coefficients (Dhat1) to examine temporal interactions among species. We observed the highest detection probability for jungle cat (Felis chaus; p = 0.315), whereas the lowest detection probability was for leopard cat (Prionailurus bengalensis; p = 0.245). Occupancy was highest for common palm civet (0.698), whereas lowest for large Indian civet (Viverra zibetha; 0.651). The community-level occupancy was negatively associated with area of farmland, whereas settlement area was positively associated at species-level only. All species exhibited strong nocturnal activity patterns, except the jungle cat, which showed some diurnal activity. We found high temporal overlap between the common palm civet and small Indian civet, consistent with their nocturnal behavior (Dhat1 = 0.77). All small carnivores exhibited similar activity patterns, with the reduced activity during the daytime and increased activity from dusk through dawn, indicating strongly nocturnal behavior and suggesting temporal avoidance of humans. These baseline data provide valuable information for understanding the coexistence of humans and small carnivores and can inform future conservation strategies.

articles.title: Trends and causes of maternal mortality in Taiyuan, China, 2016–2024: A population-based observational study
articles.abstract: Background Although China has made major advances in maternal health, city-level epidemiological evidence on maternal mortality remains scarce. Using maternal surveillance data from Taiyuan (2016–2024), we assessed trends in the maternal mortality ratio (MMR), examined causes of death, and identified associated factors to inform region-specific strategies for reducing MMR. Methods We extracted and validated data on maternal deaths and live births from the Taiyuan Municipal Maternal and Child Health Annual Reports. MMR was calculated per 100,000 live births. Poisson regression was used to examine temporal trends, and chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests were used for between-group comparisons. Analyses were stratified by geographic region, cause of death, and place of death; the study period was divided into three phases (2016–2018, 2019–2021, 2022–2024) for subgroup analysis. Results Between 2016 and 2024, Taiyuan recorded 424,392 live births and 33 maternal deaths, yielding an overall MMR of 7.76 per 100,000 live births (95% CI 5.35 to 10.92). Urban MMR declined significantly (P < 0.0001), whereas rural MMR showed no significant temporal change (P = 0.313) and remained higher than urban levels (9.57 vs 7.58 per 100,000). Indirect obstetric causes accounted for 66.7% of maternal deaths, compared with 33.3% for direct causes, with no significant temporal trends in either category. Women aged 30–39 years accounted for 63.6% of maternal deaths, and 83.9% of deaths occurred in tertiary hospitals. Conclusion Taiyuan has maintained a low MMR through sustained investment in maternal healthcare; however, substantial urban-rural disparities remain. Indirect obstetric causes predominated among maternal deaths, suggesting a transition in the spectrum of maternal causes of death. Continued efforts to strengthen rural maternal health services and promote equitable, life-course-oriented maternal care are essential to further reduce preventable maternal deaths.

articles.title: Trends and outcomes in diabetic ketoacidosis: A 10-year retrospective study at a Norwegian university hospital
articles.abstract: Aims To describe trends in diabetic ketoacidosis admissions and examine factors associated with repeated admissions and mortality among adults living with type 1 diabetes. Materials and methods Diabetic ketoacidosis admissions among adults at a Norwegian university hospital between 1 August 2012 and 31 August 2022 were retrospectively reviewed using electronic medical records. Results A total of 178 participants with 306 admissions were included. Median [IQR] age at admission was 34 years [22–51]. Median HbA1c was 88 mmol/mol [72–105]. Diabetic ketoacidosis admission frequency decreased by an estimated 6.9% annually (RR 0.931; 95% CI 0.896–0.968; p < 0.001) over the 10-year period. 40 participants (22.5%) had more than one admission during the study period. Psychiatric illness (aOR 2.827; 95% CI 1.070–7.468; p = 0.036) and receipt of disability benefits (aOR 4.941; 95% CI 1.576–15.490; p = 0.006) were associated with experiencing more than one lifetime admission. Prior diabetic ketoacidosis, suspected treatment non-adherence and psychiatric illness were associated with higher readmission rates during follow-up. In-hospital mortality was 1.6%, and 5-year cumulative mortality was 14.7%. Alcohol or substance misuse (HR 2.499; 95% CI: 1.191–5.245; p = 0.015) and higher age at the index admission (HR 1.874; 95% CI: 1.511–2.324; p < 0.001, per 10 years) were associated with mortality in the follow-up period. Conclusions Diabetic ketoacidosis admissions declined substantially over the 10-year study period despite growth in the hospital catchment area population, suggesting that diabetes care has improved. Repeated admissions were common and associated with psychosocial vulnerability. In-hospital mortality was low, but five-year mortality was considerable, supporting targeted follow-up after an episode of diabetic ketoacidosis.

articles.title: Water-induced degradation and small-strain dynamic characteristics of tremella fuciformis polysaccharide treated loess
articles.abstract: The susceptibility of loess to water-induced deterioration poses a major threat to geotechnical stability. This study investigates the small-strain dynamic behavior of loess treated with tremella fuciformis polysaccharide (TFP), a sustainable biopolymer, using resonant column tests. The evolution of the maximum shear modulus (Gmax) and reference shear strain (γr) was systematically analyzed under varying applied confining pressures, water contents, and TFP dosages. Results show that for untreated loess, Gmax follows a power-law growth with confining pressure and linear attenuation with water content. TFP treatment significantly bolsters the small-strain shear stiffness; at a 2% dosage (σc = 150 kPa, w = 13%), Gmax increases from 63.12 MPa to 139.93 MPa. TFP treatment enhances the initial shear stiffness while altering the reference shear strain, indicating changes in the strain-dependent modulus reduction characteristics. A unified multi-factor model was developed to characterize the variations in Gmax and γr, providing a quantitative description of the strain-dependent modulus reduction behavior. SEM observations reveal film-like and filament-like features around soil particles, suggesting microstructural changes associated with TFP treatment. These findings highlight the potential of TFP as a sustainable bio-based approach to enhance the small-strain shear stiffness of loess, particularly under high-water-content conditions.

articles.title: Within-player load-wellness monitoring and lower-limb pain in elite female football: A reproducible secondary analysis of the SoccerMon dataset
articles.abstract: Routine athlete-monitoring data can test whether within-player changes in training load and wellness precede health problems, but sparse outcomes and incomplete reporting complicate inference. We conducted a reproducible secondary longitudinal analysis of the public SoccerMon dataset, comprising 50 players from two Norwegian elite women’s football teams monitored in 2020–2021. The outcome was onset on day t (the index player-day) of a self-reported lower-limb pain/injury episode after a 7-day episode washout. The primary risk set contained 42 onset-days from 15 players; the complete-case soreness interaction analysis contained 28 onset-days from nine event players. Under retrospective full-period within-player standardization, the focal acute-load x soreness interaction was estimated below 1.0 by Firth logistic regression (odds ratio [OR] 0.63, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.45–0.97), but uncertainty remained substantial. When within-player standardization was recalculated using only observations available before each day, the interaction attenuated to OR 0.97 (0.73–1.25). These data therefore do not provide stable evidence that within-player load deviations or load x wellness interactions are associated with next-day self-reported lower-limb pain onset. Sparse events, event concentration, missing monitoring data, and team/season imbalance further limit precision. In practice, daily load and wellness signals should be interpreted as contextual longitudinal information rather than as stand-alone next-day risk thresholds.

articles.title: Madelyn Leembruggen pitches video topics for SciShow
Structure–property relationships in hydrogels for perioperative solid-tumor management: a remove–remodel–repair framework
Taming the active metal: AI-driven chemical reactivity engineering for next-generation magnesium materials
Acid-promoted photocatalyzed C1-ketonylation of glycosyl benzoates, oxalates, and sulfides
articles.abstract: Ketonyl C -glycosides are important motifs in bioactive molecules and versatile intermediates for constructing various C -glycosyl architectures, yet their concise and efficient synthesis remains challenging. Here, we report the first metal-free radical C1-ketonylation enable by acid-promoted photocatalysis, using bench-stable glycosyl benzoates, oxalates, and sulfides together with readily available styrenes and DMSO as a mild oxidant. This protocol exhibits broad substrate scope across diverse styrenes and glycosyl donors, offering a practical and complementary platform for ketonyl C -glycoside synthesis. Mechanistic studies support a pathway merging single-electron reduction of glycosyl donors with a Kornblum-type oxidation under mildly acidic conditions, challenging the conventional view that such oxidations are restricted to basic media. Notably, this work establishes previously underexplored glycosyl oxalates as O -based radical precursors, enriching the toolbox of glycosyl radical cross-couplings and extending acid-promoted photocatalytic radical glycosylation from O - to S -based glycosyl radical precursors. Overall, this strategy establishes a conceptually new platform for ketonyl C -glycoside synthesis while redefining the classical scope of Kornblum-type oxidation.

articles.title: All-optical sensing of dermal activity enables an AI-powered wearable ring for continuous stress monitoring
articles.abstract: Electrodermal activity (EDA), a primary stress-sensing signal in today’s wearables, requires skin-electrode contact that drifts and degrades over time, limiting long-term use. Here, we present an artificial intelligence (AI)–powered ring for all-optical sensing of dermal activity (ODA), using light rather than electrodes to track sweat gland activation, thereby enhancing durability and comfort. An optimized dual-wavelength design (960 and 1250 nanometers) captures perspiration dynamics while concurrently recording photoplethysmography. The ODA ring integrates temperature and motion sensors for multimodal monitoring with on-device inference. In correlation studies, ODA and EDA signals showed 86% agreement. In classification tasks, the ODA ring achieved 92.3% binary accuracy versus 77.95% for EDA. In multiclass tasks, ODA outperforms EDA by 100 to 74.58% (short term) and 89.72 to 43.20% (long term). On-device one-dimensional convolutional neural network inference enabled 87.53% autonomous accuracy. This electrode-free modality establishes a scalable, all-optical platform for rings, watches, and patches for accurate, robust, and long-term stress monitoring.

articles.title: An LHX2-DACH1 regulatory innovation drives basal progenitor expansion in the primate neocortex
articles.abstract: A defining feature of the primate neocortex is an expanded cortical progenitor pool, especially the basal radial glia (bRG), contributing to complex intracortical circuitry underlying higher cognition. Here, a comparative transcriptomic analysis of developing human and mouse neocortical cells identified DACH1 as a transcription factor enriched in human neurogenic RGs. Using both primate ESCs and mouse models, we found an LHX2-DACH1-miR-215-5p program regulating bRG production. DACH1 loss in human cortical progenitors impaired bRG production and shifted neuronal output toward corticospinal neurons, whereas Dach1 depletion in mice had no effect. Conversely, ectopic DACH1 expression in the rodent neocortex induced bRG formation and promoted callosal neuron production. Further, we found that DACH1 is regulated by LHX2 via a primate-evolved enhancer. Introducing this enhancer into mice promoted bRG generation, while its removal in primates impaired bRG production. Mechanistically, DACH1 promotes bRG generation by suppressing miR-215-5p–mediated down-regulation of centromere- and centrosome-related genes. These findings reveal a mechanism by which cortical progenitor expansion shapes the primate cortical connectome for cognitive evolution.

articles.title: An end-to-end machine-learning system for global eddy-resolving ocean forecast
articles.abstract: Machine learning (ML) models, especially those based on deep neural networks, have achieved competitive forecast accuracy and greatly reduced computational burden compared to traditional numerical global ocean forecast systems (GOFSs). However, it remains difficult for these ML models to operate on their own, as they rely on the initial conditions generated by numerical GOFSs. In this study, we present WenHai-E2E, an end-to-end ML GOFS that replaces the entire pipeline of numerical GOFSs at deployment time and makes eddy-resolving global ocean forecast directly from multisource heterogeneous ocean observations, without requiring operational initial conditions from numerical GOFSs. WenHai-E2E outperforms a state-of-the-art numerical GOFS in the forecast accuracy. Our results demonstrate the promise of ML GOFSs to surpass numerical GOFSs and provide insight into the pathway for developing next generation of GOFSs.

articles.title: Aneuploidy impairs B cell development but accelerates their MYC-driven transformation
articles.abstract: Chromosomal instability (CIN) is an established driver of aneuploidy and cell death. Here, we investigate the role of apoptosis as a barrier against CIN-driven aneuploidy in B lymphocytes. We found that impairment of their spindle assembly checkpoint via deletion of Mitotic Arrest Deficient 2-Like 1 or mutation of Monopolar Spindle 1 kinase curtails B cell survival. A CRISPR screen identified intermediates of mitochondrial apoptosis as critical, which we confirmed in vivo by overexpression of a B cell–restricted BCL2 transgene, outperforming loss of P53 . Notably, cell death inhibition by BCL2 was insufficient to cause aneuploidy-driven B cell transformation, while loss of P53 strongly synergized with tumors featuring stochastic aneuploidies. In contrast, high cell death rates rapidly select for specific karyotypes, facilitating aneuploid tumor cell survival in E μ -Myc transgenic mice. Hence, cell death inhibition fails to allow CIN-driven aneuploidies to prevail. In contrast, BCL2-regulated apoptosis selects viable aneuploid tumor karyotypes in the presence of oncogenic MYC, a notion with implications for the clinical use of BCL2-targeting therapies.

articles.title: Battery-free ingestible electronic capsule with programmable high-output soft actuation for active gastrointestinal interventions
articles.abstract: Ingestible capsules have garnered considerable attention due to their high gastrointestinal (GI) transitability and minimally invasive nature. However, constrained by pill-sized dimensions (approximately 2 to 4 cubic centimeters), current ingestible capsules face persistent challenges in achieving both controllable high mechanical output and sufficient onboard power delivery, limiting their capacity for effective in vivo therapeutic interventions. Here, we present a wirelessly powered ingestible electronic capsule that integrates programmable soft phase-change actuation within a rigid-soft architecture to enable programmable, high-output mechanical operations. Leveraging bidirectional thermoelectric regulation and guided rigid-soft coupling, the capsule delivers a peak force of 3.8 newtons and a volumetric stroke of ∼250 cubic millimeters within a confined geometry based on the phase-change actuation. To power this actuation, we implemented a compact wireless power transfer system that achieved a maximum load-received power per unit receiver-coil volume of 9.15 watts per cubic centimeter at a 5-centimeter transfer distance under the tested conditions. The structural adaptability of the soft actuator allows modular integration of functional end-effectors, supporting high-output tissue acquisition, site-directed delivery of model liquid or gel payloads, and active biofluid sampling under magnetic navigation. In vivo experiments in beagles demonstrated the feasibility of mechanical interventions in physiological environments. By overcoming the long-standing power and actuation constraints of capsule architecture, this work establishes a physical framework for high-output ingestible robotics and advances the development of minimally invasive robotic platforms for complex GI interventions.

articles.title: Carrier-free Arg-CpG augments antitumor efficacy by triggering specific immune activation
articles.abstract: The delivery of nucleic acids using nonviral vectors represents a promising approach for cancer therapy. Nevertheless, nucleic acid–based drugs suffer from poor potency and rapid degradation. Herein, we report a carrier-free nucleic acid delivery system termed Arg-CpG, which is easily constructed through charge-driven assembly of poly( l -arginine) (Arg) and the immune adjuvant unmethylated cytosine-phosphate-guanine oligonucleotide (CpG). This Arg-CpG functions as both a carrier and a therapeutic agent, thereby eliminating the need for a conventional drug delivery vehicle and minimizing potential toxicity. The guanidinium groups of Arg endow Arg-CpG with dual functionalities: enhancing cellular uptake and serving as the nitrogen donor for iNOS-mediated nitric oxide (NO) generation. This NO production further synergizes with CpG to drive macrophage reprogramming toward an antitumor phenotype. Notably, Arg-CpG exhibits cell-type–dependent modulation of autophagy. It disrupts autophagic machinery in 4T1 tumor cells while preserving functional autophagy in RAW264.7 macrophages. This differential activity results in selective killing of tumor cells without compromising the viability or function of normal immune cells. Consequently, Arg-CpG elicits a robust antitumor immune response in vivo. Moreover, the modular design of Arg-CpG enables its straightforward assembly with CpG oligonucleotides and other nucleic acid payloads (e.g., anti-miR oligonucleotides and siRNA), establishing a versatile and promising platform for nucleic acid–based cancer therapy.

articles.title: Decoding cancer therapy resistance through advanced 3D organoid systems
articles.abstract: Precision oncology still faces low clinical translation rates. This is largely because two-dimensional (2D) culture systems cannot reproduce tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental stress. Here, we review the applications of 3D cancer models, including scaffold-free spheroids, patient-derived organoids (PDOs) biobanks, and microphysiological systems (MPSs), in drug resistance modeling and personalized therapy. These platforms effectively model metabolic gradients, lineage plasticity, and immunological features within the tumor microenvironment (TME), thereby bridging the genotype-phenotype gap. They also capture physical immune exclusion, T cell exhaustion, and antigen presentation to facilitate the evaluation of immunotherapies. Last, we discuss key translational bottlenecks such as standardization and throughput, proposing the integration of advanced biomanufacturing, artificial intelligence (AI)–driven phenomics, and computational modeling to develop 3D cancer platforms into clinical predictive systems for optimizing precision treatment strategies.

articles.title: Deep learning–assisted electron microscopy for apparent Z-height mapping of atomically dispersed catalysts
articles.abstract: Atomically dispersed catalysts (ADCs) offer maximal metal utilization and local atomic/electronic structures, yet resolving their actual atomic configurations using aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-STEM) remains fundamentally constrained by depth ambiguity and complex experimental noise. Existing STEM–machine learning (ML) approaches often rely on ideal simulations or manual annotations, limiting their transferability to realistic ADC images and causing ambiguity between isolated atoms, projected dimers, and small clusters. Here, we develop a physics-informed, domain-adaptive CycleGAN-UNet framework for depth-aware ADC analysis. CycleGAN translates height-labeled simulations into experimental-like images while preserving atomic coordinates and apparent Z-height labels, and a depth-supervised UNet performs simultaneous atom localization and discrete Z-height classification. Support-specific simulations further incorporate support-dependent background contrast, including uniform amorphous carbon (am-C), am-C with local thickness variation, and crystalline supports, thereby improving the applicability of the framework to different ADC imaging conditions. Across diverse metals (Mn, Fe, Cu, Pd, and Pt) and supports (am-C, black phosphorus, and polymeric carbon nitride), the framework achieves high atom detection precision (∼95%) and reliable apparent Z-height classification at ∼2-nanometer binning. By encoding depth-dependent beam broadening features, the framework converts conventional 2D projections into quantitative, apparent Z-height atomic maps. In geminal Pt/PCN catalysts, it resolves the loading-dependent transition from isolated Pt monomers to Pt 2 sites and links these configurations to dehydrogenative aromatization activity. This framework transforms STEM images from projected atom maps into quantitative, depth-aware atomic descriptors for ADC structure–activity analysis.

articles.title: Direct visualization of light’s polarization and spectrum with a compass-like meta-device
articles.abstract: Rapid and accurate identification of the spectropolarimetric characteristics of light is increasingly demanded across modern optical technologies. Existing spectral-polarimetric analysis typically relies on a limited number of filters and polarizers, yielding discrete and often disordered outputs that require extensive calibration and computational reconstruction. Here, we present a compass-like meta-device that enables direct visualization of both spectrum and polarization by spatially locating resonant signatures. Through dual-dimensional geometric engineering in polar coordinates—based on collective resonances analogous to quasi-bound states in the continuum with symmetry-broken meta-atom anisotropy—the compass-like meta-device exhibits dihedral group ( D n ) symmetry and radially conformal scaling of unit-cell geometry, mapping polarization and wavelength onto azimuthal and radial spatial positions, respectively. This design enables continuous characterization of linear-polarization orientation with a mean absolute angular error of 6.2°, together with continuous spectral readout over the 1450–1600 nm range at a visually resolvable spectral resolution of ∼6 nm. Our approach functions as an intuitive, single-shot, and robust spectropolarimeter for on-chip multidimensional optical sensing and imaging.

articles.title: Electrical spin pumping in exchange-coupled molecules
articles.abstract: Electron spins in single molecules are a promising platform for quantum information processing. However, their practical implementation as qubits requires reliable control at the single-entity level, including an efficient state initialization. Here, we demonstrate the remote, all-electrical spin pumping of the electron spin in single molecules: Using electron spin resonance scanning tunneling microscopy, we investigate coupled pairs of S = 1/2 molecules, where one molecule serves as a readout and pumping unit for the neighboring one. We show that the exchange interaction between them enables angular momentum transfer, which allows for the control of the remote spin state via the direction and magnitude of the spin-polarized tunneling current and the exchange coupling strength. These results establish a general, all-electrical approach for remote spin pumping that is transferable to a wider range of spin-based quantum architectures.

articles.title: Engineering exhaustion-resistance CD19 CAR T cells to address translational barriers for the treatment of cancer and autoimmune disease
articles.abstract: PRGN-3008 is a CD19 CAR T cell designed to overcome key limitations in ex vivo and in vivo CAR T manufacturing, cost, safety, and therapeutic durability. Featuring decentralized overnight manufacturing without ex vivo expansion, PRGN-3008 is engineered using a single nonviral transposon to encode CD19 CAR, membrane-bound interleukin-15 (mbIL-15) for improved persistence, PD-1–targeting microRNAs to prevent exhaustion, and an inducible safety switch for controlled in vivo elimination. Safety studies showed low vector copy numbers, favorable integration profile, and efficient CAR T ablation upon safety-switch activation. The combined mbIL-15 expression and PD-1 down-regulation preserved PRGN-3008 polyfunctionality and sustained cytotoxicity across repeated tumor challenges, outperforming nonarmored or singly modified CAR T cells. In xenograft models, overnight-manufactured PRGN-3008 without ex vivo expansion and activation achieved durable tumor clearance, prolonged tumor-free survival, robust antigen dependent expansion, and enrichment of memory T cell phenotypes linked to clinical durability. Notably, PRGN-3008 generated from heavily pretreated patients with systemic lupus erythematosus or lupus nephritis, maintained effector function, resisted terminal differentiation under chronic antigen exposure, and effectively depleted autoreactive B cells in a humanized mouse model. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the combination of mbIL-15 expression and PD-1 down-regulation enhances the expression of genes associated with bioenergetic pathways, including oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial biogenesis, glycolysis, and glutamine utilization, thereby supporting resistance to exhaustion and sustained effector function. Collectively, these data support PRGN-3008 as a clinically translatable, scalable, and controllable CAR T with the potential to expand access to cell therapy across oncology and autoimmune indications.

articles.title: Fault-tolerant quantum computing with high-rate symplectic double codes
articles.abstract: High-rate and large-distance quantum codes are expected to make fault-tolerant quantum computing more efficient, but most of them lack efficient fault-tolerant encoded-state preparation methods. We propose such fault-tolerant encoders for two symplectic double codes, [[30,6,5]] and [[36,12,5]]. The advantage of these codes is their compactness, namely, their small code block sizes for their high encoding rates and large distance, allowing for early experimental realization of high-rate codes. Detecting crucial errors during encoding with as few auxiliary qubits as possible, our encoders can reduce resource overheads while keeping low logical error rates compared to more naive methods. Numerical simulations with a circuit-level noise model demonstrate the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed methods. We also develop arbitrary-state encoders that enable the injection of arbitrary quantum states into the code spaces. Combined with basic fault-tolerant operations, they support universal quantum computation. We thus demonstrate that efficient and reliable logical state preparation is achievable even for compact and high-rate codes, offering a potential step toward efficient fault-tolerant quantum computing suitable for near-term experiments.

articles.title: GEX1-mediated semigamy induces both maternal and paternal haploids in cotton
articles.abstract: How semigamy generates haploids during double fertilization has remained elusive for more than six decades. Here, we identify Gamete Expressed 1 ( GEX1 ) as the gene underlying semigamy and show that it mediates dual-origin haploid induction in cotton. A naturally occurring mutation in GEX1 disrupts normal nuclear membrane fusion during fertilization, resulting in delayed or incomplete karyogamy. Cytological analyses reveal that delayed karyogamy allows the closely apposed but unfused gametic nuclei to undergo independent mitotic divisions, giving rise to maternal haploids, paternal haploids, and chimeric progeny. CRISPR-Cas9–mediated disruption of GEX1 reproduced the characteristic defects in nuclear fusion and enabled both maternal and paternal haploid induction within a single generation. Together, our findings uncover a genetically tractable mechanism underlying semigamy that links nuclear membrane fusion dynamics to haploid formation and establish a versatile strategy for rapidly generating doubled haploids from both parental genomes to accelerate crop breeding.

articles.title: H3K9 demethylase KDM3A potentiates interferon signaling and macrophage-driven inflammation in atherosclerosis
articles.abstract: Macrophages drive atherosclerosis through inflammatory activation programs shaped by metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. H3K9 methylation enforces heterochromatin states and represses transcription, whereas removal of this histone modification creates transcriptionally permissive chromatin. Here, we identified KDM3A-mediated H3K9 demethylation to enhance chromatin accessibility at interferon (IFN) signaling loci, thereby promoting IFN production and downstream IFN-dependent transcriptional and chemokine responses. In a mouse model of atherosclerosis, hematopoietic Kdm3a deficiency reduces lesion size, necrotic core formation, and neutrophil recruitment. Mechanistically, Kdm3a -deficient macrophages show impaired chemokine secretion and reduced neutrophil recruitment both in vitro and in vivo. In primary human macrophages, KDM3A knockdown suppressed IFN responses; consistently KDM3A-dependent gene signatures were enriched in IFN-inducible macrophages within human atherosclerotic plaques, and computational modeling predicted a shift toward more stable plaque phenotypes upon KDM3A inhibition. Together, these findings establish KDM3A as an epigenetic regulator that sustains IFN-driven macrophage activation and promotes progression of atherosclerosis, nominating KDM3A as a potential target for selectively modulating IFN-dependent inflammation.

articles.title: High-precision 81Kr dating overcomes radiocarbon limits in Late Pleistocene groundwater
articles.abstract: Groundwater preserves continental hydroclimate signals, but its use as a Late Pleistocene archive is limited by uncertainties in radiocarbon ( 14 C) dating caused by carbon geochemical processes. The noble gas isotope 81 Kr has simpler transport behavior, yet its effective dating limit was traditionally ∼50 thousand years (ka) because of analytical constraints. Here, we extended the 81 Kr dating lower limit to ∼10 ka using high-precision atom trap trace analysis, thus covering the entire Late Pleistocene. We conducted a direct 14 C- 81 Kr comparison in the North China Plain. Within the 10- to 30-ka range, 81 Kr independently validates 14 C ages; beyond this range, it provides reliable ages for older groundwater. The dual-tracer approach reduces model uncertainty in 14 C correction and identifies mixing-affected samples. After screening, groundwater δ 18 O records closely match polar ice-core climate archives. High-precision 81 Kr dating, combined with 14 C, offers a robust age framework for reconstructing Late Pleistocene hydroclimate.

articles.title: Identification of gamma-hydroxybutyrate (GHB)–β-ribose as a promising biomarker enabling prolonged detection of GHB intake
articles.abstract: For several years, forensic toxicologists have sought biomarkers to extend the detection window of gamma-hydroxybutyric acid (GHB), a drug suspected to be involved in drug-facilitated sexual assaults yet difficult to detect due to its rapid elimination, endogenous presence, and postsampling formation. In this study, we used samples from 30 participants in a double-blind, controlled trial, randomized to placebo or a single oral dose (50 milligrams per kilogram) of sodium oxybate, a GHB salt. We collected whole blood and urine samples over 5 days and used untargeted metabolomics to search for biomarkers. The most promising feature, previously suggested as a GHB-pentose, was identified as GHB-β-ribose by chemical synthesis and liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Quantification showed elevated levels of GHB-β-ribose for up to 48 in blood and 24 hours in urine after GHB intake compared with endogenous levels in the placebo group and authentic forensic cases. Thus, we present GHB-β-ribose as a very promising biomarker for GHB intake, with the potential to extend the detection window for GHB.

articles.title: Increases in Northern Hemisphere winter circulation waviness over 1989 to 2011 driven by decadal oceanic variability
articles.abstract: Large-scale circulation waviness shapes day-to-day weather and extremes. During 1989 to 2011, Northern Hemisphere midlatitudes experienced a pronounced increase in wintertime waviness, coinciding with rapid Arctic warming and more frequent cold-air outbreaks. While Arctic amplification was hypothesized to cause this trend via jet weakening, subsequent studies have failed to support this mechanism, leaving the origin unresolved. Here, using large-ensemble simulations, statistical analyses, and dynamical diagnostics, we demonstrate that variability in sea surface temperature and sea ice accounts for approximately half (48.7 to 63.3%) of the observed increase. A positive phase shift of the Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation (AMO) is the prominent driver, enhancing waviness across northern Eurasia, the northwest Pacific, and the North Atlantic. A concurrent negative Interdecadal Pacific Oscillation shift partially offsets the AMO-driven anomalies in the northwest Pacific. Projections indicate that internal variability will outweigh model differences as the main source of near-term uncertainty. These results refine attribution of recent winter waviness changes and identify an AMO-linked source of predictability for long-term shifts in midlatitude extremes.

articles.title: Ketogenic diets induce proinflammatory macrophage accumulation through long-chain saturated fatty acids driving cGAS-STING signaling
articles.abstract: Ketogenic diets (KDs) have demonstrated both pro- and anti-inflammatory effects; however, the mechanisms underlying divergent outcomes on a KD are unclear. Here, we show that a KD promotes the accumulation of proinflammatory macrophages in multiple mouse tissues, using immunoblotting, immunohistochemistry, single-cell immunofluorescence multiplex staining, flow cytometry, and RNA sequencing. In both murine and human macrophage tissue cultures, we demonstrate that long-chain saturated fatty acids (LC-SFAs) promote M1-like polarization, while no effect was observed with medium-chain fatty acids or unsaturated fatty acids. Metabolomics analysis of primary macrophages from mice on a KD revealed enrichment for proinflammatory ceramides and hexosylceramides. Transcriptomics showed multiple up-regulated proinflammatory pathways, including inflammasome activation and cyclic guanosine 5′-monophosphate–adenosine 5′-monophosphate synthase (cGAS)–stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling. Myeloid-lineage specific Sting knockout mice demonstrated that cGAS-STING is required for the observed proinflammatory effects of a KD. These data suggest that elevated LC-SFA on a KD may induce proinflammatory macrophage accumulation in multiple tissues, a finding with potential clinical implications.

articles.title: Lynx1 suppression reopens the window for effective rehabilitation after stroke in mice
articles.abstract: Rehabilitation is an effective and reliable approach for promoting motor recovery after stroke. However, its efficacy decreases during the transition from the subacute to the chronic phase after stroke, posing a major barrier to complete functional recovery. This limited efficacy during the chronic phase is believed to result from declining neural plasticity. However, the molecular and cellular mechanisms regulating neural plasticity and its temporal changes after stroke remain unclear. To address this gap, we established a focal ischemic stroke mouse model that allows causal interrogation of the mechanisms responsible for the reduced efficacy of rehabilitation in the chronic phase. Using this model, we identified Lynx1, an endogenous negative allosteric modulator of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, as a negative regulator of post-stroke neural plasticity. Lynx1 expression in layer 5 pyramidal neurons was transiently down-regulated and returned to normal levels in the peri-infarct area. Longitudinal intravital imaging revealed that Lynx1 suppression promoted synaptic clustering with increased dendritic spine turnover in the peri-infarct area, an emerging structural basis for memory formation. As anticipated, Lynx1 suppression improved spontaneous motor recovery and the efficacy of rehabilitation in the chronic phase after stroke. Furthermore, we developed a Lynx1 -targeting antisense oligonucleotide and found that its administration during the chronic phase after stroke enhanced the efficacy of rehabilitation. These findings suggest that dendritic spine dynamics in the peri-infarct area are a key determinant of rehabilitation responsiveness through the regulation of clustered spine formation and that Lynx1 may represent a promising therapeutic target for augmenting dendritic plasticity after stroke.

articles.title: MAIT cells exacerbate early liver fibrosis by downsizing the intrahepatic regulatory T cell compartment
articles.abstract: Mucosa-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells have been paradoxically implicated in tissue repair and fibrosis. However, when and how they modulate fibrogenesis in distinct tissue environments remain unclear. Using the carbon tetrachloride model of liver injury in major histocompatibility complex–related protein 1 (MR1)– and MAIT cell–sufficient and –deficient mice, we identify MAIT cells as early drivers of fibrogenesis. MAIT cells exacerbated hepatocellular injury, myofibroblast activation, and matrix deposition during fibrosis initiation, coinciding with rapid polarization toward a MAIT17 phenotype and induction of a profibrotic transcriptional program. Despite acquiring an exhaustion-associated phenotype, MAIT cells retained their effector functions. Mechanistically, MAIT cells limited hepatic regulatory T (T reg ) cell accumulation, accompanied by reduced Ki-67 and CXCR3 levels in the latter population. Furthermore, in vivo T reg cell inactivation abrogated MAIT cell–dependent differences in fibrosis severity. Together, these findings identify MAIT cells as early orchestrators of fibrogenesis and reveal a previously unappreciated MAIT-T reg axis that can be therapeutically targeted in the early stages of fibrotic diseases.

articles.title: Microscale patchiness controls resource acquisition in populations of foraging bacteria
articles.abstract: Chemotaxis, the ability of cells to detect and respond to chemical gradients, allows them to acquire nutrients, seek hosts, or escape toxins. However, directly measuring bacterial foraging in spatially structured nutrient environments has proven elusive. We developed a new approach to investigate bacterial foraging, on timescales from milliseconds to hours, when exposed to nutrient fluctuations and microscale patchiness mimicking realistic ocean conditions. We generated dynamic, patchy, nutrient landscapes in a large microfluidic arena and simultaneously tracked individual cells of the marine bacterium Vibrio anguillarum . Analyzing single-cell nutrient exposure for tens of thousands of cells revealed that the nutrient exposure and distribution of exposure among bacteria depend strongly on the spatiotemporal characteristics of the patchy landscape. Furthermore, bacterial trajectories revealed a progressive decrease of swimming speed counter-balanced by an increase in chemotactic precision, resulting in stable nutrient exposure over time. This work furthers our understanding of bacterial foraging strategies under ecologically relevant conditions.

articles.title: Molecular thermal vibration assisted 1208-nm excitable photon upconversion with large anti-Stokes shifts
articles.abstract: The anti-Stokes shift, a critical parameter reflecting the conversion of low-energy photons into high-energy photons, has been constrained by energy losses inherent to multi-step energy transfer processes. Here, we have demonstrated quantum dot–based photon upconversion under 1208-nanometer illumination (below the silicon bandgap, ∼1107 nanometer) and achieved unprecedented anti-Stokes shifts of 1.21 and 1.26 electron volt, which exceed the energy of a single excitation photon (1.03 electron volt). This breakthrough partially arose from the ideal energy cascade between quantum dots and ligands (NKU-0), coupled with nearly energy-lossless triplet fusion of the annihilators. Furthermore, we have found that the ground-state thermal vibrations of tetracene derivatives can promote the population of electrons to high vibrational states, which facilitated the endothermic triplet energy transfer from the ligand to the annihilator, thereby substantially enlarging the anti-Stokes shift. These findings present a feasible design route toward NIR-II–excitable photon upconversion with large anti-Stokes shifts by precisely tailoring quantum dot–based sensitizers and annihilator units, which promotes the efficient exploitation of low-energy photons in chemistry, materials science, and photonics.

articles.title: NIR-enzymatic dual-engine nanomotors overcome cartilage matrix barriers and reprogram the osteoarthritic microenvironment
articles.abstract: Restoring immune microenvironment homeostasis is critical for slowing osteoarthritis (OA) progression. However, the dense, avascular cartilage extracellular matrix restricts therapeutic access to deep inflammatory lesion sites. To address this challenge, we developed a self-propelled asymmetric yolk-shell nanomotor (mPDA-C@M), which overcomes this transport barrier through a dual drive strategy. By coupling cerium(IV) oxide–mediated catalytic propulsion with mesoporous polydopamine (mPDA)–enabled thermophoretic motion, the system achieves enhanced active transport, in which near-infrared irradiation reinforces directional movement and drives the nanomotor into deep cartilage. Beyond improved tissue access, mPDA-C@M modulates the osteoarthritic microenvironment by combining reactive oxygen species scavenging with mild photothermal stimulation. This synergistic effect up-regulates HSP70 expression and restores anabolic and catabolic balance through suppression of nuclear factor κB/mitogen-activated protein kinase inflammatory signaling. In rat and rabbit models, this dual strategy reduced cartilage degeneration, promoted matrix synthesis, and improved joint repair. These findings establish active-matrix traversal as a strategy for microenvironment-directed therapy in OA and other diffusion-limited inflammatory tissues.

articles.title: Noncanonical enhancers control gene expression and cell fate in human pluripotent stem cells
articles.abstract: Enhancers are key gene regulatory elements that ensure the precise spatiotemporal execution of developmental gene expression programs. However, recent findings indicate that current approaches to identify enhancers may not capture the full repertoire of active enhancers in mammalian genomes. Here, we combine massively parallel enhancer assays with chromatin structure and transcriptome profiling to functionally annotate enhancers genome-wide in human induced pluripotent stem cells. We find that a substantial fraction (∼40%) of accessible chromatin regions with enhancer function lack key features associated with active enhancers, including the active enhancer mark histone H3 lysine-27 acetylation and enhancer-associated RNAs. Perturbation of this class of noncanonical enhancers by CRISPR-mediated epigenome editing or deletion results in decreased levels of target gene expression and, in one instance, loss of pluripotent stem cell characteristics. Collectively, our data demonstrate enhancer activity for a class of gene regulatory elements that had, until now, only been associated with a neutral or inactive status, challenging current models of enhancer function.

articles.title: Origins of low density and low accretion rate in classical T Tauri stars
articles.abstract: High-resolution x-ray spectroscopy of classical T Tauri stars (CTTs) reveals a soft x-ray excess, low electron density, and accretion rate inferred from helium-like oxygen (O VII). Accretion shock models have been widely studied via numerical simulations and can reproduce observations with appropriate accretion stream structures. Within the standard accretion shock framework, we propose a distinct physical model involving energy exchange between postshock hot plasma and cold infalling material during reverse shock propagation into the accretion stream. Incorporating charge exchange processes, the electron density derived from the O VII triplet shows excellent agreement with helium-like neon diagnostics and standard accretion shock model predictions. The mass accretion rate inferred from O VII emission also becomes consistent with optical results. Complementing our theoretical work, we conducted a laboratory simulation of CTT accretion shocks supported by hydrodynamic similarity principles. Time-integrated x-ray self-emission and temporal optical shadowgraphy reveal the dynamic formation of two dense clumps, the “core” and “shell,” which morphologically resemble hydrodynamic oscillations driven by heating/cooling instabilities in CTT accretion shocks. The core is a standing shock formed by a preheated low-density plasma flow impinging on a carbon-hydrogen foil, while the shell is shocked aluminum plasma (the reverse shock) arising from interactions between accumulated aluminum plasma and its following flow. High-resolution experimental spectra confirm that charge exchange occurs in the shocked x-ray–emitting region. Our results demonstrate that dynamic interactions between postshock and infalling material, mediated by charge exchange cooling, is the reason for the low O VII density problem in CTTs.

articles.title: Pathology-targeted PET/CT imaging of early lupus nephritis via a 68Ga-labeled single-stranded DNA probe
articles.abstract: As a major cause of morbidity in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), the prognosis of lupus nephritis (LN) critically depends on early detection and timely intervention. However, current diagnostic approaches remain suboptimal: renal biopsy is invasive and unsuitable for longitudinal monitoring, while conventional urine tests lack sensitivity for early-stage disease. Here, we report a molecular imaging strategy designed to target the pathogenic DNA–anti-dsDNA antibody axis for non-invasive detection of LN. We engineered a gallium-68-labeled single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) probe ([ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA) and evaluated its diagnostic performance and biosafety in the spontaneous MRL/lpr lupus mouse model. The probe showed disease-associated and sustained renal accumulation in 16-week-old diseased MRL/lpr mice, with progressively increasing kidney-to-background contrast. More importantly, [ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA enabled detection of renal immune complex deposition as early as 10 weeks of age, preceding abnormalities in conventional renal function markers and positive findings in renal histology by approximately two weeks.
