Osteoclastogenesis and osteoblastogenesis were evaluated using murine and human samples. Untargeted and targeted metabolomics analyses were performed using an ultra-high-performance liquid chromatographic system coupled with high-resolution Orbitrap mass spectrometry (HRMS). Secondary analysis of 16S rRNA sequencing data was performed using R programming. Results GM analysis and plasma metabolomics revealed an alteration in bacterial taxa associated with secondary BA synthesis and reduced circulating DCA levels. DCA administration improved impaired trabecular and cortical bone microarchitecture in the OVX mice by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis and enhancing osteoblastogenesis. Moreover, DCA altered circulating osteoclastogenic (IL-6, Il-9, IL-17A, IFN-γ, RANKL) and osteoblastogenic (OPG, TGF-β, IL-10) factors. Mechanically, DCA suppressed osteoclast differentiation and the expression of genes associated with osteoclast formation (NFATC1, NFΚB, TRAF6, TREM2, SYNB), fusion (CSF1R, DC-STAMP, CD47), and resorption (CTSK, ATP6VOD1, ATP6VOD2, CAR2, SPP1) in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), while promoting osteogenic differentiation and matrix mineralization in bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) from PMO women. Additionally, DCA enhanced the nascent calcium deposition at the fracture site and improved bone healing via inhibiting osteoclastogenesis. Conclusion Overall, reduced DCA availability was associated with PMO, while DCA treatment mitigated OVX-induced bone loss and improved bone healing. This study highlights the therapeutic potential of DCA for maintaining both bone homeostasis in PMO and fracture healing with immense orthopaedic applications. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Indian Council of Medical Research, https://ror.org/0492wrx28, 61/05/2022-IMM/BMS, EMDR/IG/13/2024-01-00842

articles.title: Development of African Swine Fever Virus Pseudotype Systems for Ba71v and Georgia 2007 strains
articles.abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) is a large, complex DNA virus that causes a severe haemorrhagic disease in domestic swine and Eurasian wild boar. Due to its high pathogenicity, research involving ASFV is restricted to high-containment laboratories, which significantly limits investigations into its biology, host interactions and the development of effective control measures. To overcome these limitations, this study utilised pseudotyped virus (PV) technology to identify ASFV proteins involved in cell entry. Candidate proteins were identified through bioinformatic analysis and a review of the published literature, incorporated into PVs, and subsequently assessed for their ability to facilitate cellular entry. This approach identified a combination of three ASFV proteins that, when combined, resulted in the most efficient cell entry. This work represents the successful generation of the first functional ASF pseudotype system for both Ba71v and Georgia 2007 strains, enabling the safe study of ASFV entry mechanisms under containment level 2.

articles.title: Direction of oscillatory networks in the human medial temporal lobe reverses across verbal working memory phases
articles.abstract: Working memory (WM) requires neural circuits to change how they interact as information is encoded, maintained and used. Directional oscillatory interactions in the medial temporal lobe (MTL) contribute to memory processing, but how these interactions are spatially organized during verbal WM remains unclear. Here, we analyzed intracranial electroencephalogram and neuronal spiking recorded from the human MTL during a verbal Sternberg task. Theta- and gamma-band activities in MTL showed predominant directionality in the posterior-to-anterior axis during WM encoding, but this direction was reversed to anterior-to-posterior during retrieval. Theta activities reflecting the WM load were more prevalent in left than right MTL, and theta in left MTL coordinated spike timings more strongly. Moreover, interhemispheric interactions showed a predominant left-to-right influence, with posterior-to-anterior interactions enhanced during encoding and anterior-to-posterior interactions enhanced during retrieval. Together, these findings suggest that verbal WM engages a spatially organized MTL network in which the predominant direction of oscillatory interactions changes across task phases.

articles.title: Dual cellular targeting of complement receptor 2 (CR2/CD21) synergistically suppresses autoreactive germinal center activity and autoimmunity in lupus
articles.abstract: Pathogenic germinal center (GC) activity persists in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) because current B cell-targeting therapies do not consistently eliminate the resilient GC niche that sustains autoimmunity. Complement receptor 2 (CR2/CD21) presents a unique bicellular therapeutic target to impede GC-associated autoimmune disease. For B cells, it has been previously shown to lower the threshold for B cell activation, and for follicular dendritic cells (FDCs), it sustains the GC response. Using a CD21-blocking antibody in a spontaneous lupus-prone mouse model, we demonstrate that dual CD21 blockade on both B cells and FDCs synergistically inhibited GC B cell responses and suppressed autoantibody production, memory recall, and renal antibody deposition. Mechanistically, B cell-specific blockade impaired GC entry by limiting initial activation, whereas FDC-specific blockade disrupted GC architecture and curtailed ongoing responses. Further, dual blockade uniquely reshaped immunological memory by promoting accumulation of a CD21low/-CD38+ memory B cell subset with attenuated antibody-secreting cell (ASC) recall potential. These findings identify CD21 blockade as a precision immunomodulatory strategy capable of suppressing pathogenic humoral immunity without complete B cell depletion.

articles.title: DynamicsPLM: A Dynamics-Enriched Small Protein Language Model for Protein Variant Effect Prediction
articles.abstract: Predicting how mutations impact protein function and stability remains a key challenge in computational biology. Current state-of-the-art protein language models (PLMs) primarily scale parameter size on sequence corpora to capture evolutionary constraints but remain blind to the explicit physical dynamics of folded proteins. Conversely, models trained strictly on physical dynamics neglect critical evolutionary sequence statistics. In this paper, we bridge this gap by introducing DynamicsPLM, a highly parameter-efficient 35-million-parameter model that unifies evolutionary and biophysical representation learning. Utilizing a second-stage, multi-task continual pretraining strategy on over 60,000 proteins, we enrich a foundational sequence encoder with explicit residue-level and pairwise molecular dynamics heads while preserving its original evolutionary knowledge. At inference, DynamicsPLM computes zero-shot mutation effects from sequence alone by balancing an evolutionary plausibility score against a structural dynamics disruption score. Across the massive ProteinGym benchmark and natural variants of the Tsuboyama folding stability dataset, DynamicsPLM achieves state-of-the-art accuracy among all models under 100M parameters, and matches or outperforms several billion-scale sequence-based models of its size. Our findings demonstrate that explicit structural-dynamics supervision provides a parameter-efficient alternative to raw scale. Availability: All codes including data preparation scripts, training and validation recipes, and experimental configurations for LoMuS are available at: https://github.com/kabir-ai2bio-lab/DynamicsPLM.

articles.title: ECMExplainer: a functional matrisome framework for decoding cellular stress states and aging trajectories
articles.abstract: The extracellular matrix (ECM) is increasingly recognized as both a hallmark of aging and a durable record of the cellular stress states that shape age-related tissue dysfunction. Despite its apparent role in aging and disease, translating matrisome gene expression into interpretable biological meaning remains an unresolved challenge. Here we introduce ECMExplainer, a framework that uses 180 matrisome gene-pair ratios, partitioned into 76 Assembly/Destruction and 104 Signaling/Signaling pairs to position fibroblast transcriptomes within a functional matrisome phenotype space defined by six reference fibroblast states spanning physiological and stress-associated conditions: Proliferating, Quiescence, Senescence, Fibrosis, Inflammation, and Hypoxia. Because each ratio records only which of the two genes is more highly expressed, it is largely insensitive to sequencing depth and batch offsets, allowing ECMExplainer to outperform magnitude-based classifiers on unseen data. Rather than assigning only a single phenotype label, ECMExplainer measures a sample's coordinate distance to each reference state, enabling quantitative mapping of matrisome state trajectories while giving biological meaning even to conditions that fall between or outside the training phenotypes. Across 20 independent fibroblast datasets, ECMExplainer uncovered conserved ECM signatures underlying diverse fibroblast states and showed that they capture multiple aging-related processes. Specifically, it identified FST/ITGA1 as a rapamycin-sensitive senescence-associated ratio, revealed a fibrosis-biased ECM trajectory in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome distinct from chronological aging, and distinguished successful from failed OSKM reprogramming using an ECM Aging Score without retraining. Together, these findings establish the matrisome as a compact and biologically interpretable carrier of cellular state information, and ECMExplainer as a quantitative foundation for interpreting aging, fibrosis and rejuvenation through the lens of the ECM. ### Competing Interest Statement RAA is the Chief Scientific Officer (CSO) of Sustayn Bioscience GmbH. JSPS Kakenhi, 25H01053 Grant-in-Aid Transformative Research Areas (A) Multimodal ECM, 23H04927, 23H04928 RIKEN BDR Life-Cycle Redesign Project German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, FKZ 03EGTMV007

articles.title: Electrophysiology of multisite direct electrical stimulation in the human brain
articles.abstract: Human cognition and neurological disorders reflect properties of distributed networks, yet how best to engage these networks therapeutically remains unknown. Multisite stimulation is a principled strategy for engaging brain networks, but a key translational barrier is understanding how a network combines concurrent inputs from multiple nodes. Here, we investigated the electrophysiology of simultaneous multisite direct electrical stimulation in 20 participants implanted with stereo-EEG electrodes. Synchronized dual-site stimulation engaged a larger effective network than single-site stimulation. Linear superposition explained most responses, but distinct nonlinear responses were also observed. Sublinear responses, consistent with saturation, occurred proximal to stimulation sites, while supralinear responses arose in network-connected sites during the response's late component. Moreover, low-intensity dual-site stimulation matched or exceeded single-site stimulation at higher intensities. These principles extended to three-site stimulation. These findings systematically characterize how responses to simultaneous multisite stimulation interact in the human brain, a foundational step towards principled, network-guided neurostimulation therapies.

articles.title: Empirical optimization of dCas12a-based CRISPRi/a for pooled screening in Yarrowia lipolytica
articles.abstract: Yarrowia lipolytica is an important host for biotechnology and metabolic engineering, valued for its ability to accumulate lipids and produce a wide range of industrially relevant compounds. This creates a growing need for genome-scale tools that can accelerate the identification of genes underlying complex phenotypes. Although Cas9-based CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) and activation (CRISPRa) tools are well established in Y. lipolytica, Cas12a offers a complementary platform with a T-rich PAM that can expand access to promoter regions and facilitate multiplexed regulation. Despite these advantages, Cas12a-based CRISPRi/a remains comparatively underdeveloped in Y. lipolytica, particularly for large-scale functional screening. Here, we establish and systematically benchmark dCas12a-based CRISPRi/a platforms for pooled screening in Y. lipolytica. We first compared two widely used effectors, dLbCas12a and denAsCas12a, across single-gene assays and a pooled CRISPRi library targeting nine essential or conditionally essential genes with 752 crRNAs. Both orthologs supported robust transcriptional repression, but their relative performance was crRNA- and condition-dependent, with dLbCas12a showing more consistent and stronger late-stage depletion across targets. dLbCas12a also enabled enrichment-based CRISPRi and CRISPRa screens, recovering expected drug-resistance and lipid-associated phenotypes. The broad design of the pooled library further enabled identification of crRNA features associated with CRISPRi efficacy. Highly active crRNAs were enriched near transcription start sites, with an effective targeting interval extending from approximately -260 to +50 bp. Intermediate GC content was associated with higher efficacy, while PAM identity showed a weaker but consistent effect, with TTTA and TTTT PAMs linked to stronger depletion than TTTC and TTTG PAMs. Spacer length showed the strongest association with CRISPRi efficacy, with 18-nt crRNAs consistently outperforming matched longer 20-, 23-, and 25-nt variants. Finally, we tested dHyperLbCas12a, an engineered LbCas12a variant with enhanced activity, and found that it produced substantially stronger CRISPRi and CRISPRa phenotypes than dLbCas12a. Together, these results establish Cas12a as a versatile platform for pooled CRISPRi/a screens in Y. lipolytica, identify practical crRNA prioritization rules for improved library performance, and highlight dHyperLbCas12a as a promising effector for future large-scale gain- and loss-of-function screens.

articles.title: EveD, a vesicle-associated rhizobial candidate effector shaping nodulation competitiveness and host genotype responses
articles.abstract: Bacterial extracellular vesicles (EVs) are an ancestral secretion route that delivers cargoes to host cells. Although rhizobial EVs transport Nod factors and other bacterial components, their role in protein delivery during symbiosis remains unexplored. Here we characterise EveD, a large soluble repeat-containing protein of Sinorhizobium fredii HH103. Its export is independent of the type III secretion system, and EveD is recovered only in EV-containing fractions. eveD expression is not induced by genistein or soybean seed exudates and does not follow the canonical NodD1-TtsI pathway, but partially depends on the symbiotic regulator SyrM. When expressed in plant cells, EveD localises mainly to the cytoplasm, associates with endoplasmic reticulum-like structures and occasionally occurs in the nucleus. The eveD mutant shows increased nodule occupancy relative to the wild type in Glycine max cv. Williams 82. EveD modulates early responses in wild Glycine soja accessions in a genotype-dependent manner, constraining pseudonodule organogenesis in JL2 while promoting it in CH2. These findings identify EveD as an EV-associated rhizobial protein contributing to bacterial competitiveness and genotype-dependent symbiotic responses, and highlight EVs as an additional route for protein export during legume symbiosis.

articles.title: Evolutionarily Conserved Fragments reveal modular architecture and expand functional coverage in bacteriophage proteins
articles.abstract: Bacteriophage proteins evolve through extensive modular exchange, yet the sequence units underlying this process remain poorly defined. Classical domains are plausible evolutionary modules, but they incompletely annotate phage proteins and may not always coincide with the regions conserved across protein families. Here, we constructed 13,035 Evolutionarily Conserved Fragments (ECFs), grouped into 3,167 families, through large-scale HMM-HMM comparisons of proteins from 5,396 RefSeq phage genomes, without imposing predefined domain boundaries. ECFs overlapped substantially with ECOD and Pfam annotations but formed a heterogeneous spectrum comprising subdomains, domain-equivalent units, composite regions and fragments with no counterpart in either resource. Their relationships were frequently nested, indicating that conserved modules occur at multiple organisational scales. ECFs annotated 50% of phage representative proteins (at least doubling the coverage of either database), with the largest gains in structural and infection-related functions, a pattern replicated in independent metagenomic data. ECF families also showed function-dependent patterns of diversity and spatial segregation and provided functional associations for 23,925 protein families lacking detectable Pfam or ECOD domains. In receptor-binding proteins, ECFs subdivided established domains, delineated previously unannotated structural elements and recovered homologous regions where structural similarity was ambiguous. These results show that the evolutionary building blocks of phage proteins do not always coincide with classical domains, highlighting that evolutionary processes act across multiple scales. ECFs provide a complementary, sequence-derived framework for investigating how complex viral proteins are assembled, diversified and functionally organised.

articles.title: Excitatory neurons downregulate synaptic proteins before motor onset and glia reduce neuronal support in Huntington disease mice
articles.abstract: Background: Huntington's disease burdens protein homeostasis and affects neurons and glia differently across brain regions, but how these two main cell populations respond as the disease progresses remains unresolved. Whole-tissue proteomes mix these cell types and hide how the proteome of each changes. We therefore measured the proteome of each cell type separately at different disease stages. Methods: We metabolically labelled cell-type-specific proteomes in living R6/1 mice and wild-type littermates for 15 days at different disease stages. We examined cortical and hippocampal excitatory neurons at 1.5, 3 and 7 months, cerebellar inhibitory neurons at 3 and 7 months, and cortical, striatal and cerebellar glia at 7 months. We combined mass spectrometry with functional enrichment and competitive protein-set tests to understand the differential proteostatic response to mutant huntingtin across disease progression, brain regions and cell types. Differential abundance was tested with a peptide-centric linear mixed model (msqRob, Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.1), and proteins whose levels varied together in cortical and hippocampal neurons were grouped into modules by weighted correlation network analysis. Results: Hippocampal excitatory neurons showed broader and more coordinated regulation than cortical neurons already before motor onset, whereas the cortical response increased with age and no cortical protein module differed between genotypes before the most severe stage. All three neuronal populations upregulated ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) proteins as the disease advanced. Protein folding changed, with more subunits of the chaperonin CCT/TRiC but fewer J-domain proteins and, in excitatory neurons, fewer HSP70 chaperones. At the most severe stage, glia of the three studied regions regulated mainly different proteins, but all increased UPS proteins and decreased key proteins of neuronal support, among them the main glial glutamate transporter GLT-1. Cholesterol-related proteins decreased in cortical and cerebellar glia, and respiratory-chain proteins in striatal glia. Conclusions: Synaptic proteins decreased early in cortical and hippocampal neurons and were not restored at later ages. A later and broader maintenance response coexisted with their continued and increasing downregulation. In this first cell-type-resolved view of the labelled proteome in a Huntington's disease mouse model, progression appears as a change in the coordination of cellular functions, which whole-tissue measurements would dilute.

articles.title: Exploratory positional differences in observed CDRH2 lineage-state transitions following HIV-1 germline-targeting vaccination
articles.abstract: Background: Germline-targeting HIV-1 vaccination recruits VRC01-class B-cell precursors, but the positional patterns of observed longitudinal B-cell receptor lineage-state changes remain incompletely described. We compared CDRH2 profiles between homologous and heterologous boosting regimens using published IAVI G002 data. Methods: Participant-specific Week-8 lineages were prospectively matched to Week-24 observations. Germline-to-nongermline changes in sampled lineage-modal residues were evaluated at seven IGHV1-2*02 CDRH2 positions using participant-balanced, mean-centered profiles and exact participant-label permutation inference. Sampling-depth and sorting-probe sensitivity analyses assessed observability. A separate participant-held-out benchmark evaluated antibody-language-model representations for predicting observed Week-24 lineage detection. Results: The CDRH2 analysis included 332 lineages, 15 participants, 2,179 eligible lineage-position observations, and 241 observed state changes. The regional profile statistic was 0.027066 (exact p = 0.001709; six-region adjusted q = 0.010256), with descriptive differences at V-relative positions 51, 54, and 55. Most eligible longitudinal observations had one assessable cell per visit. In seven Group-1 participants, Week-24 dual-probe sampling recovered 181 baseline lineages with eOD-GT8 and 143 with Cg28v2, including 60 detected by both probes. In a separate cohort of 2,739 lineages from 17 participants, IgBERT and AbLang-2 representations did not improve participant-balanced average precision over a four-feature biological baseline. Conclusions: Observed CDRH2 lineage-modal-state profiles differed between regimens in this exploratory secondary analysis. Sparse sampling, potentially probe-related ascertainment, and absent linked functional validation preclude inference about mutation timing, functional improvement, or causal booster effects.

articles.title: Exploring taxonomic diversity in the genus Suberites Nardo, 1833: Insights from microbial, phylogenetic, and morphological analyses
articles.abstract: Marine sponges (phylum Porifera) are a highly diverse and polymorphic group of marine invertebrates whose taxonomic delimitation is often challenging due to high intraspecific variability and the scarcity of diagnostic morphological characters. Their close association with microbial symbionts also makes them an important source of secondary metabolites, some of which may contribute to sponge colouration. Here, we use morphological characters, molecular phylogenetic markers, and 16S metabarcoding of the symbiont community to understand speciation in a common Mediterranean sponge lineage. We collected 43 specimens of the genus Suberites from the Mediterranean Sea and the North and South Atlantic Oceans, between 55-150 m depths, and sequenced two barcoding genes, cytochrome c oxidase I and 28S rDNA, as well as studied their spicular complements. We identified five closely-related species: S. domuncula , S. ficus/pagurorum , S. dandelenae , S. ambulodomus , and a new species of Suberites from the Balearic Islands, Suberites sp. nov. The latter represents a potential new pseudo-cryptic species closely related to S. domuncula , because of their strong morphological and molecular affinities. The potential new Mediterranean species exhibits six colour morphotypes (yellow, gray, orange, brown, red, and blue), and the microbiome analyses of the symbiotic communities revealed significant differences in bacterial community composition among colour morphotypes, specially of bacteria that produce different pigments which potentially give the sponge is colouration. These results provide valuable insights into species boundaries and evolutionary relationships within the genus Suberites and support a role for the microbiome in sponge colouration.

articles.title: Global mapping of VEGF-A driven changes in the RNA bound phospho-proteome reveals a molecular switch to coordinate angiogenesis in endothelial cells
articles.abstract: RNA binding proteins (RBPs) serve as upstream master regulators of cellular fate transitions at the post-transcriptional level. RBP-RNA interactions are dynamically regulated by post-translational modifications to coordinate cellular responses. We hypothesised that changes in RBP phosphorylation will play a key role in coordinating angiogenesis, the formation of new blood vessels, in endothelial cells (ECs). Therefore, we used phospho-proteomic analysis of the mRNA bound proteome to identify global phosphorylation changes in mouse cardiac ECs during acute and prolonged VEGF-A stimulation. Of the differentially phosphorylated RBPs, we found that the phosphorylation of serine 199 within mRNA bound Phf6 (PHD finger protein 6) was consistently increased following VEGF-A stimulation. Phf6 phosphorylation at this specific site was sufficient and required to induce a pro-angiogenic phenotype, facilitating a change in Phf6 conformation promoting interaction with distinct RNAs. We show here that Phf6 phosphorylation at serine 199, downstream of VEGF-A, acts as a molecular switch to differentially coordinate a decrease of anti-angiogenic RNAs (i.e. extracellular matrix genes) and an increase in pro-angiogenesis related RNAs, in part by differentially regulating their stability, to promote angiogenesis.

articles.title: Graph-guided flow matching enables biologically informed prediction at single-cell resolution
articles.abstract: Perturb-seq enables systematic interrogation of massively parallel genetic perturbations at single-cell resolution, yet exhaustive characterization of the full perturbation space remains impractical. Here, we present Graph-guided Flow Matching (GFM), a generative framework that integrates biological knowledge graphs with latent flow matching to predict post-perturbation single-cell transcriptomes. Across multiple large-scale Perturb-seq datasets, GFM outperforms a strong linear baseline and current deep-learning models in predicting unseen single-gene perturbations, while training up to 30x faster and remaining robust with limited training data. GFM also demonstrates competitive performance in the two-gene perturbation prediction task when neither perturbed gene is observed during training. Ablation experiments show that combining flow matching with knowledge graphs enables accurate prediction of perturbation responses. Finally, GFM accurately calculates transcriptional consequences of HSP90AA1 inactivation and identifies target candidates unseen by the model in chronic myeloid leukemia. Our study establishes GFM as a biologically informed generative framework that predicts single-cell perturbation responses for prioritization of therapeutic targets.

articles.title: HieraPTM: From PTM Site Recognition to Functional Phosphosite Prediction through Hierarchical Context and Protein Mechanics
articles.abstract: Protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate cellular signaling and protein function, making accurate site identification essential for understanding protein regulation. However, PTM site recognition and functional phosphosite prediction are largely modeled independently, limiting the transfer of large-scale recognition knowledge to functional prioritization. Here, we introduce HieraPTM-HieraFuncPhos, a cross-task hierarchical framework that separately models and conditionally integrates transferable PTM recognition representations and function-specific mechanical evidence. HieraPTM integrates local sequence patterns, protein language model representations, and three-dimensional structural information to recognize multiple PTM types. HieraFuncPhos transfers these representations through parameter-efficient adaptation and adaptively retrieves local and distal mechanical evidence conditioned on functional representations. At HSP90AA1 T36 and T115, the model reveals distinct mechanical response patterns consistent with published nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) observations, suggesting that the framework not only prioritizes functional phosphosites but also provides biophysically grounded, testable hypotheses regarding site-specific regulation. HieraPTM achieved macro-averaged AUROC and AUPRC values of 0.9237 and 0.8425 across eight PTM tasks, while maintaining competitive performance on severely imbalanced external benchmarks. HieraFuncPhos achieved an AUROC of 0.8274 and an AUPRC of 0.8188, outperforming existing comparison methods. Together, this framework connects PTM site recognition, functional prioritization, and structure-informed hypotheses regarding potential regulatory processes.

articles.title: High +Gz Exposure Alters Urinary Extracellular Vesicle miRNAs in Humans
articles.abstract: High +Gz exposure elicits complex cardiovascular, autonomic, and endocrine responses, but the associated molecular responses in humans remain poorly understood. We investigated whether microRNAs (miRNAs) encapsulated in urinary extracellular vesicles (uEVs) are altered following acute high +Gz exposure. Twenty-one healthy young men undergoing human centrifuge training provided urine samples before, immediately after, and on the morning after exposure. Candidate uEV-encapsulated miRNAs were identified by RNA sequencing and Gene Ontology analysis, and 16 miRNAs related to ischemia, hypoxia, blood pressure regulation, and mechanical stress were quantified by quantitative PCR. Salivary cortisol, urinary catecholamines, and heart rate were also assessed. Six uEV-encapsulated miRNAs increased significantly after high +Gz exposure. miR-20b-5p, miR-125b-5p, and miR-130a-3p increased immediately after exposure and returned to baseline by the following morning, whereas miR-335-5p, miR-17-5p, and miR-92a-3p remained elevated. Urinary adrenaline, noradrenaline, and dopamine increased immediately after exposure; adrenaline returned to baseline by the following morning, whereas noradrenaline and dopamine remained elevated. Salivary cortisol and heart rate also increased. These findings demonstrate distinct transient and sustained temporal responses of uEV-encapsulated miRNAs to high +Gz in humans, paralleling different catecholamine response patterns. Although their tissue origins and functional roles remain unresolved, these findings provide new molecular-level insights into the human physiological response to high +Gz.

articles.title: High-Performance All-Atom Continuous Constant-pH Molecular Dynamics and Native Asynchronous Replica Exchange in Amber
articles.abstract: Conformational dynamics of biomolecules, including proteins and nucleic acids, are often coupled to changes in protonation states. All-atom particle-mesh Ewald continuous constant-pH molecular dynamics (PME-CpHMD) enables proton-coupled dynamics, but its routine use has been limited by computational cost. Here we report a second-generation CUDA implementation of PME-CpHMD in Amber, in which the CpHMD-specific nonbonded corrections are evaluated in a separate kernel. Across protein systems ranging from 45 to 1,338 residues, the new implementation increases throughput by 1.5-2 fold relative to the previous fused-kernel implementation and limits the overhead relative to conventional MD to 12-18%. We also implemented the asynchronous pH replica-exchange (pH-REX) algorithm natively in pmemd.cuda.MPI, allowing simulations to run on fewer GPUs than replicas without the overhead of the previous Python wrapper. Furthermore, we derived CpHMD titration parameters for all six titratable residue types (Asp, Glu, His, Cys, Tyr, and Lys) for use with three protein force fields: CHARMM c22/CMAP, Amber ff14sb and ff19sb. The new implementations and parameterization were validated using pKa calculations of model peptides and hen egg white lysozyme (HEWL). The HEWL simulations revealed force-field-specific limitations, including overestimation of the pKa downshift 20 of H15 and sensitivity of the proton donor assignment in coupled E35/D52 dyad. Comparison with our previous work and the PME-CpHMD simulations in GROMACS with the CHARMM c36m force field demonstrated the robustness and sampling efficiency of pH-REX PME-CpHMD simulations. The new implementation provides a foundation for routine all-atom constant-pH simulations in Amber. The analysis highlights the need for continued development of protein force fields to more accurately balance intramolecular electrostatics and solvation of charged residues.

articles.title: Identifying aligned tensor decompositions across heterogeneous neural datasets
articles.abstract: Large-scale neural recordings increasingly span many sessions, brain regions and animals, but differences in neuronal sampling make it difficult to identify and interpret shared patterns. We introduce Neuralign, a tensor- based model that jointly aligns and decomposes recordings into components, each pairing a shared temporal pattern with its expression in individual trials and neurons, without requiring matched neurons, matched trials or behavioural labels. In simulations, pooling recordings improved recovery of shared components; in recurrent networks, Neuralign distinguished related from distinct task solutions. In the macaque motor cortex, label-free components recovered the ring-like organisation of reach directions. Across 93 brain-wide mouse recordings, Neuralign discovered a single component that isolated the response to inhibition of the anterior lateral motor cortex (ALM). A reference learned from correct, uninhibited trials revealed inhibition-related activity outside the choice direction on error trials, most strongly in the ALM and thalamus. Neuralign provides an interpretable framework for studying the shared structure of large neural datasets, linking shared patterns to individual trials and recorded populations.

articles.title: Impaired cholinergic modulation of striatal spiny projection neurons in repetitive behaviors associated with TSHZ3-linked autism spectrum disorder
articles.abstract: Alterations in central cholinergic systems are implicated in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We previously identified TSHZ3 as an ASD-linked gene and provided evidence, from transgenic mouse models, supporting the view that striatal cholinergic interneurons (SCINs) are key players in the core ASD trait represented by repetitive behaviors (RBs). Indeed, conditional deletion of Tshz3 in cholinergic neurons (Chat-cKO model) results in RBs associated with reduced SCIN firing activity and decreased striatal cholinergic tone. Here we tackled the resulting adaptations in the striatal circuitry underlying RBs in Chat-cKO, focusing on the two populations of striatal projection neurons (SPNs) that express dopamine D1 (D1R) or D2 (D2R) receptor. Using patch-clamp electrophysiological recordings, as well as behavioral, pharmacological and molecular approaches, we show reduced cholinergic transmission through the muscarinic M1 receptor onto SPNs, with no changes in the functionality or expression of this receptor. Notably, we demonstrate a loss of the differential excitability of D1R- vs. D2R-SPNs. Finally, acute in vivo treatment with the acetylcholinesterase inhibitor donepezil significantly alleviates RBs in mutant mice. These findings point to dysfunction of SCINs as a pathological and druggable mechanism underlying RBs in Tshz3-linked ASD, and to altered SPN excitability as a critical contributor in the resulting pathophysiological functioning of the striatum.

articles.title: Inactivation of tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase reduces phosphatidylcholine amounts in the brain of infant mice
articles.abstract: Hypophosphatasia is a rare disease caused by dysfunctions of tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (TNAP). TNAP is expressed in numerous tissues, notably the brain, and patients with hypophosphatasia exhibit neurological symptoms, including epilepsy in the most severe forms of the disease. TNAP knockout (KO) mouse models have provided a wealth of information regarding TNAP functions. Specifically, metabolomic studies focusing on the aqueous fraction of the brain of TNAP KO mice identified numerous molecules whose amounts were altered as a direct or indirect consequence of TNAP inactivation. Among these molecules, several are involved either directly (e.g., vitamin B6) or indirectly (e.g., N-acetylaspartate) in lipid metabolism. In this study, we therefore extended these investigations by examining the consequences of TNAP inactivation on the brain lipidome. We used a targeted lipidomic approach, examining four main categories of lipids: fatty acids, neutral lipids, sphingolipids and glycerophospholipids, subdivided into 16 lipid classes and amounting to 296 lipid species. Eleven lipid species showed significantly reduced amounts in the brain of TNAP KO mice. All belonged to the phosphatidylcholine class. As phosphatidylcholines are major constituents of brain cell membranes, our results suggest that hypophosphatasia could be associated with alterations in membrane structure and functions, which could contribute to the neurodevelopmental disorders associated with the disease.

articles.title: L-selectin shedding regulates post-infarction neutrophilia without altering myocardial injury or ventricular remodelling.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers rapid neutrophil mobilisation from the bone marrow (BM), resulting in systemic neutrophilia that is widely associated with myocardial injury. However, whether the magnitude of this response directly influences cardiac injury and subsequent ventricular remodelling remains unclear. Ectodomain shedding of L-selectin is a hallmark of neutrophil activation, although its contribution to neutrophil mobilisation following MI has not been established. Using mice expressing a non-cleavable L-selectin mutant (L(E)), we investigated the role of L-selectin shedding in post-MI neutrophilia. Under homeostatic conditions, WT and L(E) mice exhibited comparable BM neutrophil maturation and circulating neutrophil representation. Following permanent coronary ligation, however, L(E) mice exhibited markedly attenuated neutrophilia, associated with reduced circulating CXCL2 and decreased surface CXCR2 expression on BM neutrophils. Intravenous recombinant CXCL2 increased circulating neutrophil representation in WT but not L(E) mice, suggesting that impaired mobilisation cannot be explained solely by reduced ligand availability. Despite attenuated neutrophilia, myocardial neutrophil representation was comparable between genotypes at 24 hours post-MI. Circulating cardiac troponin I concentrations and MRI-quantified infarct size also showed no detectable differences. Longitudinal cardiac MRI at days 1, 14 and 28 revealed comparable ventricular structure and function, while histological scar size was similar at day 28. These findings identify L-selectin shedding as a regulator of post-MI neutrophilia and suggest that the magnitude of this systemic response can be dissociated from acute myocardial injury and subsequent ventricular remodelling.

articles.title: LRPPRC gene replacement therapy preserves cardiac function and prevents premature death in a mouse model of mitochondrial disease
articles.abstract: Pathogenic variants in LRPPRC disrupt mitochondrial gene expression, causing severe and incurable mitochondrial disease with neurological involvement accompanied by hepatopathy or cardiomyopathy. The development for gene therapy for LRPPRC-linked disease is hindered by the large LRPPRC coding sequence exceeding AAV cargo capacity when combined with classical regulatory elements. Here, we engineered compact single rAAV9 vectors expressing human or mouse LRPPRC and administered them intravenously to heart and skeletal muscle-specific Lrpprc knockout mice. This approach restored cardiac LRPPRC expression, preserved oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) function, prevented cardiomyopathy and markedly extended survival. While skeletal muscle rescue was partial, the therapy effectively prevented fatal cardiac dysfunction. These findings provide the first in vivo proof-of-concept that AAV-mediated LRPPRC gene replacement can preserve OXPHOS function and prevent lethal cardiomyopathy, supporting its potential as a therapeutic strategy for mitochondrial disease linked to LRPPRC deficiency. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. DIM (Domaine dIntérêt Majeur) of the Paris Ile-de-France Region, France AFM-Telethon, # 22251, #24318 The Dillon Fund

articles.title: Light-induced melatonin suppression in school-aged children before and during camping: associations with circadian phase and daytime light exposure
articles.abstract: Prior light exposure can influence the magnitude of melatonin suppression in response to evening light, even within the same individual. We examined whether light-induced melatonin suppression in school-aged children differed before and during a camp with approximately two weeks of exposure to a natural light-dark cycle. We also explored interindividual variation in melatonin suppression and its associations with circadian phase, habitual sleep timing, and daytime light exposure. Twenty-one healthy children aged 9--14 years underwent evening light experiments at the start of camp (Pre-camp session) and approximately two weeks later (Camp session). Melatonin suppression was calculated by comparing the area under the melatonin concentration curve between the evening light condition (200 {+/-} 30 lx, 5000 K) and the dim light condition (< 30 lx, incandescent lamps), with integration starting at dim light melatonin onset (DLMO). We assessed sleep habits from 14-day sleep diaries before camping and measured wrist-level illuminance during camping. We examined associations using Spearman correlations and compared Pre-camp and Camp melatonin suppression using a paired t-test. Melatonin suppression did not differ significantly between Pre-camp and Camp sessions (p = 0.21). Greater suppression in the Pre-camp session was associated with later DLMO (rho = 0.49, p = 0.028), but not with habitual sleep variables. In the Camp session, higher same-day geometric mean illuminance was associated with lower suppression (n = 15; rho = -0.58, p = 0.024), whereas 7-day light-exposure metrics were not. Mean melatonin suppression did not significantly change across the camping period. Meanwhile, children showed large interindividual variation in melatonin suppression, and circadian phase and recent daytime light exposure are candidate correlates of this variation in the responsiveness to the evening light.

articles.title: The zoo of the gene networks capable of pattern formation by extracellular signaling
articles.abstract: A fundamental question of developmental biology is pattern formation, or how cells with specific gene expression end up in specific locations in the body to form tissues, organs, and, overall functional anatomy. Pattern formation involves communication through extracellular signals and complex intracellular gene networks integrating these signals to determine cell responses (e.g. further signaling, cell division, cell differentiation, etc.). In this article, we address two questions: (1) Are there any logical or mathematical principles determining which gene network topologies can lead to pattern formation by cell signaling over space in multicellular systems? (2) Can gene network topologies be classified into a small number of classes that entail similar dynamics and pattern transformation capacities? We combine logical arguments and mathematical proofs to show that, despite the large amount of formally possible gene network topologies, all gene network topologies capable of pattern formation fall into only three fundamental classes and their combinations. Additionally, we show that gene networks within each class share the same logic on how they lead to pattern formation, and hence, lead to similar patterns. We characterize the main features of each class. This zoo includes the complete gene networks that, to the best of our knowledge, have been experimentally reported to lead to pattern formation as well as other gene networks that have not yet been found experimentally.

articles.title: "Wow, this could be massive": Donor-Conceived Families Experience with Unexpected Recontact for Risk of Inherited Cardiac Conditions
articles.abstract: Introduction: Recontacting families post-gamete donation, after a genetic diagnosis is made in the donor, can create complex challenges for healthcare providers and families. However, there is little literature that explores the family experience. This study aimed to explore the experiences of parents and donor-conceived young people navigating the recontact process and undergoing predictive genetic testing for an inherited cardiac condition. Methods: Semi-structured interviews were conducted to explore participants' experiences in unexpectedly being recontacted and undergoing predictive genetic testing for an inherited cardiac condition. Interviews were recorded and transcribed verbatim. A reflexive thematic analysis was performed. Results: Thirteen participants agreed to be interviewed, nine were parents and four were donor conceived young people. Four overarching themes were identified: (1) Out of the Blue, (2) A ripple effect on the family, (3) Calm after the storm, (4) Beneath the Ripples: the psychological impact. Discussion: Interviews provided insights into fertility services recontact and the predictive genetic testing process. From the themes, we conceptualize a ripple effect model. Findings highlight how cardiac genetics and fertility services are evolving, and the critical role of genetic counselors. The recontact process affects the entire family. However, most participants adapted and moved forward from this event.

articles.title: A multinational pharmacoepidemiology atlas of prescription medication associations with all-cause mortality across six population cohorts
articles.abstract: Observational studies sometimes report that individual medications are associated with lower mortality, but such signals are rarely compared across drugs and health systems. We screened prescription medications for associations with all-cause mortality using time-dependent Cox models in six cohorts from the UK, US, Finland, Hong Kong and Japan (8.93 million individuals aged 40 years or older; 1.49 billion prescriptions). Most medications were associated with higher mortality, reflecting confounding by indication. A few medications showed inverse associations with mortality, notably the varicella-zoster virus (VZV) vaccine, the antimalarials atovaquone-proguanil (Malarone) and mefloquine, and the hormone replacement therapy estradiol. These associations were only modestly attenuated by adjustment for comorbidity, lifestyle and socio-economic factors, and persisted within strata defined by pre-existing disease. While adjustment for self-reported health abolished the Malarone association, probably reflecting a healthy traveler profile, the VZV association was maintained. In FinnGen, deaths from external causes, which vaccination cannot prevent, were lower among VZV vaccine users, but much less so than all-cause mortality. In a target trial emulation in All of Us, the VZV association was maintained against matched unvaccinated individuals (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.53-0.70) and pneumococcal vaccine recipients (HR 0.64, 0.55-0.74), but was attenuated against recipients of tetanus-diphtheria vaccines, a group that also has low mortality (HR 0.85, 0.70-1.03). Healthy-user selection contributes to these signals but does not appear to fully explain the VZV vaccine association, which warrants confirmation in randomized trials. This multinational atlas provides a resource for prioritizing drug-repurposing candidates in ageing research.

articles.title: Age and body-mass index account for part of the sex differences in cerebral venous thrombosis
articles.abstract: Background. Women with cerebral venous thrombosis are younger than men and more often present with headache, but the cohorts reporting these differences did not account for age or body-mass index, both of which differ by sex. Methods. Single-center cohort of 219 consecutive adults with confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis admitted in Zurich in 2001-2021. Presentation, imaging and laboratory findings were compared between women and men, and every difference was re-estimated at equal age and body-mass index. Secondary analyses compared functional outcome, residual symptoms and return to work by sex, with an audit of incomplete follow-up. Results. Women (132, 60.3%) were younger (47.3 versus 54.9 years) and had a lower body-mass index (25.9 versus 27.8 kg/m 2 ) than men. Headache (72.0% versus 57.5%) and cortical vein thrombosis (14.4% versus 5.7%) were more frequent in women, but neither association persisted after adjustment (odds ratios, 1.17 [95% CI, 0.54-2.54] and 2.05 [95% CI, 0.59-7.06]). Higher platelet counts (+56 × 10 9 /L [95% CI, 26-86]) and elevated acute-phase markers without documented infection (59.1% versus 33.3%; odds ratio, 2.91 [95% CI, 1.44-5.87]) persisted after adjustment for age, body-mass index and calendar period. Among assessed patients (38% at 6 months), functional independence (86.3% versus 87.5%), residual headache, return to work and recanalization did not differ by sex. Conclusions. At equal age and body-mass index, the female excess of headache and cortical vein involvement was no longer apparent, whereas a higher platelet count and a non-specific acute-phase response remained. Neither translated into a difference in outcome among assessed patients.

articles.title: Antimicrobial stewardship strategies to optimise antibiotic prescribing in primary care: physicians awareness, beliefs, and strategy use
articles.abstract: Background: National efforts to promote antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) and prevent antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in primary care need strengthening. Research supports clinician-targeted AMS strategies to optimise antibiotic prescribing, but implementing them in clinical settings is challenging. Aim: Assessment of primary care physicians' awareness of, use of, and beliefs about evidence-based AMS strategies, and perceived barriers and facilitators to implementing them in a country with high antibiotic consumption rates (Poland). Methods: A pre-registered observational survey study. Eligible physicians worked in primary care in Poland for 6+ months and were recruited via professional networks and social media. Data were collected through a pre-piloted online questionnaire and analysed descriptively. Results: 270 physicians (68.2% Specialists/Residents in Family Medicine) participated. Respondents were aware of the threat of AMR (88%), the importance of AMS (93%) and their role in AMS (89%). They most recognised, utilised, perceived as effective, and recommended rapid diagnostic tests, clinical guidelines, and scales/criteria. Respondents reported high familiarity but lower engagement with communication strategies, national actions, education/training, and campaigns. Delayed prescriptions were the least used and recommended. Main barriers were time constraints and insufficient awareness of which strategies to implement. Recommended strategies included tests, guidelines, scales/criteria, AMS action plans for general practices, patient communication resources, and promoting awareness of AMS and its role in high-quality care. Conclusion: Awareness and use of evidence-based AMS strategies among physicians working in Polish primary care clinics appear high. Improvements may require reaching disengaged physicians, increasing uptake of underutilised strategies, and strengthening the impact of already used strategies.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence for pulmonary tuberculosis detection on chest X-ray images: A systematic review and diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based computer-aided detection (CAD) of tuberculosis (TB) on chest X-ray (CXR) may standardize screening and triage in settings with few radiologists but its accuracy in clinical cohorts remains uncertain. We searched five databases (PubMed, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, OpenAlex, Lens.org) on 15 March 2026 for studies published between January 2020 and March 2026, and we appraised these studies using QUADAS-2. Evaluations from clinical cohorts with complete 2 x 2 data and a microbiological or composite reference standard for all participants were pooled using a bivariate random-effects model, with 95% prediction intervals. We accounted for overlapping participants by performing a post hoc analysis with one evaluation per cohort and used GRADE to assess the certainty of the evidence. No protocol was prepared or registered. We included 21 studies (26 evaluations of AI models). Nine evaluations from three independent cohorts were pooled. Pooled sensitivity was 0.896 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.874 to 0.915, prediction interval 0.798 to 0.950) and pooled specificity was 0.689 (95% CI 0.642 to 0.732; prediction interval 0.499 to 0.831). Both confidence intervals include the World Health Organization (WHO) triage thresholds (sensitivity 90%, specificity 70%). When a screening study with partial verification was added, pooled specificity increased to 0.735. Eighteen of 24 assessed evaluations were at high risk of bias and only 1 of 21 studies was prospective, fully verified, externally validated and met the WHO thresholds. Certainty of evidence was low for sensitivity and very low for specificity. A subsequent PubMed search found additional eligible clinical evaluations that were not screened, so the review is incomplete for those studies. In clinical cohorts, AI-CXR sensitivity is close to the WHO triage target, and specificity is close to, but not clearly above, its target. The evidence is pooled across only three cohorts, and specificity varies by product and setting. Thresholds need to be calibrated locally, and prospective, externally validated evaluations are needed before widespread deployment.

articles.title: Automatic classification of seizure adequacy in electroconvulsive therapy: A proof-of-concept study
articles.abstract: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is the most effective treatment of a range of severe mental dis-orders and is annually given to more than a million patients worldwide. Dosing of the electrical charge is critical for efficacy and side-effect burden; however, it is currently based on manual assessment of seizure quality and exhibits substantial clinical heterogeneity. Here, we collected 1,000 ECT session electroencephalograms (EEG) from 130 individual ECT patients and made an expert-level classification of the EEGs into actionable seizure quality categories (null-response [0], threshold [T], and adequate [A]). We then trained a range of machine learning algorithms on the raw EEG data to classify the EEGs into these categories and tested for classi-fication accuracy. The highest performing algorithm was able to classify the seizures with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curves of >0.9 for both the 0 vs. T and the T vs. A categories corresponding to excellent discrimination. In contrast, the accuracy of predicting seizure quality in subsequent treatments was only moderate. The addition of clinical variables to the models, such as demographics, anesthesia and anticonvulsant exposure, did not improve model performance. These results provide proof-of-concept of machine learning classification of seizure adequacy in ECT based on raw EEG data. The findings could pave the way for the de-velopment of more objective and personalized decision-support tools in ECT.

articles.title: BenchmarkHub: an open-source platform for reproducible evaluation of large language models in healthcare
articles.abstract: Background: Large language models (LLMs) are solely judged by their scores on biomedical benchmarks, yet these scores are rarely reproducible since the prompts, inference settings and model builds are seldom reported. We developed BenchmarkHub, an open-source platform for auditable evaluation of language and vision-language models for biomedical research. Methods: BenchmarkHub is a Python web application (Django 5.2, SQLite) released under the MIT licence and available at https://github.com/juanjuanignacio/benchmarkhub. The application can be accessed through a browser interface, a set of command-line tools and a REST API, so interactive exploration and scripted pipelines produce identical, comparable records. The platform samples questions with fixed seeds, runs models directly or as tool-using agents in a code sandbox, grades answers with deterministic rules and stores every prompt, reply and tool call. The interface provides a leaderboard to rank performance of the models, allowing model comparison without any preexisting programming knowledge. Findings: We used BenchmarkHub to evaluate 12 open-weight models in five experiments on 15 biomedical benchmarks (11 text, two multimodal and two computational biology) and two general benchmarks. The pooled accuracy ranged from 46.1% (95% CI 43.0-49.3) to 80.9% (78.3-83.3). Re-grading the responses with simple answer-extraction rules lowered a model's accuracy by up to 33.1 percentage points, leading to a reorder of the leaderboard. Published scores were found for 23 out of the 143 benchmark/model combinations tested. The accuracy measured by BenchmarkHub was lower than in the published results in 19 out of the 23 available comparisons. The effect of four prompting protocols (1: default prompt; 2: asking the model to answer the letter only; 3: chain-of-thought prompting; 4: three-shot prompting) changed MedQA accuracy by up to 11.3 points but was not significant after multiple-testing correction with 150 questions. We also tested the impact of ablation on benchmarking using the MMMU benchmark dataset. Removing images lowered the accuracy by 18.0 and 19.3 points respectively for the two strongest models. Finally, the accuracy of agentic benchmarks using a sandboxed interpreter increased on computational biology tasks by 36-63 points. Interpretation: Benchmarking is essential to assess the impact and validity of LLMs for medical applications. BenchmarkHub allows a fair and rigorous comparison of models across established datasets, including the possibility to upload their own datasets. The suite includes visual tools to ease model comparison and ranking without any programming knowledge. Self-hosted infrastructure that records every choice and parameter makes benchmark claims checkable without data leaving the institution.

articles.title: Bivariate Multiscale Sample Entropy of Frontoparietal-Subgenual ACC Dynamics in Depression During Accelerated TMS at 7 T
articles.abstract: Objective: To examine whether longitudinal changes in frontoparietal (FP) - subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) joint temporal complexity differ between sgACC hemispheres in patients undergoing accelerated TMS (aTMS) and untreated healthy controls. Methods: Twenty-four patients with current depressive episodes and fifteen healthy controls underwent 7T resting-state fMRI at baseline and follow-up. Patients received aTMS localized to the left DLPFC using Beam-F3. The same bilateral FP time series was paired separately with left and right sgACC time series. Bivariate multiscale sample entropy (bMSE) across scale factors a1-a10 was summarized by trapezoidal integration as a complexity index (bMSE-CI). The primary test was the Group x Time x sgACC Hemisphere interaction in a mixed repeated-measures ANOVA. Scale-specific interactions and clinical Spearman correlations were evaluated with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. Change scores were follow-up minus baseline. Results: The bMSE-CI Group x Time x Hemisphere interaction was significant (F(1,37) = 6.043, p = 0.0188, partial Eta squared = 0.140). Mean left/right bMSE-CI changes were -0.286/+0.124 in patients and +0.323/+0.112 in controls. Of ten scale-specific three-way interactions, only a2 survived FDR correction (q = 0.0435). No baseline or change-score bMSE-MADRS association survived the specified FDR corrections. A random-intercept-only mixed-model sensitivity analysis did not reach statistical significance for the three-way interaction (p = 0.0718). Conclusion: FP-sgACC joint temporal complexity showed hemisphere-dependent longitudinal differences between patients undergoing aTMS and healthy controls. These exploratory findings motivate further evaluation of bMSE as a candidate measure of longitudinal neural change in depression. Independent replication, more precise reliability estimates, and prospective validation of clinical relevance are needed.

articles.title: Cardiovascular and metabolic trajectories in men engaged in a multidimensional preventive care program: a prospective observational study
articles.abstract: Objectives: To describe within-individual changes in cardiometabolic, functional and neuroendocrine markers between two standardized evaluations in men engaged in a structured preventive care program, and to examine transitions across clinical risk categories. Design: Prospective observational cohort study using routinely collected data; paired within-individual analyses. Setting: Single preventive health center in Paris, France, offering a standardized multidisciplinary assessment with individualized lifestyle, supplementation and, when indicated, pharmacological recommendations. Participants: 279 men aged 18 years or older with a first evaluation (CU1) between October 2022 and November 2025 and a second evaluation (CU2) by May 2026 (32.3% of 865 eligible men); median interval 13.3 months (IQR 12.0 - 15.6). No exclusion criteria were applied. Primary and secondary outcome measures: Within-individual change in continuous markers (Hodges-Lehmann estimate, 95% CI; Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment over 36 tests) and transitions across fixed clinical thresholds (paired odds ratios). Results: Median age was 51.2 years, BMI 24.5 kg/m2 and SCORE2 2.9%. Visceral adipose tissue mass decreased (delta -49 g, 95% CI -80.5 to -18.5; q=0.006), with small decreases in body mass and fat mass. Handgrip strength increased (right +2.35 kg, 1.70 to 3.00; left +1.70 kg, 1.05 to 2.30; q<0.001). HDL cholesterol increased (+3.5 mg/dL, 2.5 to 4.5; q<0.001), with decreases in the triglyceride/HDL and total/HDL ratios. Blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, fasting glucose (after adjustment), insulin, HOMA-IR, SCORE2 and salivary cortisol and DHEA did not change. The proportion of men below the grip strength reference value decreased from 60.1% to 47.6% (paired OR 0.34, 0.19 to 0.61) and with HDL cholesterol superior to 46 mg/dL from 26.7% to 16.5% (OR 0.25, 0.12 to 0.54). Conclusions: In this selected, health-engaged population of men who completed both evaluations, changes in a favorable direction were observed for handgrip strength, HDL cholesterol and visceral adiposity, whereas blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, glycemic markers and SCORE2 were stable. Without a comparison group, these changes cannot be distinguished from regression to the mean, test retest effects or secular trends.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of bio-interventional cyclodialysis with one or multiple allogeneic reinforcements: a multicenter real-world evidence study
articles.abstract: Introduction: Bio-reinforced cyclodialysis uses an acellular scleral allograft spacer to maintain a surgically created cleft and enhance uveoscleral outflow. Surgeons may place one spacer or two, but whether the second adds IOP lowering has not been reported. We tested whether two spacers achieve greater 12-month IOP reduction than one, and whether any difference persists after adjustment for measured baseline differences. Methods: Observational analysis of 310 eyes in the prospective, multicenter CREST study undergoing combined phacoemulsification and bio-reinforced cyclodialysis with one spacer (n = 170) or two (n = 140). The primary endpoint was IOP change from baseline to month 12. Analyses comprised unadjusted comparison, baseline-adjusted regression, 1:1 propensity-score matching, doubly robust overlap weighting, and models accounting for enrolling site. IOP after a secondary IOP-lowering procedure was censored. Results: At baseline, IOP was 17.9 (4.4) versus 18.7 (5.8) mmHg and medications 1.19 (1.11) versus 1.46 (1.35), with one versus two spacers. The largest imbalance was enrolling site: one center contributed 43.6% of two-spacer eyes but 7.1% of one-spacer eyes. The unadjusted difference in IOP reduction was 2.52 mmHg (95% CI 1.20, 3.84; p<0.001), and persisted after propensity-score matching (2.36 mmHg; 0.94, 3.77; p=0.001) and overlap weighting (1.99 mmHg; 1.18, 2.79; p<0.001). After accounting for site it attenuated to 0.86 mmHg (-0.10 to 1.81; p=0.080), and to 0.42 mmHg (-0.61 to 1.45; p=0.42) within sites using both strategies. Medication reduction (-0.69 versus -0.62; p=0.64) and secondary IOP-lowering procedures (2.9% versus 2.9%; p=1.0) did not differ. Conclusion: Two-spacer treatment was associated with greater 12-month IOP reduction in unadjusted and patient-level adjusted analyses, but this association was substantially attenuated after accounting for enrolling site. These real-world data are compatible with, but do not establish, an independent incremental effect of a second spacer. A randomized comparison is required to determine whether spacer number independently influences IOP reduction.

articles.title: Design and Validation of a Compact Sensor for Peripheral Pulse Waveform Capture
articles.abstract: Peripheral pulse waveforms captured across different sites of the vascular tree provide valuable insights into cardiovascular health. This study presents a low-cost compact sensor designed to minimize intrusion at the measurement site while capturing the pulse waveform. The sensor performance was characterized and evaluated through both in-vitro benchtop experiments and a pilot in-vivo clinical study against invasive arterial pressure waveforms. The proposed sensor was able to capture pulse waveform morphology with reliable beat to beat tracking. Although offsets were present in the calculated features, fundamental temporal trends and cardiac cycle profiles were preserved. Thus, this work lays the foundation for a scalable hardware platform capable of multi-site pulse monitoring, enabling its integration with emerging computational frameworks for cardiovascular risk screening.

articles.title: Do Rule-Derived Labels Improve Prediction When Reported Labels Are Limited? A Two-Site Machine Learning Study
articles.abstract: **Background.** Rule derived (weak) labels can enlarge a training set when reported labels are scarce. Their value depends on label quality, on how the extra records shift the training distribution, and on whether the comparison accounts for reported labels set aside for tuning or calibration. **Methods.** We ran an exploratory label-budget experiment on *Escherichia coli* urine cultures from two de-identified electronic health record datasets: Stanford ARMD and UT Southwestern ARMD-UTSW. The task was to predict reported non-susceptibility to cefepime, cefoxitin and ceftazidime (Stanford) and to cefepime and ceftazidime (UT Southwestern). Reported-label budgets of 10%, 25%, 50% and 100% of development patients were drawn over five patient-disjoint outer splits. Logistic regression and histogram gradient boosting were trained with reported labels only, or with added rule-derived labels using equal weights, a tuning-selected weight, class-proportion adjustment or prior-probability correction. These were compared with an all-budget reported-only baseline that used every budgeted reported label for training. Stanford used the inferred labels released with the dataset and a feature set including resistance history. UT Southwestern used researcher-derived labels from Stanford rule text, which were not validated for that site, and an age-only primary model. Brier-score differences were assessed with paired patient-cluster bootstrap intervals. **Results.** All rule-derived labels were susceptible. Equal-weight augmentation lowered mean predicted risk well below observed prevalence (for example, Stanford cefepime at the 10% budget: 0.35% versus 4.85%) and had a higher Brier score than the all-budget baseline in every drug, model and budget summary. The tuning-selected weight did not consistently improve on the all-budget baseline. Its median Brier difference was positive in 38 of 40 drug, model and budget summaries. Its paired intervals lay above zero in 100 of 296 Stanford analyses and 31 of 198 UT Southwestern analyses, and below zero in 3 and 5. The tuning set often selected a weight of zero (146 of 296 and 153 of 198 analyses). At UT Southwestern, the age-only models showed little discrimination (median AUROC 0.49 to 0.54), so those comparisons mainly reflect calibration. **Conclusions.** Under these designs, rule-derived labels did not consistently improve probability prediction over a reported-only model that used the whole reported-label budget for training. Evaluations of weak supervision should include such a baseline and should report calibration as well as discrimination. **Keywords:** weak supervision; limited-label learning; label budget; probability calibration; class imbalance; antimicrobial resistance

articles.title: DxToniaNet: A Neural Network for Estimating the Severity of Leg Dystonia in Children with Cerebral Palsy
articles.abstract: Importance: Leg dystonia affects 50-80% of children with cerebral palsy (CP), but severity assessment remains subjective and time-consuming. Objective tools are urgently needed to quantify leg dystonia severity in clinical care and clinical trials. Objective: To develop and validate a deep neural network (DxToniaNet) for leg dystonia severity estimation using 2D clinical video recordings. Design, Setting, and Participants: We retrospectively analyzed video recordings of 298 children with cerebral palsy undergoing a seated hand open-close task as part of routine clinical care (Center 1: 193 videos, 720p/30fps; Center 2: 105 videos, 4K/60fps). Videos were rated for leg dystonia severity by a group of 7 experts using the Global Dystonia Rating Scale (GDRS) leg subscore (range 0-40) which has a minimum clinically important difference (MCID) of 4 points. Videos displaying leg dystonia (median expert GDRS score [≥]1) were used to develop and test a machine learning model (DxToniaNet) for estimating leg dystonia severity. Open-source software (OpenPose) estimated bilateral knee, ankle, and toe coordinates, normalized for height and camera positioning, and 69 variance and amplitude features were calculated based on established expert-cited features of leg dystonia. A neural network, DxToniaNet, was developed, trained and validated using 5-fold cross-validation on Center 1 videos before final testing on independent Center 2 videos. Main Outcome(s) and Measure(s): Mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and accuracy in differentiating between videos with clinically meaningful differences in GDRS scores were calculated relative to experts' median GDRS scores. Results: When estimating experts' leg GDRS scores in testing data, the proposed machine learning (ML) model yielded a MAE of 1.71 {+/-} 1.68 and RMSE of 2.21 {+/-} 0.34 (significantly less than the GDRS MCID of 4), and 90-94% accuracy in differentiating between videos with greater than a 4-point difference in the GDRS. Conclusions and Relevance: We have demonstrated that DxToniaNet can accurately estimate leg dystonia severity compared to experts' assessments with a small (clinically insignificant) error margin. Our methodology supports generalizability since DxToniaNet was developed and tested using independent videos datasets from different centers, recorded under different conditions. In the future, DxToniaNet may help facilitate standardized leg dystonia severity estimation in clinical care and clinical trials.

articles.title: Enrollees and Early Lessons from an Agentic Healthcare Platform with Physicians in the Loop
articles.abstract: Agentic healthcare platforms that combine large language models with physician oversight are growing quickly, but little is known about who uses them. We characterized 3,223 enrollees of Lotus AI, a free, physician-supervised agentic platform, who completed onboarding, messaged the agent, and had a linked health record between February and July 2026, and compared them with national benchmarks. Median age was 51 years and 62% were male. Chronic condition prevalence exceeded 2024 National Health Interview Survey estimates in every age band by 4 to 7 percentage points; 18% had a functional or symptom-defined disorder; among the 30% with four or more ambulatory visits in the prior year, care was spread across nearly five providers, with 44% meeting a threshold for high fragmentation. Users with functional disorders generated 1.8 times as many physician escalations and 2.6 times as many laboratory orders as other users, but no more prescriptions. This profile differs from the younger, predominantly female populations reported for direct-to-consumer telemedicine. It moves chronic disease management, functional disorder pathways, and care coordination from aspirations to design requirements, and we argue that deployed AI care platforms should characterize their populations against national benchmarks early.

articles.title: Epidemiology of zero-dose among children aged 12-35 months in Ethiopia: Burden, correlates and spatial patterns; Evidence from a 2025 national survey
articles.abstract: Background: Children who have not received the first dose of a diphtheria–tetanus–pertussis-containing vaccine are classified as zero-dose. Understanding how many children remain without this dose beyond infancy, the correlates, and their geographic distribution can inform routine and catch-up vaccination services in Ethiopia. This study aimed to estimate the burden of zero-dose, identify its correlates, and map its spatial distribution among children aged 12–35 months in Ethiopia. Methods: We analyzed data from 2,097 children aged 12–35 months in the Pathways for Ethiopia survey, a recent national population-based cross-sectional household survey conducted from August to November 2025. The burden estimates and regression analyses accounted for sampling weights, stratification, and clustering. Adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) were obtained through marginal standardization of survey-weighted logistic regression models. Spatial autocorrelation, hotspot, and spatial-scan analyses assessed geographic clustering. Ordinary kriging predicted prevalence at unsampled locations. Results: The weighted prevalence of zero-dose status was 20.6% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 15.9–26.3), with regional point estimates ranging from 0.8% in Addis Ababa to 35.9% in Somali. Its burden was 20.4% among children aged 12–23 months and 20.8% among those aged 24–35 months. Higher burden was associated with no antenatal care compared with four or more visits (aPR: 2.39; 95% CI: 1.61–3.53), unimproved compared with improved drinking-water sources (aPR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.18–1.97), and caregivers rating vaccination as less than very important compared with very important (aPR: 2.68; 95% CI: 2.03–3.54). Zero-dose prevalence showed significant spatial clustering (Moran’s I = 0.229; p = 0.0001). Hotspots occurred among sampled communities in Somali, Oromia, Central Ethiopia, Afar, and South Ethiopia. Predicted prevalence was highest across parts of eastern and south-central Ethiopia. Conclusion: Approximately one in five children aged 12–35 months had not received the first pentavalent dose. High zero-dose prevalence clustered among sampled communities in eastern and south-central Ethiopia. Moreover, antenatal care and drinking water source were independent factors. Immunization programs should prioritize these communities for identifying and vaccinating missed children, including those aged 24–35 months.

articles.title: Evidence availability for 1-year obesity treatment-initiation decisions: an estimand-aligned Bayesian longitudinal network meta-analysis
articles.abstract: Background Obesity pharmacotherapy strategies differ in maintenance dose, titration, and lifestyle support, but existing syntheses primarily compare drugs rather than treatment-initiation decisions. We assessed 1-year weight reduction, permanent discontinuation, and incremental dose-related trade-offs while mapping the availability of eligible trial evidence. Methods We searched eight databases and two trial registries through October 2026 for randomised trials (at least 12 weeks) of obesity pharmacotherapy initiation in adults with overweight or obesity. Maintenance, withdrawal, and switching trials were excluded. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data, and assessed bias and certainty. Bayesian longitudinal network meta-analysis estimated treatment-policy-compatible weight change at 52 weeks. Additional analyses examined discontinuation, dose escalation, titration, lifestyle support, and diabetes-related attenuation. The study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261532130). Findings We included 180 reports from 178 trials (196 randomisation units; 81,014 participants). Only 78 units reached the 1-year evidence layer, 50 informed the primary longitudinal model in adults without diabetes, and 45 of 160 target strategies had non-extrapolated 52-week estimates. Placebo-adjusted weight reductions were greatest with retatrutide 12 mg (-19.80 percentage points, 95% CrI -21.81 to -17.78), tirzepatide 15 mg (-16.87, -18.07 to -15.51), and cagrilintide-semaglutide 2.4/2.4 mg (-16.37, -18.10 to -14.70). Only tirzepatide 15 mg and semaglutide 2.4 mg had high-certainty evidence. Thirteen of 32 strategies increased adverse-event-related permanent discontinuation versus placebo; none increased all-cause discontinuation. Five of 22 adjacent dose steps had at least 0.80 probability of adding more than 2 percentage points of weight reduction. Eight 1-year titration contrasts and three trials of randomised lifestyle-support increments were identified. Weight reduction in adults with type 2 diabetes was 62% of that without diabetes (ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.58-0.66). Interpretation Evidence directly supporting 1-year obesity treatment-initiation decisions remains limited. Higher-dose and multi-receptor strategies achieve substantial weight reduction, but certainty and discontinuation trade-offs vary. Better treatment-policy reporting and randomised evidence on titration and lifestyle support are needed.

articles.title: Gene-based map of cardiovascular diseases
articles.abstract: Background: Rare coding variants contribute to cardiovascular disease, but their effects across disease groups remain incompletely characterized. In particular, the influence of functionally and clinically informed variant classification and sex-specific genetic effects on gene-phenotype associations remains understudied.
