Methods: We analyzed whole-genome sequencing data from up to 483,311 UK Biobank participants across six genetic ancestry groups and eight cardiovascular phenotype groups. Gene-burden testing integrated state-of-the-art missense classification and predicted pathogenic germline variants. We performed combined-sex and sex-stratified analyses, followed by cross-ancestry meta-analysis. We additionally adjusted for cardiometabolic traits in sensitivity analyses, estimated penetrance among qualifying-variant carriers, and assessed genetic prevalence across eight ancestry groups. Results: We identified 86 exome-wide significant gene-phenotype associations: 40 established and 46 novel. Novel associations included EHMT2 with atrial fibrillation, P2RX1 with arrhythmias, P2RY4 with complete atrioventricular block, and NOSTRIN with atherosclerotic heart disease in females. After cardiometabolic adjustment, 60 associations retained exome-wide significance and 18 additional associations emerged, including CDH11, PARVA, and ADAMDEC1 with atherosclerosis-related phenotypes. Conclusions: These findings identify novel cardiovascular gene-phenotype associations implicating purinergic signaling, endothelial nitric oxide regulation, and vascular wall biology. Variant selection shapes penetrance estimates and the interpretation of inherited susceptibility.

articles.title: Genomic diversity of respiratory pathogens in clinical versus community surveillance: a comparative analysis of SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza viruses in Washington State
articles.abstract: Background Genomic surveillance of respiratory viruses typically relies on sequences from individuals seeking health care, and whether these sequences represent the viruses circulating in the community is not well-characterized. We aimed to compare the diversity, proportion, and dynamics of influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 between clinical and community samples. Methods In this retrospective comparative genomic analysis, we used whole-genome sequences from community-based surveillance studies in the Seattle area, and clinical sequences from the Washington State Department of Health. We compared clade proportions and dynamics, sequence-cluster diversity, non-synonymous mutations, and Ct values between clinical and community samples. Findings We analyzed 538 RSV sequences collected between 2019 and 2021 (278 community, 260 clinical), 1506 influenza sequences (260 community, 1246 clinical) between 2019 and 2020, and 8660 SARS-CoV-2 sequences (5923 community, 2737 clinical) from 2020 to 2022. Clade proportions did not differ between clinical and community samples for RSV or influenza, but differed for SARS-CoV-2: clades 21J (Delta) and 21K (Omicron BA.1) were more frequent in community samples and clade 22B (Omicron BA.5) in clinical samples. SARS-CoV-2 clinical sequence clusters were more diverse than community clusters, whereas RSV and influenza showed no significant difference. Several spike mutations associated with monoclonal antibody resistance were more prevalent in community samples for SARS-CoV-2. Ct values were lower in clinical samples for multiple SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza clades. Interpretation Seasonal respiratory viruses had similar dynamics and diversity in clinical and community samples, whereas pandemic SARS-CoV-2 differed between settings. Genomic surveillance programs should combine clinical and community sampling, particularly during pandemics in order to better capture viral diversity.

articles.title: How inherited variation shapes human disease trajectories
articles.abstract: Although inherited variation is fixed at birth, its effects on health change with age and differ between common and rare variants. Here, we introduce Mendelnoulli, a longitudinal model that combines the age-dependent effects of polygenic and monogenic variation on health records, separating how much disease each individual accumulates overall from diseases to which they are prone. Mendelnoulli further allows polygenic and monogenic components to exert different influences on latent disease trajectories. We apply the model to 348 diseases, 36 polygenic scores, and 34 monogenic conditions across three biobanks and provide an atlas of the age-dependent effects of inherited variation on common human diseases. We show that polygenic effects change significantly with age, with Mendelnoulli improving held-out one-year discrimination for all 28 diseases tested compared with a model whose polygenic effects are constant over age (median AUC 0.95 vs 0.92). For individuals with no prior diagnoses, Mendelnoulli identified 8.6 more of every 100 new cases than that model, when each flagged the 5\% at highest risk. For genes with an established disease, Mendelnoulli selected that disease for 27 of 30 genes and ranked it first for 17 (7 expected by chance), and recovered known differences in timing, such as earlier breast cancer effects for BRCA1 than BRCA2 (peak 48 vs 66 years). Mendelnoulli provides a unified model of common and rare genetic influences on disease trajectories across the life course.

articles.title: Incidence of unruptured intracranial aneurysms: A nationwide population based longitudinal study
articles.abstract: Background: Understanding the epidemiology of unruptured intracranial aneurysm (UIAs) is crucial for risk stratification, clinical decision making, and public health planning. The aim of this study was to perform a nationwide population-based analysis to examine the incidence of unruptured intracranial aneurysms in Sweden. Methods: Data were obtained from the Swedish National Patient Register for all persons, aged 18 years and older, diagnosed with an intracranial aneurysm (ICD-10: I67.1) between the years 2000 and 2020. Crude incidence was calculated for the total population and age- and gender-stratified groups. Age standardized incidence was assessed using the European standard population. The incidence of intracranial aneurysms diagnosed with concurrent subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) was also examined. Results: During the study period, 8681 patients were diagnosed with UIA. The median age of diagnosis was 63 years and 65.1% were women. The age-standardized incidence increased approximately 74% % between 2000 and its peak: from 4.6 (95% CI: 4,26-4.95) per 100,000 in the year 2000 to 7.99 (95% CI: 6.7-7.54) per 100,000 in the year 2019. The increase in incidence of UIAs was most pronounced among women and those aged above 60. During the study period, the number of cases with SAH decreased slightly. Conclusions: The increasing incidence of UIAs in Sweden might be due improved clinical detection rates, demographic changes, and changes in the prevalence of risk factors. These findings highlight the importance of enhanced surveillance, effective risk stratification, and targeted public health strategies to address the growing burden of UIAs.

articles.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Advance Care Planning in Patients with Neurosurgical Conditions and Their Caregivers
articles.abstract: Introduction: Advance care planning (ACP) enables quality end-of-life (EOL) care that reflects patients' values and preferences. However, ACP remains limited among individuals with neurosurgical conditions -- such as stroke, glioma, or metastatic brain tumours -- who often experience rapid decline and short prognoses. When ACP discussions occur only after cognitive deterioration or acute events, opportunities for meaningful conversations are lost. This study aims to assess the baseline knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of ACP among neurosurgical patients and their caregivers in Singapore. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 30 patients with symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage (SICH) or brain tumours at the National University Hospital and their caregivers. Using validated ACP engagement questionnaires, we assessed participants' KAP, and readiness on 5-point Likert scales (1 lowest - 5 best), alongside nine ACP knowledge statements. Results: Patients demonstrated below-average ACP knowledge (mean = 4.1 / 9) and largely neutral attitudes (3.2 / 5) and perceptions (3.1 / 5). Misconceptions were common, including beliefs that ACP documents are legally binding, that preferred care cannot be delivered without ACP, and that ACP is solely a doctor's responsibility. Consequently, both patients and caregivers showed low levels of ACP engagement. Conclusion: The findings highlight the need to introduce ACP education and conversations earlier in the care journey, especially for individuals at risk of cerebrovascular or cardiovascular events. Early engagement, particularly among those with hypertension or other risk factors, presents a crucial window for preparing patients and families for future care decisions.

articles.title: Middle Temporal Gyrus Neurite Microstructure and Scam Susceptibility in Older Adults Without Dementia
articles.abstract: Background: Financial exploitation is a prevalent public health concern among older adults, and emerging evidence links vulnerability to gray matter macrostructure and white matter microstructure, including within brain regions and networks implicated in early Alzheimer's disease. Although diffusion tensor imaging is sensitive to age-related variation in brain microstructure, its scalar metrics cannot distinguish among the tissue properties contributing to observed differences. Neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI) models distinct tissue compartments, yielding estimates of neurite density, dendritic complexity, and extracellular free water. Methods: This study examined associations between scam susceptibility and NODDI metrics using ultra-high-field 7-Tesla imaging in 116 older adults without dementia. Neurite density index (NDI), orientation dispersion index (ODI), and free-water fraction were quantified within seven a priori regions of interest linked to early Alzheimer's disease. Multivariate regressions evaluated associations between scam susceptibility and NODDI metrics, adjusting for age, sex, education, and global cognition, with multiple comparison correction within each metric. For significant regions, post-hoc hierarchical regression models tested whether NODDI metrics explained variance beyond regional cortical thickness, total gray matter, and total intracranial volume. Results: Greater scam susceptibility was associated with higher NDI ({beta}=0.30, pFDR=.025) and lower ODI ({beta}=-0.28, pFDR=.044) in the middle temporal gyrus (MTG). No other regions survived correction. Additionally, MTG NDI and ODI explained variance beyond macrostructure measures. Conclusions: These findings identify NODDI metrics as novel microstructural correlates of scam susceptibility beyond macrostructure, supporting investigation of their relevance to financial vulnerability in older age.

articles.title: Monocyte-to-lymphocyte and Platelet-to-lymphocyte ratios in Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorders: systematic review and meta-analysis
articles.abstract: Background: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorders (NMOSD) are a group of neuroinflammatory conditions that affect the nervous system. MLR and PLR are simple inflammatory biomarkers and are studied in many autoimmune and demyelinating diseases. In this study, we investigate the available evidence to determine whether MLR and PLR are higher in NMOSD patients than in healthy subjects. Methods: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies measuring levels of PLR and/or MLR in both NMOSD patients and healthy controls were conducted. Mean difference (MD) and 95% confidence interval (CI) were used to measure the difference in levels of MLR and PLR between patients and healthy subjects. Results: For MLR, the main meta-analysis yielded a pooled MD of 0.125 [-0.114; 0.363]. I2 was 83.8%. Subgroup meta-analysis of age- and sex-matched studies, demonstrated a pooled MD of 0.066 [0.012; 0.12]. For PLR, meta-analysis revealed a pooled MD of 23.99 [6.03; 41.96]. I2 was 82.3%. Subgroup analysis for age- and sex-matched studies for PLR, showed a pooled MD of 14 [-19.68; 47.68]. Conclusion: The main analysis suggests that MLR is not higher in NMOSD patients than in healthy controls. However, subgroup analysis of age- and sex-matched studies and leave-one-out analysis excluding the outlier study showed a statistically significant MLR increase in patients. PLR was found to exhibit a modest increase in NMOSD patients compared with healthy controls. Nonetheless, subgroup analysis of age- and sex-matched studies showed a statistically non-significant increase. Results should be interpreted cautiously. The available evidence is inconsistent and further research is needed.

articles.title: Ontology-Based SEA-CDM Integration for Vaccine Clinical Trials: Query, Similarity, and Design Recommendation
articles.abstract: ClinicalTrials.gov provides valuable information for vaccine research, but fragmented data structures and inconsistent vaccine naming complicate systematic cross-trial analysis. The Study-ExperimentAssay Common Data Model (SEA-CDM) provides a standardized structure for biomedical study data, while biomedical ontologies supply semantic relationships among concepts. We extracted 9,147 vaccinerelated study records from the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT) database, mapped their records into SEA-CDM, and linked vaccine products and reported adverse events (AEs) to the Vaccine Ontology (VO) and Ontology of Adverse Events (OAE), respectively. Building on the existing Ontology-based SEA Network (OSEAN), we organized the integrated data into relational tables and a Neo4j knowledge graph while retaining links to original registrations. We evaluated three applications to assess semantic trial retrieval, context-aware AE ranking and trial similarity, and trial design recommendation. First, VO-based query expansion retrieved 41 candidate RNA vaccine trials compared with 16 using exact VO identifier matching. Second, a context-aware AE ranking model incorporating SEA-CDM features and VO-derived vaccine families improved recall@10 from 0.317 to 0.383 over a frequency-based baseline. TransE and CompGCN embeddings achieved Hits@10 of 0.950 and 0.946, respectively, for retrieving trials sharing the same VO identifier within disease-specific candidate sets. Third, an ontology-based clinical trial design recommendation model was developed using several machine learning methods under leave-one-Material-out evaluation across 23 vaccine classes, although performance varied across classes. These findings demonstrate how structural and semantic integration can support multiple clinical trial analyses using vaccine studies as a case study. This framework provides a foundation for extending ontology-supported data integration and analysis to other clinical research domains.

articles.title: Oxygen Uptake Efficiency Slope (OUES) and Mortality in Chronic Heart Failure: Comparisons of Absolute and Percent-predicted Values across Different Equations
articles.abstract: Aim: The oxygen uptake efficiency slope (OUES) is a prognostic indicator obtained from cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPX) in chronic heart failure (CHF) patients. Although various equations exist for calculating predicted OUES, it remains unclear whether absolute or percent-predicted values offer a more accurate prognostic assessment. To investigate and compare mortality prediction in CHF patients using the OUES absolute values or the percent-predicted approach, incorporating the equations of Hollenberg, Buys, and Milani. Methods: Retrospective cohort study involving CHF patients evaluated at a tertiary university hospital between July 2013 and July 2023. All patients underwent maximal CPX and were followed in a specialized outpatient clinic. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. To compare the prognostic accuracy between different approaches, we performed receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression. Results: A total of 1.180 patients were included, 57% male, with a mean age of 55 {+/-} 12 years. The median follow-up was 5.0 years (IQR 3.0 to 7.2 years), resulting in 147 deaths (12.5%). The area under de curve (AUC) was 0.71 to 0.72 for males, and 0.60 to 0.63 for females, without statistical difference in the AUC between absolute and percent-predicted OUES. Different cut-offs were identified for each sex for predicting mortality and all OUES metrics remained independent predictors in multivariate models using sex and age. Conclusions: OUES, in both absolute and percent-predicted forms, demonstrated similar accuracy in predicting mortality in CHF, with sex-specific cut-offs influencing clinical assessment.

articles.title: PSEN1 loss-of-function variants do not cause early-onset Alzheimer's disease
articles.abstract: PSEN1 variants are the most common cause of familial early-onset Alzheimer's disease (EOAD), but it is debated whether they act through a loss- or gain-of-function. Following a recent report of a duo with EOAD carrying a predicted loss-of-function (LoF) stop-gain variant (p.K109*) in PSEN1 , we sought to determine whether PSEN1 LoF variants, as a class, cause EOAD. We identified 45 carriers of PSEN1 LoF variants predicted to trigger nonsense-mediated decay in the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project, UK Biobank, and BioVU databases. None of these carriers had a recorded case of early-onset dementia, and 17 were older than 65 years at last follow-up with no dementia or AD reported. Re-analysis of the reported AD-associated variant p.K109* revealed a cryptic splice site predicted to produce an in-frame deletion of 5 amino acids (p.K109_L113del). These results suggest that PSEN1 variants must produce an altered PSEN1 protein product to cause EOAD, while true null LoF PSEN1 alleles do not cause EOAD.

articles.title: Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Incidence During and After COVID-19 Social Distancing in Korea: A Nationwide 16-Year Interrupted Time-Series Analysis
articles.abstract: Background Pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a rare but devastating event. However, the extent to which large-scale public health interventions, such as COVID-19 social distancing policies, affected the incidence of pediatric OHCA remains unclear. Methods We conducted a nationwide interrupted time-series analysis using data from the Korea Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Registry (2008-2023). The primary outcome was the monthly incidence of OHCA among individuals aged 0-18 years. The study period was divided into three phases: pre-intervention (January 2008-February 2020), social distancing (March 2020-April 2022), and post-lifting (May 2022-December 2023). We used segmented Poisson regression, adjusted for population size and seasonal variation, to estimate changes in monthly incidence at each policy change and reported the results as incidence rate ratios (IRRs). To determine whether these changes differed by age, we compared children with adults (19-64 years) and elderly individuals ([≥]65 years). Results Of the 456,839 registry entries, 10,965 were pediatric OHCAs, of which 6,891 underwent resuscitation in the emergency department. The crude incidence was 7.04, 7.14, and 8.35 per 100,000 person-years in the three phases, respectively. Before the pandemic, incidence rose slightly (annual IRR 1.006 [95% CI 1.001-1.012]; P = 0.032). At the implementation of social distancing, incidence fell immediately (IRR 0.926 [95% CI 0.865-0.991]; P = 0.027), without a significant change in slope (P = 0.081). After restrictions were lifted, incidence rose immediately (IRR 1.138 [95% CI 1.048-1.235]; P = 0.002) and then declined gradually (monthly IRR 0.993 [95% CI 0.988-0.999]; P = 0.023). These changes were confined to children aged 1-11 years (implementation IRR 0.812 [95% CI 0.666-0.991]; post-lifting IRR 1.562 [95% CI 1.278-1.909]). The pattern of change differed significantly by age group (P < 0.001), mainly because incidence rose in children, but not in adults or elderly individuals, after restrictions were lifted. Conclusions Nationwide social distancing was associated with a transient decrease in pediatric OHCA incidence, which was concentrated among children aged 1-11 years and was followed by a rebound above the expected level after restrictions were lifted. Surveillance of pediatric OHCA should account for abrupt changes in children's daily environments, including the closure and reopening of schools and childcare facilities.

articles.title: Physical and psychosocial outcomes in children with limb loss 2-years after the 2023 Kahramanmaras-Türkiye earthquakes
articles.abstract: Introduction: The 2023 Kahramanmaras-Turkiye earthquakes resulted in many paediatric amputations. While prosthetic provision following disasters has been described, little is known about longer-term physical and psychosocial outcomes in children with earthquake-related limb loss. Aim: Evaluate health-related quality of life, prosthesis experience, pain, and function approximately two years post-amputation. Method: Retrospective analysis was conducted of children with earthquake-related limb loss who attend the XXX Center. Socio-demographic and amputation-related data, psychological status, outcome scores for pain, the Paediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL) and the Trinity Amputation and Prosthesis Experience Scales (TAPES) were included. Results: Fifty-six children (50% female; 13.7{+/-}5.0 years old) were included. Children had unilateral upper limb loss (n=15), unilateral lower limb loss (n=31), bilateral lower limb loss (n=7), or combined upper and lower limb loss (n=3). Data were obtained 2.3{+/-}0.4 years following amputation. Median child-reported PedsQL scores were 72.3/100.0, with high social functioning (85.0/100.0) but lower emotional functioning (60.0/100.0). No differences in PedsQL outcomes were found between limb loss groups. Children rated their physical and emotional quality of life higher than carers rated them. TAPES median scores were 50.0/75.0 for psychosocial adjustment, 16.0/36.0 for activity restriction, and 34.5/45.0 for prosthetic satisfaction. Children with unilateral lower limb loss demonstrated superior adjustment and prosthetic satisfaction than children with unilateral upper limb or bilateral lower limb loss (p<0.05). Conclusions: Children demonstrated favourable physical, social, and school-related quality of life 2.3 years after the earthquakes. However, emotional wellbeing remained affected, highlighting the importance of long-term mental health support alongside prosthetic and rehabilitation services.

articles.title: Pneumococcal nasopharyngeal carriage in children 2-60 months of age in Novi Sad (Serbia), October 2022-September 2026
articles.abstract: Background: Streptococcus pneumoniae nasopharyngeal carriage in young children is an important source of transmission and may precede pneumococcal disease. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines can alter circulating serotypes. Continued surveillance is needed to monitor serotype replacement, vaccine serotype coverage, and antimicrobial resistance. Methods: A prospective surveillance study was conducted in outpatient pediatric practices from October 2022 to September 2026 among children aged 2-60 months in Novi Sad, Serbia. Healthy children attending preventive visits and children with acute respiratory tract infections were enrolled. Nasopharyngeal specimens were collected and cultured for S. pneumoniae. Participant-level analyses used the first eligible specimen per child, while isolate-level analyses included all recovered isolates. Serotyping and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed. Theoretical vaccine serotype coverage was estimated for licensed and selected investigational pneumococcal conjugate vaccines, with 23-valent polysaccharide vaccine evaluated separately. Results: Among 3,373 included children, 911 were pneumococcal carriers, giving an overall carriage prevalence of 27.0%. Carriage was higher among children with acute respiratory tract infection than among healthy children and was also associated with daycare attendance, chronic medical conditions, age, season, and surveillance year. In total, 1,312 pneumococcal isolates were recovered, of which 87.9% were typeable. The most frequent serotypes included 11A, 10A, 15A, 15B, 23A, 23B, 19A, and 6B. Theoretical serotype coverage was 8.2% for PCV10, 17.5% for PCV13, 20.0% for PCV15, and 47.3% for PCV20. More than half of typeable isolates were non-PCV20 serotypes. Resistance was most frequent to erythromycin, clindamycin, and tetracycline, while multidrug resistance was observed in 18.1% of isolates. Penicillin G non-susceptibility was uncommon. Conclusion: Pneumococcal carriage in children aged 2-60 months in Novi Sad was associated with age, clinical presentation, season, and surveillance year and involved diverse serotypes. Continued carriage surveillance, linked with invasive-disease and antibiotic-use data, would help determine whether the observed serotype and resistance patterns persist.

articles.title: Prevalence and biochemical patterns of thyroid dysfunction among children and young adults with Type 1 Diabetes in Kenya: A multicenter cross-sectional study
articles.abstract: Background: Thyroid dysfunction is a common endocrine comorbidity in type 1 diabetes (T1D), yet most evidence on its burden and biochemical patterns comes from higher-income settings. Data among African children and young adults with T1D remain limited. Objective: To determine the prevalence and pattern of thyroid dysfunction and examine demographic and diabetes-related factors associated with thyroid dysfunction among children and young adults with T1D in Kenya. Methods: We conducted a multicentre cross-sectional study among children and young adults with T1D aged [≤]34 years attending four diabetes clinics in Kenya. Serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and free thyroxine (FT4) were measured. Thyroid status was classified as euthyroidism (normal TSH and FT4), subclinical hypothyroidism (elevated TSH with normal FT4), overt hypothyroidism (elevated TSH with low FT4), subclinical hyperthyroidism (low TSH with normal FT4), overt hyperthyroidism (low TSH with elevated FT4), or discordant TSH-FT4 profiles that did not meet these predefined biochemical categories. Prevalence estimates with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated, and multivariable logistic regression examined associations with age, sex and duration of diabetes. Results: Among 244 participants with paired TSH and FT4 measurements, 77.5% (n=189) were euthyroid. Twenty-seven participants (11.1%; 95% CI 7.7-15.6%) had biochemically defined thyroid dysfunction: 18 (7.4%) had subclinical hypothyroidism, 5 (2.0%) overt hypothyroidism, and 4 (1.6%) subclinical hyperthyroidism. No overt hyperthyroidism was identified. An additional 28 participants (11.5%) had discordant TSH-FT4 profiles. Hypothyroidism accounted for 85.2% of biochemically defined thyroid dysfunction and was predominantly subclinical (78.3%). Age, sex and duration of diabetes were not significantly associated with thyroid dysfunction in adjusted analyses. Conclusion: Thyroid dysfunction affected approximately one in nine Kenyan children and young adults with T1D and was predominantly hypothyroid, particularly subclinical hypothyroidism. Discordant TSH-FT4 profiles were also frequent, underscoring the importance of careful biochemical classification and confirmation of abnormal thyroid-function tests.

articles.title: Prevalence and risk factors for human papillomavirus infection among women living with HIV in Sierra Leone: A cross-sectional study
articles.abstract: BackgroundCervical cancer, a malignancy affecting the cervix, is the fourth most common cancer and cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide. This burden disproportionately affects low-resource regions, where approximately 90% of cases occur. HIV-positive women are at high risk of persistent Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection and cervical cancer, but screening for this cancer is not yet integrated into HIV care in Sierra Leone. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and risk factors of high-risk HPV infection among women living with HIV (WLHIV) attending Connaught Hospital in Sierra Leone. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study of women living with HIV aged 25-65 years attending the HIV clinic at Connaught Teaching Hospital in Freetown between September and December 2024. Endocervical swabs were collected for HPV DNA testing. Data was analyzed using R (v4.4.0). Logistic regression analysis was used to determine the independent risk factors for HPV positivity. Results A total of 191 WLHIV were enrolled. The mean age was 36.8 years; 44.5% were single, and 67% were employed. High-risk HPV DNA was detected in 60 (31.4%) (95% CI 25.3%-38.3%) participants, with 50% (30/60) having multiple serotypes. The most common genotype was HPV 52, followed by 16 and 51. Only 30% of HPV-positive women had genotypes 16 or 18, targeted by the bivalent vaccine. On multivariable analysis, former contraceptive use was independently associated with increased HPV positivity (aOR=4.86, 95% CI: 1.65-17.37, p = 0.0032). Conclusion The high prevalence of high-risk HPV infection and predominance of non 16/18 genotypes among WLHIV in Sierra Leone underscore the need to integrate HPV screening within HIV services and consider broader HPV vaccine coverage in Sierra Leone. Former contraceptive use is an independent predictor of HPV positivity, emphasizing the need for robust screening strategies in women using contraceptives.

articles.title: Prevalence of Self-Reported Auditory Dysfunction Among Call Center Employees and Its Association with Shift Work Across Various Call Centers in Cairo, Egypt, March 2026
articles.abstract: Background The rapid, unregulated expansion of the call center industry in developing countries has increased occupational health risks for young adults, particularly with regard to auditory health. Prolonged exposure to acoustic trauma, long working hours, and the high intensity nature of call center work can negatively affect young adults at the start of their working lives and may contribute to permanent noise induced hearing loss (NIHL). This damage is often irreversible but preventable if identified at an early stage. This study aims to evaluate the burden of auditory impairment among call center employees in Egypt and to propose evidence based mitigation strategies. Methods A pilot cross sectional study was conducted among employees of various medical call centers over approximately three months (January to March 2026). Participants were recruited through voluntary (self selected) sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire on work history, and statistical analysis was performed to examine associations with work duration and intensity. Three semi structured, open ended interviews were conducted in March 2026 to explore the symptoms in greater depth. Results Forty six call center employees completed the questionnaire. The most frequently reported symptoms were mishearing words (82.6%), difficulty understanding speech in background noise (80.4%), needing others to repeat themselves (78.3%), and sensitivity to loud sounds (78.3%); 60.9% reported tinnitus. Higher auditory symptom severity was associated with a history of acoustic shock (Mann Whitney U = 344.0, p = .004) and with greater cognitive symptom burden (Spearman's {rho} = .416, p = .004), but not significantly with shift type (p = .177), years of work (p = .885), or daily and weekly working hours. Qualitative interviews described auditory strain that builds through the shift, disrupted sleep, informal coping, and the absence of employer guidance or symptom reporting pathways. Conclusion and Recommendations Self reported auditory symptoms were common in this preliminary sample of call center employees and were associated with acoustic shock exposure and cognitive symptom burden, but not significantly with shift pattern or length of service. Because the study was cross sectional, relied on self reports, and used a small volunteer sample (pilot study), the findings cannot establish causation or true prevalence. Recommended measures include acoustic shock limiters with incident reporting, audiometric screening that prioritizes at risk employees, safe volume education with regular breaks, and educational programs on auditory hazards and early warning signs to prevent actual auditory damage. Larger multi site studies with audiometric confirmation are also needed. Keywords: noise induced hearing loss; call center employees; occupational health; auditory dysfunction; tinnitus; acoustic shock; shift work; Egypt

articles.title: Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan for the Hyperangulated versus Standard Geometry Laryngoscope Blade (ANGLE) Trial
articles.abstract: Background: Emergency tracheal intubation is common and high risk. Although guidelines recommend using a video laryngoscope to intubate critically ill adults, whether a hyperangulated or standard-geometry blade is more likely to achieve successful intubation on the first attempt remains unknown. Research Question: Does the use of a video laryngoscope with a hyperangulated blade increase the incidence of successful intubation on the first attempt among adults undergoing emergency tracheal intubation, compared to use of a video laryngoscope with a standard-geometry blade? Study Design and Methods: The HyperANgulated versus Standard Geometry Laryngoscope BladE (ANGLE) trial is a pragmatic, multicenter, unblinded, parallel-group, randomized trial being conducted in 28 sites (10 emergency departments and 18 intensive care units) in the United States. The trial compares use of a video laryngoscope with a hyperangulated blade versus a standard-geometry blade among 2,500 critically ill adults undergoing emergency tracheal intubation. The primary outcome is successful intubation on the first attempt. The secondary outcome is the incidence of hypoxemia during intubation. Enrollment began on December 30, 2025, and is expected to conclude in 2027. Interpretation: The ANGLE trial will provide important data on the effects of the use of a video laryngoscope with a hyperangulated blade versus standard-geometry blade on successful intubation on the first attempt and other outcomes of emergency tracheal intubation. Specifying the protocol and statistical analysis plan before the conclusion of enrollment increases the rigor, reproducibility, and transparency of the trial. Trial Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov; No.: NCT07223762 ; URL: www.clinicaltrials.gov

articles.title: Quasi-experimental evaluation of a social media campaign to promote HPV vaccination in Bauchi state, Nigeria
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer is the leading cause of cancer death in women in 26 countries, including in sub-Saharan African countries. Cervical and other cancer risks can be greatly reduced through timely HPV vaccination and early screening. But it continues to pose a significant public health challenge in LMICs such as Nigeria. This study reports on the implementation and evaluation of a pair of social media behavior change campaigns to increase HPV vaccination amongst girls ages 9-14 and reduce vaccine hesitancy amongst girls and their parents in Bauchi state, Nigeria. The primary objectives are to conduct a quasi-experimental evaluation of the social media campaign; to examine the effect of higher versus lower levels of campaign exposure on HPV vaccination and related outcomes; to determine whether the social media campaign followed its planned theory of change; and to identify which social media messages were most effective in promoting HPV vaccination. We implemented an HPV vaccination social media promotion campaign, using videos designed to encourage parents to vaccinate their daughters, at scale in Bauchi state on the Meta and TikTok social media platforms. We used a quasi-experimental design, a heavy-up approach, that experimentally manipulated the level of social media content delivered in Bauchi. We used the Virtual Lab platform, an open-source platform that uses social media to recruit participants using advertising and creates panels of respondents for data collection through an online survey, and also collected social media metrics including impressions and engagement. The campaign was effective in increasing HPV vaccination rates from 69% at baseline to 86% at endline over 2 campaign phases that spanned approximately 3 months. Based on GEE modeling, we found that higher levels of engagement with the campaign were associated with higher vaccination rates at midline and endline. Pro-vaccine attitudes and reduced vaccine hesitancy also predicted higher vaccination rates. Also, the campaign produced additional HPV vaccinations at low cost: Adjusted for campaign exposure cost of $0.81 per additional vax in campaign phase 1, $2.10 per vax in phase 2, and $2.40 for the total campaign period. Evidence from this study indicates that social media may be an effective strategy to promote HPV vaccination at low cost. Future rigorous trials using experimental methods are needed to further evaluate social media to promote HPV vaccination.

articles.title: Reliability-Aware Clinical Relation Learning for Uncertainty-Robust Multi-Label Chest X-ray Classification
articles.abstract: Background: Automated multi-label classification of chest radiographs is complicated by overlapping imaging findings, noisy report-derived labels, and changes in disease co-occurrence across clinical settings. Existing clinical-hierarchy methods can encode label relationships, but a rigid hierarchy may conflate categorical membership with empirical association and propagate annotation errors. Methods: We investigated Reliability-Aware Clinical Relation Learning (ReCaRL), a graph-assisted framework for multi-label chest radiograph classification. An image encoder produces initial finding scores, while a graph constructed from training-label associations provides reliability-weighted, confidence-gated updates. Uncertain annotations are handled with observation masks. The evaluation compares flat, weighted, graph-based, and hierarchy-penalty baselines, with internal and external discrimination and calibration assessments. Results: In the internal evaluation, ReCaRL achieved macro AUROC 0.821 and macro AUPRC 0.437, compared with 0.812 and 0.423 for the masked/weighted baseline. Mean AUROC across five common findings was 0.865 versus 0.858. External testing yielded AUROC 0.799 and AUPRC 0.409. Post-hoc calibration reduced the internal Brier score from 0.113 to 0.102 and the external expected calibration error from 0.082 to 0.061, without changing AUROC or AUPRC. Conclusions: Reliability-aware graph propagation and confidence gating were associated with modest improvements in multi-label chest radiograph classification relative to the matched masked/weighted baseline. Post-hoc calibration improved probability reliability in the reported evaluations. The findings do not establish a benefit in prospective clinical decision-making.

articles.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Stage 5 Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Cardiovascular and Kidney Outcomes
articles.abstract: **Background:** Evidence supporting sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use in stage 5 chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains limited because major randomized trials have largely excluded this population. We evaluated associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in patients with stage 5 CKD. **Methods:** We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Google Scholar through April 10, 2026. Studies comparing SGLT2 inhibitors with nonuse or other glucose-lowering therapies were eligible. Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled using random-effects models, and risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. **Results:** Five observational cohorts met inclusion criteria, of which three contributed to the meta-analysis, comprising 57,156 participants, including 28,559 SGLT2 inhibitor users. SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with fewer heart failure hospitalizations (HR 0.78; 95% CI 0.72-0.85) and acute myocardial infarctions (HR 0.64; 95% CI 0.56-0.72). Associations with all-cause mortality (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.58-1.21) and dialysis initiation (HR 0.63; 95% CI 0.30-1.33) were not statistically significant. In analyses restricted to treatment-initiation cohorts, the association with fewer heart failure hospitalizations persisted, whereas the myocardial infarction association was no longer significant. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across outcomes. **Conclusions:** Observational evidence suggests potential cardiovascular benefits of SGLT2 inhibitors in stage 5 CKD, particularly fewer heart failure hospitalizations. Effects on mortality, dialysis initiation, and myocardial infarction remain uncertain. Dedicated randomized trials are needed to establish efficacy and safety in this population.

articles.title: Socioeconomic Position, Kidney Outcomes, and Mortality: A Longitudinal Cohort Study from the All of Us Research Program
articles.abstract: Background: Socioeconomic position is associated with kidney disease, but it remains unclear whether these differences are greater for worsening kidney function than for a first recorded diagnosis. We examined how household income, education, and neighborhood deprivation relate to mortality and kidney outcomes. Methods and findings: We conducted a retrospective cohort study involving 218,098 individuals using data from the All of Us Research Program, with follow-up to January 1, 2025. Primary outcomes involved all-cause mortality and sustained 40% estimated glomerular filtration rate decline. Secondary outcomes were incident recorded chronic kidney disease (CKD) diagnosis, incident recorded CKD category G3a or worse, and kidney failure. We also evaluated income inequalities and estimated standardized 3-year mortality risks for each baseline kidney state. Median follow-up was 3.62 years for mortality and 2.76 years for kidney outcomes. Among 218,098 individuals, 4,777 deaths, 6,423 sustained declines, 7,870 incident recorded chronic kidney disease diagnoses, 4,716 incident category G3a-or-worse events, and 1,799 kidney failure events were observed. Adjusted hazard ratios (95% CIs) for household income below $25,000 compared with $200,000 or more were 2.68 (2.31-3.12), 3.57 (3.08-4.13), 2.13 (1.90-2.38), 2.15 (1.86-2.49), and 3.08 (2.30-4.11), respectively. Relative index of inequality estimates were approximately twice as large for sustained decline and kidney failure than for recorded CKD diagnosis. Within baseline kidney states, standardized 3-year absolute mortality differences by income did not differ significantly across states. The main limitations are the observational design, baseline creatinine measured up to a year after the survey, and outcome ascertainment from health records that may differ by income. Conclusions: Lower income was associated with higher mortality and greater risk of all kidney outcomes. Education and neighborhood deprivation showed different patterns of association, which supports considering individual and neighborhood circumstances together.

articles.title: Socioeconomic position, socioenvironmental conditions, and subjective cognitive decline among midlife and older LGBTQIA+ adults in California
articles.abstract: Objectives: To examine which measure of socioeconomic position and socioenvironmental conditions has the strongest relationship with subjective cognitive decline (SCD) among midlife and older lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, asexual, and other sexual and gender minority (LGBTQIA+) adults. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 3869 LGBTQIA+ adults aged 50 years or older participating in a community-engaged survey in California. Using logistic regression, we examined overall associations between each indicator of socioeconomic position and socioenvironmental conditions and SCD. We used a dominance analysis to assess the relative importance of each indicator based on the proportion of variance in SCD it explained. Results: Overall, 14.7% of the sample reported SCD. Midlife and older LGBTQIA+ adults in a lower socioeconomic position (i.e., lower education, unemployment, lower household income, fewer assets, financial insecurity, food insecurity, and unstable housing) had higher odds of SCD than those in a higher position, with significant odds ratios (OR) ranging from 1.44 to 1.93. In contrast, perceiving one's community as safe for LGBTQIA+ people was associated with lower odds of SCD (OR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.48, 0.76). Dominance analysis indicated that household assets was the most important factor, explaining 2.8% of the variance in SCD (95% CI 2.2%, 3.6%), followed by household income (1.9%; 95% CI 1.2%, 2.7%) and perceived community safety (1.6%; 95% CI 1.1%, 2.3%). Discussion: Supporting the cognitive health of LGBTQIA+ people may require attention to both financial security across the life course and the broader social environments.

articles.title: The contribution of Neanderthal ancestry to cancer risk
articles.abstract: Modern human genomes harbor DNA inherited from interbreeding with Neanderthals. Genetic variants inherited from Neanderthals associate with variation in many immune and metabolic phenotypes, two systems with direct relevance to cancer. However, the influence of Neanderthal variants on germline cancer risk has not been comprehensively evaluated. Here, we evaluated genome-wide association study (GWAS) hits for 17 cancer types for Neanderthal ancestry. Twelve cancers have multiple Neanderthal alleles significantly associated with variation in risk. Next, we fine-mapped these risk loci and identified 32 associations across seven cancers where Neanderthal variants are likely causal (>= posterior inclusion probability). Fine-mapped loci include Neanderthal alleles that both increase and decrease cancer risk. Nine of the 32 Neanderthal associations, including the high frequency BNC2 Neanderthal variants, have signatures of adaptive introgression, and several suggest evidence of both mediated and antagonistic pleiotropy. Finally, we tested for enrichment of cancer heritability in genomic regions with Neanderthal ancestry. As expected, Neanderthal variants are depleted of heritability for most cancers. However, Neanderthal variants were enriched for heritability in breast cancer GWAS in both East Asian and Europeans, and this enrichment replicated using individual-level UK Biobank data. These results suggest that Neanderthal alleles that influence germline cancer risk were largely selected against. However, introgressed Neanderthal variants implicated in many cancers persist, potentially due to adaptive pleiotropic effects. This evolutionary perspective provides new insights into the complex evolution and etiology of cancer risk among modern human populations.

articles.title: The phenomic landscape of rare gain- and loss-of-function variation
articles.abstract: Current large-scale phenome-wide association studies do not distinguish between genetic variants with distinct functional consequences, despite evidence that gain-of-function (GoF) and loss-of-function (LoF) variants can produce different phenotypes. Consequently, the phenotypic consequences of variants stratified by predicted GoF and LoF effects have not been systematically characterized at scale. Here, we systematically analyzed rare predicted GoF and LoF variants in 18,214 genes across 1,244 binary and 202 quantitative traits using whole-exome sequencing and electronic health records from the Mount Sinai Million Health Discoveries Program, a phenotypically rich hospital-based biobank comprised of 50,067 participants, primarily representing African, Admixed American and European ancestries. We identified numerous established and previously unreported ancestry-specific and shared gene- and variant-level associations, many of which were supported by complementary evidence from both diagnostic phenotypes and clinical measurements. Proteomic evaluation of the previously unreported association between VNN1 LoF variants and body mass index in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis revealed reduced circulating vanin-1 levels with LoF variants, which in turn were associated with body composition and additional cardiometabolic phenotypes. Functional stratification of predicted GoF and LoF variants revealed gene-trait associations that were attenuated when these variants were combined, demonstrating that traditional aggregation of variants with different functional effects can obscure association signals. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating predicted functional consequences into association analyses and establish a comprehensive resource linking exome-wide predicted GoF and LoF variants to the human phenome across ancestry-specific and multi-ancestry analyses.

articles.title: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Risk of Colorectal Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
articles.abstract: Epidemiologic studies suggest that type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with an increased risk of colorectal cancer (CRC). However, prior meta-analyses have relied heavily on studies published more than a decade ago and have often combined distinct epidemiologic effect measures. We conducted an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies published from January 2012 through January 2026 evaluating the association between T2DM and incident CRC. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched, and eligible studies reporting associations between T2DM and CRC were included. Effect estimates were synthesized separately using random-effects models to calculate pooled estimates with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sex-specific and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were also conducted. Fourteen studies were included, comprising nine cohort and five case-control studies; six reported odds ratios (ORs), seven reported hazard ratios (HRs), and one reported a standardized incidence ratio (SIR). T2DM was associated with higher odds of incident CRC (OR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.13-1.46) and a higher hazard of incident CRC (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.23-1.31). The study reporting an SIR also showed higher CRC incidence among individuals with T2DM (SIR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.39-1.45). Sex-specific analyses generally showed positive associations in both females and males, and sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the pooled findings. Overall, T2DM was associated with an increased risk of incident CRC, with a consistent direction of association across distinct epidemiologic effect measures. These findings provide updated evidence supporting consideration of T2DM as a marker of increased CRC risk and may inform CRC prevention strategies among individuals with T2DM.

articles.title: Unraveling the Lifespan Trajectory of White Matter Hypointensity on T1-weighted MR Images and Clinical Application in Various Brain Disorders
articles.abstract: White matter hypointensity on T1-weighted MRI (T1-WMHypo), a putative marker of white matter pathophysiological changes, has been less systematically investigated than the widely studied T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (T2-FLAIR) hyperintensity lesions. Here, we built the lifespan normative reference and assessed the clinical significance of T1-WMHypo across various brain disorders using a large multicenter dataset. We first established lifespan normative reference for T1-WMHypo volume by 34,148 healthy individuals (aged 4-85 years). Then, in 7,587 patients across 21 neurological and psychiatric disorders, normative reference-derived deviations revealed disease-specific patterns, with marked deviations in neurological diseases. Deviations of T1-WMHypo volume contributed to differential diagnosis, larger deviations correlated with brain atrophy, cognitive impairment, and poorer outcomes in various brain disorders. Elevated burden of T1-WMHypo volume predicted poor medication response in Parkinson's disease and accelerated disability progression in multiple sclerosis. These associations persisted after adjusting for conventional T2-FLAIR hyperintensity lesions. T1-WMHypo deviations provide an individualized marker of white matter pathophysiological changes, offering novel insights for precision medicine across development, aging and brain disorders.

articles.title: VectBox Sync: a web application for vectorcardiographic analysis of ventricular synchrony from 12-lead electrocardiograms
articles.abstract: We introduce VectBox Sync, a browser-based application that implements a published vectorcardiographic (VCG) dyssynchrony index for exploratory assessment of ventricular electrical synchrony from the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG). Despite guideline-directed patient selection, a substantial fraction of patients who receive cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) do not obtain the expected benefit. QRS duration and morphology remain the principal electrical criteria, yet they do not capture the three-dimensional trajectory of ventricular activation. VectBox Sync prioritizes native digital ECG recordings, including matrices and common clinical and research waveform formats; optional manufacturer-PDF import and externally digitized numerical files extend access when paper-like archives are the only available source. After optional preprocessing, the user selects a QRS interval, and the application calculates the dyssynchrony index relative to a calibrated control cutoff. It also provides companion VCG descriptors (voltage and speed integrals, loop angles, and planarity), together with VCG trajectories, synchrony-field maps, and a multilingual PDF report. Labeled conditions from the same session can be overlaid for comparison, for example across successive pacing settings. VectBox Sync makes this VCG-based assessment accessible through an integrated web application, providing quantitative descriptors that complement conventional ECG criteria. The application is available at https://vectbox.com/sync for research and educational use.

articles.title: Adaptive Dynamic Evolution of Substitutional Pt Single Atoms in CeO2 for CO Oxidation
articles.abstract: Platinum-substitutional ceria solid solutions (PtxCe1–xO2) have attracted considerable attention owing to their high stability and activity for low-temperature CO oxidation. However, their catalytic behavior and reactant-induced structural evolution under reaction conditions remain under debate. Here, we investigate the CO-induced structural evolution of substitutional Pt single-atom sites in CeO2(111) and their dynamically catalytic activity for low-temperature CO oxidation by means of density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Our results show that the commonly proposed octahedrally coordinated Pt species are unstable in a CO atmosphere since CO adsorbed on Pt readily reacts with lattice oxygen with a low energy barrier. The resulting CO2 formation induces a dynamic evolution of the Pt coordination environment, driving the transformation from octahedral coordination to a more energetically stable square-planar configuration. In addition, oxygen vacancies (VO) and CO adsorption synergistically promote the displacement of substitutional Pt atoms, leading to the formation of distorted Pt–CO complexes adjacent to vacancy sites that serve as the active centers for CO oxidation. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and deep-potential molecular dynamics (DPMD) simulations further verify that the octahedral-to-square-planar dynamic evolution occurs spontaneously, while similar coordination evolution on the various ceria facets indicates that this behavior is not limited to CeO2(111) but is a general feature of Pt1-substituted CeO2. Further experimental characterization results corroborate the calculated coordination evolution of Pt sites and support the proposed dynamic structural transformation. These findings provide atomistic insights into the reaction-induced structural evolution of Pt species in CeO2 and clarify the origin of the catalytic activity of Pt-substituted ceria for low-temperature CO oxidation.

articles.title: Brønsted Acid Site-Mediated Proton Injection and Redistribution Regulate Phosphoric Acid Electrochemical Interfaces
articles.abstract: Molecular control of the proton environment in phosphoric acid (PA) based electrochemical interfaces is critical for efficient proton transport and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet effective strategies for actively regulating this environment remain limited. Here, we show that Brønsted acid sites (BASs) in HY zeolite function as solid-state proton regulating centers that directly participate in and reorganize the interfacial PA hydrogen bond network. By combining ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations, free energy calculations, variable-temperature diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (VT-DRIFTS), and electrochemical measurements, we reveal a BAS-mediated proton injection and redistribution mechanism. The framework BAS proton transfers to an adjacent PA molecule, generating an excess proton defect that dynamically redistributes among neighboring PA molecules through hydrogen-bond-assisted proton hopping. The potential of mean force (PMF) along δ01 reveals a favorable free energy change for BAS to PA1 proton transfer (–0.122 eV), while density functional theory (DFT) calculations show lower electronic energies for representative PA-associated configurations, with PA2 exhibiting the lowest energy. AIMD simulations further demonstrate preferential excess-proton accommodation and dynamic redistribution within the PA network. VT-DRIFTS measurements reveal PA-induced changes in the temperature-dependent hydroxyl response of HY, while calculated harmonic infrared spectra of representative proton configurations provide molecular-level insight into interfacial proton interactions and hydrogen bond reorganization. Electrochemical measurements further show that HY incorporation reduces proton transport and ORR charge transfer resistances while increasing Pt electrochemical accessibility. These findings identify BAS-mediated proton injection and redistribution as a promising molecular strategy for regulating PA-based electrochemical interfaces.

articles.title: Cyclative Carbon Quaternization of Alkyl Boronic Esters via Copper-Catalyzed Aminyl Radical Transfer
articles.abstract: Despite the rich chemistry of alkyl boronic esters (alkyl Bpins) in C–B bond transformations, carbon quaternization via concurrent C–B and C–H bond scission on the boron-substituted carbon has remained elusive. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed aminyl radical-mediated cyclative C-quaternization of alkyl Bpins with acrylamides to access valuable carbo- and spirocyclic scaffolds. Central to this transformation is a sequential C–B/C–H bond-cleavage, in which ART triggers C–B cleavage and HAT enables site-selective C–H functionalization. The method has a broad substrate scope, high functional group tolerance, and exquisite site selectivity and allows late-stage diversification of drugs and natural products. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations were conducted to elucidate the underlying reaction mechanism. These studies support the generation of aminyl radicals via Cu–N bond homolysis, which is effective for ART, and rationalize selective 1,5-HAT and copper-mediated PCET in the key cyclization step.

articles.title: Elucidation of Pathways in the Conversion of CO2-Rich Syngas to Methanol over Cu-Based Catalysts
articles.abstract: The efficient conversion of CO2-rich syngas to fuels remains challenging because of distinct thermodynamics between CO2 and CO hydrogenation. In this work, we investigate the structure–performance relationship and reaction mechanism of CO2-rich syngas conversion to methanol over a series of Cu-based catalysts, with CO2 contents ranging from 4% to 25%. We find that the CuZnZr catalyst exhibits the best overall performance because of the enhanced adsorption/activation of CO and CO2, resulting from the strengthened Cu–oxide interaction and promoted Cu–ZnO–ZrOx interface. The catalytic performance of CuZnZr is highly sensitive to both the Zn/Zr ratio and the CO2 content in the feed gas, with a Cu/Zn/Zr ratio of 6:3:1, giving the highest activity. We find that CO is mainly adsorbed on Cu sites, whereas CO2 is preferentially activated at Cu–ZnO/ZrOx interfacial sites to form formate and methoxy species. In CO2-containing syngas, CO*, HCOO*, and CH3O* coexist on the surface, and a small amount of CO2 effectively promotes the hydrogenation of HCOO* to CH3O*. Isotope-labeled experiments further confirm that CO2 not only undergoes the reverse water–gas shift reaction to form CO but also directly participates in methanol formation through oxygen-containing intermediates. Both the carbon and oxygen atoms in methanol can originate from the CO2 in feed gas, demonstrating a coupled hydrogenation mechanism involving both CO and CO2. In addition, a trace amount of water vapor increases the surface coverage of both HCOO* and CH3O* and promotes methanol formation, rather than only acting as a spectator. Therefore, the improved catalytic performance of CuZnZr originates from the optimized Cu–ZnO–ZrOx interface and the cooperative transformation of CO*, HCOO*, and CH3O*. These findings provide mechanistic insights and guidance for the design of efficient Cu-based catalysts in the direct methanol synthesis from CO2-rich syngas.

articles.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Accelerates Rational Design of Dual-Site Catalysts for Synergistic Catalytic Aerobic Oxidative Synthesis of Benzimidazole
articles.abstract: The aerobic oxidative synthesis of benzimidazole requires heterogeneous catalysts that combine high activity with practical stability. Because conventional catalyst optimization depends heavily on laborious experimental screening, we established an interpretable machine learning (ML) workflow to accelerate catalyst selection and identify the variables governing performance. An XGBoost model was trained to relate catalyst descriptors and reaction conditions to benzimidazole synthesis, and partial-dependence-plot (PDP) analysis was used to determine favorable catalyst compositions and operating windows. Guided by the model, we prepared the cobalt-based dual-site catalyst CoNP-CoSA@NC-800. Under mild conditions (90 °C, 9 h) with atmospheric air as the oxidant, this material delivered 100% conversion and 96% benzimidazole selectivity. It also tolerated a broad range of substrates and retained its activity during recycling. Control experiments and theoretical calculations indicate that the Co nanoparticle (CoNP) and Co single atom (CoSA) sites act cooperatively: the CoNP component modifies the d-band center and electronic structure of CoNP-CoSA@NC-800, thereby enhancing O2 adsorption and activation to facilitate benzimidazole formation.

articles.title: Light-Driven Reconstruction of MoS2 Nanosheets Boosts Photothermal Reverse Water Gas Shift Reaction with Near-Unity Selectivity
articles.abstract: In-depth understanding of the reconstruction behaviors during photothermal reactions is of paramount importance for the design of highly efficient photothermal catalysts. Here, we demonstrate the photothermal effect-induced reconstruction of MoS2 nanosheets during the photothermal reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reaction. Specifically, under the operating photothermal reaction conditions, the MoS2 nanosheet catalyst undergoes rapid surface temperature increase up to around 380 °C, which can react with the H2 gas to produce in-plane S vacancies, thereby leading to the reconstruction of MoS2 nanosheets for enhanced RWGS reaction activity. An approximately 7.8 mmol g–1 h–1 evolution rate with a near-unity selectivity of CO (>99%) is achieved over MoS2 nanosheets during 100 h stability testing under flow-bed reaction and atmospheric pressure. Detailed structural characterizations combined with density functional theory simulations unravel that the photothermal effect-induced reconstruction of MoS2 can facilitate the charge separation and adsorption of reactants, lower the energy barrier of the *COOH intermediate, and meanwhile, improve the H2 dissociation ability for promoting the RWGS reaction.

articles.title: Modular Synthesis of α-Tertiary Amines Enabled by Nickel-Catalyzed Reductive Alkylation of N -unprotected Ketimines
articles.abstract: The straightforward construction of sterically hindered α-tertiary primary amines remains a stubborn challenge in organic synthesis. Although a wide array of approaches for the synthesis of this motif has been developed, the leveraging of ketimines as an amine source is underexplored. General reductive alkylative additions of unactivated alkyl halides to N-unprotected ketimines remain unknown. Herein, we disclose a nickel-catalyzed cross-electrophile coupling between N-unprotected heteroaryl ketimines and readily available alkyl halides, including primary, secondary, and tertiary ones, to directly furnish diverse primary amines with steric congestion without attendant deprotection sequences. This synthetic protocol circumvents the use of preformed organometallic reagents, leading to broad functional group tolerance and high step-economy. Preliminary mechanistic investigations support a radical-type cross-coupling pathway of N-H ketimines with unactivated alkyl radicals involving a Ni(I)/Ni(II)/Ni(III) redox cycle. The practicality of this method has been demonstrated in successful application in the synthesis of various cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) inhibitors.

articles.title: Nonlinear Field-Reorganization Coupling Dictates Cation-Steered Proton Transfer at Electrified Interfaces
articles.abstract: Electrolyte cations in the electric double layer strongly influence electrocatalytic CO2 reduction to multicarbon products, yet the microscopic origin of this cation effect remains elusive. Using metadynamics-biased ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, we identify a cation-driven electrostatic traction mechanism, where the cation-induced local electric field promotes the interfacial water activation and directly steers nascent protons toward adsorbed *CO2 via an Eley–Rideal path, effectively bypassing the Volmer H adsorption intermediate as the dominant channel under these interfacial conditions. At the electrified interface, strong electronic coupling in this inner-sphere proton-coupled electron transfer process renormalizes the classical solvent reorganization energy to effective quantum reorganization energy, flattening the reaction potential energy surface. We further establish an adiabatic Marcus–Stark framework by nonlinearly coupling the interfacial electric field with the effective reorganization energy, which quantitatively accounts for a substantial part of the experimentally observed exponential acceleration of C2 product formation with K+ over Li+ and identifies interfacial proton supply as an important rate-modulating factor within the broader C2 reaction network. This finding partially decouples reaction kinetics from intermediate binding energy scaling relations, providing a physical framework for manipulating electrochemical selectivity through interfacial microenvironment engineering.

articles.title: Palladium(II)-Catalyzed Denitrogenation of Alkyl Diazirines
articles.abstract: [PdCl2(NCPh)2] catalyzes the denitrogenation of mono(alkyl) diazirines in CDCl3 at 25 °C for 16 h to form the corresponding alkene in up to 70% yield. Reaction of (4-fluorophenyl)diazirine with a catalytic amount of [PdCl2(NCPh)2] (20 mol %) and excess styrene forms 1-(4-fluorophenyl)-2-phenylcyclopropane in 48% yield (cis/trans = 6.7:1). Kinetic experiments, in situ analysis of palladium coordination complexes, and DFT calculations support a mechanism for Pd(II)-catalyzed denitrogenation of benzyl diazirine involving C─N oxidative addition (ΔG‡ = 22.4 kcal/mol) of a four-coordinate trans-palladium σ-diazirine complex to form a five-coordinate Pd(IV) diazometallacyclobutane complex. Subsequent Pd─C bond cleavage (ΔG‡ = 8.8 kcal/mol) to form an N-bound diazo complex followed by isomerization to the corresponding C-bound diazo complex, presumably via intermolecular ligand exchange, and facile (ΔG‡ = 4.2 kcal/mol) extrusion of dinitrogen forms a trans-palladium alkylidene complex. Concerted, 1,2-H migration (ΔG‡ = 5.0 kcal/mol) forms the corresponding four-coordinate palladium π-styrene complex.

articles.title: Radical-Based Catalytic Transformations of 1-Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes: Opportunities and Future Directions
articles.abstract: 1-Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABBs) have emerged as versatile strained precursors to saturated, three-dimensional azetidine scaffolds that are increasingly valuable in modern drug discovery. This Perspective contends that the recent proliferation of radical-based catalytic platforms, encompassing photoredox, metallaphotoredox, energy-transfer, and electrochemical manifolds, serves as an effective complement to classical polar chemistry, enabling diverse transformations and the construction of sterically congested carbon–carbon and carbon–heteroatom bonds through distinct reactivity profiles. We illustrate how open-shell intermediates enable the precise, regiodivergent, and multicomponent construction of sterically congested azetidines and azabicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes. We argue that while several mechanistic patterns have now been proposed, their underlying reactivity principles remain incompletely understood, and the broader synthetic potential remains largely underexplored. We therefore chart a forward-looking agenda: the development of alternative radical transformations, the expansion of radical coupling partners to include abundant and readily available feedstocks, the integration of electrochemistry for scalable and catalyst-free processes, and the design of radical relay sequences that access architecturally complex bridged azabicycles beyond simple azetidines. By framing these frontiers as both timely and achievable, we aim to catalyze the evolution of radical ABB chemistry from a specialized tool into a broadly enabling strategy for constructing the nitrogen-containing, sp3-rich chemical space that next-generation drug discovery demands.

articles.title: Reverse Water Gas Shift Reaction over a Homogeneous Iron Catalyst and the Underlying Mechanism
articles.abstract: The CO production by the reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reaction is a promising bridge between CO2 conversion and well-established C1 chemistry. Currently, heterogeneous catalysts are mostly reported for this reaction, which usually require high operating temperatures (above 600 °C) and encounter poor selectivity of CO at lower temperatures (below 400 °C). Homogeneous catalysis may offer distinct advantages at a low temperature. Nevertheless, only some noble metal homogeneous catalysts for this reaction have been reported to date. Herein, we report the iron phthalocyanine (FePc) as a homogeneous catalyst to selectively produce CO via the RWGS reaction in the N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) solvent. The reaction started at a low temperature of 120 °C with a CO selectivity of 98.1%, and high CO selectivity was attained under various conditions. Large-scale DFT calculations and control experiments revealed a tri-active-center mechanism, wherein the Fe center and Pc ligand separately and simultaneously activate CO2 and H2 and then cooperatively catalyze their conversion to CO and H2O. In addition, this work quantitatively demonstrates that the dispersion interactions between the catalyst and solvent molecules play a critical role in homogeneous transition-metal-catalyzed CO2 conversion reactions.

articles.title: Vacancy-Directed Phytate Coordination Couples Ni-Site Polarization with Interfacial Hydration for Durable Photoelectrochemical Seawater Oxidation
articles.abstract: Photoelectrochemical seawater oxidation is limited by a coupled interfacial challenge: low-coordinated metal sites that favor hole utilization and oxygen evolution are also susceptible to chloride attack, whereas protective surface modification can compromise water access. Here, oxygen vacancies in amorphous NiCr2O4–x on α-Fe2O3 are repurposed to direct multidentate phytate coordination, constructing a molecular interface that couples Ni-site polarization with interfacial hydration. Catalyst-facing M–O–P coordination withdraws electron density from vacancy-activated Ni sites, strengthens interfacial polarization, accelerates hole delivery, and reconstructs oxygenated-intermediate bonding, lowering the free-energy requirement of the *O → *OOH step from 0.66 to 0.45 eV. Meanwhile, electrolyte-facing phosphate groups remain exposed as persistent hydrogen-bonding nodes, preferentially stabilize O-down interfacial water, and organize a continuous hydration network that preserves H2O/OH– accessibility while suppressing Cl– approach and adsorption. Operando infrared spectroscopy, in situ ATR-SEIRAS, molecular dynamics simulations, ion mapping, and dissolution analyses collectively connect this coupled solid–liquid interfacial regulation with accelerated intermediate turnover and reduced corrosion. The resulting photoanode delivers 4.43 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V versus RHE, operates for 300 h with negligible decay in alkaline simulated seawater, and retains 82% of its initial photocurrent after 200 h in alkaline real seawater. These results establish vacancy-directed molecular coordination as a strategy for coupling active-site polarization with hydration-mediated protection in durable seawater photooxidation.

articles.title: Anion Sublattice Engineering Induced Niobium-Tungsten Oxide with Near-Zero Residual Strain for Stable 100 C Cycling Capability
articles.abstract: Wadsley-Roth W3Nb14O44 is a fast-charging anode material but suffers from low electronic conductivity and electrochemical polarization. Here, anion-sublattice engineering is employed to regulate its electronic structure and Li+ storage kinetics. Density functional theory and kinetic analyses reveal that an appropriate concentration of oxygen vacancies enhances electronic conductivity, moderates Li+ adsorption, and facilitates Li+ diffusion, thereby reducing charge-transfer and diffusion impedances at low temperatures. In situ XRD and synchrotron radiation X-ray 3D nanocomputed tomography reveal reversible structural evolution with near-zero residual strain after cycling. Consequently, WNO-x delivers 77.4 mAh g–1 at 200 C and retains 72.6% capacity after 6000 cycles at 100 C while exhibiting low-temperature electrochemical activity. Moreover, the WNO-x||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 full cell delivers 85.8 mAh g–1 at 20 C and retains 77.1% capacity after 3000 cycles, with cycling capability at –30 °C. Such structure-property insight provides a strategy for designing niobium-based oxide anodes toward fast-charging and low-temperature batteries.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Advances the Uncovering of Solid–Liquid Interfaces in Batteries
articles.abstract: A more profound understanding of battery interfaces, characterized by multiple components and dynamic interactions, can provide a theoretical foundation for the development of next-generation energy storage systems. The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) technology is enhancing scientific paradigms, offering significant benefits for the study of complex battery interfaces. Here, we examine how AI can facilitate a deeper understanding of these intricate interfaces in batteries, promote more standardized characterization analyses, and assist in designing interface materials. The introduction of AI models may facilitate the discovery of additional mechanisms and materials. Moreover, we discuss the trade-off between interpretability and accuracy in AI models, as well as the risk of narrow cognitive perspectives among researchers. We hope this perspective will inspire and advance the technological integration of AI in battery interface research.

articles.title: Cu-Doped Highly Porous SnO2 for Long-Lasting Acidic CO2 Electroreduction at 1000 mA cm–2
articles.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) to formic acid (HCOOH) provides a carbon-neutral route. SnO2-based catalysts suffer from limited activity and instability at industrial current densities. We develop a Cu-doped highly porous SnO2 catalyst (SnO2-Cu) that enhances activity and stabilizes the SnO2 framework. The porous structure exposes numerous active sites while confining local OH– within the bulk acid electrolyte, enabling high-current-density operation. Cu doping strengthens CO2 chemisorption and Sn–O bond covalency, boosting CO2RR activity while suppressing SnO2 self-reduction. SnO2-Cu sustains 1000 mA cm–2 for 19 h with 98.5% FE and 800 mA cm–2 for 72 h with 94.1% FE in a flow cell at pH 1.82. It achieves a HCOOH production cost of 722.7 USD tonne–1 in a solid-state electrolyte (SSE) device calculated based on onshore wind power, demonstrating economic competitiveness. This work demonstrates that rational Cu doping of porous SnO2 addresses activity and durability limits, offering an effective platform for high-rate, economically viable HCOOH electrosynthesis.

articles.title: Engineering Ultrathin, Tough Polymer Networks for Stable Lithium Metal Anode Interphases
articles.abstract: Interfacial degradation and dendritic lithium (Li) growth remain critical bottlenecks for practical Li metal batteries (LMBs). Herein, we introduce a tough, ion-conductive poly(2-(dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate) (pDMAEMA) nanolayer on Li metal via photo-initiated chemical vapor deposition (piCVD). The photo-mediated, solvent-free piCVD enables nanometer-scale coatings with systematic control over photo-crosslinking and chain entanglement without compromising Li surface integrity. This systematic control yields an optimized polymer network balancing toughness (36.3 MJ m–3) and viscoelasticity (10.3% linear viscoelastic strain limit) to accommodate repeated Li volume changes. Furthermore, interactions between pDMAEMA and PF6– anions promote a mechanically durable LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase, thereby supporting uniform Li deposition. Pouch-type bi-cells employing the optimized 100 nm polymer-coated Li anode achieve an energy density of 338 Wh kg–1 and 80% capacity retention after 90 cycles under practical conditions (N/P = 2, E/C = 3 g Ah–1). This ultrathin, tough polymer network offers a promising design principle for high-energy LMBs.

articles.title: Non-ionic Phthalocyanine Additives Enable Synergistic Passivation and Strain Buffering in Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: The long-term stability of high-efficiency n-i-p perovskite solar cells is limited by coupled defect migration, residual lattice strain, and thermal–mechanical degradation. Here, we develop a non-ionic, interface-enriched zinc phthalocyanine derivative, 4PCSZnPc, as a molecular stabilizer for simultaneous defect anchoring and strain buffering. Unlike ionic additives that may introduce mobile species, 4PCSZnPc is distributed throughout the film, with enrichment near the buried SnO2/perovskite interface.
