Peripheral N/O/S heteroatoms coordinate with under-coordinated Pb2+ sites, while the Zn-regulated macrocyclic center interacts with iodide-related defects, forming dual-site Lewis acid–base anchoring. Meanwhile, the rigid phthalocyanine framework reduces residual tensile stress and may hinder strain-assisted ion migration. These combined effects of defect passivation and strain buffering reduce non-radiative recombination, improve film uniformity, and enhance thermal robustness. Consequently, 4PCSZnPc-treated devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.88% (certified 26.74%), a T80 lifetime of 1358 h under 1-sun at 85 °C, and 95% retention after 200 thermal cycles, providing a design principle for future thermally resilient photovoltaics.

articles.title: Regulation of Anionic Redox Reaction Voltage by Energy Band Modulation for Li-Rich Cathodes
articles.abstract: Anionic redox reaction (ARR) promises high energy density for Li-rich cathodes yet suffers from severe voltage decay. Here, we investigate ARR voltage modulation in a Li2S-modified quasi-solid Li-rich cathode (Li2S-LRM), which exhibits a distinct low-voltage ARR plateau (2.0–2.8 V). Combining in situ XRD, S K-edge XANES, EELS, Ar-etched XPS and DFT calculations, we validate in situ electrochemical sulfur doping. Upon cycling, the material forms bulk LixS/Li–S–O species alongside a dominant Li2SO3/Li2SO4 polyanion interphase that realizes oxygen trapping. Vacancy-cluster formation facilitates reversible S-involved charge compensation, where sulfur redox activity progressively intensifies during long cycling. Enabled by the band-modulation and oxygen-trapping effects, Li2S-LRM achieves a high average Coulombic efficiency of 99.6% and suppressed voltage decay (0.28 vs. 0.83 mV cycle–1 for pristine LRM). This work deepens mechanistic insights into ARR and provides rational design guidance for high-performance anionic-redox cathodes.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal Molecular Control of Crystallization for Efficient Perovskite/Organic Tandem Photovoltaics
articles.abstract: Perovskite/organic tandem solar cells (PO-TSCs) offer a route toward overcoming the efficiency limitations of single-junction photovoltaics. However, wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite sub-cells limit their performance, where uncontrolled crystallization leads to compositional heterogeneity, defect accumulation, and severe halide phase segregation. Here, we develop a template-bridge dual-control (TBDC) strategy using 2-thiophenemethylammonium bromide (2-ThMAB). Precisely controlling the introduction timing and spatial distribution of 2-ThMAB maximizes molecular regulation of crystallization. Surface-anchored 2-ThMAB molecules act as growth templates to induce (100) crystal growth, while grain-boundary-localized molecules regulate halide migration through molecular bridging, enabling homogeneous crystallization. The WBG perovskite films exhibit enhanced out-of-plane (100) orientation, reduced defect density, and suppressed halide phase segregation. Consequently, the optimized WBG device achieves a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.13% with improved operational stability. Integrated into PO-TSCs, the optimized WBG sub-cells deliver a PCE of 26.62%. This strategy enables concurrent control of crystallization and halide redistribution of efficient, stable tandem photovoltaics.

articles.title: 5DSTEM of Liquid-Phase Nanocrystal Growth Bridges Ensemble Kinetics and Nanoscale Dynamics
articles.abstract: Resolving how ensemble growth kinetics emerge from particle- and grain-level dynamics is essential for predictive control of nanocrystal synthesis. Here, time-resolved four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM), extended into five dimensions (5DSTEM) through continuous acquisition, is used to simultaneously resolve morphology, crystallographic orientation, and lattice strain during Au nanocrystal growth in aqueous HAuCl4. Although ensemble growth follows surface-reaction-limited kinetics, individual nanoparticles exhibit distinct pathways, including continuous growth and discrete coalescence through oriented attachment. These pathways display characteristic orientation dynamics, with stable or gradually selected orientations during continuous growth and abrupt reconfiguration followed by alignment during coalescence. At the ensemble level, the out-of-plane orientation distribution is established early and remains stable, whereas in-plane orientations remain broadly distributed without global alignment. Tensile strain develops progressively from particle surfaces and interfaces, directly linking lattice distortion with evolving morphology and crystallographic structure. By connecting ensemble kinetics with particle- and grain-resolved structural evolution, 5DSTEM provides a general framework for uncovering heterogeneous growth mechanisms and for relating synthesis pathways to structure-dependent properties in functional nanomaterials.

articles.title: Accelerating the Discovery of Synthesizable 2D Hybrid Double Perovskites through Human–LLM Collaborative Descriptor Engineering
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional hybrid perovskites offer exceptional structural diversity and multifunctional properties, yet their synthesis remains a major bottleneck due to low hit rates and strong reliance on empirical intuition. Here we introduce AL-SynAgent, a human-in-the-loop, ML-guided screening workflow that integrates literature-derived synthetic priors, expert-refined chemical descriptors, and active learning to assess the synthesis feasibility of two dimensional (2D) hybrid organic–inorganic rare-earth double perovskites (HORDPs). By converting LLM-assisted literature knowledge and expert chemical reasoning into system-specific computable descriptors, AL-SynAgent reduces dependence on large experimental data sets while retaining chemically interpretable decision rules. With experimental feedback from only 4.8% of candidate space, the model converged and achieved successful target-phase formation for 11 of the 14 candidates in the prospectively selected experimental set, corresponding to a hit rate of 78.6%. Screening of an enumerated virtual library of 280,000 candidates further prioritized 64,482 compositions with high predicted synthesis feasibility. Notably, three newly obtained compounds also exhibit both excellent ferroelectricity and photoluminescence, including (4-F-321)4RbEu(NO3)8, which displays an exceptionally high Curie temperature of 388 K and strong emission at 592 nm. This work establishes a practical, human-in-the-loop strategy for data-efficient prioritization of candidate compositions within chemically constrained 2D HORDP space under a standardized laboratory synthesis protocol.

articles.title: Chronic Stress-Triggerable Nanoprodrugs Ameliorate Metabolic Abnormalities Driven by Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal Axis Dysregulation in Early Alzheimer’s Disease
articles.abstract: Chronic stress-induced dysregulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis is a crucial early risk factor that triggers brain energy metabolism disorders to accelerate the onset and progression of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Herein, an amphiphilic precursor conjugate of ginsenoside Rc (Rc) covalently linked with a reactive oxygen species-sensitive thioketo bond is constructed to form stimuli-responsive prodrug assemblies, which are further modified with the TGN-Tet1 dual-ligand fusion peptide TPL to obtain a chronic stress-triggerable programmed nanoprodrug (TLRN). Following TPL-mediated blood-brain barrier penetration and neuronal preferential targeting, nanoprodrugs specifically disintegrate to selectively release active Rc in the chronic stress-induced excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) microenvironment. Benefiting from the restoration of HPA axis homeostasis by normalizing glucocorticoid receptor nuclear translocation, TLRN treatment exhibits multifaceted rectification of cerebral metabolic abnormalities, including enhancing glucose uptake, promoting oxidative phosphorylation, and mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction. In young amyloid precursor protein/presenilin 1 (APP/PS1) transgenic mouse models exposed to chronic stress, this intervention can alleviate brain energy deprivation and amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation, ultimately rescuing depressive-like behaviors and cognitive deficits, offering a promising approach for early prevention and flexible management of AD at high risk of chronic stress.

articles.title: Competing Surface Dynamics of Copper Catalyst Particles during Electrochemical Carbon Dioxide Reduction
articles.abstract: Copper is a powerful catalyst for the electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR), but it faces challenges with selectivity and stability dependent on its structural characteristics. We developed a platform that combines graphitized carbon nanofibers with identical-location transmission electron microscopy (IL-TEM) to study individual copper nanoparticles at the atomic scale under various reaction conditions. Notably, we observed that competing phenomena such as Ostwald ripening, coalescence, selective etching, and Coulomb-explosion-like fragmentation coexist in the same reaction area, with the latter being qualitatively consistent with a charge-driven fission pathway in larger nanoparticles (>10 nm). By tracking uniquely identifiable nanoparticles both individually and in groups, our findings focus on the range of surface-confined restructuring pathways during CO2RR. This contrasts with solution-mediated phenomena, such as dissolution–precipitation, which dominate under open-circuit potential (OCP) and significantly destabilize the catalyst prior to the reaction, highlighting the importance of eliminating this effect. Under CO2RR conditions, Cu nanoparticles are highly sensitive to subtle variations in the support’s nanotexture, defects, and electronic structure, leading to the coexistence of counteracting mechanisms we observed. These observations provide a structural framework for understanding the dynamic behavior of copper-on-carbon catalysts under CO2RR conditions, guiding the development of strategies to improve catalyst stability and performance.

articles.title: Direct Observation of Chirality-Dependent Berry Curvature Dipole via Cross-Axial Nonlinear Hall Effect in Trigonal Te
articles.abstract: Quantum geometric quantities, such as Berry curvature (BC) and quantum metric, are known to govern the physical and topological properties of materials, making access to these quantities critically important for the comprehensive understanding of the materials. Chiral crystals offer a natural platform in which structural handedness can control quantum geometry and nonlinear transport, but direct experimental access to the quantum geometric quantities has remained elusive. Here, we show that trigonal tellurium (Te) hosts an enantiomer-dependent Berry curvature dipole (BCD) that can be accessed through the measurement of the cross-axial nonlinear Hall effect (NHE), unlike in previously studied in-plane configurations, where the BCD contribution vanishes. Angle-resolved measurements on left- and right-handed Te devices reveal a second-order transverse response whose sign reverses with crystal chirality. The extracted cross-axial nonlinear susceptibility, χyxz, exceeds the in-plane susceptibility, χxxx, by more than two-fold, indicating a strong BCD-driven contribution. First-principles calculations attribute this behavior to a topologically nontrivial hedgehog-like BC texture near the H points and predict a BCD that reverses sign between opposite enantiomers, consistent with experiment. These results establish cross-axial nonlinear Hall transport as a symmetry-selective probe of chirality-controlled quantum geometry in tellurium and related chiral materials.

articles.title: Electrically Reconfigurable Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Cavities on Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
articles.abstract: Interfacing integrated photonics with solid-state spin defects holds great promise for future quantum networks, but the scaling of spin-photon architectures is hindered by frequency mismatches arising from fabrication-induced variations in photonic cavity resonances and inhomogeneous optical transition frequencies of individual spins. These challenges call for a photonic platform with deterministic and wide-range tunability. Here, we demonstrate a hybrid nanophotonic platform based on direct bonding of silicon carbide photonic crystal nanocavity arrays onto a thin-film lithium niobate-on-insulator, enabling deterministic electrical tuning of multiple SiC nanocavities into mutual spectral resonance. By exploiting the strong electro-optic response of lithium niobate, we achieve continuous and wide-range cavity tuning of 380 GHz (∼1.1 nm), sufficient to compensate both cavity disorder and spin spectral inhomogeneity. The nanocavities balance strong optical confinement with electrical tunability, exhibiting a theoretical Purcell factor of approximately 400. This hybrid platform enables electrically reconfigurable spin-photon interfaces for large-scale integrated quantum photonics.

articles.title: Engineered Living Materials: A Therapeutic Paradigm beyond Conventional Biomaterials
articles.abstract: Development of biomaterials in the past two decades has profoundly advanced modern medicine. However, the relatively simple and insufficiently biological functions and lack of self-renewal capability limit their ability to dynamically adapt to complex physiological environments. Engineered living materials (eLMs) use living organisms as core functional units and provide a therapeutic approach for addressing these limitations. Thus, this review systematically summarizes the recent advancements in eLMs, beginning with an overview of the primary biological chassis, including bacteria, microalgae, fungi, and mammalian cells. eLMs hold the valuable capabilities of long-term self-sustainment and self-proliferation within complex biological environments, which are endowed with intelligent regulation. For instance, they can sense environmental signals and execute programmed functional outputs, including therapeutic protein secretion or targeted migration. Moreover, they achieve precise control over therapeutic actions, encompassing spatial localization at the disease site, temporal dynamics of the intervention, and quantitative regulation of outputs. Furthermore, we highlight the broad therapeutic applications of these dynamic systems in addressing complex diseases. Finally, we discuss the current translational challenges and future directions of the field, emphasizing the potential of integrating artificial intelligence with synthetic biology and nanomaterial engineering to develop next-generation programmable eLMs and expand their utility across diverse sectors.

articles.title: Fluorinated Copper(I) Iodine Cluster Scintillators Enable High-Temperature X-ray Imaging
articles.abstract: The development of scintillators that maintain excellent performance under high temperatures is a critical challenge. Here, by simply replacing the triphenylphosphine ligand with its fluorinated analogue, we successfully switched the emission pathway of Cu2I2 clusters from pure phosphorescence to a hybrid phosphorescence/thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) mechanism, enabling adaptive high-temperature X-ray imaging. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that the fluorination strategy reduces the singlet–triplet energy gap to an exceptionally small value of 35 meV, thereby promoting efficient reverse intersystem crossing. The TADF contribution reaches 95.7% at room temperature. This temperature-responsive characteristic endows the fluorinated cluster with adaptive X-ray imaging capability across a broad temperature window from 293 to 413 K, overcoming the thermal quenching phenomenon in traditional phosphorescence-only scintillators. This work establishes a molecular design approach for smart scintillators capable of reliable operation in demanding thermal environments.

articles.title: Frozen 2D Adatom Gas at the Surface of Gold–Copper Alloys
articles.abstract: Isolated, undercoordinated metal atoms exhibit enhanced reactivity central to catalysis, yet their stabilization on surfaces remains challenging. In heterogeneous single-atom catalysis, activity derives from interactions between individual atoms and a host matrix, but the absence of stabilizing ligands often leads to diffusion, aggregation, and sintering, obscuring structure–activity relationships. On metal surfaces, reactivity is typically limited to sparse, dynamic, undercoordinated sites lining step edges or lattice defects. Here we report a defect-engineering strategy to stabilize isolated adatoms on dilute metal alloy substrates. Scanning tunneling microscopy reveals a high density of uniformly distributed adatoms on Au–Cu(111) terraces that persist under thermal cycling. Combined experiments and modeling attribute this stability to alloy-induced subsurface dislocation networks that trap adatoms and suppress diffusion, forming a two-dimensional frozen gas. These adatoms act as a reactive reservoir, enabling on-surface coordination chemistry inaccessible on pure metals, and providing insights into atomic-scale processes on the surfaces of defect-engineered alloys with implications for heterogeneous catalysis.

articles.title: Hybridization State Engineering of Coal Pitch-Based Carbon Materials Enabling Ultrastable Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries with 150,000 Cycles
articles.abstract: Carbon materials with superior porosity and conductivity are widely adopted in aqueous zinc–iodine batteries to host iodine, but suffer from the polyiodide shuttle and cycling stability challenges. Traditional strategies mainly focus on pore structure engineering or heteroatom doping of carbon hosts to confine iodine, but fail to address the sluggish iodine conversion kinetics. Herein, we initially reveal the significant yet overlooked role of hybridization state in reforming the carbon intrinsic activity toward high-efficiency iodine conversion chemistry. With pitch-derived porous carbon as an example, we controllably regulate the C(sp2)/C(sp3) ratio (from 1.23 to 2.21) while maintaining high surface area. These properties lower the activation energy of iodine conversion and effectively suppress the polyiodide shuttle. The zinc–iodine battery exhibits ultrahigh cycling stability after 150,000 cycles and a low self-discharging rate with only 12.5% capacity loss after 20 days. Ah-level pouch cell with 66.6 mgiodine cm–2 achieves a cumulative discharging capacity of 103.51 Ah. The hybridization engineering was successfully extended to commercial porous carbon (YP-50F), prolonging the lifespan from 7425 to 27,000 cycles. This work presents a hybridization state engineering strategy to reform the intrinsic activity of the carbon host to favor the iodine conversion chemistry and beyond.

articles.title: Micro-LED-Activated Formaldehyde Sensing via Au Loading-Regulated Interfacial Engineering in Anatase TiO2 Nanofibers
articles.abstract: Photoactivated metal-oxide gas sensors reduce the energy demand associated with continuous heating, yet selective detection of volatile organic compounds remains constrained by weak electrical transduction and complex surface oxidation pathways. Here, Au-functionalized anatase TiO2 nanofibers (Au/aTiO2 NFs) were integrated with a 395 nm microlight-emitting diode (LED) for low-power formaldehyde (HCHO) sensing. One-pot electrospinning followed by calcination enabled systematic control of Au loading while preserving the anatase nanofiber architecture. Au loading regulated TiO2 crystallite growth, defect states, dispersion, interfacial Au chemical states, and photoexcited carrier relaxation. At 0.15 wt % Au, finely dispersed Au nanoparticles produced a distinct Au/TiO2 interfacial environment and carrier-relaxation behavior, whereas higher loadings induced nanoparticle aggregation and additional nonradiative energy-loss pathways. Under UV micro-LED illumination at 2.63 mW, the optimized sensor exhibited a response of 1093 toward 1 ppm of HCHO, an estimated detection limit of 4.9 ppb, and stable operation over 40 consecutive cycles. Density functional theory calculations further supported the loading-dependent selectivity, showing that changes in the local Au environment selectively modify HCHO adsorption and bond reconstruction. These results identify local Au-site density as a key design parameter governing interfacial reactivity and molecular selectivity in low-power photoactivated gas sensing.

articles.title: Nano-Optical Switching of Photochromic Material through Ultraviolet and Visible Plasmon Nanofocusing
articles.abstract: Optical control of photochromic properties is essential for optoelectronic devices. The manipulation of such properties has been limited to the microscale because of the wave nature of light; however, scaling down the volume is highly demanded for the future nanosized devices. Herein, we demonstrate optical switching at the nanoscale in an organic photochromic material. Photochromic materials such as diarylethene derivatives exhibit two different states with distinct optical and electronic properties under ultraviolet (UV) and visible light irradiation. We employed plasmon nanofocusing for optical switching of photochromic materials, which allowed the creation of a nanolight source at the apex of a tapered aluminum structure over a broad frequency range. We achieved in situ wavelength control between visible and UV light at the nanoscale for photochromic reactions. Using this technique, we demonstrated nanoscale optical switching between the two states of diarylethene. The switching performance was confirmed for at least nine cycles without degradation. This demonstration would constitute a significant step toward next-generation optoelectronic devices and benefit diverse scientific fields owing to the broad wavelength tunability of plasmon nanofocusing.

articles.title: Polarization-Controlled Dual-Mode Switching in van der Waals α-In2Se3 Memristors for Multitime-Scale Reservoir Computing
articles.abstract: Electrochemical-metallization (ECM) memristors can implement both nonvolatile memory switching and volatile threshold switching, making them attractive for neuromorphic and reservoir computing; however, the stochastic formation of metallic filaments causes variability in the threshold voltage and switching instability. Here, we report a van der Waals α-In2Se3-based ferroelectric-semiconductor ECM (FeS-ECM) memristor in which a bidirectionally polarized α-In2Se3 layer is inserted between the inert electrode and the switching layer. The out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization, programmed through a decoupled in-plane poling terminal, deterministically selects within the low-compliance operating regime between nonvolatile bipolar memory switching and volatile unipolar threshold switching within a single device, with a coefficient of variation in the set voltage of 4.7% and stable operation over more than 9000 cycles. Exploiting these two modes, a single α-In2Se3 platform exhibits both the volatile reservoir dynamics and the nonvolatile conductance modulation required for the readout weights of a physical reservoir-computing system, in which the pulse width electrically programs multiple relaxation time constants. This pulse-width multitime scale reconfigurability enables efficient temporal information processing, demonstrated through MNIST classification and chaotic time-series prediction.

articles.title: Shield-and-Amplify Nanoparticle Vaccines Retune Immunodominance for Broad Protection against SARS-CoV-2
articles.abstract: Antigenic variation severely constrains the durability and breadth of vaccine-induced protection against rapidly evolving viruses. Although conserved epitopes can support cross-variant immunity, antibody responses to viral glycoproteins are often biased toward exposed, mutable immunodominant epitopes, leaving conserved protective sites subdominant. We previously identified a cryptic, conserved class 5 epitope (the 6D6/7D6 epitope) on the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) capable of eliciting broad cross-neutralization. Here, we present a modular “shield-and-amplify” nanoparticle vaccination strategy to redirect immunodominance toward this subdominant epitope. We engineered site-specific N-linked glycans─alongside the native N343 glycan to mask variable immunodominant regions while preserving accessibility to the class 5 epitope. The resulting glycan-masked RBD antigen (RGM) was displayed on p239 nanoparticles via nanobody-mediated assembly, yielding multivalent RGM@p239 immunogens. Antigenic profiling revealed that glycan shielding preserved recognition by 6D6 and 7D6 antibodies while reducing binding of representative class 1–4 antibodies by at least 80%. In immunized animals, RGM@p239 enriched 7D6-competitive serum antibodies blocking approximately 70–80% of serum binding to RGM and broadened cross-variant neutralization against 8 representative variant strains, including detectable activity against Omicron lineages. Furthermore, RGM@p239 reduced disease severity after Omicron EG.1 challenge in a hamster model. These results support a model in which glycan shielding and nanoparticle multivalency act as complementary immune-focusing modules: shielding attenuates competing responses, while multivalency amplifies responses to conserved subdominant epitopes. This study establishes a nanovaccine design strategy to address antigenic variation by focusing immunity on conserved viral vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Silencing MSR1 in Macrophages Attenuates the Cochlear Foreign Body Response and Preserves Electrode–Neural Interface
articles.abstract: Cochlear implantation (CI) provides effective auditory rehabilitation for patients with severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss. Implantation can nevertheless induce local foreign body response (FBR) and cochlear fibrosis, motivating strategies to reduce tissue reactions and preserve cochlear integrity. Macrophages play a key role in FBR, but their functions are multiple and stage-dependent, and indiscriminate intervention may aggravate cochlear injury. Therefore, more precise strategies are needed to modulate macrophage-mediated FBR after CI. Here, through transcriptomic profiling of cochlear tissues from rats 30 days after cochlear implantation, we identified macrophage scavenger receptor 1 (MSR1) as a prominent signature after CI. In vitro assays further verified the role of MSR1 in reshaping macrophage phenotype and inflammatory activation. To achieve targeted MSR1 regulation in the cochlea, we engineered iRGD-modified extracellular vesicles to deliver siMSR1 (iRGD-EV/siMSR1). iRGD modification enhanced macrophage uptake of EV and enabled efficient siRNA delivery. In a rat CI model, local administration of iRGD-EV/siMSR1 reduced cochlear fibrotic tissue formation and decreased fibrosis-related protein expression. Moreover, iRGD-EV/siMSR1 preserved spiral ganglion neurons and myelin structures, contributing to residual hearing protection after implantation. Early stage analysis at 7 days after implantation showed that iRGD-EV/siMSR1 suppressed macrophage inflammatory activation, reduced TGF-β1-related profibrotic signaling, regulated matrix remodeling, and limited early apoptosis. These findings identify MSR1 as a promising molecular target for cochlear implant-induced FBR and support iRGD-EV/siMSR1 as a potentially translatable strategy for attenuating cochlear fibrosis and preserving the cochlear neural interface, also highlighting the importance of considering neural health when modulating macrophage-mediated responses to cochlear implants.

articles.title: Switching of Exciton-Polaritons in Covalent Organic Framework-Based Optical Resonators through Interaction with the Molecular Environment
articles.abstract: We report a demonstration of a covalent organic framework (COF) integrated into an optical cavity for the realization of exciton–polaritons and their reversible switching through changes in the surrounding molecular environment. Films of COF nanoplates were integrated into Fabry–Pérot resonators engineered to achieve spectral matching between cavity modes and COF excitonic transitions, yielding strong light–matter coupling with a Rabi splitting above 300 meV. The cavity architecture preserves accessibility of the porous framework, enabling interaction with guest molecules. The potential of this interplay is shown by exposing the resonators to water vapor, which induces both a redshift and a pronounced reduction of the COF optical absorption. The observed hypochromic effect drives a reversible shift from strong to weak coupling, effectively switching exciton–polaritons on and off, as guest molecules are desorbed from or adsorbed in the reticular material host. The process is reversible upon desorption, with preservation of structural and optical integrity. These results establish COFs as a versatile platform for chemically tunable polaritonic systems, opening avenues for responsive photonic devices, sensing, and control of light–matter interactions in nanostructured materials.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Responsive Electroactive Polyetheretherketone Scaffold Promotes Bioenergetic Bone Regeneration by Regulating Mitochondrial Permeability Transition Pores
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction and energy metabolic imbalance in senescent bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are critical pathological foundations for senile bone regeneration. Existing therapeutic strategies suffer from a lack of active mitochondrial bioenergetic driving forces, failing to effectively reverse energy metabolic suppression of senescent BMSCs. Here, an ultrasound-activated electroactive scaffold was constructed by anchoring barium titanate-transition metal carbide (MXene@BaTiO3) heterojunctions on the surface of polyetheretherketone (PEEK) to reactivate mitochondrial energy metabolism and promote bone regeneration under senescence-associated bone loss conditions. These heterojunctions adhere to BMSC membranes and generate electrical stimulation upon ultrasound stimulation, which significantly inhibits abnormal opening of mitochondrial permeability transition pores (mPTP), reduces leakage of mtDNA and Cyt c, and maintains membrane potential stability. Mechanistic investigations reveal that electrical stimulation activates the PI3K/Akt/MDM2 signaling axis to promote the degradation of accumulated p53, which relieves the competitive binding of p53 to TRAP1, thereby restoring TRAP1-CypD-mediated mPTP gating and mitochondrial homeostasis. Consequently, this ultrasound-activated electroactive scaffold drives mitochondrial energy metabolism and osteogenic differentiation of senescence-like BMSCs in vitro, which is further confirmed in a rat model. These results demonstrate the potential of this electroactive scaffold as a regulator of mitochondrial energy metabolism for senescence-associated bone regeneration.

articles.title: Element-Resolved Solute-Trapping Competition Governs Nonmonotonic Grain Selection during Laser Powder Bed Fusion
Influence of Minor Alloying Elements and Impurities on Long-Range Ordering Kinetics in Ni-Cr-Based Alloys
Integrated Anode–Current Collector and High-Loading Cathode: Enabling High-Utilization Mg Metal Pouch Cells
Quantifying Lithium Plating and Mechanical Degradation in Silicon-Carbon Composite Anodes: A Reaction Competition-Driven Multiphysics Framework
Acknowledging Animal Agency: An Interdisciplinary Perspective on Giving Captive Animals Greater Freedom to Act
articles.abstract: Interest in the notion of animal agency is growing rapidly in different fields of academic inquiry. A wide range of disciplines are working to articulate an understanding of animals in fundamentally active terms, as creatures capable of shaping the way they engage with the world through exertion of choice, competence, and control. This review offers an integrated perspective on this development, outlining relevant discussions of animal agency in animal science as well as the social sciences and humanities, followed by an array of practical strategies for increasing the agency of animals in human care. The growing literature in these fields suggests that giving animals greater freedom to act and live as they prefer may in due course transform their role in science and society and substantially improve their well-being as a result.

articles.title: Evolution of 3D Genome Organization: Mechanisms, Regulation, and Comparative Genomics
articles.abstract: How 3D genome architecture varies across species, how it is encoded by molecular mechanisms and genomic sequence, and how it shapes animal evolution are questions that have become tractable only recently. Rapidly expanding chromatin-conformation data sets, chromosome-scale genome assemblies, and advances in computational modeling now enable comparative 3D genomics across broad phylogenetic scales. Here we review recent progress in 3D genome evolution, tracing how chromosome territories, polarized chromosome arrangements, compartments, and topologically associating domains have diversified across lineages. We examine the molecular and sequence determinants of this diversification, including condensin II, CCCTC-binding factor, alternative insulators, repetitive sequences, and large-scale chromosome rearrangements, and consider how architectural change may influence gene regulation, phenotypic divergence, and speciation. Finally, we discuss phylogeny-aware statistical models, sequence-to-contact map predictors, and emerging multimodal foundation models as complementary computational frameworks for identifying conserved and lineage-specific folding patterns, prioritizing sequence changes with predicted architectural effects, and generating testable evolutionary hypotheses.

articles.title: Setting the Pace of Epigenetic Aging in Mammals: A Hierarchy from Species to Individual
articles.abstract: Epigenetic clocks have transformed aging research by providing accurate molecular measures of biological age, but the factors regulating their pace across mammals remain unclear. This review proposes a hierarchy of regulation: species-level determinants that set intrinsic aging rate and lifespan, as well as individual-level modifiers acting within species. Comparative analyses show developmental tempo, rather than body mass, anchors species differences. Across individuals, caloric restriction and other perturbations of the insulin-like growth factor 1 nutrient-sensing axis alter epigenetic aging rate, whereas torpor models suggest body temperature, rather than metabolic rate per se, acts as the pacemaker. Gonadal hormones, reproduction, social environment, and ecology also contribute, with applications in livestock and wildlife conservation highlighted as means to capitalize on age-associated traits and exposures. Together, this work shows epigenetic clocks are far more than a yardstick for biological time; they reveal the multifaceted biology, and its hierarchy, that sets the pace of aging in mammals.

articles.title: Sex Differences in Biological Responses: Mechanisms, Evolution, and Environmental Interactions
articles.abstract: Sex-specific phenotypes arise from complex interactions among genetic, epigenetic, hormonal, and environmental factors throughout development and across the lifespan. Although sex-determination mechanisms establish gonadal identity, they also initiate differences in sex-specific responses beyond reproductive tissues. Here, we review the diverse genetic and environmental sex-determination systems, highlighting how these mechanisms regulate sex-specific gene expression. We further examine the roles of hormones, epigenetic modifications, and environmental factors in shaping physiological, behavioral, and life-history differences between the sexes. Early-life conditions, social environments, and reproductive strategies further modify these trajectories, producing substantial within- and among-species variations in sex-specific phenotypes during development and aging. By integrating evidence across vertebrates and invertebrates, we propose a unified framework in which sex-specific phenotypes emerge from dynamic interactions between genomes, epigenomes, and environments. This comparative perspective discusses conserved and lineage-specific principles underlying the evolution, phenotypic plasticity, and adaptive significance of sex differences across diverse taxa.

articles.title: Toxicological Susceptibility as a Complex Genetic Trait: Implications for Risk Assessment
articles.abstract: Safety limits on exposure to hazardous chemicals are typically treated as uniform across populations, but substantial variability exists between individuals. This review argues that susceptibility to chemical exposure should be understood as a complex genetic trait shaped by polygenic architecture, environmental context, and biological modifiers such as sex. Drawing on evidence from animal models, human-relevant test systems, and comparative genomics, we show that variation in toxic response is structured, heritable, and frequently predictable. We critically evaluate the limitations of traditional toxicology, which relies on simplified models and average responses, and highlight how this deterministic approach fails to capture population-level risk. We further examine genotype × sex interactions and the contribution of rare variants to extreme sensitivity. Finally, we discuss emerging risk assessment frameworks, including population-based and probabilistic approaches, and consider their implications for regulatory decision-making. Recognizing toxicological susceptibility as a complex trait provides a more realistic and protective basis for chemical risk assessment.

articles.title: Why Felids Are Prone to Chronic Kidney Disease: Micronutrient Cycling, Lipid Biology, and Water Conservation
articles.abstract: The prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in aging felids is three- to four-fold higher than in other mammals, including humans. Regardless of species, serum and urinary biomarkers of CKD become effective only when little can be done to reverse progression. We propose that felids, as super water conservers and obligate hyper-carnivores, are naturally prone to form cytoplasmic lipid droplets (LDs) in their kidney cells, which predisposes felids to age-associated CKD. Furthermore, we offer a novel mechanistic basis for renal LD formation in felids. Presence of LDs in felid urine—lipuria, which is uncommon in all other mammals—could be the earliest biomarker of metabolic events in kidney cells that underpin CKD. Felids have unique anatomical, physiological, nutritional, and metabolic features, including synthesis and subsequent excretion of felinine together with branched-chain fatty acids into urine. These features offer a unique opportunity for early intervention but also are of interest in the context of comparative biology, nephrology, and renal disease.

articles.title: Aging Stem Cells and Somatic Mosaicism as a Precursor to Malignant Transformation
articles.abstract: Adult stem cell aging and malignant transformation are inextricably linked through a complex interplay of intrinsic cellular dysfunction and extrinsic microenvironmental remodeling. Together, these factors generate a positive feedback loop that drives quiescent, tightly regulated stem cells toward dysregulated, mutation-enriched states characterized by a loss of lineage fidelity. This review synthesizes literature detailing how age-associated alterations, including epigenetic drift, genomic instability, telomere dynamics, and metabolic rewiring, converge with extracellular matrix remodeling, paracrine shifts, and inflammaging to foster permissive tissue niches. Furthermore, we discuss the mechanisms and consequences of somatic mosaicism, notably clonal hematopoiesis, in relation to malignant risk. Finally, we highlight current and potential clinical interception strategies designed to mitigate clonal expansion, optimize risk assessment, and disrupt oncogenesis across diverse human tissues.

articles.title: Beads, Springs, and Fields: Particle-Based Versus Continuum Models in Cell Biophysics
articles.journal: Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics
articles.abstract: Quantitative modeling has become an essential tool in modern biology, driven by advances in both experimental techniques and theoretical frameworks. Powerful high-resolution techniques now provide detailed datasets spanning molecular to tissue scales, allowing visualization of cellular structures with unprecedented detail. In parallel, developments in soft and active matter physics have established a robust theoretical basis for describing biological systems. In this context, two main modeling paradigms have emerged: particle-based models, which explicitly represent discrete components and their interactions, and continuum models, which describe systems through spatially varying fields. We compare these approaches across biological scales, highlighting their respective strengths, limitations, and domains of applicability. To keep our discussion biologically relevant, we focus on five systems of fundamental importance: the cytoskeleton, membranes, chromatin, biomolecular condensates and tissues. With this review, we aim to provide a framework for both theorists and experimentalists to select appropriate modeling strategies, and highlight future directions in biophysical modeling.

articles.title: Insight into Glass Problems from Machine-Learned Softness
articles.journal: Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics
articles.abstract: We are taught that liquids flow while solids don’t. But as liquids are supercooled below their freezing temperatures, their dynamics become increasingly slow until their flow becomes undetectable on reasonable timescales—this is the glass transition. Conversely, when glasses are put under mechanical load, they can flow very sluggishly—this is plasticity. In both of these glass problems, flow involves microscopic hops, in which constituent particles change their neighbors. For decades, no link between local structure and hops was found for either of these two glass problems, but it is easily detected using machine learning. We review a machine-learned local structural quantity, softness, which is predictive of hops, describing what it teaches us about both glass problems.

articles.title: 3D Scene Graphs: Open Challenges and Future Directions
articles.journal: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems
articles.abstract: 3D scene graphs (3DSGs) have emerged as a powerful representation for spatial AI by combining geometric grounding with semantic and relational abstractions of the environment. Their expressiveness has made them relevant to a broad range of problems in robotics and computer vision, including manipulation, navigation, task planning, scene understanding, and many others. However, the field remains fragmented: Different communities adopt distinct formulations, construction pipelines, and evaluation protocols, making it difficult to compare methods, identify common assumptions, and assess remaining challenges for robust real-world deployment. This survey provides a unified and critical review of 3DSGs, with particular emphasis on open challenges and future directions. We first formalize 3DSGs under a common definition and analyze the principal modeling choices that characterize existing formulations, including node and edge attributes, hierarchical structure, dynamic scene representations, and affordance-aware extensions. We then review how 3DSGs are built from raw sensory observations, discussing the most common terminologies, conventions, and techniques. Finally, we examine downstream applications and evaluation strategies, from intrinsic graph quality to task-level performance. To support the community, we also provide a dedicated website that organizes and extends the surveyed content, accessible at https://3dscenegraphs.com .

articles.title: Wildfire Smoke Chemistry, Impacts, and Interactions with the Atmosphere, Biosphere, and Built Environment
articles.journal: Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences
articles.abstract: ▪ Wildfire events are increasing in intensity and frequency around the globe, and the resulting smoke degrades air quality. Following emission, particulate matter and reactive gases in smoke chemically transform during transport through the near- (hours), mid- (days), and far-field (weeks). The chemical composition of the smoke, its intensity, and subsequent human exposure will vary as a function of not only the properties of the original wildfire but also the subsequent atmospheric chemistry. This chemistry impacts particles, ozone, volatile organic compounds, and other air toxics in urban and rural regions, and thus affects human and ecosystem health. This review synthesizes recent work and identifies key knowledge gaps in the atmospheric chemistry of the smoke plume, smoke composition from fires at the wildland-urban interface, smoke-building interactions and remediation approaches to improve indoor air, and biosphere-atmosphere exchange, including effects on plant productivity and gas exchange. Wildfire smoke is chemically complex with gases and particles that dilute, react, and transform over timescales ranging from minutes to weeks. ▪ Wildfire smoke enhances production of ozone and particulate matter in cities, increasing urban air pollution. ▪ Smoke infiltrates buildings, exposing occupants to pollutants during and after the smoke event, highlighting research needs on wildland-urban interface fires. ▪ Ecosystem productivity can increase or decrease in response to smoke depending on the intensity and location, raising concerns about future crop yield and quality.

articles.title: How I Found Joy Doing Science in India
articles.abstract: Here I recount with pleasure the twists and turns in my academic career and reflect on the many serendipitous events that have shaped the trajectory of my life. Beginning with my twin loves, molecular biology and animal behavior, I describe how I navigated between these disparate passions. Extreme fondness for the organisms and concepts I studied, a relentless desire to live and work in India with all its rewards and limitations, and a determination to do cutting-edge research without recourse to large grants and sophisticated laboratories have been the principal drivers of my scientific life. Understanding everything humanly possible about the society of Indian paper wasps, Ropalidia marginata , became my life's goal although I got there from unexpected and convoluted beginnings.

articles.title: Malevolence in Eden: Is Agrilus mali yet Another Invasive Buprestid?
articles.abstract: Agrilus mali Matsumura, native to northeast Asia, is now widespread in western China and Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region and is knocking on the door of central Asia, the Garden of Eden for the ancestor of domestic apples. The interpretation of invasions poses many challenges: Where did the species originate, how did it arrive, what are the host plants at risk, and was it always present but very rare? We review the evidence for range expansion in A. mali and how it most likely spread. We highlight what has been learned since the invasion and devastation in outbreak areas but are critical of what has not been done well and needs to be done better to put mitigation measures on a firm foundation. An integrated approach to infestations centered on timely pruning of A. mali –infested branches is highly effective for management. On balance, the evidence suggests A. mali is destined to be yet another invasive buprestid.

articles.title: Rapidly Evolving Insulin Landscape: Ultrashort Acting and Ultralong Acting
articles.abstract: Since the discovery of insulin in 1921, there has been remarkable evolution in insulin treatment for diabetes, with modern insulin analogues utilizing highly engineered recombinant technology. The purpose of this review is to focus on two revolutionary developments in contemporary insulin therapy: once-weekly ultralong-acting basal insulins and ultrashort-acting bolus insulins. Insulin icodec and insulin efsitora alfa represent a unique shift in basal insulin delivery, offering the convenience of once-weekly administration, flat pharmacokinetic profiles, and glycemic efficacy and safety comparable to those of daily basal analogues while reducing injection burden and improving patient satisfaction. With regard to bolus therapy, faster-acting aspart and ultrarapid lispro achieve accelerated absorption through novel excipient engineering, enabling more flexible mealtime dosing and improved postprandial glucose control compared to their traditional counterparts. Looking ahead, there are promising innovations on the horizon, including glucose-responsive insulins, artificial intelligence–driven automated insulin delivery, and the continued pursuit of oral insulin. Together, these advances represent an accelerating trajectory toward more physiological, convenient, and, most importantly, safe insulin therapy.

articles.title: Multiscale Molecular Simulations in the Age of Exascale Computing
articles.abstract: The interior of living cells is highly crowded with proteins, nucleic acids, and metabolites—a setting that simultaneously demands large system sizes and long simulation timescales. Exascale computing, now realized on modern supercomputers, offers a qualitatively new opportunity to address this challenge. In this review, we examine how multiscale molecular dynamics simulations—spanning all-atom, coarse-grained, and ultra-coarse-grained representations—are transforming our understanding of macromolecular crowding and liquid–liquid phase separation. We survey recent advances in force-field development, machine-learning-assisted system construction, and high-performance computing–optimized molecular dynamics engines, with particular attention to how these tools make large-scale simulations practically feasible. Key physical insights discussed include the interplay between excluded volume and nonspecific sticky interactions, crowding-induced slowdown of diffusion, metabolite-binding kinetics, and the regulatory mechanisms governing biomolecular condensate formation and maturation. We outline how exascale platforms, integrated with machine learning and experimental data, are bringing predictive whole-cell simulations within reach.

articles.title: Anatomy and Physiology of Vascular Sphincters in the Brain
articles.abstract: Brain precapillary sphincters (PSs) are located at the point where the penetrating arteriole meets the first-order capillary. Sphincters link blood flow in the capillaries to arteriolar inflow. The sphincters are encircled by contractile mural cells that can control the length and width of the enclosed vessel segment in both directions. Hemodynamic consequences include the ability of PSs to generate the largest changes in cerebrovascular flow resistance of all brain vessel segments. Using two-photon microscopy and genetically encoded reporters, we have revealed the physiology of sphincters. Our work has shown that sphincters can increase their diameter by approximately 30% within a few seconds, enabling rapid control of capillary blood flow over a wide dynamic range. In this article, we discuss the morphology and functions of sphincters, outlining their central role in rapidly adjusting blood flow in the microcirculation and protecting brain tissue against blood pressure variations in the cardiac cycle.

articles.title: Tackling the Commercial Determinants of Obesity: A Review of Key Policies and Strategies
articles.abstract: A growing body of evidence demonstrates that commercial entities play an important role in shaping the prevalence, incidence, and distribution of obesity. This narrative review examines policy solutions to address the commercial determinants of obesity. We describe how five business sectors (food, beverages, and agriculture; media and entertainment; sports and recreation; transportation; and medical care and pharmaceuticals) shape obesity prevalence through three key behavioral pathways: diet, physical activity, and use of medical care. We then examine four categories of tools available to national and subnational governments to address the commercial determinants: legal and regulatory measures, fiscal policies, market governance mechanisms, and litigation. Finally, we discuss three strategies that can support the successful implementation of these measures: building cross-sectoral support, limiting undue influence in policymaking processes, and designing policies informed by precedent and designed to withstand challenges. We conclude by highlighting key insights for policymakers seeking to make measurable progress in preventing and reducing obesity.

articles.title: A Statistical Perspective on Fairness in Insurance Pricing
articles.journal: Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application
articles.abstract: Fairness is context dependent and multifaceted. Many jurisdictions prohibit insurers from discriminating on sensitive characteristics, such as race or gender, in insurance pricing. However, some direct or indirect discrimination is inevitable: Allowed rating factors and protected characteristics are associated. As solidarity (risk pooling) and actuarial fairness (premiums proportional to expected losses) have always formed the core tension in insurance pricing, causality has recently emerged as a third essential fairness dimension. We present the dominant unfairness mitigation approaches: autocalibration, which reduces cross-subsidies; discrimination-free insurance pricing and its extensions, which mitigate proxy effects; and optimal transport approaches, which eliminate disparities. We situate the methods within a broader taxonomy of fairness methodologies. We discuss some statistical challenges to implementing antidiscrimination regulation, including the choice of sensitive characteristics, measurement under data privacy, diagnosis of unfairness in finite sample, and generalization beyond an insurer's portfolio.

articles.title: Multimodal Statistical Analysis in Neuroscience
articles.journal: Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application
articles.abstract: Multimodal analysis in neuroscience has become increasingly important as brain research comes to rely more heavily on integrated analysis of multiple neuroimaging modalities and complementary data sources. In this review, we adopt a statistics-centered perspective, organizing the literature around three core scientific questions: cross-modal association, which focuses on characterizing shared structure and dependence across modalities; outcome association and prediction, which examine how multimodal signals contribute to clinical and behavioral outcomes; and brain causal analysis, which seeks to identify directed effects and mechanistic pathways. We then discuss some emerging trends, especially the integration of unstructured, nontabular data such as clinical and radiology reports, and the growing heterogeneity of data collected across multiple cohorts, sites, and acquisition protocols. Our central message is that multimodal neuroimaging analysis goes beyond simple data fusion and requires a principled statistical foundation, one that enables clear problem formulation, provides valid and efficient inference, and ensures robustness, as modern neuroimaging and complementary data become more complex and heterogeneous.

articles.title: Statistical Challenges in the Sky: Distribution Functions, Data, and Inference for Stellar Systems
articles.journal: Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application
articles.abstract: Astrostatistics lies at the interface of astrophysics and statistics and has been growing for over two decades. Reasons for this growth include big datasets in astronomy that are often publicly available, the use of physically motivated mathematical models in inference, and the need for innovative and efficient statistical and computational methods. To highlight the kinds of statistical challenges and opportunities available in astrostatistics, we focus in this review on a specific type of astronomical objects called globular clusters. These star clusters are some of the oldest objects in the universe and are deceptively simple in appearance. In the context of studying them, we introduce and highlight challenges and opportunities related to modeling, data, inference, and computation that should be of interest to statisticians. We hope this review will inspire statisticians to become involved not only in the study of globular clusters but also in astrostatistics.

articles.title: Sub-second dopamine reinforcement shapes juvenile social play
articles.abstract: Dopamine acts moment by moment to reinforce the specific actions that make up juvenile social play. Disrupted reinforcement underlies social deficits in a Shank3-deficient autism model, and correcting it in real time restores normal play.

articles.title: SIMMPYRA1 and SIMMPYRA2 suppress triple-negative breast cancer growth through selective STAT3 inhibition
articles.abstract: Reyes et al. described two new drugs, SIM1 and SIM2, that slow aggressive triple-negative breast cancer by blocking an overactive cancer-growth protein called STAT3. In mouse models, they reduced tumor growth, promoted cancer-cell death, lowered inflammatory signals, and showed little harm to normal breast cells or general health.

articles.title: Amyloid and tau display distinct patterns across Alzheimer’s in anterior caudate
articles.abstract: Kana et al. built a single-nucleus and spatial atlas of the anterior caudate across Alzheimer’s disease. Caudate pathology is mainly diffuse amyloid-β plaques and white matter tau threads. Despite no neuronal loss, they find an increase in FLT1+/IL1B+ microglial state with vascular signaling and altered gene expression in fast-spiking interneurons.

articles.title: Population-scale integration of spatial omics networks for clinical prediction and biological discovery by SPIN
articles.abstract: Liu et al. present SPIN, a framework that turns each person’s spatial omics profile into a molecular network and links shared network patterns to clinical outcomes. In Alzheimer’s disease and breast cancer cohorts, SPIN predicts dementia status and survival and points to the genes, proteins, and pathways behind each prediction.

articles.title: Tissue-to-bytes: A digital twin for single-cell omics data integration across BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network
articles.abstract: Tao et al. present NIMP, a digital infrastructure that coordinates scarce tissue, standardized metadata, sequencing workflows, and data release across the BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network. By linking physical specimens to their evolving digital records, NIMP preserves provenance from donor tissue to sequencing outputs. Three years of deployment show how this workflow-centered approach can support large, distributed biomedical consortia.

articles.title: Degradation of mucin O-glycans by a human gut symbiont requires a complex enzyme repertoire and promotes colonization
articles.abstract: Schaus et al. reveal how the gut symbiont Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron uses a coordinated repertoire of enzymes to degrade colonic mucin O-glycans. Enzymes that act on terminal O-glycan decorations are important for colonization, identifying key steps that may shape host-microbiota interactions at the intestinal mucus barrier.

articles.title: A SIRT6-OVOL2 axis governs excitatory neuron resilience to chronic stress
articles.abstract: Current antidepressants primarily target monoaminergic and glutamatergic systems, but insufficiently protect against stress-induced neuronal dysfunction, highlighting the need for mechanism-based therapies. Here, we propose SIRT6 as a determinant of stress resilience. Excitatory neuron-specific SIRT6 overexpression attenuates chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced anhedonia, despair, anxiety-like phenotypes, and circadian disruption, whereas astrocytic or inhibitory neuronal overexpression provides no comparable effect. Conversely, excitatory neuron-specific SIRT6 deletion induces depression-like behaviors and disrupts circadian locomotor activity under basal conditions. Hippocampal single-nucleus transcriptomics identifies a stress-sensitive excitatory neuronal subtype depleted following CUMS but restored by SIRT6 overexpression. Regulatory network analysis positions OVOL2 as a central transcription factor governing stress-associated transcriptional alterations. SIRT6 directly interacts with OVOL2 and modulates its stability, thereby driving transcription of downstream targets, including Nrg1. The SIRT6 allosteric agonist MDL-800 recapitulates these findings, eliciting antidepressant-like effects. These findings elucidate SIRT6's role in promoting stress resilience and support SIRT6-targeting strategies for treating depression.

articles.title: A multiple Arc tagging approach for tracking neuronal ensembles across experiences
articles.abstract: Engrams, or memory traces, are the neuronal ensembles that collectively store individual experiences. Genetic strategies based on immediate early genes (IEGs), such as Arc/Arg3.1, allow for the ensembles active during memory encoding to be tagged and compared to those active during retrieval. However, these strategies only allow for the tagging of one neural ensemble. Here, we developed a multiple Arc (mArc) system that allows for the tagging of two Arc+ ensembles. We validated this system by investigating how context, time, and valence influence neuronal ensemble reactivation in the dentate gyrus (DG). We report that similar contextual and valenced experiences are encoded in overlapping DG ensembles and that ensembles are modulated by time, where experiences closer in time are encoded in more overlapping ensembles. These results highlight the dynamic nature of DG ensembles and show that the mArc system provides a powerful approach for investigating multiple memories in the brain.

articles.title: Cryo-EM structure of RegIIIγ filaments reveals the molecular basis of its bactericidal activity
articles.abstract: RegIII proteins execute their bactericidal activity by directly interacting with target cells and inducing cell death at acidic conditions. A previous report proposed that the antibacterial mechanism of RegIIIα is to form hexameric pores on the membrane of Gram-positive bacteria. Here, we investigated murine RegIIIγ, a homolog of RegIIIα. The cryo-EM structure of in vitro-assembled RegIIIγ filaments revealed conserved hexamer stacking and a distinct protofilament arrangement compared with RegIIIα filaments. Structure-guided mutagenesis studies showed that RegIIIγ functions as a monomer rather than a hexamer. Further experiments demonstrated that RegIIIγ catalyzes peptidoglycan degradation, yet this activity is not required for its bactericidal function. Additionally, we designed an assembly-deficient RegIIIγ mutant that exhibits bactericidal activity in both acidic and neutral conditions. Collectively, our findings provided a comprehensive understanding for RegIIIγ functions, offered novel insights into the bactericidal mechanism of RegIII proteins, and developed a promising candidate for the application of antimicrobial proteins.

articles.title: Enhancer-based AAV approach for selective AADC delivery reduces motor symptoms and dyskinesia in Parkinson’s mouse models
articles.abstract: Degeneration of dopamine (DA) neurons and reduced DA levels in the brain is recognized as an underlying cause of Parkinson's Disease (PD). Levodopa (L-DOPA) is the standard treatment, but its effectiveness wanes over time and prolonged use can cause L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia (LID). AAV-mediated aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC) expression in the striatum combined with L-DOPA shows promise for symptomatic improvement but requires invasive delivery. Here, we generate enhancer-driven AAVs to drive AADC expression in key cell types and pair them with a blood-brain barrier (BBB)-penetrant capsid. Across two delivery routes and PD mouse models, cell type-specific AADC expression improves survival and ameliorates motor deficits and LID, with similar or greater phenotypic rescue than ubiquitous AADC expression. We further demonstrate the conservation of enhancer-driven AADC specificity in non-human primates (NHP). This viral strategy, combined with L-DOPA, may enable a less invasive and better tolerated approach to alleviate PD motor deficits.

articles.title: FBXO45-mediated K63 ubiquitination of HYOU1 sustains UPR signaling and promotes chemoresistance in gastric cancer
articles.abstract: The unfolded protein response (UPR), an evolutionarily conserved protective mechanism, promotes tumor progression and acquired drug resistance, yet how UPR dynamics drive resistance through post-translational regulation remains unclear. Here, we show that acquired chemoresistance in gastric cancer is closely associated with UPR activation and enrichment of heat shock proteins (HSPs). Among them, the endoplasmic reticulum chaperone hypoxia up-regulated 1 (HYOU1) is markedly upregulated during acquired chemoresistance. Immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry identified interactions among HYOU1, FBXO45, and PPM1B. Mechanistically, FBXO45 mediates K63-linked ubiquitination of HYOU1, recruiting additional HSPs under endoplasmic reticulum stress. HYOU1 ubiquitination enhances PPM1B accessibility, which inhibits dephosphorylation of the UPR sensors PERK and IRE1α, thereby sustaining persistent UPR activation. PPM1B functions as a key phosphatase of PERK/IRE1α in acquired resistance. Targeting the FBXO45-HYOU1-PPM1B axis restores drug sensitivity in chemoresistant models. These findings reveal how HSPs hijack the UPR via post-translational modifications to support tumor resistance and provide potential therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Human neocortical glutamatergic neurons revealed through multimodal profiling
articles.abstract: The human neocortex underlies higher cognition, yet our understanding of its neuronal diversity is limited by sparse access to viable tissue, inconsistent cell-type definitions, and limited multimodal data. Although single-cell transcriptomics has transformed our understanding of cell type diversity, transcriptomic data alone cannot explain neuronal function. Here, we introduce a multimodal patch sequencing (patch-seq) resource of human neocortical glutamatergic neurons spanning cortical layers 2-6. Combining morphoelectric features with spatial transcriptomic data to provide laminar context, we sampled 39 of 42 transcriptomically defined glutamatergic neuron types. This systematic approach enabled the identification of unique phenotypes for understudied populations in the human neocortex including L4 intratelencephalic, L5/6 near-projecting, and diverse L6 neurons. Human, macaque, and mouse comparisons of transcriptomically homologous L5 neurons reveal that morphoelectric differences across species were subclass specific. This dataset provides a unified multimodal reference for studying human cortical circuitry and neuronal diversity.

articles.title: Longitudinal dynamics of gut microbiota maturation and its modulators from infancy through childhood
articles.abstract: Early-life gut microbiota development is closely linked to long-term health. We characterize gut microbiota in 695 Copenhagen Prospective Studies on Asthma in Childhood 2010 (COPSAC2010) children using 16S rRNA gene sequencing of 2,689 fecal samples collected from 1 week to 6 years of age. Gut microbiota development is rapid during the first four years and gradually slows over the subsequent two years. A random forest model predicts microbial age from community composition and defines gut age-centered high- and low-maturity states. High-maturity microbiota exhibits greater alpha diversity, lower beta-dispersion, and maturity-associated network structures, reflecting enhanced community stability. We identify putative taxa with transient, persistent, or enduring associations with maturation. Pets, housing conditions, and maternal antibiotic use at birth show transient associations with maturation, whereas sibling presence and birth season show more sustained associations. 1-year microbiota composition predicts 4-year microbial maturity with modest but non-random performance. Our findings link early-life bacterial colonization and exposures to microbiota development and ecological stability.

articles.title: Retrosplenial cortex exhibits parallel directional codes and contributes to medial entorhinal spatial coding in 3D curved-surface navigation
articles.abstract: Spatial coding is well studied in 2D, but directional and positional coding across 3D curved surfaces remains unclear. Two-photon calcium imaging in freely moving mice in a cylindrical arena indicates two directional representations in the retrosplenial cortex (RSC). In one, preferred directions shift systematically around the sidewall yet remain coherent with top-platform tuning; this organization persists in darkness with reduced precision. In the other, preferred directions remain stable across sidewall positions and are largely preserved in darkness. Medial entorhinal cortex (MEC) contains fewer, less stable direction-tuned neurons than RSC but shows more precise positional coding. MEC-projecting RSC neurons carry more precise directional and positional information than the RSC population. RSC inhibition selectively degrades MEC sidewall positional precision and cross-cylinder angular alignment in darkness. These findings indicate parallel RSC directional representations and suggest intact RSC activity contributes to stable MEC positional coding during 3D curved-surface navigation, particularly with limited visual support.

articles.title: Toward a complete diploid chicken genome
articles.abstract: The repetitive and heterochromatic parts of microchromosomes and dot chromosomes have impeded the creation of a complete, haplotype-resolved chicken genome. To overcome these challenges, we employed a trio-sequencing approach, utilizing long reads from a female chick, supplemented by parental long-read data for accurate haplotype phasing. This strategy generated nearly complete, haplotype-resolved paternal and maternal assemblies, with 14 residual gaps. Telomeric sequences remain missing from two paternal and four maternal chromosomes, suggesting a still incomplete assembly. GGswu2 resolved more than 50 Mb of previously unresolved regions, predominantly within dot chromosomes. The dot chromosomes exhibit low nucleotide diversity but a high density of structural variants between haplotypes. We found that the centromere sizes and relative positions of centromere cores sometimes differ between the two haplotype genomes. These findings suggest that comparative genomics must incorporate high-resolution analyses of these dynamic and complex regions to fully understand avian genome evolution and genetic complexity.

articles.title: ZnuB as a targetable vulnerability to combat colistin resistance
articles.abstract: Plasmid-mediated dissemination of mcr genes has severely compromised colistin efficacy, necessitating adjuvants that restore its antibacterial potency. Despite their essential roles in bacterial survival and virulence, metal ion acquisition systems remain underexplored as therapeutic vulnerabilities. Here, we identify the zinc-uptake gene znuB as a key determinant of colistin sensitivity. znuB deficiency enhances both the bacteriostatic and bactericidal activities of colistin. Mechanistically, znuB deletion upregulates leuO, driving ompS1- and dsbI-mediated membrane damage and oxidative stress upon colistin exposure. Concurrently, znuB loss elevates diacylglycerol levels, inhibiting MCR activity and potentiating colistin efficacy. Furthermore, we identify farrerol and ajmaline as potential inhibitors of both ZnuB and MCR proteins that effectively enhance colistin activity. In murine infection models, combination therapy improves survival and reduces bacterial burdens. Together, these findings demonstrate that targeting zinc homeostasis represents an effective strategy for reversing colistin resistance and combating multidrug-resistant bacterial infections.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of adoptively transferred stem-like CD8+ T cells in the tumor microenvironment following vaccination
articles.abstract: Hermans et al. show that adoptive cell therapy combining stem-like CD8+ T cells with intravenous vaccination reshapes the tumor environment to promote immune infiltration and tumor control. The findings reveal how high-quality T cells and systemic vaccination can work together to overcome barriers limiting cancer immunotherapy for advanced tumors.

articles.title: XPO5 regulates ferroptosis via MITF-ACSL4 signaling to drive CRPC progression and serves as a druggable target
articles.abstract: Wang et al. show that XPO5 drives CRPC progression by suppressing ferroptosis through the MITF-ACSL4 axis. They identify an XPO5-targeting molecular glue degrader that induces ferroptosis in cellular, CDX, and PDX models, supporting its translational potential.
