Covalent sulfur-rich a-CoS5 as a sulfur-equivalent cathode material for Li-S batteries with larger gravimetric and volumetric capacities
articles.abstract: Different from the problematic elemental sulfur cathodes that suffer from severe polysulfide shuttling, the prepared a-CoS5 stabilizes an unprecedentedly high covalent sulfur content (∼73 wt %) and enables highly reversible S–S bond cleavage and reformation without forming dissolved polysulfides. As a result, it delivers an exceptionally large capacity and long cyclability, thus establishing new benchmarks for simultaneously achieving high sulfur content and long cyclability among currently reported sulfur and sulfur-equivalent cathode materials for Li-S batteries.

articles.title: Controlled Component Segregation in Vapor-Deposited Organic Semiconductor Glass Mixtures
articles.abstract: Multicomponent vapor-deposited organic glasses are essential in organic electronic applications, but achieving controlled component segregation at the nano/mesoscale remains a challenge, hindering the rational development of high-performance devices. In this study, we investigate binary organic semiconductor mixtures of TPD (N,N′-Bis(3-methylphenyl)-N,N′-diphenylbenzidine) and TCTA (Tris(4-carbazoyl-9-ylphenyl)amine). Despite being miscible in the bulk liquid state, the co-deposited glassy films of these two organic semiconductors exhibit a range of segregation behaviors, from homogeneous to clearly phase-separated structures. We employed differential scanning calorimetry and resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) to study the component segregation behavior and used the National Institute of Standards and Technology RSoXS Simulation Suite, paired with Atomic Force Microscopy, to interpret the energy-dependent RSoXS spectra. Our results indicate that component segregation in co-deposited TPD/TCTA films is due to a kinetically-arrested nucleation-and-growth mechanism, in contrast to the segregation mechanism of a previously reported TPD/DO37 (disperse orange 37) mixture which is strongly immiscible in bulk. This work provides a demonstration of tunable molecular aggregation in organic semiconductor glasses, enabling access to a continuum of morphologies from homogeneously mixed to segregated phases.

articles.title: From Benign to Fatal: Native Surface Chemistry Controls Acid-Triggered Trap Landscapes in CsPbBr3 Nanocrystals
articles.abstract: Colloidal CsPbBr3 nanocrystals can be highly emissive, yet their chemical robustness is dictated by their native surface chemistry. Here, we show that aliphatic acids interact fundamentally differently with distinct CsPbBr3 surface terminations: they are largely benign toward conventional bromine-rich ammonium-passivated surfaces but strongly destabilizing toward carboxylate-capped, Pb-rich, Br-deficient surfaces synthesized in lauric acid-menthol deep eutectic solvent (DES). In the latter case, acid exposure quenches photoluminescence and sharply shortens the lifetime, indicating efficient activation of nonradiative decay pathways. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and 1H NMR reveal a PbBr2-terminated surface in which laurate is the dominant X-type ligand, while the DES stabilizes oleylammonium in the bulk through hydrogen-bonding interactions and thereby biases the nanocrystal surface toward carboxylate passivation. Density functional theory further shows that laurate is the thermodynamically viable bound ligand, whereas protonation to neutral lauric acid renders adsorption unfavorable once the entropic cost of binding is considered. Protonation-driven ligand desorption, therefore, exposes undercoordinated Pb and Br-vacancy motifs that act as electron traps. Further transient absorption spectroscopy links this surface transformation to ultrafast hot electron loss and rapid exciton trapping. These results reveal how the same class of aliphatic acids can be benign or fatal, depending on the initial surface termination and active ligand shell.

articles.title: Induced Structural Disorder Enables High Ionic Conductivity and Capacity in Li2Fe1− x Mn x Cl4 Cathodes
articles.abstract: The development of high-energy-density solid-state batteries is aided by the discovery of ionically conductive cathode active materials which can enable the production of cathode composites with high active material loadings. Here, we show that the ionic conductivity of Li2FeCl4 can be more than doubled by increasing the structural disorder via a facile mechanochemical and low-temperature annealing procedure. We find that the metastable Fd3̅m Li2FeCl4 phase produced by mechanochemical synthesis undergoes a room temperature structural re-ordering on the scale of months, which lowers the ionic conductivity and raises concerns for the shelf-life of metastable materials. We demonstrate that the structural disorder can be “locked-in” by introducing Mn2+ into the system without significantly impacting the ionic conductivity. We further elucidate the origin of the phase transitions and the role of enthalpic stabilization on ionic conductivity through density functional theory and machine-learning force field molecular dynamics calculations. These reveal a 3-dimensional Li+ conduction pathway in the disordered structure, which is not present when the material is ordered. By engineering high-conductivity disordered, Fd3̅m, phases of Li2FeCl4 and Li2Fe0.75Mn0.25Cl4, solid-state batteries containing zero catholyte are demonstrated with high voltage plateaus of 3.7 V and capacities of 115 mAh/gCAM and 90 mAh/gCAM, respectively. Considering the high cathode loadings, we demonstrate that the materials Li2FeCl4 and Li2Fe0.75Mn0.25Cl4 can be used to produce solid-state battery cathodes with higher energy densities than that of LiFePO4, with similar cost effectiveness.

articles.title: Synergistic Bifunctional Sites Catalysis in Atomically Mixed Ir x Os1− x Nanoparticles for Efficient NO Reduction by CO
articles.abstract: The development of cost-effective alternatives to rhodium for catalytic NO reduction by CO remains urgent and challenging. Here, we report the synthesis of atomically mixed IrxOs1−x solid-solution nanoparticles across the full compositional range. The optimized Ir0.4Os0.6/γ-Al2O3 catalyst achieved a temperature at 50% conversion of 214 °C, far surpassing those of monometallic Ir (300 °C) and Os (266 °C) and rivaling a commercial Rh benchmark. Their activities exhibited a clear volcano-type dependence on the Ir content. Combining X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, in situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations, we revealed a synergistic bifunctional site mechanism, where Os sites promoted NO dissociation, while Ir sites enabled fast N−N coupling and CO oxidation, with electron transfer from Os to Ir further facilitating N2 formation. This work demonstrated solid-solution alloying as an effective strategy for designing high-performance, low-cost NOx-removal catalysts.

articles.title: Toward Multilayer Architectures in Transition-Metal/Main-Group Cluster Oxides: Ir3Sn12In3O14, Ir2.3Ru1.7Sn19O18 and Ir10Sn45O44A Homologous Series with Progressive Band Condensation
articles.abstract: A series of cluster oxides exhibiting a systematic increase in the degree of band condensation was synthesized by the reactive Sn-flux method: Ir3Sn12In3O14 (3-fold band), Ir2.3Ru1.7Sn19O18 (4-fold band), and Ir10Sn45O44 (5-fold band). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that these compounds crystallize in the noncentrosymmetric polar space groups Cm and Cmc21 and the centrosymmetric space group C2/m, respectively. Polarized second harmonic generation (SHG) measurements corroborate the bulk noncentrosymmetric nature of Ir2.3Ru1.7Sn19O18, whereas no SHG response is detected for centrosymmetric Ir10Sn45O44. The formal oxidation states were determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), and electronic band structure calculations reveal semiconducting band gaps consistent with the measured optical properties. Increasing band condensation is accompanied by a color change from red-orange for Ir3Sn12In3O14 to black for Ir10Sn45O44. Ir3Sn12In3O14 exhibits a photoluminescence emission centered at 566 nm (yellow light). These findings establish a homologous family of multilayer transition-metal/main-group cluster oxides with systematically tuneable crystal symmetry, electronic structure, nonlinear optical response, and optical properties.

articles.title: Unraveling Molybdenum Dissolution-Induced Surface Reconstruction of Cobalt Molybdenum Oxide Electrocatalysts during the Oxygen Evolution Reaction
articles.abstract: Understanding and controlling the evolution of electrocatalyst structure, chemistry, and active sites under catalytically relevant conditions is critical in developing electrocatalysts with stable and durable activity toward the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Molybdenum (Mo) is routinely combined with cobalt hydroxide electrocatalysts to tune the electronic environment of the active sites and modulate their activity, contributing to improved OER activity. However, the phenomena that underpin the enhanced OER activity of the resulting materials largely stem from Mo dissolution, and their extent on the structure and activity remains elusive. In this work, we investigate cobalt-molybdenum oxide electrocatalysts, CoMoOx, synthesized via the electrodeposition method across a range of Co/Mo compositional ratios and CoMoO4(HT) synthesized hydrothermally, to establish how composition and synthesis route govern Co-site evolution and the ensuing OER activity. Electrochemical benchmarking revealed that the high Mo content of electrodeposited CoMoOx(1:4) produces a Mo-rich surface with fewer accessible Co sites and slower charge-transfer kinetics, as evidenced by a Tafel slope of 73.1 ± 8.1 mV dec−1 and a high charge-transfer resistance of 5.74 Ω (over 4 times higher than CoMoOx(6:1)). Operando Raman spectroscopy, ex situ X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and inductively coupled plasma−optical emission spectroscopy collectively demonstrate that MoO42− dissolution begins on contact with 1 M KOH in the absence of applied potential and continues under anodic polarization, driving irreversible reconstruction of as-synthesized materials to Co(OH)2/Co3O4 sites and subsequently to CoOOH. These materials therefore function as pre-catalysts, and the working surface is determined by the starting composition rather than being the as-synthesized phase. Crucially, the reconstruction pathway is synthesis-dependent; crystalline hydrated CoMoO4(HT) proceeds via CoOOH to further-oxidized, partially deprotonated CoOOHx, at relevant OER conditions, whereas electrodeposited films form predominantly β-CoOOH as the surface species, with progression beyond CoOOH developing only partially and to an extent that scales with the initial Mo content. These findings provide a mechanistic blueprint for leveraging controlled cation dissolution to engineer defect-rich, high-performance electrocatalytic interfaces.

articles.title: RETRACTION: Seasonal Coat Colour Moult and Mismatch in Ezo Mountain Hares (Lepus timidus ainu): Phenotypic Plasticity and Snow Cover Effects in Hokkaido, Japan
articles.abstract: RETRACTION: F. Chaudhary, J. Morimoto, T. Sakiyama and R. U. Haq, “Seasonal Coat Colour Moult and Mismatch in Ezo Mountain Hares (Lepus timidus ainu): Phenotypic Plasticity and Snow Cover Effects in Hokkaido, Japan,” Ecology and Evolution 16, no. 8 (2026): e74052, https://doi.org/10.1002/ece3.74052. The above article, published online on 18 August 2026 in Wiley Online Library (wileyonlinelibrary.com), has been retracted by agreement between the journal Editor‐in‐Chief, Allen Moore; the Executive Editor, Arley Muth; the British Ecological Society; and John Wiley & Sons Ltd. The retraction has been agreed upon following concerns raised by a third party. An investigation found that several references cited within the article were invalid or could not be verified. The authors acknowledged that multiple referencing errors had been made and proposed corrections, including the removal and replacement of affected references. However, due to the extent and nature of these errors, the Editors have lost faith in the article and therefore decided a retraction is appropriate. The authors disagree with the retraction.

articles.title: The Role of Light in Mediating Physiological Stress in Small Corals Exposed to Elevated Temperature
articles.abstract: Marine heat waves (MHW) are important stressors on coral reefs, and evaluating their implications for the population dynamics of young corals has become a key research need. However, projecting the effects of MHW on the demographics of young corals is made difficult by an incomplete understanding of how their response to high temperature is modulated by light. Here we tested for the interactive effects of temperature and light on genetically identified colonies of the Pacific coral, Pocillopora spp. from 3-m depth in the back reef of Moorea, French Polynesia. The ecological implications of the responses to manipulated temperature and light were strengthened through context provided by long-term in situ records of temperature and light. Two 14-day trials were conducted in which young P. meandrina were exposed to 28°C and 31°C at six light levels ranging from 436 to 1621 μmol photons m−2 s−1. The probability of bleaching was unaffected by temperature, but it increased across the light gradient, while the probability of partial or full mortality increased with light faster at 31°C compared to 28°C. Mortality was associated with a decline in the photophysiological performance (F v/F m) of the symbiotic algae (Symbiodiniaceae) in the corals, notably as light levels increased at 31°C but not at 28°C, and at light levels commonly reached at 3-m depth. Declines in F v/F m revealed impaired PSII functionality, although values remained higher than those usually associated with bleaching (i.e., < 0.500). These results show how light can modulate the impacts of MHWs on the physiology and demography (i.e., survival) of young Pocillopora spp., and show that corals pale enough to be scored as fully bleached on the reef can contain relict algal populations that remain photophysiologically functional at elevated temperature and high light.

Estimating spatial response distances of reef-associated communities in the Wuzhizhou Island marine ranch using generalized additive models
articles.abstract: Artificial reefs are widely used to enhance fishery resources and restore degraded marine habitats, yet quantitative information on the spatial responses of biological communities to reef distance remains limited in tropical marine ranching systems. This study investigated the spatial response distances of different catch groups to reef distance in the Wuzhizhou Island marine ranch, Sanya, Hainan Province, China. Based on five surveys conducted at 28 stations from 2019 to 2021, a total of 263 species of catches were collected using five sampling methods angling, gill net, trap, diving sampling, and bottom trawling. The catches were classified into five groups total catches, reef-dependent, reef-approaching, sand-mud bottom-preference, and strong-swimming. Generalized additive models (GAMs) were fitted using the Shannon-Wiener diversity (H), Pielou evenness (J), Margalef richness (d), and the Index of Relative Importance (IRI) as response variables. GAMs were used to characterize the relationships between community indices and reef distance, with additional sampling-method-adjusted models conducted to evaluate sensitivity to sampling heterogeneity. The strong-swimming group the reef-distance smooths were nonsignificant for all indices examined; no transition response distance was reported. The estimated response distances spanned 830–1120 m for the total catches group, 1420–1560 m for the reef-approaching group, and 1100–1450 m for the sand-mud bottom-preference group, whereas a single transition response distance of 890 m was identified for the reef-dependent group. These results demonstrate group-specific spatial responses to reef distance and provide quantitative reference information for spatial assessment and differentiated management of tropical marine ranching systems.

articles.title: Sky-lit stage: lunar and solar rhythms shape the acoustic behaviour of marine mammals and fish
articles.abstract: Rhythmic lunar and solar cycles are well recognised to influence the biology, behaviour, physiology, and ecological adaptations of many terrestrial organisms, yet their effects on marine organisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the influence of lunar and solar rhythms, together with total cloud cover as a light-blocking factor, on the acoustic behaviour of nine vocally active cetacean species, one pinniped species, and one fish species off Antarctica, the sub-Antarctic region, and the west coast of South Africa. These marine organisms exhibited species-, season-, and site-specific behavioural responses to cloud cover, lunar and solar rhythms. Total cloud cover, lunar phase or solar altitude (or, on a few occasions, moonlight intensity/lunar altitude) were the most important predictors of the observed acoustic behaviour. Observed behavioural changes related to light availability were also associated with breeding and migration phenology, communication, foraging and predator-avoidance strategies of the studied animals. On the whole, light availability drives the acoustic ecology and chronobiology of marine mammals and fish, likely as adaptations to their dynamic marine environments. Shifts in acoustic and diving behaviour relative to light availability have conservation implications, as sound production may reflect time spent near the sea surface and increase animals’ vertical risk of ship-strike. These predictable chronobiological patterns provide an empirical foundation for dynamic marine spatial management, suggesting that seasonal vessel slowdowns during dark-sky cycles could significantly reduce anthropogenic ship-strike risk in high-traffic zones like the South African coast.

articles.title: A Crystalline LaCl3 Reinforced Amorphous Oxyhalide Electrolyte for Thermally Stable All-Solid-State Batteries
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) are a promising next-generation energy storage technology, but their development is often constrained by the thermal instability and high cost of solid-state electrolytes (SSEs). Amorphous oxyhalide electrolytes, while mechanically deformable, are particularly susceptible to thermal degradation. Here, we report a novel and cost-effective composite SSE fabricated by embedding LaCl3 nanocrystals within an amorphous Li–Al–O–Cl (LAOC) matrix. This unique architecture synergistically combines the high ionic conductivity of the amorphous phase with the enhanced thermal and mechanical robustness imparted by the crystalline phase. The resulting Li–La–Al–O–Cl electrolyte achieves a high room-temperature ionic conductivity exceeding 1 mS cm–1 and demonstrates exceptional thermal stability, remaining a solid powder at 150 °C, a temperature at which the baseline LAOC melts. This enhanced thermal and thermo-mechanical integrity, combined with excellent deformability, enables superior interfacial contact and stability with cathodes. The Li–La–Al–O–Cl-based ASSBs maintain stable operation at 80 °C, in stark contrast to the rapid failure of LAOC-based cells. This strategy of reinforcing a soft amorphous matrix with a rigid crystalline offers a new pathway for designing thermally robust, high-performance, and commercially viable SSEs.

articles.title: A Double-Tethered Metallacyclobutadiene Catalyst for Cyclic Polymer Synthesis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The synthesis, characterization, and catalytic polymerization results of an unprecedented double-tethered metallacyclobutadiene complex (4) are discussed. Complex 4 is active for the polymerization of acetylenes. Complex 4 polymerizes tert-butylacetylene to form cyclic poly(tert-butylacetylene). Evidence for a cyclic polymer topology comes from size exclusion chromatography (SEC) and intrinsic viscosity (η) measurements. This unusual reactivity of complex 4 toward a tert-alkylacetylene is attributed to its fluxional behavior, which arises from the double tethering of an yne-ol proligand (2) that facilitates monomer access and catalytic turnover. The preliminary scope of this complex design is demonstrated through modification of the yne-ol proligand, which afforded two additional double-tethered metallacyclobutadiene complexes 10 and 11 that are also catalytically active for polymerization.

articles.title: A Molybdoenzyme Mediates Carbon–Sulfur Bond Making and Breaking in Ergothioneine Biosynthesis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The molybdopterin-dependent ergothioneine synthase (MES) from Caldithrix abyssi is the first molybdoenzyme known to catalyze the formation of carbon–sulfur bonds. To complete its catalytic cycle, this bifunctional enzyme desulfurates l-cysteine at a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate binding site and transfers the harvested sulfur atom (S0) to the molybdenum center of a bis-molybdopterin guanine dinucleotide cofactor more than 50 Å away. Subsequently, the sulfurated Mo-center transfers the labile sulfur atom onto the imidazole ring of Nα-trimethyl histidine (TMH). Combining experimental observations from cryo-electron microscopy, X-ray crystallography, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, sequence-activity correlation, and substrate-specificity studies, we delineate the structural basis for long-distance sulfur transfer via a persulfide relay, the identity of the imidazole sulfurating species, and key sequence motifs that are indispensable for activity. Furthermore, the reversibility of MES-mediated sulfurization of TMH under physiological conditions suggests that ergothioneine may serve as a soluble reservoir of oxidizing equivalents, supporting anaerobic metabolism in deep-branching bacteria such as C. abyssi.

articles.title: A Single Water Molecule Drives a 20-Fold Acceleration in the Gas-Phase Reaction of Iodide with Ozone
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Iodine chemistry has an outsized role in the atmosphere and environment due to its highly reactive nature. Unlike chlorine and bromine, around 80% of atmospheric iodine is emitted directly from the ocean through the reaction of iodide and ozone at the sea surface. Uncertainties remain, however, in the effects of hydration, salinity, temperature, and other factors on this globally significant reaction. Using linear ion-trap mass spectrometry, a single water molecule is shown here to provide a 23 (±6)-fold acceleration to the rate of iodide oxidation. The first step in reaction of both I– and I–·H2O with ozone is oxidation to IO– with subsequent fast reactions to yield IO3–. No evidence is found for direct routes from I–·H2O to IO2– nor any incorporation of the water oxygen into ionic products. Ab initio calculations show that the initial rate-determining step for both reactions proceeds on the singlet surface with water playing an active role to lower the barrier through hydrogen bonding. Kinetic modeling based on the computed energetics is in excellent agreement with experimental measurements and enables extrapolation of this reaction to lower temperatures relevant to polar regions and the ozone layer. This analysis shows that (i) I– may outcompete I• for ozone destruction as temperature decreases, and (ii) I–·H2O reacts more than an order of magnitude faster than I• over 350 to 230 K. This work demonstrates that iodide has a previously underappreciated role in multiphase ozone destruction in the atmosphere and lays the foundation for understanding microscopic environmental influences in salt clusters and nanodroplets.

articles.title: Acetaldehyde-Mediated Direct Conversion of Air to Nitric Acid
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The sustainable synthesis of nitric acid (HNO3) directly from air via N2 oxidation is a dream reaction but remains a long-standing challenge, owing to formidable thermodynamic and kinetic barriers. Here, we report a photoassisted thermocatalytic strategy in which acetaldehyde as a key medium enables efficient N2 oxidation to HNO3 under mild conditions. Acetaldehyde is oxidized to peracetic acid over 316L stainless steel, which subsequently generates radicals (CH3COOO•) under visible-light irradiation. These CH3COOO• radicals are highly reactive and can oxidize N2 at 200 °C and near-ambient pressures (1–5 bar), affording an HNO3 formation rate of 110.8 μmol h–1 with a concentration of 13,961 ppm and an N2 conversion of 0.45% within 2 h─approximately 2 to 4 orders of magnitude higher than previously reported systems. Notably, the kinetic irrelevance of H2O enables operation in a gas-phase flow configuration, allowing continuous and stable HNO3 production and gram-scale accumulation at the laboratory scale. This work introduces a groundbreaking reaction paradigm that couples organic radical chemistry and surface catalysis, offering a scalable and energy-efficient pathway for the green synthesis of HNO3.

articles.title: Ammonia-Driven Nanoscale Surface Restructuring of Copper Catalysts during Nitrate Reduction Reaction
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The electrolyte and applied potential are known to impact a catalyst’s structure and performance, yet the role of reaction intermediates and products in driving surface evolution remains largely unexplored. Here, using electrochemical atomic force microscopy, we show that the dynamic restructuring of copper (Cu) surfaces during nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) directly correlates with the rate and selectivity of ammonia (NH3) formation. At moderate overpotentials, where nitrite formation dominates, lateral expansion of Cu terraces is observed, whereas rapid NH3 formation at higher cathodic potentials induces Cu adislands enriched in low-coordinated step sites, revealing distinct restructuring pathways that accompany the transition from nitrite- to ammonia-selective NO3RR. These transformations are rationalized by an NH3-mediated Cu dissolution-redeposition mechanism. Our results identify reaction products as active modulators of catalyst surface structure, establishing a framework for understanding reaction-driven catalyst restructuring and enabling in situ control of catalyst surfaces through the interfacial reaction environment.

articles.title: Anti -Dihydroxylation-Enabled Dual-Resolution Profiling and Imaging of Fatty Acid C═C Bond Isomers
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Lipids are essential for membrane structure, signaling, and stress adaptation. Their diverse biological roles are largely dictated by the presence of C═C bonds in unsaturated fatty acids (FAs), which vary in both position and geometry. However, unambiguous characterization and in situ mapping of these two structural features have remained longstanding analytical challenges. Here, we present a stereochemistry-preserved chemical derivatization strategy coupled with trapped ion mobility spectrometry-tandem MS (TIMS-MS/MS), enabling complete resolution of both FA C═C bond position and geometry within a single workflow. This approach facilitates rapid and quantitative profiling of dynamic cis–trans isomerization in bacteria under diverse stress conditions and, notably, reveals a previously unrecognized dose-dependent antibiotic adaptation mechanism in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a multidrug-resistant pathogen. To translate this strategy to spatially resolved analyses, we developed an in situ derivatization workflow for mass spectrometry imaging, which uncovers the spatial heterogeneity of FA isomers in proximally cocultured, clinically relevant polymicrobial pathogens. These findings highlight colony-specific spatial dynamics of cis and trans lipid isomers and suggest lipid-mediated metabolic interactions between co-occurring microbial species. Together, this integrated platform enables both quantitative and spatial interrogation of lipid isomerization, providing new opportunities to systematically investigate its roles in microbial physiology, pathogenesis, and beyond.

articles.title: Breaking the “Micro-Size Inversion” Paradox via a Surface-Chemistry-Driven Molecular Sieving Membrane for Ambient Lithium–Air Batteries
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Lithium–air batteries suffer from moisture-induced parasitic reactions and electrolyte evaporation in ambient air. A fundamental challenge is the “micro-size inversion” paradox, where H2O (0.275 nm) is smaller than O2 (0.346 nm), rendering conventional size-based sieving ineffective. Here, we report a composite membrane composed of polydimethylsiloxane and fluorinated vinyl-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF-VF) to break this selectivity barrier. By grafting 1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorodecyl groups onto a vinyl-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF-V), we establish a surface-chemistry-driven sieving mechanism. This design creates a molecular-level hydrogen-bond-repellent barrier that specifically inhibits polar H2O penetration while maintaining high nonpolar O2 flux, effectively decoupling the permeability-hydrophobicity trade-off. Molecular dynamics simulations corroborate this mechanism, demonstrating that the COF-VF exhibits significantly reduced adsorption affinity toward H2O compared to the pristine COF-V. In 40% RH ambient air, the battery equipped with this membrane delivers a discharge capacity of 3596 mAh g–1 and sustains cycling for 2700 h (270 cycles), a 10.8-fold improvement over unprotected cells. Advanced characterizations via DRT and DEMS confirm that the membrane promotes reversible Li2O2 formation and significantly suppresses LiOH accumulation. This work provides a multiscale strategy for molecular-level selective separation in practical energy storage.

articles.title: Control of Charge Carrier Dynamics and Bandgap Renormalization in CdS Quantum Dot Hybrids by Interface Polarity
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Charge carrier dynamics in wurtzite CdS quantum dots (QDs) form the basis for applications in optoelectronics and photocatalysis. We demonstrate that the quantum dynamics, energy gaps, and energy level alignments at CdS QD interfaces can be controlled by the polarity of the CdS QD surface. By performing nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations within a density-functional tight-binding framework, we demonstrate a strong dependence of photoinitiated processes in CdS QDs/graphene nanoribbon (GNR) hybrids on interface polarity. At room temperature, hole transfer is accelerated by a factor of 2 and exciton lifetime is enhanced by nearly an order of magnitude when the CdS QD surface is switched from polar to nonpolar. Remarkably, the interfacial bandgap for the polar QD/GNR hybrid is reduced to half upon heating from 0 K to room temperature, while it remains nearly unchanged for the nonpolar hybrid. At an intermediate temperature, the ultrafast charge separation is maintained; however, charge recombination shows the opposite trend relative to room temperature. The polar interface exhibits a longer lifetime than the nonpolar interface, due to weakened electron–phonon Fröhlich interaction and decreased gap renormalization. The strong and highly nonlinear dependence of bandgap renormalization and carrier dynamics on temperature in the polar QD/GNR hybrid is associated with significant structural reconstruction, which is absent in the nonpolar counterpart. The demonstrated control of excited-state processes by interface polarity and the strong dependence of the dynamics and energy level alignment on temperature provide key fundamental insights for informed design of modern materials for optoelectronics and energy conversion.

articles.title: Electron-Catalyzed Supramolecular Assembly with High Efficiency, Robustness, and Versatility
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Although catalysis is widely exploited by nature to orchestrate noncovalent supramolecular assembly and build up complex living systems, its utilization in synthetic chemistry has conventionally been limited to accelerating covalent reactions. Consequently, the development of artificial systems for catalytic assembly remains a formidable and largely unexplored challenge. Here, we present a rationally designed strategy of electron-catalyzed supramolecular assembly, wherein the electron acts as an efficient, robust, and versatile catalyst to accelerate the formation of a donor–acceptor complex. Optimization of the elementary steps and intermediate stability yields an efficient catalytic cycle, furnishing the process with both a high turnover number and operational robustness in open air. Furthermore, the electron catalysis can be readily triggered by diverse external stimuli─including electricity, light, and mechanical force─enabling precise spatiotemporal control over the assembly process and near-quantitative synthesis of supramolecular complexes. Collectively, this work establishes a well-elucidated strategy of catalytic assembly with remarkable practicality, advancing the frontiers of noncovalent synthetic chemistry.

articles.title: Empowering HFIP as a Radical Trifluoromethylating Reagent by Photoelectrochemical Iron Catalysis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The development of practical synthetic methods for incorporating trifluoromethyl (CF3) groups into organic scaffolds is of paramount importance in medicinal chemistry, as such modifications profoundly modulate the physicochemical properties of drug candidates. 1,1,1,3,3,3-Hexafluoro-2-propanol (HFIP) is widely utilized as a unique solvent in synthetic chemistry and also represents a promising CF3 source due to its high availability and low cost. Here we report an unprecedented photoelectrochemical iron-catalyzed protocol for radical trifluoromethylation that employs commercially accessible HFIP as the CF3 radical precursor. This method enables efficient trifluoromethylation of unactivated arenes, heteroarenes, and alkenes with a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Notably, this photoelectrocatalytic system is readily scalable for practical synthetic applications, and its utility has been demonstrated in the trifluoromethylation of peptides, allowing preferential modification of tryptophan residues in a chemoselective fashion.

articles.title: Functional Specialization of Coordination Spheres Enables Site-Selective Aromatic C–H Isotope Exchange in Ni Single-Atom Catalysts
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Engineering single-atom catalysts has predominantly focused on tailoring the primary coordination sphere, whereas whether distinct coordination spheres can be endowed with independent catalytic functions remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate the functional specialization of coordination spheres by constructing a phosphorus-modified Ni–N2O2 single-atom catalyst for site-selective C–H deuteration. Advanced spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations show that phosphorus is incorporated outside the preserved primary Ni–N2O2 coordination environment and support an O-linked phosphorus environment as a preferential second-sphere motif. This architecture decouples substrate recognition from catalytic activation. Specifically, second-sphere phosphorus selectively recognizes and anchors the amino group of haloanilines to dictate deuteration site selectivity, whereas the preserved primary Ni–N2O2 coordination sphere promotes H2 activation and undergoes H2-assisted regeneration following D2O-induced hydroxylation, facilitated by P–O–Ni electronic communication, thereby sustaining efficient catalytic turnover. Consequently, the catalyst achieves highly site-selective C–H deuteration of chloro-, bromo-, and iodoanilines using H2 and D2O while completely preserving carbon–halogen bonds, whereas the phosphorus-free analogue exhibits negligible activity. This work identifies the structural origin and catalytic function of second-sphere phosphorus and establishes functional specialization of coordination spheres as a general design principle for independently programming substrate recognition and catalytic turnover in single-atom catalysis.

articles.title: General Synthesis of Functionalized 1,3-Diamines from Azoarenes and Enoates via Electrochemical Annulation and N–N Bond Cleavage Followed by Chemical Reduction
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Despite the widespread utility of N-substituted 1,3-diamines across numerous fields, their selective synthesis directly from readily available feedstocks remains a long-standing challenge. In this context, we report a room-temperature electrochemical protocol for the synthesis of both symmetrical and unsymmetrical N,N′-disubstituted 1,3-diamines through electrochemical transformation of azoarenes with enoates, followed by convergent reduction of the resulting β-amino amides. This method features broad substrate scope, operational simplicity, no need for noble transition-metal catalysts, and high chemoselectivity. Mechanistic studies indicate that the reaction is initiated by the reduction of azoarenes, facilitated by HCOOH, while Zn2+ ions leached from anodic oxidation serve as a Lewis acid to promote intramolecular cyclization via ester amidation. Subsequent cathodic reduction drives N–N bond cleavage to afford the β-amino amide intermediates, thereby endowing azoarenes with dual-nitrogen synthon capability. This work provides a practical platform for the general synthesis of N,N′-difunctionalized 1,3-diamines and convenient late-stage structural editing of biomedicals.

articles.title: Hybrid Weakly Coordinated Solvents for Fast-Charging and Wide-Temperature Sodium-Ion Full Batteries
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The application of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) in wide-temperature and fast-charging scenarios is severely constrained by the performance limitations of electrolytes. Conventional ester-based electrolytes struggle to simultaneously achieve high ionic conductivity, low desolvation energy, and excellent interfacial stability. Herein, we propose a hybrid solvent system comprising ethyl propionate and ethoxy(pentafluoro)cyclotriphosphazene (PFPN), aiming to synergistically enhance the rate capability and temperature adaptability of SIBs. The relatively weak coordination ability of both solvents effectively promotes anion participation in solvation structure, significantly lowering the Na+ desolvation energy barrier and inducing the formation of stable, inorganic-rich electrode/electrolyte interphases. Meanwhile, the dual-solvent combination increases the diversity of solvation configurations and reduces ion clustering, thereby enhancing ionic conductivity. The intrinsic nonflammability and excellent film-forming ability of PFPN further enhance safety and synergistically strengthen interfacial stability. Therefore, Prussian blue||hard carbon full cells operate stably over a wide temperature range from −50 to 100 °C. Notably, ampere-hour-level pouch cells deliver a capacity retention of 86.3% after 300 cycles at 25 °C and maintain stable operation for over 100 cycles even at −20 and 80 °C. This solvent synergy strategy offers a practical new pathway for the development of electrolytes for SIBs in extreme environments.

articles.title: Interfacial Confinement Enables Conformal IrOx Nanofilms for Low-Ir-Loading PEM Water Electrolysis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Terawatt-scale deployment of proton-exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) requires low iridium (Ir) loading, which disrupts the catalyst layer’s in-plane electronic percolation network and severely degrades performance. Here, we overcome this bottleneck via an interfacial confinement strategy that electrostatically enriches cationic Ir intermediates on the negatively charged, oxygen-deficient TiOx surface, thereby redirecting Ir deposition from three-dimensional island growth to a two-dimensional conformal film on TiO2 supports. The resulting IrOx-NF@TiO2 catalyst with low Ir packing density maintains long-range in-plane electron percolation, reducing reliance on the high Ir loading typically required by conventional IrOx nanoparticle catalysts to establish quasi-continuous conductive pathways. At a loading of 0.166 mgIr cm−2, blade-coated membrane electrode assemblies incorporating this architecture feature ∼7 μm-thick catalyst layers with an Ir packing density of only ∼0.25 gIr cm–3, allowing an ∼84% reduction in Ir use while achieving performance comparable to that of commercial IrO2. This work highlights the potential of supported conformal IrOx catalysts as competitive candidates for next-generation low-Ir PEMWEs.

articles.title: Linker Steric Hindrance-Induced Defect Engineering Enables Oxygen Vacancy-Rich MOFs for Pollutant Degradation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The widespread contamination of water by emerging contaminants (ECs) demands the development of efficient remediation technologies. Although advanced oxidation processes reliant on reactive oxygen species (ROS) show promise, they typically depend on energy- or reagent-intensive activation methods. Here, we introduce a linker steric hindrance-induced defect engineering (LSH-DE) strategy for metal–organic frameworks, which enables catalytic ROS generation using molecular oxygen (O2) as a benign terminal oxidant at ambient temperature and pressure. By systematically modulating the steric bulk of organic linkers, we precisely create missing-linker defects and direct the formation of oxygen vacancy (Vo) in robust Ce-UiO-66 during a rapid 15 min synthesis. Spectroscopic and computational analyses confirm that these oxygen vacancies promote O2 adsorption and activation to yield superoxide radicals (•O2–). The optimized catalyst, Ce-UiO-66-(CH3)2, demonstrates superior activity in degrading ubiquitous ECs without requiring external energy inputs or chemical mediators. Furthermore, integration of Ce-UiO-66-(CH3)2 into a membrane-based recirculating flow-through system enabled sustained water treatment, maintaining >90% BPA removal over 48 h with a high water permeance of 101.5 L m–2 h–1 bar–1. This work presents a general and sustainable approach for designing catalytic defects in MOFs, advancing the development of green, next-generation water purification technologies.

articles.title: Low-Temperature-Mediated Lamellar–Micelle Assembly of Wrinkled Mesoporous Carbon Nanospheres with Aligned Pores and High Interconnectivity
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Mesoporous structures with highly permeable channels are of great significance for fast diffusion; however, the delicate engineering of straightforward pores remains quite limited, with most of mesostructures are tortuous pores derived from spherical micelle assembly. Herein, we explore a novel lamellar–micelle assembly approach that enables to generate a type of wrinkled mesoporous carbon nanospheres with highly interconnected divergent mesopores. In place of the conventional spherical micelles, the key for controlling such unusual assembly is determined by the construction of laminar micelles (copolymer L121/F127 composite) and heterogeneous growth on sedimented F127 seeds at a low temperature of 5 °C. The fabricated wrinkled mesoporous carbon nanospheres after template removal possess a particle size at ∼910 nm, a high surface area of 315 m2 g–1, a uniform pore size at 36 nm, as well as radial mesochannels with high interconnectivity up to 96%. Further regulation on the reaction temperature and template ratio allows for a high tunability over the pore size and wrinkle degree. When employed as a sodium storage anode, the radially aligned large-pore structure drastically facilitates charge transport and electrolyte penetration, thus delivering rate capability (142 mAh g–1 at 10 A g–1) and long-term cyclability (90.5% retention after 1000 cycles at 2 A g–1) compared to commercial hard carbon. Our work underscores a particular assembly pathway through lamellar micelles as an effective approach for building up ultrafast mesopore highways toward promising diffusion-related applications.

articles.title: Magnetic Resonance Silent Activatable Probe with Massive Signal Amplification for Rapid Detection of Inflammation-Associated Fibrogenesis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Biomarker-specific molecular imaging is vital in precision medicine. However, a fundamental challenge of most molecular imaging methods is the difficulty of distinguishing specific molecular signal from nonspecific signal arising from the distribution of the molecular probe. This is even more pronounced in metabolically active organs such as the kidney and liver where the probe may concentrate prior to elimination. As a result, almost all molecular imaging relies on delayed imaging to achieve specificity, but this constrains clinical throughput and impedes rapid assessment of the diseased organ. Here, we report a magnetic resonance (MR) probe, Fe(II)-IAFP2, which combines 3 drivers of relaxivity enhancement to decouple disease specificity from probe distribution. Fe(II)-IAFP2 is MR-silent in its Fe(II) state, producing negligible MR signal even at high concentrations. In inflammatory, fibrogenic microenvironments common to many diseases, rapid oxidation to Fe(III) activates MR enhancement, while reversible aldehyde-mediated binding to remodeled extracellular matrix further amplifies relaxivity and promotes retention at the site of tissue injury. This dual activation–retention mechanism enables robust signal generation within minutes of administration. In mouse models of renal and liver fibrogenesis, Fe(II)-IAFP2 generated disease-associated MR contrast within minutes after intravenous administration. Together, this work demonstrates an effective strategy for rapid, activity-based molecular MR imaging through the combination of pathological activation and complementary tissue retention.

articles.title: Mapping the Slow Propagation of Disorder across a Photoreceptor’s Tertiary Structure with Time-Resolved Crystallography
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Order–disorder transitions allow many proteins to shift between compact and flexible/unfolded states, thereby acting as structural switches that regulate catalysis, signaling, recognition, and allostery. We applied time-resolved serial oscillation crystallography to establish the structural kinetics of the light-triggered order–disorder transition of an animal-like cryptochrome as a six-second-long molecular movie with near-atomic all-residue spatial resolution and millisecond temporal resolution. Our 29 structural snapshots mapped the propagation of disorder across the tertiary structure motifs of a cryptochrome’s C-terminal region, triggered by a single broken D321–R492 salt bridge. The order–disorder transition followed a nucleation-propagation mechanism reminiscent of helix–coil dynamics and proceeded over up to five seconds, with regions distal to the D321–R492 trigger initially undergoing slow zero-order disordering before switching to first-order unfolding kinetics. Our per-residue density analysis provides a detailed structural-kinetic basis for understanding how order–disorder transitions emerge through directional propagation across protein tertiary structures, as occurring in signaling and many other biological systems.

articles.title: Molecular Mechanophores Based on Stress-Enhanced Exciton Transition between Phosphorescent Probes and Polymer Matrix
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Mechanophores provide an in situ and remote tool for quantifying invisible stress in polymers by photonic signals, offering distinct advantages for stress distribution analysis of large-area surfaces and instrument-free stress observation. However, achieving an ideal mechanophore that integrates with sensitive, reversible, and molecular-level stress sensing is attractive yet challenging. Here, we report practical guidance for developing ideal mechanophores that promote the molecular probe’s exciton transition for room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) under stress, through the “assisted lowest triplet (T1) state” of the adjacent polymer chain. Systematic analyses of numerous organic probes reveal that a small energy gap (ΔEM < 0.4 eV) between the probe’s lowest singlet (S1) and the polymer’s T1 states is an empirical guideline for stress-enhanced RTP. The probe-doped polymer system demonstrates not only a remarkable increase in RTP intensity of over 2000-fold upon 160 MPa but also a low stress threshold of ∼2 MPa, which is robust under 0–10 MPa cyclic pressure loading/unloading over 500 cycles. Such RTP mechanophores enable noninvasive, reversible, and molecular-level stress detection in polymers. Their doped polymers have shown potential applications in various fields for real-time sensing of stress and its uneven distribution through visual afterglow.

articles.title: Photomediated Chromium-Catalyzed Regio-, Diastereo-, and Enantioselective Deoxygenative Coupling of Activated Allylic and Propargylic Alcohols with Aldehydes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Chromium-catalyzed asymmetric Nozaki–Hiyama–Kishi (NHK) reaction is a powerful tool for constructing synthetically valuable enantioenriched homoallylic alcohols and allenols. However, catalytic asymmetric NHK-type coupling of allylic or propargylic C–O electrophiles remains largely underdeveloped. Herein, we report a photomediated chromium-catalyzed deoxygenative coupling of activated allylic and propargylic alcohols with aldehydes, enabling the synthesis of a variety of chiral homoallylic alcohols with wide structural diversity and allenols. The reactions were performed under mild conditions, and a wide range of synthetically useful functional groups was found to be well tolerated. Importantly, this method provides a straightforward way for the construction of homoallylic alcohols bearing a chiral quaternary carbon center with high ee and dr. Furthermore, stereodivergent access to all four homoallylic alcohol stereoisomers is realized through orthogonal combinations of Z/E-configured allylic alcohols and R/S-configured ligands. Combined experimental and computational mechanistic studies provided insight into the key catalytic intermediate and the origin of stereocontrol.

articles.title: Reprogramming ThDP-Dependent Enzyme for Intermolecular [3 + 2] Annulation via a Homoenolate Intermediate
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Thiamine diphosphate (ThDP)-dependent enzymes are versatile biocatalysts for carbon–carbon bond formation, yet their catalytic repertoire has been largely confined to linear homologation and intramolecular cyclizations that rely on single-site reactive intermediates such as the Breslow or ketyl radical species. Intermolecular annulation─a powerful strategy for constructing cyclic architectures─has remained elusive within this enzyme class. Here, we report the first intermolecular [3 + 2] annulation catalyzed by a ThDP-dependent enzyme, achieved through a homoenolate-mediated nucleophilic addition pathway. A phylogeny-guided enzyme mining identified a previously uncharacterized enzyme from Variovorax boronicumulans(ThDP-5), and subsequent protein engineering yielded the F484S variant, which exhibits markedly enhanced activity and exquisite stereocontrol. This biocatalytic system exhibits a broad substrate scope (30 examples), accommodating diverse substituted cinnamaldehydes and isatins to afford chiral spirooxindole lactones with excellent stereoselectivity (up to > 20:1 dr and 99% ee). Preparative-scale reactions (2 mmol) validate its synthetic utility. This work expands ThDP-dependent biocatalysis to intermolecular annulations, providing a robust and selective platform for the construction of pharmaceutically relevant spirocyclic architectures.

articles.title: Role of (Co)substrate Coordination to Iron in Activating Its Two-Electron Reduction of Dioxygen: Mechanism of Pterin Activation in Tryptophan Hydroxylase
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Many O2-activating mononuclear nonheme iron enzymes require substrate or cofactor/cosubstrate coordination to iron to form the key peroxy-bridged intermediate necessary for catalysis with no net change in the iron redox state. The role of (co)substrate coordination, however, remained unclear. Here, we leverage a pterin-dependent enzyme, tryptophan hydroxylase, for which cosubstrate (pterin) coordination can be experimentally controlled by the absence and presence of substrate, to explicitly determine the role of pterin coordination in O2 binding and peroxo formation. EPR, absorption, circular dichroism, and magnetic circular dichroism spectroscopies on the {FeNO}7 analog of the unobservable {FeO2}8 intermediate without and with pterin coordination demonstrate that pterin coordination induces new absorption bands and enhances NO affinity by 3.6 kcal mol–1 at 277 K. These new bands are pterin-to-iron ligand-to-metal charge-transfer transitions that compensate the electron donation from iron to NO upon NO binding. Extension of our findings on {FeNO}7 to {FeO2}8 evidences that pterin coordination stabilizes O2 binding and facilitates the two-electron transfer from pterin to {FeO2}8 to reduce the transition-state barrier for peroxo formation by 12.7 kcal mol–1, corresponding to a 1010 increase in reaction rate. The electron transfer pathways established herein underscore a unified mechanism for the pterin-dependent, α-ketoglutarate-dependent, extradiol, and intradiol dioxygenase families of mononuclear nonheme iron enzymes through which (co)substrate coordination enhances O2 binding via one-electron transfer within {FeO2}8 and two-electron donation from the (co)substrate (one to bound O2 and one to iron) to generate the peroxo species with no net redox change on the iron.

articles.title: Simultaneous Selective Recognition of Two Different Anions within a Hydrogen/Halogen-Bonding Cage
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The search for selective anion receptors that can function in water is a longstanding challenge in supramolecular chemistry, motivated by anions’ fundamental roles (and potential applications) in biological, environmental, and industrial processes. Here, we incorporate halogen and hydrogen bond donors into an easy-to-prepare organic cage molecule and demonstrate that this can bind anions at either or both of a halogen-bonding pocket and hydrogen-bonding pockets depending on the nature of the anions and the solvent. The halogen-bonding pocket comprising six bromopyridinium donors is a potent host for iodide anions and can selectively bind this guest in water as strongly as biological iodide binders (Ka = 43,000 M–1 measured by 1H NMR spectroscopy) with the exclusion of other halide anions. In DMSO/water mixtures, the hydrogen-bonding pockets are able to recognize chloride anions, resulting in the formation of mixed anion iodide/chloride complexes with an iodide bound in the center of the cage and chlorides in the peripheral binding sites. This demonstrates the exquisite selectivity afforded by halogen-bonding systems and reveals a general route to a range of supramolecular anion hosts that bind multiple guests in different locations.

articles.title: Solvent/Anion Codepleted Solvation Engineering Enables Low-Coordination Electrolytes for High-Energy and Low-Temperature Sodium-Ion Pouch Cells
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Widespread deployment of sodium-ion batteries demands both high energy density and reliable low-temperature (LT) operation, but is constrained by a persistent trade-off between high-voltage stability (cathode/electrolyte) and LT ion-transport kinetics. Herein, we report a solvent/anion codepleted solvation engineering strategy to construct low-coordination electrolytes through competitive anion complexation mediated by a bulky electron-deficient additive, TMSB (tris(trimethylsilyl)borate). We reveal that TMSB preferentially complexes with PF6– to suppress direct anion-Na+ coordination, while its bulky steric backbone disrupts conventional ion-pair networks and restricts excessive solvent-Na+ coordination. This strategy fundamentally boosts ionic conductivity (from 2.41 to 5.34 mS cm–1) and lowers the desolvation energy barrier (from 44.82 to 33.97 kJ mol–1). Moreover, such a strategy enables a high-modulus (2.7 GPa), inorganic-rich cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI), which can not only mitigate surface degradation, but also suppress bulk phase transitions of cathode materials. Consequently, the electrolyte demonstrates broad compatibility across diverse cathodes (NFM, NVP, and P2-NNMO) under extreme voltage (up to 4.5 V) and temperature (−40 to 25 °C) conditions. Remarkably, the scaled-up 6.8 Ah pouch cell achieves a record-high energy density of 200 Wh kg–1 at 25 °C, while maintaining 162 Wh kg–1 even at −20 °C, offering a generalizable molecular paradigm for extreme-environment energy storage.

articles.title: Specific Amino Acid Imaging of Protein Condensates in Live Cells by Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Intracellular protein condensates formed by liquid–liquid phase separation have gained increasing attention in recent years due to their key roles in many physiological and pathological processes. However, fluorescence imaging of protein condensates is limited by the bulky fluorescent tags that could perturb the protein localization and interaction. Imaging techniques that can visualize protein condensates in live cells with minimal perturbations remain lacking. Here, we develop a strategy to image intracellular protein condensates by coupling stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy to specific amino acid labeling. Different types of amino acids are found to exhibit distinct incorporation patterns in the live cells. By metabolic labeling of deuterated tyrosine-d4 and arginine-d7, ALS-related fused in sarcoma (FUS) protein condensates can be visualized with a high specificity. In addition, two-color pulse-chase imaging reveals protein translation arrest in FUS condensates under stress conditions. Furthermore, heterogeneous tyrosine phosphorylation is imaged in live cells and FUS condensates based on the Raman blue shift of phosphorylated tyrosine-d4. Thus, our technique to image specific amino acids by SRS provides a new platform to visualize the metabolic turnover and post-translational modifications of protein condensates in live cells with minimal perturbation.

articles.title: Visible-Light-Driven Dearomatization via Electrocyclic Ring Expansion for Solar Energy Storage
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Molecular solar thermal (MOST) energy storage compounds capture solar photon energy in the strained chemical bonds of metastable photoisomers and release it on demand as heat, yet simultaneously achieving visible-light absorption and high energy storage density has remained a persistent challenge. Here we introduce 9-aryl acridine N-oxides as MOST compounds based on visible-light-driven dearomative ring expansion. Irradiation at 470 nm, near the solar irradiance maximum at 482 nm, quantitatively converts these compounds to metastable 1,2-oxazepines, which thermally revert to the parent N-oxides and discharge the stored energy. The system achieves energy storage densities of up to 0.54 MJ/kg, comparable to Dewar anthracenes, while absorbing substantially more red-shifted light and offering nearly 3 orders of magnitude longer storage lifetimes of up to 1.4 years in the solid state. The thermal half-lives of the 1,2-oxazepines are tunable through para-substitution on the aryl ring and solvation, enabling up to a 1,300-fold reduction in half-life. Crucially, the 9-aryl substituent biases the transient oxaziridine intermediate toward selective reversion to the N-oxide over competing decomposition pathways, overcoming the limitations of other acridine N-oxides reported to date. This work establishes light-induced ring expansion as an effective strategy for MOST and expands the scope of viable MOST compounds.

articles.title: Soft fibrous networks overcome mechanical constraints to suppress stem cell aging and promote bone repair
Mechanocatalysis: From energy coupling to electronic behavior
articles.abstract: Mechanocatalysis harnesses ubiquitous mechanical energy for sustainable chemical transformations, but its development is hindered by conceptual fragmentation. This review proposes a process-oriented framework, deconstructing mechanocatalysis into four sequential stages: energy coupling, transduction, charge transport, and electronic behavior. This framework provides a mechanistic basis for the rational design of mechanocatalytic systems, paving the way for standardized evaluation and broader applications.

articles.title: ct: An R package for camera trap data management and multi‐method ecological analysis
articles.abstract: Camera trap surveys have become central to terrestrial wildlife monitoring, yet the route from raw detections to defensible inference is long, and in R it is walked with many single‐purpose packages. Researchers therefore spend disproportionate effort reshaping data and writing glue pipelines to move it between tools, and that effort peaks in density estimation for unmarked populations, where current guidance to compare several estimators is what the tooling makes hardest. In addition, there are few tools for behavioural and interspecific analyses of camera trap data. We present ct, an R package that carries an entire camera trap study from raw image metadata through cleaning, temporal‐independence filtering, effort accounting, modelling, and visualisation within a single tidy data structure. The package wraps and harmonises existing engines behind one consistent interface and extends the ecosystem with analyses it has lacked. At its core, ct places six density and abundance estimators for unmarked populations (camera trap distance sampling, random encounter model, time‐to‐event, space‐to‐event, instantaneous sampling, and the random encounter and staying‐time model) behind one interface, and documents for each the implementation it builds on, the data it requires, and the basis of its uncertainty interval. It also adds three analyses that, to our knowledge, no other camera trap package provides: an encounter response model that detects directed short‐term changes in one species' detection rate after another passes; a temporal shift statistic that measures how the diel activity window of a species moves between periods; and a spatial coverage surface that summarises where a species was detected. We demonstrate each capability on camera trap surveys from Benin and Taï National Park, Côte d'Ivoire. By standardising the workflow end to end, placing six density estimators behind one interface, adding new methods and providing data exploration utilities, ct lowers the technical cost of multi‐method camera trap ecology and brings reproducible analyses within reach of a much wider range of users. Résumé Les pièges photographiques sont devenus centraux dans le suivi de la faune terrestre, mais le chemin qui mène des détections brutes à une inférence solide est long et, dans R, il s'effectue à l'aide de nombreux packages à usage unique. Les chercheurs consacrent ainsi un effort disproportionné à remettre les données en forme et à écrire des scripts de liaison pour les faire circuler d'un outil à l'autre. C'est dans l'estimation de la densité des populations non marquées que cet effort est le plus lourd. Or, la recommandation actuelle d'y comparer plusieurs estimateurs est précisément ce que les outils rendent le plus difficile. En outre, peu d'outils existent pour les analyses comportementales et interspécifiques des données de pièges photographiques. Nous présentons ct, un package R qui accompagne l'intégralité d'une étude par pièges photographiques, des métadonnées brutes des images jusqu'à la modélisation et à la visualisation, en passant par le nettoyage, le filtrage pour l'indépendance temporelle et le calcul de l'effort. Toutes ces étapes s'effectuent au sein d'une même structure de données « tidy ». Le package encapsule et harmonise des moteurs existants derrière une interface cohérente, et enrichit l'écosystème d'analyses qui lui faisaient jusqu'ici défaut. Au cœur de ct, six estimateurs de densité et d'abondance pour les populations non marquées (échantillonnage par distances avec pièges photographiques, modèle de rencontre aléatoire, temps‐avant‐événement, espace‐avant‐événement, échantillonnage instantané et modèle de rencontre aléatoire et de temps de séjour) sont réunis derrière une interface unique. Pour chacun, ct documente l'implémentation sur laquelle il s'appuie, les données qu'il requiert et le fondement de son intervalle d'incertitude.…

articles.title: A lysosomal DRAM1-GLUT1-NADPH axis coordinates glucose sensing with metabolic reprogramming
articles.abstract: Li et al. identify a lysosome-based feedback system that helps cells adapt to excess glucose. High glucose increases DRAM1 and NADPH, promoting GLUT1 retention at lysosomes, reducing glucose entry and glycolysis, and shifting cells toward greater reliance on glutamine to fuel metabolism.

articles.title: Flexible triboelectric nanogenerator based tactile sensor array for machine-learning-assisted robotic
Wireless battery-free deep brain stimulators with extendable microelectrode probes
Endogenous Fe Single-Atom-Induced Short-Range Graphitization Enables Integrated Electromagnetic Wave Absorption and Thermal Management in PTFE Composites
articles.abstract: Modern electronics require polymer composites that integrate electromagnetic wave absorption (EWA) and thermal dissipation, yet these functions impose competing structural requirements. Herein, we construct Fe single-atom@short-range graphitized porous carbon (Fe1@SGC) that integrates electromagnetic attenuation and thermal conduction within a single material. Distinct from conventional exogenous metal-introduction routes, egg white serves as both the carbon source and coordination medium, enabling Fe single-atom anchoring without metal salts or organic ligands. Fe single atoms induce charge redistribution, polarization centers, and local ordering of carbon domains, synergistically regulating dielectric loss, thermal transport, and impedance matching. The multiscale carbon network further promotes electromagnetic wave penetration and multiple reflections/scattering. After incorporation into polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), the Fe1@SGC/PTFE composite achieves a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 7.92 GHz and improved thermal conductivity. This work establishes endogenous single-atom-induced local graphitization as a ligand-free and structurally precise strategy for designing single-component fillers toward integrated EWA and thermal management.

articles.title: Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
articles.abstract: Solution-processed thin films of colloidal lead halide perovskite (LHP) nanocrystals (NCs) show great potential for next-generation optoelectronic devices. However, these NC solids exhibit non-negligible size and shape polydispersity, which introduces both structural and energetic disorder. Here we resolve the exciton dynamics in space, time, and energy to elucidate the impact of disorder on exciton transport. We show that the disorder depends sensitively on the alkylamine ligand used in the synthesis. While shorter alkyl chain lengths lead to high polydispersity, longer alkyl chains lead to a narrower size distribution and smaller particles where quantum confinement becomes more pronounced, consequently leading to increased energetic disorder. Strikingly, we find that exciton transport is less efficient in NC solids with long alkyl chains, despite the fact that they have significantly more narrowly size-distributed ensembles. This demonstrates that energetic disorder rather than structural disorder is the dominant factor for predicting exciton transport within these disordered systems.

articles.title: Hierarchical Ionic Programming of Stretchable Organic Electrochemical Transistors for Dual-Mode Sensing and Computing
articles.abstract: Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) are promising building blocks for flexible in-sensor computing, yet the conflicting ionic dynamic demands of high-fidelity sensing and nonvolatile memory remain challenging to reconcile within a unified hardware platform. Here, we report a hierarchical compositional programming strategy that addresses this trade-off across a standardized stretchable OECT architecture. Regulating 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl (TEMPO)-oxidized cellulose nanofiber content in poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) tunes channel capacitance and mechanical compliance, while tailoring the supramolecular network in a deep eutectic solvent gel electrolyte dictates ion retention kinetics. This strategy establishes distinct operational regimes via tailored formulations: a rapidly reversible, low-hysteresis state for sensing and a persistent ion trapping state for neuromorphic computing. The sensing OECT enables real-time electrocardiogram acquisition with a 35.6 dB signal-to-noise ratio and 98.9% biometric identification accuracy across 15 subjects. The computing state supports temporal Morse code demodulation and Pavlovian associative learning, demonstrating application-adaptive stretchable bioelectronics.

articles.title: Resolving the Quantum Origin of Anisotropic Raman Response in Quasi-1D Ta2Ni3Te5
articles.abstract: Probing anisotropic electron–phonon interactions (EPIs) is fundamental to understanding low-dimensional quantum materials, yet isolating their intrinsic signatures remains a challenge due to the confounding influence of extrinsic effects. Here, we resolve this ambiguity in quasi-one-dimensional Ta2Ni3Te5 through a combination of angle-resolved polarized Raman spectroscopy and density functional perturbation theory (DFPT). Anomalous four-lobe angular dependences were observed in Ag phonon modes, which deviate from the real-valued Raman tensor prediction. Further, we explicitly highlight that, despite their distinct physical origins, light absorption and birefringence yield mathematically identical angular dependencies in Ta2Ni3Te5, rendering phenomenological fitting alone insufficient to identify the true physical mechanism. By employing a full quantum treatment incorporating detailed interaction mechanisms, we capture the qualitative characteristics and mode-to-mode diversity of the anomalous angular responses observed experimentally. The DFPT calculations further reveal mode-specific and momentum-resolved EPIs, providing microscopic support for anisotropic EPIs as the mechanism of anomalous Raman responses.

articles.title: Sequential Monomer Addition Regulates Hydration in Branched Poly(aryl piperidinium) Membranes for Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: The conductivity-swelling trade-off limits anion exchange membranes (AEMs) for water electrolysis. Here, we investigated how the timing of tetraphenylmethane (TPM) incorporation influences precursor assembly and membrane hydration in poly(aryl piperidinium) AEMs. Introducing TPM before backbone extension alters precursor formation and favors a more uniform distribution of hydrophilic domains in the resulting membranes. Spectroscopic and NMR analyses further associate this route with enhanced hydrogen-bond organization and increased local mobility within the hydrated membranes. The optimized P-TPM5 membrane reaches an OH– conductivity of 229.4 ± 6 mS cm–1 at 80 °C while maintaining a swelling ratio of approximately 15%. In an AEM water electrolyzer containing a NiFe-LDH anode and Pt/C cathode, the membrane delivers 5.74 A cm–2 at 2.0 V and operates for more than 1100 h in a staged-current test. These results identify the timing of branching-unit incorporation as a synthesis variable for tailoring hydration environments and improving the conductivity-swelling balance of AEMs.

articles.abstract: A new type of long-period radio transient has been discovered, consisting of a white dwarf and a Sun-like star. This system raises questions about the role of binary interactions and magnetic fields in generating the radio emission.

articles.title: A comprehensive analysis of CBER experience with AAV gene therapy IND submissions
articles.abstract: An analysis of Investigational New Drug (IND) submissions to the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) from 1995 to 2025 reveals a rapid growth in adeno-associated virus (AAV) development over three decades and highlights common reasons for regulatory holds that should be considered for successful product development.

articles.title: A single-cell lung cancer atlas reveals cellular and molecular drivers of metastasis and clinical outcome
articles.abstract: Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, characterized by extensive cellular and molecular heterogeneity. Here, to capture this complexity, we present LuCaS+, a multicenter single-cell RNA sequencing atlas comprising over 2.5 million nuclei from 454 clinically annotated patients with NSCLC with long-term follow-up. LuCaS+ consists of a discovery dataset (Berlin and Cologne, 364 patients) and an independent validation dataset (Munich, 90 patients). Leveraging this dataset, we identified tumor subpopulations with high metastatic potential associated with oncogenic signaling, immune evasion and epithelial–mesenchymal transition. In early-stage adenocarcinoma (lung adenocarcinoma), these cells showed strong prognostic value. Integrating tumor and microenvironmental cell profiles improved survival prediction across all stages, identifying distinct tumor–immune–stromal interaction patterns. These included monocyte- and fibroblast-driven inflammation (lung adenocarcinoma), VEGF–TGFβ-mediated angiogenic feedback loops (lung squamous cell carcinoma) and immune-permissive niches promoting antitumor immunity. LuCaS+ offers a clinically anchored single-cell resource to enable personalized, biology-driven therapies in NSCLC.

articles.title: Discovery and development of antimicrobial polymers
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial polymers offer an attractive tool for combating the crisis of antimicrobial resistance. This Review highlights recent advances in antimicrobial polymer development and discusses future directions, including the use of machine learning to guide polymer design and the development of scalable production methods to ensure global accessibility of these materials.

articles.abstract: Single-atom catalysts can mitigate reliance on scarce noble metals, but isolated sites can be fragile. Here a catalyst with proximal Ru−O−Cr motifs is fabricated that demonstrates proximal oxidation damping where the Cr neighbour buffers Ru overoxidation, improving stability for acidic oxygen evolution.

articles.title: Effect of two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens on the gut microbiome in a randomized phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: In a prespecified companion study (BMT CTN 1801) of the randomized phase 3 BMT CTN 1703 trial comparing two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens, microbiome diversity at engraftment did not associate with non-relapse mortality, but secondary analyses found baseline microbiome diversity was associated with clinical outcomes.
