Under CO2 regeneration, Ni/Al2O3 oxidized rapidly and uniformly with parabolic kinetics, while Ni/MgAl2O4 showed a delayed reoxidation front propagating from inlet to outlet. During a subsequent DRM step, Ni reduction propagated oppositely, from outlet to inlet due to in situ H2 production. These spatially resolved apparent kinetic measurements reveal how support composition governs local redox dynamics and reaction front propagation, demonstrating the importance of spatial resolution to resolve gradients that bulk techniques miss.

articles.title: Quantitative Pertechnetate Capture by a Bambusuril‐based Material: From Seawater Decontamination to Radiopharmaceutical Solutions
articles.abstract: Pertechnetate is central to nuclear waste management (99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$−) and nuclear medicine (99mTcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$−), yet its selective capture from saline media at ultratrace concentrations remains an unsolved challenge. Here we show that bambusuril macrocycles binds 99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$− in water with micromolar affinity, forming well‐defined host‐guest complexes. Immobilization of bambusuril on silica translates this molecular recognition into efficient solid‐phase extraction, enhancing binding under highly competitive conditions of seawater and medicinal generator eluents. The resulting material quantitatively captures 99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$− from saline solutions at femtomolar concentrations and enables direct elution of preconcentrated 99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$− using commercial nuclear medicine kit formulations. These findings establish bambusuril‐based materials as the first supramolecular platform for ultratrace pertechnetate capture from highly competitive saline media, bridging molecular recognition with applications in nuclear medicine and environmental remediation.

articles.title: Structural Evolution and Oxygen Evolution Performance of NiFe‐Based Electrocatalysts in Phosphate‐Containing Electrolytes at Non‐Extreme pH
articles.abstract: Solid/liquid interfacial interactions play an important role in electrochemical reactions when supporting electrolyte components, such as buffer anions, interact directly with catalyst surfaces. Here, we show that phosphate addition selectively suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance of Ni‐rich NiFeOx electrocatalysts at pH ∼9. Operando Raman spectroscopy and Ni K‐edge X‐ray absorption near‐edge structure/extended X‐ray absorption fine structure (XANES/EXAFS) analyses suggest that phosphate decreases a high‐potential γ‐NiOOH‐like state and attenuates the associated Ni‐centered structural response. No Fe K‐edge change larger than the experimental uncertainty was resolved during OER. The current and redox response recovered immediately after phosphate was removed, demonstrating a reversible short‐term electrolyte effect. In contrast, on‐off cycling through the Ni reduction region caused progressive loss of redox charge and catalyst material, particularly for Ni‐rich compositions. These findings highlight the importance of integrated electrolyte–electrocatalyst design for improving OER performance and durability, especially under mild pH conditions.

articles.title: Synergistic Cu–Co Sites Enabled Reversible H2 Storage and Release in Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carriers
articles.abstract: Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) offer a practical platform for reversible hydrogen storage, a critical bottleneck in the global transition to clean energy. However, their reliance on noble-metal catalysts and separate catalysts for hydrogenation and dehydrogenation cycles remains a major barrier to practical deployment. Here, we report an earth-abundant, heterostructured ternary oxide catalyst (CuCoCeOx) that enables efficient, reversible, and bidirectional hydrogenation–dehydrogenation of LOHCs such as carbazoles over multiple cycles without any pretreatment. Driven by the in situ reaction-induced reconstruction, the catalyst dynamically evolves and stabilizes functionally decoupled Cu(δ +)–CoOx interfacial sites, where the defective, amorphous CoOx nanodomains anchor bulky LOHC substrates, complementing adjacent Cu sites for reversible hydrogen shuttling. Detailed characterizations and comparison with CuCeOx and CoCeOx reveal the indispensable synergy between coexisting Cu and Co sites. Reduced Cu species facilitate the generation of low-valence Co sites, while Co species suppress the over-reduction and sintering of Cu, collectively stabilizing abundant Cu(δ +)–CoOx interfacial sites as the catalytically active centers. This dynamic structural reconstruction delivers 98.4% H2 uptake and near-quantitative H2 release, with stable performance over five consecutive LOHC cycles, substantially surpassing commercial noble-metal benchmarks.

articles.title: The blood-brain barrier imports diverse neuroprotective proteins through pathways impaired early in Alzheimer’s disease models
articles.abstract: Bioorthogonal proteomics reveals that the blood-brain barrier (BBB) imports diverse plasma proteins to specific brain cell types through receptor-mediated transport, a process dysregulated early in an Alzheimer’s model. Restoring one diminished protein, liver-derived apolipoprotein A1, rescues Alzheimer’s glial and neuronal dysfunction, recasting the BBB as an interface recruiting peripheral signals for brain health.

articles.title: Genome-wide association study meta-analysis identifies susceptibility loci informing Ewing sarcoma etiology and potential mechanisms of risk
articles.abstract: Hubbard et al. perform a genome-wide association meta-analysis combined with a case-parent trio study to identify 14 Ewing sarcoma susceptibility loci. Most loci contain GGAA microsatellites bound by the tumor-defining EWSR1::FLI1 fusion protein, highlighting interplay between inherited genetic variation and somatically acquired oncogenic fusions in Ewing sarcoma.

articles.title: Alternaria leaf spot-induced phyllosphere microbiota and metabolite interact to combat leaf spot disease
articles.abstract: Pathogen-mediated induced resistance (IR) and beneficial microbe-mediated IR are key for plant survival during pathogen attack, yet how these two forms of IR interact remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that foliar pathogen-triggered induced resistance (IR) orchestrates the assembly of a specific phyllosphere microbiota that can activate IR. Pathogen-triggered IR caused plant flavonol accumulation, which in turn enriched Aureimonas spp., especially the native A. phyllosphaerae Leaf1, in the phyllosphere endophytic microbiota near infection sites. Genetically impairing the capacity of Leaf1 to utilize flavonols reduced its proliferation during pathogen infection. Moreover, Leaf1 protected plants against leaf disease by activating IR and extended the protective range of pathogen-mediated IR. Importantly, pathogen-mediated IR-induced mobilization of native microbiota represented a common yet underrated component of plant resistance to foliar disease. These findings reveal a plant defense "relay" mechanism, whereby pathogen-mediated IR reassembles a specific microbiota that in turn activates IR to jointly combat further pathogen infection.

articles.title: Extracellular vesicle-mediated CD47 transfer rewires integrin-IGF1R signaling and tumor immune remodeling to propagate cetuximab resistance
articles.abstract: Resistance to EGFR-targeted antibody therapy is generally attributed to tumor cell-intrinsic adaptations. The contribution of intercellular communication to this resistance remains unclear. Here, we identified extracellular vesicle (EV)-mediated transfer of CD47 as a transmissible mechanism of cetuximab resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). CD47-enriched EVs circulated systemically and were associated with poor therapeutic response. Mechanistically, CD47 functions as a membrane signaling scaffold that stabilizes integrin-dependent IGF1R signaling and promotes signaling rewiring toward IGF1R. IGF1R signaling, in turn, promotes CD47-ALIX association and ALIX-dependent EV trafficking, facilitating the incorporation of resistance-associated signaling complexes into CD63+ EVs. EV-mediated CD47 transfer enhanced IGF-1R activity and conferred resistance in a cell-nonautonomous manner to remodel the tumor immune microenvironment. Pharmacologic inhibition of EV release reduced CD47 cargo loading and enhanced cetuximab efficacy. Collectively, these findings establish EV-mediated dissemination of resistance-associated signaling states as a therapeutically actionable mechanism of resistance in HNSCC.

articles.title: Multi-ancestry genetic analysis of lung function identifies candidate causal variants and improves polygenic prediction
articles.abstract: Most genome-wide association studies (GWASs) and polygenic score (PGS) models for lung function are based on European-ancestry individuals. Here, we performed GWASs in 17,738 Chinese individuals from the Dongfeng-Tongji (DFTJ) and Wuhan-Zhuhai (WHZH) cohorts, followed by meta-analysis with lung function GWASs from the China Kadoorie Biobank (sample size, n = 100,285), the Taiwan Biobank (n = 62,901), and European-ancestry studies (n = 400,102). Multi-ancestry fine-mapping pinpoints four novel candidate causal variants: one insertion (rs56381615, LINC02270) and three SNPs (rs6941411, PTK7; rs13315867, EPHA3; and rs2713769, ABI3BP). Cross-ancestry genetic correlations are high (0.682-0.811) but significantly lower than 1 (p < 0.005). Transcriptome-wide association analysis across 16 tissues identifies 1,374 genes, including PTK7, CUL7, and EPHA3 as leading novel candidates. Finally, we develop multi-ancestry PGS models that outperform existing models. Overall, this study quantifies cross-ancestry genetic correlation, prioritizes candidate genes, and enhances PGS prediction accuracy of lung function traits in East Asian populations.

articles.title: Platelet VEGFR3 suppresses activation and thrombosis through p190A-mediated inhibition of RhoA signaling
articles.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 3 (VEGFR3) is a key regulator of lymphangiogenesis, but its role in platelets remains undefined. Here, we identify VEGFR3 as an intrinsic inhibitory regulator of platelet function. Using PF4-Cre-mediated conditional deletion, pharmacological inhibition, and biochemical analyses, we show that VEGFR3 deficiency enhances platelet activation, aggregation, secretion, cytoskeletal remodeling, thrombosis, and myocardial injury. Mechanistically, VEGFR3 interacts with the Rho GTPase regulator p190A to limit RhoA activation and Ezrin/Radixin/Moesin phosphorylation, thereby restraining platelet activation. In patients with myocardial infarction, reduced platelet VEGFR3 expression is associated with increased platelet reactivity and greater coronary lesion severity. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized VEGFR3/p190A/RhoA signaling axis that restrains platelet activation and thrombosis and highlight its potential therapeutic relevance in thrombotic disorders.

articles.title: Programming intestinal immune tolerance: The pivotal role of gut microbial metabolites
articles.abstract: Intestinal immune tolerance enables the host to coexist with commensal microorganisms and dietary antigens while retaining effective defense against pathogens. The review describes mechanisms underlying the development and maintenance of immune tolerance and how the intestinal barrier and local immune system cooperate to maintain immune homeostasis. Particular attention is given to microbial metabolites, and we summarize mechanisms by which they act as key signals between the gut microbiota and the host, regulating barrier function and immune cell responses. We highlight the dynamic, context-dependent nature of metabolite-mediated immune regulation, influenced by local exposure and host factors including age, genetic background, and inflammatory or infectious conditions. Additional metabolites and regulatory pathways are discussed to broaden understanding of microbe-host interactions. Microbial metabolites may serve as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for inflammatory bowel disease and other immune-related disorders. However, broad clinical application requires further human validation and more precise intervention strategies.

articles.title: Retraction Notice to: A 20-amino-acid Cardiovirus protein exhibits cytokine-mimicry activity to regulate viral replication
The fungal phosphate starvation regulator CtPHO4 couples nutrient adaptation to host colonization through the effector NFC1
articles.abstract: Plant-associated microbes must balance environmental adaptation with virulence and host colonization to survive in fluctuating ecosystems, yet the molecular mechanisms coupling these processes remain poorly understood. Here, we identify the effector NUTRIENT-DEPENDENT FACILITATOR OF COLONIZATION 1 (NFC1) in a conditionally pathogenic Colletotrichum tofieldiae strain, whose expression is tightly regulated by both temperature and phosphate availability. By leveraging plant phosphate starvation response (PSR) mutants and phosphate supplementation, we demonstrate that NFC1 expression is driven by the internal phosphate status of the host. Notably, the fungal PSR regulator CtPHO4 represses NFC1 and colonization during phosphate starvation, while simultaneously activating canonical fungal PSR-related genes. Conversely, under phosphate sufficiency, NFC1 is strongly induced and promotes infection. This host colonization and adaptation machinery is partially conserved in a beneficial C. tofieldiae strain. This study uncovers a molecular link between metabolic adaptation and host colonization, providing a conceptual framework for understanding fungal lifestyle transitions under changing environments.

articles.title: Uncoupling hypersensitive cell death response and disease resistance activated by effector-triggered immunity
articles.abstract: Effector-triggered immunity (ETI) is frequently accompanied by the hypersensitive response (HR), a localized form of programmed cell death considered closely associated with disease resistance. However, the mechanistic relationship between HR and effective immunity remains incompletely understood. We show that the Arabidopsis cbp60g sard1 double mutant exhibits exaggerated ETI-associated HR while retaining partial resistance to bacterial pathogens, providing a genetically tractable system uncoupling disease resistance from cell death without visible pleiotropic defects. Transcriptome profiling reveals that CBP60g and SARD1 coordinate positive and negative immune regulatory programs, including activation of the Nudix hydrolase NUDT7, a downstream target that partially restrains HR. The incomplete restoration of the mutant phenotype by NUDT7 overexpression suggests that additional CBP60g/SARD1-dependent negative regulators buffer excessive cell death. Our findings demonstrate that hypersensitive cell death is genetically separable from effective disease resistance and reveal how CBP60g/SARD1 coordinates transcriptional networks to balance immunity with protection against self-inflicted damage.

articles.title: Distinct T cell subsets associated with responses to different neoadjuvant treatments in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
articles.abstract: Song et al. find that neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy maintains immunoresponsive CXCL13+ CD8+ T cells, with responders showing a shift toward a less exhausted, progenitor-like phenotype, whereas chemoradiotherapy reduces this compartment and enriches PD-1- effector CD8+ T cells. Their findings provide a cellular rationale for optimizing the sequencing of immunotherapy and radiotherapy.

articles.title: Temporal control of CAR expression by a tumor-targeting albumin adapter and logic gating enhances CAR-T cell therapy for solid tumors
articles.abstract: Chen et al. develop MANAGE CAR-T cells that employ an artificial-antigen-sensing synNotch receptor to gate CAR expression and an albumin-based tumor-targeting adapter bearing the artificial antigen for priming. Adjusting the adapter dosing schedule enables tumor-restricted and intermittent CAR expression. These temporally tuned CAR-T cells exhibit reduced exhaustion and improved efficacy against solid tumors.

Improving label-free cell classification through offline fusion of mechanical and molecular phenotypes
Photon-driven alloy nanostructures trigger paraptosis through organelle disruption
Harnessing Contact Electrification and Static Charge for Chemical Reactions: Fundamentals and Applications of Contact Electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: The chemical industry is the largest industrial energy consumer and the third-largest emitter of CO2 globally. Despite efforts to enhance energy efficiency, many chemical reactions still require significant external energy due to fundamental thermodynamic barriers. Thus, transitioning to a sustainable chemical industry requires new renewable energy or catalytic technologies that reduce energy demand. In catalytic systems, flowing liquids, moving parts, and gas separation mean local static charge is often generated on the nanoscale. This review explores the static charge formation at solid–solid, solid–liquid, and solid–gas interfaces, such as those that occur in catalytic reactions, and then extends this discussion to a deeper focus on how these generated static charges can be used for catalysis, including electrostatic catalysis, static charge electrochemistry, and contact electrocatalysis (CEC). CEC, where motion-induced charge separation leads to local static charge formation, is then specifically examined, exploring why and how it has emerged as an exciting tool to enable these green chemical transformations. The focus is to highlight the most recent developments in CEC, with mechanistic interpretation, factors that affect CEC performance, and emerging applications, and to provide outlook and guidance for the field─specifically highlighting the need to build structure–property relationships for CEC performance and static charge formation for target chemical reactions.

articles.title: Lithium–Oxygen Batteries: Fundamental and Practical Considerations
articles.abstract: Lithium–oxygen batteries (LOBs) have emerged as a compelling next-generation energy storage technology for aviation due to their high theoretical energy densities and the use of abundant oxygen as a cathode reactant. Unlike conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), which are limited by the mass of intercalation materials and one-electron redox processes, LOBs leverage multielectron oxygen redox chemistry to achieve gravimetric energy density exceeding 3,500 Wh kgLi2O2–1 based on lithium peroxide and up to 5,200 Wh kgLi2O–1 for lithium oxide. However, practical implementation of LOBs remains constrained by significant challenges including low round-trip efficiency and low system-level energy density, the latter arising from the need for oxygen management in both open and closed architectures. The electrolyte viscosity, oxygen solubility, volatility, and chemical stability toward reactive oxygen species can profoundly influence discharge capacity, rate capability, reversibility, and long-term stability. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of recent progress in LOBs, focusing on electrolyte designs, electrode engineering, and strategies for mitigating parasitic reactions as well as the interplay between material-level properties and system-level constraints, offering a critical perspective on the path toward realizing high-energy, practical LOB systems.

articles.title: Named Reactions under Mechanochemical Conditions: A Critical Survey
articles.abstract: Mechanochemistry has progressed from a niche interest to a core method for solvent-free synthesis, providing sustainable and mechanistically unique alternatives to traditional solution-based chemistry. When controlled impact, shear, or vibrational energy is applied under solvent-free or solvent-lean conditions, reactions are promoted within dynamically renewed interfacial regions, revealing new patterns of selectivity, energy efficiency, and process design. This review surveys the historical development, fundamental principles, and analytical frameworks of mechanochemistry, together with an extensive compilation of named organic reactions conducted under mechanochemical conditions. By comparing mechanochemical reactions with their solution-phase counterparts, this review clarifies how stress-induced activation, microsolvation (η control), and auxiliary-mediated interfaces influence reaction kinetics, selectivity, and scalability. Emerging platforms, such as twin-screw extrusion (TSE), resonant acoustic mixing (RAM), and bead mills, extend these advantages toward scale-up and, in the case of TSE, continuous manufacturing, bridging laboratory-scale discoveries and industrial applications. Mechanochemistry functions both as a practical enabling platform and as a conceptual framework for Green Chemistry, embracing atom economy, solvent reduction, and operational safety within a unified solid-state synthetic framework.

articles.title: In-field crop disease surveillance: from phenotypes to molecules
articles.abstract: This review outlines crop pathogen biomarkers and in-field molecular detection advances, evaluates in-field tool readiness, and details their applications in early disease detection, field pathogen survey, pesticide guidance, and mechanism research.

articles.title: Monolayer molecular crystals: controlled-growth technologies, structure–property relationships, and device applications
articles.abstract: This review establishes a mechanism-driven framework for monolayer molecular crystals (MMCs), integrating controlled growth, structure–property relationships, and device applications. It outlines pathways toward scalable molecular electronics.

articles.title: Silanols in zeolite catalysis: from defects to designable functionality
articles.abstract: Zeolite silanols were long treated mainly as structural defects, but recent catalytic studies show that specific silanol populations can also function as catalytically relevant sites or local environments.

articles.title: Exciton Dynamics and Charge Diffusion in Supramolecular Porphyrin Polymers
articles.abstract: Controlling chromophore aggregation across nano- to mesoscale dimensions provides a powerful strategy for tailoring the properties of π-conjugated materials and accelerating advances in organic optoelectronic technologies. Because exciton generation, migration, and dissociation in organic assemblies are governed by molecular packing, precise control over nanoscale order is critical for defining structure−function relationships in organic semiconductors. In this context, one-dimensional supramolecular polymers offer compelling design platforms, where assembly pathways and packing geometries can be leveraged to modulate excitonic coupling, promote delocalization, and direct transport. Although porphyrin superstructures with J-type excitonic coupling have been widely studied as models for efficient energy migration, the excited-state processes of H-type porphyrin assemblies remain comparatively underexplored, despite the structural robustness of these constructs and their potential to promote directional exciton and charge diffusion. Here, we address this gap using a novel zinc porphyrin derivative PZn-OTEG-OH, which undergoes cooperative supramolecular polymerization to form one-dimensional aggregates with H-like photophysics. Ultrafast pump−probe transient absorption measurements in solution reveal that the supramolecular polymer exhibits a nanosecond excited-state lifetime together with diffusive exciton migration over nanometer length scales. In the solid state, the preorganized aggregate translates into an interconnected fibrillar network, in contrast to the comparatively featureless films obtained from monomeric solution. Solid-state electrochemical measurements reveal only modest shifts in redox inflection potentials between monomer- and aggregate-derived films, whereas chronoamperometry indicates faster charging dynamics and an increased apparent diffusion coefficient for the aggregate-derived films. Together, these results demonstrate that cooperative H-like porphyrin assemblies can integrate efficient exciton migration in solution with enhanced charge accumulation in the solid state, establishing a molecular design strategy for light-harvesting organic semiconducting materials.

articles.title: Phase- and Thickness-Controlled Chemical Vapor Deposition of SnSe and SnSe2 Films: Thermodynamic and Kinetic Insights into Phase Selection
articles.abstract: Phase selection among competing stoichiometric compounds during nonequilibrium vapor-phase growth remains a fundamental challenge because experimentally accessible growth parameters ultimately influence phase formation through both thermodynamic driving forces and atomic-scale kinetic processes. Here, we investigate phase selection between SnSe and SnSe2 during low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (CVD) by integrating systematic growth experiments, first-principles thermodynamic calculations, and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. Systematic regulation of the relative Sn/Se chemical environment and growth temperature establishes distinct SnSe- and SnSe2-dominant growth regimes. Thermodynamic calculations show that SnSe is preferentially stabilized under Sn-rich conditions with low Se chemical potential, whereas increasing the Se chemical potential shifts the thermodynamic preference toward SnSe2. Complementary atomistic simulations reveal that increasing Se availability progressively promotes SnSe2-like local coordination, while elevated temperature enhances Sn−Se interdiffusion and redistributes Se toward more spatially dispersed, locally Se-deficient configurations. Building on the established phase-selective growth conditions, we further demonstrate independent thickness tunability through growth-time control, with SnSe and SnSe2 film thicknesses spanning 15−123 and 13.5−120 nm, respectively. Together, these results show that stoichiometry-dependent phase competition under nonequilibrium growth conditions reflects the combined effects of thermodynamic stability and atomic kinetics, while film thickness can be adjusted through growth-time control. These results provide insight into the relationship between growth conditions, phase selection, and film thickness in compositionally related layered chalcogenides.

articles.title: Abstract P1060A: CPR Training Perception and Willingness to Act: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Pre-Medical Students
articles.abstract: Introduction/Background: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is critical step for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest survival. Pre-medical students represent an unstudied and high-potential bystander population, yet predictors of post-training CPR willingness remain poorly characterized. Hypothesis: Pre-medical students from a public university in Argentina perceiving CPR training as highly important would demonstrate greater willingness to perform CPR after course completion. Methods: Prospective, cross-sectional study post mandated CPR-course survey of all pre-medical students (full cohort 2026) at Universidad Nacional de La Matanza, Argentina. The educational program comprised a 3-hour, theoretical-practical course led by university instructors in accordance with the 2025 AHA guidelines. Variables included demographics, prior CPR exposure (awareness, prior formal course, real-life CPR performance), perceived training importance (Likert 1-5), post-course CPR willingness (Likert 1-5; high=4-5). Real-life CPR performance was operationally defined as the delivery of chest compressions with or without the use of an automated external defibrillator (AED). Bivariate analyses used chi-square and crude odds ratios (OR, 95%CI). Two multivariable logistic regression models identified independent factors associated to: Model 1: high post-course CPR willingness and model 2: prior real-life CPR performance. Results: 448 students responded (mean age 21.9±5.5 years; 70.8% female). Prior awareness of CPR was high (94.9%); 32.1% had completed a prior formal CPR course; only 6.5% had performed CPR in a real-life emergency. Perceived importance was: 96.2% rated 5/5. High post-course CPR willingness was reported by 67.2%. In bivariate analysis, maximum importance perception was associated with high willingness to render CPR in real life (OR=3.07, 95%CI:1.14-8.23, p=0.020), as was prior formal CPR course (OR=1.82, 95%CI:1.16-2.84, p=0.008). In multivariable analysis (Model 1), maximum importance perception independently predicted high willingness (adjusted OR=2.96, 95%CI:1.07-8.22, p=0.037). For real-life CPR performance (Model 2), prior formal CPR course (adjusted OR=5.24, 95%CI:2.06-13.36, p<0.001) and older age (adjusted OR=2.18 per SD, 95%CI:1.63-2.92, p<0.001) were the sole independent predictors. Gender was not associated with either outcome. Conclusions: Perceiving CPR training as maximally important independently predicted greater willingness to perform CPR post-course. Prior formal CPR training was the strongest predictor of real-life CPR performance. These findings support early, repeated CPR training in medical curricula and emphasize framing instruction within clinical relevance to enhance motivation and real-world application. These cross-sectional associations warrant confirmation in longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Health Promotion for US Veterans: Current State, Gaps, and Strategies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: US veterans represent a large and diverse population with distinctive demographic characteristics, comorbidity profiles, and social determinants of health shaped by military service. These factors contribute to a high burden of cardiovascular risk and low attainment of ideal cardiovascular health. At the same time, the Department of Veterans Affairs, which operates the nation’s largest integrated healthcare system, provides a unique infrastructure for delivering population-level cardiovascular disease prevention for veterans. Understanding its successes and ongoing challenges can inform broader strategies across all health systems for promoting health among veterans. This scientific statement applies the American Heart Association’s Life’s Essential 8 framework, expanded to include mental health and substance use, to evaluate veteran cardiovascular health. For each domain, we review guideline recommendations, barriers to achieving optimal health, and major Veterans Affairs programs such as Patient Aligned Care Teams, the MOVE! Weight Management Program for Veterans, Whole Health, telehealth-based interventions, and integrated mental health and substance use disorder services. Across domains, veterans receiving Veterans Affairs care often achieve outcomes that are equal to or better than those of their non–Veterans Affairs counterparts, reflecting the strengths of the system in coordinated, team-based care and research-driven implementation. Despite substantial progress, opportunities remain to improve veteran lifestyle behaviors, metabolic health, lipid and blood pressure control, engagement in mental health and substance use care, and detection and management of sleep disorders. Addressing these challenges at the Veterans Affairs will require continuing to expand care access, enhancing digital data integration, tailoring interventions to high-risk subgroups, and strengthening implementation strategies to improve uptake and engagement across Veterans Affairs services.

articles.title: Accounting for hidden wild inputs in conservation substitutes
articles.abstract: Artificial propagation, wildlife farming, ranching, cultivation, and aquaculture support commercial markets and livelihoods, and their products may be promoted as substitutes for wild harvest. However, production labels for these products cannot be used to determine conservation benefit because output may depend on wild inputs. Thus, we developed hidden wild‐input (HWI) accounting as a bounded assessment framework. HWIs are wild‐derived biological inputs that are important for producing substitutes but also potentially for conservation, and they are underrepresented in labels, statistics, and assessments. Through conceptual analysis and comparison, we identified establishment, maintenance, and scaling production inputs and conducted a counterfactual evaluation to determine the avoided harvest of wild targets, source‐population burdens, and other ecological effects, such as wild‐input intensity, wild‐origin proportion, supplementation frequency, and elasticity. We examined four examples of wild‐input use to illustrate the framework: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) source code Y exposed the gap between production‐origin categories and upstream accounting; crocodile ranching showed recurring wild inputs can coexist with conservation gains under regulated management; capture‐based European eel (Anguilla anguilla) aquaculture demonstrated production–extraction coupling; and the artificial production of Chinese caterpillar fungus (Ophiocordyceps sinensis) revealed potential commercial dependence when recurring inputs are not reported. Together, the examples showed that source categories cannot be used to quantify upstream burdens, recurring inputs do not indicate conservation failure, and input–output coefficients demonstrate coupling but not net effects. Conservation benefit should be assessed against a credible no‐expansion counterfactual by asking whether additional output reduces target harvest, added wild‐input burdens remain sustainable, and other ecological effects reverse the gain. Complete biological independence is neither necessary nor sufficient. When input, demographic, and market‐substitution data are unavailable, uncertainty should be reported rather than replaced by assumptions based on production labels. Atención a los insumos silvestres ocultos en los sustitutos para la conservación Resumen La reproducción artificial, la cría de fauna silvestre, la ganadería, el cultivo y la acuicultura sustentan los mercados comerciales y los medios de vida, y sus productos pueden promocionarse como sustitutos de la recolección silvestre. Sin embargo, las etiquetas de producción de estos productos no pueden utilizarse para determinar el beneficio para la conservación, ya que la producción puede depender de insumos silvestres. Por ello, hemos desarrollado la contabilidad de los insumos silvestres ocultos (HWI) como un marco de evaluación delimitado. Los HWI son insumos biológicos de origen silvestre que resultan importantes para la producción de sustitutos, pero también, potencialmente, para la conservación, y que están infrarrepresentados en las etiquetas, las estadísticas y las evaluaciones. Mediante el análisis conceptual y la comparación, identificamos los insumos necesarios para el establecimiento, el mantenimiento y la ampliación de la producción, y llevamos a cabo una evaluación contrafactual para determinar la captura evitada de especies silvestres objetivo, la presión sobre las poblaciones de origen y otros efectos ecológicos, como la intensidad de los insumos silvestres, la proporción de origen silvestre, la frecuencia de suplementación y la elasticidad.…

articles.title: Indicators for tracking progress of effective, representative ecosystem protection
articles.abstract: To halt and reverse rapid biodiversity loss, countries are pursuing the ambitious goals and targets in the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) to restore and protect biodiversity in representative networks of protected areas. However, the associated monitoring framework lacks indicators of ecosystem representativeness for Target 3. Using South Africa as an example, we tested different indicators that could fill this gap and made recommendations for globally relevant options for national and international reporting. Specifically, we calculated seven indicators that use different combinations of data on protected areas, ecosystem types, and ecological condition. We used these indicators to measure progress in effective, representative ecosystem protection at different scales in South Africa: country, ecosystem group (e.g., realm), and ecosystem type. The indicators revealed more informative insights, such as which ecosystem types are best progressing toward meeting their protection targets and where protection levels could improve if degraded habitat within protected areas was restored, than protected area coverage (PAC; total % protection). We tabulated the data requirements, advantages, and disadvantages for the indicators and provided recommendations for their use. We recommend condition‐adjusted representativeness (CAR) and the ecosystem protection level index be added as component indicators in the GBF monitoring framework for Target 3. These two indicators could also be assessed using the Global Ecosystem Typology (GET) for standardized aggregation or disaggregation of ecosystem types at different levels. For single time points, plotting PAC, representativeness, CAR, and ecosystem protection level by ecosystem functional groups (GET level 3) can be informative. Applying these indicators can strengthen biodiversity reporting under the GBF. Indicadores para rastrear los avances de la protección efectiva de los ecosistemas representativos Resumen Para detener y revertir la rápida pérdida de biodiversidad, los países están persiguiendo los ambiciosos objetivos y metas del Marco Global de Biodiversidad (GBF) de Kunming‐Montreal con el fin de restaurar y proteger la biodiversidad en redes representativas de áreas protegidas. Sin embargo, el marco de seguimiento asociado carece de indicadores de representatividad de los ecosistemas para la Meta 3. Con Sudáfrica como ejemplo, evaluamos diferentes indicadores que podrían subsanar esta carencia y formulamos recomendaciones sobre opciones de relevancia mundial para la presentación de informes a nivel nacional e internacional. En concreto, calculamos siete indicadores que utilizan diferentes combinaciones de datos sobre áreas protegidas, tipos de ecosistemas y estado ecológico. Utilizamos estos indicadores para medir los avances en la protección eficaz y representativa de los ecosistemas a diferentes escalas en Sudáfrica: a nivel nacional, de grupo de ecosistemas (p. ej., reino) y de tipo de ecosistema. Los indicadores revelaron información más relevante, como qué tipos de ecosistemas están avanzando mejor hacia el cumplimiento de sus objetivos de protección y en qué casos podrían mejorarse los niveles de protección si se restauraran los hábitats degradados dentro de las áreas protegidas, que la cobertura de las áreas protegidas (PAC; porcentaje total de protección). Capturamos en tablas los requisitos de datos, las ventajas y las desventajas de los indicadores y formulamos recomendaciones para su uso. Recomendamos que la representatividad ajustada a las condiciones (CAR) y el índice de nivel de protección de los ecosistemas se añadan como indicadores componentes en el marco de seguimiento del GBF para la Meta 3. Estos dos indicadores también podrían evaluarse utilizando la Tipología Global de Ecosistemas (GET) para la agregación o desagregación estandarizada de los tipos de ecosistemas a diferentes niveles.…

articles.title: A Multi‐Stage Framework for Diagnosing Structural Redundancy Between Selected Functional Diversity Metrics: Empirical Applications Under an A Priori Expectation of Overlap
articles.abstract: Functional diversity (FD) is widely used to study ecosystem processes, leading to the continuous development of FD metrics. However, the proliferation of these descriptors raises concerns regarding structural redundancy, particularly in ecological modelling, where the simultaneous use of highly concordant FD metrics may compromise model parsimony. We propose a multi‐stage approach to diagnose structural redundancy among selected FD metrics when theoretical, mathematical, or empirical considerations suggest overlap, using complementary analyses across continuous and categorised representations. We illustrate the approach through two pairwise comparisons: the community‐based weighted functional dendrogram index (wFDc), which incorporates the species community pool, versus richness–quadratic entropy (RQ) and Rao's quadratic entropy (Q) versus functional dispersion (FDis). The framework was applied to both metric pairs using benthic macroinvertebrate assemblages from three contrasting freshwater ecosystems in Ecuador. Both metric pairs exhibited high concordance across the three ecosystems, with strong continuous associations and substantial agreement in percentile‐based classifications. By incorporating richness‐controlled analyses, the framework evaluates whether concordance persists after accounting for shared richness dependence. For both pairs, residual associations remained strong, supporting suspected structural overlap in the examined datasets. Our findings suggest that the simultaneous use of highly concordant FD metrics could be unnecessary. Rather than questioning the development of new FD metrics, the proposed framework provides a practical diagnostic protocol for evaluating their structural redundancy. To facilitate its application, we provide the R package FD Concordance https://github.com/Gonpa83/FD_concordance.git and a companion Shiny application of the same name https://01a168d6‐1a69‐a0e6‐7a29‐7e329e9dbbdb.share.connect.posit.cloud/ enabling researchers to apply the protocol to their own index values. These tools support targeted assessments of suspected overlap and more parsimonious ecological modelling and biomonitoring.

articles.title: Evaluating Metabarcoding of Wildflower Associated eDNA to Assess Butterfly Presence and Abundance
articles.abstract: Rapid and accurate assessment of insect communities is increasingly important in the context of climate change and biodiversity loss. Environmental DNA (eDNA) analysis has proven useful as a noninvasive method for detecting insects in aquatic systems, and methods for terrestrial eDNA sources are being developed. Analysis of wildflower‐associated DNA may be useful for identifying insect pollinators. This study paired traditional butterfly netting surveys in a montane protected area with wildflower‐associated eDNA metabarcoding to test whether the presence and abundance of butterfly species can be accurately assessed. Specifically, Lepidoptera targeting primers were used to amplify two regions of the cytochrome oxidase subunit I (COI) gene from wildflower‐associated eDNA samples. Analysis of the ~350 million sequences obtained identified ~94% as insects, with ~23% assigned to Lepidoptera. Six butterfly taxa, including four at the species level, were identified, including five that were consistent with species captured during netting surveys conducted in parallel. However, butterfly detections from eDNA did not correspond with either contrived or natural flower visitation, and traditional surveys identified 44 butterfly species not captured by eDNA. The most prevalently detected taxa were small‐bodied insects closely associated with flowers. Together our results indicate that additional refinement of protocols and primers is needed before wildflower‐associated eDNA can reliably survey butterfly species.

articles.title: Satellite Tracking and Citizen Science Provide Complementary Insights Into Spatial and Temporal Migration Patterns of Eastern Buzzards
articles.abstract: Individual bird tracking can resolve continuous migration processes but is limited by small sample sizes, whereas citizen‐science records provide broad spatial and multi‐year coverage but are affected by observation effort and spatial accessibility. However, few studies have evaluated how citizen‐science records and individual tracking correspond across both spatial and temporal components of the same migratory system, including migration routes, stopover sites, migration timing, and broad‐scale spatial coverage. We integrated 105,630 valid satellite locations from 22 rescued and released Eastern Buzzards (Buteo japonicus), of which 10 completed 27 full migrations, with 25,651 records of this species from eBird and GBIF. We compared the two data sources in terms of migration routes and continental‐scale latitudinal coverage, repeatedly used stopover sites, migration timing, and landscape composition. Both data sources revealed northward migration in spring and southward migration in autumn. The latitudinal spans represented by citizen‐science records were 661 km narrower in spring and 937 km narrower in autumn than those derived from tracking. Five of the 10 repeatedly used stopover sites identified by satellite tracking had citizen‐science records within 100 km during the corresponding migration season. The overlap coefficients between their 24‐h distributions were 0.594 in spring and 0.585 in autumn. Bray–Curtis similarity in landscape composition between the two data sources was 0.545. These results show that the two data sources provide convergent evidence of seasonal migration progression and continental‐scale movements, while local differences highlight potential gaps in citizen‐science coverage.

articles.title: Fluorine-free CO 2 electrolyzer for multicarbon products
articles.abstract: Integrating a PDMS-based gas diffusion electrode, ionic polymer brushes, and a fluorine-free membrane provides a fully fluorine-free architecture for CO 2 electrolysis, achieving 43% ethanol faradaic efficiency under acidic conditions.

articles.title: Interfacial engineering accelerates desolvation kinetics for high-performance alkaline zinc–iron flow batteries
articles.abstract: Cyclooctaamylose regulates interfacial zincate desolvation and promotes uniform zinc nucleation and growth, enabling high power density and high areal capacity in alkaline zinc–iron flow batteries.

articles.title: Diversity and composition of benthic marine communities under contrasting management and temperature regimes
articles.abstract: The sustainable management of small-scale fisheries is key for the well-being of coastal communities. Environmental conditions are known to influence the ecology of the coastal zone, yet their interactions with fisheries management regimes remains poorly understood. We examined spatial changes in the structure of benthic communities under distinct management regimes (TURF or Territorial Use Rights for Fisheries, and OA or open access areas) located in areas with different temperature patterns (warm and cold). Using underwater visual censuses, we assessed benthic community patterns across four locations in northern-central Chile and examined how species diversity and composition varied between management and environmental regimes. Our results showed that communities differed significantly between management and temperature regimes. In general, sessile community richness was 65% higher under cold regimes compared to warm regimes. For mobile invertebrates, richness and diversity were 42% and 41% greater in TURF areas than in OA areas, while both attributes were 4% and 5% higher under cold than warm temperature regimes. In the case of fish communities, species composition varied as a function of the interaction between management and temperature regimes. In cold sites, benthic communities within TURF areas were characterized by the kelp Lessonia trabeculata, the whelk Concholepas concholepas, and keyhole limpets (Fissurella spp.), whereas OA areas were dominated by kelp, the sea urchin Arbacia nigra, and the starfish Meyenaster gelatinosus. Benthic communities of TURF areas in warm sites were associated with anemones, sea urchins and kelps, whereas OA areas were dominated mainly by anemones and sea urchins. Overall, our results support the notion that the structure of benthic communities can be influenced by an interaction between management regime and environmental conditions. The two temperature regimes stem from the differential exposure to coastal upwelling between sites, which suggests that other environmental processes, such as productivity or wave exposure, are implicated. Overall, the marked ecological differences between TURF and OA areas under contrasting temperature patterns suggest that environmental conditions should be incorporated into the design of novel fishery policies to promote the sustainable management of small-scale coastal fisheries.

articles.title: Late Triassic Dipnoi from south Gondwana, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
articles.abstract: Mesozoic lungfishes are often represented in the fossil record by isolated tooth plates, which impose limitations on their taxonomic identification and on the interpretation of their diversity. In the Triassic of South America, these organisms remain poorly documented. The present study describes eight isolated tooth plates from the Candelária Sequence of the Santa Maria Supersequence (Carnian, Late Triassic), southern Brazil, being attributed to three taxa: Ptychoceratodus phillipsi, P. eliseui sp. nov., and Ferganoceratodus cabreirai sp. nov. The description was made using morphological and morphometric approaches and the tooth plates. The results highlight the strong morphological similarity between Ptychoceratodus and Ferganoceratodus, as well as the overlap of diagnostic characters, which reinforces the difficulties in distinguishing between these genera when only isolated tooth plates are available. The association with other ichthyofauna and the presence of deposits indicative of varying depositional energies suggest a seasonal environment, with alternation between wet and dry periods. From a paleobiogeographic perspective, the record of Ferganoceratodus represents the first occurrence of the genus in the Triassic of South America, extending its previously known distribution. The occurrence of P. phillipsi, in turn, reinforces the wide dispersal of lungfishes throughout Pangaea during the Mesozoic. In this context, the materials described herein represent a relevant contribution to the Gondwanan record of Mesozoic lungfishes and reinforce the importance of the Candelária Sequence as a key unit for Triassic dipnoan paleobiogeography and biostratigraphy. The occurrence of these genera in Brazilian continental deposits is consistent with the distribution pattern observed for Mesozoic lungfishes and suggests faunal affinities with assemblages from other portions of Gondwana.

articles.title: Forged by frost, ready for heat: Integration of metabolomics and functional traits investigated along a latitudinal gradient reveals relaxed trade‐offs and enhanced heat tolerance in individuals from cold regions
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Acquiring a critical understanding of how organisms respond to environmental changes requires integrating molecular and whole‐organism perspectives while investigating how latitudinal gradients shape thermal responses. We explored trade‐offs between thermal tolerance and performance in the marine intertidal gastropod Littorina littorea collected from 10 locations across a wide latitudinal gradient in North America. Snails were exposed under laboratory conditions to a wide range of temperatures (from 5 to 27°C) for 30 days, after which we characterised their metabolomic profiles in relation to whole‐organism responses obtained from a previous study on the same individuals, including growth, feeding rate, metabolic rate and critical thermal maximum (CTmax). Relationships between growth, feeding rate, CTmax and one major metabolomic axis revealed clear trade‐offs between fitness‐related traits and thermal tolerance. The decreased concentrations of metabolites contributing most to such trade‐offs were negatively associated with growth and feeding but positively associated with CTmax. Many of these metabolites also differed consistently among locations, with individuals from warmer (lower latitude) regions showing lower concentrations. Their higher concentrations in snails from colder environments may provide them with a greater metabolic capacity, potentially relaxing the trade‐off between thermal tolerance and fitness. Highly abundant metabolites in snails from colder locations were often linked to antioxidant and cellular stress responses. Furthermore, metabolites linearly and non‐linearly related to temperature showed variation in their thermal sensitivity depending on the location, with snails from colder sites showing greater thermal responses. Our results suggest that increased thermal tolerance may come at the expense of reduced investments in fitness‐related traits. The relaxed trade‐offs, the higher production of cellular heat stress defences and the enhanced metabolomic thermal response of snails from colder regions may explain their higher thermal tolerance and acclimation capacity. We show how energy metabolism trade‐offs can shape species thermal tolerance variation across broad environmental gradients. The integrated whole‐organism and molecular perspective we provide offers new insights into the potential adaptive mechanisms governing species responses to current and future climate change. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Intensive Agriculture and Erosion Affect Composition of Soil Organic Matter
articles.abstract: Land‐use changes induced by human activities usually accelerate soil erosion, leading to losses of soil organic matter (SOM). The mechanisms by which cultivation‐associated degradation affects SOM composition via changes of content and quality of particulate (POM), mineral‐associated (MAOM), dissolved organic matter (DOM), and microbial biomass are not elucidated. We investigated the C:N stoichiometry of these fractions, and erosion (using 137Cs activity) along a chronosequence of cultivation‐associated degradation (0–114 years) in Mollisols. Two‐pool and Bayesian three‐source mixing models estimated contributions of microbial biomass, DOM, and POM to MAOM to the total SOM. Erosion intensity ranged locally from 440 to 4800 t km−2 year−1, resulting in cumulative soil losses of 11,000 to 320,000 t km−2 over 114 years of cultivation. As cultivation duration and eroded amounts increased, the C/N ratios of POM, MAOM, and DOM declined owing to (i) the faster loss of C than N, (ii) a decrease in C/N with soil depth involved in tillage horizon, and (iii) N input by fertilization. These higher C than N losses reflect that erosion is not the sole process leading to the decline of C stocks, but intensive cultivation also accelerates organic matter mineralization and CO2 release to the atmosphere. As the C/N ratios of POM and MAOM declined but microbial C/N increased, the estimated contribution of microbial inputs to MAOM increased from 6% to 32%. The Bayesian model partitioned MAOM sources into DOM (8%), microbial (11%), and POM (81%), reinforcing that POM dominates MAOM formation in croplands. Cultivation‐associated degradation led to SOC losses by reducing POM‐C/N and MAOM‐C/N ratios, while erosion strongly accelerated these effects. Furthermore, cultivation‐associated degradation is also based on the limited inputs of organic C as the precursors for MAOM formation by depleting POM. These results from a > 100‐year chronosequence indicate that cultivation‐induced degradation reduces SOM content, while also shifting the MAOM composition progressively towards a greater contribution of microbial C.

articles.title: Mineral‐Associated Carbon Accrual Masks Labile Particulate Carbon Loss in Permafrost Region on the Tibetan Plateau
articles.abstract: Permafrost regions store vast quantities of soil organic carbon (SOC), yet the future trajectories of functionally distinct SOC fractions across soil depths remain poorly constrained. Integrating depth‐explicit soil fractionation data from 104 sites across the Tibetan permafrost region with a process‐based SOC model, we project century‐scale dynamics of particulate (POC) and mineral‐associated organic carbon (MAOC) under three emission scenarios. We show that MAOC currently comprises 56.5% of regional total SOC stock and remains far from saturation throughout the profile. Consistent with this large stabilization capacity, total SOC was projected to increase over the 21st century under all scenarios, with the largest gains under SSP5‐8.5. However, this positive net gain masked a significant restructuring of SOC fractions. MAOC accumulated across all depths and scenarios, and heavy POC remained comparatively buffered, whereas light POC declined under SSP5‐8.5. The strongest relative light POC losses occurred in the 10–30 cm layers, where warming‐driven decomposition remained strong while plant‐C input compensation weakened. These divergent trajectories indicate a shift toward a “carbon‐rich yet energy‐poor” state, where mineral‐bound carbon increases while the labile particulate pool supporting microbial activity is depleted. Our findings reveal SOC vulnerability in permafrost region is governed by both fraction identity and soil depth, and that net SOC gains can conceal the loss of metabolically active carbon. Incorporating measurable, depth‐resolved SOC fractions into Earth system models is therefore essential for constraining permafrost–climate feedbacks.

articles.title: Three‐Phase Mobilization of Organic Phosphorus Sustains Phosphorus Bioavailability Under Long‐Term Nitrogen Addition in a Subtropical Plantation
articles.abstract: Nitrogen (N) input is expected to intensify phosphorus (P) limitation in tropical and subtropical forests. However, how soil and microbial processes mobilize P from poorly available pools to sustain soil P bioavailability remains unclear. We conducted a nine‐year experiment with low (20 kg N ha−1 year−1) and high (80 kg N ha−1 year−1) N addition treatments in a subtropical Moso bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis) plantation. We quantified soil P fractions, P‐cycling functional genes, phosphatase activity, P sorption capacity (PSC), iron and aluminum oxides, and plant properties throughout the experiment. Our results reveal three distinct stages in the regulation of soil bioavailable P with prolonged N addition. Phase I: N addition reduces P bioavailability, and labile organic P decomposition becomes the main source of bioavailable P, associated with increased phosphatase activity. Phase II: when labile organic P becomes insufficient to meet P demand, bioavailable P is replenished through the depletion of moderately labile organic P; this is related to decreased PSC and enhanced acid phosphomonoesterases activity. Phase III: stable organic P decreases significantly, jointly sustaining bioavailable P with the depletion of other organic P fractions, alongside a further decrease in PSC and enriched microbial organic acid‐ and phosphatase‐related genes. This study uncovers a novel “three‐phased P supply” model revealed through long‐term observations. These mechanistic insights reveal the pathways of soil P mobilization under continuous N input in a subtropical forest and establish a framework for predicting the buffering capacity of soil P pools in P‐limited ecosystems under global change scenarios.

articles.title: Beyond the value of reproductive value
articles.abstract: Where does the future of a population reside? Reproductive value provides an answer. We show how new technologies could make this century‐old concept dynamic and individualised, and propose extending it to communities to reveal demographic resilience, portfolio effects and vulnerabilities that conventional measures of abundance may miss. Abstract Research Highlights: Lebreton, J.‐D., & Oli, M. K. (2026). Reproductive value as a key concept in ecology and evolutionary biology. Journal of Animal Ecology. https://doi.org/10.1111/1365‐2656.70343. Ecologists are good at counting things. Yet individuals are not interchangeable in what they contribute to a population's future. Lebreton and Oli's synthesis of reproductive value (RV) shows that this deceptively simple idea connects demographic theory, life‐history evolution, spatial ecology, epidemiology and conservation. Indeed, RV provides a common currency for asking not simply how many individuals occupy a population, but where its demographic future resides. Here, I highlight this unifying perspective and argue that new technologies could take RV from a predominantly class‐based quantity towards a dynamic, individualised and spatially explicit description of populations. Combining demographic models with biologging, automated monitoring, genomic information and ecological digital twins could reveal reproductive value at resolutions Fisher himself could scarcely have imagined. I further suggest that RV could enrich community‐stability theory by weighting species' fluctuations by their contribution to future population persistence, thereby connecting population resilience, biodiversity insurance and ecosystem stability.

articles.title: Introduction bias and debt in Australia's non‐native trees
articles.abstract: Humans have introduced non‐native species around the world. Once introduced species can become naturalised (self‐sustaining population) and invasive (spread with negative consequences). We characterised introduction biases, and quantified introduction debt in trees introduced to Australia. Australia's introduced trees were selectively introduced. They are therefore not a random subset of non‐native trees. Introductions have altered characteristics of Australia's tree flora. Abstract Humans have transported and introduced thousands of non‐native species around the world, some of which then naturalise and become invasive. Introduction bias indicates characteristics of non‐native species that have been preferentially introduced, which could subsequently bias characteristics associated with species invasiveness. Introduction debt captures non‐native species that have not yet been introduced but could be in the future, highlighting potential threats. We test for introduction bias and debt in non‐native trees introduced to Australia using a dataset of 57,958 tree species known globally. We examine trends in family, functional traits (height, seed mass, specific leaf area [SLA], wood density), home region, human uses and invasion history elsewhere. We test for biotic homogenisation by comparing the taxonomic and functional characteristics of trees introduced to Australia with Australia's 3114 native trees. Of 54,844 tree species that aren't native to Australia, 6066 have been introduced to Australia, of which 657 have become naturalised and 106 have become invasive. This leaves an introduction debt of 48,778 species. We found that species naturalised in numerous other countries and more heavily used by humans are more likely to have been introduced to Australia. Species from certain families (e.g. Arecaceae), countries (e.g. China) and continents (e.g. Europe) were more likely to have been introduced. Naturalised and invasive trees were more likely to originate from Europe. We detected introduction biases towards shorter and lighter‐seeded species, which were accentuated in the invasive species subset. Species with lower SLA have been preferentially introduced to Australia, but the mean SLA of non‐native trees was still higher than that of native trees. Differences between native and introduced trees across all four functional traits suggest that tree introductions have homogenised Australia's tree flora, making it more functionally similar to global tree flora. Synthesis. Australia's introduced trees are not a random subset of all non‐native trees but have been selectively introduced. Non‐native introductions have homogenised and altered characteristics of Australia's tree flora. Of the almost 49,000 tree species that could still be introduced, species from the tropics and South America pose an especially high future introduction risk for Australia.

articles.title: All-Visible Wavelength-Gated Multistate Photochromic AIEgen: High-Efficiency Photocyclizations in a Single Luminogenic System
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Synthetic photochromic molecules that enable noninvasive orthogonal control using distinct wavelengths of light are still in their infancy, yet ensuring the independence of photoreaction pathways and multiple addressable states in a single luminogenic system remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report an aggregation-induced emission (AIE) luminogen capable of undergoing wavelength-selective photocyclizations under visible-light irradiation, exhibiting a photorearrangement at 410 nm purple light and an oxidative photocyclization at 465 nm blue light to yield two stable yet distinct photochromic states. Experimental and theoretical results provide insight into the wavelength-dependent reaction pathways, as well as the corresponding synergistic mechanism of aromaticity, steric strain, and inductive effect in its photocyclizations. Eventually, a model information encryption system was developed to showcase its practical potential for all-visible-light-controlled multistate operations. This work thus offers both a viable strategy and a versatile structural motif for developing visible-light-controlled multistate luminogens and advanced multifunctional systems.

articles.title: An Experimental MOF-Polymer Latent Space for Composite Design
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have tremendous promise for filtration, catalysis, and sequestration, but they are limited by the polymer matrices in which they must be embedded to form functional composites. Here, we find an experimental approach in which composite performance can be predicted using a single MOF particle. In particular, we attach single MOF particles to atomic force microscope (AFM) probes and find that the forces between the MOF-tipped probe and polymer films can be transformed into an instructive low-dimensional descriptor of MOF-polymer interactions. This two-dimensional latent space provides direct measures of chemical compatibility as well as the work of adhesion and can be used to understand interfacial phenomena in MOF-polymer composites. For example, polymer intercalation is observed via X-ray scattering for MOF-polymer combinations with high chemical-compatibility latent-space variables. Bulk composite performance can also be predicted using the latent space values for cases where the MOF is held constant. For example, a simple linear model was trained to predict CO2 absorption into composites of UiO-66-NH2 based solely on the latent space variables. In addition to providing a rapid way to screen polymer matrices to complement a MOF chosen for its bulk properties, these results suggest that composite performance may be a separable function of bulk properties and the interfacial latent space. In this way, this transfer-learning approach can vastly accelerate the design and understanding of functional composites.

articles.title: Conjugate Chiral Carbon Dots for Scalable Asymmetric Photocatalysis in Flow
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Carbon dots (CDs) have emerged as scalable, metal-free photocatalysts, but their use as conjugate organo-photocatalysts for enantioselective chemistry remains unexplored. Here, we covalently anchor a chiral imidazolidinone organocatalyst to amorphous, citric acid-derived CDs, giving a colloidal conjugate that acts as both photosensitizer and enantiodetermining component. This chiral CD material promotes the asymmetric radical α-alkylation of aldehydes in up to 84% yield and 93% e.e. Its semihomogeneous nature enables catalyst recovery by precipitation and reuse over five cycles with only minor loss in yield and e.e. The well-dispersed conjugate is also compatible with continuous photoflow, where Bayesian optimization in only 10 experiments enabled a gram-scale reaction in 80% yield and 91% e.e. This work establishes chiral conjugate CDs as a practical, recoverable platform for sustainable asymmetric photocatalysis.

articles.title: Decyanation, Dioxygenation, and Oxidative Ring Contraction Catalyzed by the DUF4243 Oxidase OzmD Rely on Ferric Oxygen Activation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Domain of unknown function 4243 (DUF4243) family proteins are an emerging class of nonheme mononuclear iron enzymes characterized by a distinctive iron-binding motif comprised of four histidine (His) and one Nε-carboxylysine (Kcx) residue. Although predominantly found in fungi, OzmD is the only characterized bacterial member. OzmD catalyzes oxidative rearrangement of an aminopyridone ring into a 1,3-oxazine moiety with concomitant cyanide elimination in the final step of oxazinomycin biosynthesis. Herein, the X-ray crystal structure of OzmD is solved, demonstrating the presence of a conserved 4-His-1-Kcx iron-binding motif similar to other DUF4243 family proteins. Biochemical characterization using a substrate analog carrying a hydroxypyridone ring reveals that OzmD also exhibits intrinsic dioxygenase activity, catalyzing a transformation analogous to those of fungal DUF4243 dioxygenases. Electron paramagnetic resonance and Mössbauer spectroscopic characterization of MinCC, a functionally equivalent homologue of OzmD, reveals that the as-isolated protein predominantly contains ferric iron, which can be reduced to the ferrous state upon binding with either the native substrate or the hydroxy analog under anaerobic conditions. These findings support a unified mechanism in which catalysis begins with single-electron transfer from the substrate to ferric iron, enabling molecular oxygen activation and formation of an alkylperoxide intermediate. Overall reaction mechanisms for substrates bearing aminopyridone and hydroxypyridone rings are proposed based on chemical precedents and computational analyses. These findings reveal that OzmD employs a distinctive FeIII-dependent path for oxygen activation in contrast to the classical FeII-dependent route used by most oxygenases and establish a functional connection between bacterial and fungal DUF4243 enzymes.

Layer-Number-Controlled Symmetry Breaking and Surface-State Transport in Rhombohedral Graphene Multilayers
articles.abstract: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene hosts layer-polarized flat bands, providing an intriguing platform for correlated and topological states; however, how layer number governs symmetry breaking and surface screening remains elusive. Here, we prepare rhombohedral graphene multilayers and systematically conduct electrical transport measurements. We uncover an unconventional layer dependence of phase transitions: the critical displacement field Dc for the layer-antiferromagnetic-to-semimetal transitions remains nearly constant across tetralayer to hexalayer graphene, whereas Dc for the semimetal-to-layer-polarized-insulator transition increases with layer number, defying unscreened Coulomb interaction models. In hexalayer graphene, surface-state-dominated transport emerges with Landau levels and resistive peaks predominantly controlled by adjacent gates, revealing strong interlayer screening. High magnetic fields further reveal valley-layer-locked Landau levels and dissipative states associated with interlayer backscattering, highlighting the presence of decoupled surface states. Our findings establish the layer number as a key tuning knob for engineering correlated and topological phases in rhombohedral graphene multilayers.

articles.title: Magnetic Exciton-Based On-Chip Optical Attenuators Using CrSBr
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors, in which excitonic resonances are coupled directly to the underlying spin order, offer a fundamentally distinct route to active photonic functionality unattainable in conventional dielectrics. The van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr exemplifies this class: its sharp excitons exhibit large oscillator strengths and energies that are continuously and reversibly tunable through the magnetic state of the material, producing dramatic field-induced changes in the permittivity. Here, we exploit this magneto-excitonic response to realize compact, magnetically tunable optical attenuators in standard silicon nitride waveguides. We demonstrate up to 2.5 dB/μm continuous attenuation from CrSBr flakes under in-plane magnetic fields below 1 T. We further show that the device response depends nontrivially on the CrSBr thickness through coupled-mode physics with the polarity of the field response inverting between the perturbative and strongly coupled regimes. This work highlights two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors as a promising materials platform for compact, continuously reconfigurable control of guided light.

articles.title: Measurement of Parity-Dependent Energy-Phase Relations in a Potential Artificial Kitaev Chain Utilizing a Transmon Qubit
articles.abstract: Artificial Kitaev chains have emerged as a promising platform for realizing topological quantum computing. Once the chains are formed and Majorana zero modes are braided/fused, reading out the parity of the chains is essential for verifying the non-Abelian property of Majorana zero modes. Here, we demonstrate a transmon-based microwave probe for a four-site quantum dot–superconductor chain based on a Ge/Si nanowire. One end of the chain is incorporated into a superconducting transmon circuit, enabling spectroscopic identification of the chain’s singlet/doublet ground state and thereby inference of its total Fermion parity. We also demonstrate that, for multiple-dot chains, there are two types of 0−π transitions between different charging states: the parity-flip 0−π transition and the parity-preserved 0−π transition. Furthermore, we demonstrate electrostatic tunability of the interdot coupling. This phase-sensitive microwave platform provides a tool for studying complex hybrid superconducting quantum dot systems and for future extended artificial Kitaev chains.

articles.title: Revealing Polar Walls in CsPbBr3: Herringbone Structure and Formation Pathway
articles.abstract: Domain walls in ferroic materials can host nanoscale functionalities absent from the periodic crystal, offering new opportunities to control electronic transport and polarization in semiconductor devices. Metal halide perovskites demonstrate important photophysical properties; however, their ferroic properties remain unclear. Here we discover a hierarchical herringbone network of polar walls within the nonpolar halide perovskite CsPbBr3 comprising ferroelastic twin walls and antiphase walls. Atomic-scale imaging reveals that both wall types comprise nanoscale regions whose inversion-symmetry is broken compared to the surrounding bulk lattice. In-situ heating experiments show that these interfaces form sequentially during symmetry-lowering phase transitions, revealing a different formation pathway compared with ‘conventional’ oxide perovskites. These polar nanowalls, together with their enclosed topology, may impact carrier transport. This reveals a previously unrecognized structural motif in CsPbBr3, providing new insights into their photophysical and optoelectronic behavior.

articles.title: Ultralow Electron Temperature Plasma for Damage-Reduced Processing of High-k/Metal Gate Films toward Vertically Stacked Nanosheet Devices
articles.abstract: In vertically stacked nanosheet devices, repeated plasma-processing steps are required to realize multiple threshold voltages (Vth), but such repeated exposure can accumulate plasma-induced damage (PID) in ultrathin high-k/metal gate (HKMG) stacks. Here, we demonstrate that ultralow electron temperature (ULET, Te < 1 eV) plasma generated using a DC-biased grid suppresses PID by controlling the electron temperature and ion energy distribution function (IEDF). Compared with conventional inductively coupled plasma processing at the same substrate bias (−100 V), ULET plasma reduces the mean ion energy from 131 to 101 eV and reduces the IEDF standard deviation by 44% (from 37.4 to 20.9 eV). Consequently, surface roughness decreases by up to 58%, fluorine incorporation decreases by up to 58%, and HfO2 Raman-band intensities are 1.32–1.81 times those under conventional ICP processing. These results establish electron-temperature control as a key parameter for minimizing PID in HKMG films relevant to vertically stacked nanosheet devices.

articles.title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
articles.abstract: Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity1–5. We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells)6. Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by Nr3c1) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 (Rgs2), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of Nr3c1 during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal–immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals. IL-1β from neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby brown adipocytes in a low-UCP1 state; cold temperature reduces IL-1β via sympathetic nerves, leading to transition to a high-UCP1 state and increased thermogenesis, while higher temperatures have the opposite effect.
