The results show that turbulence may reduce rotor entry while simultaneously increasing swimming effort and disrupting passage. From an engineering perspective, the framework provides a way to evaluate turbine siting, clearance, layout and operating conditions using behaviourally relevant turbulence metrics in addition to conventional performance and blade-strike criteria.

articles.title: Operant conditioning in Indian free-ranging dogs: effects of positive and threatening cues on sociability
articles.abstract: Sociability towards humans is an adaptive trait in free-ranging dogs (FRDs), enabling them to access resources while navigating the risky anthropogenic habitat. We investigated whether operant conditioning shapes sociability in Indian FRDs and whether learned responses generalize to an unfamiliar individual. We exposed 54 dog groups to either a positive or a threatening cue over five consecutive days, followed by tests on day 6 with an unfamiliar and then the familiar experimenter. Using Bayesian GLMMs, we analysed approach proportion, approach latency and demeanour. The threatening cue reduced approach behaviour, increased approach latency and caused a shift towards neutral responses to the familiar experimenter, with the changes occurring earlier compared with the positive cue. The positive cue reduced approach latency towards the familiar experimenter, but did not increase the proportion of approach. Towards the unfamiliar experimenter on day 6, positive-cue groups approached more often, threatening-cue groups approached more slowly than on day 1, and demeanour changes under the threatening cue were specific to the familiar experimenter. Our results suggest that FRDs adjust their behaviour primarily towards the person associated with an outcome, which may help them balance resource acquisition with risk avoidance. These insights have implications for informing management strategies to enable dog–human coexistence.

articles.title: Optimizing voyages for biodiversity: rerouting vessels around ocean giants can have minimal impact on shipping
articles.abstract: Vessel strikes are a significant and growing threat to marine megafauna, yet few mitigation measures are implemented at scale owing to perceived economic costs to shipping. Here, we present a proof of concept for integrating biodiversity considerations into commercial voyage optimization, using critical aggregation sites for the endangered whale shark (Rhincodon typus) as a case study. We simulated eight port-to-port voyages for two vessel classes—a crude oil tanker and a container ship—under three routing scenarios: baseline optimization, speed reduction to 10 kts within core habitats and complete avoidance of these areas. Across routes, fuel-use changes ranged from −0.13% to 9.65%, with minimal impacts (less than 1%) for most long-distance voyages. Results indicate that speed reduction is the more efficient mitigation for short voyages, while area avoidance is preferable for longer voyages, with impacts varying by vessel type and operational constraints. Incorporating dynamic, species-specific habitat layers into voyage planning could enable targeted vessel strike mitigation with negligible disruption to global trade. Adoption of such measures, supported by improved data pipelines, dynamic forecasting and integration into regulatory and incentive frameworks, offers a scalable pathway to align biodiversity conservation with decarbonization goals in the maritime sector.

articles.title: Perception and misperception of social corrections: the case of challenging violations of gender equality and social inclusion on social media
articles.abstract: Social media platforms enable both gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) advocacy and GESI violations, such as hate speech and harassment. Challenging such violations through social correction by active users is essential, yet little is known about whether users accurately perceive others' attitudes towards this behaviour across cultural contexts. This cross-sectional study, based on an online survey of 325 UK and 312 Arab participants, examines self-reported attitudes and perceptions of others' attitudes towards three barriers to social correction: Relationship Consequences, Negative Impact on others and Futility, using linear mixed modelling. Findings indicate a discrepancy between self-reported attitudes and perceptions of others' attitudes, indicating a misperception. In the UK sample, misperceptions relate to Relationship Consequences and Futility, with participants expecting greater relational costs and less behavioural change when challenging others than when being challenged themselves. In the Arab GCC sample, participants perceived the challenged person as more negatively affected than they believed they themselves would be, though this pattern was less consistent across individual measures. These findings suggest that integrating social norm nudges into social media design could correct misperceived norms and empower users to challenge GESI violations. Limitations include sample representativeness and self-reported data; future research should use broader samples and qualitative methods.

articles.title: Prophylaxis in ant societies: a social response to pathogen vulnerability?
articles.abstract: Social insects rely on multiple defence mechanisms to limit pathogen transmission within colonies. Prophylactic sanitary behaviours are performed in the absence of immediate pathogenic threats and contribute to routine disease prevention. Among these behaviours, grooming and necrophoresis help manage potentially harmful biological material, but how their expression relates to variation in pathogen susceptibility among colonies remains poorly understood. We investigated the relationship between susceptibility to the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana and the expression of prophylactic grooming and necrophoresis in the ant Lasius flavus. We found strong and consistent intercolonial differences in pathogen susceptibility, as well as marked variation in the expression of prophylactic sanitary behaviours. None of the grooming behaviours examined were associated with pathogen susceptibility. However, more pathogen-susceptible colonies tended to remove corpses more rapidly during the early phase of necrophoresis. This pattern is consistent with a possible compensatory relationship among defence components, but may also arise from demographic and organizational differences among colonies, as worker age structure and task allocation can influence both susceptibility to infection and corpse removal behaviour. Overall, our results reveal substantial intercolonial variation in multiple components of disease defence but provide little support for a compensatory relationship between pathogen susceptibility and prophylactic sanitary behaviour.

articles.title: Structurally related Ca2+-release activated Ca2+ channel inhibitors exhibit distinct extracellular and intracellular modes of action
articles.abstract: Ca2+-release activated Ca2+ (CRAC) channels, formed by stromal interaction molecule (STIM) and Orai proteins, mediate store-operated Ca2+ entry and are implicated in autoimmune diseases, acute pancreatitis and cancer. Some small molecule inhibitors of these channels such as BTP2, Pyr6, Synta66 and GSK-7975A, are widely used as experimental tools, yet their precise mechanisms of action remain incompletely understood. Using whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology in rat basophilic leukaemia (RBL-1) cells, we determined whether each of these inhibitors acts from the extracellular or intracellular side of the plasma membrane. We found that BTP2 and GSK-7975A could suppress CRAC currents only when applied extracellularly, whereas Pyr6 and Synta66 were equally effective from either side. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations using a rat Orai1 channel model identified plausible extracellular binding sites for all four inhibitors and additional putative intracellular binding sites for Pyr6 and Synta66. These predicted sites are located near regions that are likely to influence pore geometry and channel gating. Our findings suggest that, despite considerable structural similarity, these popular CRAC channel inhibitors exhibit mechanistically distinct interactions with Orai1, with important implications for their use as research tools and for future CRAC channel drug discovery.

articles.title: The benefits of providing absolute rather than relative risks: evidence from a naturalistic study with the BBC
articles.abstract: Health stories in the media often contain relative risks, for example, ‘Eating bacon increases your risk of colorectal cancer by 20%’. While the reported changes in risk may be accurate, they do not allow the reader to know the relevant absolute risks (i.e. their chances of developing cancer if they do, or do not, eat bacon). We investigated what people infer the absolute risks to be when they are only given relative risks. Visitors to the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) news website read a story about the protective effects of mushroom consumption against mild cognitive impairment. Participants either saw the change in risk presented in relative format (50% decrease) or absolute format (from 19 per 100 to 9 per 100). Over 1000 people took part in the study and their data were analysed according to a pre-registered plan. We found that the median estimates of the absolute risks were correct even when participants only saw relative information, indicative of a ‘wisdom of the crowd’ effect. However, the relative format led people to have much larger errors in their estimates of the true risks when compared to the absolute format. Furthermore, the absolute format did not reduce participants' self-reported comprehension or interest in the story.

articles.title: The bird-like complexity of hadrosauroid beaks
articles.abstract: Duck-billed dinosaurs evolved complex cornified oral structures whose soft-tissue biology remains poorly understood. Here we investigate the rostral anatomy of the hadrosauroid Tethyshadros insularis using gross morphology and micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) data, focusing on the premaxillae and predentary. Structures previously interpreted as anomalous ‘spiked’ beak ornamentation are reinterpreted as osteological correlates of an extensive neurovascular network. Circumflex vessels, palatine and narial circulation and a median premaxillary sinus supplied a hypertrophied keratinous rhamphotheca that probably exceeded the extent of the underlying bone in both size and morphological complexity. Comparative evidence indicates that marginal denticulations reflect vascular excavation and/or ossified dermal papillary structures, implying vascular and somato-sensory functions analogous to avian beaks. Mesowear marks and functional correlates support a major role in cropping abrasive, grit-laden vegetation, while the dense vascularization suggests an additional thermoregulatory function via beak–nares heat exchange. These findings re-evaluate the hadrosauroid beak as a multifunctional sensory, mechanical and thermal organ, representing a key innovation that may have underpinned the ecological expansion and gigantism of later diverging hadrosaurids.

articles.title: The evolutionary structure of acoustic learnability: a deep learning approach to neotropical birdsong
articles.abstract: Passive acoustic monitoring offers a scalable solution for biodiversity assessment in the Neotropics, although classifying hundreds of sympatric species in complex soundscapes remains challenging. We developed a deep learning framework for large-scale avian classification by training convolutional neural networks on recordings from 667 Neotropical bird species across northern South America. EfficientNetV2L performed best, achieving 94.48% accuracy, 94.30% macro F1-score and 0.998 macro ROC-AUC. After training, we conducted a post hoc analysis of species-level F1-scores using phylogenetically informed models (phylogenetically generalized least squares (PGLS) and phylogenetic generalized linear mixed models (PGLMM)) to test morphological, ecological and geographic predictors under phylogenetic control. Broad traits explained little interspecific variation: the best-supported PGLS accounted for approximately 2.2% of the variance, whereas the null model received the strongest support among PGLMM candidates. Geographic range size showed the most consistent negative association with F1-score, while morphological and ecological predictors added little explanatory power. Performance nevertheless showed weak but significant phylogenetic signal, and frequent confusions tended to involve more closely related species. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping and Monte Carlo Dropout provided complementary descriptions of saliency and predictive uncertainty. Overall, deep learning performed effectively for regional biodiversity monitoring and provided a comparative framework for assessing how much of the variation in acoustic classification performance could be explained by broad biological predictors.

articles.title: Two-fold hidden diversity of diminutive horned frogs (Megophryinae: Jingophrys ) highlights overlooked in situ diversification in the Himalayas
articles.abstract: Jingophrys is a genus of Asian horned frogs known from six species with disjunct distributions in the Himalayas and Indo-Burma. By integrating evidence from molecular phylogeny, morphology and behaviour, we uncover five new species, recognize two distinct species groups, report two new country records for India and identify additional unnamed lineages. These additions constitute a seven-fold increase in the diversity of Indian Jingophrys and a more than two-fold increase for the genus overall. We also describe the first vocal repertoires of all eight Indian members, provide accounts of umbelliform tadpoles for three members and report a previously unknown snail-eating behaviour for the family Megophryidae. Present-day patterns of diversity and endemism may have been shaped by interplay between major rivers that subdivide the Eastern Himalayas from west to east and elevational range divergence at regional scales, which yields up to four congeners within a 10 km radius. The Himalayas are an overlooked and important centre of in situ diversification for frogs in the subfamily Megophryinae. Divergence timing, rapid diversification rates and biogeographical patterns across the large megophryine radiation are coincident with active Himalayan–Tibetan orogeny through the Late Oligocene and Miocene and intensification of the South Asian monsoon system starting around 10 Ma, in Late Miocene.

articles.title: Using polarizable flexible force fields to design metal-organic framework-containing mixed matrix membranes for hydrogen purification from solar water splitting
articles.abstract: In this study, mixed matrix membranes (MMMs) consisting of a continuous polymer phase and a dispersed metal-organic framework (MOF) phase were designed to purify hydrogen from the solar water splitting process. We first identified 20 MOFs with a small pore limiting diameter of less than or equal to 3 Å to restrict the passage of larger molecules such as N2 and O2, thereby allowing the smaller H2 molecule to pass through. These MOFs were assessed for water stability, thermal stability, solvent removal stability, and to identify open-metal sites. We developed atomistic polarizable flexible force fields for these 20 MOFs and used these in molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations to calculate diffusion constants and adsorption isotherms. Using these results, we selected stable MOFs with the highest permeability and ideal selectivity for hydrogen separation. We used experimental data for polymer permeability and selectivity. Finally, we used the Maxwell model to predict the permeability and ideal selectivity of each MMM. We observed that selectivity is primarily governed by polymer properties, and permeability increases by adding MOFs as the dispersed phase. Our computed results showed that MMMs have approximately a twofold reduction in required membrane area compared with pure polymers. Triptycene-based polybenzoxazole (TPBO)-1.0/ARIBOS performed the best, requiring the smallest membrane area.

articles.title: A LiDAR-based reconstruction reveals increasing Arctic phytoplankton production during low-light winter-shoulder period
articles.abstract: Arctic marine productivity is traditionally considered concentrated in the sunlit season, yet low-light winter-shoulder periods remain poorly constrained because passive ocean color observations require sufficient solar illumination. Here, we use 2.39 million spaceborne LiDAR profiles from CALIOP (2006–2023) to reconstruct Arctic net primary production (NPP) and evaluate how active-sensor observations reduce this seasonal blind spot. The bio-optical retrieval model was trained using MODIS-constrained observations under illuminated conditions; accordingly, low-light estimates represent physically constrained extrapolations beyond the primary MODIS-observable training domain rather than direct NPP measurements. Within this framework, LiDAR increases winter half-year observational coverage from ∼20 to 30% to ∼70 to 75% and reveals widespread low-light winter-shoulder production across marginal seas and seasonal ice-edge regions. Pan-Arctic NPP integrated over this period increased at an estimated rate of 0.75 Tg C year −1 during 2007–2023, whereas the corresponding passive-sensor signal was negligible. Accounting for this component raises annual Arctic NPP estimates by ∼13.3% indicating that passive sensor-based assessments may underrepresent the magnitude and seasonal structure of Arctic productivity. Associations with declining sea ice and surface warming suggest this underrepresented production is consistent with ongoing seasonal reorganization of Arctic carbon fixation. Uncertainties from model parameterization, low-light extrapolation, and limited in situ validation are largest in the lowest-light and highest-latitude regimes. These findings do not imply photosynthesis during absolute polar night, but show that active LiDAR observations with explicit light constraints and transparent extrapolation limits can test how unresolved low-light winter-shoulder production may alter Arctic NPP seasonality under continuing sea-ice loss.

articles.title: A TROP2-targeting aptamer enables selective drug delivery and potent antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer
articles.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains difficult to treat, highlighting the need for strategies that selectively deliver cytotoxic agents to tumor cells. Trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP2) has been proposed as a candidate therapeutic target in PDAC, but non-antibody-based delivery formats remain underexplored. Using protein-SELEX, we identified T17, a high-affinity aptamer that specifically binds to TROP2, and conjugated it to monomethyl auristatin E through an MC-Val-Cit-PAB linker to generate the aptamer-drug conjugate T17-M. Preclinical evaluation in cellular and animal models showed that T17-M retained TROP2-dependent binding, underwent clathrin-mediated internalization and lysosomal processing, and suppressed tumor growth in cell-line-derived and patient-derived xenografts. T17-M also reduced liver metastasis and induced calreticulin exposure, ATP release, and HMGB1 secretion, consistent with immunogenic cell death. In immunocompetent models, T17-M promoted dendritic-cell activation and CD8 + T cell infiltration, while its combination with PD-1 blockade further enhanced tumor control and prolonged survival. These findings provide preclinical proof-of-concept for T17-M as an alternative TROP2-targeted drug-delivery strategy for PDAC.

articles.title: A fully hydrogel implantable patch for in situ ultrasonic monitoring of gastric leakage
articles.abstract: Gastric leakage is a common and life-threatening postoperative complication, while delayed detection often leads to severe abdominal organ damage. Current radiological imaging modalities are limited in their ability to provide timely detection of gastric leakage, while the mechanical mismatch and long-term persistence of conventional electronic sensors limit their implantable applications. In this work, we developed a fully hydrogel-based ultrasonic metagel patch (USMP) for direct, real-time monitoring of gastric leakage via ultrasound imaging. The USMP incorporates a tree-ring air cell array, in which densely distributed air cells arranged in concentric rings create a strong back-scattering effect, thereby producing distinctive and stable ultrasound imaging signatures for rapid and sensitive detection. The air cells are encapsulated within biocompatible, hydrolytically degradable pH-responsive hydrogels, forming a fully hydrogel sensing architecture. The potential of the USMP for gastric leakage monitoring up to 7 days postimplantation is validated in the live rabbit model.

articles.title: A primordial heavy water reservoir in the outer solar system
articles.abstract: The oxygen (O) isotopic composition of outer solar system ices is believed to be enriched in heavy O isotopes owing to photochemical processes, but evidence for this O reservoir is exceedingly rare in meteorites. Hydrated interplanetary dust particles (IDPs) collected in Earth’s stratosphere that display high densities of solar energetic particle tracks originate from Edgeworth-Kuiper belt objects. Their mineralogy is dominated by hydrated minerals that formed by alteration of anhydrous precursor minerals at low temperatures through reactions with water (H 2 O)–carbon dioxide fluids. The O isotopic compositions of track-rich hydrated IDPs implicate 17,18 O-rich ices as the source of H 2 O involved in their alteration, providing compelling evidence for the presence of a major heavy water reservoir beyond the orbits of the gas giant planets that was largely isolated from inner solar system materials.

articles.title: Arbitrarily cuttable and ultrathin MXene structural colors for customizable and wearable multispectral information management
articles.abstract: Structural colors based on natural and artificial microstructures show promising light manipulation. As atomically thick building blocks, Ti 3 C 2 T x sheets have been successfully assembled into the ultrathin, flexible, arbitrarily cuttable, large-size structural colors by the simple and low-cost spray methods based on the lossy thin-film interference. By ordered stacking atomically thick Ti 3 C 2 T x layer by layer at well-organized low–surface tension semidry assemble state, rich colors from yellow to gray with the thickness from ∼22 to ∼154 nanometers of uniform Ti 3 C 2 T x colors are obtained, having the thinnest framework among solution-processed flexible structural colors with similar optical performance. Low-infrared emissivity from room to 300°C temperature and region-selective patterns make highly information-fused and complex visible-infrared (VIS-IR) Ti 3 C 2 T x colors camouflage. Without conventional dielectric layer between Ti 3 C 2 T x and substrate, automated spraying system can produce meter-scale films that can be cut and sewn into VIS-IR concealment “camouflage cloaks” easily, promising ultrathin multifunctional information systems and beyond.

articles.title: Asymmetric cell division is predictive of human T cell vaccine responses
articles.abstract: Vaccine-induced protection relies on the generation and maintenance of stem-like memory B and T cells, a process sustained by two conserved mechanisms: asymmetric cell division (ACD) and autophagy. In T cells, ACD enables them to produce progeny with the same T cell receptor but with divergent metabolic and functional fates upon antigen encounter through the unequal inheritance of cellular cargoes. Autophagy recycles cellular components, provides metabolic substrates essential for sustaining energy demands, and is relevant for the maintenance of T cell memory. Direct evidence of how these processes synergize and affect human immunity is still lacking. Here, we show that mitotic human CD8 + T cells asymmetrically segregate autophagy-related organelles, including autophagosomes and lysosomes. Furthermore, we show that ACD drives divergent transcriptional and functional fates in daughter cells. Extending these findings to an influenza vaccine trial, we demonstrate that autophagic flux follows the dynamics of clonal expansion and contraction of antigen-specific T cells. Notably, individuals with enhanced ACD capacity, especially with increased LC3B asymmetry, exhibit better vaccine responses, linking early cellular segregation events to long-term immune fitness. Last, transient use of the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 inhibitor rapamycin improved memory survival, which was associated with improved ACD, measured by the asymmetric inheritance of both CD8 and LC3B. Together, these findings highlight that the asymmetric inheritance of the autophagy machinery represents another layer of human adaptive immunity and offers a potential therapeutic target to enhance vaccine outcomes.

articles.title: Basin-scale changes in net primary production from the biogeochemical-Argo array
articles.abstract: Marine net primary production is expected to be affected by climate change. Although remote sensing offers broad spatial and temporal coverage, it is limited to surface observations and cannot capture subsurface variability. Autonomous profiling floats provide critical depth-resolved measurements that help bridge this gap. Here, we use data from the biogeochemical-Argo array to estimate basin-scale change in net primary production using the carbon-based production algorithm. We find statistically significant negative trends across the Atlantic and Southern Oceans and positive trends in the Pacific Ocean. These changes, if occurring in response to climate forcing, raise concern due to the key role of phytoplankton productivity in sustaining marine ecosystems. These trends typically agree in direction and magnitude with those from satellites. Our findings highlight the value of the biogeochemical-Argo array in detecting change in ocean productivity, demonstrating its potential for sustained monitoring. These results underscore the need for integrated observing systems to capture the full extent of changing marine productivity.

articles.title: Boosting stability and charge transfer of conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) through complementary topology
articles.abstract: Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) is a benchmark n-type conjugated polymer known for its record-high electrical conductivity. Nevertheless, its thermal robustness and charge/ion transport characteristics remain insufficient. To address this issue, we report a hierarchical complementary topology strategy via doping PBFDO with choline chloride (ChCl). At the molecular scale, the cations Ch + selectively intercalate along the out-of-plane direction while simultaneously densifying the in-plane π-π stacking, accompanied by partial removal of H + . At the submicrometer scale, this induces distinct phase separation into high- and low-density stacking domains. As a result, the product PBFDO-ChCl exhibited a synergistic performance boost, with a 2.8-fold enhancement in high-temperature resilience, a 1.6-fold increase in sheet conductance, and a 15.9-fold reduction in ion diffusion resistance. Then, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) using PBFDO-ChCl as channel material further confirm these performance enhancements. As a whole, this work closes the performance gap between n-type PBFDO and state-of-the-art p-type conjugated polymers, potentially advancing its applications from energy storage to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing.

articles.title: Brown carbon in biomass burning aerosol enhances HONO production
articles.abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is an important source of hydroxyl radicals (•OH). •OH drives ozone and aerosol formation, affecting air quality, health, and climate. Elevated HONO concentrations have been observed in biomass burning (BB) plumes. However, the mechanism remains unclear, hindering parameterization and quantification of the impacts. Here, we conducted flow tube experiments with BB aerosol samples and proxies to investigate renoxification, a process that converts nitrate into HONO and NO x (NO and NO 2 ). Our results reveal that renoxification in BB aerosol is enhanced by brown carbon (BrC) through electron transfer to nitrate as an alternative to surface-enhanced nitrate photolysis. We develop parameterization to assess the potential global impacts of BrC-enhanced renoxification, which suggests that BrC enhances surface-level HONO production by up to one order of magnitude in BB-affected regions, with surface HONO production exceeding 1 part per trillion per hour in regions with high aerosol nitrate. These impacts are expected to worsen as BB intensifies in a warming climate.

articles.title: Cell adhesion molecule–related proteins signal to promote cytoneme elongation from Sonic Hedgehog–producing cells
articles.abstract: Tissue morphogenesis and postdevelopmental homeostasis rely on efficient information exchange between communicating cells. Cytonemes are actin-based protrusions that contribute to precise information flow by facilitating contact-mediated directional transport of diverse signaling cargoes. How pathway-specific cytonemes are formed is poorly understood, as are the molecular mechanisms promoting actin organization for elongation and stability of the dynamic cellular extensions. We investigated biogenesis of Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) cytonemes, revealing functional repurposing of cell adhesion molecule-related proteins Brother of CDON (BOC) and Cell adhesion molecule-related, Down-regulated by Oncogenes (CDON) into recruiters of actin regulators FARP1 and Cdc42 for cytoneme elongation. Loss of BOC and CDON function blunts protrusion-localized Cdc42 activity, reducing cytoneme lengths and occurrence in SHH-expressing cells. Live imaging of developing murine spinal cords reveals that CDON loss in SHH-expressing cells reduces the frequency of neuroepithelial cytonemes and alters neuronal cell fate specification. These results inform a model whereby SHH-binding proteins promote ligand transport through stimulating formation of long cytonemes.

articles.title: Autane: An autonomous crane for sustained port operations
articles.abstract: Fully automated cranes are revolutionizing modern port operations by addressing labor shortages, improving precision, and enhancing safety. Toward this goal, we present the Autane (autonomous crane) system specifically developed for rubber tire gantry (RTG) cranes handling standardized containers in port yards, enabling autonomous safety-critical container grabbing, transport, and placement with high accuracy, adaptability, and efficiency. Autane overcomes the challenges of safe motion of large-scale cranes with centimeter-level precision requirements, providing long-distance high-precision perception. It uses multisensor fusion, real-time obstacle detection, and simultaneous localization and mapping to perceive the environment, identify container features, and dynamically adjust trajectories. By tightly coupling perception, planning, control, and operation and maintenance, Autane achieves safe and precise alignment, seamless interaction with transport vehicles, and robust execution of long-distance handling tasks. Deployed in multiple ports, Autane shows full-day operation and has autonomously handled more than 2 million 20-foot equivalent units. This work highlights the potential of fully autonomous RTG cranes to enable sustained, resilient, and low-intervention port automation.

articles.title: Heavy metal acrobatics: Learning dynamic control for skid-steer loaders
articles.abstract: Automation of heavy machinery offers the opportunity to improve productivity in mechanized industries such as construction, mining, and material handling. Yet, automation of such machines is challenged by their complex dynamics, in part because of hydraulic actuation that involves fluids, flexible elements, and nonlinear delays. A concomitant challenge is the size and weight of these machines, which can make experiments on the physical systems exceedingly dangerous. Here, we show that reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation, followed by transfer of the learned policies from simulation to reality, can successfully automate acrobatic maneuvers that push a heavy construction machine to the limits of its actuation and have only previously been accomplished by a small number of elite human operators in official world-record performances. We trained policies that perform autonomous acrobatic maneuvers on a John Deere 332G, an operational 5-tonne skid-steer loader. The policies can autonomously swing the machine up onto two wheels and, while balancing on two wheels, drive over rough terrain, trace out specified trajectories, spin around, and swing the bucket back and forth before landing it safely back onto four wheels. This work demonstrates that RL and sim-to-real transfer enable dynamic autonomous control of heavy machinery, directly contributing to greater automation in heavy equipment sectors.

articles.title: Through human eyes: How perception and interaction shape humanoid robot acceptance
articles.abstract: Robot acceptance is shaped by dynamic, multimodal interactions that influence trust, comfort, and behavioral intentions.

articles.title: Albumin-bound paclitaxel–induced stromal reprogramming drives resistance to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with pancreatic cancer
articles.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy for which neoadjuvant chemotherapy with albumin-bound paclitaxel combined with gemcitabine (AG) is a standard first-line approach for borderline resectable and locally advanced disease. However, secondary resistance to this regimen is common, and its underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. In this study, we investigated how neoadjuvant AG therapy shapes the tumor stroma in PDAC. Single-cell transcriptomics of patient tumors revealed that AG treatment induces a phenotypic switch of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) from myofibroblastic (myCAF) to inflammatory (iCAF) states and identified a previously unrecognized TMEM100 + CAF subset enriched in nonresponders. Mechanistic studies showed that albumin-bound paclitaxel activates IL-2–STAT5 signaling to drive TMEM100 expression and that TMEM100 + CAFs promote chemoresistance through paracrine secretion of amphiregulin (AREG) and activation of tumor EGFR signaling. Genetic ablation of TMEM100 + CAFs in mouse models reversed CAF switching and enhanced the antitumor efficacy of AG therapy. These findings map chemotherapy-induced CAF plasticity, reveal a TMEM100-AREG axis of resistance, and highlight TMEM100 + CAFs as a promising target to sensitize PDAC to neoadjuvant treatment.

articles.title: Dual inhibition of TNF-α and IL-1β signaling through BIG2 ameliorates osteoarthritis in mouse and primate models
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA), a leading cause of disability, is characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation and metabolic dysregulation in chondrocytes. TNF-α and IL-1β are key inflammatory drivers in OA pathogenesis, but clinical trials targeting them individually have been unsuccessful, highlighting the potential need for dual-targeting strategies. By screening a US Food and Drug Administration–approved drug library, we identified dabigatran, a thrombin inhibitor, as a potent dual suppressor of TNF-α and IL-1β signaling that restored chondrocyte metabolism. In preclinical OA models, including both mice and cynomolgus macaques, dabigatran attenuated cartilage degeneration, alleviated pain, and improved joint function. To elucidate the molecular mechanisms, we performed biochemical copurification coupled with mass spectrometry, identifying brefeldin A–inhibited guanine nucleotide–exchange protein 2 (BIG2) as a previously unknown dabigatran-binding target. Mechanistically, dabigatran binds to BIG2, promoting BIG2-dependent TNFR1 release to dampen TNF-α signaling while enhancing BIG2-mediated IL-1R1 degradation through the autophagy-lysosome pathway to limit IL-1β effects. These findings establish BIG2-mediated receptor trafficking and membrane dynamics as a regulatory node that concurrently inhibits TNF-α and IL-1β signaling, suggesting this pathway as a potential therapeutic strategy for OA.

articles.title: Erratum for the Research Article “Preclinical and clinical evaluation of systemic danegaptide for the treatment of nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy”
Frequency of pharmacogenomic variation and medication exposures among participants in the All of Us Research Program
articles.abstract: Pharmacogenomics promises improved outcomes through individualized prescribing. However, the lack of diversity in pharmacogenomics studies impedes clinical translation and the application of precision medicine across populations. We evaluated the frequencies of variants in 16 pharmacogenes ( ABCG2 , CACNA1S , CYP2D6 , CYP2C Cluster , CYP2C19 , CYP2C9 , CYP3A5 , CYP4F2 , DPYD , G6PD , NUDT15 , RYR1 , SLCO1B1 , TPMT , UGT1A1 , and VKORC1 ) and predicted phenotypes and medication exposures using whole-genome sequencing and electronic health record data from nearly 100,000 All of Us Research Program participants. We report that 100% of participants carried at least one pharmacogenomic variant and nearly all (99.5%) had a predicted phenotype with prescribing recommendations. Clinical impact was high with 24.4% of participants having both an actionable phenotype for these pharmacogenes and a prior exposure to an impacted medication with pharmacogenomic prescribing guidance. Importantly, we report thousands of previously unrecognized pharmacogene variants and hundreds of alleles and predicted phenotypes that deviate from known frequencies across populations or were previously unreported, especially in the Americas and African ancestry groups.

articles.title: Human antibody combinations determined by epitope mapping of orthopoxvirus A33/A35 confer therapeutic protection in mice
articles.abstract: Human infections with mpox virus (MPXV) since 2022 have resulted in more than 188,000 cases reported globally as of June 2026, highlighting the urgent need for effective therapeutics. Here, we recruited smallpox vaccinees and donors with incidental vaccinia virus (VACV) exposure and isolated a panel of human anti-A33/A35 monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) from the latter using recombinant MPXV A35 as a cross-reactive bait. These mAbs recognized four distinct nonoverlapping epitopes (epitopes 1 to 4) and one composite epitope (epitope 3 + 4) on MPXV A35 and exhibited cross-reactivity against multiple orthopoxviruses (OPXVs). Cryo–electron microscopy structural analysis revealed that the high-affinity epitope 3 + 4 mAb HD15 engages an epitope at the A35 dimer interface that is conserved across OPXVs. Combinations of mAbs targeting nonoverlapping epitopes mediated synergistic, Fc-dependent neutralization in vitro; conferred therapeutic protection against lethal VACV challenge; and reduced viral burden and disease severity after MPXV challenge in mice. Together, these findings establish a single-antigen, multiepitope strategy for the development of broadly protective therapeutics against OPXVs.

articles.title: Osimertinib, platinum, and etoposide for patients with metastatic EGFR/TP53/RB1-mutant lung cancers at risk for histological transformation
articles.abstract: Although EGFR inhibitors are highly effective for treating EGFR- mutant lung adenocarcinomas ( EGFR + LUADs), resistance inevitably emerges, with histologic transformation to small cell lung cancer (SCLC) representing a particularly aggressive mechanism. Our prospective trial enrolled patients with EGFR + LUAD at high risk of transformation ( TP53 / RB1 -deficient) and treated them with first-line osimertinib combined with platinum and etoposide. Despite the addition of SCLC-directed chemotherapy, nearly half of patients (5 of 11) underwent SCLC transformation, with median progression-free survival of 11 months and overall survival of 33 months. Genomic and single-cell transcriptomic profiling of patient samples revealed clinical and subclinical plasticity associated with TP53 / RB1 comutations, including histological transformation to SCLC, as well as mesenchymal and squamous histologies. These changes in plasticity were linked to progressive disruption of the RB pathway, leading to altered chromatin accessibility and induction of neuronal differentiation and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition transcriptional programs, further intensified by osimertinib treatment. These findings provide insights into the role of plasticity in mediating drug tolerance.

articles.title: Sleep-like slow waves during wakefulness are associated with hallucinations and poorer cognition in Parkinson’s disease
articles.abstract: Slow waves during sleep are fundamental for neural homeostasis, metabolic regulation, and waste clearance and are known to be altered in neurodegenerative diseases. Sleep-like slow waves (SLSWs) have been observed in awake, healthy individuals, where they are linked to fluctuations in vigilance and mind-wandering. Whether SLSWs are altered in Parkinson’s disease (PD), and whether such alterations contribute to psychiatric or cognitive complications, remains unknown. In a cohort of 84 nondemented patients with PD and 30 healthy older adults, we found that SLSWs occurred more frequently in patients with PD. Hallucinatory traits in patients with PD were associated with higher SLSW amplitude, especially over frontocentral regions. Moreover, more prominent SLSWs were associated with poorer cognitive functions. We conclude that, whereas slow waves during sleep have positive physiological functions, exacerbated diurnal SLSWs may reflect responses related to PD neuropathology, at the cost of hallucinations and reduced cognitive function.

articles.title: High resolution structures of rat brain V-ATPase with concanamycin
articles.abstract: Nishida et al. reveal how the macrolide inhibitor concanamycin blocks V-ATPase by wedging between moving and stationary components of the proton pump. Structural analysis in native membranes further shows that membrane environment can alter inhibitor occupancy, highlighting the value of in situ structural biology for drug design.

articles.title: Changes in pregabalin use and overdose after government interventions and media coverage: retrospective observational study
articles.abstract: ObjectivesTo evaluate trends in pregabalin use and overdose in Australia and examine temporal relationships with media coverage (December 2018), prescribing and dispensing restrictions (April 2020), and boxed warnings (February 2021).DesignRetrospective observational study of dispensing and overdose data, with changepoint, interrupted time series, and latent class analysis.Setting and participantsPharmaceutical Benefits Scheme data (PBS; 10% random sample of people with drug subsidies) and overdose calls (self-harm, recreational use, and misuse) reported to Australia’s largest Poisons Centre (50% national sample), 2016-24.Main outcome measuresPopulation adjusted rates of dispensing and overdose, timing of breakpoints and rate ratios, proportion of people who use pregabalin at high risk of misuse.Results227 864 people were dispensed 3 441 851 pregabalin prescriptions in the PBS 10% sample and 4871 pregabalin overdose calls were made to the Poisons Centre. Pregabalin use peaked in 2018 before plateauing and declining. Three breakpoints were found in dispensing data, with major decreases in level and slope: December 2018, May 2020, December 2021. The combined rate ratio for dispensing was 0.748 (95% confidence interval 0.700 to 0.800). Compared with the projected historical trend in the absence of interventions (counterfactual), approximately 118 390 (93 960 to 140 940) fewer pregabalin prescriptions were recorded nationally in December 2021, and an ongoing reduction of 0.7% (0.5% to 0.9%) was found each month. All breakpoints were associated with declines in overdose rates, with a combined rate ratio of 0.532 (95% CI 0.406 to 0.695). This reduction corresponded to approximately 41.3 (26.9 to 52.4) fewer pregabalin overdose calls in December 2021 and an ongoing reduction of 1.6% (1.0% to 2.3%) each month. Latent class analysis of 57 744 people dispensed pregabalin in the 12 months after the final breakpoint revealed four groups. The high risk group (7790, 13.5%) were more likely male, younger, dispensed more pregabalin, with shorter refill interval and high rates of opioids and benzodiazepine co-use (5120 (65.7%) and 2455 (31.5%), respectively).ConclusionsPregabalin use and overdose in Australia have declined in recent years. Major decreases in trend corresponded with media coverage (December 2018) and prescribing and dispensing restrictions (May 2020). The third breakpoint may be a delayed impact of boxed warnings (implemented February 2021). These findings suggest that regulatory and risk communication measures may contribute to reducing pregabalin related harm.

articles.title: Consultants’ strike in England is called off as union “pauses” action
articles.abstract: Consultants in England have called off their two day strike later this month after the BMA agreed to enter formal negotiations with the government on pay and working conditions.The BMA’s Consultants Committee has been in dispute with the government since May 2025. In July this year consultants voted for strike action unless an improved offer was made.1 The existing pay offer would raise pay by only 2.4% in 2027-28.2However, after the committee met on 10 November, members agreed to “pause” planned action on 25 and 26 November3 to allow negotiations to take place.The BMA had been seeking “meaningful progress” on consultants’ real term pay cuts, “increasingly unsustainable” workloads, and worsening working conditions, the union said. Union representatives say that consultants have lost a quarter of their pay in real terms over the past 17 years.Helen Neary and Shanu Datta, co-chairs of the BMA Consultants Committee, said, “We’ve always said strikes...

articles.title: Effect of discontinuing antihypertensives on perioperative hypotension in older patients before non-cardiac surgery: multicentre, randomised, double blind, controlled trial
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo determine whether discontinuing versus continuing angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) on the morning of surgery reduces perioperative hypotension in older patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery.DesignMulticentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled trial.SettingFive tertiary teaching hospitals in China, November 2020 to December 2023.Participants2036 older patients (60-80 years) using ACE inhibitors or ARBs for at least two weeks and scheduled for non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia.InterventionsPatients were randomised to receive their usual ACE inhibitor or ARB or a placebo in identical capsules on the morning of surgery.Main outcome measuresThe primary outcome was the incidence of perioperative hypotension (mean blood pressure <65 mm Hg or a ≥30% decrease from baseline requiring treatment). Secondary outcomes included duration of hypotension, requirement for a vasopressor, intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, and 30 day complications (neurocognitive disorders, major cardiocerebral events) or mortality.Results2012 patients (mean age 68.8 years; 54.4% male) completed the study: 1004 were included in the antihypertensive group and 1008 in the no antihypertensive group. The incidence of perioperative hypotension was lower in the no antihypertensive group (314/1008, 31.2%) versus antihypertensive group (457/1004, 45.5%): adjusted odds ratio 0.52 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43 to 0.63); absolute risk difference -14.4% (95% CI -18.5% to -10.1%); P<0.001. The duration of hypotension and requirement for a vasopressor were both reduced in the no antihypertensive group: adjusted mean difference -1.3 minutes (95% CI -1.8 to -0.8 minutes) and 28.5% v 41.1%; adjusted odds ratio 0.54 (95% CI 0.44 to 0.66). Intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, 30 day complications, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups.ConclusionsDiscontinuing ACE inhibitors or ARBs on the morning of surgery in older patients with hypertension statistically significantly reduced perioperative hypotension and the requirement for vasopressors without increasing 30 day complications or mortality. This simple strategy provides high certainty evidence for preoperative drug management in this patient population.Trial registrationChinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2000039376.

articles.title: Pregabalin: the case for dialling back on a mediocre analgesic
articles.abstract: Since its commercial launch in 2005, pregabalin has generated more than $50bn (£37bn; €44bn) in global revenue. Originally developed as an anticonvulsant, it became a “blockbuster” largely through its use for pain, including diabetic neuropathy, postherpetic neuralgia, fibromyalgia, and low back pain. Yet behind its commercial success lies a less flattering story: mounting evidence of harms ranging from oedema and weight gain to withdrawal, misuse, and death.In a linked study, Cairns and colleagues (10.1136/bmj-2026-101021) examine prescribing patterns and overdose trends involving pregabalin in Australia.1 Drawing on nine years of dispensing claims and poison centre data, they assessed changes following regulatory interventions (including tighter prescribing restrictions, strengthened safety warnings, and prescription monitoring) and media reports highlighting pregabalin’s harms. Compared with projections based on earlier trends, prescriptions were 25% lower and intentional poisoning calls 47% lower than expected. The study is timely and rigorous, but these figures warrant caution. The ecological design...

articles.title: We should be wary of campaigns by pharmaceutical companies to destigmatise obesity
articles.abstract: Eli Lilly’s UK “Obesity is a Disease” campaign is easy to applaud and easier to underestimate.1 Adverts across the UK explain that obesity is a complex disease rather than a failure of willpower, that the body can resist weight loss, and that people who have struggled for years deserve compassion, not blame. The advert invites people to check their body mass index (BMI), answer a few questions, and prepare for a conversation with a doctor, nurse, or pharmacist. Drugs are not mentioned though the campaign is by a pharmaceutical company whose drug tirzepatide is now a principal treatment for obesity.2Almost everything it says about stigma is true: weight stigma is harmful, shame does not produce sustainable weight loss, and the claim that obesity is a disease is accurate.3 In 2025 a Lancet Commission proposed formal diagnostic criteria for “clinical obesity,” endorsed by dozens of medical bodies.4 The framing is at...

articles.title: Yvette Cooper unveils new NHS quango as part of abolishing “world’s largest quango”
articles.abstract: A new NHS body separate from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) is being set up to take on NHS England’s regional work, the health secretary has confirmed.1The government announced last year that it would abolish “the world’s largest quango”—NHS England. At the time the former prime minister Keir Starmer said that he could not justify spending taxpayers’ money “on two layers of bureaucracy.”234Following through on this announcement has been far from easy, however, with reports of problems in integrating NHS England staff into the civil service because of pay discrepancies,5 as well as huge redundancy costs.6 Experts have questioned the government’s lack of forethought and planning before announcing that it would abolish NHS England.Now the health secretary, Yvette Cooper—who inherited the job of seeing the abolition through from Wes Streeting7—has announced that while the “vast majority of [NHS England’s] current national delivery functions will transfer” into a...

articles.title: [Articles] Trevogrumab (anti-GDF8) with or without garetosmab (anti-activin A) for prevention of muscle loss during semaglutide-induced weight reduction in people with obesity (COURAGE): a two-part, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial
articles.abstract: This study establishes proof of concept for GDF8 inhibition by trevogrumab alone as a generally well tolerated strategy to preserve lean mass during GLP-1 receptor agonist-induced weight loss. Although the addition of ActA inhibition by garetosmab further improved body composition and weight loss, the combination did not have favourable safety and tolerability. Further study is required to understand whether improved body composition during weight loss might preserve physical function and overall metabolic health.

articles.title: IGF binding proteins: emerging endocrine mediators of cancer-associated muscle wasting
articles.abstract: Cancer-associated sarcopenia is a key determinant of treatment toxicity and mortality. Recent data indicate that insulin-like growth factor binding protein 1 and insulin-like growth factor binding protein 2 may be endocrine mediators connecting tumor-derived signals, hepatic reprogramming, and defective muscle regeneration. Furthermore, aging may contribute to susceptibility to cancer-associated muscle loss through alterations in the insulin-like growth factor (IGF)/insulin-like growth factor binding protein (IGFBP) axis and decreased muscle’s anabolic and regenerative capacity. Recent mechanistic studies have identified the IGF/IGFBP axis as a promising source of biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets in cancer-associated muscle wasting.

articles.title: Noncanonical metabolic and immune checkpoint topography in cancer
articles.abstract: Tumor metabolism and immune regulation are traditionally interpreted through global metabolic reprogramming and canonical, membrane-bound immunosuppression. Emerging evidence, however, indicates that metabolic components and immune checkpoints frequently undergo subcellular spatial redistribution, generating highly localized microdomains of accumulation and specific depletion zones within tumor cells. These compartmentalized events drive noncanonical molecular functions that extend far beyond their classical roles. By reshaping epigenetic regulation, oncogenic signaling, and local protein-interaction networks, these spatial shifts influence malignant phenotypes, immune evasion, and therapeutic responses. In this review, we highlight the subcellular compartmentalization of metabolic and immune checkpoint components, alongside their corresponding localized enrichment and depletion states, and discuss their intricate interplay. We illustrate how these spatially restricted dynamics establish a highly organized layer of tumor immunometabolic crosstalk.

articles.title: Decoupling language and emotion in the bilingual brain
articles.abstract: In a recent article, Davydova et al. showed that affect labeling fails in a second, less-proficient language due to the amygdala–ventrolateral prefrontal cortex functional connectivity. This subcortical decoupling also explains the emotional blunting that bilinguals report when using their less-proficient language.

articles.title: The development of individuality: beyond nature and nurture
articles.abstract: How does behavioral individuality arise? Theoretical models have highlighted the potential roles of genes and the environment. However, Gallagher et al. show that behavioral individuality occurs in the absence of genetic variation and is unaffected by experimentally manipulating the developmental environment. This suggests that behavioral individuality may originate even before birth.

articles.title: Buffer-Gas-Assisted Fluorescence Spectroscopy of Molecular Ions
articles.abstract: Sustained fluorescence detection of generic molecules has been challenging due to the lack of cycling transitions and limited photon budgets. We demonstrate a nondestructive method for continuous fluorescence of strongly rovibronically open molecular ions, $^{232}$ThF$^+$. Effective quasi-cycling transitions are established by room-temperature buffer-gas collisions, which replenish the population back to the laser-addressed states. In situ images and rotationally resolved spectra are obtained without optical repumping or auxiliary atomic readout ions. Combined with low-background spectroscopic detection, this approach achieves a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 6 in a 1 s exposure on the P(1) line of $^{232}$ThF$^+$, despite a thermal population of only approximately 0.17% in the addressed state at room temperature. The ability to repeatedly interrogate trapped ions is particularly promising for scarce molecular samples, broadband spectroscopic searches, and in situ monitoring of molecular reactions.

articles.title: Crystal Nucleation Driven by Microjets from Hydrodynamically Interacting Thermocavitation Bubbles
articles.abstract: Primary nucleation predominantly dictates the physicochemical, optical and mechanical properties of crystals emerging from solution. Here, we reveal a previously unrecognized nucleation mechanism arising from bubble-bubble hydrodynamic interactions using laser-induced thermocavitation bubble pairs. Under confinement, antiphase generation of two bubbles produces a micron-scale, high-speed liquid jet. Upon impact with the surrounding supersaturated liquid, this microjet generates intense localized shear, thereby inducing crystallization of the model inorganic salt, potassium permanganate. Under identical laser energies and supersaturation levels, crystallization was not observed in single-bubble experiments, in which no microjet was present. We show that the crystallization probability increases with microjet velocity. Boundary integral simulations reveal how experimental parameters such as confinement, bubble spacing, and laser energy govern microjet formation and velocity. We quantify the relationship between jet velocity and the observed enhancement in crystal nucleation kinetics by incorporating shear into the kinetic prefactor in classical nucleation theory. By combining experiments, theory, and simulations, we establish how microjets emerging from bubble-bubble hydrodynamic interactions may influence crystallization kinetics, opening new opportunities for the manufacture of crystalline materials.

articles.title: Detrital Remanent Magnetization Analysis at the Particle Scale: Implications for Prebiotic Origins of Homochirality
articles.abstract: Detrital remanent magnetization (DRM), the alignment of ferromagnetic grains with the geomagnetic field during sedimentation, is the primary mechanism of paleomagnetic remanence acquisition in sedimentary rocks, yet its microphysical mechanism remains contested. Measured DRM intensities consistently fall below theoretical predictions-the long-standing "DRM efficiency gap"-and no single-particle resolving observations have been available to test DRM acquisition models directly. Here we apply quantum diamond microscopy (QDM) to laboratory-redeposited lacustrine sediments to obtain the first single-particle magnetizations of DRM carriers. We compare these measurements with the results of bulk magnetometry and a Langevin-based kinetic model. We observe a statistically significant mean alignment of individual detrital particle moments with the applied field, $10\%$ when averaged as unit vectors and $24\%$ when weighted by moment magnitude, with the vector sum of all particles reproducing the direction of the bulk DRM, which is $\sim1.8\%$ of saturation remanence. Particle-level analysis shows that alignment rises with particle moment, a trend reproduced by our kinetic model in which floc-hosted magnetite rotates toward the field until the surrounding sediment locks it in place. Even where post-depositional disturbance is minimal and the measured DRM reaches the upper end of reported efficiencies, it remains well below its theoretical maximum, limited in comparable measure by incomplete particle-level alignment and sub-saturation within-particle magnetization. Beyond its implications for the DRM mechanism, this strong particle-level bias provides a quantitative foundation for magnetic minerals as natural chiral agents, a proposed pathway for the emergence of biomolecular homochirality on the prebiotic Earth.

articles.title: Hybrid Machine Learning for Physically Consistent Prediction of Mutual Diffusion Coefficients in Binary Liquid Mixtures
articles.abstract: Experimental data on mutual diffusion coefficients in liquid mixtures are scarce, and existing prediction methods are unreliable for non-ideal mixtures. Building on HADES, our hybrid model for self-diffusion coefficients, we introduce the Enhanced Vignes Equation (EVE), which augments the Vignes equation with a deep-set model. Its inputs are molecular descriptors derived from SMILES and activity-coefficient information from HANNA, a machine-learning model for activity coefficients. EVE predicts Maxwell--Stefan diffusion coefficients; the corresponding Fickian coefficients follow from the thermodynamic factor, likewise obtained from HANNA. Trained and evaluated on 2106 experimental data points for 123 binary mixtures, EVE outperforms all available semi-empirical models, halving the mean absolute relative error for mixtures without experimental infinite-dilution diffusion data. Combined with HADES, EVE yields the complete set of self- and mutual diffusion coefficients of a binary mixture from SMILES and pure-component viscosities alone. EVE and HADES are available at https://ml-prop.mv.rptu.de/, and the code is fully disclosed.

articles.title: Open Quantum System Embedded in an Optimized Reservoir of Molecules
articles.abstract: Open-boundary Quantum Mechanics/Molecular Mechanics (QM/MM) simulation provides a direct way to test whether a quantum subsystem and its surrounding classical reservoir are physically consistent. Here we use this framework to replace a standard flexible TIP3P reservoir by a dipole-renormalized (DR) Amber-compatible three-site water model optimized against a full \textit{ab initio} trajectory of liquid water. The renormalization targets the molecular dipole distribution and adjusts the atomic charges, bonded, and Lennard-Jones interaction parameters through a stochastic optimization procedure. In the case of a large QM region ($\langle N\rangle\approx 440$), where the surface-to-volume ratio is small, the DR reservoir induces, as expected, Grand Canonical statistics for the quantum subsystem. In smaller subsystems ($\langle N\rangle\approx 190$), where the surface-to-volume condition is deliberately less favorable, the same reservoir shows substantially improved molecular consistency with the QM region relative to the non-renormalized flexible TIP3P model. These results show that quantum information at molecular dipole level is crucial for the microscopic physics of liquid water. When this concept is transferred into a classical reservoir, it can be used to extend the reliable regime of adaptive open-QM/MM water simulations even beyond the physically dictated Grand Canonical conditions. \end{abstract

articles.title: Potential for helicity-mediated reverse intersystem crossing in boron--nitrogen-substituted polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons with inverted singlet-triplet gaps
articles.abstract: The prospect of exothermic reverse intersystem crossing (rISC) in organic chromophores with inverted singlet-triplet (INVEST) excited states has stimulated considerable interest in next-generation emitters. However, realizing efficient spin conversion remains challenging because energetic inversion does not necessarily imply the appreciable spin-orbit coupling (SOC) required for rISC. Here, we investigate direct ${\rm S}_1-{\rm T}_1$ SOC in 85 INVEST candidates comprising 32 azaphenalenes, 7 non-alternant hydrocarbons, and 46 boron-nitrogen-substituted polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (BNPAHs), all previously predicted to exhibit negative singlet-triplet gaps using a correlated wavefunction method at reliably optimized molecular geometries. While the azaphenalenes and non-alternant hydrocarbons exhibit negligible direct SOC, 28 of the 46 BNPAHs display finite coupling. Analysis of molecular geometries and natural transition orbitals suggests that SOC variations depend on molecular topology, orbital orientation, and electronic-state symmetry rather than nonplanarity or excited-state character alone. We estimate direct-rISC rates with a Marcus model, identifying selected BNPAHs with rates approaching $10^7\,{\rm s}^{-1}$.

articles.title: Quantum-logic detection of rotationally inelastic collisions of single molecules
articles.abstract: Collisions between molecules govern chemical reactions and energy transfer across a range of different environments from interstellar space to the Earth's atmosphere. Despite their fundamental importance, molecular collisions have traditionally been studied through ensemble-averaged experiments which obscure the dynamics of individual scattering events on the quantum level. Probing single molecular collisions with quantum-state resolution has thus far remained a major experimental challenge. Here, we demonstrate a method for detecting individual rotationally inelastic collisions of single molecular ions with neutral atoms using quantum-logic techniques. We prepare individual trapped N$_2^+$ ions in their rotational ground state, subject them to a beam of helium atoms and detect isolated collision events through their effects on the motion of the trapped ions. Quantum-logic-spectroscopic measurements reveal changes of the molecular state upon collision enabling the determination of the probability of rotationally inelastic scattering. The experiments are analysed by comparison with quantum and classical scattering calculations yielding detailed insights into the underlying collision dynamics. By combining single-collision detection with non-destructive readout of the molecular quantum state, our approach establishes a new experimental framework for investigating molecular scattering beyond conventional ensemble measurements. It opens a route towards investigating state-to-state scattering in individual molecules and exploring molecular interactions at the level of single quantum-state resolved events.

articles.title: TGen-SQD: Physics-Informed Transferable Configuration Generator for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization
articles.abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) avoids iterative variational circuit optimization, but its accuracy and cost depend on selecting a compact determinant subspace that captures the ground state. Existing machine-learning selectors use task-specific physical cues and typically retrain for each Hamiltonian. We introduce TGen-SQD, a physics-informed generator jointly trained across multiple Hamiltonians. It learns from configuration-interaction-weighted data and uses orbital- and system-level descriptors to guide generation. After training, its weights remain frozen for inference on seen and zero-shot geometries. On a 20-qubit H10 chain, TGen-SQD achieves mean energy errors of 40.18 +/- 1.52 and 43.97 +/- 1.20 mHa on seen and unseen geometries, respectively, 12.7% and 11.7% lower than the state-of-the-art PIGen-SQD baseline under matched shot and proposal budgets.

articles.title: The infrared vacuum reduces the laser energy needed to break molecular bonds of simple molecules
articles.abstract: Vibrational strong coupling within a few molecules has recently been demonstrated in infrared nanocavities at room temperature, opening new alternatives to explore chemical reactions assisted by the confined electromagnetic vacuum. However, the intrinsic mechanisms of how the quantized electromagnetic mode modifies reactivity are not fully understood. We study infrared photodissociation of a single molecule strongly coupled to a resonant infrared nanocavity mode. The coupled system is driven by a monochromatic infrared laser that vibrationally excites the molecule directly or injects photons into the nanocavity field. We compare the intracavity dynamics of CO2 and H2O molecules and demonstrate that the driving energy required for dissociation is up to three orders of magnitude lower inside the cavity by injecting photons into the nanocavity than by driving the molecule directly. We show that photodissociation enhancements are due to the interplay between nuclear anharmonicity, stronglight-mattercoupling, and vacuum field polarisation according to the dipolar nature of the molecular bond. Our results provide the conceptual and numerical tools for understanding how to control chemical processes and to design nanophotonics experiments at the few-molecule level within a cavity quantum electrodynamics perspective.

articles.title: A Hierarchical Harmonic-to-Anharmonic Framework for ab initio Screening and Mechanistic Analysis of Negative Thermal Expansion in ZrV2O7
articles.abstract: Negative thermal expansion (NTE) in framework materials arises from complex lattice dynamics that are challenging to capture using conventional theoretical approaches. Here, we establish a hierarchical computational strategy for investigating NTE in ZrV2O7, integrating the quasiharmonic approximation (QHA), temperature-dependent effective potentials (TDEP), and machine-learning-accelerated ab initio molecular dynamics (ML-MD). Quasi-harmonic lattice-dynamical calculations identify low-frequency phonon modes with negative Grüneisen parameters as inexpensive screening descriptors, while TDEP incorporates finite-temperature anharmonicity and ML-MD further reveals temperature-dependent structural distortions that drive the lattice contraction. The observations are further corroborated with X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements. The concurrent increase in transverse displacement (uT) provides microscopic evidence for a quasi-rigid-unit-mode (QRUM) mechanism underlying the NTE behaviour at elevated temperatures. This is consistent with previous reports on other framework materials, including ZrW2O7, where collective polyhedral rotations and transverse atomic motions have been linked to NTE. Overall, our results demonstrate how relatively inexpensive lattice-dynamical descriptors can identify potential NTE materials, while higher-level anharmonic simulations can then resolve the underlying structural mechanisms at the atomic scale.

articles.title: A New High $γ$-$γ'$ Fraction Polycrystalline Co/Ni Superalloy
articles.abstract: An ingot-processable Co/Ni-based $γ/γ'$ superalloy has been developed for wrought parts in aircraft engines. An 8.5 kg VIM ingot was homogenised and hot rolled to a true strain of 1. A heat treatment was then developed to produce 50% $γ'$ and a grain size of 142 $μ$m. High-temperature tensile testing showed yield strengths of 820 MPa at 700 $^\circ$C, 785 MPa at 800 $^\circ$C and 783 MPa at 850 $^\circ$C. Creep tests at 750 $^\circ$C/600 MPa and 800 $^\circ$C/300 MPa demonstrated reduced minimum creep rates and extended rupture lives relative to current wrought Ni-base alloys. Oxidation at 800 $^\circ$C for 100 h formed a 1 $μ$m dual chromia/alumina scale with minimal subsurface degradation. Long-term exposure at 800 $^\circ$C for 8000 h showed limited $γ'$ coarsening and no deleterious intermetallic or grain boundary phases. The alloy therefore offers a promising balance of processability, strength and oxidation resistance for high-temperature static and rotating components.or grain boundary phases. The alloy therefore offers a promising balance of processability, strength and oxidation resistance for high-temperature static and rotating components.

articles.title: Anisotropy driven critical phenomena in a van der Waals ferromagnet
articles.abstract: We report a detailed investigation into the field-dependent critical behavior of the van der Waals ferromagnet $\mathrm{Fe_3GeTe_2}$ to elucidate how applied magnetic fields ($B$), strong magnetocrystalline anisotropy, and emerging other energy scales modulate its critical behavior. Utilizing the recently developed method, viz., the average of normalized slope (ANS), for analysis of critical behavior, we evaluate the critical exponents ($β$, $γ$, and $δ$) across distinct field windows up to $\rm{7\,T}$. For $B$ applied along the crystal's easy axis ($B\parallel c$), the system exhibits long-range interactions dominated by competing double-exchange and itinerant Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) mechanisms, which is systematically suppressed with increasing $B$ to converge toward the long-range 3D Ising universality class ($β\sim0.330$, $γ\sim1.00$). Conversely, under an in-plane hard-axis configuration ($B\perp c$), the critical behavior study exhibits a sub-unity regime ($γ<1$) across the measured range of $B$. This behavior is attributed to the intense competitive interplay between the external Zeeman energy and strong out-of-plane magnetocrystalline anisotropy. Our findings demonstrate that critical behavior in nontrivial van der Waals magnets is fundamentally modulated by the orientation of $B$ and the strength of magnetocrystalline anisotropy, demonstrating the necessity of $B$-dependent critical behavior investigation over conventional frameworks.

articles.title: Are Scaling Laws of Universal MLIPs Universal?
articles.abstract: Neural scaling laws enable the prediction of returns from larger training datasets, but machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) datasets are heterogeneous and expensive to generate, and equal numbers of structures need not contain equal amounts of useful information. We study data scaling under fixed model configurations for M3GNet, MACE, and PET trained on subsets of a combined MatPES-MP-ALOE training pool. Across training structure subsets from 10,000 to 640,000, together with the full 1.16-million-structure training set, we compare uniform random sampling, three chemistry- and structure-informed stratification policies, iterative DIRECT, and furthest-point sampling using embeddings from three pretrained MLIPs. Models are evaluated using cohesive-energy, force, stress, and aggregate losses on both a held-out test set from the parent distribution and the distribution shifted MP-r$^2$SCAN test set. We observe power-law scaling improvements with increasing data, but the fitted scaling exponent, apparent error floor, and relative sample efficiency depend on the model architecture, target quantity, data sampling policy, and test set distribution. Sampling-policy rankings can reverse across test distributions: chemical stratification can improve cross-dataset performance while degrading in-distribution performance, whereas the embedding-space diversity policies frequently under-perform random sampling. Relative loss is strongly associated with test-to-train chemical-space divergence. These results show that structure count is a necessary but insufficient scaling variable for MLIPs. For training MLIPs, the return on additional first-principles calculations depends not only on how many additional structures are included, but also on how their chemical and configurational content aligns with the model's intended use.

articles.title: Atomistic simulations of electrochemical systems with machine learning potentials
articles.abstract: Modern machine learning potentials (MLPs) enable large-scale atomistic simulations at unprecedented accuracy. The incorporation of explicit physical interactions such as long-range electrostatics has continuously broadened their applicability to increasingly complex systems in chemistry and materials science. Extending MLPs to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis, however, is still challenging as it requires the consideration of electrode potentials and electric fields in the atomic interactions. Such approaches have emerged only recently, and although the field is evolving rapidly, further conceptual advances are still needed for carrying out reliable simulations at finite temperature under applied potential. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview about recent progress in the atomistic simulation of electrified interfaces using MLPs. Current developments fall into three different categories. The first comprises linear response models that describe polarisation, polarisability, and Born effective charges, extending conventional MLPs to finite electric fields. The second includes methods that directly learn a field-dependent potential energy surface. The third consists of a series of hybrid approaches combining classical models with machine learning. Although still under active development, these methods represent a major step toward more realistic simulations approaching the quality of electronic structure calculations. Finally, we discuss open challenges and possible future directions for advancing MLP-based simulations aiming for a bottom-up understanding of atomistic processes at electrified interfaces.

articles.title: Brute-force molecular dynamics simulation of aging in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$
articles.abstract: Chalcogenide alloys such as the prototypical Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ compound are used in phase change electronic memories due to their ability to undergo a fast and reversible transition between the amorphous and crystalline phases upon heating. The amorphous phase is subject to aging that leads to an increase in the electrical resistance, which is detrimental to the operation of the devices. Using a machine learning interatomic potential, we have investigated the structural relaxations responsible for aging in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ in molecular dynamics simulations at temperatures slightly below the glass transition. The aging simulation, lasting about 100 ns, follows an equilibration of 24 ns at 400 K. During aging we observed an enhancement of the Peierls distortion in axial bonds which is a typical feature of these alloys that we relate to the widening of the electronic band gap computed within Density Functional Theory in smaller aged amorphous models. We also observed a marked reduction of the atomic mobility with an increase of the bond lifetimes during aging. However, we do not see a reduction in homopolar bonds, which are expected to be absent in the ideal aged glass and which should be removed on a much longer time scale.

articles.title: Cation-intermixing driven evolution from a narrow avoided crossing to an enlarged inverted gap in Ge$_2$Bi$_2$Te$_5$
articles.abstract: Combining the building blocks and structural motifs of the topological insulator Bi$_2$Te$_3$ and the ferroelectric Rashba semiconductor GeTe, we synthesized and comprehensively characterized the resulting Ge$_2$Bi$_2$Te$_5$ compound, which exhibits pronounced cation intermixing. Using momentum-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and ab initio calculations, we demonstrate how cation intermixing drives the evolution of its electronic structure from a narrow avoided crossing to a substantially enlarged inverted band gap.
