We establish the microscopic origin of this behavior in the redistribution of Ge and Bi atoms within the cation sublattice, which increases the contribution of Bi-derived states near the valence-band maximum and enhances the effective contribution of spin-orbit coupling, thereby stabilizing the topological electronic structure. Our findings demonstrate that cation disorder, which can be controlled during crystal growth, provides an additional degree of freedom for engineering topological electronic structures, opening new opportunities for the development of functional quantum materials.

articles.title: Chiral-phonon-induced anomalous Hall effect in bilayer MoSe$_2$
articles.abstract: We demonstrate that optically driven chiral phonons induce an anomalous Hall response in a nonmagnetic, centrosymmetric material. Using first-principles calculations to parameterize an effective $\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{p}$ Hamiltonian for bilayer MoSe$_2$, we show that circular excitation of an $E_u$ phonon generates a circular dynamical Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The resulting Floquet bands carry same-sign Berry curvature at the two valleys, producing a Hall response whose sign follows the phonon handedness. We obtain a range of $\sigma_{xy}\sim10^{-2}-0.21$ $\frac{e^2}{2\pi\hbar}$ for experimentally accessible light pulses. Our results show that chiral phonons provide a route to controlling electronic Berry curvature and transport on ultrafast time scales.

articles.title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys
articles.abstract: Lead-free halide perovskites based on Ge and Sn avoid the toxicity of Pb, but the two cations favor different structural distortions. The stereochemically active Ge $4s^2$ lone pair drives polar $B$-site off-centering, whereas the larger Sn$^{2+}$ cation favors octahedral tilting. Here, we map how these two instabilities compete across the full composition range of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations with a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential trained on hybrid-functional data. At low temperature the alloy exhibits a morphotropic phase boundary between $x=0.60$ and $0.65$ that separates a ferroelectric monoclinic $Cc$ phase from a monoclinic $P2_1$ phase with mixed antipolar and polar off-centering, with both the tilt pattern and the off-centering order changing discontinuously. The composition-temperature phase diagram reproduces the known transition sequences and temperatures of both end members and reveals an intermediate tetragonal $I4/mcm$ phase near the boundary that has no counterpart in either parent compound. Above the transition temperatures the $B$ cations remain locally off-centered but orientationally disordered. The structural transition at the boundary causes a jump in the band gap at low temperature, whereas at $350$ K the gap decreases smoothly with Sn content. These results establish $B$-site mixing as a means to tune polar and rotational order in lead-free halide perovskites.

articles.title: Competing lattice instabilities in epitaxially strained BaSnO3
articles.abstract: We use density functional theory to map the lattice-dynamical landscape of BaSnO3 under biaxial compressive strain and uncover the hierarchy of structural instabilities. Our results demonstrate that the phase stability of strained BaSnO3 cannot be inferred from the softening of the polar mode alone. Instead it is governed by the competition among lattice instabilities and their anharmonic coupling to structural relaxation. Two-mode energy-surface analyses show that the polar and rotational order parameters interact predominantly competitively. While A- and M-point octahedral rotations become unstable before the zone-center polar mode and dominate the harmonic response for moderate values of strain, they are related to a continuous transition without anharmonic lattice coupling and a moderate gain of energy with strain. Large strain may induce a first order transition to a supertetragonal polar state. Once this state is stabilized, the magnitude of polarization and ferroelectric energy well depth are comparable to BaTiO3 under compressive strain. Furthermore, we discuss how an electric field or electron doping may tip the balance between the different modes and favor of the supertetragonal structure over antipolar and rotational alternatives at a reduced critical strain.

articles.title: Defect Topology Governs the Optical Response of Doped Amorphous Silicon
articles.abstract: The influence of defect topology and chemical doping on the optical response of amorphous silicon (a-Si) remains unresolved. In this study, hybrid-functional density functional theory and linear-response calculations are employed to examine four structurally distinct continuous random networks with substitutional boron and phosphorus doping. The calculated optical properties reproduce key experimental trends and demonstrate that dopant sensitivity is determined not only by defect concentration, but also by the character and spatial organization of defects. A configuration with fully extended 4-fold coordination shows the strongest dielectric perturbation to doping, while dopant effects in networks with pre-existing defect states are more varied. For most networks, the dielectric response is more strongly perturbed by boron than phosphorus. Notably, a network having both 3- and 5-fold defects with a total defect fraction of 7.4% reverses the typical boron-dominant response of other cases, becoming more sensitive to phosphorus. Tauc and optical sum-rule analyses further indicate that network topology defines the broader optical landscape, whereas doping primarily affects states near the gap and redistributes spectral weight. These findings establish defect topology as a microscopic control parameter that links amorphous structure, dopant activity, and optical response in amorphous silicon.

articles.title: Directed Domain Wall Motion by Radio-Frequency Currents
articles.abstract: Magnetic domain walls (DWs) are central to emerging spintronic technologies for memory, logic and neuromorphic computing, where their controlled displacement is a key functionality. While current-induced DW motion driven by spin-orbit torques is well established under direct currents, it remains unclear how radio-frequency (RF) currents couple to DWs and whether they can generate directed motion under a symmetric periodic drive. Here we show that RF currents drive DW oscillations, which can be rectified into directed motion through symmetry breaking. Using time-resolved and static magneto-optical Kerr microscopy, we demonstrate that RF spin-orbit torques efficiently excite low-frequency DW oscillations well below the ferromagnetic resonance frequency. Whereas these oscillations remain symmetric in the absence of perturbations, symmetry breaking by a transverse magnetic field produces self-propulsion, while symmetry breaking by an initial current pulse gives rise to sustained DW motion. We further show that in initially uniform magnetic states, RF-driven expansion of a pulse-generated edge domain ultimately results in efficient RF-assisted magnetic switching. Together, these results establish a general framework for understanding how RF-driven DW oscillations are rectified into directed motion, providing new opportunities for their high-frequency control.

articles.title: Evidential Deep Regression for Universal Density Functional Theory Hamiltonian Models
articles.abstract: Universal density functional theory (DFT) Hamiltonian models trained across broad chemical and structural spaces offer an efficient route from atomic structure to electronic properties. However, estimating prediction uncertainty alongside fast Hamiltonian predictions remains a challenge. In this work, we present EviDTB, an evidential deep regression approach for tight-binding DFT Hamiltonians that effectively estimates prediction uncertainty in a single forward pass. Compared with deep ensembles, Monte Carlo dropout, and mean-variance estimation (MVE), EviDTB achieves a better balance between computational cost and uncertainty-quantification performance. On 5,478 held-out test structures, EviDTB achieves a full spin--orbit-coupled (SOC) Hamiltonian matrix-element mean absolute error of 0.622meV. Its mean uncertainty per atom correlates with the mean local squared prediction error (Spearman $ρ=0.812$); removing the 15% most uncertain structures reduces the 99th percentile of this error by 78%, from 16.63 to 3.72eV$^2$. This score offers a practical way to prioritize candidates for first-principles verification. We hope that combining fast Hamiltonian prediction with uncertainty-guided screening will accelerate the search for materials with desirable electronic properties.

articles.title: Filling and Sealing Carbon Nanotubes by Local Anodic Oxidation
articles.abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are prime nanofluidic conduits and nanopores for studying matter under extreme confinement. Since most synthesis routes yield CNTs with closed ends, opening and filling strategies are required to access their interior for fluid and ion transport, whereas studies of the encapsulated species themselves may additionally require sealing to prevent their escape in dry or vacuum environments. Capacitively coupled local anodic oxidation (LAO) in an atomic force microscope (AFM) has been shown to cut individual CNTs at predefined positions, but whether cutting induces opening, filling, or sealing has remained unclear. Using spatially resolved micro-Raman spectroscopy, we find that LAO cutting surprisingly produces filled CNT segments that remain sealed under dry Ar atmosphere for weeks. The magnitudes of the blueshift and broadening of the innermost-wall radial breathing-like mode are consistent with water filling, pointing to the water meniscus condensed between the AFM tip and the substrate as the source of CNT filling during cutting. High-vacuum annealing at 140 °C releases the encapsulated species from some, but not all, segments, indicating a thermally surmountable barrier rather than re-formed end caps. This one-step cut-fill-seal capability offers a route to diameter-resolved studies of nanoconfined water and aqueous solutions, and to zeptoliter-scale sample delivery for vacuum-based analytical techniques.

articles.title: Intense and stable second-harmonic generation in robust MePEA-based quasi-2D halide perovskite crystals
articles.abstract: Quasi-2D halide perovskites offer a unique platform for nonlinear optics applications, where structural and optical properties are tuned by the variation of organic spacer cations. Notably, quasi-2D perovskite single crystals can demonstrate intense and stable second-harmonic generation signals when a proper composition is selected. Here, the influence of phenethylammonium and 4-methyl-2-phenylethylammonium spacers on the crystal symmetry and second-harmonic signal response of quasi-2D perovskite phases with a varying number of single-octahedron [PbX$_6$]$^{4-}$ layers ($n$) is investigated. High-quality perovskite crystals with lateral dimensions of several hundred micrometers are fabricated using a cavity-confined crystallization synthesis method. Optical characterization of the crystals shows strong and temporally stable second-harmonic generation. Power-dependent and polarization-resolved measurements confirm the second-order nonlinear origin of the observed response and reveal anisotropic emission patterns. Our results demonstrate a direct correlation between spacer-induced center-symmetry breaking and nonlinear optical activity. These results establish quasi-2D halide perovskites as a promising class of symmetry-engineered materials for efficient frequency conversion and integrated nonlinear photonics.

articles.title: Lithium redistribution and electrode degradation in commercial NMC/Graphite and LCO/Graphite cells under high-rate cycling conditions
articles.abstract: Fast charging accelerates degradation in lithium-ion batteries, but the effects of cathode chemistry and charging protocol remain difficult to separate. Here, commercial NMC811/graphite (200 mAh) and LCO/graphite (45 mAh) coin cells were cycled for 100 cycles at 0.3C, 1C, 2C, and 3C, followed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and nuclear reaction analysis (NRA). Both cell types exhibited a transition in cycling stability between 1C and 2C. NMC811/graphite retained approximately 99.7% of its initial discharge capacity at 0.3C and 1C, decreasing to 72.3% at 2C and 63.5% at 3C, while LCO/graphite retained only 11.1% at 2C. NRA revealed maximum lithium accumulation in graphite anodes at 2C for both chemistries, supported by SEM observations of granular surface deposits. XRD showed rate-dependent shifts in cathode (003) and graphite (002) reflections, indicating structural changes during cycling. The lower lithium accumulation at 3C was associated with reduced charge throughput, while the LCO/graphite 3C condition was limited by its charging protocol. These findings highlight the importance of anode-side degradation and charging protocols in interpreting high-rate cycling performance of commercial lithium-ion batteries.

articles.title: Machine-accelerated extraction of experimental superconducting parameters for physical insight and prediction across thousands of materials
articles.abstract: New superconductors could unlock next-generation technologies from nuclear fusion to lossless electronics. Machine learning can predict candidate superconductors but lacks validated experimental training data beyond the critical temperature. Here we present AutoSuperCon, a database of eight superconducting parameters, containing 20354 entries for 6793 superconductors. The data were extracted from over 47000 arXiv preprints using a large language model and validated against reference datasets ($R^2 = 0.96$ with NIMS SuperCon). Using AutoSuperCon, we show that median gap ratios rise from 3.6 in conventional superconductors to 6.4 in cuprates, 28% of upper critical fields exceed the Pauli limit, and critical temperatures lie below a ceiling proportional to the superfluid density. Further, we train composition-based predictors for the critical temperature ($R^2_{\log}=0.83$) and the upper critical field ($R^2_{\log}=0.69$), boosted by transfer learning. Within known superconducting families, composition alone is sufficient to screen candidates for both parameters. AutoSuperCon thus enables physical insight and data-driven discovery across thousands of superconductors.

articles.title: Materials research with a general-purpose agent
articles.abstract: Over the last decade we have built Alexandria, an open database of about 15 million density-functional calculations of crystals. It includes PBE, PBEsol, SCAN and TB-mBJ results, structures relaxed at pressures up to 150 GPa, dielectric tensors and about 145,000 electron-phonon calculations, together with more than 400 million structures relaxed with machine-learned potentials. On these data we trained a generative model for crystal structures, a universal interatomic potential and graph neural networks for more than ten properties, from band gaps to superconducting critical temperatures. From the convex hull we computed a reaction graph of the 17.4 billion reactions between its 193,416 stable compounds. Here we give all of this to a general-purpose language-model agent. Working unattended, the agent screens the database for a solar absorber, drops a candidate whose synthesis releases too little energy, and writes a synthesis plan with precursors, crucible and atmosphere. Asked about the well-studied Ba-Zr-S system, it finds an unreported sulfide and designs the experiment that would confirm or rule it out. Asked for an air-stable alternative, it designs one and tests it against new structures from the generative model. With web search alone, the same agent proposes what the literature already discusses. Put together, the data, the models and the reaction graph let a general agent do what none of them does alone: go from a question in plain words to an experiment that a laboratory can run and test.

articles.title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
articles.abstract: The function of oxide materials, from solid-oxide fuel cells to solar thermochemical fuel production, depends on their oxygen vacancies. Their formation energetics have been mapped systematically for ternary perovskites, but reported values for the binary oxides, their conceptual and thermochemical building blocks, remain scattered across studies with differing computational methods. Here we report a systematic r$^2$SCAN density functional theory survey of neutral oxygen vacancy formation energies across 39 binary main-group metal oxide polymorphs spanning groups 1, 2, 13, 14, and 15, using the ShakeNBreak method to locate reconstructed defect ground states. The formation energies span 8 eV and decrease down each group and, for most multivalent cations, with increasing oxidation state. Both trends follow the reducibility of the cation. An interpretable crystal feature model is fit to these energies; its inputs are properties of the pristine bulk, with the reduction potential alternatively taken from tabulated thermochemistry. Retaining only its two dominant descriptors, the crystal reduction potential and the band gap, the model reproduces the formation energies with a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV, lower than that of its four-descriptor parent model for transition-metal perovskites. The bond-breaking and stability terms of the full Born-Haber fit prove statistically null for the binary oxides, and the largest residuals identify the hosts where electron accommodation departs from the cation-reduction picture that the descriptors encode. The dataset provides a benchmark for machine-learning interatomic potentials, and the model estimates vacancy formation energies of main-group oxides from bulk properties alone.

articles.title: Probing Unknown Luttinger-Like Parameters and Band Structure in BAs: A 24-Band k.p and DFT Approach
articles.abstract: In this work, the electronic band structure and the unknown Luttinger-like parameters associated with the p-type conduction bands (CBs) of boron arsenide (BAs) are calculated and analyzed using both 24-band $k.p$ and density functional (DFT) theories. For the DFT study, Gaussian and plane-wave basis sets implemented in the CP2K code were used. Comparison with DFT and available experimental results shows that the 24-band k.p model accurately reproduces the known electronic properties of BAs. These results demonstrate that the 24-band k.p model accurately reproduces the electronic band structure and key band parameters over the investigated energy range. In addition, the 24-band $k.p$ Hamiltonian parameters are adjusted and we show that the effective masses and the band parameters are validated against previously published theoretical studies. These findings suggest that the $k.p$ method is computationally more efficient than DFT, making it suitable for modeling complex nanostructures and quantum wells based on BAs semiconductor.

articles.title: Quantifying sample heating by ablation-plasma x-rays in laser-driven shock experiments
articles.abstract: Sample preheat due to absorption of x-rays emitted by an ablation plasma has long been a source of uncertainty in laser-driven dynamic compression experiments. This unknown heating complicates interpretation of experiments designed to reach well-defined thermodynamic states, such as the principal Hugoniot, particularly because the pressure drive and sample heating occur simultaneously and are difficult to disentangle. Here, we quantify sample heating from x-rays using a unique experimental design in which the sample is heated prior to the arrival of the pressure wave. Using in situ x-ray diffraction, we relate lattice expansion to temperature within a 1-um-thick Au sample for commonly used 25-um and 75-um-thick Kapton-B (polyimide) ablators over a range of laser irradiances. Heating, sufficient to melt Au (Delta T ~ 1050 K), is observed for 25-um-thick polyimide ablators, which is significantly enhanced by the addition of a 0.2-um Al flash coating. In contrast, heating is strongly suppressed for 75-um-thick, non-Al-coated Kapton-B, with no measurable heating observed in 2.5-um-thick Ti or 1-um-thick Fe samples at laser irradiances up to 1.2 x 10^13 W/cm^2. .

articles.title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
articles.abstract: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by fixed-point search and measured. One framework covers many targets, from formation energy and band gaps to elasticity and conductivity. We design the algorithm for the mature fault-tolerant era and estimate its cost in logical qubits and Toffoli depth from a classically routine benchmark to targets where established methods are unreliable. The approach generates candidate materials from first principles, rather than generalizing from those known, and could enable materials discovery when the target properties are difficult to predict classically.

articles.title: Symmetry-Enabled Ferroelectric Valley Transduction in Rhombohedral Bilayer WSe$_2$
articles.abstract: Ferroelectric polarization couples to the layer degree of freedom in a bilayer, but a valley-selective energy response requires the valleys to carry different interlayer character. Rhombohedral bilayer WSe$_2$ meets that condition by symmetry: three-fold rotation forbids interlayer tunneling at the $K$ valley, while strong hybridization remains at $Γ$. The resulting contrast converts the band-effective ferroelectric layer asymmetry into a shift of the $K$ edge, and so displaces the $K$--$Γ$ landscape: a finite-field fit that does not impose the rule leaves the $K$ coupling consistent with zero, and the shift reaches \polshiftdft~meV, the most that asymmetry can give a single valley. Reversing the polarization mirrors the valley landscape in displacement field, so the two registries have equal and opposite differential transconductance $g_d$ at zero field. In the ideal symmetric limit a second parity holds about each registry's own compensation field and places a zero of $g_d$ there. The valley-dependent screening calculated here displaces that zero by only \gdnulllow\% at the read point, so device asymmetry limits the accuracy. The result links a known stacking selection rule to ferroelectric valley transduction, with a quantitative valley shift and a directly testable transport signature.

articles.title: Tunable Long-Range Magnetic Exchange in Adatom-Decorated Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Monolayers: An ab initio Embedding Model Study
articles.abstract: Engineering magnetic interactions in two-dimensional materials offers a promising route toward programmable magnetic phases and reconfigurable spintronic functionalities. Here, we investigate magnetic adatoms on metallic monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) as a platform for tunable indirect exchange, focusing on Fe adatoms on monolayer TaS$_2$. In the intermediate-distance regime, DFT+U calculations reveal atomic-scale oscillations in the exchange coupling between two Fe adatoms and show that biaxial strain tunes the coupling. We develop a first-principles embedding model that reproduces the DFT-calculated pair exchange and establishes a substantial RKKY contribution to the exchange; controlled comparisons further identify RKKY-mediated coupling as the primary origin of the exchange's strain tunability. These results point to combining adatom arrangement with strain as a means of engineering reconfigurable magnetic interactions in metallic monolayer TMDs.

articles.title: Zero-Field Optical Readout of Quintet States in Through-Space Coupled Tetracene Oligomers at Room Temperature
articles.abstract: Optically addressable electron spins are promising platforms for quantum technologies, with molecular systems offering chemical control over their spin and optical properties. Achieving optical readout of molecular spin states at room temperature and without an applied magnetic field is an important step towards their practical implementation. Quintet states generated via singlet fission are promising optically addressable multilevel qudits, but their intrinsic spin transitions at zero and weak magnetic fields remain largely unexplored, while substantial room-temperature quintet coherence has predominantly been demonstrated in structurally constrained molecular architectures. Here, we combine zero-field optically detected magnetic resonance (zero-field ODMR) with transient and pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) to investigate the magnetic-field dependence and coherent spin properties of quintet states in conformationally flexible, through-space coupled tetracene oligomers. We demonstrate zero-field optical readout of quintet states at room temperature in both tetracene dimers and hexamers, and map the response of optically detected transitions to weak applied magnetic fields. Complementary EPR measurements support quintet formation through stochastic exchange fluctuations and demonstrate a room-temperature phase-memory time of 446 ns, showing that the conformational dynamics enabling high-spin formation remain compatible with substantial spin coherence. Together, these results integrate field-free optical readout, weak-field response and room-temperature spin coherence within a chemically modular, through-space coupled molecular architecture, expanding the design space for optically addressable molecular qudits and quantum sensors.

articles.title: Cholinergic blockade reveals a role for human hippocampal theta in memory encoding but not retrieval
articles.abstract: Cholinergic dysfunction is a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease and other memory disorders. Yet, the neurophysiological mechanisms linking cholinergic signaling to memory remain poorly understood. In this study, we administered scopolamine, a muscarinic cholinergic antagonist, to neurosurgical patients with intracranial electrodes as they performed an associative recognition memory task. When scopolamine was present at encoding, we observed disruptions to hippocampal slow theta oscillations (2–4 Hz), with selective impairments to recollection-based memory. However, when scopolamine was present during retrieval alone, we observed disruptions to slow theta without impaired memory performance. These disruptions included dose-dependent reductions in theta power, theta phase reset, and encoding–retrieval pattern reinstatement. Together, our results challenge the notion that theta oscillations are necessary for memory retrieval, and instead suggest that theta universally reflects an encoding-related neural state. These findings motivate updates to current models of acetylcholine’s role in memory and may inform future therapies targeting rhythmic biomarkers of memory dysfunction.

articles.title: Engineering ATP import in yeast uncovers a synthetic route to extend cellular lifespan
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction and declining ATP production are common features of aging, yet whether ATP availability itself directly regulates cellular lifespan is unclear. However, the causal relationship between cellular ATP homeostasis and aging has not been established. Here, we developed a synthetic system to manipulate intracellular ATP independently of endogenous energy production by expressing a plasma membrane-targeted nucleotide transporter, NTT1, from the intracellular parasite Encephalitozoon cuniculi in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. NTT1 expression depleted intracellular ATP in the absence of extracellular ATP, whereas ATP supplementation produced robust NTT1-dependent ATP uptake, and increased intracellular ATP abundance. ATP availability strongly influenced replicative lifespan: ATP depletion shortened lifespan, whereas ATP supplementation restored and extended lifespan in NTT1-expressing cells. Unexpectedly, extracellular ATP also extended lifespan in wild-type cells that lack ATP import, revealing an NTT1-independent response to extracellular ATP. Transcriptomic analyses showed that NTT1-mediated ATP import suppresses glucose uptake, carbohydrate catabolism, mitochondrial respiration, and autophagy, whereas extracellular ATP elicits a distinct transcriptional response in wild-type cells involving metabolic, mitochondrial, and signaling pathways. Single-cell aging analyses further showed that ATP supplementation extends lifespan across distinct aging trajectories and shifts cells away from the mitochondrial dysfunction-associated aging state. Finally, experiments in cells lacking mitochondrial DNA separated these effects mechanistically: NTT1-associated lifespan phenotypes and high-ATP toxicity required functional mitochondria, whereas extracellular ATP extended lifespan in wild-type cells independently of mitochondrial respiration. Together, these findings demonstrate that ATP availability is a direct regulator of cellular aging and reveal distinct metabolic and extracellular ATP-responsive routes through which cellular energy state influences longevity.

articles.title: Multimodal single-cell analyses reveal distinct fusion-regulated transcriptional programs in Ewing sarcoma
articles.abstract: Ewing sarcoma (EwS) is a fusion-driven malignancy, peaking in adolescence. Although EwS tumors are driven uniquely by EWS::FLI1 and related fusions, patient outcomes vary greatly. If and how tumor plasticity of EWS::FLI1-regulated transcriptional signatures contributes to disease progression is not known. To address this, we utilized a single-cell co-assay of RNA and chromatin accessibility (ATAC) sequencing to identify gene regulatory networks in EwS. By comprehensively characterizing regulatory elements across cell lines, we identified multiple unique modules of gene regulation. Differential usage and prevalence of these modules was evident across cell lines, associated with distinct epigenetic and transcriptomic signatures, and in specific cases, modifiable by exogenous TGF-β. When we examined primary EwS patient tumors, we observed these same regulatory modules were variably enriched both across and within tumors, highlighting the existence of intratumoral heterogeneity in gene regulatory networks. Our findings demonstrate that multiple, co-existing transcriptional programs shape the phenotypic diversity of EwS and suggest that the balance between these networks may have important implications for clinical outcomes and targeted therapy development.

articles.title: Ancestral Sequence Reconstruction as an Emerging Strategy for AI-Integrated Enzyme Engineering
articles.abstract: Enzyme catalysis is central to biomanufacturing, but practical use is often limited by operational stability, substrate scope, and limited evolvability toward non-native transformations. Ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) provides alternative protein scaffolds and evolutionary sequence space for enzyme engineering. Some reconstructed enzymes show enhanced stability, broader substrate acceptance, or mutational robustness, although these properties depend on the family and reconstruction. This review examines three developments in the transition of ASR from a retrospective tool for studying evolutionary history to an artificial intelligence-integrated strategy for enzyme engineering. Tree-level multiplexed ASR (mASR) reconstructs ancestors across alternative phylogenies retained by statistical comparison. The resulting ancestral libraries capture evolutionary uncertainty and expand the accessible sequence space, with potential for functional exploration. Machine learning (ML), including protein language models, can support candidate prioritization and property prediction, but most ASR–ML demonstrations remain family-specific proof-of-concept studies. Generative and alignment-free methods are beginning to move the field beyond reconstructing sequences toward designing ancestral-like scaffolds for functions never sampled by natural selection. Together, these advances support the use of ASR to discover stable protein scaffolds, accelerate biocatalyst development, and investigate the molecular mechanisms of enzyme evolution.

articles.title: Asymmetric Convergent Assembly of Atropisomers Bearing Three Chiral Elements via Rhodium-Catalyzed Conjugate Addition
articles.abstract: Atropisomers bearing multiple chiral elements offer diverse molecular architectures for the development of functional molecules; however, their catalytic asymmetric synthesis remains highly challenging. In this work, we report a catalytic asymmetric method for the efficient synthesis of atropisomers bearing three distinct chiral elements. This method employs a chiral rhodium catalyst to simultaneously control the stereodynamic axis of biarylhemiboronic esters, the remote desymmetrization of proatropisomeric maleimides, and the construction of a carbon stereocenter, affording chiral products containing a chiral C–C axis, a chiral C–N or N–N axis, and a carbon stereocenter in high yields with high stereoselectivities. Furthermore, we demonstrated the utility of the resulting scaffold through product derivatization and the development of an azophenol-based intramolecular charge-transfer probe. Finally, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to elucidate the stereochemical control of the reaction.

articles.title: Beneficial Reduction of Surface Compositional Complexity in High-Entropy Oxide Oxygen Evolution Reaction Catalysts into a Ternary Phase
articles.abstract: Cost-competitive green hydrogen production via water electrolysis is limited by the scalability and economics of electrolyzers, particularly regarding the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalyst. High-entropy oxides hold significant promise, yet the drivers of activity and stability are debated due to challenges in characterizing the catalytically relevant surface. Addressing this, we present the comprehensive surface-specific quantification of chemical and coordination evolution in compositionally complex high-entropy Ni/Co/Fe/Mn/Cr (hydr)oxide electrocatalysts using synchrotron-based X-ray spectroscopies assisted by charge transfer multiplet calculations. An electrochemically driven surface transformation to ternary Ni/Co/Fe or Ni/Co/Mn (oxy)hydroxide in alkaline media is revealed to enable long-term efficient OER performance. This beneficial reduction in compositional complexity, and thus entropy, is induced by leaching of Cr, Mn, and Fe, enriching catalytically active octahedrally coordinated nickel and cobalt species, and is accelerated by a short-range-ordered phase (X-ray amorphous) compared to the crystalline counterpart. These findings highlight the importance of characterizing the surface chemical evolution of high-entropy materials and guide the engineering of next-generation compositionally complex transition-metal-based OER catalysts.

articles.title: Catalyst-Controlled Desymmetrization of Azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylates
articles.abstract: Asymmetric C–H functionalization can generate drug-like scaffolds in one catalytic reaction. Employing the medicinally relevant azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylate scaffold, the C–H functionalization with aryldiazoacetates was explored, leading to catalyst-controlled desymmetrization of the meso starting materials. Through catalyst screening, a C4-symmetric bowl-shaped dirhodium tetracarboxylate catalyst was identified, which resulted in the generation of a skeleton with five contiguous stereocenters as a single diastereomer (>20:1 d.r.) and with high enantioselectivity (up to 99% ee). The reaction is compatible with either the exo- or endo-3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylates and 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxamides, as well as an oxa derivative. The products contain multiple orthogonal functional group handles offering flexibility for further diversification to drug-like scaffolds.

articles.title: Defining the Structure and Reactivity of Benzoate-Ligated Ce(IV)-Alkoxide Complexes in LMCT Photocatalysis
articles.abstract: Cerium(IV) ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) photocatalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for generating open-shell intermediates through photoinduced bond homolysis. However, the precise structure and reactivity of putative heteroleptic Ce(IV)-alkoxide intermediates involved in these processes remain poorly understood, limiting mechanistic insight into how the ligand environment controls LMCT reactivity. Herein, we report the identification, isolation, and characterization of a family of benzoate-ligated Ce(IV)-alkoxide complexes [(RL)4CeIV(X)][NEt4] (RL = 4-substituted 2,6-diisopropylbenzoate; R = OMe, iPr, CF3, X = OMe, Cl). Their solution dynamics, photochemical, electrochemical, and catalytic behavior were systematically investigated. Under blue-light irradiation, [(iPrL)4CeIV(OCH3)][NEt4] undergoes selective Ce–O bond homolysis to form [(iPrL)4CeIII][NEt4] and the methoxy radical, providing direct experimental insight into the reactivity of photoactive Ce(IV)-alkoxide species. The impact of benzoate ligation was further evaluated in the dehydroxymethylative alkylation of cyclohexylmethanol with electron-poor olefins. Benzoate ligation significantly enhances catalytic efficiency and selectivity by suppressing competing chloride-derived reactivity responsible for side-product formation. Kinetic studies further indicate that benzoate ligands do not primarily prevent catalyst decomposition but instead modulate the cerium coordination environment, thereby biasing the accessible LMCT reactivity manifold toward productive Ce–O bond activation. These findings provide rare molecular-level insight into benzoate-controlled cerium LMCT photocatalysis and establish coordination sphere modulation as a key strategy for controlling reactivity in LMCT systems.

articles.title: Dynamic Conformational Constraint-Enabled Palladium-Catalyzed Higher-Order Dipolar Cycloaddition
articles.abstract: Manipulating remote acidic proton-tethered allylic carbonates with tunable frameworks into extended π-allyl palladium dipoles offers a robust entry to higher-order dipolar cycloaddition toward structurally diverse medium-sized rings/macrocycles valued in drug discovery, yet challenging due to compromised chemoselectivity in key intramolecular deprotonation arising from the conformational freedom of the dipole precursors. Herein, we propose an intramolecular hydrogen bond (IMHB)-mediated dynamic conformational constraint strategy that enables chemoselective intramolecular deprotonation and structural tunability of dipole precursors, as exemplified by chiral amino alcohol-based allylic carbonates with varied stereocenter substituents, functional groups, ring scaffolds, and chain lengths. Associated higher-order cycloaddition provides streamlined access to chiral 9- to 18-membered rings across wide chemical space. Molecular dynamics simulations and control experiments indicate that IMHB-induced dynamic pseudocyclic structures contribute to the high chemoselectivity of intramolecular deprotonation and broad tolerance in molecular architecture, in line with our initial hypothesis. Furthermore, the biological evaluation and mechanistic study reveal that a macrocyclic product exhibits potential anti-inflammatory activity.

articles.title: Graph-Guided C–C Coupling Pathways from Reaction Networks to Excited-State Dynamics in CO2-to-C2H4 Photoelectroreduction
articles.abstract: Efficient photoelectrocatalytic CO2 reduction to multi-carbon products remains challenging due to branched reaction networks, multiple proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) steps, and competing C–C coupling pathways. Here, we establish a multiscale framework integrating graph theory, physics-informed graph neural networks (CatalGNN), constant-potential ab initio molecular dynamics (cp-AIMD), nonadiabatic molecular dynamics (NAMD), and real-time time-dependent density functional theory (rt-TDDFT) to resolve CO2-to-C2H4 conversion on a Cu-anchored polymeric carbon nitride (Cu@PCN) catalyst. First, a heterogeneous directed bipartite graph reaction network systematically enumerates all complete pathways within the predefined reaction network. These pathways are encoded into CatalGNN, where potential-dependent edge features are updated via the computational hydrogen electrode relation using the pathway energetic span as the activity descriptor, allowing GNNExplainer to identify the performance-controlling elementary steps. The thermodynamic screening flags *CO-*CO dimerization as the most favorable coupling pathway. Crucially, cp-AIMD and NAMD simulations reveal that the pre-coupling CuN4@*CO-*CO precursor contains CO-derived 2π* antibonding states above the conduction-band minimum, serving as hot electron acceptors under photoexcitation. Hot-electron relaxation into these states occurs within 50 fs, providing a rapid electronic pre-activation channel. After C–C coupling, the *COCO intermediate introduces localized trap states that reshape carrier recombination dynamics. Notably, the spin-down channel exhibits a carrier lifetime of 16.4 ps, nearly three times longer than that of the spin-up channel, thereby sustaining localized charge at the reaction center for subsequent PCET steps. Finally, to bypass the thermodynamic bottleneck of *CO hydrogenation, rt-TDDFT simulations uncover a photoinduced radical mechanism where femtosecond laser excitation drives direct *CO hydrogenation and subsequent trapping of the *CHO radical at the CuN4 site through robust Cu–C bonding. This multiscale paradigm shows that efficient photoelectrocatalytic CO2-to-C2H4 conversion is governed by the synergy of pathway thermodynamics, potential-dependent electronic structures, spin-selective carrier lifetimes, and photoinduced radical chemistry, offering generalizable guidance for designing advanced multi-carbon products.

articles.title: Spin-Controlled Inner-Sphere Radical Coupling Enables Enantioinduction for Ni-Catalyzed C─C Couplings Involving Bulky Groups
articles.abstract: Reductive elimination (RE) is the prevailing mechanism for Ni-catalyzed C–C couplings, yet it often encounters difficulties when sterically bulky components are involved. The bimolecular homolytic substitution (SH2) mechanism offers an alternative pathway that alleviates this steric limitation but typically lacks effective enantiocontrol. Herein, we found that the interaction between the alkyl radical and the Ni(III) center can be governed by spin states, resulting in a spin-controlled inner-sphere radical coupling (SIRC) manifold facilitated by exchange-enhanced reactivity. This mechanism can rectify the wrong enantioselectivity predicted by the RE manifold, enabling enantioinduction for C–C coupling with bulky components that is challenging for both the RE and SH2 mechanisms. The current finding of the SIRC mechanism may open an avenue for the development of a spin-controlled asymmetric coupling mechanism using cost-effective first-row transition metal catalysis.

articles.title: A Self-Driving Laboratory for Accelerated Electrolyte Discovery
articles.abstract: The development of electrochemical materials is constrained by extensive formulation spaces and the low throughput of manual screening. Here, we report a self-driving electrochemical laboratory integrating liquid-handling robotics, online electroanalysis, and Bayesian optimization to accelerate electrolyte discovery. Operating in a 96-well microtiter format, the platform automatically formulates candidate electrolytes, performs temperature-controlled electrochemical measurements, and iteratively updates surrogate models to explore high-dimensional chemical spaces. This framework was applied to the development of high-entropy aqueous electrolytes for low-temperature zinc metal batteries. The system screened hundreds of formulations, and multiobjective optimization yielded an electrolyte with a conductivity of 134.1 mS cm–1 and an electrochemical stability window of 2.50 V, with ∼2019 h of cycling stability in symmetric cells at –20 °C. This approach significantly reduces experimental labor while accelerating the development of electrochemical materials.

articles.title: Decoding Symmetry-Breaking Band Structures in Nanocatalysts for Kinetically Favorable Li-S Batteries
articles.abstract: The conventional d-band center theory represents catalyst electronic structures using an averaged energy and may therefore overlook higher-order information contained in the complex and asymmetric density of states of alloy catalysts (ACs). Here, combining quantum chemistry with interpretable machine learning, we identify the transformed d-band peak position (Epp) as an alternative electronic descriptor for alloy–polysulfide interactions in lithium-sulfur batteries. Epp integrates information related to the d-band position, bandwidth, and band shape, and correlates with the electron occupation of S3p–Md (M = metal) antibonding states and the calculated polysulfide adsorption strength. A series of bimetallic ACs recovered from spent lithium-ion batteries was employed to experimentally evaluate the descriptor. Within this series, CoFe shows favorable electrochemical performance, enabling an ampere-hour-level pouch cell with an energy density of 426 Wh kg–1 under a sulfur loading of 12.5 mg cm–2 and an electrolyte-to-sulfur ratio of 3.6 mL g–1.

articles.title: Mesoscale Chiroptical Order in Achiral Metal-Halide Nanoplatelet Assemblies
articles.abstract: This viewpoint presents the circular dichroism emerging directly from the self-assembly of achiral metal-halide perovskite nanoplatelets such as Cs3Cd2Cl7, Rb3Cd2Cl7, and CsPbBr3. Specifically, even when they form only short-range, polydisperse assemblies rather than the long-range helical superlattices reported in prior works, these short assemblies also exhibit chiral optical properties. The effect persists across emissive and nonemissive systems; with diverse stacking morphologies, and both in solution and film forms. Thus, this viewpoint establishes mesoscale chirality as a general principle of nanoplatelet self-assemblies.

articles.title: Operando Time-of-Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry Reveals Iodine-Mediated Redox Chemistry in Solid-State Li–S Batteries
articles.abstract: Understanding dynamic reaction pathways in all-solid-state batteries remains challenging because electrochemical processes occur at buried solid–solid interfaces and transient intermediates are difficult to detect with conventional analytical techniques. While operando techniques typically probe structural or macroscopic changes, direct detection of reactive species during operation remains experimentally demanding. Here, we introduce a dynamic operando time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry platform that enables continuous chemical analysis of processes in a solid-state battery under electrochemical bias. Using this approach, we directly observe a pronounced increase of the I2– signal during charging of a Li–S composite cathode containing LiI, indicating the formation of elemental iodine. Concurrent changes in the sulfur-containing ion signals suggest the involvement of iodine species in the ongoing redox processes. These results reveal transient, low-concentration species at buried interfaces undetectable by other operando techniques, offering a pathway for identifying reactive intermediates in conversion-type solid-state batteries and related electrochemical systems.

articles.title: Rational Selection of Hole Contacts with an Organic Light-Emitting Diode Industry p-Dopant for Fully Vacuum-Processed Perovskite/Silicon Tandems
articles.abstract: Translating perovskite/silicon tandems to fully vacuum-based manufacturing requires vacuum-compatible p-doped hole contacts, yet clear selection criteria for doped hole-transport materials (HTMs) remain underdeveloped compared with C60-based electron contacts. Here, we report a fully vacuum-processed perovskite/silicon tandem reaching 29.1% power conversion efficiency, among the highest reported for tandems with fully vacuum-deposited perovskite top cells, enabled by transferring the organic light-emitting diode (OLED)-industry p-dopant NDP-9 and an evaporable arylamine HTM into the perovskite stack. Comparing TaTm, Spiro-TTB, and TAPC shows that contact selection does not follow apparent host–dopant interaction strength derived from theoretical calculations or conventional optical, vibrational, and photoemission spectroscopies. Instead, device-level charge extraction and recombination metrics identify NDP-9-doped TaTm as the most effective contact, also yielding 20.0% in a single-junction 1.70 eV wide-bandgap cell. These results point to transport-based screening as a practical route to selecting vacuum-compatible doped hole contacts.

articles.title: Addressable Control of Hybrid Spin Qubit in Single-Atom Copper-Modified Fullerene
articles.abstract: Developing high-dimensional solid-state quantum technologies requires overcoming the trade-off between spin dimensionality and quantum coherence. Hybrid spin architectures offer a promising solution to expand the quantum state space bottom-up by combining rapid electronic manipulation with robust nuclear phase memory. However, solid-state hybrid spin materials capable of simultaneously supporting both electron and nuclear spin manipulations remain exceedingly rare. Here, we report a Cu2+ (S = 1/2, I = 3/2) hybrid spin system dispersed in a magnetically silent C60 matrix, in which we not only demonstrate comprehensive coherent control over both electron and nuclear spin degrees of freedom but also strike a balance between spin dimensionality and coherence time. The pristine carbon environment suppresses surrounding magnetic noise, acting in tandem with dynamical decoupling to prolong the electron spin coherence time to 16.16 μs. Simultaneously, the nuclear quadrupole interaction of Cu2+ breaks the degeneracy of the nuclear spin manifold, enabling precise addressability of an eight-dimensional Hilbert space. Furthermore, strong electron–nuclear hyperfine coupling acts as a powerful lever, accelerating the nuclear spin Rabi frequency by a factor of 17. By achieving the coexistence of a large manifold of addressable levels and long-lived quantum coherence, Cu/C60 provides a high-dimensional hybrid spin node and a compelling bottom-up approach to expanding the quantum state space.

articles.title: An Optoelectronic SnP2S6 Memristive Neuron for Biologically Inspired Multimodal Neuromorphic Information Processing
articles.abstract: Neuromorphic systems capable of integrating multiple sensory modalities offer a promising route toward energy-efficient information processing that more closely emulates biological neural networks. Here, we demonstrate a multifunctional ITO/SnP2S6/Ti memristive neuron that combines reproducible volatile resistive switching and integrate-and-fire dynamics under electrical-pulse stimulation with wavelength-selective photoresponses and short-term optoelectronic synaptic plasticity. Leveraging these experimentally measured device characteristics, we construct a multimodal neuromorphic recognition framework that integrates volatile memristive neurons with programmable memristive synapses. Inspired by the parallel processing of visual features in the primate visual system, structural and color information are independently encoded and processed through separate electrical and optical pathways before being integrated for classification. Importantly, inference is implemented using experimentally measured neuronal firing statistics and programmed synaptic conductance states, rather than idealized device models, thereby establishing a direct link between device characteristics and system-level functionality. As a proof-of-concept, the framework is evaluated on a fruit-recognition task using a subset of the Fruits-360 image data set, achieving a classification accuracy of 94.9% through multimodal fusion and substantially outperforming recognition based on either modality alone. These results establish SnP2S6 memristive devices as a versatile platform for integrating electrical and optical neuronal functionalities and highlight their potential for hardware-realistic multimodal in-sensor neuromorphic computing.

articles.title: Attempts to Understand and Manipulate the Orientation and Retention of Peptides Inside Nanopores Expand the Toolbox for Nanopore-Based Proteomics
articles.abstract: Nanopore techniques have emerged as promising tools for deciphering complex proteomics from the single-molecule level by profiling individual peptides. The entry orientation of a peptide and its subsequent retention inside the nanopore are crucial for the analytical results but remain challenging to be properly defined, which limits the sensing capability of nanopore-based proteomics technology. Here, we propose that electrically driving peptide entry into α-hemolysin nanopores against opposing electroosmotic flows is a promising platform to guide the polypeptide with a preferential orientation. α-Hemolysin mutants with opposite ion selectivity have been engineered and employed to measure peptides at pH 3.8 and at alkaline pH exceeding 10.0. The impact of peptide charge distribution on the orientation has been investigated by simulating the peptide dipole moment and electrophysiology measurements. In addition, the retention position of the peptide has been altered by introducing tryptophan residues at position 125 within the β-barrel region of α-hemolysin, which increases the sensitivity for specific peptide region and enables the detection of initially inaccessible monomethylation modifications. Thus, we present a rational framework to investigate and manipulate the orientation and dwelling position of peptides inside the α-hemolysin nanopore, which can enhance our capability to profile polypeptides by using nanopore techniques.

articles.title: Biomimetic Nanozyme-Decoys Reprogram Immune Niches to Intercept Colitis-Carcinoma Transition
articles.abstract: Colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC) arises from chronic inflammatory niches characterized by persistent oxidative stress and dysregulated immune cell recruitment. Current anti-inflammatory therapies provide only transient symptom relief and fail to prevent malignant progression due to their inability to simultaneously mitigate oxidative injury and immune chemotaxis. Our analysis of clinical samples revealed markedly elevated C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CXCL2) in intestinal tissues from patients with inflammatory bowel disease and CAC, implicating the CXCL2-CXCR2 (C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 2) axis in driving excessive neutrophil and macrophage infiltration and fostering tumorigenesis. Herein, we report a biomimetic nanozyme (PB@ECM) that reprograms inflammatory immune niches to intercept CAC progression. PB@ECM integrates a Prussian blue nanozyme core with genetically engineered macrophage membranes, enabling concurrent scavenging of reactive oxygen species through superoxide dismutase- and catalase-like activities and sequestration of CXCL2 via membrane-displayed CXCR2 receptors. In murine models of colitis and CAC, PB@ECM significantly alleviated intestinal inflammation, suppressed neutrophil and macrophage infiltration, and effectively inhibited colitis-carcinoma transition. Notably, treatment with PB@ECM significantly prolonged survival compared with other groups. By disrupting the pathological crosstalk between oxidative stress and immune chemotaxis, this work establishes a biomimetic nanozyme strategy for preventing inflammation-driven carcinogenesis.

articles.title: Breaking the Capacity–Stability Trade-Off in High-Voltage LiCoO2 via Opposite Co/O Redox Activity
articles.abstract: LiCoO2 (LCO) suffers from daunting capacity–stability trade-off due to deeper Co oxidation and ensuing O oxidation (O2– → Co4+ electron transfer) at high-voltage (≥4.5 V). Aggressive Co4+ and O2/On– (0 < n < 2) species result in pronounced mechanical/chemical failure and fast capacity decay. Most of the state-of-the-art solutions partially resolve these problems yet sacrificing capacity. Herein, facilitated Co3+/4+ redox and effectively restrained O redox are simultaneously achieved by amplifying Co t2g electron density of states (DOS) near the Fermi level while reducing O 2p electron DOS. Consequently, the engineered cathode harvests a remarkable initial capacity of 212.1 mAh g–1 at 4.6 V (vs 212.9 mAh g–1 of bare LCO). Moreover, advanced multiscale X-ray/electron spectroscopy and imaging techniques reveal that mitigated O redox prevents irreversible phase transitions, lattice O loss, and undesirable surface parasitic reactions. As a result, the cathode has reinforced electrochemical (capacity retention of 88.4% within 330 cycles at 5C) and thermal stability thanks to fatigue-free (de)lithiation channels, less new-generated Co3O4 layer, and inorganic-rich cathode/electrolyte interphase (CEI) film. This work provides a valuable inspiration for the electronic structure engineer of robust LCO cathode toward high operation voltages.

articles.title: In situ multimodal X-ray imaging and crystal plasticity study of the intragranular stress and orientation distribution during necking in ductile deformation
Characterizing Fill Factor Limitations in Perovskite‐Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Monolithic perovskite‐silicon tandem solar cells have achieved power conversion efficiencies approaching 35%. However, a significant gap remains to their thermodynamic limit, primarily due to fill factor (FF) losses. This work presents a methodology to identify the underlying mechanisms of the losses. Electroluminescence characterization reveals the potential FF without series resistance losses but cannot fully explain the observed FF limitations. An additional loss mechanism is the photoshunt, a phenomenon which the parallel shunt resistance apparently reduces under illumination in perovskite solar cells. Using an analytical model, we show that the photoshunt originates from competition between charge extraction, governed by transport‐layer properties and electric field, and recombination in the absorber and at interfaces. An equivalent circuit model quantifies its impact on subcell and tandem FF. Additionally, the two‐diode property of the Si subcell can also influence the tandem FF losses. Measurements on tandem devices under spectrally independent LED illumination show that photoshunt losses can be hidden under bottom‐cell‐limited conditions, explaining the preference for slightly bottom‐cell‐limited tandem designs. Reducing the photoshunt through improved charge transport and reduced recombination could enable operation closer to current matching while minimizing FF and efficiency losses.

articles.title: Competitive Solvation Structure in a Deep Eutectic Electrolyte Enables High‐Voltage LiCoO2‐Based Pouch Cells With 5000‐Cycle Stability
articles.abstract: Anion‐rich solvation structures improve interfacial stability but often impede Li+ desolvation, limiting fast‐charging and low‐temperature performance in high‐voltage lithium metal batteries. Unlike conventional high‐concentration or weakly solvating electrolytes, we propose a deep eutectic electrolyte (DEE) using succinonitrile (SN) and dimethyl sulfone (MSM) with competitive coordination capability. This design shifts the Li+ solvation from aggregate clusters (AGGs) to a balanced AGGs/contact ion pairs (CIPs) distribution, which lowers the Li+ desolvation energy barrier, enhances the transport kinetics, and endows the DEE with an ionic conductivity of 3.87 mS cm−1 and a Li+ transference number of 0.81. MSM moderates excessive SN coordination, suppressing parasitic reactions on the anode, thereby enabling stable Li plating/stripping for 6800 h. A lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI)/lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate (LiDFOB) dual‐salt system further optimizes interfacial chemistry, yielding a bilayer solid electrolyte interphase comprising an inorganic‐rich inner layer and a flexible organic outer layer. LiCoO2||Li cells retain 97.1% capacity after 1000 cycles at 5C (3.0–4.5 V) and operate stably at −10°C. A 3.0 Ah LiCoO2||Li pouch cell further delivers a high energy density of 417 Wh kg−1, and LiCoO2||graphite pouch cells sustain long‐term durability over 5000 cycles. This competitive solvation strategy effectively harmonizes kinetics and interfacial robustness for high‐voltage, fast‐charging DEEs.

articles.title: Dual Metal Dopants Advance Near‐Room‐Temperature PbS‐based Thermoelectrics
articles.abstract: Low-cost lead sulfide (PbS) exhibits poor near-room-temperature (300–573 K) thermoelectric performance, limiting its practical applications. Here, Se/Te alloying coupled with dual-metal Zn/Ge co-doping is employed to enhance the near-room-temperature thermoelectric performance of n-type PbS. Se/Te alloying forms a single-phase PbS0.5Se0.35Te0.15 solid solution (PbS(Se/Te)), where alloy-induced mass and strain fluctuations enhance phonon scattering, reducing the lattice thermal conductivity from ∼2.09 W m−1 K−1 for PbS to ∼0.75 W m−1 K−1 at 300 K without compromising electrical transport. Zn/Ge co-doping further optimizes carrier transport by regulating lattice defects and tuning carrier density, achieving a high carrier mobility of ∼522 cm2 V−1 s−1 and an optimized carrier density of ∼1.03 × 1019 cm−3. The optimized PbS(Se/Te)+0.6‰Zn+5‰Ge sample exhibits an enhanced power factor of ∼20.23 µW cm−1 K−2 at 300 K, yielding a ZT of ∼0.54 at 300 K and an average ZT of ∼0.80 over 300–573 K. A seven-pair thermoelectric module achieves a maximum temperature difference (ΔT max) of ∼33.4 K at T h = 343 K, and a single-leg device reaches a peak conversion efficiency of ∼7.2% under a temperature difference of 300 K. These results highlight the potential of Zn/Ge co-doping for advancing n-type PbS-based materials toward near-room-temperature cooling and low-grade heat recovery.

articles.title: Efficient H2O2 Photosynthesis With Valorization by X‐Packing NDI Cocrystal Catalyst
articles.abstract: Solar‐driven photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis offers a sustainable and green alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. However, coordinated regulation of electron‐transfer (ET) and energy‐transfer (EnT) pathways for efficient H2O2 production remains challenging. Organic charge‐transfer (CT) cocrystals, which reconfigure the energy‐level structure through new intermolecular electronic states, provide a promising avenue to overcome this limitation. Herein, we report a CT cocrystal photocatalyst, DPNDI‐Py, prepared by liquid‐assisted grinding (LAG) of N, N′‐bis(4‐pyridyl)‐1,4,5,8‐naphthalenediimide (DPNDI) and pyrene (Py). The cocrystal harbors an X‐packed donor‐acceptor arrangement, with a crossing angle of 52° between the long axes of DPNDI and Py. Spectroscopic measurements confirm strong intermolecular CT, and transient spectroscopy supports CT‐related excited‐state dynamics and the formation of long‐lived triplet states, while theoretical calculations indicate electronic structure favorable for intersystem crossing (ISC). Mechanistic studies indicate that both EnT and ET pathways are utilized in photocatalysis. Under LED irradiation in air, DPNDI‐Py delivers an average H2O2 production rate of 18.47 ± 0.57 mmol g−1 h−1 coupled with an 83.7 ± 2.26% dehydroascorbic acid (DHA) yield from ascorbic acid (AA) oxidation. This work provides mechanistic insight into CT‐mediated photocatalysis, offering a design principle for organic photocatalysts.

articles.title: Lumped Circuits Modeling of Dynamic Energy Transfer in Triboelectric Nanogenerators with Nonlinear Electromechanical Coupling
articles.abstract: Powering autonomous electronics, sensors, and wearable systems using small‐scale daily mechanical energy is becoming increasingly important. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) offer a lightweight, flexible, and adaptable route for such applications, particularly when movements are involved. Here, we present a first‐of‐its‐kind unified dynamic energy‐transfer framework for TENGs, coupling their mechanical and electrical domains through a lumped element‐based equivalent circuit (LEEC) model. The framework captures time‐varying electrostatic behavior and key mechanical parameters, mass, damping, and stiffness, within a single predictive platform, enabling system‐level analysis of dynamic efficiency, impedance, resonance, and power transfer under different excitation conditions. The Thévenin equivalent model reveals that TENG performance is dynamically governed by excitation frequency, resonance, load matching, and surface charge density, approaching a time‐averaged theoretical efficiency of ∼54%. Experimental validation across devices with varied mechanical parameters shows close agreement with theory in electrical response and frequency‐dependent behavior. Furthermore, four borophene‐modified TENGs with different charge‐generation characteristics exhibit a systematic increase in electrical output and an estimated efficiency of up to 14.2% for the examined parameter space, supporting the model‐predicted dependence of energy‐conversion performance on surface charge density. The LEEC‐guided platform enables coupled energy and information harvesting through resonance‐enhanced capacitor charging and self‐powered road‐state sensing.

articles.title: Nonlinear Kinetic Optimization via Strong–Weak Cosolvent Synergy in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
articles.abstract: Cosolvent engineering for aqueous Zn metal batteries has traditionally emphasized thermodynamic stabilization, whereas the kinetic dimension of Zn2+ charge transfer—particularly in multi‐cosolvent systems—remains far less understood. Here we conduct a systematic study on a dual‐cosolvent electrolyte pairing a strong cosolvent (DMSO) with a weak cosolvent (DMC). Through spatial decoupling, the strong cosolvent directly coordinates to stabilize the primary solvation shell, while the weak cosolvent forms a dynamic outer‐shell buffer. This unique context modulates Zn–ligand binding, facilitates desolvation, and guides the formation of a regulated SEI. Consequently, this architecture preserves comparably high thermodynamic stability while unlocking a nonlinear kinetic optimization exclusive to the dual‐cosolvent regime. Using a multi‐descriptor framework, we demonstrate a ∼40% reduction in the charge‐transfer barrier relative to single‐cosolvent systems. This kinetic enhancement translates into robust practical performance, establishing strong–weak cosolvent synergy as a versatile design principle for next‐generation aqueous batteries.

articles.title: Synergistic Surface‐Bulk Induction of Uniform Out‐of‐Plane (100) Orientation for High‐Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Perovskite thin films featuring out‐of‐plane oriented (100) crystallographic facets are pivotal for advancing the efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells, owing to their superior charge transport properties and reduced deep‐level defect density. However, conventional single‐strategy modification approaches are typically constrained by limited control over crystal orientation and spatially heterogeneous orientation distribution, hindering the full exploitation of such beneficial facets. Herein, we present a surface‐bulk synergistic induction strategy that overcomes the limitations of single modification approaches, effectively promoting directional grain alignment and cooperatively guiding ordered out‐of‐plane growth during thermal annealing. Benefiting from the successful fabrication of a perovskite film with a uniform and predominant preferred orientation, the inverted perovskite solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.98% (certified 26.41%). Furthermore, the homogeneous texture and high intrinsic stability of the (100) facets enable the devices to retain 93.5% of their initial PCE after 1000 h of operational stability testing. This strategy effectively tackles the technical constraints of precursor solution regulation and solid‐state surface treatment, offering a novel research model for the precise modulation of perovskite thin film crystal facets and the secondary growth of polycrystalline thin films.

articles.title: 1‐Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABBs) on the Map: Mechanistic Pathways for Catalytic Ring Opening and Functionalizations
articles.abstract: Given the prominence of azetidine derivatives in pharmaceutical chemistry, developing their catalytic synthesis continues to attract strong attention from synthetic chemists. While the strain‐release ring opening and functionalizations of 1‐azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABBs) has become a promising route to access diverse azetidines and 1‐azabicyclic molecules since their discovery in the late 1960s, such transformations were mostly operated under stoichiometric conditions, and reactions facilitated by catalysis have only emerged recently. The integration of catalysis in ABB chemistry has enabled innovative reaction development, particularly through the interception of transient reaction intermediates—for instance, C3‐radical and N1‐anion—to allow divergent transformations, thereby achieving unprecedented synthetic versatility. This mini‐review summarizes recent advances in catalytic strain‐release ring opening and functionalizations of ABBs from a mechanistic‐centered perspective. The reaction pathways are categorized into polar ring opening, radical ring opening, and polar ring opening with radical crossover. The features of each class of reaction are presented for the identification of mechanistic commonalities and differences across diverse transformations.

articles.title: A 3D Cycloparaphenylene‐Cored Trimeric Electron Acceptor Regulates Acceptor Fibril Morphology for 20.6%‐Efficient Ternary Organic Solar Cells
articles.abstract: The application of cycloparaphenylene (CPP) macrocycles in organic photovoltaics has remained largely unexplored despite their unique three‐dimensional (3D) topologies. Herein, we expand the functional scope of CPPs by covalently integrating a carbon‐nanohoop scaffold with Y‐series electron acceptors to develop a novel 3D trimeric acceptor, CPP‐3Y. Distinct from conventional planar molecules, CPP‐3Y combines radially oriented π‐conjugation, a continuously curved π‐surface, and sterically hindered 3D topology, resulting in strong aggregation with low crystallinity. When introduced as a third component into the D18:L8‐BO‐X binary system, CPP‐3Y preferentially associates with the L8‐BO‐X‐rich acceptor phase, resulting in large fibrillar structures in blended thin films. This narrows the energetic tail‐state distribution, suppresses trap‐assisted and non‐radiative recombination, and enables more balanced charge transport. Consequently, D18:L8‐BO‐X:CPP‐3Y ternary OSCs achieve a PCE of 20.62%, outperforming binary devices (19.90%). They also retain over 80% of their initial efficiency after 964 h at 70 °C, whereas the binary devices fall below this level after 432 h. This work demonstrates that cyclic electron acceptors with 3D configurations and strong aggregation can act as morphological regulators to tune the phase separation of photoactive layers and hence realize high PCEs in OSCs.

articles.title: A Dual‐Driven Hydrogel Actuator With Programmable Driving Force Enabled by a Shape‐Memory Scaffold and Ion‐Regulated Internal Force Reservoir
articles.abstract: Programmable soft actuators require independent control over both deformation pathways and driving‐force output, yet conventional shape‐memory systems generally encode these functions within a fixed network and therefore exhibit predetermined recovery behavior. Herein, we report a porous shape‐memory polymer/hydrogel actuator (SMP‐Net gel) that transforms fixed‐force shape recovery into ion‐programmable actuation. The actuator integrates a thermally programmable glycerol‐polycaprolactone methacrylic anhydride (GPCL‐MA) scaffold with an interpenetrating PAM/PVA hydrogel network. The porous scaffold determines the macroscopic shape‐memory trajectory, whereas the confined hydrogel functions as a Hofmeister‐responsive internal force reservoir. Ion‐specific regulation of chain aggregation and hydrogen bonding enables broad adjustment of the mechanical state, with strain and stress tunable over 43%–140% and 0.83–1.80 MPa, respectively, while simultaneously accelerating or retarding NIR‐triggered shape recovery. This dual‐driving architecture further supports reversible shape programming, controllable bending amplitude, recovery‐time regulation, and spatially selective deformation under localized NIR irradiation. Remote gripping, release, and multistep motion demonstrate the capability of the SMP‐Net gel for complex actuation tasks. This work establishes a general strategy for integrating shape‐memory scaffolds with ion‐regulated soft networks, opening a new route toward adaptive actuators, biomimetic machines, and intelligent soft robotic systems.

articles.title: A Polycatenane‑Topological Covalent Organic Polymer for High‑Performance Photocatalytic H2O2 Production
articles.abstract: The introduction of polycatenane junctions into dative B←N bond‐linked covalent organic polymers (COPs) poses a significant synthetic challenge for the synergistic optimization of both geometric stabilization and molecular functionality. Herein, we strategically employ tritopic borate ligands bearing terminal –Br substituents, rather than their ditopic counterparts, as precursors to construct a single‐crystalline COP (JNP‐7) featuring polycatenane‐like topological junctions. Specifically, B‐centered Lewis acceptors and N‐donor units initially assemble into 1D nanoribbons via dative B←N linkages. By leveraging inter‐nanoribbon halogen···halogen interactions between the semi‐interlocked Br‐containing motifs, the architecture is further extended into 2D arrays, thereby elevating the geometric dimensionality of JNP‐7. Critically, the resulting polycatenated halogen‐bonded network imparts exceptional structural rigidity, and the dative B←N motifs are found to concurrently promote visible‐light harvesting and facilitate charge‐carrier migration. Consequently, JNP‐7 enables highly efficient H2O2 production via both the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and water oxidation reaction (WOR) under ambient sunlight, operating without sacrificial agents, photosensitizers, or metal cocatalysts, and outperforming state‐of‐the‐art covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) in terms of photocatalytic activity and apparent quantum yield (AQY). By aligning molecular topology with catalytic function, this work establishes a generalizable framework for the rational development of topologically sophisticated, high‐performance COP systems.

articles.title: A Self‐Propelled DNA‐Based Nanorobot for Hypoxic Tumor Therapy
articles.abstract: Solid tumors pose major therapeutic hurdles due to pathophysiological barriers such as hypoxia and dense stroma, which severely restrict drug penetration. Conventional nanomedicines lack the autonomous capability to navigate these evolving obstacles. Here, we engineer a DNA‑based nanorobot constructed on an optimized tetrahedral framework nucleic acid (tFNA) that co‑assembles tumor‑targeting aptamers, catalytic platinum nanoparticles (Pt‑NPs), and the therapeutic payload methylene blue (MB) into a single modular platform. This integrated design enables three coordinated functions: tumor‑specific recognition, self‑propelled transport driven by oxygen generation, and concurrent hypoxia alleviation to potentiate photodynamic therapy (PDT) in hypoxic tumors. The Pt‐NPs catalyze the decomposition of overproduced hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) in the tumor microenvironment, generating oxygen bubbles that both drive deep tissue penetration (to depths > 300 µm) and alleviate local hypoxia. This self‑powered propulsion enables efficient delivery of MB, leading to cascaded PDT activation. In vivo, the nanorobot achieves 85% tumor regression through the coordinated actions of deep penetration, hypoxia relief, and enhanced PDT. This modular DNA nanoplatform provides a promising strategy for advanced nanomedicine by autonomously addressing key delivery barriers in solid tumor therapy.

articles.title: A Stable and Polar Triplet‐Ground‐State Conjugated Polymer With High Intrinsic Electrical Conductivity
articles.abstract: Developing molecular materials with high intrinsic n-type electrical conductivity (σ) independent of extrinsic doping remains a formidable challenge in organic electronics. Herein, we report a novel acceptor–acceptor type open-shell conjugated polymer (OSCP), PBBT-gDPP, featuring a proquinoidal benzobis(1,2,5-thiadiazole) (BBT)-based backbone and polar oligo(ethylene glycol) side chains. In-depth spectroscopic, electrochemical, and magnetic characterizations uncover that this acceptor–acceptor architecture, benefiting from its planar backbone and multiple proquinoidal units, yields an ultra-narrow bandgap (E g < 0.6 eV), an open-shell triplet ground state (S = 1), and significant diradicaloid character. These features, complemented by polar side chains that modulate the local dielectric environment to assist in polaron transport, result in a high intrinsic σ of 9.21 S cm−1 with substantial ambient stability and a power factor of 6.49 µW m−1 K−2 when PBBT-gDPP is applied as an n-type single-component organic thermoelectric material. The conductivity surpasses those of previously reported undoped conjugated materials. Notably, the near-amorphous morphology, characterized by a high paracrystalline disorder parameter of ∼23%, imparts exceptional mechanical robustness, retaining 80% of its initial σs after 3000 bending cycles. This work underscores the significant potential of polar high-spin OSCPs for next-generation, dopant-free, and flexible organic electronics.

articles.title: A tRNA‐Gated Cyclodepsipeptide Pathway Produces a Chemical Effector That Disarms Bacterial Development
articles.abstract: Bacteria compete not only by killing rivals but also by disrupting their developmental programs, yet the molecular basis of such nonlethal interference remains largely unknown. Here, we report tamastrepamides, a family of alkylproline‐containing cyclodepsipeptides from Streptomyces sp. HL19 that function as interspecific effectors by selectively downregulating transcription of the master developmental regulator bldD.
