The horizontally acquired tam biosynthetic gene cluster is conspicuously enriched in rare TTA codons, functionally coupling its expression to the developmentally regulated tRNALeu(UAA) encoded by bldA. Tamastrepamide A arrests sporulation and diminishes secondary metabolite production in diverse actinomycetes without inhibiting vegetative growth, thereby chemically phenocopying a ΔbldD mutant. Promoter‐specific reporter assays demonstrate that tamastrepamide A reduces bldD promoter activity, while the producer strain is intrinsically insensitive to this effect. Production of tamastrepamides strictly depends on the functionally specialized tRNALeu(UAA), revealing a self‐contained regulatory circuit in which a developmentally gated metabolite disables the same developmental program in neighboring competitors. These findings illustrate an ecological strategy in which a developmentally regulated biosynthetic pathway produces a diffusible metabolite that interferes with the sporulation program of competing actinomycetes.

articles.title: Agostic Hydridoborate Complexes as Masked Coinage‐Metal Hydrides: Hydride Migration Between Boron and Gold Unlocks CO2 Reactivity
articles.abstract: Hydride addition to diphosphine‐borane (DPB) coinage‐metal complexes affords an unprecedented series of Cu(I), Ag(I), and Au(I) hydridoborate complexes 2‐M featuring bridging B–H···M interactions. Combined multinuclear NMR, IR, single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, and DFT studies reveal the presence of agostic‐type σ(B–H)→M interactions across the series, with the strongest interaction observed for copper. These hydridoborate species are thermodynamically favored over the corresponding metal hydrides. Markedly distinct reactivity is observed depending on the coinage metal. Whereas, the Cu and Ag congeners proved to be unreactive toward CO2, the Au complex 2‐Au cleanly and reversibly fixes CO2 to form the isolable Au(I) formate complex 3‐Au. In addition to quantitative and reversible CO2 uptake and release, the Au hydridoborate complex 2‐Au is an efficient and robust catalyst for the hydroboration of CO2 to HCO2Bpin and the dehydrogenation of formic acid, both with complete selectivity. Experimental and computational studies support a cooperative mechanism in which the B─H─Au motif acts as a masked gold hydride, thanks to hydride transfer.

articles.title: Ampere‐Level CO2‐to‐Formate Electrosynthesis Over Grain‐Boundary‐Rich Sulfur‐Doped SnO2 in Alkaline–Neutral–Acidic Electrolytes
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic reduction of CO2 to formate offers a sustainable route for carbon utilization, converting a greenhouse gas into a valuable chemical feedstock. Although Sn‑based catalysts are among the most promising candidates, their formate selectivity often suffers a marked decline at ampere‑level current densities, and operating efficiently in various electrolytes, especially acidic media, remains a major challenge. In this work, we report a grain boundary‑rich sulfur (S)‐doped SnO2 catalyst that enables CO2‐to‐formate electrosynthesis at ampere‐level current densities across alkaline, neutral, and acidic electrolytes. The catalyst achieves formate Faradaic efficiencies exceeding 90% at 1 A cm−2 in acidic, neutral, and alkaline electrolytes. In situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations reveal that S doping reduces the reaction free energy change for the key *OCHO intermediate and promotes its protonation to formate. Meanwhile, S‑doped SnO2 with abundant grain boundaries facilitates the formation of an enhanced interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network, which promotes efficient proton transfer while suppressing the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). This work provides new insights into the design of high‐performance electrocatalysts through elemental doping and elucidates the governing role of the interfacial microenvironment in reaction activity and selectivity, offering design principles applicable to broader electrochemical syntheses.

articles.title: An Asymmetric Phytochemical as a Building Block for Robust Structurally Resolved Crystalline Frameworks
articles.abstract: Plant polyphenols and related oxygen‐donor phytochemicals are attractive natural ligands for metal–organic materials owing to their rich chemical reactivity, structural diversity, and sustainability. However, current phytochemical coordination chemistry remains dominated by amorphous systems, and structurally resolved crystalline frameworks are still largely restricted to simple and symmetric molecules. This gap has hindered atom‐level understanding of phytochemical coordination and limited the rational development of crystalline materials from these abundant natural ligands. Here, we report SCU‐1, the first structurally resolved crystalline coordination framework constructed from hematoxylin (HMT), a historically important but structurally complex and asymmetric phytochemical. Structural modeling, three‐dimensional electron diffraction (3DED), Rietveld refinement, and quantum‐chemical calculations together reveal that such an asymmetric phytochemical can assemble into periodic crystalline frameworks while generating coordination heterogeneity. Structural resolution further defines precise pore architectures, coordination environments, and host–guest interaction sites, thereby enabling direct elucidation of structure–property relationships. Importantly, SCU‐1 exhibits exceptional robustness, strong CO2 affinity, and visible‐light‐driven photocatalytic CO2 conversion in water with selective ethanol production. These results establish asymmetric phytochemicals as viable building units for robust crystalline metal–organic materials and demonstrate the importance of structural determinacy in advancing phytochemical coordination chemistry and structure–property relationships.

articles.title: Andrey Belyaev
articles.abstract: “I chose chemistry as a career because I fell in love with it in eighth grade, and the reaction has proved irreversible… The most important feature of a good working environment is a shared sense of humor and the ability to discuss mistakes openly, learn from them, and move forward together…” Find out more about Andrey Belyaev in his Introducing… Profile.

articles.title: Anion Engineering of Surface Frustrated Lewis Pairs for Light‐Assisted CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol
articles.abstract: Surface frustrated Lewis pairs (SFLPs) have been widely studied as active sites for light‐assisted CO2 hydrogenation, while most efforts have focused on cation engineering to tune the Lewis acidity of metal centers, leaving the Lewis‐basic component less directly controlled. Here, we report an anion engineering strategy based on nitridation to prepare nitrogen‐doped, non‐stoichiometric spinel zinc gallium oxide catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol. Nitrogen incorporation modifies the local anion coordination environment, promotes oxygen vacancy formation, and reconstructs the coordination structure around Ga sites, thereby generating defect‐associated Ga–O/N Lewis acid–base pairs that favor heterolytic H2 splitting. Nitridation also narrows the band gap and introduces localized electronic states, leading to improved light absorption. As a result, the optimized catalyst achieves a methanol production rate of 1203.7 µmol h−1 g−1 with enhanced methanol selectivity and apparent quantum efficiency (AQE) under illumination. This work demonstrates that anion engineering provides an effective route to regulate oxide SFLPs and promote light‐assisted CO2 hydrogenation to methanol.

articles.title: Anion‐Doped Manganese Oxides Enabling Relay Catalysis for Aerobic Alcohol Ammoxidation
articles.abstract: The development of noble-metal-free heterogeneous catalysts for room-temperature aerobic ammoxidation of alcohols to nitriles represents an enduring challenge, primarily hampered by unselective lattice-oxygen over-oxidation via the classical Mars–van Krevelen (MvK) pathway and strong site-blocking effects. Herein, we report a dual-anion (C/N) doped MnO x (C/N–MnO x ) synthesized via a green, solvent-free crystallization strategy, which exhibits excellent catalytic performance (95.3% benzyl alcohol conversion, >99% benzonitrile selectivity) and broad substrate versatility (35 diverse alcohol substrates) under ambient conditions (25°C, 1 atm O2) without external energy inputs. Structural analyses and theoretical calculations demonstrate that N-doping introduces medium-strong Lewis acidic Mn–N sites to capture NH3, while C-doping generates localized oxygen vacancies for O2 activation. Crucially, kinetic isotope effect experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations prove that this anion dopant-programmed relay catalysis successfully bypasses the MvK pathway, fundamentally shifting the rate-determining step from initial alcohol dehydrogenation to the homolytic α–C–H bond scission of the aldimine intermediate. This work presents a paradigm shift in designing multifunctional non-precious catalysts for ambient-condition green organic transformations.

articles.title: Aromatic Pummerer‐Promoted Stereospecific Cross‐Coupling of Thiazoles With Boronic Esters
articles.abstract: Thiazoles are ubiquitous motifs in bioactive molecules, making strategies for the stereospecific installation of chiral C(sp3)‐rich substituents on this scaffold particularly valuable for drug discovery. However, achieving such transformations remains nontrivial, as conventional C(sp2)–C(sp3) cross‐coupling approaches are often compromised by catalyst deactivation and deleterious side reactions, such as β‐hydride elimination. Although electrophile‐mediated coupling of alkyl boronic esters with lithiated aromatic compounds offers a potential route to C(sp2)–C(sp3) bond formation, it is ineffective for thiazoles because the heteroaromatic core lacks sufficient nucleophilicity to engage electrophiles and promote productive 1,2‐migration. Herein, we report a lithiation–borylation–aromatic Pummerer (LiBAP) strategy that enables stereospecific C5 cross‐coupling of thiazoles with boronic esters. A pendant sulfinyl group enables exocyclic electrophilic activation, triggering a Pummerer‐type 1,2‐migration while avoiding unproductive C─B bond fragmentation. The reaction proceeds with complete stereospecificity and broad functional‐group tolerance, furnishing a C2 sulfide handle on thiazole that serves as a versatile linchpin for downstream C–S diversification. A formal asymmetric synthesis of a bioactive thiazole γ‐secretase inhibitor was demonstrated to further highlight the synthetic utility of our LiBAP protocol.

articles.title: Atomic Contact With Cu Single Atom Promoting Pt3 Clusters for High‐Performance Acetylene Semihydrogenation
articles.abstract: Understanding how second metal species modulate catalytic performance remains a central challenge in bimetallic heterogeneous catalysis. Here, we report a controllable strategy to construct atomically contacted and spatially isolated structures between Pt3 clusters and Cu atoms on γ‐Al2O3 by atomic layer deposition (ALD), enabling direct interrogation of metal–metal synergy. By regulating anchoring sites around Pt clusters, Cu atoms can be selectively positioned either by bonding to Pt to form Pt3Cu1 clusters or by separating into isolated Cu single atoms. Comprehensive characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that Cu single atom can act as an effective promoter only when directly bonded to Pt3 clusters. As electron donator, the bonded Cu atom can enhance the hydrogen dissociation ability of Pt clusters, weaken their strong acetylene adsorption, and facilitate ethylene desorption, thereby overcoming the activity‐selectivity trade‐off in selective hydrogenation of trace acetylene. In contrast, isolated Cu single atom fails to promote Pt3 clusters and even deteriorate selectivity. These results demonstrate that Pt─Cu bond formation, rather than simple proximity, governs synergistic effects in bimetallic cluster catalysts. This work establishes a clear design principle for atomically engineered catalysts and offers a general strategy to independently optimize catalytic activity and selectivity.

articles.title: Atroposelective Pd(0)‐Catalyzed Direct Intermolecular C─H Arylation of Thiazole N‐Oxides Provides Access to Heterobiaryls
articles.abstract: Despite the importance of heteroaryl atropisomers in medicinal chemistry and catalysis, straightforward access to these motifs via direct enantioselective C─H heteroaryl‐aryl coupling remains challenging. We report an enantioselective Pd(0)‐catalyzed arylation at the C4‐position of thiazole N‐oxides, forging the critical atropochiral axis. A designer point‐ and axially chiral monodentate phosphine is instrumental to enable high reactivities along with tight stereocontrol. A broad range of substrate combinations is coupled in high enantioselectivities, including two different heteroarenes. The enantioenriched thiazole N‐oxides are amenable to derivatizations around the substituents contributing to the stability of the chiral axis, including a reduction of the N‐oxide moiety without racemization.

articles.title: Aza‐Büchner–Curtius–Schlotterbeck Reaction Enables Selective Construction of Quaternary Carbon Centers
articles.abstract: Herein, we report the Aza‐Büchner–Curtius–Schlotterbeck reaction (ABCS)– a novel method for the uncatalyzed C─C insertion reaction of photogenerated donor‐donor diazo compounds into aryl aldimines. The transformation proceeds under very mild conditions and high chemoselectivity, favoring C─C over C─H insertion pathways. In a single step, two C(sp2)─C(sp3) bonds are formed, granting access to homologated imines bearing a newly constructed quaternary carbon center in good yields. Subsequent hydrolysis gave homologated aldehydes, enabling versatile downstream transformations. The diazo intermediate is generated using a continuous‐flow microreactor, enhancing both safety and scalability. Mechanistic insights, supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, reveal the origins of the observed selectivity and reactivity.

articles.title: Bioinspired Face‐to‐Face Supramolecular Co‐Assembled Arrays Enabled by Cation‐π Interaction With Programmed Electron Transport for Efficient Hydrogen Peroxide Photosynthesis
articles.abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production has emerged as a sustainable alternative to the energy-intensive anthraquinone process, yet its efficiency remains fundamentally limited by inefficient charge transport and electron-hole recombination. Here, we report a bioinspired strategy for constructing face-to-face supramolecular co-assembled arrays (FF-SCAAs), in which periodic co-facial organization serves as a structural platform for programming electron transport pathways toward enhanced photocatalytic H2O2 production. Inspired by the signal-transport arrays of natural compound eyes, cationic trioxatriangulenium (TOTA+ ) and electron-rich benzophenanthrene derivatives are integrated into highly ordered FF-SCAAs through directional cation-π interaction. The resulting FF-SCAAs feature enhanced dipole moments and favorable orbital alignment, enabling extended charge transport channels while intrinsically suppressing electron-hole recombination. On this basis, FF-SCAAs achieve a H2O2 photosynthesis rate up to 6.46 mmol g−1 h−1 with a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 0.84%. Ultrafast spectroscopic and mechanistic studies demonstrate that the periodic co-facial arrays promote directional excited-state electron migration and selective two-electron oxygen reduction pathways for H2O2 generation. Furthermore, the in situ generated H2O2 is fed into a cascade wastewater treatment system and consumed in a downstream Fenton process for efficient degradation of phenolic pollutants.

articles.title: Boosting Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation of BiVO4 Photoanodes With an Iron‐Based Metal–Organic Framework as a Hole Transport Layer
articles.abstract: Sluggish bulk hole transport fundamentally limits the performance of bismuth vanadate (BiVO4) photoanodes in photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. Herein, we report a BiVO4/Fe-MOF/NiFeOOH trilayer photoanode, wherein an iron-based bipyridine dicarboxylate metal–organic framework (FeBPDCA), grown on BiVO4 via coordination-assisted in situ synthesis, serves as a dedicated hole-transport layer. The Fe-MOF layer provides a favorable band alignment and a built-in electric field at the BiVO4/Fe-MOF interface to drive directional bulk hole extraction, while NiFeOOH acts as a surface water-oxidation cocatalyst. Experimental characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the Fe-MOF primarily accelerates bulk hole extraction, whereas NiFeOOH suppresses surface recombination through rapid water oxidation, together boosting both bulk charge-separation efficiency (η bulk) and surface charge-transfer efficiency (η trans) up to 97%. The optimized photoanode achieves a high photocurrent density of 7.15 mA cm−2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE, with an onset potential of 0.24 V and a maximum applied bias photon-to-current efficiency (ABPE) of 2.56%. This work demonstrates that deliberate tuning of MOF energy levels through metal node and ligand selection enables the simultaneous engineering of favorable band alignment and efficient charge separation at semiconductor/MOF junctions, providing a practical design strategy for photoanodes where bulk charge extraction is the primary efficiency bottleneck.

articles.title: Borane‐Catalyzed Water Dehydrogenation at Dioxaphospholes and ‐Phospholanes
articles.abstract: We report that water undergoes rapid oxidative addition to readily accessible dioxaphospholes and ‐phospholanes within minutes at room temperature. The resulting phenylphosphinate esters release dihydrogen under mild conditions (room temperature to 60°C) in a borane‐catalyzed process. Remarkably, a pinacol‐derived dioxaphospholane reacts spontaneously with atmospheric moisture under ambient conditions to form the corresponding phenylphosphinate ester, thereby enabling the direct utilization of water from air for catalytic hydrogen evolution. The mechanism of the borane‐catalyzed dehydrogenation was investigated by variable time normalization analysis, targeted synthesis of intermediates, and DFT calculations. These studies support a catalytic pathway initiated by hydrogen elimination from the borane adduct of the phosphinate ester, followed by retro‐hydroboration to regenerate the catalyst.

articles.title: Breakthrough Design of Highly Potent Antivirals Against Wild‐Type HIV‐1 and Lenacapavir‐Resistant M66I Variant
articles.abstract: Lenacapavir (LEN), the first-in-class HIV-1 capsid inhibitor (CAI) with picomolar potency and long pharmacokinetics (PK), is approved for both treatment and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). However, the frequently selected M66I mutation confers complete resistance to LEN. Potent antivirals against the M66I variant remain elusive. In this work, we have designed LEN analogs featuring a distinctive R 2 moiety to directly address the molecular mechanism of resistance. Our analog synthesis also entailed developing a new synthetic procedure for R 2 incorporation. Significantly, the newly designed analogs were highly potent against both WT HIV-1 and the M66I mutant. Particularly, lead compound 3S conferred 2.6-fold higher potency than LEN against WT HIV-1 and remained highly potent (EC50 = 5.8 nM) against the M66I mutant, a drastically advanced activity profile over LEN (EC50 > 15 µM). The unprecedented potency of our lead 3S against M66I was corroborated by a thermal shift assay. In a head‑to‑head intravenous (IV) PK study in rats, lead 3S demonstrated superior systemic exposure, showing a 4.6‑fold greater plasma area-under-curve (AUC) than LEN and largely retaining the long PK characteristic of LEN. These results strongly validate our design and represent a breakthrough in LEN-based HIV-1 therapy and prophylaxis.

articles.title: Capturing an Elusive [Cp*Co(Allyl)CO]+ Complex for Catalytic Allylic C─H Amidation of Unactivated Olefins
articles.abstract: Transition‐metal‐catalyzed nitrene transfer reactions offer a powerful strategy for direct C─H bond amination; however, the nature of the key reactive intermediates, particularly with Cp*Co(III) systems, remains elusive. Herein, we report a cobalt‐catalyzed allylic C─H amidation of unactivated alkenes using dioxazolones as practical nitrene precursors. The isolation of a well‐defined π‐allyl‐cobalt(III) complex provides a platform for direct interrogation of the reactive nitrene species. Mechanistic studies, including EPR spectroscopy and DFT calculations, support the involvement of an open‐shell singlet cobalt–nitrenoid intermediate. Both the neutral cobalt(III) precatalyst and the synthesized π‐allyl‐cobalt(III) complex are catalytically active, and the catalytic system displays broad substrate scope, good functional‐group tolerance, and moderate to high regioselectivity. These results provide key mechanistic insights into cobalt‐mediated nitrene transfer reactions and establish a foundation for the development of selective cobalt‐catalyzed C─H amination reactions.

articles.title: Catalysis by a Metastable Photoswitchable Cage
articles.abstract: The introduction of ortho‐methyl substituents on aryl‐substituted ortho‐tetrafluoroazobenzene photoswitches breaks the π‐conjugation and improves photoswitching selectivity and increases the thermal half‐life of the metastable isomer. Using this approach, a visible‐light‐responsive ligand was assembled with a non‐switchable ligand and palladium(II) ions into a mixture of molecular cages. When irradiated with 530 nm light, the system converges to form a single product, a metastable, mixed‐ligand molecular cage. This cage can be reversibly disassembled using 424 nm light, an example of integrative self‐sorting controlled by light. The metastable assembly can catalyze both Michael addition and nitroaldol reactions. Importantly, visible light accesses a metastable catalytic state inaccessible under thermodynamic control. We demonstrate that the active assembled species can be switched on and off at will using visible irradiation and the metastable species is the most catalytically active assembly.

articles.title: Catalyst‐Controlled Divergent Strain‐Release Amination and Skeletal Remodeling of Bicyclo[1.1.0]Butanes
articles.abstract: Catalyst‐controlled nitrene transfer enables divergent amination reactions of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes through distinct modes of activation of their highly strained central σ‐bond. Under Rh(II) catalysis, bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes undergo selective strain‐release amination to furnish aminocyclobutenes, which provide efficient access to cyclobutane amino acids through a simple amination–hydrogenation sequence. In contrast, photocatalytic nitrene activation redirects the reaction pathway toward double amination and skeletal remodeling, affording functionalized dihydropyrrolidines that can be readily converted into pyrrole heterocycles under acidic conditions. The synthetic utility of both approaches is further demonstrated, for example, in a telescoped synthesis of cyclobutane amino acids from diazo precursors or downstream diversification reactions. Mechanistic experiments and computational studies reveal distinct catalyst‐dependent nitrene activation pathways that govern the fate of a common reactive intermediate and underpin the observed divergent reactivity.

articles.title: Catalytic Anionic Substituents Effects as Selectivity Mediators in Photocatalytic Hydrogen Atom Transfers
articles.abstract: Photo‐induced hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) catalysis has become a powerful platform for the direct and selective functionalization of ubiquitous C─H bonds. Traditionally, the outcome of these transformations is dictated by the interplay between C─H bond dissociation energies and polar effects, enabling predictable yet inherently substrate‐controlled selectivity. Recently, a fundamentally new strategy has emerged that relies on the catalytic and reversible modulation of substrate electronics to transiently enhance the reactivity of targeted C─H bonds. Notably, catalytic full or partial deprotonation of oxygen‐ and nitrogen‐containing functional groups has proven remarkably effective in selectively activating adjacent C─H bonds toward HAT, a phenomenon known as the anionic substituent effect. Rather than relying solely on the intrinsic properties of a substrate, this concept allows chemists to reprogram C─H bond reactivity in situ, unlocking previously inaccessible levels of selectivity in the direct functionalization of abundant functional groups under mild photocatalytic conditions. In this minireview, we discuss the mechanistic principles underpinning catalytic anionic substituent effects (CASE), the diverse strategies developed to generate them, and their impact on photocatalytic HAT‐mediated C–H functionalization. By highlighting recent advances and emerging opportunities, we illustrate how transient electronic activation is reshaping the design of selective C–H functionalization reactions.

articles.title: Catalytic Enantioselective Remote Transannular Desymmetrization of Calix[4]Arenes to Inherently Chiral Double‐Macrocycles
articles.abstract: There has been a recent surge in research aimed at synthesizing inherently chiral macrocycles that lack point, axial, planar, or helical chirality. To overcome the structural limitations of existing inherently chiral macrocyclic systems, which often suffer from facile racemization due to conformational flexibility, we report herein an asymmetric synthesis of a new class of inherently chiral double‐macrocyclic molecules through an intramolecular macrocyclization strategy, employing calix[4]arenes as the starting platform. Catalyzed by [Pd(allyl)Cl]2 and a chiral phosphoramidite ligand, calix[4]arene derivatives bearing a monoaryl bromide linker at the upper rim underwent a facile enantioselective remote transannular Suzuki–Miyaura coupling with the adjacent upper‐rim position of the neighboring arene unit, furnishing the desired inherently chiral double‐calixarene macrocycles in up to 71% yield and 91% ee. The resulting double macrocycles feature stable conformations and unique semi‐enveloped chiral cavities, and exhibit promising chiral catalytic and chiroptical properties.

articles.title: Chalcogen‐Driven Conformational Control for Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence and Zn2+ Coordination‐Induced Delayed Fluorescence in Phenazine Derivatives
articles.abstract: Purely organic luminescent materials are pivotal for optoelectronics, with chalcogen‐fused phenazines serving as basic building blocks owing to their strong electron donating ability and enhanced spin–orbit coupling effect. However, a systematic understanding of how the chalcogen identity governs intrinsic conformational preference between quasi‐axial (QA) and quasi‐equatorial (QE) forms remains elusive. To address this, we designed a series of derivatives featuring phenoxazine, phenothiazine, and phenoselenazine donors coupled with a terpyridine acceptor. We demonstrate that the chalcogen atom dictates molecular conformation: phenoxazine derivative exclusively adopts the QE conformation, phenothiazine derivative predominantly favors QE, while phenoselenazine derivative stabilizes in the QA form. Notably, heating induces a phase transition in polymorphs toward their thermodynamically favored conformations. Furthermore, Zn2+ coordination enhances intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) strength, shifting the thermodynamically preferred conformation and triggering a switch from room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) to dual RTP–delayed fluorescence (DF) emission. This work validates the chalcogen‐determined conformation and ICT strength can effectively modulates DF/RTP performance, deepening the fundamental understanding of the chalcogen‐mediated conformation and properties for the rational design of organic luminescent materials.

articles.title: Characterization of a Fungal Modular Polyketide Synthase System Reveals an Unusual Strategy for Polyketide Chain Initiation
articles.abstract: Polyketides constitute a major class of natural products with remarkable structural diversity and biological activities. While bacteria predominantly produce polyketides via modular type I polyketide synthases (PKSs), eukaryotic modular PKSs remain largely unexplored. Here, we report the functional characterization of a fungal modular PKS system from Lasiodiplodia theobromae through heterologous expression in Aspergillus oryzae, leading to the production of the antimalarial macrolide strasseriolide C (1). Intriguingly, biosynthesis of 1 involves C‐methylation of the starter malonyl unit despite the absence of a methyltransferase domain in the loading module. Furthermore, module 2 of the PKS system contains an unusual arrangement of four consecutive acyl carrier protein (ACP) domains. Although the catalytic basis of this methylation remains unresolved, our isotope‐labeling experiments, mutational analyses, and in vitro biochemical assays support a model in which the malonyl unit loaded onto the module 2 ACPs is transferred to the loading ACP, where starter‐unit methylation is proposed to occur prior to chain initiation. Our study reveals unexpected biosynthetic logic and establishes a foundation for mechanistic studies and engineering of eukaryotic modular PKSs.

articles.title: Chiroptical Switching by Stereoselective Photochemical Sigmatropic Rearrangements: Experimental Realization of Calderoselectivity
articles.abstract: The stereochemical outcomes of pericyclic reactions provide direct insight into the geometry and directionality of concerted bond reorganization. Although torquoselectivity has emerged as a defining concept for electrocyclizations, an analogous principle for sigmatropic rearrangements on a single cyclic π system has remained unknown. We report that a homoannulene‐based photoswitch undergoes an auxiliary‐controlled, stereoselective photochemical [1,11]‐sigmatropic rearrangement, thereby establishing selectivity over directional migration on a single cyclic π framework. We coin the term calderoselectivity for such an unreported stereoselective sigmatropic rearrangement. The switching process is reversible, proceeds to photostationary mixtures of homoannulene and iso‐homoannulene isomers, and furnishes diastereomeric products in a 56:44 ratio; combined chiral HPLC, NMR, ECD, and DFT studies assign the major directionality of acyl migration in pro‐R directionality. This study provides the first experimental realization of calderoselectivity and reveals a direct analogue in sigmatropic rearrangements to torquoselectivity with implications for both mechanistic physical organic chemistry and chiroptical switch design.

articles.title: Cobalt‐Catalyzed Desymmetrizing Hydrogenation of Cyclic Anhydrides
articles.abstract: Achieving general asymmetric catalytic manifolds that accommodate broad substrate diversity remains a long‐standing and highly sought‐after goal in synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report an efficient cobalt‐catalyzed desymmetric hydrogenation of structurally diverse cyclic 1,2‐ and 1,3‐diacid anhydrides, enabling access to pharmaceutically relevant chiral γ‐ and δ‐lactones with broad substrate scope and excellent enantioselectivity (up to 99% ee). The reaction is readily scalable, as demonstrated by gram‐scale synthesis of several representative products. Notably, this 3d‐metal catalytic platform represents a rare example that outperforms platinum‐group‐metal‐based counterparts in both generality and stereoselectivity. DFT studies identify a catalytically active d7 Co(II) dihydride complex with an outer‐sphere hydride transfer mechanism, wherein a relatively flexible chiral pocket underlies the broad substrate compatibility of this catalytic system.

articles.title: Cobalt‐Catalyzed [2σ+2π] Cycloaddition via Site‐Selective Capture of Bicyclobutane Diradical
articles.abstract: Strained bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) have emerged as versatile precursors for accessing highly reactive intermediates, enabling unconventional bond constructions through strain‐release pathways. Herein, we report a cobalt(II)‐catalyzed strategy that combines thermal activation of BCBs with selective radical capture by Co(II) to afford head‐to‐head fused bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (BCHex). We propose that thermal activation of the BCB generates a reactive diradical intermediate, which is intercepted by a tailored bidentate phosphine Co(II) cationic complex via oxidative radical coupling, followed by a [2σ+2π] cycloaddition with indoles. Mechanistic investigations, including 31P NMR spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), and density functional theory (DFT) studies, provide insights into the plausible reaction pathway. The involvement of paramagnetic Co(II) species is consistent with the broad features observed in both EPR and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra of the catalyst. In addition, four structurally distinct Co(II) complexes were synthesized, fully characterized by UV–Vis and Fourier‐transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and evaluated as catalysts for the transformation. The cationic nature of the Co(II) species was further confirmed by phosphine oxide trapping experiments and single‐crystal X‐ray crystallography.

Doxycycline and Risk for Pregnancy Loss
articles.abstract: BackgroundDoxycycline is commonly prescribed to reproductive-aged women, but evidence about safety during pregnancy is limited.ObjectiveTo evaluate the risk for pregnancy loss after doxycycline exposure in the first trimester.DesignRetrospective active-comparator cohort study.SettingMerative MarketScan commercial (2005-2021) and Medicaid (1999-2019) claims data.ParticipantsPregnancies ending in loss or live birth among women aged 12 to 55 years.Intervention3 cohorts of pregnancies with first-trimester oral doxycycline or comparator antibiotic prescription fills and concomitant diagnoses of respiratory tract infection (RTI) or acne.MeasurementsPregnancy loss was evaluated using validated algorithms. Doxycycline-exposed pregnancies were matched on propensity score and gestational age to comparator pregnancies (exposed to amoxicillin or a macrolide for RTI or topical clindamycin for acne). Adjusted risk differences and adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) were estimated via binomial and modified Poisson regression separately for each database and comparison.ResultsThe study included 218 234 pregnant participants with RTI (110 254 in MarketScan, 107 980 in Medicaid) and 6636 with acne (4719 in MarketScan, 1917 in Medicaid). Among those with RTI, doxycycline use was associated with an increased risk for pregnancy loss compared with amoxicillin use (MarketScan aRR, 1.54 [95% CI, 1.41 to 1.68]; Medicaid aRR, 1.40 [CI, 1.28 to 1.53]). Results were similar for the comparison with macrolides (MarketScan aRR, 1.39 [CI, 1.28 to 1.51]; Medicaid aRR, 1.36 [CI, 1.25 to 1.48]). Among patients with acne, the comparison with topical clindamycin was statistically significant in MarketScan (aRR, 1.49 [CI, 1.26 to 1.76]) but not Medicaid (aRR, 1.03 [CI, 0.80 to 1.33]). Among cohorts with statistically significant aRRs, risk differences ranged between 7 and 11 percentage points.LimitationResidual confounding and exposure or outcome misclassification are possible, and congenital malformations were not evaluated.ConclusionDoxycycline use for RTI or acne during early pregnancy was associated with an increased risk for pregnancy loss. Clinicians may use this information to weigh risks and benefits when prescribing doxycycline to reproductive-aged women.Primary funding sourceCenters for Disease Control and Prevention.

articles.title: Preconception Care
articles.abstract: Optimizing health and management of medical conditions before conception can improve the likelihood of becoming pregnant and of an uncomplicated pregnancy. This article reviews best practices in preconception medical care for cisgender pregnancy-capable women desiring conception to optimize their fertility, improve their perinatal well-being, and decrease the likelihood of pregnancy complications. Given that almost half of all pregnancies in the United States are unintended or mistimed, internal medicine physicians are well positioned to proactively provide reproductive counseling and care.

articles.title: COP1 is a temperature-responsive switch in Arabidopsis
articles.abstract: COP1, a central integrator of light signaling, senses temperature via an intrinsically disordered region, suggesting how thermomorphogenesis can be modulated according to different climates.

articles.title: Nicotianamine-driven nickel transport to sink organs underpins maize productivity
articles.abstract: A node-phloem-localized nicotianamine efflux transporter in maize regulates Ni delivery to sink organs, including seeds, where Ni-dependent urease activity promotes amino acid metabolism, revealing an unappreciated role of Ni in the yield formation of graminaceous plants.

articles.title: Plasmodium falciparum Hsp90 supports DNA replication
articles.abstract: Malaria parasites depend on PfHsp90, but the cellular pathways supported by this essential chaperone remain poorly defined. Ibrasheva et al. identify PfHsp90-dependent proteins enriched in DNA replication, demonstrate that Hsp90 inhibition impairs parasite DNA synthesis, and uncover synergistic interactions between Hsp90 and DNA replication inhibitors.

articles.title: A redox route from cysteine to glucagon secretion
articles.abstract: In this issue of Cell Reports, Behera et al.1 show that cysteine metabolism sustains α-cell excitability and glucagon secretion via voltage-gated Na+ channels. Redox control of excitability thus emerges as a component of α-cell nutrient sensing.

articles.title: ECHS1 K115 succinylation inhibits fatty acid β-oxidation in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
articles.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of cancer and involves alterations in glucose metabolism. Increasing evidence shows that acylation modifications mediated by metabolic intermediates play vital roles in cancer progression. Toward understanding the lysine succinylation (Ksu) that regulate pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) development, we conduct a comprehensive succinylproteome study on a prospectively collected PDAC cohort. Succinylome integration identifies a range of dysregulated Ksu sites closely associated with metabolic perturbations. Moreover, cross-talk analysis of Ksu and lysine lactylation (Kla) reveals the functional roles of Ksu in proteins specifically related to the fatty acid β-oxidation (FAO), among which, the succinylation at lysine 115 (K115su) of short-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase 1 (ECHS1) is downregulated in pancreatic cancer. It is further verified that K115su reduces the conversion of ECHS1 for its substrate, thereby inhibiting FAO metabolism. Therefore, our study delineates multiple cancer-specific Ksu sites and unravels the significance of ECHS1 K115su in PDAC progression.

articles.title: IFN-γ coordinates macrophage-mediated inflammatory resolution and matrix remodeling in heart regeneration
articles.abstract: Heart regeneration requires coordinated immune responses that support tissue remodeling and myocardial renewal. Here, we identify interferon-γ (IFN-γ) as an injury-responsive regulator of macrophage function during zebrafish heart regeneration. Loss of ifng1 disrupted immune cell dynamics, impaired debris clearance and collagen remodeling, reduced cardiomyocyte (CM) protrusion and proliferation, and delayed scar resolution. Cardiac macrophage transcriptomes revealed altered inflammatory and ECM-remodeling programs, including reduced expression of matrix metalloproteinases and increased tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (timp4.3) expression. Macrophage-specific blockade of IFN-γ signaling recapitulated key regenerative defects and was associated with similar dysregulation of ECM-remodeling genes. Nanoparticle-mediated timp4.3 silencing reduced its expression in injured adult hearts and FACS-isolated cardiac macrophages, improved collagen remodeling and CM protrusion, and partially rescued CM proliferation and scar resolution in ifng1 mutants. Together, these findings link macrophage IFN-γ signaling to regenerative ECM remodeling and identify Timp4.3 as a functional downstream regulator.

articles.title: Lineage-specific metabolic transcription across environmental gradients in geothermal microbial communities
articles.abstract: Understanding how environmental heterogeneity shapes microbial metabolism remains a central challenge. While metagenomics has revealed extensive metabolic potential, how these functions are transcriptionally represented across environmental gradients and microbial lineages remains unclear. Here, we integrated genome-resolved metagenomics and metatranscriptomics with co-expression network analysis to examine metabolic transcription across geothermal environments. Across Tengchong hot springs, metabolic transcription varies with pH, temperature, and organic matter. Acidic, organic-rich springs show prominent heterotrophic and sulfur-metabolism-related transcription, with Mesoaciditogales primarily associated with coenzyme and purine biosynthesis and Thermoplasmatales with sulfur reduction and central carbon metabolism. In contrast, non-acidic thermal springs show carbon fixation transcripts from Aquificales and Cyanobacteriales and sulfur oxidation transcripts from Aquificales and Deinococcales. Under more extreme conditions, carbon-fixation pathways become less diverse and increasingly biased toward energetically efficient strategies, while nitrogen-cycling transcription remains restricted. These findings reveal how microbial functional programs and their lineage associations reflect environmental heterogeneity across geothermal habitats.

articles.title: Metabolic reprogramming by caloric restriction enhances acute phase virological control and reduces chronic inflammation during SIV infection
articles.abstract: Nutrient metabolism influences HIV-1 replication, antiviral immunity, and chronic inflammation, yet remains difficult to leverage therapeutically. Using a non-human primate model of HIV-1, we modulated metabolism through caloric restriction (CR). Four months of 30% CR was safe and induced metabolic reprogramming in rhesus macaques. Compared with ad libitum-fed animals, CR reduced gut mucosal CCR5+ CD4+ T cell frequencies. Following SIV infection, CR reduced acute viremia, dampened type I interferon signaling, and enhanced CD8+ T cell cycling in lymphoid tissues. CR-associated protection coincided with glycolytic upregulation, supporting an early reduction in viremia that waned over time. Following antiretroviral therapy, CR limited gastrointestinal immune activation, improved tricarboxylic acid cycle flux, and reduced plasma sCD14 and TNF-related molecules. Blood SIV DNA remained unchanged, suggesting GI inflammation can be decoupled from viral persistence. These findings demonstrate that dietary intervention can limit lentiviral pathology while revealing the temporally constrained nature of glycolysis in supporting antiviral responses.

articles.title: Mouse APOE Christchurch protects against Aβ-induced tau and α-synuclein aggregation
articles.abstract: Apolipoprotein E (APOE) genotype alters the risk for Alzheimer's disease (AD) but also affects dementia risk in Parkinson's disease (PD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). Recent evidence suggests that the APOE Christchurch (CC) mutation protects against AD, however, its effects on PD and DLB are unknown. We generated an APOE CC knock-in mouse to understand its effects on amyloid-β (Aβ), tau, and α-synuclein (α-syn) aggregation. APOE CC mice show increased plasma cholesterol and triglyceride levels, decreased Aβ and Aβ-induced tau pathology after intracortical AD-tau injection into 5xFAD mice but do not change Aβ or tau pathology in individual transgenic mouse models without injection. Interestingly, APOE CC reduces formation and spread of α-syn aggregation in the brain, peripheral-to-spinal cord spread, and directly increases binding affinity to α-syn compared to APOE WT. Our study emphasizes the remarkable protective effects of a point mutation in murine APOE against Aβ-induced tau and α-syn aggregation.

articles.title: RNA-binding protein NOC4L governs early natural killer cell development through dual post-transcriptional mechanisms
articles.abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are critical regulators of immune cell biology, yet their roles in innate lymphoid cell development remain largely undefined. We identify NOC4L, a conserved ribosome biogenesis factor with extraribosomal functions, as an essential RBP governing early natural killer (NK) cell development. NOC4L is enriched in NK progenitors (NKps) and dynamically upregulated by IL-15 signaling. Conditional deletion of NOC4L in mouse NKp cells severely disrupts NK cell homeostasis and causes a developmental blockade at the NKp stage, compromising anti-tumor immunity. Mechanistically, NOC4L exerts dual post-transcriptional functions: (1) as an RBP, it directly binds and stabilizes Nfil3 (also known as E4bp4) mRNA, encoding the master transcription factor for NK lineage commitment; and (2) independently of its RBP activity, it interacts with CDK9 to regulate cell-cycle progression. This study establishes NOC4L as the RBP coordinating post-transcriptional control and cell-cycle dynamics in early NK cell development, revealing potential targets for immune-based therapies.

articles.title: RNA-binding protein RBM34 promotes hepatic fibrosis by enhancing DROSHA-mediated nuclear export of Loxl2 mRNA
articles.abstract: Hepatic fibrosis is driven by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition from activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). Although RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are emerging as key regulators of HSC activation, the role of RBM34 in liver fibrosis remains unexplored. Here we show that RBM34 is markedly upregulated in human and murine fibrotic livers, predominantly in activated HSCs, and is potently induced by TGFβ. RBM34 enhances fibrotic marker expression and HSC contractility, and HSC-specific knockdown attenuates liver fibrosis in vivo. Mechanistically, STAMP (survey targets by APOBEC-mediated profiling) and RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) analyses identified lysyl oxidase-like 2 (Loxl2) mRNA as a direct RBM34 target. RBM34 interacts with DROSHA to promote nuclear export and translation of Loxl2 mRNA independently of DROSHA's canonical RNase III activity. Collectively, these findings uncover a non-canonical role for DROSHA in mRNA trafficking and establish the RBM34-DROSHA-LOXL2 axis as a driver of hepatic fibrogenesis, highlighting RBM34 as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: TNIP1 acts as an aggrephagy receptor that assembles clearance machinery for protein aggregate removal
articles.abstract: Selective autophagy receptors recognize and recruit harmful intracellular components to autophagosomes for degradation, and their dysfunction is linked to neurodegeneration, metabolic disorders, and cancer. Here, we identified TNFAIP3 interacting protein 1 (TNIP1) as an aggrephagy receptor implicated in neurodegenerative diseases. TNIP1 accumulated at polyubiquitinated protein aggregates upon proteotoxic stress. Genetic depletion of TNIP1 reduced protein aggregate clearance and increased axonal degeneration under proteotoxic stress. Mechanistically, TNIP1 enhanced protein aggregate clearance by assembling aggrephagy receptors, such as SQSTM1/p62 and TAX1BP1, onto protein aggregates. Gene expression analysis revealed that TNIP1 expression levels are reduced in patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) with TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) inclusion pathology. Additionally, an ALS-associated TNIP1 mutant exhibited impaired association with TDP-43 aggregates and failed to rescue their autophagy-mediated degradation. These findings establish TNIP1 as an aggrephagy receptor and reveal its potential role as a therapeutic target for ALS and other proteinopathies.

articles.title: A sliding annular in situ bioprinting strategy for rapid and robust fabrication of small-diameter vascular grafts
articles.abstract: Chen et al. develop a sliding annular in situ bioprinting strategy that combines a detachable annular printhead, PH hydrogel, and sacrificial PVA scaffold for rapid small-diameter vascular repair. In a rabbit carotid artery model, the strategy restores blood flow and supports vascular tissue integration.

articles.title: In-context learning for medical artificial intelligence
articles.abstract: Wong et al. review how in-context learning enables large language models to adapt to medical tasks using examples rather than model parameter updates. They map its applications and limitations and propose a risk-proportionate framework for evaluation, governance, and monitoring to guide responsible clinical translation.

articles.title: Microbiome-antibiotic-immune interactions influence mortality in preterm infant gut microbiota-humanized gnotobiotic mice
articles.abstract: Preterm infants are commonly treated with antibiotics. Schwartz et al. discover associations between antibiotic administration, systemic immune responses, microbiome composition, and death in gnotobiotic mouse pups humanized with stool from preterm infants. These findings can help contextualize the unintended consequences of antibiotic administration for preterm infants.

articles.title: Routes to cleaner critical metals
Diffusion Models for Small-Molecule Design
articles.abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have emerged as a class of generative models for controllable small-molecule design in drug discovery capable of progressively transforming noisy or partially specified molecular states into candidate structures under structural, geometric, and property constraints. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the methodological foundations and representative applications of diffusion-based molecular generation, emphasizing the alignment among molecular representations, generative dynamics, controllable design, and evaluation and validation. Particular attention is given to recent advances in property- and structure-guided generation, target-aware and fragment-based design, multiobjective optimization, and synthesis-aware generation. We also discuss the roles of data sets, computational evaluation, and prospective experiments in assessing the chemical and biological relevance of generated molecules. By organizing these developments within a unified conceptual framework, we provide computational chemists and drug discovery researchers with a structured roadmap that balances the mathematical rigor with chemical intuition. Throughout, we highlight current methodological limitations and unresolved challenges and conclude with future directions toward chemically credible and experimentally grounded molecular design. To facilitate navigation of this rapidly evolving field, we introduce an interactive companion platform (https://diffsmd.scbdd.com) that provides a curated, continuously updated repository of model architectures and visualizations.

articles.title: Electrochemical conversion of low-concentration carbon dioxide to multicarbon products: advances, challenges, and perspectives
articles.abstract: This review highlights advances in electrochemical conversion of low-concentration CO 2 to multicarbon products, covering dilute and impurity-containing CO 2 , capture-solution electrolysis, bioelectrocatalysis, and techno-economic analysis.

articles.title: Hydrogen borrowing with heterogeneous catalysis
articles.abstract: Hydrogen borrowing (HB) enables sustainable C–N, C–C, and C–S bond formation using alcohols as alkylating agents. Heterogeneous HB catalysts offer improved recyclability and scalability (continuous production).

articles.title: Magnetic Skyrmions in CrGaTe3 Monolayer
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) magnetic skyrmions hold great promise for next-generation high-density information storage, yet their low-dimensional behavior and controllable size remain challenging. Here, combining first-principles calculations and Monte Carlo simulations, we identify monolayer CrGaTe3, derived from the Ga2S3 structure, as a ferromagnetic half-metal and a robust platform for hosting topological spin textures. The system exhibits a substantial Dzyaloshinskii−Moriya interaction (DMI) of 2.36 m V, arising from intrinsic inversion asymmetry and strong spin−orbit coupling, alongside sizable Kitaev exchange and magnetic anisotropy. At zero field, the ground state adopts a Néel-type cycloid state, which evolves into stable skyrmion phases under moderate external magnetic fields. Remarkably, beyond field tuning, we find that biaxial strain not only modulates the skyrmion size but also induces skyrmion states under tensile conditions, offering an additional degree of freedom for topological phase engineering. Furthermore, our parameter-resolved analysis reveals that while DMI is pivotal for skyrmion nucleation, the Kitaev interaction and magnetic anisotropy collectively govern the size and density of the skyrmion lattice. These findings establish monolayer CrGaTe3 as a promising candidate for sub-10 nm spintronic devices and demonstrate that the synergy between intrinsic symmetry breaking and external stimuli provides a generalizable strategy for designing functional 2D magnets.

articles.title: ZnO Vacancy Homojunction for Phonon-Enhanced Directional Charge Transfer
articles.abstract: Directional charge transport is essential for efficient photocatalysis, yet carrier transfer in semiconductor nanocrystals is often random and limited by recombination. Although electron−phonon coupling strongly influences carrier dynamics, phonons are more commonly associated with energy dissipation than with enhanced charge transport. Here, we construct a ZnO vacancy homojunction composed of donor-type oxygen vacancies and acceptor-type zinc vacancies, establishing an intrinsic pathway for directional charge transfer. The resulting n−p junction introduces both an internal electric field and asymmetric lattice distortion, enabling phonon-assisted directional carrier transport under ultrasonication and leading to significantly enhanced photocatalytic performance in methylene blue degradation compared with conventional ZnO. Combined spectroscopic measurements, radical-trapping experiments, and density functional theory calculations reveal a phonon-enhanced directional charge-transfer mechanism. These findings provide a general strategy for regulating directional charge transport through lattice dynamics.

articles.title: Generation of Human Cardiomyocytes With Adult-Like Metabolism by a Chemically Defined Medium for Mitochondrial Disease Modeling
articles.abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)–derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC cardiomyocytes) as a model for cardiac disease have become increasingly important, bolstered by the Food and Drug Administration’s initiative to promote novel alternative methods for biomedical research. A key limitation of metabolically immature iPSC cardiomyocytes is their limited ability to accurately recapitulate mitochondria-dependent pathologies, such as Friedreich ataxia–associated cardiomyopathy. Adult cardiomyocytes are characterized by a high density of interfibrillar mitochondria, abundant respiratory complexes (I–V) that form supercomplexes, and efficient utilization of fatty acids to drive mitochondrial respiration. These unique metabolic structures and functions are largely missing in iPSC cardiomyocytes. Further, whether iPSC cardiomyocytes can efficiently utilize fatty acids for respiration in the presence of glucose, a unique adult feature, remains unclear. We developed a chemically defined, 11-component maturation medium (MM11) designed using a bioinformatics-guided strategy that identified high-fidelity transcriptional markers of adult cardiac metabolic maturity. Human iPSC cardiomyocytes were treated with MM11 for 2 weeks and evaluated at the molecular, structural, and functional levels, with an emphasis on mitochondrial maturity. We benchmarked our results with isolated primary adult human cardiomyocytes. Last, we tested whether this method could enable us to more accurately model Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy. MM11 treatment increased expression of metabolic pathways, including mitochondrial respiration and fatty acid metabolism, at the transcript and protein levels. Ultrastructural analyses revealed the formation of interfibrillar mitochondria and mitochondrial respiratory supercomplexes, a feature never shown in previous reports. Functionally, MM11-treated iPSC cardiomyocytes exhibited substantially increased oxidative phosphorylation and a metabolic preference for fatty acid utilization in the presence of physiologic substrates, as determined by oxygen consumption assays and 13 C isotope tracing. MM11 promotes robust metabolic maturation of human iPSC cardiomyocytes, enabling sophisticated mitochondrial architecture and substrate utilization. These metabolically matured cardiomyocytes more faithfully model mitochondria-dependent cardiac pathologies, including ischemia-reperfusion injury and Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy, improving the use of iPSC cardiomyocytes for mechanistic studies of human heart disease.

articles.title: Off-Pump versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Prefrail and Frail Patients: 30-Day and 1-Year Outcomes From the FRAGILE Randomized Trial
articles.abstract: Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain. This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated. A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0–73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94–2.31]; P =0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P =0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively ( P =0.099). In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT02338947.

articles.title: A Comparison of Owl Pellet Analysis and Conventional Trapping: A Review of Central European Cases for the Study of Small Mammal Communities and More Efficient Paleoenvironmental Reconstructions
articles.abstract: Due to their rapid reproductive cycles and short generation times, small mammals—particularly rodents and shrews—are widely used as bioindicators in ecological studies. While traditional live trapping provides detailed demographic data for such monitoring, it is labour‐intensive and subject to sampling bias. In contrast, owl pellet analysis presents a non‐invasive and cost‐effective alternative for evaluating small mammal community structure over broad spatial and temporal scales, though potential prey preferences should be considered. This study evaluates the effectiveness of owl pellet analysis in comparison to conventional trapping methods for monitoring small mammal communities. We synthesised data from 26 published studies and additional unpublished field reports, comprising a uniquely robust dataset of 40 systematically processed case studies across seven countries in Central Europe, a biogeographically coherent region. In all cases, trapping and pellet collection were carried out at the same locations and during the same periods, allowing for an exceptional level of methodological consistency. Results reveal that owl pellet analysis detects higher species diversity and provides a more efficient, non‐invasive means of monitoring small mammal assemblages over larger spatial and temporal scales. However, prey preferences and hunting behaviour of owls introduce biases, often overrepresenting abundant prey such as the common vole, Microtus arvalis and underrepresenting species associated with specific habitats or microclimates. These biases have significant implications for biodiversity assessments and paleoenvironmental reconstructions, where accurate community composition is essential. Our findings indicate that while owl pellet analysis is a valuable tool for ecological monitoring, careful consideration of predator selectivity is necessary to accurately interpret the results. Further research into owl hunting ecology is recommended to refine the application of this method in biodiversity studies and paleoecology.

articles.title: Building a Framework for Peatland Assessment in Europe by Combining Spectral and Molecular Data
articles.abstract: Peatlands provide critical ecosystem services, including carbon storage, water regulation, and climate mitigation, yet spatial information on their ecological condition remains limited despite widespread degradation. Specific biogeochemical analyses (e.g., biomarkers, molecular compounds, compound specific stable isotopes) can characterize drainage‐related changes in peat properties but are time‐consuming, costly, linked to sophisticated analytical set‐up and thus spatially restricted. We therefore investigated whether high‐resolution PlanetScope imagery capture consistent spectral differences between pristine and drained areas and explored their multivariate correspondence with complementary site‐level biogeochemical properties. Spectral indices, including NDVI, EVI, gNDVI, Greenness Index, and albedo were derived from PlanetScope Analysis‐Ready Surface Reflectance (ARPS) data for nine European peatland sites spanning three climatic zones and contrasting open and sparsely treed vegetation structures. Peat biogeochemistry was characterized using elemental carbon and nitrogen contents and molecular composition determined by pyrolysis–GC/MS. NDVI and Greenness Index differed most consistently between the investigated pristine and drained areas, with higher values under drained conditions across both vegetation structures. In contrast, EVI and albedo, even though also suitable indicators, depended more strongly on vegetation structure and the patterns differed between open and sparsely treed systems. Spectral differences were most pronounced during May and June, identifying the early growing season as the period of strongest spectral separation within the investigated dataset. Drained areas were additionally characterized by higher nitrogen contents, lower C/N ratios, and a greater relative abundance of compounds indicative of metabolized organic matter. Exploratory principal component analyses indicated complementary site‐level patterns between spectral and biogeochemical variables associated with hydrological condition. Consequently, this study demonstrates the potential of high‐resolution PlanetScope spectral data to differentiate between pristine and drained peatland conditions across the investigated sites. However, predictive classification of previously unknown peatland areas will require dedicated modeling and independent validation especially in differentiating from surrounding transition peats and mineral grassland soils.

articles.title: Ecological and Structural Drivers of Song Amplitude Variation in Passerines
articles.abstract: Song amplitude is an important but comparatively understudied dimension of avian acoustic communication, influencing signal transmission, detectability and social interactions. We investigated ecological and structural drivers of song amplitude variation in six passerine species using 3265 songs recorded from 120 territorial males. Body size was associated with cross‐species variation in amplitude only when the largest and loudest species, the Great Reed Warbler, was included. Across species, song amplitude declined with increasing temperature, relative humidity and time after sunrise, whereas ambient noise showed no evidence of a generalised Lombard effect. Song rate, song length and peak frequency were consistent predictors of amplitude, with peak frequency showing the strongest association. Within‐species analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity in environmental effects, whereas relationships between amplitude and song structure were more consistent across species. Individual identity explained considerable variation in amplitude, indicating pronounced within‐species variability in vocal output. Overall, our results suggest that song amplitude is a flexible component of vocal performance shaped primarily by song structure and signalling context rather than by body size alone. These findings emphasise the importance of considering both behavioural and ecological sources of variation when interpreting patterns of acoustic signalling in birds.

articles.title: Genomic Diversity and Population Structure of Tibetan Antelopes Sampled From the Selincuo Region
articles.abstract: Based on genome‐wide SNP data, this study assessed genomic diversity and population structure in Tibetan antelopes sampled from the Selincuo National Nature Reserve. The analyses included runs of homozygosity (ROH), genomic inbreeding coefficients, genetic diversity, linkage disequilibrium (LD), effective population size, genomic relatedness, principal component analysis (PCA), and sNMF. Genomic inbreeding varied among the sampled individuals, with substantial variation among individuals. Short and medium‐length ROHs predominated, whereas long ROHs contributed little to total ROH coverage. This pattern indicates that population‐wide homozygosity is mainly associated with older shared ancestry, genetic drift, and historical demographic change, with limited evidence of severe recent inbreeding. Several individuals had relatively high ROH‐based inbreeding coefficients, indicating heterogeneous individual‐level autozygosity. The samples retained considerable genome‐wide SNP variation, although allele frequencies were unevenly distributed. PCA showed dispersion among individuals, while sNMF identified multiple ancestry components with substantial overlap in individual genetic backgrounds. Kinship analysis detected no first‐ or second‐degree relatives among the sampled individuals. Linkage disequilibrium declined with increasing physical distance between markers, providing a basis for estimating recent effective population size and evaluating demographic history. Overall, the analyzed individuals showed variation in genomic autozygosity, with several exhibiting elevated homozygosity. The LD‐based estimate of recent effective population size provides a baseline for continued genomic monitoring of Tibetan antelopes sampled from the Selincuo region. Broader geographic and temporal sampling is needed to assess population boundaries and changes in genetic diversity. Future work should expand sampling across geographic regions and time periods and compare multiple populations using genome‐wide differentiation, IBD sharing, isolation‐by‐distance analysis, demographic modeling, and direct estimates of migration or gene flow. These analyses will clarify historical demographic changes, recent effective population size variation, and genetic connectivity among protected areas.

articles.title: Population Genetics of Small Hive Beetles in Their Native Range Indicates High Gene Flow and Male‐Biased Dispersal
articles.abstract: The success of biological invasions depends strongly on the genetic diversity and dispersal abilities of invading populations. In many species, males and females differ in their dispersal behavior, potentially contributing unequally to the establishment and spread of invasive populations. Population genetic approaches provide powerful tools for investigating genetic diversity and dispersal patterns. When applied to populations in their native range, these approaches can improve our ability to predict the spread and potential impacts of species following their introduction into new environments. However, such studies remain scarce for many invasive species. This holds true for small hive beetles (SHB), Aethina tumida, which are free‐flying parasites of social bee colonies native to sub‐Saharan Africa that have recently become a widespread invasive species. Here, we show high gene flow across A. tumida populations from Western Kenya. Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and nuclear DNA (nuDNA) markers were used to study SHB genetic diversity and differentiation and to infer short‐ and medium‐range dispersal across host colonies (N = 15) and neighboring apiaries (N = 5; ≤ 30 km apart). The mtDNA diversity was high (29 haplotypes in 87 samples), but no significant differences were detected in haplotype diversity and distribution within and across apiaries. The nuDNA diversity and differentiation levels also did not differ significantly between apiaries. However, genetic differentiation among apiaries was significantly lower in males than in females. Moreover, significant isolation by distance was detected in the females but not in the males, suggesting sex‐biased dispersal. Overall, the results suggest that the observed high gene flow underlies the high genetic diversity of SHB, which may contribute to its invasion success.

articles.title: Primary Cavity Excavators in Community‐Managed Lowland Forest of Nepal: Woodpecker Assemblage, Nest‐Tree Preference, and Its Implications for Forest Management
articles.abstract: Woodpeckers are keystone species playing a crucial role as ecosystem engineers, with their highest species richness and diversity in the tropical and subtropical regions. Although most research on the species' ecology originates from the temperate regions, it leaves a substantial gap in woodpecker assemblage and nesting ecology in tropical and subtropical areas. Our study fills this gap in the subtropical region of South Asia, exploring woodpecker diversity, abundance, and factors influencing cavity nest occurrence in the lowland sal Shorea robusta forests of Nepal. The study was carried out in May and June 2024 in the Pathlaiya Community Forest (CF), with 24 line transects established. Each transect was surveyed twice for woodpecker abundance and nesting cavities, with data gathered on the perpendicular distance of woodpecker observation from the transect, tree characteristics, and nesting variables. Distance sampling analysis was used to estimate an overall woodpecker density and detection probability in the study area, which were found to be 0.54 ± 0.07 birds/ha and 0.79 ± 0.05, respectively. Overall, 51 individuals from nine woodpecker species were recorded. In Nepal's lowland sal forests, the nesting occurrence of woodpeckers was significantly influenced by factors: canopy cover, tree condition and tree Diameter at Breast Height (DBH), with emphasis on sal and jamun Syzygium cumini as preferred tree species. It was found that woodpecker cavity nest occurrence depends substantially on mature forest structure for nesting, highlighting the importance of retaining adequate amount of snags and larger trees, aligning with sustainable forest management practices. These findings emphasize community‐managed tropical sal forests as important habitats for primary cavity excavators, particularly Picidae. Our study highlights the importance of retaining large native trees, snags, and cavity‐bearing tree species in forest management plans to support woodpeckers and the larger cavity‐nesting species in South Asia.

articles.title: Temperature‐Dependent Warning Colour Variation in an Aposematic Insect
articles.abstract: Aposematic colouration in animals advertises prey toxicity and unpalatability to predators. However, intra‐specific variation in aposematic signals is widespread and often thought to be the result of environmental factors such as temperature. To investigate how temperature affects warning colour, we used the aposematic seed bug Lygaeus simulans as a model. Wild‐type adults of this species exhibit the typical red and black pattern common among many aposematic insects, while “pale” mutants are yellow and black. Here, we investigated how rearing temperatures affect their warning colour, fitness traits, and protein expression. We found that L. simulans warning colouration is temperature sensitive, with both pale‐mutant and wild‐type individuals redder at lower temperatures (24°C) compared to higher (32°C) temperatures. Reduced body size (weight and length) was also found at this lower temperature. Utilising SWATH‐proteomic analysis, we identified 15 differentially expressed proteins between the two morphs, including Glutathione S‐transferase (GST), a protein involved in oxidative states. Subsequent analysis of GST activity showed higher activity in pale‐mutants compared to wild‐types at 29°C. Furthermore, in males, this difference between morphs mirrored the colour change as it was not evident at 24°C, although this was not the case in females. Our research reveals a distinctive temperature‐dependent variation in aposematic colouration, providing a greater understanding of how warning signals evolve with temperature changes.
