Bridging the hearing data gap in the endangered Australian sea lion (Neophoca cinerea) through biomechanical modelling
articles.abstract: The endangered Australian sea lion (Neophoca cinerea) divides its functional ecology between land (for mating and pup-rearing) and sea (for foraging). Given this amphibious lifestyle, it is susceptible to natural and anthropogenic sound exposure in both air and water. Hearing data for the species are limited to a small sample size (two individuals) of behavioural measurements in air at only a few frequencies, and no underwater hearing thresholds are currently available. Understanding its auditory sensitivity is important for assessing potential risks from anthropogenic sound across its habitat. This study used computed tomography-based finite-element modelling of three post-mortem Australian sea lion heads to simulate frequency-dependent sound reception across broad frequency ranges in air and under water. Transfer functions were calculated as the ratio of stapes-footplate velocity to incident sound pressure, providing a quantitative measure of mechanical sound transmission to the inner ear. The models indicated differences in sound reception between the two media. The transfer functions were subsequently converted into estimated audiogram curves by anchoring the minimum thresholds to published values for Australian sea lions and closely related otariid species. The resulting curves were broadly consistent with published otariid audiograms. This study provides a mechanistic description of aerial and underwater sound reception in Australian sea lions, together with an anatomically informed basis for estimating hearing sensitivity and identifying frequency ranges relevant to anthropogenic sound exposure. More broadly, it provides the first mechanistic estimate of underwater hearing in ASLs and demonstrates the potential of CT-based finite-element modelling as a conservation physiology tool for inaccessible marine mammals.

articles.title: Consistent specialization on roe deer across contrasting prey communities: diet and prey selection of Eurasian lynx in the Western Carpathians
articles.abstract: The Carpathian population of the Eurasian lynx (Lynx lynx carpathicus) represents one of the most important native source populations for lynx conservation and reinforcement in Central Europe, yet ecological drivers of prey selection remain poorly understood. We investigated diet composition, and factors influencing prey selection in the Western Carpathians using an integrated approach combining GPS telemetry and systematic kill-site inspections, snow tracking, scat analysis, camera trapping and microsatellite genotyping for individual lynx identification from scats. Based on 446 prey remains and 386 scat samples collected across several mountain regions, we found that the lynx diet was overwhelmingly dominated by wild ungulates, which accounted for 96.0% of prey remains and 96.3% of total consumed biomass. Roe deer (Capreolus capreolus) was the main prey species, representing 64.6% of prey remains and 69.0% of consumed biomass, followed by red deer (Cervus elaphus; 27.6% and 24.8%, respectively). Despite substantial variation in ungulate community composition and the availability of alternative prey, roe deer remained consistently positively selected across all study areas. In contrast, red deer consumption increased with its relative availability and was more frequent in males, particularly during winter, indicating context-dependent flexibility in prey use. Non-ungulate prey contributed only marginally to the diet, and we found little evidence that lynx age, social status or population density substantially influenced prey selection. Our results demonstrate that Carpathian lynx remain strongly specialized on roe deer while retaining capacity to exploit alternative ungulate prey under specific ecological conditions. These findings improve our understanding of predator–prey interactions in a key European lynx population and provide an important scientific basis for conservation and management of lynx and its prey. Our integrated approach and findings also provide an ecological benchmark for anticipating predator–prey relationships as lynx recover across their former range through natural recolonization, reinforcement and reintroduction.

articles.title: Ecological context supports image-based fungal species recognition in citizen-science observations
articles.abstract: Citizen-science initiatives generate large numbers of image-supported fungal observations that can contribute to biodiversity recording, but their scientific value depends partly on reliable species identification. Recognition from field photographs is challenged by variable imaging conditions, a long-tailed species-frequency distribution, and visual similarity, while ecological descriptors recorded with the same observations provide context unavailable to image-only models. We examined whether habitat, substrate, and month improve fungal species recognition and compared matched strategies for incorporating these fields. Using Danish Fungi 2024-Mini (36,393 images from 20,618 observations of 182 species), we developed the Multi-scale Ecological Fusion Network (MEF-Net), which combines pooled multi-scale ConvNeXt descriptors with ecological descriptors through direct fusion and bounded channel recalibration. At an input resolution of 224 × 224 pixels, MEF-Net achieved mean Top-1 accuracy, Top-3 accuracy, and Macro-F1 values of 72.21%, 88.35%, and 61.68%, respectively, across five independent runs, a 5.51-percentage-point increase in Macro-F1 over the matched image-only ConvNeXt-Base model. At 384 × 384 pixels, mean Macro-F1 was 63.72%, 4.21 percentage points higher than the matched image-only model. These overall gains reflected the combined contributions of the multi-scale visual representation and ecological-context integration. Habitat produced the largest mean gain among the individual fields, whereas using all three fields jointly produced the best metadata-aware result. In the controlled strategy comparison, ecological conditioning of the pooled visual descriptors achieved the highest mean performance, while direct concatenation and calibrated Bayesian Late Fusion also improved upon the matched multi-scale image-only reference. MEF-Net achieved higher Macro-F1 across rare, medium-frequency, and frequent species, with the largest difference in the rare group. These findings indicate that ecological observation context can complement image evidence and support candidate ranking within human-validated fungal biodiversity-recording workflows.

articles.title: Seasonal shifts in phthalate ester composition and ecological risks along the Mudanjiang River–Jingpo Lake continuum
articles.abstract: Phthalate esters (PAEs) are widespread contaminants in freshwater ecosystems, yet how temporal shifts in congener composition relate to environmental gradients and ecological-risk patterns remains poorly understood in connected river–lake systems. In this study, 16 PAEs were investigated in 36 surface-water samples collected from 12 sites along the Mudanjiang River–Jingpo Lake system during spring, summer, and autumn 2024. Water-quality conditions and surrounding landscape pressures were also examined to evaluate the environmental context of PAE variation. Thirteen PAEs were detected, with Σ16PAEs concentrations ranging from 210.90 to 852.11 ng L−1 and averaging 513.35 ± 144.86 ng L−1. DBP was the predominant congener, accounting for 31.9% of Σ16PAEs, whereas DNP showed the highest detection frequency (86.1%). Σ16PAEs concentrations were highest in summer. The congener profile shifted from DBP dominance in spring and summer to a more even composition of DNP, DNPP, DPhP, and DNOP in autumn. PAE composition was associated with water-quality and landscape gradients, indicating that contaminant profiles varied across the observed environmental conditions. Σ16PAEs concentrations were positively associated with cumulative fish risk, but concentration dominance did not correspond directly to congener-specific risk contribution. DBP dominated the PAE burden, whereas DPhP contributed most strongly to fish risk. Non-priority PAEs also contributed substantially to both mixture composition and ecological risk. These results show that ecological-risk patterns in connected freshwater systems are shaped not only by total contaminant burden but also by temporal changes in mixture composition and environmental context. Considering congener-specific composition, non-priority contaminants, and multiple environmental pressures may therefore improve ecological-risk assessment and monitoring of river–lake ecosystems.

articles.title: End-of-Life Care for People Who Are Incarcerated—Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We appreciate the response to our article by Ms Ofori-Darko and Dr McClelland and agree wholeheartedly that the definition of palliative care for incarcerated patients should be comprehensive and match the community standard. This standard includes all evidence-based interventions that palliate symptoms during serious, life-limiting illness. We also agree that short-course or single-fraction regimens of radiation therapy may be indicated for incarcerated patients with serious illness who may face additional barriers to longer-duration treatments. Other palliative treatments may also include some forms of chemotherapy, immunotherapy, antibiotics, blood transfusions, and diuresis. Some treatments may lose palliative effectiveness over time and thus be stopped as a person transitions to hospice care.

articles.title: Etiologies: Seeking Causation in Medicine and Poetry
articles.abstract: One of the most central animating questions in medicine is “What is the cause?” Clinicians assiduously seek the diagnosis of a patient’s perplexing symptoms or probe what pathophysiology underlies the disease. Poetry is similarly engaged in a quest for knowing and by its enlarging of the field of inquiry as to the deepest roots of human suffering, it is complementary to, and thus useful in, medical practice. In the poem “Etiology,” medical language (“neoplastic transformation,” “terminology”) is placed beside unscientific explanatory systems (“feng shui,” “fortune stick[s]”), suggesting that illness may arise from several causal worlds at once. A malignancy may be cellular, environmental, familial, cultural, and even spiritual, depending on the kind of history being taken and by whom. “[A]bbreviations and poor penmanship” evokes the insufficiency patients may feel when their illness is summarily translated into clinical shorthand or technical jargon; poetry re-expands the diagnostic arena, restoring texture and richness to causation (“…white rice you relish/is it incense you burnt for your parents, black/on your fingertips blooming dust on the wall”). The poem’s cascading interrogatives become like a differential diagnosis, its syntax and persistent rhetorical questioning resembling good clinical reasoning. Yet the poem tolerates uncertainty, without discounting rigor. In the end, “Etiology” does not oppose medicine’s pursuit of an explanation, but rather amplifies it: “is it the blood you own, now rushing back to you again?” it concludes without really concluding, helping us understand that merely naming or owning is never the end of our questions.

articles.title: Intravenous Vitamin C and Mortality and Organ Dysfunction in Severe Burn Injury
articles.abstract: To the Editor We read with interest the article from the recent VICTORY trial that reported increased mortality in patients with severe burns who were randomized to 4-day administration of vitamin C vs placebo. The rationale for vitamin C administration was the massive release of oxygen free radicals following severe burns. However, the median time to discharge alive from the intensive care unit was 42.5 days in the placebo group, suggesting that a 4-day course of vitamin C may have been too short to affect outcomes. Notably, 2 previous randomized clinical trials in critically ill patients reported that abrupt discontinuation of a 4-day course of vitamin C was associated with increased mortality.

articles.title: Intravenous Vitamin C and Mortality and Organ Dysfunction in Severe Burn Injury—Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We thank Dr Hemilä and Ms Chalker for their interest in our VICTORY trial. They propose that the increased mortality in the vitamin C group reflected a rebound effect following abrupt discontinuation of therapy after 96 hours, rather than a direct effect of the drug itself. While one can never definitively rule out that different timing or dosing of a treatment could result in different outcomes, based on a post hoc analysis of the precise timing of treatment and subsequent mortality, we do not believe the VICTORY study provides evidence to suggest that the higher mortality rate observed in the vitamin C group was due to its abrupt termination.

Results demonstrated that the highly motivated DPP cohort derived significant benefit from the original intervention’s 16 individualized, hour-long health coaching sessions during 6 months, reinforced by monthly group and individualized follow-up meetings during the next 1.5 years. However, when the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention later assumed management of the program, this staff-intensive individualized coaching was eliminated for budgetary efficiency, altering a motivationally core feature of the intervention.

articles.title: Lifestyle and Metformin Interventions and Risk of Multimorbidity in Individuals With Prediabetes—In Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We thank Dr McCarthy and colleagues for their letter about our study, which demonstrated less multimorbidity among persons with prediabetes who underwent a lifestyle intervention. They raise the central implementation challenge of maintaining the essential components of an intervention that ensure its proven effectiveness while making necessary adaptations for real-world application. Incorporating new scientific findings that offer potentially short-term benefits must be done cautiously to avoid undermining the intervention’s long-term outcomes. We appreciate recent advances in pharmacotherapy, nutrition, and gut microbiome science and the evolving understanding of disease prevention. Although contemporary science has expanded available treatment modalities, lifestyle interventions continue to serve as a cornerstone of public health strategies for chronic disease prevention, with the behavior modification strategies to address energy balance remaining a core principle.

articles.title: Neuroprotective Therapy for Acute Ischemic Stroke
articles.abstract: A remarkable era in acute ischemic stroke care is now coming to a close—the period of the “reperfusion revolution.” Over the past few decades, pharmacological and mechanical flow restoration therapies became steadily more effective. By restoring blood flow and terminating the ischemic period, reperfusion salvages those cerebral tissues not yet irreversibly injured. However, the reperfusion strategy in acute stroke care is now reaching its limits. Current endovascular thrombectomy approaches reopen over 85% of occluded arteries, leaving little scope for further advance. And successful reperfusion treatment alone clearly only partially solves the therapeutic challenge. Among patients with ischemic stroke due to large-vessel occlusion who receive endovascular thrombectomy, more than two-thirds nevertheless have a disabled final outcome. Restoring blood flow yields incomplete recoveries because some irreversible injury accrues before recanalization can be achieved and additional injury is generated by reperfusion itself. To fully eradicate stroke-related disability, complementary therapies are needed, including: bridging neuroprotection agents, which allow brain cells to tolerate ischemia until reperfusion is attained; reperfusion neuroprotection agents, which avert reperfusion injury; and neuroreparative agents, which promote postinjury reorganization of neurons and synapses.

articles.abstract: There is little question that the American language was derived mainly from the English by the colonists who settled the eastern seaboard. articles.title: Boundary density predicts catalyst-layer utilization in membrane-electrode assemblies
articles.abstract: Catalyst layers in membrane-electrode assemblies are often underutilized, limiting the efficiency of electrochemical devices. This work identifies the mechanism that localizes reaction near the boundaries between contacted and non-contacted regions of the catalyst layer. Based on this insight, boundary density is introduced as a geometric descriptor of the porous-transport-layer/catalyst-layer interface and a predictor of catalyst-layer utilization.

articles.title: Behavioural plasticity in snowshoe hares reflects predator recognition but not camouflage mismatch
articles.abstract: Researchers conducted field experiments with both winter‐white and winter‐brown snowshoe hares in the Oregon Cascades to assess how these sympatric colour morphs adjust their behaviour to escape terrestrial and avian predators. While hares did not adjust their behaviour when mismatched, the researchers documented a specific technique for avoiding hawks. Abstract Shifts in predator–prey interactions in response to environmental change can affect population dynamics and community structure, but have received relatively little attention in the climate change literature. Seasonally colour‐moulting species face increased predation risk when winter‐white individuals experience camouflage mismatch in snowless conditions. While hares (genus Lepus) exhibit behavioural plasticity to reduce predation risk in other contexts, hares in populations of winter‐white individuals have demonstrated limited capacity to adjust behaviour to mitigate mismatch or its consequences. Little is known about antipredator behaviour in polymorphic populations of sympatric polyphenic winter‐white and invariant winter‐brown individuals that experience contrasting camouflage mismatch across seasons. We examined escape behaviours in a polymorphic population of snowshoe hares (Lepus americanus) including both winter‐white and winter‐brown individuals. In field experiments, we assessed plasticity in escape behaviour in response to predator type and camouflage mismatch. Using 224 measurements of concealment and flight initiation distance in 74 wild hares, we tested whether escape behaviour varied with colour morph and camouflage mismatch. We also quantified discrete escape decisions (flight, vegetation refuge or subsurface refuge) by 29 individual hares in 52 predator escape trials to test for behavioural responses to predator type (humans, hunting dogs Canis familiaris and goshawks Astur atricapillus). Linear mixed‐effects models revealed no relationship between colour morph or mismatch and either concealment or flight initiation distance, suggesting a lack of behavioural adjustment to reduce mismatch‐associated predation risk in both winter‐white and winter‐brown hares. In contrast, hares exhibited strong behavioural plasticity in response to predator type, using subsurface refuges more often in trials with avian, but not terrestrial predators. The odds of subsurface refuge use were 14.3 times higher in trials with goshawks compared to human trials. Collectively, we find that winter‐white and winter‐brown snowshoe hares exhibit predator recognition and corresponding behavioural plasticity to different predator types, but not to camouflage mismatch, highlighting limits to behavioural plasticity in response to climate‐driven increases in predation risk.

articles.title: Immediate challenges and costs of elevational shifts in mountain lizards evaluated through reciprocal translocation
articles.abstract: Our study provides experimental evidence of the immediate physiological and behavioural costs faced by mountain lizards moving to higher elevations, integrating home range data with behavioural, physiological and body condition metrics to offer new insights into how elevation shifts constrain species' ability to cope with rapid climate change. Abstract Animals are known to move across elevations in response to climate change. However, the costs and challenges associated with these movements are not well‐understood. Therefore, it is essential to explore how animals respond to a novel elevation to comprehensively understand their strategies for mitigating the effects of climate change. In this study, we examined fitness‐related traits of the high‐elevation toad‐headed agama (Phrynocephalus vlangalii) on the Qinghai–Xizang Plateau following elevational translocation using a 2 (population origins) × 2 (elevational environments) design. We switched lizards between habitats at 2600 and 3600‐m elevation, assessing their body condition, home ranges, behavioural thermoregulation, thermal physiology, locomotor performance and resting metabolic rates at both native and translocation sites. We found that the lizards from the 3600 m a.s.l. performed equally well at both 2600‐m and 3600‐m elevation sites. In contrast, the lizards from the 2600 m a.s.l. performed well at their native elevation but struggled at the 3600‐m site, indicated by decreased accuracy and effectiveness of thermoregulation, reduced locomotion and resting metabolic rates, shrunken home ranges and a significant decline in body condition. Our study highlights the challenges and costs animals face when moving to higher elevations to escape the impacts of climate change. It also emphasizes the importance of assessing immediate responses to novel environments when evaluating the efficacy of dispersal as a buffering strategy against climate change.

Migrant frugivorous birds assist plants in tracking climate change: A first spatially explicit approach
articles.abstract: Migrant frugivorous birds can partially assist fleshy‐fruited plants fruiting during spring migration to track climate change, although severe warming and land‐cover alteration may strongly constrain seed‐dispersal range filling. Importantly, range filling capacity is uneven across plant species: differences in climatically suitable ranges and intrinsic traits, particularly seed size, influence the ability of species to reach newly suitable areas. Interspecific variation in plant capacity to redistribute could be crucial for the reassembly of ecological communities under climate change. Abstract Climate change is causing biodiversity redistributions towards cooler areas at an unprecedented velocity. Plants are an essential component of terrestrial ecosystems that primarily rely on seed dispersal to redistribute. Yet, most seed dispersal occurs over short distances (i.e. less than 1 km), which is insufficient to track ongoing climate change. Bird migration can support seed dispersal at longer distances. However, we lack spatially explicit estimations of seed dispersal by migratory birds towards future climatically suitable ranges of plants. Thereby, it remains unclear to what extent they can facilitate plant redistribution in the coming decades. We integrated spatially explicit, seed‐dispersal models with projections on plant climatic suitability using species distribution models. We simulated long‐distance dispersal of 14 fleshy‐fruited plant species across Europe during the northward spring migration of song thrushes (Turdus philomelos), an adequate model species given its abundance, migratory behaviour and key role as disperser of native European plants. Dispersal models were replicated under three global warming projections and three scenarios of dispersal sensitivity to land‐cover alteration. Plant climatically suitable ranges will shift northwards by 248–948 km under severe warming projections by the year 2090. We identified a strong negative effect of warmer climate projections and higher dispersal sensitivity to land‐cover alteration on seed‐dispersal range filling (i.e. the proportion of future climatically suitable area that is currently unsuitable and receives seed‐dispersal events). Seed‐dispersal range filling averaged 22.2% across species under severe warming and assuming no sensitivity to land‐cover alteration. We found substantial interspecific variation in seed‐dispersal range filling, which was higher in species with lesser changes in their potential ranges and with smaller seeds dispersed over longer distances. Synthesis. Migrant frugivorous birds can partially assist fleshy‐fruited plants fruiting during spring migration to track climate change, although severe warming and land‐cover alteration may strongly constrain seed‐dispersal range filling. Importantly, range filling capacity is uneven across plant species: differences in climatically suitable ranges and intrinsic traits, particularly seed size, influence the ability of species to reach newly suitable areas. Interspecific variation in plant capacity to redistribute could be crucial for the reassembly of ecological communities under climate change. Resumen El cambio climático está provocando una redistribución global de la biodiversidad hacia áreas más frías a una velocidad sin precedentes. Las plantas son un componente clave de los ecosistemas terrestres y dependen principalmente de la dispersión de sus semillas para redistribuirse. Sin embargo, la mayoría de las semillas son dispersadas a distancias cortas (inferiores a un kilómetro), lo que resulta insuficiente para seguir el ritmo del cambio climático actual. La migración de las aves puede favorecer la dispersión de semillas a mayores distancias. No obstante, carecemos de estimaciones espacialmente explícitas de la dispersión de semillas por aves migratorias hacia las regiones que presentarán condiciones climáticas adecuadas en el futuro.…

Multiscale insights into zinc metal anodes for aqueous zinc ion batteries
articles.abstract: This review examines how the intrinsic properties of zinc metal influence its stability in aqueous electrolytes, highlighting multiscale correlations among morphology, microstructure, electronic structure, and electrochemical behavior. It outlines emerging strategies and future directions for enhancing zinc reversibility and utilization toward practical aqueous zinc ion batteries.

articles.title: Ultraviolet exciton-polaritons in silver phenylthiolate
articles.abstract: Hybridization of light and excitons can change how materials absorb and emit light, but achieving this in the ultraviolet remains challenging. We show that a layered silver phenylthiolate forms hybrid light-matter states in simple mirror structures. This material expands the options for controlling ultraviolet light and provides a foundation for exploring future light sources and light-driven chemistry.

articles.title: pamflow: An open‐source workflow for simplified passive acoustic monitoring data analysis
articles.abstract: Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) is becoming increasingly popular but has not yet achieved its full potential due to the lack of cohesive workflows for processing large volumes of data. Although several tools support specific components of PAM analysis and some platforms integrate multiple functionalities, researchers often still rely on combinations of software and custom scripts to move from raw recordings to standardized and reproducible outputs. We present pamflow, an open‐source workflow for PAM built on Python and the robust Kedro framework, which provides a command‐line interface that enables execution of complete pipelines through standardized configuration files. It prioritizes broad usability through three key traits: open access, low computational requirements and streamlined workflow configuration. These features are intended to facilitate adoption in biodiverse but geographically isolated contexts, where limited budgets, constrained computational resources and scarce programming training are common. The tool is designed for users with varying levels of technical experience. While its use requires basic familiarity with command‐line tools and configuration files, its modular design also enables experienced programmers to extend, adapt, and customize workflows for research‐specific purposes. To illustrate our framework, we present the outputs obtained from a sampling conducted in Colombian Amazonia to support community forestry initiatives. The project was co‐led by the Humboldt Institute and the Foundation for Conservation and Sustainable Development (FCDS). The sampling was carried out through a participatory approach. Fourteen families and a local school participated in the installation of 38 recorders, capturing over 720 h of the local soundscape. Framed within open‐science principles, pamflow promotes data and technological sovereignty. In particular, we expect pamflow to (a) increase the adoption of PAM by providing an inclusive and open‐source solution that supports complete data processing workflows; (b) increase the number of biodiversity records reported from PAM projects to global biodiversity platforms such as GBIF; and (c) improve collaboration and data sharing among research groups and institutions by transforming input data into a globally accepted data standard. Resumen El Monitoreo Acústico Pasivo (PAM, por sus siglas en inglés) está adquiriendo una creciente popularidad, pero aún no ha alcanzado todo su potencial debido a la falta de flujos de trabajo integrados para procesar grandes volúmenes de datos. Aunque existen herramientas que apoyan componentes específicos del análisis acústico y algunas plataformas integran múltiples funcionalidades, los investigadores todavía suelen depender de combinaciones de programas y scripts personalizados para transformar grabaciones en bruto en resultados estandarizados y reproducibles. Presentamos pamflow, un flujo de trabajo de código abierto para monitoreo acústico pasivo desarrollado en Python y basado en Kedro. La herramienta proporciona una interfaz de línea de comandos que permite ejecutar procesos completos mediante archivos de configuración estandarizados. Su diseño prioriza la accesibilidad a través de tres características principales: licencia abierta, bajos requerimientos computacionales y una configuración simplificada del procesamiento de datos. Estas características buscan facilitar su adopción en lugares de alta biodiversidad pero geográficamente aislados, donde son comunes los presupuestos limitados, las restricciones en infraestructura computacional y las escasas oportunidades de formación en programación. La herramienta está diseñada para usuarios con distintos niveles de experiencia técnica aunque su uso requiera familiaridad básica con la línea de comandos y archivos de configuración.…

articles.title: The C-terminal tail of the RBR E3 ligase RNF14 defines branched K6/K48 polyubiquitin specificity in ribosomal quality control
articles.abstract: Trevelyan et al. report that the E3 ubiquitin ligase RNF14 forms branched K6/K48 polyubiquitin and identify RNF14’s C-terminal tail as a critical component for its chain-type and branching activity. This work opens research avenues for branched K6/K48 ubiquitin in ribosomal quality control and the biological functions of branched ubiquitin.

articles.title: Demographic Recovery Masks Matrilineal Lineage Compression in the Chinese Alligator
articles.abstract: Demographic recovery is often used as evidence of conservation success, yet population growth does not necessarily restore maternally inherited genetic diversity. The Critically Endangered Chinese alligator (Alligator sinensis) has increased numerically under captive breeding, but contemporary maternal‐lineage representation remains poorly resolved. Here, we assembled control‐region‐excluded mitochondrial genomes from 356 individuals across six groups (F1, F2, F3, F4, wild and ZJ). Mitochondrial nucleotide diversity was extremely low (π = 5.41 × 10−5). Although 16 haplotypes were detected, 88.2% of sampled individuals carried only two dominant haplotypes, revealing pronounced matrilineal lineage compression. These findings show that demographic recovery can coexist with restricted contemporary representation of maternal lineages, underscoring that census growth alone does not constitute matrilineal recovery. Monitoring maternal lineages alongside nuclear genomic variation and census size can therefore provide a more complete assessment of conservation recovery.

articles.title: Life Cycle Complexity Shapes Parasite Sharing Amongst Migratory and Resident Hosts
articles.abstract: Migratory animals are potentially important parasite dispersers. However, understanding the impact of host migration on parasite distributions is challenging because variation in parasite life histories can mediate dispersal potential. Furthermore, studies of parasite dispersal via host migration often compare parasites in different species of migrant and resident hosts, despite differences in host phylogeny, ecology, and exposure history, which can complicate ascertaining the impact of migration. The Tasmanian population of silvereye Zosterops lateralis lateralis) exhibits partial migration. Some members of the population overwinter on the Australian mainland, where they co‐occur with residents of another silvereye subspecies (Z. l. cornwalli). Utilising targeted PCR, metabarcoding and high‐throughput sequencing, we characterise a range of parasite genera from blood and faecal samples in Tasmanian resident, migrant and mainland resident birds. Greater parasite richness was documented in migrant individuals, possibly reflecting exposure to varied parasite faunas at stopovers or during overwintering. The increased richness was primarily driven by parasites with simple life cycles. Reduced sharing of parasites with complex life cycles amongst migratory and resident host populations may be explained by ecological constraints in establishing transmission, such as vector or secondary host availability. Our study exemplifies the utility of molecular methods for characterising multi‐parasite systems and makes use of a single host species to provide insights on patterns of parasite distributions that result from migratory movements. Knowing how parasite life histories constrain or promote dispersal via regular host migration will be essential for predicting future patterns of pathogen dispersal under climate change and shifting migratory regimes.

A Scalable Nonsuperconducting Tunnel Junction Technology
articles.abstract: Tunnel junctions are essential for various technologies ranging from classical microelectronics to quantum information and cryogenic electronics. Aluminum and its oxide (AlOx) have long dominated cryogenic and quantum tunnel junction applications for their excellent material quality and superconductivity. However, some applications require junctions to remain normal conducting, either as standalone components or integrated with superconducting circuitry. Magnetic fields, impurity doping, or proximity effects can suppress superconductivity, but often pose challenges for scalability and integration. Here, we present a CMOS-compatible normal conducting tunnel junction platform using TiW alloy electrodes and AlOx tunnel barriers, achieving high yield and uniformity through wafer-scale fabrication. As a cryogenic use-case, the wafers incorporate junction arrays designed for Coulomb blockade thermometry, confirming reliable normal conducting state performance down to 20 mK. These results demonstrate a scalable and integrable normal conducting junction technology, supporting its use in cryogenic, quantum, and nanoelectronic systems, including hybrid superconducting-normal metal circuits.

articles.title: Correction to “Physical- and Chemical-Dually ROS-Responsive Nano-in-Gel Platforms with Sequential Release of OX40 Agonist and PD-1 Inhibitor for Augmented Combination Immunotherapy”
Direct Visualization of Na,K-ATPase Clustering by 3D DNA-PAINT MINFLUX Nanoscopy
articles.abstract: The sodium–potassium pump (Na,K-ATPase) is an essential plasma-membrane transporter that consumes 20%–30% of cellular energy, and up to approximately 50% in the kidneys. Whether it assembles into defined oligomers in its native membrane has been debated for decades. Resolving this question demands imaging precision at molecular length scales. Here, we combine 3D MINFLUX nanoscopy with DNA-PAINT to map EGFP-tagged Na,K-ATPase α1 and β1 subunits in mammalian cells with 3–5 nm localization precision. We introduce two point-cloud analysis tools: a data-driven algorithm that assigns localizations to the apical or basal membrane, removing trans-membrane artifacts, and a sequential nearest-neighbor analysis that estimates oligomer stoichiometry without structural priors. Both subunits show preferential nearest-neighbor distances of approximately 7 nm, direct evidence of dimerization, and are further organized into nanoclusters of approximately 7 to 12 molecules. These results provide direct structural evidence of Na,K-ATPase self-assembly and a framework for quantifying membrane-protein clustering at single-molecule resolution.

articles.title: Gold Nanoclusters with Wavelike Chiral Lattices Interact with Outer Membrane Protein BamA to Kill Gram-Negative Bacteria through the Screw-in Effect
articles.abstract: Resistance threatens to render antibiotics ineffective, which is posing a threat to global public health. Innovative strategies against drug-resistant bacteria are urgent. The outer membrane protein BamA, a hollow barrel with a pore of 2–4 nm, is a unique and essential structure in Gram-negative bacteria. We prepared chiral 3 nm gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) targeting BamA, exhibiting enantiomer-dependent antibacterial activity against drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The AuNCs with right-handed wavelike lattices (D-AuNCs) preferentially interacted with BamA through the screw-in effect, creating pores in the cell wall and resulting in bacterial death. P. aeruginosa was still susceptible to D-AuNCs due to their excellent antibiofilm activity even after 20 successive passages. D-AuNCs were applied to P. aeruginosa-infected skin wounds in mice, achieving superior wound healing compared to levofloxacin. Our work documented that chiral nanoclusters targeting BamA can efficiently kill P. aeruginosa through the screw-in effect, providing an innovative strategy to combat Gram-negative bacteria.

articles.title: Highly Reliable Sub-2-nm Hafnia Ferroelectric Tunnel Junction via All-Atomic Layer Deposition Growth
articles.abstract: Hafnia-based ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for post-Moore memories, offering fast, low-power polarization switching and compatibility with the technological maturity of the hafnia platform. Yet nanometer-scale barrier thinning, while desirable for higher speed and energy efficiency, introduces a critical reliability bottleneck. Here, we develop an all-atomic layer deposition (ALD) process for reliable sub-2 nm hafnia FTJs through precise growth and low-roughness interface formation. The resulting devices combine sub-2-V operation with a high breakdown field of ∼12.1 MV/cm, while maintaining stable ferroelectric switching through 1010 cycles without breakdown. Further interface optimization extends the resistance-state endurance toward 1010 cycles, reconciling aggressive barrier scaling with reliable device operation. We further exploit 4-bit nonvolatile multilevel operation to demonstrate an in-memory computing simulation with 95.78% accuracy. By combining the advantages of scaling with high reliability, this work advances hafnia-based FTJs toward high-speed, energy-efficient, and robust memory applications.

articles.title: Intrinsically Moiré-Patterned Two-Dimensional Polymorphic Networks for Modulated Charge Order and Proximity Superconductivity
articles.abstract: Moiré superlattices provide a versatile route to engineering correlated electronic and topological states in van der Waals heterostructures, yet their use to organize structural polymorphism and phase-selective charge, magnetic, and superconducting states within a single two-dimensional material remains elusive. Here, we report modulated charge order and proximity superconductivity in an intrinsically moiré-patterned 1T/1T′ polymorphic network of monolayer VTe2 grown epitaxially on superconducting NbSe2. Scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy and first-principles calculations show that in situ annealing of twist-moiré VTe2/NbSe2 creates alternating 1T and 1T′ domains. The origin of the selective 1T-to-1T′ conversion is due to the moiré-induced anisotropic strain. This moiré-registered network hosts phase-specific short-range charge orders: 4 × 4 in 1T and 3 × 3 in 1T′. In the proximity-superconducting regime, spatially modulated in-gap bound states and suppressed coherence peaks reveal phase-dependent magnetic pair breaking. This work establishes intrinsically moiré-patterned polymorphism as a route to programmable two-dimensional quantum materials.

articles.title: Machine-Learning-Accelerated Metallene Stabilization from High-Throughput Sandwich Modeling
articles.abstract: Metallenes have appealing properties, but stabilizing them in a monolayer phase poses synthesis challenges. A recent experiment showed that the van der Waals squeezing method can stabilize certain metallenes in a MoS2 sandwich. This pioneering work motivates systematic studies, but such studies are experimentally impractical, while first-principles modeling remains prohibitive. Here, using universal machine-learning interatomic potentials, we constructed 1620 metallene sandwich heterostructures containing 6 different sandwich layers and 45 metals. We performed phonon calculations, which revealed 1208 dynamically stable structures and narrowed them to 331 after structural filtering. We found that Se-based transition-metal dichalcogenides stabilize metallenes effectively. Specifically, hexagonal and buckled hexagonal crystal lattices exhibit the greatest stability. We further evaluated the thermal stability of selected heterostructures with density-functional-theory molecular dynamics simulations at room temperature. By uncovering the physical and chemical factors that govern metallenes stabilization, our results provide systematic insights to guide and accelerate synthesis for future applications.

articles.title: Optical Resonance Tuning of Single Polystyrene Microspheres Using the Phase-Change Material In3SbTe2 as a Switchable Mirror
articles.abstract: Dielectric nanoparticles and microparticles show rich optical responses due to their electric and magnetic multipolar Mie modes and low losses. These optical resonances can be modified via the particle size, shape, and dielectric environment. Here we tune the infrared multipolar Mie resonances of dielectric polystyrene microspheres using the plasmonic phase-change material In3SbTe2 (IST). IST exhibits a phase change between a dielectric amorphous phase and a crystalline phase that is metallic in the infrared. We show that a reversibly switchable particle-on-mirror geometry can be created by locally switching the IST under the polystyrene microspheres. Measuring the light-scattering spectra of single polystyrene microspheres before and after crystallization and reamorphization, we observe huge shifts of the resonance wavelength, e.g., from 5.2 to 8.9 μm and back for 6 μm diameter spheres. Our work is a first step toward a controlled tuning of multipolar Mie modes of various particles using reprogrammable IST mirror structures.

articles.title: Quasi-One-Dimensional Topological Band Structure and Van Hove Singularities in Monolayer TaIrTe4 from Laser μ-ARPES
articles.abstract: Recent transport experiments reported a quantum spin Hall insulator phase in monolayer 1T-TaIrTe4 gated away from charge neutrality. This phase is not predicted by band structure calculations and has been attributed to an electronic instability induced by strong correlations at a putative Van Hove singularity. Here, we investigate the electronic structure of exfoliated monolayer 1T-TaIrTe4 using microfocus laser angle resolved photoemission. We find a strongly anisotropic band structure susceptible to density wave instabilities. Our data further reveal a saddle point singularity in the density of states. However, we find that the saddle point lies at a density for which linear transport experiments found no anomalies. Moreover, the quasiparticle line widths suggest weak electron correlations only. This points to a secondary role of Van Hove singularities and electron correlations in the transport phase diagram of monolayer 1T-TaIrTe4.

articles.title: Single-Twinned Seed-Mediated Synthesis of Au Right Bipyramids for Uniform Near-Field Focusing
articles.abstract: Noble metal nanoparticles with sharp edges and corners, such as triangles, tetrahedrons, bipyramids, etc., support superior plasmonic field enhancement for enhanced spectroscopy. However, high-yield synthesis of gold right bipyramids (Au RBPs) with sharp tips has remained limited because they have a single-twinned (ST) crystal structure whose growth pathway is hard to control. Here, we report the seed-mediated growth of Au RBPs using ST seeds, achieving a yield exceeding 70% by moderately increasing the size of these seeds. Au RBPs with sizes from 34 to 94 nm and controlled corner sharpness are achieved through the regulation of seed and bromide amounts. Uniform and strong near-field enhancement is generated in the Au RBPs-on-mirror configuration, which outperforms the well-established nanocube-on-mirror configuration in Raman enhancement. This work highlights the merits of ST seed-mediated growth for anisotropic nanocrystals and their potentials in plasmonic near-field focusing.

articles.title: Tungsten–Carbon Nanohelix Arrays by Helium-Ion Direct Writing: Geometry-Dependent Circular-Polarization Response in the Visible
articles.abstract: 3D nanohelices provide a direct route to control light–matter interactions with circular polarization at the nanoscale. Here, we report periodic arrays of W–C nanohelices fabricated by He+ focused-ion-beam-induced deposition (FIBID), combining direct-write 3D growth with high spatial resolution and W-rich deposits (∼65 at. % W). Two arrays with the same lateral geometry were fabricated while varying only the vertical pitch, corresponding to helical ratios HR ≈ 1 and HR ≈ 2. Transmittance measurements under circularly polarized light reveal a clear geometry-dependent response. The compact nanohelices (HR ≈ 1) show a larger circular-polarization-dependent transmission contrast (g ≈ 0.17, θ ≈ 2.35°), moderate transmittance (∼30–50%), and a sign inversion near 600 nm. The larger-pitch helices (HR ≈ 2) show higher transmittance (∼35–100%) with a weaker but stable response (g ≈ 0.13, θ ≈ 1.60°). Qualitative simulations reproduce the main spectral trends and support distinct optical responses of the two pitch geometries.

articles.title: Twin gas rings observed around a white dwarf
articles.abstract: The observation of quadruple-peaked emission lines from WD J1328−1450 suggests that there are two separate, concentric rings of gas around the white dwarf. This finding could indicate the presence of two asteroid-sized to Pluto-sized planetary bodies that have survived disruption by the gravitational forces of the white dwarf.

articles.title: Benchmarking mechanistic credibility in electrocatalysis through data-driven evaluation
articles.abstract: The performance of electrocatalytic reactions has rapidly advanced in recent years, yet there remain numerous controversies in the underlying mechanistic understanding of these systems. This Perspective proposes a framework for rating the strength of evidence and cross-community validation of mechanistic claims for the most-studied electrocatalytic reactions.

articles.title: Programming golden triple helices
articles.abstract: Chiral helical superstructures provide a platform to control photon polarization and electron spin, yet they are challenging to construct using inorganic materials. Now, homochiral triple helices that exhibit pronounced circularly polarized luminescence have been assembled from gold by tailoring the steric and stereochemical properties of supporting chiral cyclic ligands.

articles.abstract: Soft polymer coatings spontaneously rearrange on nanosphere surfaces to form directional bonds, unlocking an alternative route to delicate nanoparticle superlattices.

articles.title: A novel candidate biomarker for detecting premalignant and early ovarian cancer
articles.abstract: New data suggest that the long noncoding RNA known as Tu-Stroma represents a promising new circulating biomarker for the detection of ovarian cancer at premalignant and early stages, for which sensitive screening methods currently are lacking.

articles.title: Blood-based RNA biomarker for the early detection of ovarian cancer
articles.abstract: Flower-Win/Lose signaling underlies a tumor–host fitness conflict in ovarian cancer, in which tumor-derived exosomal Tu-stroma reduces the fitness of surrounding host cells, favoring tumor expansion within host tissues. High-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC), the most prevalent histotype of epithelial ovarian cancer and leading cause of ovarian-cancer-related mortality, arises from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC), a noninvasive precursor typically identifiable only by histopathologic examination of excised fallopian tube tissue. Here we evaluated Tu-stroma, a tumor-associated long noncoding RNA enriched in serum extracellular vesicles (EVs), as a circulating biomarker in STIC and early-stage HGSC, representing the earliest histopathologically defined phases of disease. Tu-stroma was quantified in serum EVs from 506 individuals with histologically normal adnexa, benign-adnexal lesions, isolated STIC and HGSC across International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stages I–IV. Normalized EV Tu-stroma ΔCT values were elevated in STIC (n = 43) and HGSC (n = 232) versus controls (n = 143) and benign-adnexal lesions (n = 88), including premenopausal women (controls = 57, benign = 34, STIC = 32, HGSC = 88). In paired receiver operating characteristic analyses, Tu-stroma showed higher discrimination than cancer antigen 125 (CA125) for STIC versus controls (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.99 versus 0.59, P < 0.001) and benign-adnexal masses (0.99 versus 0.31, P < 0.001), and for HGSC versus controls (AUC = 0.99 versus 0.96, P = 0.001) and benign-adnexal masses (0.98 versus 0.84, P < 0.001). Tu-stroma showed no systematic elevation across inflammatory or physiologic comparators (n = 116) or nonovarian malignancies (n = 160), each assessed against healthy controls (n = 100), supporting disease-context specificity. Modeled risk-enriched contexts yielded predictive values compatible with intended-use populations. These findings identify Tu-stroma as a candidate EV-RNA marker associated with pre-invasive and early HGSC biology. Prospective evaluation in consecutively enrolled real-world cohorts is required to validate diagnostic performance, predictive value and clinical utility. Tested in a cohort of 506 individuals, the RNA-based biomarker of microenvironment fitness Tu-stroma shows high performance in discriminating early-stage ovarian cancer from benign lesions, outperforming CA125.

articles.title: Next-generation KRAS G12C inhibitor improves survival in lung cancer
articles.abstract: Phase 3 trial data show that the next-generation KRAS G12C inhibitor divarasib leads to longer progression-free survival than the first-generation inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib in patients with non–small-cell lung cancer.

articles.abstract: BCR-MERFISH enables tracking of plasma cell clones by combining V gene-specific detection with spatial transcriptomics.

articles.title: Information formatting in neuronal populations predicts differential functional contributions to behavior
articles.abstract: Using experiments in monkeys and modeling, the authors demonstrate that the formatting of population information predicts the contribution of different brain areas to behavior.

articles.title: 3D models to capture and perturb tumour heterogeneity in vitro
articles.abstract: Tumour heterogeneity drives disease progression yet remains difficult to capture in experimental systems. In this Review, Fomina and McGuigan discuss how emerging 3D tumour models, including organoids, assembloids and microfluidic platforms, recapitulate distinct dimensions of tumour heterogeneity to enable mechanistic studies of cancer biology and drug response. They also outline future directions for improving model fidelity, scalability and translational utility.

articles.title: Activated TILs are restricted by iron availability in pancreatic cancer
articles.abstract: A preprint by Schoenfeld et al. investigates the relationship between iron restriction and the function of tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

articles.title: The small intestine microbiome: composition, host interactions and therapeutic potential
articles.abstract: In this Review, Britton and colleagues examine the composition of the small intestinal microbiome and its interactions with the host, highlighting emerging insights into its roles in physiology and health. They also discuss the challenges of studying this understudied microbial community and its potential as a source of future microbial therapeutics.

articles.title: Honour McCann
Speciation and biogeographical history in the European Alpine System: the radiation of Ranunculus sect. Euromontani (Ranunculaceae)
articles.abstract: Biogeographical analysis of species of Ranunculus sect. Euromontani and related taxa. Summary High mountain systems provide manifold preconditions for allopatric and sympatric speciation. We hypothesize that allopatric speciation due to geographical isolation of mountain chains, and sympatric speciation via allopolyploidy played major roles for a radiation within Ranunculus sect. Euromontani within the European Alpine System (EAS). We used target enrichment of 1249 nuclear gene loci on 81 samples for phylogenomics, biogeographical analysis, species delimitation, SNPs for genetic structure and NeighborNet analysis, flow cytometry for ploidy determination, and morphometrics for selected species pairs. We also included type material. The core R. sect. Euromontani comprises 12 monophyletic species, most of them (sub)endemic to one mountain system. The section originated probably from a widespread lineage and diversified 1.39 million years ago. Founder‐event speciation was the most common mechanism; only one species (Ranunculus montanus) originated likely in situ via allopolyploidy. In the West Carpathians, the new species Ranunculus tatrimontanus was recognized as different from Ranunculus gruinalis (= Ranunculus pseudomontanus) in the South Carpathians. In the Pyrenees, clinal variation suggested inclusion of Ranunculus ruscinonensis into Ranunculus gouanii. Peripatric speciation during the Pleistocene was the predominant mechanism for this geographical/climatic radiation in the EAS, whereas sympatric speciation via allopolyploidy happened only in the Alps.

articles.title: The evolutionary history of brackish specialization from marine ancestry in the seagrass Ruppia sinensis
articles.abstract: Conceptual model of waterfowl‐mediated long‐distance dispersal in Ruppia sinensis. Summary Ruppia sinensis, a unique seagrass species that originated in the marine environment yet successfully colonized extreme inland habitats, offers a rare window onto how plants cope with major habitat shifts and clarifies the mechanisms of adaptive evolution during marine‐to‐brackish transitions. We assembled a chromosome‐level genome, conducted comparative phylogenomic analyses, assessed salinity tolerance through physiological experiments, and analyzed whole‐genome resequencing data from 103 individuals representing 19 coastal and inland populations. R. sinensis falls in the core seagrass PRC (Posidoniaceae, Ruppiaceae, and Cymodoceaceae) clade with a Ruppiaceae‐specific whole‐genome duplication yet has lost tolerance to full‐strength seawater and is an obligate brackish specialist. Coastal and inland lineages diverged c. 25 000 yr ago; dramatic sea‐level fluctuations since the Last Glacial Period repeatedly displaced coastal populations, causing reductions in effective population size, loss of genetic diversity, and elevated genetic load. Inland populations persisted in saline‐lake refugia and retain nearly twice the genetic diversity. The marine‐to‐brackish shift is an evolutionary trade‐off rather than passive habitat tracking, with inland saline lakes serving as refugia that preserved diversity. Such shifts may be a recurrent adaptive strategy in seagrass evolution, and these diverse inland populations warrant conservation priority under climate change.

articles.title: Emergent-Gravity Hall Effect from Quantum Geometry
articles.abstract: We theoretically propose a Hall effect driven by effective gravitational fields arising from quantum geometry. We identify four mechanisms for this “emergent-gravity Hall effect”: real-space gravity, momentum-space gravity, gravitational anomalous velocity, and gravitational Lorentz force, all of w…

articles.title: Kovacs Memory Effect in a Thin Granular Layer: Experimental Evidence and Its Physical Origin
articles.abstract: A memory phenomenon known as the anomalous Kovacs effect has been experimentally observed in a granular system for the first time.

articles.title: Many-Body-Driven Ultrafast Exciton Relaxation Enabled by Phonon-Activated Coulomb Coupling
articles.abstract: Coulomb interactions underpin the formation of excitons, yet their role in nonequilibrium exciton relaxation has remained unexplored. Here, using first-principles real-time Bethe-Salpeter formalism combined with nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, we study the ultrafast relaxation of optically bright excitons into momentum-dark states in monolayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$. It is demonstrated that Coulomb-mediated couplings between excitonic configurations are strictly forbidden in a perfect lattice but are dynamically activated by phonon excitation. This activation enables the long-range Coulomb interaction to dominate exciton relaxation, reshaping kinetic pathways and surpassing conventional electron-phonon scattering. These findings reveal a new paradigm in which Coulomb interactions actively govern nonequilibrium exciton kinetics, while phonons act as a dynamical switch that unlocks many-body relaxation channels.

articles.title: Nonequilibrium Equation of State for a Turbulent 2D Bose Gas
articles.abstract: Nonequilibrium equations of state can provide an effective thermodynamiclike description of far-from-equilibrium systems. We experimentally construct such an equation for a direct energy cascade in a turbulent two-dimensional Bose gas. Our homogeneous gas is continuously driven on a large length scale and, with matching dissipation on a small length scale, exhibits a nonthermal but stationary power-law momentum distribution. Our equation of state links the cascade amplitude with the underlying scale-invariant energy flux, and can, for different drive strengths, gas densities, and interaction strengths, be recast into a universal power-law form using scalings consistent with the Gross-Pitaevskii model.

articles.title: Page Curve for Local-Operator Entanglement from Free Probability
articles.abstract: The local-operator entanglement (LOE) measures the classical simulability of a Heisenberg operator and is conjectured to witness many-body chaos in locally interacting systems. Using tools from free probability, we analytically compute its asymptotic value for Haar random dynamics for all R\'enyi indices. We find that to the first two orders in large dimension, for traceless operators it exactly reproduces the Page curve for random states. In contrast to higher-order out-of-time-ordered correlators, which depend on more complex operator correlations via free cumulants, the leading-order LOE is independent of the initial operator. We detail exactly how these higher-order correlations are encoded in the coefficients of the finite-size corrections. Guided by our Haar result, we argue that the long-time value of the LOE entropies in chaotic systems is robust: they depend only on a simple subsector of the hierarchy of correlations encoded by the full eigenstate thermalization hypothesis. Our results therefore provide a conceptual boundary between operator simulability and higher-order scrambling diagnostics.

articles.title: Rapid Cavity-Based Midcircuit Measurement and Feedforward in a Neutral Atom Array
articles.abstract: Measuring part of a quantum system in the midst of its evolution and acting on the result in real time is essential for numerous quantum information protocols. Neutral-atom arrays are a leading platform for quantum information processing, but their midcircuit measurement-and-feedforward cycle times have remained slow, typically exceeding 1 ms. Here, we demonstrate fast midcircuit measurement and real-time feedforward in an array of atomic qubits coupled to a high-finesse optical cavity. Local light shifts tune individual data qubits out of resonance with the cavity, shielding their coherence, while a near-resonant probe drives a selected qubit whose emission is collected with Purcell enhancement. Midcircuit measurements of four qubits with subpercent infidelity reduce the coherence of a fifth unmeasured data qubit by less than 2%. We implement real-time feedforward to correct measurement-induced phase shifts and to realize an adaptive circuit for optimal quantum-state discrimination and conditional state preparation. Our approach reduces the measurement-and-feedforward cycle time to below $100\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{\ensuremath{\mu}}\mathrm{s}$ and establishes optical cavities as a route to fast control of neutral-atom quantum systems.

articles.title: Observation of Topological Berry Phases with a Single Phonon in an Ion Microtrap Array
articles.abstract: Trapping individual ions in a highly programmable two-dimensional microtrap array and precisely controlling their motion allows for the direct observation of a topological Berry phase.
