articles.title: [Comment] A digital intervention to strengthening parenting in Tanzania
articles.abstract: Preventing children's exposure to hardship, trauma, and abuse in childhood is a global public health priority. This exposure is associated with a substantial burden of disease and is one of the most important risk factors for experience and perpetration of violence against women, with all the entailed health consequences.1–3 Over recent years, research on and development of interventions to prevent child abuse and neglect through strengthening of parenting have intensified. Reviews show considerable success with some interventions, including in llow-income and middle-income countries (LMICs), but also signal room for further work developing scalable, affordable interventions.

articles.title: [Review] Reframing disease elimination: an update from the Lancet Commission on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with increasing global burden driven by population growth and ageing, persistent harmful exposures, and substantial health inequities. The Lancet Commission on COPD articulated an ambitious vision for disease elimination with prevention, early detection, and intervention. This Review revisits that vision, assesses progress since 2022, and calls for a broader commitment to lifelong lung health as an update of the Commission.

articles.title: Safety, tolerability, and efficacy of bepranemab in people living with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial
articles.abstract: BackgroundTau aggregation is a defining feature of the pathophysiology of Alzheimer's disease and an appealing therapeutic target, yet tau-directed antibodies tested to date-primarily targeting N-terminal epitopes-have failed to slow tau progression or cognitive decline. Bepranemab targets the tau mid-region, predicted in cell-based assays to more effectively block neuron-to-neuron tau spread than anti-tau antibodies targeting the N-terminus. We aimed to investigate the safety and efficacy of bepranemab in slowing progression of tau pathology and clinical decline in people with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease.MethodsThis double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial recruited participants across 101 outpatient sites in Europe (eight countries), Canada, and the USA. Participants (aged 50-80 years) with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease were randomly assigned 1:1:1 (using an interactive response system) to intravenous bepranemab 45 mg/kg, bepranemab 90 mg/kg, or placebo (every 4 weeks for 76 weeks), stratified by diagnosis, apolipoprotein E ɛ4 carrier status, and symptomatic treatment use. The primary endpoint was change from baseline to week 80 in Clinical Dementia Rating Scale-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) total score. Efficacy was assessed in the full analysis set (ie, all randomly assigned participants who received at least a partial dose of trial medication and had at least one valid post-baseline clinic visit and efficacy assessment). Safety was assessed in all randomly assigned participants who received at least a partial dose of the trial medication. No imputation was done for missing data. The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04867616) and is complete.FindingsBetween Aug 24, 2021, and Oct 25, 2022, 466 participants were randomly assigned to bepranemab 45 mg/kg (n=154), bepranemab 90 mg/kg (n=155), or placebo (n=157) at 85 sites. Median age was 72·0 years (IQR 66·0-76·0), 259 (56%) were female, and 207 (44%) were male. In total, 460 participants were included in the full analysis set: bepranemab 45 mg/kg (n=152), bepranemab 90 mg/kg (n=152), and placebo (n=156). Least-squares mean CDR-SB total score change from baseline to week 80 was 2·15 in the bepranemab 90 mg/kg group and 1·85 in the bepranemab 45 mg/kg group versus 1·81 in the placebo group, with differences versus placebo of 0·34 (95% CI -0·09 to 0·78, p=0·12; 80% CI 0·06 to 0·63) for the bepranemab 90 mg/kg group and 0·04 (-0·40 to 0·47, p=0·87; -0·25 to 0·32) for the bepranemab 45 mg/kg group. Frequency of treatment-emergent adverse events with bepranemab was similar to the placebo group (139 [91%] with bepranemab 45 mg/kg, 140 [91%] with bepranemab 90 mg/kg, and 142 [90%] with placebo); no treatment-related neuroinflammatory safety signals were identified clinically or on brain MRI scans. There were adverse events leading to death in four (1%) participants in the combined bepranemab groups and six (4%) in the placebo group; none were considered related to the trial treatment.InterpretationTreatment with bepranemab was associated with an acceptable safety profile. However, the primary endpoint was not met. Hypothesis-generating differences favouring bepranemab in tau PET and 14-item Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale should be tested prospectively in trials powered for tau PET outcomes and stratified by baseline tau burden and apolipoprotein E ɛ4 status.FundingUCB.

articles.title: Genomically matched targeted therapy for ovarian clear cell carcinoma
Risovalisib for PIK3CA-mutated recurrent or persistent ovarian clear cell carcinoma: a single-arm, multicentre, phase 2 trial
articles.abstract: BackgroundOvarian clear cell carcinoma is a rare but aggressive and biologically distinct subtype of ovarian cancer, in which PIK3CA mutations are common. Advanced ovarian clear cell carcinoma is very difficult to treat, and after failure of platinum-based chemotherapy, therapeutic options are limited. We aimed to evaluate the anti-tumour activity and safety of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, for treatment of patients with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma.MethodsWe conducted a single-arm, phase 2 trial of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, in 27 centres in China and 12 centres in Japan. Eligible participants were adult patients (aged 18 years or older, with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1) with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma and one to three lines of previous systemic anti-tumour treatment. Risovalisib was given orally at 40 mg daily in 21-day cycles until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or other protocol-defined reasons for discontinuation. The primary endpoint was objective response rate assessed by blinded independent review committee (BIRC) using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (version 1.1), among all treated patients with a confirmed PIK3CA hotspot mutation and baseline tumour assessments with measurable lesions per BIRC (efficacy analysis set). The primary endpoint was considered met if the lower 95% CI was greater than 8%. Safety analyses were performed in all patients who received at least one dose of risovalisib (safety analysis set). The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05043922) and is ongoing but no longer recruiting patients.FindingsBetween Oct 6, 2021, and Jan 31, 2024, 93 patients were enrolled and received risovalisib. The median age was 49 years (IQR 43-58), all patients were female, 52 (56%) were from Japan, 41 (44%) were from China, and 63 (68%) had two or more previous lines of therapy. The median duration of follow-up was 14·5 months (IQR 8·6-18·3). The objective response rate was 29 (35% [95% CI 25-46]) of 84 patients in the efficacy analysis set. The most commonly reported grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events in 93 patients were rash (30 [32%]), hyperglycaemia (28 [30%]), and decreased weight (7 [8%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 36 (39%) patients, the most common being rash (eight [9%]), pneumonitis (six [6%]), and decreased appetite (four [4%]). There were no treatment-related deaths.InterpretationThese results support risovalisib as a potential novel treatment option for PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma, a rare yet lethal cancer in dire need of additional treatment options. Combination strategies including risovalisib could also be explored to further increase efficacy observed in this study.FundingHaihe Biopharma.

articles.title: Immune evasion in cancer dormancy and metastatic reactivation
articles.abstract: Metastatic dormancy reflects a dynamic immune–tumor equilibrium in which disseminated tumor cells, either as individual cells or multicellular ecosystems, may persist for years before relapse. Recent studies show that dormant cells evade elimination through spatial and numerical rarity, insufficient immune effectors, suppression of innate immune signaling and inflammasome pathways, and adaptation to local immune niches. Inflammatory stress leading to tissue remodeling dampens immune restraint and promotes metastatic outgrowth. Emerging spatial and single-cell genomic and evolutionary profiling approaches now offer a potential path toward defining dormant disseminated tumor cell states and niches directly in patients. Here, we review mechanisms of tumor–immune interactions in dormant cells or incipient metastases and discuss how these could be leveraged to develop strategies to eradicate minimal residual disease, restore immune surveillance, and prevent inflammatory reawakening. We also provide a perspective on how predominantly murine studies in this field may be extended to studying the dormancy paradigm directly in patients.

articles.title: A Margin Perspective on LoRA: Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting and Adapter Merging (MaLoRA)
articles.abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is the de facto method for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large neural networks, achieving strong task adaptation with minimal trainable parameters and low optimization cost. Beyond this efficiency, practitioners have observed two striking properties: \textit{robustness to catastrophic forgetting} and the ability to \textit{merge independently trained adapters} into a single model that performs competitively across multiple tasks. These properties are central to continual and multi-task learning, yet remain poorly understood. In this work, we provide a theoretical explanation through a unified \textit{margin-based perspective}. We analyze LoRA in multiclass linear classification under a near-orthogonal task regime with $\ell_2$-regularization, and characterize the optimal LoRA adapter across regularization regimes. Our analysis shows that, in an intermediate regime of regularization parameters, the optimal adapter aligns with the \emph{max-margin solution} on the fine-tuning data. Building on this characterization, we derive two key consequences. First, we obtain closed-form expressions for the margins on pre-training and fine-tuning data, revealing a precise margin trade-off: the regularization parameter controls the balance between retention and adaptation. Second, we analyze adapter merging, proving that merged models achieve positive margin on each task and deriving optimal mixing coefficients that balance margins across tasks and maximize the margin over their union. These results lead to a simple, training-free merging rule, which we term \textit{margin-based LoRA merging} (MaLoRA). Experiments on modern architectures and real datasets validate our theoretical predictions, showing that MaLoRA matches or outperforms several adapter-merging baselines across a range of vision and language classification tasks.

articles.title: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance
articles.abstract: Cross-validation estimates predictive performance by repeatedly splitting the data into training and validation sets, fitting the model on the first and evaluating it on the second. Every observation influences the estimate in two roles, through its own evaluation when it is held out and through the models it helps fit when it trains. The random splits determine its weight in each role. From this representation, we prove an exact finite-sample identity for the variance of the cross-validated estimate. For a given splitting scheme with a common training set size, the variance is a function of these weights, with constants of the model, the metric, and the population. It covers metrics averaged over observations, such as mean squared error, and over case--control pairs, such as the AUC. The identity shows which schemes to use. The variance decomposes into sampling variance, which depends only on the training size, and variance due to the random fold splitting, which arises when the weights change from one draw of the splits to the next. K-fold cross-validation, whose weights are equal across observations by design, is therefore variance optimal at first order; Monte Carlo and bootstrap cross-validation are not. The first-order variance of K-fold does not depend on K, and under reasonable conditions on the model leave-one-out has the smallest variance of any K-fold scheme. For the AUC the same holds for leave-pair-out, which evaluates every case--control pair. Finally, we show the cross-validated estimate is asymptotically normal with the identity's full variance. Together, these results provide a general theoretical foundation for inference on cross-validated performance and establish principles for selecting variance-optimal cross-validation designs.

articles.title: A Hardware-Trained Generative Quantum Eigensolver for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization of Organotin Hydroxides up to 70 Qubits
articles.abstract: Quantum hardware can provide feedback for training circuit generators beyond the reach of exact classical simulation. We train generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) policies, transformers conditioned on molecular descriptors, to generate the state-preparation circuits for sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD). Training runs first on a noiseless simulator and then with the IBM Heron processor ibm_kobe inside the loop, at 46 and 70 qubits ($1.2 \times 10^8$ shots for the four main training runs). A classical CCSD(T) reference energy of the training molecules enters only an admission gate and two auxiliary reward terms. During hardware training, a reward penalty prevents collapse to circuits that sample only the Hartree-Fock determinant. Policies trained on transition-metal complexes are applied without retraining to Sn(OH)$_3$-Me and its hydrates, minimal models of organotin photoresists for extreme-ultraviolet lithography, from 32 to 70 qubits. After one round of hardware sampling, followed by classical ranking and recovery of the cached counts with the molecular Hamiltonian and no further QPU calls, 27 of 28 runs at 46-70 qubits are within 15 mHa of the density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) reference (median 4.5 mHa), and in all eight runs with an untrained control the trained policy is more accurate. At 56-70 qubits the selected circuits use 34-72 times fewer two-qubit gates than the local unitary cluster Jastrow (LUCJ) circuit transpiled for the same device. These results demonstrate that circuit generators can be trained with quantum hardware at 70 qubits.

articles.title: A New Computational Model for the Spin-Free Sum-of-Squares Energy Bounds of Electronic Hamiltonian
articles.abstract: Optimizing spin-free sum-of-squares (SOS) energy bounds for electronic Hamiltonians leads to semidefinite programs whose expanded size grows rapidly with the orbital dimension. We derive an exact reformulation of an established spin-free SOS model as a convex quadratic problem over a single symmetric matrix constrained between zero and the identity. Explicit recovery maps connect feasible quadratic-program iterates to certificates in the original SOS formulation, and identify the Frank--Wolfe gap with the separation between recovered primal and dual objectives. We implement the quadratic action through GPU-accelerated Coulomb contractions and solve the reformulated problem using a cached implementation of fully corrective Frank--Wolfe, referred to here as the dimension-reduced simplicial method (DRSM) that caches operator products and optimizes convex-combination weights in a small corrective quadratic program. Numerical experiments cover 65 FCIDUMP models, molecular geometries, and regular hydrogen rings, including original-coordinate recovery checks on nine instances and comparisons with FISTA and a boundary-point SDP solver. On eight H100 GPUs, a cold-start calculation for C$_{720}$ with 10,080 spatial orbitals reaches a freshly recomputed Frank--Wolfe gap of $8.82\times10^{-9}$ hartree in 5.02 hours. Full-space hydrogen-ring calculations reach 10,000 orbitals, with cyclic reduction providing further computational savings. These results show how exact reformulation, data structure exploitation and reuse of Coulomb actions make optimization of the selected large-scale SOS relaxation practical.

articles.title: A fast two-phase model for PEM fuel cell impedance
articles.abstract: We report a physics-based matrix model for PEM fuel cell impedance that takes into account liquid water transients in the cathode catalyst layer (CCL). This model is an extension of our previous single-phase matrix model for functionally graded CCLs. The solution to the boundary-value problem for the perturbation amplitudes is constructed from basic solutions to the respective Cauchy problem with constant coefficients on numerical cells. The single-phase model employed analytical solutions to this problem. Here, for a larger system of ODEs, the analytical solution does not exist and we used spectral decomposition of the ODE system matrix to obtain the basic solutions numerically. Our impedance model is two orders of magnitude faster than a model based on a standard, general-purpose boundary-value solver. Fitting the matrix model to an experimental spectrum takes about a minute on a laptop. The developed matrix method can be used to numerically solve high-order linear boundary-value problems with variable coefficients.

articles.title: ANTIOCH-VS: From Sequence to Hits with Modular, Open-Source Ensemble Virtual Screening
articles.abstract: Structure-based virtual screening needs a receptor conformation that fits the ligand class, but for most targets no ligand-bound crystal is available -- and a single predicted model or an apo structure often misses the binding-competent state. We present ANTIOCH-VS, an open-source framework that runs an entire in silico screening campaign, from a protein sequence to a ranked shortlist of candidate binders, as one plug-and-play workflow. It first builds a conformational ensemble by reduced-MSA subsampling with ColabFold, then uses AlphaFold2-RAVE (AF2RAVE) -- short molecular-dynamics simulations with State Predictive Information Bottleneck analysis -- to pick out docking-ready, Boltzmann-weighted metastable states. It then detects the binding pocket, prepares receptors and ligands, docks the library across the ensemble with DOCK6 or AutoDock Vina, builds a consensus ranking, and triages the top hits by physics-based metadynamics (CTMD). We benchmark it on two very different targets, JAK2 kinase and ADRB2 GPCR, using their DUD-E benchmark sets of known binders and property-matched decoys. Starting from sequence alone -- no ligand-bound crystal, no manual intervention -- the AF2RAVE ensembles gave top-20 shortlists strongly enriched for true binders: a 20% hit rate for JAK2 and 60% for ADRB2 (random ~1-2%), on par with ligand-bound crystals and, for the kinase, above single AF2 models and an apo crystal. The full pipeline runs end to end on a workstation or HPC from a single command, or each module can be run on its own with user-supplied inputs. ANTIOCH-VS is freely available at https://github.com/tiwarylab/antioch-vs

articles.title: Classical phase unwrapping enables large-time-step unitary quantum Krylov subspace diagonalization
articles.abstract: For computing molecular energies on early fault-tolerant hardware, unitary quantum Krylov subspace diagonalization (UQKSD) avoids both the deep circuits of quantum phase estimation and the Pauli-term sampling of variational methods by extracting the energies from a projected real-time propagator. At a small time step $τ$, nearly linearly dependent Krylov vectors make the overlap matrix ill-conditioned. Our tests at fixed total evolution time show that additional Krylov vectors then add no accuracy, while the thresholded energy becomes increasingly sensitive to the choice of cutoff. A larger time step improves the conditioning and reduces the Krylov dimension $M$ needed for a target accuracy, but the energies are then known only modulo $2π/τ$. We present Classical Unwrapping for Resolving Eigenvalues (CURE-QKSD), a classical post-processing method that leaves the UQKSD circuits and generalized eigenvalue problem unchanged and recovers the missing multiples of $2π/τ$ from phase-consistency landscapes of one or, when needed, two UQKSD runs. In noiseless tests on six molecules with 12--20 qubits, all 28 targeted energies are recovered in their aliased regimes with final errors of at most $1.1\times10^{-7}$~Ha. Under Gaussian noise with $σ=10^{-4}$, the median error of the ground or first excited state reaches chemical accuracy at large aliased time steps with $M=20$--$65$, whereas uncorrected principal-branch energies are off by $0.7$--$115$~Ha. CURE-QKSD therefore makes aliased time steps usable for UQKSD calculations with smaller, better-conditioned Krylov bases.

articles.title: Correlation-Consistent Gaussian Basis Sets for Periodic Solids. I. Hydrogen and p-block Elements from Boron to Chlorine
articles.abstract: We present the cc-pVXZ-s series (X = D, T, and Q) of correlation-consistent Gaussian basis sets for solids, covering hydrogen and the p-block elements from boron to chlorine. The series includes basis sets of consistent quality for the all-electron potential and for various pseudopotentials and effective core potentials commonly used in periodic calculations. Our design combines Dunning's construction of the molecular cc-pVXZ series with a revised material-constrained atomic optimization (MCAO) algorithm for improved numerical performance. MCAO regularizes standard atomic optimization to suppress overly diffuse basis functions and ensure numerical stability in a set of reference solids. Benchmarks against standard cc-pVXZ calculations for molecules and plane-wave calculations for periodic solids establish the accuracy, transferability, and numerical stability of cc-pVXZ-s in both mean-field and correlated wavefunction calculations and confirm reliable extrapolation to the complete-basis-set (CBS) limit. As an application, we use all-electron cc-pVXZ-s to compute basis-set-converged lattice constants, bulk moduli, and cohesive energies for 7 bulk semiconductors. Using a hierarchy of correlated wavefunction methods up to local coupled cluster with singles, doubles, and perturbative triples [CCSD(T)], we find systematic convergence toward experimental bulk moduli and cohesive energies, while a small systematic overestimation of lattice constants suggests potential limitations in the approximate finite-size treatment. This work provides a foundation for the further development of systematically convergent Gaussian basis sets for periodic calculations.

articles.title: Coupled Cluster Simulations of Vibrational Circular Dichroism Spectra
articles.abstract: We report the first simulations of vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) spectra at the coupled-cluster level of theory. Using a generalization of Stephens's pioneering magnetic-field perturbation theory framework for the magnetic-dipole vibrational transition moment to biorthonormal wave functions, we have derived generalized expressions for the corresponding atomic axial tensors (AATs) and velocity-gauge atomic polar tensors that collapse to Stephens's expressions for real, Hermitian states. Adapting these exact-state expressions to coupled-cluster left- and right-hand biorthonormal wave functions and using our recently developed density-based formulation yields compact equations that involve only perturbed ground-state amplitudes, as well as unperturbed and perturbed, unrelaxed one-electron densities; two-electron-density contributions vanish exactly. We have validated the resulting AATs by comparison with our previous configuration interaction formulation for a two-electron system, size-intensivity tests, a translational sum rule, and other tests. Simulated VCD spectra for (S)-3-chloro-1-butyne at the coupled-cluster singles and doubles level with the correlation-consistent triple-zeta basis set reveal significant discrepancies between length and velocity gauges. We find that the addition of large-exponent functions via a core-valence basis set for the Hartree--Fock reference components yields substantially improved gauge invariance without the need for gauge-including atomic orbitals.

articles.title: Memory-gated transient anomalous transport of quasiparticles out of equilibrium
articles.abstract: Anomalous transport is ubiquitous across condensed matter, materials science, and biophysics. Yet, in far-from-equilibrium settings, what determines when, how much, and in which direction transport departs from diffusion remains a fundamental open question. By adopting the dispersive Holstein model of small polarons as representative of a wide class of dissipative systems, we show that a signed bath memory time governs the direction and the strength of the transient departure, and that when it vanishes, diffusion emerges without an asymptotic delay. Tuning the dissipative environment from resonant to off-resonant with the carrier density of states, transport turns from subdiffusion to superdiffusion as the memory time changes sign. Microscopically, we trace this memory effect to a competition between polaron formation and coherent polaron motion. These findings establish a unified memory-based description of transient anomalous transport, offering a path to control nonequilibrium quasiparticle flow through environmental tuning.

articles.title: SOPPA with the Complete Third-Order A Matrix: Singlet Excitation Energies
articles.abstract: We present the derivation and implementation of the complete third-order correction of the A matrix in the M{\o}ller-Plesset polarization propagator approximation. A new contribution to the third-order correction was discovered and we thus report the first results obtained with the complete third-order A matrix. The performance of the Second Order Polarization Propagator Approximation including the third order A matrix (SOPPA-A3) method in calculation of vertical excitation energies was assessed by comparing to the reference methods FCI or CCSDTQP. A substantial improvement over SOPPA was found with the inclusion of the complete third-order A matrix as the SOPPA-A3 method yields excitation energies of a quality comparable to CC2. The inclusion of the new contribution results in a change in the individual excitation energies of varying size and direction depending on the molecule and state and the contribution should therefore be included for a formally complete third-order treatment of the A matrix.

articles.title: Stochastic Discrete Variable Representation: Tensor Network Eigenstates on General Potential Energy Surfaces
articles.abstract: Tensor network states such as tree tensor network states (TTNS) or matrix product states (MPS) allow very compact representations of high-dimensional wave functions. Using them efficiently relies on a compact representation of the Hamiltonian, and many methods are limited to the sum-of-products (SOP) form. General potential energy surfaces (PESs) do not have this form. To overcome this issue, a stochastic discrete variable representation (SDVR) is presented. The matrix elements of the potential operator in the node-local basis are estimated stochastically by importance sampling of grid configurations. The estimator of the matrix elements is unbiased, and the PES is only evaluated pointwise. The variance is reduced by representing parts of the potential with a 2-mode representation and only sampling the remainder. Sampling noise biases the eigenvalues. A noise-control scheme mitigates this bias. Final energies are obtained from an unbiased variational Monte Carlo estimator. The method is demonstrated by calculating vibrational states of CH3 (6D) and acetonitrile (12D), as well as the zero-point vibrational energy of uracil (30D). For all three systems, the energies agree with the exact references to sub-wavenumber accuracy.

articles.title: An infrared divacancy color center in bulk hexagonal diamond for quantum communication
articles.abstract: Intrinsic color centers are investigated in bulk hexagonal diamond as potential emitters for fiber-based quantum communication. Hybrid density functional theory and constrained-occupation delta SCF calculations identify five carbon-vacancy and divacancy configurations with stable optical excited states. A comparison of their radiative and nonradiative properties within a three-point configuration-coordinate model identifies the positively charged axial divacancy, VVa1+, as the most promising candidate. It exhibits the highest calculated zero-phonon-line (ZPL) emission rate of 43.9 MHz and ZPL quantum efficiency of 11.8% among the five candidates. Its weak structural relaxation yields a Huang-Rhys factor of 0.395, while a multimode photoluminescence calculation gives a Debye-Waller factor of 69.37%, indicating a dominant zero-phonon contribution. The predicted ZPL at 0.603 eV (2057.3 nm) also has the smallest photon-energy separation from the 1310 and 1550 nm telecom targets among the candidates. These results identify VVa1+ as a promising intrinsic color center for fiber-based quantum communication, with quantum frequency upconversion offering a route from its strong infrared ZPL to the telecom O and C bands.

articles.title: Design of Self-Folding Origami Architectures for Biomedical Implants: A Finite Element Simulation Framework
articles.abstract: Minimally invasive brain implants require compact deployment geometries and controlled shape transformation for delivery through confined vessels. Origami-inspired structures enable large shape changes from compact to tailored deployed configurations, but implementation at microscale dimensions remains challenging, as conventional designs rely on predefined mountain and valley folds that become increasingly difficult to fabricate and assemble as unit-cell size is reduced to meet clinical requirements. To address this, we propose a self-folding methodology based on thermally induced stresses in thin-film bimetallic composites. Pairing the shape memory alloy Nitinol (NiTi) with molybdenum or stainless steel (SS316L) exploits their differing thermal expansion coefficients to generate localized hinge bending, enabling deterministic, autonomous folding into prescribed mountain and valley configurations. Using finite element simulations, we systematically optimize hinge length, layer thickness, width, and shape, identifying a hinge geometry achieving a ~50% reduction in unit-cell dimensions relative to previously reported designs. Integration into a complete waterbomb origami unit cell confirms that the strip-level folding mechanism scales to produce coordinated, self-folding deformation across the tessellated structure. These results demonstrate the feasibility of stress-induced, self-folding thin-film origami architectures built from clinically established biomaterials, providing a scalable design framework for next-generation, active neurovascular implants with integrated sensing and monitoring functionality.

articles.title: Direction-Selective Anomalous Quantum Transport from Saddle-like Topological Surface States Coupled to an Electronic Instability in YbSb$_{2}$
articles.abstract: We report direction-selective anomalous quantum transport in epitaxial YbSb$_{2}$ thin films associated with an interplay between anisotropic topological surface states and an electronic instability. Quantum oscillations reveal a quasi-two-dimensional orbit with a non-trivial Berry phase and Dirac-like dispersion, observable for current along the $a$-axis but absent along the orthogonal in-plane $c$-axis. Together with first-principles calculations, these observations support its assignment to a saddle-like topological surface state. Its oscillation amplitude exhibits a field-dependent, non-monotonic temperature evolution that departs from conventional Lifshitz-Kosevich behavior. Raman and coherent phonon spectroscopy reveal additional low-temperature modes consistent with a density-wave instability. Their pronounced polarization anisotropy and colossal field-induced Raman enhancement suggest a strongly anisotropic, field-enhanced electronic susceptibility associated with the density-wave modes. Our findings point to dynamical coupling between anisotropic topological surface states and a field-responsive density-wave instability as a route to direction-selective anomalous quantum transport.

articles.title: Elastic Landau states as martensite nuclei in austenite
articles.abstract: In this article, we investigate the geometric closure of austenite--martensite interfaces. Classical compatibility conditions permit stress-free interfaces between the two phases: the condition $λ_2 = 1$ admits planar interfaces, whereas the cofactor conditions additionally admit curved interfaces. However, neither, guarantees the geometric closure of these interfaces. We identify two-parameter families of martensitic deformations that overcome this limitation and enable the formation of closed, stress-free martensite nuclei embedded in an austenite matrix. A main result is the interpretation of the classical deformation modes of simple shear and pure shear as martensitic phase transformations. These correspond to cubic to monoclinic-II and cubic to orthorhombic transformations, respectively. The former naturally satisfies the \emph{extreme compatibility conditions}, which are stronger than the cofactor conditions, and gives rise to \emph{elastic Landau states}, a self-accommodating martensitic nuclei embedded in austenite. We show that these states can be assembled to form arbitrarily shaped, stress-free martensitic islands surrounded by austenite. Such states can arise even in conventional shape memory alloys that do not satisfy supercompatibility, provided hierarchical twinning produces an average deformation that is a simple shear. The theory provides a geometric mechanism for self-accommodation. Its predicted deformation gradients agree with those reconstructed from experimentally observed microstructures. This agreement suggests that these microstructures originate from simple shear.

articles.title: Electronic Origin of Contrasting Li and Na Clustering on Graphene
articles.abstract: The electrochemical performance of anode materials is often defined by the ability of metal ions (e.g., Li and Na) to be effectively stored within the host material over a specific range of chemical potentials. This is particularly true for adsorbed Li and Na atoms on carbon surfaces (e.g., graphite or pore surfaces in hard carbon), where the interplay between ionic and metallic bonding often takes place - while metal atoms act as ionic species, in a finite concentration limit, they tend to form metallic bonding when they approach each other. What makes the case special is that, despite similar chemical identities, Li and Na atoms exhibit distinct tendencies for cluster formation; for example, the formation of Li metallic clusters on a graphene surface is only thermodynamically favorable after reaching a finite metal-ion concentration. Motivated by this, herein, we use first-principles calculations on graphene to examine the electronic origin of Li and Na clustering. Specifically, we demonstrate that the separated adsorbed atoms donate electrons to graphene, shifting the Fermi level to higher energies; however, the formation of metal clusters can result in the formation of lower-energy orbitals that are specifically associated with metal-metal bonding, thus lowering the Fermi level (and hence total energies). Importantly, while the process is somewhat similar for Na and Li atoms, the energy levels of the newly formed metallic states govern the difference in metallic cluster formation between Li and Na.

articles.title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for higher-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
articles.abstract: The time to solution of an iterative solver depends on the number of iterations and the cost per iteration. This paper develops algorithms that reduce both for elliptic problems discretized with high-order continuous finite elements on distributed GPUs, implemented in a unified matrix-free code supporting CUDA, HIP and SYCL. A distributed direct fast-diagonalization (FD) Poisson solver provides exact solutions on tensor-product meshes with direction-wise grading and coefficients varying along one coordinate direction. Its tensor data stay distributed, moved between slab layouts by collective transposes or kept in place by a Schur-complement approach. It is also an exact coarse solver. A two-level hybrid Schwarz preconditioner with FD cell solves (HS-FD) is extended to 2:1 hanging-node octrees with exact local cell inverses, while a \(p\)-multigrid preconditioner with Chebyshev--Jacobi smoothing (CJ-\(p\)MG) resolves hanging-node constraints at every level within fused kernels. Both approaches exploit FP32, where cell shapes and coefficients allow, within an FP64 conjugate-gradient iteration, adaptively select replicated or distributed coarse levels, support block solves for multiple right-hand sides and determine all parameters from the operator without case-specific tuning. Comparisons with Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradients (Jacobi PCG), MFEM, nekRS and deal.II span uniform, graded and octree meshes, layered coefficients, and four applications across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs. The direct solver is two to three orders of magnitude faster than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes. HS-FD converges in 11 iterations for an octree generalized Poisson problem across 8 to 1024 MI250X graphics compute dies. The results guide solver selection by mesh structure and coefficients

articles.title: An Alignment Microscope for Imaging Rotational Wavepacket Dynamics
articles.abstract: We introduce a new method for encoding polarization-angle-dependent molecular alignment signals directly into the transverse spatial profile of a femtosecond laser beam. The approach employs a pump-probe setup in a common-path geometry. A radial-azimuthal polarization converter placed in the probe beam produces a doughnut-shaped beam whose local polarization varies continuously with azimuthal angle, thereby encoding the full range of linear polarization orientations from 0 to $2π$ within a single transverse beam profile. Consequently, the angular dependence of the molecular response can be recorded simultaneously rather than reconstructed through sequential measurements at different polarization angles. By varying only the pump-probe delay, this spatial encoding enables single-shot acquisition of the complete angular response at each delay and real-time visualization of the evolving molecular alignment pattern as the delay stage is scanned. This technique has enabled the experimental realization of an alignment microscope.

articles.title: Angle-Resolved Reflectance Measurements in the Vacuum Ultraviolet for Metallic Samples
articles.abstract: The light yield of noble-element scintillation detectors depends strongly on the reflective properties of detector materials in the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV), where optical measurements are scarce. For this reason, we built a custom rotary setup at IFIC, equipped with a monochromator and operated in a gaseous argon atmosphere, to perform angle-resolved reflectance measurements in the specular reflection plane. We describe the setup and its extensive characterization, together with the procedure used to measure the bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) of materials at various angles of incidence, for wavelengths from 128 to 500 nm, covering both the argon (128 nm) and xenon (175 nm) scintillation wavelengths. To illustrate the capabilities of the setup, we present results for rough aluminum and stainless-steel surfaces as reference materials. Fitting the measured angular profiles with the analytical GGX microfacet model allows us to extract the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index and the surface roughness parameter of each sample. These parameters are then used to extrapolate the in-plane measurements to the full hemisphere and from gaseous argon to liquid media, enabling the inference of the hemispherical reflectance in gaseous argon, liquid argon and liquid xenon.

articles.title: CV-TF-QKD
articles.abstract: We introduce a continuous-variable version of twin-field quantum key distribution, using independent Gaussian-modulated coherent states and an untrusted single-photon relay. Full-record reconciliation and a binary phase-disclosure protocol achieve nearly equal asymptotic key rates against collective attacks. At fixed weak input-referred excess noise per arm, both rates per relay use scale as $\sqrtη$, where $η$ is the end-to-end transmissivity. For phase disclosure, we establish composable security against general coherent attacks using a bounded test of preparation intensities and sign-parity complementarity. For specified apparatus parameters, finite-key calculations incorporating detector inefficiency, dark counts, phase fluctuations, and reference overhead predict rates exceeding the pure-loss and matched thermal-loss repeaterless bounds. These results extend the twin-field advantage to Gaussian-modulated continuous-variable quantum cryptography.

articles.title: Coherent-Dissipative Crossover of Quantum Synchronization
articles.abstract: Quantum synchronization in open systems can arise from both coherent interactions and collective dissipation, yet their interplay remains poorly understood. Here we develop a general framework for two quantum oscillators coupled through a fast mediator. Adiabatic elimination reveals two distinct synchronization channels, coherent exchange and collective dissipation, and yields an analytical description connecting dissipation and coherence-dominated regimes. We show that synchronization is governed by the joint balance of coherent coupling, dissipation, and reservoir-induced fluctuations, rather than by coherent coupling alone. Continuous monitoring of the shared output further converts reservoir information into a resource, substantially enhancing conditional synchronization, with the strongest gain near the coherent-dissipative crossover. These results establish a general mechanism for coherent-dissipative quantum synchronization and its measurement-enabled control in open quantum systems.

articles.title: Cross-Platform Benchmarking of GHZ-State Generation in Quantum Processors via Cloud Services
articles.abstract: Quantum computing has rapidly evolved into a diverse ecosystem of hardware platforms that differ in their underlying technologies and operational characteristics. Consequently, benchmarking has become essential for identifying the strengths of quantum processors, comparing their performance, and enabling informed decisions when selecting the most appropriate quantum computing platform for specific applications. In this work, we benchmark nine commercially accessible quantum processors from five vendors, spanning superconducting and trapped-ion technologies, using the multipartite entanglement benchmark from the QuSquare suite. All experiments were performed through remote cloud-access services, with the default compilation of each provider and without error mitigation, reflecting the performance experienced by end users. The benchmark estimates the fidelity of Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) states by direct fidelity estimation and searches for the largest GHZ state whose fidelity is compatible, within the statistical error, with the genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) threshold $F=1/2$. Our results reveal a substantial gap between the total number of physical qubits available on a processor and the size of the largest GHZ state passing the benchmark: the best superconducting processors reach $N^*=27$ and $N^*=24$ qubits, less than a quarter of their registers, whereas the 12-qubit trapped-ion processor passes with its full register. We further show that median calibration data are poor predictors of the benchmark outcome, and that the reported sizes depend strongly on the statistical decision rule: requiring certified GME reduces the number of devices that succeed at any tested size from nine to four. These results provide a baseline for future cross-platform benchmarking of quantum processors.

articles.title: Disorder-Induced Logarithmic Spreading and Localization of Quantum Fluctuations
articles.abstract: Disorder can localize quantum particles, even in the presence of interactions, but its influence on quantum fluctuations beyond mean--field dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the propagation of quantum fluctuations in weakly interacting disordered bosonic systems by comparing the Bose--Hubbard model with the Gross--Pitaevskii equation. We find that, in contrast to ballistic spreading in the disorder--free system, quantum fluctuations exhibit logarithmic spreading at intermediate times under both random and quasiperiodic disorder, before eventually saturating. The spreading rate decreases algebraically with increasing disorder strength, and this behavior persists across different particle numbers and extends to two dimensions. Using a time--dependent Bogoliubov--de Gennes framework, we identify the localized mean--field wavefunction as a time--dependent pairing background that generates quantum fluctuations. The exponential suppression of fluctuation--generation rates with distance provides a physical mechanism for the logarithmically advancing fluctuation front. Our results reveal a distinct regime of disorder--controlled quantum--fluctuation dynamics and establish disorder as a means of controlling their spreading.

articles.title: Dynamical GKP codes
articles.abstract: Dynamical codes protect quantum information with sequences of measurements, generalizing the stabilizer formalism of static codes. However, the dynamical formalism has been developed exclusively for qubit systems. While Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes are promising candidates for quantum computing that encode qubits in the continuous phase space of oscillators, no dynamical formalism has been developed for them. In this work, we bridge this gap and introduce dynamical GKP codes, combining continuous-variable lattice encodings with time-dependent translation measurement dynamics. To obtain the update rules and the distance of a given measurement sequence, we first generalize GKP codes to subsystem GKP codes using scaled symplectic lattices. Building on this structure, we adapt the ancestry, detector, and benign-error machinery originally developed for dynamical qubit codes. From this construction, we obtain a general and efficient method to compute the syndrome and distance of a dynamical GKP code from a persistent stabilizer lattice and a bounded inference window. We illustrate the framework with the example of the two-mode square-hexagonal Floquet GKP code. This code has reduced measurement weight compared to both the square and hexagonal GKP codes, while combining their set of logical gates, resulting in easier implementation of the full single-qubit Clifford group. Finally, we show that measurements with irrational symplectic overlap, which have no analog in discrete qubit codes, reduce to destructive homodyne detection in the single-mode case. These results extend an important qubit-code tool to continuous-variable systems and identify a new bridge between discrete stabilizer measurements and continuous homodyne detection.

articles.title: Electrical Stark Tuning and In Situ Field Sensing of $V_{2}$ Silicon Vacancies in a 4H-SiC a-Plane Lateral pin-Diode
articles.abstract: Silicon carbide has emerged as a highly promising platform for scalable quantum technologies, with the silicon vacancy serving as a robust spin qubit and quantum sensor. However, conventional c-plane 4H-SiC restricts the experimental scheme and resonant optical excitation to the sample's geometry. The usage of a-plane substrates enables more versatile resonant optical access to the color center through the wafer surface. Here, we demonstrate the electrical control and optical addressability of $V_{2}$ (cubic lattice site) silicon vacancies within the intrinsic region of lateral pin-diodes fabricated on a-plane 4H-SiC wafers using a scalable complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) process. Despite extensive semiconductor processing, the integrated color centers exhibit good optical quality, evidenced by narrow optical transition linewidths below 80 MHz at zero bias. These embedded quantum sensors are utilized for in situ measurement of local electric fields at cryogenic temperatures via the Stark effect. Comparisons with macroscopic technology computer-aided design simulations reveal the value of these integrated quantum sensors to help understand cryogenic device behavior, for example in predicting highly localized field crowding. Furthermore, to address the spectral indistinguishability required for quantum networks, we precisely tune the zero-phonon line (ZPL) of individual emitters via the reverse-bias Stark effect. This successfully compensates for the spectral variations of distinct emitters. Following the relaxation of transient charge fluctuations, the Stark-tuned emitters exhibit spectral stability over measurement periods exceeding four hours. Our results establish a-plane 4H-SiC as a robust platform for future interference experiments and quantum photonic integrated circuits.

articles.title: Error Resilience and Unitary 2-Designs
articles.abstract: Encoding-error-decoding circuits provide a setting for studying protection of quantum information against errors. In these circuits, an encoding unitary is followed by an error layer, decoding by the inverse unitary, and ancilla postselection. For encoders drawn from unitary 2-design ensembles, these circuits exhibit an error-protecting phase below a threshold error strength in which the fidelity between the input and recovered logical states approaches unity. Here, we show how departures from Haar second-moment statistics of the encoder can destabilize the error-protecting phase and derive a universal inequality linking recovery fidelity to the second unitary frame potential, which quantifies the ensemble's proximity to a unitary 2-design. This connection is exemplified by matchgate circuits doped with a tunable number of non-Gaussian gates. We analytically show that undoped circuits lack a stable error-protecting phase in the thermodynamic limit and that increasing the doping restores the error protection mechanism as the encoder ensemble approaches an approximate unitary 2-design. Further examples of Hamiltonian encoders, including an experimentally motivated all-to-all spin model, follow the same mechanism. Our results identify recovery fidelity as a diagnostic of departures from unitary 2-design behavior in quantum many-body systems.

articles.title: Exponential Control of Adiabatic Time Reflection by Complex-Time Singularities
articles.abstract: Nearly identical temporal switching profiles can produce very different reflections even when both have small local adiabatic measures. In a lossless dielectric, we obtain this difference by adding a weak feature that changes the complex-time singularities while preserving monotonicity, endpoints, and central slope. A perturbation bounded by $0.6\%$ of the total inverse-permittivity change raises the reflected mode amplitude from $8.02\times10^{-10}$ to $1.28\times10^{-3}$. The complex action and pole residue predict this amplitude to within $0.32\%$. Within this waveform family, deviation and monotonicity constraints select three design regimes. At fixed deviation bound, reoptimization keeps the central feature's time scale comparable to the inverse incident angular frequency. The optimal amplitude is then proportional to $1/T$ as the switching time $T$ tends to infinity. Stretching a fixed profile gives exponential suppression. Full-wave Maxwell simulations resolve the backward packet, and filtering calculations quantify its sensitivity to modulation bandwidth.

articles.title: Finite-Key Readiness and Authentication-Key Replenishment in QKD-Assisted UAV Edge Computing
articles.abstract: A service that needs fresh quantum keys must wait for key release, and may be denied it, before protected computation starts. We quantify this cost for a trusted stationary UAV serving two ground gateways, each obtaining its keys from one finite-key decoy-state BB84 attempt with parameters fixed in advance. A count-level Monte Carlo model, reproduced by a semi-analytic model, links key acceptance to protected upload, computation, and download, including failed attempts and hover energy. At 26~dB effective optical loss, with authentication hashing at its proxy-benchmarked, near-zero cost, fresh keys raise the 95th-percentile completion time of both tasks from 10.37 to 28.65~s; hover energy grows in proportion. The scalar rate models evaluated here miss the deadline limit on the block size. The pulse budget lies in a window bounded below by authentication-key replenishment and above by the deadline; for a fixed source, channel, and acceptance model, the authentication debit shifts the floor, whereas hashing cost does not. At a 35-s deadline the largest tested loss with a non-empty window is 27~dB at 1\% misalignment and 22~dB at 2\%; at 3\% no tested setting has one. Conditional on the assumed acquisition probability, the selected configurations meet this deadline with simultaneous lower confidence bounds of 96.9--97.3\% on held-out trials, at 26~dB and at 18--20~dB with 2\% misalignment. A high-cost stress reference that charges hashing in full narrows the window and lowers these loss limits to 26 and 20~dB at the reference processing capacity. A small rise in error rate or loss pushes the deadline probability well below its target and drains authentication keys, while the protocol's security parameter is unchanged.

articles.title: High-Speed Control of a Fluxonium Qubit via Picosecond Pulses from Josephson Digital Circuits
articles.abstract: We develop a control strategy for fluxonium qubits based on picosecond single-flux-quantum (SFQ) pulses generated by Josephson digital circuits. A major challenge is that SFQ protocols originally designed for transmon control become inefficient for low-frequency fluxonium. In this regime, the asymmetry of flux and charge couplings leads either to excessive leakage or excessively long gate times. We show that this limitation can be overcome by two complementary protocols. The first protocol employs high-frequency SFQ pulse packets applied through the flux channel, offering a simple, analytically transparent, and robust approach for high-fidelity single-qubit control. The second protocol combines phase-shifted flux and charge pulse sequences to enhance the resonant drive and reduce the gate duration. Multilevel simulations demonstrate single-qubit gate fidelities above $99.99\%$; the simpler protocol remains robust under moderate variations of qubit parameters and flux bias, while the combined protocol preserves high fidelity while substantially accelerating the gate. These results establish SFQ-based cryogenic control as a realistic route to fast, accurate, and scalable manipulation of fluxonium qubits.

articles.title: Implementing rapid reset of superconducting qubits with on-chip dissipation
articles.abstract: Rapid and high-fidelity qubit reset is essential for quantum state initialization and quantum error correction. Conventional reset protocols for superconducting qubits often rely on dissipative elements connected to external circuitry, exposing qubits to thermal noise from higher-temperature environments. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a scalable approach to qubit reset and leakage removal over multiple transmon qubits using dedicated dissipation units comprising resonators coupled to on-chip resistive loads. This architecture provides Purcell protection while isolating the qubits from warmer external circuitry. We achieve a median reset time constant of approximately 48 ns for the $|g\rangle-|e\rangle$ transition, with an effective bath temperature of 30 mK. A 400-ns reset pulse yields residual excited-state populations of $0.29\%$ and $0.67\%$ for qubits initialized in $|g\rangle$ and $|e\rangle$, respectively. We further demonstrate efficient leakage removal from the $|f\rangle$ state, reducing its residual population to $0.51\%$. These results establish a simple, reproducible, and easy-to-integrate approach to dissipation engineering in superconducting quantum processors.

articles.title: Intracycle Interference in Strong-Field Photoemission from a Tungsten Needle Tip
articles.abstract: Electrons photoemitted by strong laser fields can rescatter, generating attosecond high harmonics. Spectral peaks arise from inter- and intracycle interference of coherent electron wave packets. While intercycle interference is well known, intracycle interference of plateau electrons has not been observed. We present carrier-envelope phase-resolved photoemission spectra from a nanometric tungsten needle tip driven at 1570 nm revealing such interference, supported by quantum orbit and TDSE simulations that elucidate attosecond-scale electron dynamics.

articles.title: Life-history trade-offs explain local adaptation in Arabidopsis thaliana
articles.abstract: Local adaptation has been demonstrated in many organisms, but the traits involved and the temporal and spatial scales at which selection acts are generally unknown. We carried out a multi-year study of 200 accessions (natural inbred lines) of Swedish Arabidopsis thaliana using local field sites and a combination of common-garden experiments that measured adult survival and fecundity, and selection experiments that measured fitness over the full life cycle. We found evidence of strong and variable selection, with particular genotypes favored more than fivefold in certain years and locations. Fecundity showed evidence of classical local adaptation, with accessions generally performing better closer to their home. However, relative to other accessions, southern ones usually had the highest fecundity—but were far more sensitive to harsh winters and slug herbivory, which strongly decreased both survival and fecundity. Furthermore, accessions originally sampled on beaches had low fecundity in all common-garden experiments, but massively outperformed all other accessions in the selection experiments, presumably due to an advantage during seedling establishment associated with their very large seeds. We conclude that local adaptation in A. thaliana reflects strong temporally and spatially varying selection on multiple traits, generally involving trade-offs and different life-history strategies, making fitness difficult to predict and measure.

articles.title: Midbrain somatostatin-expressing cells control pain-suppression during defensive states
articles.abstract: In threatening situations, animals exhibit a broad range of behavioral and autonomic responses. As such, a crucial adaptive response is the inhibition of pain, which facilitates relevant defensive behaviors that promote survival. Whereas the structures and mechanisms involved in fear and pain behaviors are well documented, little is known about the precise neuronal mechanisms mediating the emotional regulation of endogenous pain-suppression. Here, we used a combination of behavioral, anatomical, optogenetic, and electrophysiological approaches to investigate, in male mice, the role of somatostatin-expressing cells in the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray matter (SST+ vlPAG cells) in the control of analgesia induced during defensive states. Our data indicate that optogenetic inhibition of SST+ vlPAG cells promotes analgesia irrespective of animal defensive state. In contrast, optogenetic activation of long-range SST+ vlPAG cells that project to the rostral ventromedial medulla (RVM) abolishes the analgesia mediated by fear behavior. Together, these results identify a novel circuit mechanism composed of long-range SST+ vlPAG cells projecting to the RVM that regulate analgesia elicited during defensive states.

articles.title: Molidustat targets a synthetic lethal vulnerability in APC-mutant colorectal cancer through GSTP1 and PHD2 co-inhibition
articles.abstract: Mutations in the adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) gene are a defining feature of colorectal cancer (CRC) and impose metabolic and stress adaptation requirements that may create exploitable vulnerabilities. Prolyl hydroxylase domain (PHD) inhibitors have been explored as therapeutic agents in CRC; however, their mechanisms of action and off-target effects remain elusive. Serendipitously, we found that Molidustat, a PHD2 inhibitor, induced cell death in human APC-mutant CRC cells. Ablation of PHD2 alone did not affect cell viability, suggesting an off-target mechanism. Using thermal proteome profiling and chemical proteomics, we identify glutathione S-transferase P1 (GSTP1) as a previously unrecognised off-target of Molidustat and demonstrate direct inhibition of its enzymatic activity. Genetic ablation of PHD2 alone did not phenocopy the cytotoxic effects of Molidustat, whereas combined loss of PHD2 and GSTP1 induced synergistic proteomic changes associated with cell-cycle suppression and apoptotic signalling. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic analyses further revealed energetic and metabolic perturbations specific to simultaneous GSTP1 and PHD2 loss. Consistent with these findings, APC-mutant mouse organoids displayed selective sensitivity to Molidustat that was not reproduced by hydroxylase inhibition alone, supporting a synthetic lethal interaction between GSTP1 and PHD2 in APC-mutant contexts. Together, these results identify a functional interaction between GSTP1 and PHD2 in a subset of CRC and suggest that off-target engagement of GSTP1 contributes to the anti-tumour activity of Molidustat.

articles.title: Accelerating CO2 Biocatalysis through Multimodal AI-Guided Enzyme Prioritization and Spatial Confinement
articles.abstract: Direct biological conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals is severely restricted by sluggish enzyme kinetics and inefficient intracellular carbon flux. Here, we address these catalytic bottlenecks by synergizing multimodal deep learning, mechanistic enzyme engineering, and synthetic organelle assembly. Using CASKP, a TransKP-guided candidate-prioritization framework that integrates sequence representations with a docking-derived scalar feature, we prioritized and experimentally identified a highly active β-carbonic anhydrase, PbCA, for improving intracellular CO2 supply. Structural analysis and molecular dynamics simulations guided the design of the R71A and V112A variants. The R71A–V112A variant displayed a specific activity of 26.1 U/mg and increased the intracellular 13C-labeled 3-phosphoglycerate ratio 4.9-fold. The simulations were consistent with a more hydrated active-site environment and a strengthened Tyr108-centered hydrogen-bond network. To overcome diffusion and thermodynamic limitations, these optimized biocatalysts were encapsulated into hybrid carboxysomes and coupled with an ATP-generating carboxykinase. 13C tracing confirmed incorporation of inorganic carbon into l-malate, with 95.2% of malate detected as 13C-labeled isotopologues. Subsequent promoter optimization yielded an l-malate titer of 22.7 g/L. This multiscale approach provides an integrated strategy for heterotrophic CO2-incorporating biocatalysis.

articles.title: Catalytic Stereoselective Inverse Electron Demand Formal Aza-Diels–Alder: Access to Highly Congested Molecular Bowl-Shaped 3D Tertiary Amines
articles.abstract: Diastereoselective sp3-rich heteroatom-based bowl-shaped polycyclic molecules are a key structural scaffold in various bioactive molecules. Due to the inherent steric congestion of these structures, achieving precise stereochemical control remains a significant challenge in contemporary synthetic chemistry. We herein disclose a practical iron-catalyzed assembly of an indole-derived tertiary amine-based pentacyclic molecule through an intermolecular, iminium-triggered dearomative inverse electron-demand formal aza-Diels–Alder (IEDFADA) reaction. Detailed computational and deuterium labelling experiments strongly suggest that the diastereoselective formation of this complex core involves a stepwise in situ generation of a short-lived, highly reactive azadiene. Moreover, the negative slope (ρ = –0.29) from the Hammett plot indicates the formation of a partial positive charge and that the electron-donating groups enhance the reaction rate. Notably, the concise tagging of drug molecules and downstream synthetic transformations with good yields and diastereoselectivity should highlight the potential applications of this methodology in drug discovery settings in medicinal chemistry.

articles.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Accelerated Discovery of Doped Spinel Co3O4 Catalysts for the Oxygen Evolution Reaction
articles.abstract: The discovery of doped spinel Co3O4 electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is hindered by the large catalyst design space and the high computational cost of density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Here, we establish a hierarchical interpretable machine learning (ML) framework that decouples electronic structure prediction from catalytic activity prediction. By starting with predicting the electronic descriptor (d-band center) from readily accessible structural descriptors and subsequently predicting adsorption energetics, the framework removes the need for expensive electronic structure DFT calculations during catalyst screening while preserving physical interpretability. A random forest model was trained on adsorption free energies of OH*, O*, and OOH* from 144 representative active sites and achieved a test mean absolute error of 0.21 eV. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified surface energy, active site undercoordination, and the d-band center as the dominant descriptors governing adsorption energetics. To avoid additional DFT calculations of the d-band center during screening, a second ML model predicted it directly from structural and elemental descriptors with a test mean absolute error of 0.23 eV. The resulting framework enabled rapid evaluation of OER overpotentials across 252 active sites, while subsequent targeted DFT calculations identified Al-, Ca-, Fe-, and Mn-doped Co3O4 as promising candidates. Targeted DFT calculations and electrochemical measurements further validated the improved OER activity of Al- and Fe-doped Co3O4. This work establishes an interpretable and computationally efficient strategy for connecting structural descriptors, electronic properties, adsorption energetics, and experimentally measurable catalytic activity, thereby accelerating the discovery of high-performance spinel oxide catalysts.

articles.title: Structural Insights and Functional Expansion of an Aerobic Skatole Synthase
articles.abstract: SktA from the cyanobacterium Nostoc punctiforme NIES-2108 belongs to the versatile heme oxygenase-like domain-containing nonheme oxidase superfamily, whose natural function is to transform 5-bromotryptophan (5-Br-Trp) to 5-bromoskatole in an oxygen-dependent manner. As SktA is also capable of transforming tryptophan (Trp) to skatole, this enzyme represents a skatole synthase that operates under aerobic conditions. Here, the crystal structure of SktA and its complex with 5-Br-Trp and Trp are reported. The amino acids responsible for the substrate binding and the diiron cluster formation were revealed, and their roles in the catalytic reaction were examined via mutagenesis experiments. In addition, we found that SktA is capable of transforming 7-bromotryptophan and 5,7-dibromotryptophan to yield 7-bromoskatole and 5,7-dibromoskatole, respectively, and resolved the crystal structures of SktA in complex with these alternative substrates to elucidate the plasticity of the substrate-binding pocket. Finally, we show that combining SktA and regiospecific self-sufficient Trp halogenases in one-pot reaction systems efficiently transforms Trp to 5-bromo-7-iodo-skatole or 5-iodo-7-bromo-skatole. In summary, this study reveals the structural information, substrate scope, and potential applications in synthetic biology as a module to generate differentially halogenated skatoles of SktA.

articles.title: Tuning Supported Fe-Ag Catalysts for Selective Acetylene Hydrogenation: A Combined Experimental and Computational Study
articles.abstract: The selective hydrogenation of acetylene is a key reaction step for purification in ethylene production, as trace amounts of acetylene can poison downstream polymerization catalysts. Industrial acetylene hydrogenation is currently performed almost exclusively using palladium-based catalysts, motivating the search for more abundant alternatives. In this study, supported Fe-Ag catalysts with different Fe:Ag ratios were synthesized and evaluated for the selective hydrogenation of acetylene under industrially relevant front-end conditions. The catalysts were characterized by XRD, N2-physisorption, TPR, XPS, STEM-EDX, ICP-OES and XRF, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations on idealized local Fe-Ag surface motifs were used to investigate composition-dependent trends in adsorption energetics. Catalyst characterization revealed no evidence for the formation of an extended Fe-Ag alloy phase after air exposure. Instead, Fe- and Ag-rich domains were found to coexist in close nanoscale proximity providing a structural basis for considering possible local Fe-Ag interactions. Accordingly, the DFT calculations were performed on idealized local Fe-Ag surface motifs to investigate how the local chemical environment around adsorption sites affects the adsorption energetics of reaction intermediates. DFT calculations predict a gradual weakening of adsorption strength with increasing local Ag content, while the experimental catalyst series independently shows a decrease in ethane selectivity with increasing Ag loading. Under CO-containing front-end conditions, catalyst selectivity increased further due to competitive adsorption effects, while the influence of catalyst composition became less pronounced. The combined experimental and computational results indicate that changes in the local Fe-Ag environment influence adsorption energetics and may contribute to the composition-dependent catalytic behavior in acetylene hydrogenation. These findings provide design principles for the development of palladium-free hydrogenation catalysts based on earth-abundant metals.

articles.title: Dual-Solvent Screening for Nondestructive In-Situ Optical Patterning of CsPbX3 QDs/PMMA
articles.abstract: Perovskite quantum dot (PQD)-polymer composites are widely pursued for display devices due to their excellent film-forming capacity, low cost, and favorable process compatibility. However, interfacial incompatibility between PQDs and polymers from mismatched surface chemistry triggers PQD aggregation and severe photoluminescence quenching, hindering microdisplay applications. Herein, a dual-solvent screening strategy is demonstrated for I-184-initiated crosslinked PQD-PMMA photoresists to balance solubility and lead-ion coordination strength. Undesired lead-solvent intermediate formation and residual solvent accumulation are suppressed to homogenize PQD dispersion and preserve optical performance. The 20 μm green patterned film retains 93% of the initial photoluminescence quantum yield with no photoluminescence peak shift and a narrow full width at half-maximum of 16.6 nm. The PQD pattern presents sharp pixel edges, 7.10% critical dimension deviation, 97.1% replication rate, and intersection over union of 0.92. This solvent engineering enables the revitalization of conventional polymers and addresses bottlenecks in photolithographic patterning of PQD-polymer composites.

articles.title: Martensitic vs strain glass transformation in Ti–Nb alloys mediated by oxygen and nitrogen interstitial site reconfiguration
Data‐Driven Host Microstructure Design Toward Efficient and Durable Room‐Temperature Sodium–Sulfur Batteries
articles.abstract: Porous carbon materials are critical hosts for chalcogen‐ and halogen‐based conversion‐type cathodes, as they govern the activity and durability of electrochemical reactions. Understanding how their microstructures regulate electrolyte‐electrode interactions remains challenging given multiple coupling factors and dynamic changes during electrochemical cycling. Herein, machine learning was first used to screen three pore structure parameter windows relevant to electrochemical features from a large experimental dataset (23 carbon hosts and 1055 specific‐capacity data points). Based on these screened windows, three representative carbon hosts, namely micropore‐rich carbon, balanced carbon, and meso/macropore‐rich carbon, were synthesized as model systems. We reveal that pore structure governs sulfur species evolution, thereby dictating the competition between polysulfide‐mediated reactions and solvent self‐decomposition. The resulting spatial‐compositional differences of the cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) were found to profoundly impact energy efficiency, reversibility, and rate performance. The balanced carbon cathode with optimized inorganic‐organic distribution delivers an initial capacity of 1249.4 mAh g−1 and retains a capacity of 784.8 mAh g−1 after 500 cycles. This work not only proposes a data‐driven strategy for identifying CEI‐relevant pore structure windows, but also provides mechanistic insight into how physical metrics of porous carbon modulate multi‐step complex reactions and ultimately influence electrochemical performance.

articles.title: Renewable Intermittency Redistributes Catalyst Recovery and Membrane Degradation in Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Renewable intermittency is widely regarded as a durability stressor in water electrolysis, yet its impact on competing degradation and recovery processes within the cell remains unclear. Here, we show that realistic intermittent operation redistributes catalyst recovery and membrane degradation in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE). A Ni–Fe‐based AEMWE single‐cell was operated under high‐resolution, solar‐mimicking load profiles that reproduce day–night intermittency without external buffering. Electrochemical diagnostics reveal reversible changes in activation, Ohmic, and mass‐transport losses, indicating partial performance recovery during zero‐current intervals. In situ X‐ray absorption spectroscopy attributes this behavior to reversible oxidation‐state and coordination changes of Ni and Fe, associated with the reversible formation and relaxation of amorphous (oxy)hydroxide surface layers. In contrast, hydrogen crossover measurements reveal increased crossover under low‐current operation, while post‐mortem membrane analyses provide independent evidence of membrane deterioration, identifying a critical system‐level limitation. These results show that intermittency does not uniformly mitigate degradation but redistributes it across cell components, enabling catalyst self‐restoration while exacerbating membrane vulnerability. This work establishes intermittency as a double‐edged operational parameter and provides a framework for designing materials and operating strategies for durable, battery‐free AEM water electrolysis.

articles.title: Understanding Charge Acceptance Limitations During Extreme Fast‐Charging of Li‐ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Extreme fast charging in lithium‐ion batteries is limited by their poor charge acceptance at high C‐rates. We use overpotential component analysis to decouple ohmic, kinetic and transport voltage losses during fast charging. The concentration gradients are identified as the primary culprit in poor charge acceptance, so we study carbonate electrolytes that utilize acetonitrile, a low viscosity, high dielectric liquid, as a co‐solvent to improve ion transport. Our results indicate acetonitrile co‐solvent successfully reduces fast charging concentration gradients and therefore improves charge acceptance at high C‐rates, particularly when used in combination with interface‐stabilizing additives. Molecular dynamics simulations show that ACN enhances Li+ transport through a combination of reduced bulk viscosity and increased solvation‐shell lability, with shorter solvent residence times and faster coordination exchange producing transport gains beyond those expected from viscosity reduction alone. Finally, we use three‐electrode cells to deconvolute overpotential at each electrode, and the specific LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2 (NMC811) electrode architecture and loading used in our study is found to have much higher overpotentials than our graphite electrode. In particular, the significant differences in NMC811 concentration gradients between electrolytes with or without acetonitrile indicate that the design of electrode architecture is crucial for extreme fast charging applications.
