articles.title: Reconstructing developmental and disease progression with sample-level embeddings
articles.abstract: An scRNA-seq framework that embeds each sample by the density distribution of its cells across cellular states is used to resolve continuous variation in infection, neurodegeneration, embryonic development, and whole-organism perturbation that discrete sample labels obscure.

articles.title: The calcium signaling links to fungal pathogenicity by a dual-action regulator
articles.abstract: Wang et al. characterize Cas5 as a fungus-specific regulator linking calcium-stress responses and pathogenicity in Candida albicans. By orchestrating distinct calcium-response and virulence pathways, Cas5 enables this fungal pathogen to integrate environmental adaptation with infective potential.

articles.title: The CD39/CD73 adenosinergic pathway is increased by proinflammatory states and modified by chemo-radiation in human non-small cell lung cancer
articles.abstract: Ashley et al. report local expression of adenosine-producing enzymes CD39 and CD73 as an inducible and inflammation-driven immunosuppressive pathway present in >85% of NSCLCs. This pathway displays preferential expression in lung adenocarcinomas with elevated TILs and PD-L1 or in tumors lacking STK11/KEAP1 mutations and is suppressed by radio-chemotherapy.

articles.title: Tumor-colonizing Bifidobacterium dentium promotes tumor progression and chemotherapy resistance via MMP3 and GABA-FOXA2-P-gp axis
articles.abstract: Pan et al. report that tumor-colonizing B. dentium promotes tumor progression and chemotherapy resistance. Their findings link B. dentium to MMP3 induction and GABA-mediated FOXA2-dependent P-gp upregulation, supporting a role for intratumoral host-microbe interactions in tumor progression and chemotherapy response.

articles.title: Thermophysical properties of battery electrolytes and binary electrolyte mixtures
Exploring Charge Distribution and Rate Variation in LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2/LiMn0.7Fe0.3PO4 Blends for High Rate Electrodes
articles.abstract: Composite electrodes containing physical mixtures (“blends”) of multiple active materials have generated commercial interest for lithium battery applications due to the possibility of enhanced electrochemical performance, which are not fully characterised. This investigation uses mixtures of well-known LiMn0.7Fe0.3PO4 (LMFP) and LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2 (NMC) materials as a model blend system to investigate rate- and composition-dependent effects on performance. A combination of electrochemical and operando techniques reveals that deviations in performance with respect to the linear combination of the component materials originate from uneven current distribution, leading to different effective rates between components and spontaneous lithium-ion redistribution, commonly termed the “buffer effect”. Results of experiments using a specially adapted three-electrode setup show that the effective rates of the components vary considerably depending on the cell state of charge, with much higher effective rates being reached than the applied cell rate. The same setup allows the direction of lithium redistribution to be visualised when the system relaxes following a current pulse, and this directionality also varies with cell state of charge. Electrochemical investigations and Raman spectra reveal that blending reduces chemical sensitivity to ambient storage conditions and leads to reduced degradation by forming a protective LMFP layer around the more reactive NMC particles. Operando data shows that the blend components evolve largely as expected when taking into account their specific effective rates, in line with the materials retaining their individual electrochemical properties. This study highlights the importance of considering relative windows of electrochemical activity when selecting blend components and paves the way for future optimisation of electrode blends for high rate lithium-ion batteries.

articles.title: Internal Free Volume Directs Hydration-Induced Amorphization of Hollow α-V2O5
articles.abstract: Hollow particles are designed to keep their cavities open, but a cavity can also be consumed as a structural resource. Thin-walled hollow α-V2O5 converts in aqueous ZnSO4 at 80 °C into a filled, hydrated, amorphous phase, Zn0.23(OH)0.46V2O5·1.0H2Oa charge-balanced composition from ICP-OES and TGA that assumes V5+ and hydroxide compensation of the zinc. Electron tomography shows the cavity disappearing as the particle grows from 246 to about 420 nm, with 6% of the vanadium lost to solution. The hollow shell takes up three times the water of commercial V2O5. Diffraction and vibrational spectroscopy show loss of long-range order and a 13 Å hydrated gallery; V K-edge XANES shows the vanadyl V5+ site of α-V2O5 surviving. Zn K-edge EXAFS gives Zn−O = 2.03 Å with a six-coordinate model in every state. The transformed phase has a smaller slow-process impedance and a larger initial utilization than crystalline controls, and DFT + U models of a reduced amorphous network with the same Zn content stabilize ionized Zn in O-rich disordered sites. Cycling changes the vanadium site, which does not recover on charge, and buries the surface under zinc hydroxy-sulfate. Internal free volume directs hydration-induced amorphization; stabilizing the product is a separate problem.

articles.title: Plasmon-Defined Chemical Templates for the Nanoscale Assembly of Colloidal Nanoparticles
articles.abstract: Controlling matter with nanoscale spatial selectivity is a key hurdle for plasmonic applications such as nanophotonics, sensing, and catalysis. Plasmon-assisted nanolithography has recently emerged as a powerful strategy to address this challenge by exploiting the highly confined electromagnetic fields and hot carriers generated during plasmon excitation to confine organic or inorganic layers at the nanoscale. Among the surface chemistries compatible with this approach, aryl diazonium salts are particularly attractive because their reduction produces highly reactive aryl radicals that form robust covalent bonds with metallic surfaces under mild conditions. Under light excitation, the plasmon-induced reduction of aryl diazonium salts enables the rapid and site-selective grafting of functional organic layers confined to plasmonic hot spots. The resulting functional films provide versatile chemical handles for further modification. However, to date, the use of plasmon-mediated diazonium grafting as a spatially controlled primer layer to direct the site-selective immobilization of colloidal nanoparticles remains unexplored. We address this gap by using lithographic gold nanodisc arrays as optically programmable templates. Under plasmon excitation, these nanostructures enable the formation of positively charged nanoscale anchoring domains at plasmonic hot spots, derived from diazonium salts bearing amine groups. These localized charged domains can then guide the spatial organization of negatively charged colloidal gold nanoparticles. The geometrical parameters of the plasmonic arrays, including nanodisc diameter and interparticle spacing, were carefully tuned to access different plasmon excitation regimes around the 633 nm laser wavelength, enabling blue-shifted, near-resonant, and red-shifted conditions, and expanding the variety of achievable hybrid patterns. Complementary characterization using SEM, UV−vis spectroscopy, and FDTD simulations demonstrates that this approach provides a straightforward and versatile strategy to direct the assembly of colloidal nanoparticles on lithographic nanostructures via optical excitation.

articles.title: Letter by Fan et al Regarding Article, “Systemic Embolic Events in Atrial Fibrillation: An Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis of 71 683 Participants Randomized to NOAC Versus Warfarin”
Leveraging Multimodality Imaging to Inform Therapeutic Mechanism, Treatment Response, and Patient Discussions in ATTR-CM
Low Peak Volume of Oxygen Consumption on Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing
Myocardial Responses to Eplontersen in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: The CARDIO-TTRansform CMR study
articles.abstract: Background: Transthyretin-lowering therapies target the underlying cause of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), but their effects on myocardial amyloid burden and cardiac remodelling remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the myocardial effects of sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen using serial multiparametric cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR). Methods: This CMR study was a pre-specified, international, prospective study embedded within the randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 CARDIO-TTRansform trial. Participants underwent CMR at baseline and planned assessments at weeks 25, 49, 97, and 140. The primary imaging analysis evaluated longitudinal changes in CMR parameters using mixed models for repeated measures. Myocardial amyloid regression and progression were defined as ≥5 percentage-point decreases and increases in extracellular volume (ECV), respectively. All other patients were considered stable. Results: We enrolled 120 participants with baseline and ≥1 follow-up CMR assessment (eplontersen, n=58; placebo, n=62; mean age, 76.7±6.5 years; 95% male; baseline stabilizer, 12.5%). At week 140 eplontersen resulted in lower ECV, compared with placebo (least-squares mean difference [95% CI], –6.7 percentage points [ –8.7 to –4.7]; P<0.001) and lower native T1 ( –25.9ms [–41.7 to –10.2 ]; P=0.002) and left ventricular mass (–19.1g [–28.0 to –10.2]; P<0.001). Eplontersen also increased left ventricular ejection fraction (+5.1% [1.8–8.3]; P=0.002), right ventricular ejection fraction (+4.6% [0.6–8.7]; P=0.03), and left ventricular global longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain and right ventricular longitudinal strain (all P<0.05), compared to placebo. At week-140, myocardial amyloid regression occurred in 12.5% receiving eplontersen versus 0% receiving placebo, whereas progression occurred in 12.5% versus 76%, respectively. Conclusions: Sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen resulted in substantially lower myocardial ECV and favorable changes in cardiac structure, biventricular systolic function, and myocardial deformation compared with placebo in a cohort of patients mostly not on background stabilizer at baseline. These findings provide randomized evidence that lowering circulating transthyretin modifies myocardial disease progression in ATTR-CM and support serial multiparametric CMR for characterizing myocardial treatment response.

articles.title: Progressive Calcification and Stenosis of a Quadricuspid Aortic Valve
Reconsidering β-Blockers in HFpEF: An Urgent Priority

Response by Al Said et al to Letter Regarding Article, “Systemic Embolic Events in Atrial Fibrillation: An Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis of 71 683 Participants Randomized to NOAC Versus Warfarin”
Technology and Intelligence: Staying on Target for the Next Decade of Electrophysiology
Triglycerides and Risk of Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease and Acute Pancreatitis: 4 Population-Based Cohorts
Building evolutionary resilience as a framework for managing safe haven populations
articles.abstract: Safe havens are widely used to mitigate the impacts of invasive predators on threatened species, yet their isolation often disrupts evolutionary processes and can leave these species vulnerable to environmental change and stochastic events. Effective approaches to overcome these limitations and promote adaptive capacity in safe haven populations are lacking in conservation biology. Thus, we developed a pragmatic, heuristic management framework for integrating evolutionary principles into safe haven management with a focus on establishing a metapopulation of individuals distributed across geographically separated safe havens spanning environmental gradients. We used genetic simulations to demonstrate how this approach can enhance adaptive potential and persistence and to explore the optimal configuration of safe havens and number of individuals in each haven. Using demographic simulations for two threatened Australian mammals, we illustrated how this approach can be practically implemented. Based on spatially explicit population models, we predicted that many existing safe havens for these species are at risk of collapse within decades. However, our simulations showed that selection based on standing genetic variation can drive fitness gains within tens of generations, improving population resilience to novel conditions. Integrating these processes revealed that safe haven networks can promote adaptation and resilience, substantially improving long‐term persistence and providing robust sources for reintroductions. El desarrollo de la resiliencia evolutiva como marco para la gestión de las poblaciones en refugios seguros Resumen Los refugios seguros se utilizan ampliamente para mitigar el impacto de los depredadores invasores sobre las especies amenazadas; sin embargo, su aislamiento a menudo altera los procesos evolutivos y puede dejar a estas especies vulnerables a los cambios ambientales y a los eventos estocásticos. En la biología de la conservación se echan en falta enfoques eficaces para superar estas limitaciones y fomentar la capacidad de adaptación en las poblaciones de los refugios. Por ello, hemos desarrollado un marco de gestión pragmático y heurístico para integrar los principios evolutivos en la gestión de los refugios, centrándonos en el establecimiento de una metapoblación de individuos distribuidos entre refugios geográficamente separados que abarquen gradientes ambientales. Hemos utilizado simulaciones genéticas para demostrar cómo este enfoque puede mejorar el potencial de adaptación y la persistencia, así como para explorar la configuración óptima de los refugios y el número de individuos en cada uno de ellos. Mediante simulaciones demográficas de dos especies de mamíferos australianos amenazados, hemos ilustrado cómo se puede aplicar este enfoque en la práctica. Basándonos en modelos poblacionales espacialmente explícitos, predijimos que muchos de los refugios existentes para estas especies corren el riesgo de colapsar en unas décadas. Sin embargo, nuestras simulaciones mostraron que la selección basada en la variación genética existente puede impulsar mejoras en la aptitud en unas pocas decenas de generaciones, mejorando la resiliencia de la población ante condiciones nuevas. La integración de estos procesos reveló que las redes de refugios seguros pueden promover la adaptación y la resiliencia, mejorando sustancialmente la persistencia a largo plazo y proporcionando fuentes sólidas para las reintroducciones.

articles.title: Evaluating social media portrayals of imperiled problem species to devise improved conservation messaging strategies
articles.abstract: Understanding public sentiment toward wildlife is important for developing effective conservation practices and policies, and securing funding support. This holds true especially in the case of species such as the endangered dhole (Cuon alpinus), which carries a perception debt from centuries of negative attitudes. To examine whether historical negative perceptions are being amplified online, we applied a novel natural language processing (NLP) approach to >6,000 social media posts from Instagram, X (formerly Twitter), Facebook, and YouTube. We compared sentiment and engagement patterns associated with dholes against three other sympatric carnivores that vary in charisma and cultural visibility: Bengal tiger (Panthera tigris), sloth bear (Melursus ursinus), and golden jackal (Canis aureus). We quantified caption descriptors and sentiment across species and platforms, finding that dholes were disproportionately associated with negative adjectives and attitudes. Contrary to expectations, negative captions did not consistently accompany threatening or distressing visuals, highlighting a more complex relationship between language and media. Although audience engagement varied across thematic categories for some species, these differences were relatively small. Visual media outperformed text‐based content in eliciting online engagement. Together, these findings demonstrated how digital perceptions of wildlife are shaped by not only species identity but also content framing, platform dynamics, and media format. By integrating scalable NLP tools with targeted media analyses, we developed a replicable framework for decoding online sentiment and provided empirical insights that can inform conservation messaging strategies. Such approaches can be beneficial to researchers and organizations in rebalancing attention toward overlooked species and strengthening conservation narratives. Evaluación de la imagen que se ofrece en las redes sociales de especies problemáticas en peligro de extinción para diseñar mejores estrategias de comunicación en materia de conservación Resumen Comprender la opinión pública respecto a la fauna silvestre es importante para desarrollar prácticas y políticas de conservación eficaces y garantizar el apoyo financiero. Esto es especialmente cierto en el caso de especies como el perro silvestre asiático (Cuon alpinus), en peligro de extinción, que arrastra una «deuda de percepción» derivada de siglos de opiniones negativas. Para analizar si estas percepciones negativas históricas se están amplificando en Internet, aplicamos un novedoso enfoque de procesamiento del lenguaje natural (PLN) a más de 6.000 publicaciones en redes sociales procedentes de Instagram, X (antes Twitter), Facebook y YouTube. Comparamos los patrones de opinión y de interacción asociados a los perros silvestres asiáticos con los de otros tres carnívoros simpátricos que varían en cuanto a carisma y visibilidad cultural: el tigre de Bengala (Panthera tigris), el oso perezoso (Melursus ursinus) y el chacal dorado (Canis aureus). Cuantificamos los descriptores de los pies de foto y el sentimiento en todas las especies y plataformas, y descubrimos que los perros silvestres asiáticos se asociaban de forma desproporcionada con adjetivos y actitudes negativas. Contrariamente a lo esperado, los pies de foto negativos no acompañaban sistemáticamente a imágenes amenazantes o angustiosas, lo que pone de relieve una relación más compleja entre el lenguaje y los medios de comunicación. Aunque la interacción del público variaba según las categorías temáticas para algunas especies, estas diferencias eran relativamente pequeñas. Los medios visuales superaron al contenido basado en texto a la hora de generar interacción en línea.…

articles.title: Noted with interest
The commercial trade in exotic pets has had little impact on wild populations of reptiles and amphibians
articles.abstract: The commercial trade in exotic pets has raised concerns about population‐level impacts from collection in the wild; however, proponents of the trade claim that such concerns are unfounded. To resolve this debate, more information is needed on the volume of the pet trade, the species involved, their conservation status in the wild, and the relative numbers of wild‐caught versus captive‐bred animals. To examine these issues for reptiles and amphibians, we assembled and analyzed data on >255,000 specimens over a 16‐year period from the pricelists of a major commercial supplier in the United States and >85,000 specimens over a 6‐year period from suppliers in Europe. A small number of species dominated: 31% of listings included 22 species (14 snakes, four lizards, three frogs, and one turtle were all listed >2000 times). Of the 27 most commonly listed taxa, all were rated by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as least concern, except for two python species where collection for the pet trade is likely to be a minor threat compared with habitat destruction. The proportion of all listings that were described as captive‐bred rather than wild‐caught was approximately 34% and increased over time. There was no overlap between species that were in high demand for the pet trade versus for their meat and skins. We concluded that the major risks to reptiles and amphibians from the pet trade do not involve the unsustainable harvest of wild animals, but there are animal welfare issues and threats related to the spread of disease to wild populations and ecological and genetic impacts of released pets. Over the period that we surveyed, the numbers and types of reptiles and amphibians offered for sale by the U.S. and U.K. suppliers were unlikely to have imperiled populations of most species that were traded. Impacto mínimo del mercado comercial de mascotas exóticas sobre las poblaciones silvestres de reptiles y anfibios Resumen El mercado de mascotas exóticas ha suscitado preocupaciones sobre el impacto que tiene la captura en el medio natural sobre las poblaciones; sin embargo, los defensores de este comercio afirman que dichas preocupaciones carecen de fundamento. Se requiere de más información sobre el volumen del comercio de mascotas, las especies implicadas, su estado de conservación en su ambiente y las proporciones entre los animales capturados en estado silvestre y los criados en cautiverio para resolver este debate. Para realizar este análisis con reptiles y anfibios, recopilamos y analizamos datos sobre más de 255,000 ejemplares a lo largo de un periodo de 16 años, procedentes de las listas de precios de un importante proveedor comercial de Estados Unidos, y sobre más de 85,000 ejemplares a lo largo de un periodo de 6 años, procedentes de proveedores europeos. Un pequeño número de especies fue predominante: el 31% de las entradas correspondió a 22 especies (14 serpientes, 4 lagartos, 3 ranas y 1 tortuga, todas ellas mencionadas más de 2, 000 veces). De los 27 taxones que aparecieron con mayor frecuencia en las listas, todos estaban clasificados por la Unión Internacional para la Conservación de la Naturaleza (UICN) como de menor preocupación, salvo dos especies de pitón, en las que la captura para el comercio de mascotas probablemente suponga una amenaza menor en comparación con la destrucción de su hábitat. La proporción de todas las entradas descritas como criadas en cautiverio, en lugar de capturadas en estado silvestre, fue de aproximadamente el 34% y aumentó con el tiempo. No observamos que las especies con mayor demanda en el comercio de mascotas y aquellas con mayor demanda por su carne y sus pieles se traslaparan.…

articles.title: Effects of Historical Isolation and Current River Fragmentation on the Genetic Structure of a Freshwater Fish
articles.abstract: Habitat fragmentation is a major threat to freshwater biodiversity. In river networks, the dendritic structure of drainage systems can compound the effects of barriers to dispersal, which have greatly increased as a result of anthropogenic activities. Yet, disentangling the relative contributions of these natural and anthropogenic barriers remains challenging. We assessed how historical catchment isolation and contemporary river fragmentation jointly shape the genetic structure of a low‐dispersal freshwater fish, the Pyrenean minnow (Phoxinus bigerri), across northern Spain by genotyping 280 individuals from five independent catchments at 26 microsatellite loci and analysing genetic structure at regional and within‐catchment scales using STRUCTURE. The effects of fragmentation metrics on pairwise genetic differentiation were quantified with Maximum Likelihood Population Effects mixed models, and demographic histories were reconstructed using BOTTLENECK and DIYABC‐RF. Strong genetic differentiation among catchments was consistent with long‐term isolation, while pronounced substructure within several catchments suggested restricted contemporary connectivity. Among fragmentation metrics, the number of barriers between river reaches emerged as the strongest predictor of genetic differentiation, whereas cumulative barrier height and river distance showed weaker effects. Demographic analyses revealed signatures of recent bottlenecks, likely dating to the post‐medieval period and coinciding with intensified human modification of river networks. Together, these findings suggest that contemporary river fragmentation may reinforce genetic differentiation superimposed on older patterns of catchment isolation, highlight the pervasive impact of barriers on connectivity and provide insights relevant for the conservation and management of fragmented freshwater ecosystems.

articles.title: Elevational Adaptation in the Moth Thitarodes xiaojinensis: HSP60A‐Mediated Thermal Tolerance Evolution Under Gene Flow
articles.abstract: Climate warming intensifies thermal selection on high-elevation species, yet the molecular mechanisms enabling rapid adaptation under ongoing gene flow remain poorly understood. We examined differentiation between High-elevation (High) and Low-elevation (Low) ecotype samples of Thitarodes xiaojinensis, an endemic ghost moth of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, using SLAF-seq, RNA-seq profiling and survival experiments. Phylogenetic analyses confirm the two ecotype samples are conspecific, and they differ in forewing phenotype. Population structure at K = 2 uncovers elevation-correlated clustering despite weak genome-wide structure (optimal K = 1). Genome-wide F ST scans (Weir & Cockerham) identify HSP60A as a prominent outlier locus (F ST = 0.391, top 1.4% of genome-wide windows). Targeted PCR amplification and sequencing confirmed a nonsense mutation (Glu378*) in the HSP60A coding sequence. This derived allele was carried by 80% (4/5) of Low individuals and by none of 5 High individuals (0 of 10 chromosome copies, one-sided 95% upper bound on allele frequency ≈ 26%), suggesting that it is associated with incipient ecological divergence between the two ecotypes. Co-expression network analysis grouped the chaperone genes into two systems with divergent thermal responses. The small HSPs were induced 2.3-fold from 8°C to 16°C, whereas the classical chaperones were not induced, and HSP60A was consistently placed within the latter (median biweight midcorrelation +0.56 with classical chaperones versus −0.27 with small HSPs, p = 3.5 × 10−9). Across the three temperatures the Low ecotype expressed HSP60A at lower levels than the High ecotype, significant under log2(TPM + 1) (p = 0.020) but not under the other two scales, and survived better at 16°C (p = 0.0342). These results link a coding variant at HSP60A, its lower transcript level in the Low ecotype and the better survival of that ecotype at 16°C, and identify HSP60A as a candidate locus for ecotype-informed conservation of the Ophiocordyceps sinensis host insect.

articles.title: Global Potential Distribution and Climatic Niche Dynamics of the Invasive Alien Weed Solanum rostratum Dunal
articles.abstract: Whether invasive species conserve their ancestral climatic niches or undergo realized niche changes during global spread fundamentally affects the reliability of invasion risk projections. We integrated ensemble species distribution models (SDMs), the extended COUE framework, and Multivariate Environmental Similarity Surfaces (MESS) to quantify the global climatic niche dynamics and invasion risk of Solanum rostratum Dunal (Solanaceae) across its native North America and four invaded regions. Macroecological modeling revealed a temperature‐driven, precipitation‐constrained distribution, where thermal availability and mean diurnal range dictated suitability, while precipitation extremes imposed strict limits. Cross‐regional analyses comparing true occurrence records revealed a highly heterogeneous continuum of realized niche dynamics. Populations in Australia and Russia–Eastern Europe exhibited strict climatic conservatism, occupying analogous climates with complete niche stability (S = 1.000). Western European populations displayed substantial niche unfilling (U = 0.321); however, 80.4% of this constituted abandonment (native climates absent from Europe), suggesting genuine dispersal limitation. In contrast, Chinese populations exhibited extensive colonization of novel climatic conditions. Although showing near‐complete stability strictly within available analogous climates (S = 0.998), 48.5% of the expansion‐related niche quantity in China occurred in non‐analog environments (pioneering), leading to poor projection transferability of the native SDM (Continuous Boyce Index = 0.166). These findings demonstrate that S. rostratum maintains ancestral climatic preferences where suitable environments are available while possessing the capacity to pioneer novel climatic spaces during global invasion. Integrating these expanded realized tolerances into a global ensemble SDM provides a robust, region‐specific risk assessment framework that improves projection accuracy and supports adaptive management under global environmental change.

articles.title: Human Tolerance in Romanian Brown Bears (Ursus arctos): Access to Human Food Sources Can Lead to Changes in Bear Behaviour
articles.abstract: Tolerance to humans in wild animals can lead to several conflict situations and contribute to a generally negative perception of these animals among people. When a wild animal becomes reliant on human‐derived food, dangerous situations can arise, posing risks to both animals and humans. The brown bear (Ursus arctos) is a controversial species in Romania, as it is protected but also responsible for incidents with livestock, crops, or even humans. In our study, we aimed to identify the factors that facilitate bear visits to the town of Băile Tușnad and assess their effects on bear behaviours associated with increased tolerance of humans. Using city surveillance cameras, we analysed bear behaviour in relation to the use of electric fences and the presence of garbage scattered around the bins, seeking for a better understanding of which factors should be mitigated or adjusted to improve the safety of both bears and citizens. Our results supported our hypotheses that frequent bear visits to garbage container islands are linked to the availability of garbage and insufficient protective measures, such as non‐activated electric fences. As the frequency of bear visits increased, we observed a decrease in fearful behaviours, such as hesitation before entering the container islands or scanning their surroundings while foraging. This suggests that the bears of Băile Tușnad, in addition to showing signs of food conditioning, were also exhibiting increased tolerance to the urban environment, both of which could serve as precursors of a more persistent tolerance to human activity in the long term.

Symmetry breaking drives topological dissociation of grain-boundary heterophases for single-crystal regeneration of spent NCM cathodes
Changing in the face of invasion and urbanization: meta-analytical support for context-dependent morphological adaptation in Anolis lizards
articles.abstract: Employing a meta-regression analytical approach, we aimed to identify patterns of morphological change based on the impacts of anthropizing habitat pressures and the competition between native and invasive congeners. We harvested data from records for two species of Anolis lizards: Green Anoles (Anolis carolinensis), native to the southeastern USA, and invasive Cuban Brown Anoles (Anolis sagrei). We compared forest and urban habitats and for A. sagrei, native and invasive ranges. Our model analyzed variation in patterns of morphological size from 126 sex-specific samples measured in snout–vent lengths (SVL). We used two temporal scales: collection intervals (grouped in 5-year bins) and the estimated length since regional establishment of invasive A. sagrei (measured in decades). In post-hoc weighted regression analyses we evaluated the impact of island size on native and invasive populations. We found males were consistently larger than females and invasives were larger than natives. Island native anoles’ size correlated negatively with island area while invasive populations showed no correlation. Temporal predictors counteracted each other. We interpret these contradictions to show patterns of publication bias (5-year interval) and time since invasive establishment showing pressure driven morphological change. In forested habitats, invasives A. sagrei increase in size the longer the congeners coexist while A. carolinensis appear to shrink. In urban habitats, both congeners decrease in size the longer they coexist.

articles.title: Mytho-ecological isomorphism: a study of marine restoration through mythological narratives
articles.abstract: Nature is understood as a part of human life through sacred narratives to sustain the environmental resources. When nature is exposed to environmental disturbances such as climate change, it adapts to these imbalances and restructures itself to maintain a stable state. This article employs the idea of ‘isomorphism’ to investigate self-regulation and transformation of marine ecology through mythological narratives. By drawing on Eugene Odum’s idea of ‘Homeostasis’ and Sterling and Eyer’s ‘Allostasis’, the self-regulation and transformation process of the marine system is explored in the paper. The marine ecosystem undergoes internal self-regulations naturally to sustain equilibrium despite minor fluctuations reflecting ‘homeostasis’. However, when environmental disturbances such as coral bleaching, rise in ocean temperature, etc., exceeds the ecological resilience, the ecosystem reorganizes the structure itself and continues to function without collapsing, reflecting the ‘allostatic’ state. ‘Homeostatic’ and ‘Allostatic’ self-regulatory functions find narrative parallels in Greek and Hindu mythological traditions. Mythological marine narratives often portray the disrupt symbolic orders, reorganise divine authority and restructure the system, reflecting restoration and transformation of the systematic order. The mythological marine narratives and the marine ecosystem restoration exhibit binary oppositions, presenting conflicting forces within a single ecological system. The article employs Levi-Stauss’ theory of binary oppositions to argue that both ecological and mythological systems are bridged through opposing elements such as purification and pollution, creation and destruction, etc. This research explores marine space as a common entity where equilibrium is repeatedly disturbed, destabilised and restructured. The restoration of marine equilibrium has been adopted as one of the key objectives by the United Nations under Sustainable Development Goals. The paper also focuses on Sustainable Development Goal 14 – ‘Life Below Water’, by highlighting the conservation and sustainment of marine resources.

articles.title: eDNA metabarcoding and random forest identify super-connector fish species across mangrove–seagrass–coral reef continuums in the South China Sea
articles.abstract: BackgroundTropical coastal seascapes rely on ecological connectivity between mangrove, seagrass, and coral reef habitats to sustain fish biodiversity and fisheries productivity. However, identifying key fish species that facilitate cross-habitat energy flows remains challenging due to limitations of traditional survey methods in turbid, structurally complex environments.MethodsWe integrated environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding with Random Forest (RF) machine learning to map fish assemblages across a mangrove-seagrass-coral reef continuum in Hainan Island, South China Sea.ResultsWe detected 234 fish species across 78 families - a 4.03-fold increase over conventional gillnet surveys (58 species, paired t-test, t = 11.34, p < 0.001). Using RF classification, we identified 23 "connector species" with high cross-habitat fidelity, of which three super-connectors - Lutjanus russellii, Siganus fuscescens, and Gerres oyena - accounted for 47% of cross-habitat network flow. Simulated removal of these three species reduced overall network connectivity by 68%. The RF model achieved 90.7% accuracy (Kappa = 0.86) in predicting habitat occurrence from eDNA data. Variable importance analysis revealed a salinity threshold at 28 PSU and a distance-to-reef threshold at 2.5 km as primary drivers of community turnover. Our bipartite network analysis showed significant nestedness (NODF = 47.3, p < 0.001), indicating that generalist species disproportionately maintain seascape connectivity.DiscussionThese findings demonstrate that integrating eDNA with machine learning provides a scalable, high-resolution toolkit for defining functional connectivity and prioritizing species for ecosystem-based fisheries management in the Anthropocene.

articles.title: Trait co‐occurrence networks reveal changes in community functional structure from local to landscape scales
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract The functional composition of communities reflects species performance and its interplay with local and regional drivers. Yet trait‐based analyses often overlook regional heterogeneity (geographic and environmental differences among communities), despite its central role for community assembly. This limits our ability to assess functional change across broad spatial extents or long time periods, which is essential to understand the functional consequences of global change. To overcome this limitation, here, we expand the network analysis of traits (NATs) to assess community functional structure along spatial and environmental gradients by shifting the focus from species–trait associations to trait–trait co‐occurrences. We sequentially aggregated communities by (1) spatial proximity, (2) environmental similarity or (3) random selection to quantify how spatial and environmental gradients determined the density of links between trait co‐occurrences (i.e. trait associations) within networks (measured as edge density) and the position of individual traits within those networks (measured as trait strength and betweenness). We developed this approach using long‐term datasets of aquatic benthic invertebrate communities from Sweden: 56 lakes (spanning 21 years) and 39 streams (spanning 12 years) and compared their patterns with those obtained using in silico metacommunities. We found clear scale dependence on functional structure and contrasting regional drivers across ecosystems. While streams were only structured by geographic distance, the influence of environmental filtering increased over time in lakes, potentially signalling the effects of climate change on their functional structure. These results demonstrate that the relative importance of spatial and environmental drivers of functional structure can differ among freshwater ecosystems and change over time, highlighting the need to consider both regional heterogeneity and temporal dynamics when assessing functional metacommunity structure. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Resum La composició funcional de les comunitats reflecteix el rendiment de les espècies i la seva interacció amb els factors determinants locals i regionals. No obstant això, les anàlisis basades en trets sovint passen per alt l'heterogeneïtat regional (diferències geogràfiques i ambientals entre comunitats), tot i el seu paper central en l'assemblatge de les comunitats. Això limita la nostra capacitat per avaluar el canvi funcional al llarg d'àmplies extensions espacials o de llargs períodes temporals, la qual cosa és essencial per entendre les conseqüències funcionals del canvi global. Per superar aquesta limitació, ampliem l'Anàlisi de Xarxes de Trets (Network Analysis of Traits, NATs) per avaluar l'estructura funcional de les comunitats al llarg de gradients espacials i ambientals, canviant el focus de les associacions espècie–tret cap a les concurrències tret–tret. De manera seqüencial, es van agregar les comunitats per (1) proximitat espacial, (2) similitud ambiental, o (3) selecció aleatòria per tal de quantificar com els gradients espacials i ambientals determinen la densitat d'enllaços entre les concurrències de trets (és a dir, associacions de trets) dins de les xarxes (mesurada com a densitat d'enllaços) i la posició dels trets individuals dins d'aquestes xarxes (mesurada com la força i la centralitat d'intermediació del tret). Vam desenvolupar aquest enfocament utilitzant conjunts de dades a llarg termini de comunitats d'invertebrats bentònics aquàtics de Suècia: 56 llacs (al llard d'un període de 21 anys) i 39 rius (al llarg d'un període de 12 anys) i vam comparar els seus patrons amb els obtinguts mitjançant metacomunitats in silico.…

articles.title: Protected Areas Reduce Heat Exposure in Squamates Globally
articles.abstract: Protected areas (PAs) are central to biodiversity conservation, yet their capacity to buffer species from climate‐driven heat exposure, that is, the duration and frequency of exposure to temperatures exceeding species' critical thermal limits, remains poorly quantified at global scales. Here, we assessed whether squamate reptiles inside PAs experience lower heat exposure than conspecifics in unprotected, human‐modified landscapes, and how this buffering effect varies across latitudes, biomes, and evolutionary lineages. Using biophysical modelling of operative temperatures across 248 species, we show that PAs consistently reduced both annual hours above critical thermal maximum (CTmax) and the frequency of critical days under current and future climatic scenarios (+2°C and + 4°C). We found that under current climate, protected sites had 51 fewer hours above CTmax and 3.5 fewer critical days than unprotected sites, and the proportional reduction persisted under +2°C and + 4°C warming scenarios. The buffering effect was most pronounced at low latitudes and tropical biomes, where species already operate close to their thermal limits. Deserts and xeric shrublands, together with tropical grasslands and savannas, emerged as biomes with elevated heat exposure, reinforcing growing concern for arid‐zone reptiles under climate change. Substantial phylogenetic signal in heat exposure indicated that evolutionary history shapes thermal vulnerability beyond geography and biome alone, with the magnitude of PA buffering varying considerably across squamate lineages. Our findings demonstrate that PAs can provide refugia from heat exposure, and that their conservation value under climate change depends on the retention of structurally complex habitats and thermally heterogeneous microhabitats.

articles.title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Optimize Ecological Restoration for Climate and Biodiversity
articles.abstract: The restoration of degraded ecosystems is critical for mitigating climate change and reversing biodiversity loss. Depending on the primary objective—such as maximizing carbon sequestration or protecting threatened species—and within the boundaries of budget limitations, different spatial priorities have been identified at global and regional scales. Funding mechanisms to support such work comprise public sources, philanthropy, and the private sector, including the sale of carbon and biodiversity credits. However, effectively exploring trade‐offs among restoration objectives and estimating the price of biodiversity and carbon credits to design financially viable projects remains scientifically challenging. Here we harness the power of artificial intelligence implemented in the software CAPTAIN to identify spatial priorities for ecological restoration that maximize multiple objectives at once and to allow a robust evaluation of biodiversity and climate outcomes. We find through a series of simulations that even low‐to‐moderate consideration of biodiversity in the design of restoration projects leads to the selection of restored areas that disproportionately improve the conservation of threatened species, while the carbon captured is only slightly reduced. We propose the bundling of biodiversity and carbon credits to support restoration efforts even in areas previously excluded for economic reasons. Applying our methodology to plant diversity in the Atlantic Forest of eastern South America, one of the most biodiverse and threatened ecosystems globally, we demonstrate its potential to guide restoration and to quantify trade‐offs between multiple optimization scenarios. Our study provides a robust, scalable method to maximize the joint benefits of ecological restoration for climate and nature. RESUMO A restauração de ecossistemas degradados é fundamental para mitigar as mudanças climáticas e reverter a perda de biodiversidade. Dependendo do objetivo principal—como maximizar o sequestro de carbono ou proteger espécies ameaçadas—e dentro dos limites impostos por restrições orçamentárias, diferentes prioridades espaciais têm sido identificadas em escalas globais e regionais. Os mecanismos de financiamento para apoiar esse tipo de trabalho incluem fontes públicas, filantropia e o setor privado, incluindo a venda de créditos de carbono e de biodiversidade. No entanto, um grande desafio científico é como explorar de forma eficaz as perdas e ganhos entre objetivos alternativos de restauração, e como estimar o preço de créditos de biodiversidade e de carbono para o planejamento de projetos financeiramente viáveis. Neste artigo, utilizamos o poder da inteligência artificial implementada no programa CAPTAIN para identificar prioridades espaciais para a restauração ecológica que maximizem múltiplos objetivos simultaneamente, e para permitir uma avaliação robusta dos resultados para a biodiversidade e o clima. Por meio de uma série de simulações, constatamos que mesmo uma consideração baixa a moderada da biodiversidade no planejamento de projetos de restauração leva à seleção de áreas restauradas que aumentam de forma desproporcional a conservação de espécies ameaçadas, enquanto o carbono capturado é reduzido apenas ligeiramente. Propomos a combinação de créditos de biodiversidade e de carbono para apoiar esforços de restauração mesmo em áreas anteriormente excluídas por razões financeiras. Ao aplicar nossa metodologia à diversidade de plantas da Mata Atlântica—um dos ecossistemas mais biodiversos e ameaçados do planeta—demonstramos o potencial da nossa ferramenta para planejar a restauração sob múltiplos cenários de otimização. Nosso estudo fornece um método robusto e escalável para maximizar os benefícios conjuntos da restauração ecológica para o clima e a biodiversidade.

articles.title: Behavioural flexibility within ecological constraints: Local‐scale landscape composition modulates habitat selection and foraging strategies in a forest‐dependent carnivorous bat
articles.abstract: Animals increasingly move through landscapes very different from those in which their ecological strategies evolved, posing new challenges for ecologically specialized species. By tracking a forest‐dependent carnivorous bat across contrasting landscapes, this study shows how local habitat composition shapes landscape use, while behavioural flexibility remains bounded by species‐specific ecological requirements. Abstract Behavioural flexibility may allow animals to use heterogeneous landscapes, but the extent of this flexibility remains bounded by species‐specific habitat requirements. We examined how local landscape composition relates to habitat selection and foraging behaviour in Chrotopterus auritus, a forest‐dependent Neotropical carnivorous bat. We tracked 17 individuals across 57 nightly trajectories in 3 landscapes differing in local habitat composition and combined resource selection functions with hidden Markov models to evaluate habitat selection and the spatial expression of two inferred foraging strategies, active search and sit‐and‐wait. Evergreen and subdeciduous forests were consistently selected across trajectories and landscapes, whereas other forest types and most non‐forest land‐cover classes were not consistently selected. Associations with non‐forest elements were nevertheless highly variable among local contexts. Agricultural areas, roads and other open elements were incorporated into some trajectories in the more heterogeneous landscapes, whereas movements in the most continuously forested landscape remained largely within forest. Despite this context‐dependent variation in landscape use, both inferred foraging strategies were expressed predominantly within evergreen and subdeciduous forest. Across individuals, these two forest types together accounted for more than 75% of the locations assigned to each strategy, whereas median percentages within individual non‐forest classes were generally below 5%. Land‐cover composition was more clearly associated with where the two strategies were expressed than with when individuals switched between them. Our findings show that behavioural flexibility can generate context‐dependent landscape use without removing the ecological requirements that constrain it. More broadly, the use of modified landscape elements should not be interpreted as reduced habitat dependence without identifying which components of habitat use vary across landscapes and which remain consistent.

articles.title: Elephants as imperfect gardeners: How megafauna reshape, not degrade, rainforest bird communities
articles.abstract: This Research Highlight explains why African forest elephants reduce bird species richness about as much as human disturbance does, but not for the same reason. New data from Mount Cameroon show elephant grazing reshapes bird communities while better preserving functional redundancy than human‐driven forest fragmentation, challenging how megaherbivore impacts are assessed. Abstract Research Highlight: Korejs, K., Hořák, D., Krystof, C., Sedlacek, O., Motombi, F., Ewome, F., Molua, L., Tache, J., Kamga, S., Christopher, J. & Riegert, J. (2026). Megafaunal engineering in the tropical rainforest: African forest elephants (Loxodonta cyclotis) reduce avian species richness but elevate functional diversity. Journal of Animal Ecology, https://doi.org/10.1111/1365‐2656.70369. Elephants are major ecosystem engineers, but their effects on animal communities may be more complex than expected. A 4‐year study on Mount Cameroon found that grazing by African forest elephants (Loxodonta cyclotis) reduced avian species richness to levels comparable with those in forest degraded by human activity. Yet, unlike human‐driven degradation, elephant grazing did not promote the replacement of forest‐specialist birds by open‐habitat generalists. Instead, it shifted communities towards understorey and terrestrial invertivores at the cost of large frugivores. Despite lower species richness, elephant‐grazed forests showed higher functional diversity but lower functional redundancy than undisturbed forest, suggesting a change in community composition rather than simple ecological impoverishment. These findings show that the ecological signature of megaherbivore‐driven disturbance differs fundamentally from anthropogenic disturbance, and that species richness alone may not adequately capture the ecological role and conservation value of large herbivores.

Nanoimprint lithography for metasurfaces built from functional nanoparticles
articles.abstract: Combining nanoimprint lithography with functional nanoparticles brings two design levers into the same platform: the geometry of a metasurface and the optical properties of its material. This review shows how these two levels of control are combined across the metallic, dielectric, light-emitting, and hybrid systems, providing a scalable framework for flat optics with tunable and multifunctional responses.

articles.title: Tunable molecular selectivity in CO2 conversion via exsolution-engineered catalytic interfaces
articles.abstract: Turning CO2 into useful hydrocarbons usually means broad product mixtures and high-pressure reactors since conventional catalysts offer little control over chain length and require high pressures to form C–C bonds. Here, we provide a generalizable route to C–C selectivity control through the formation of distinct catalytic interfaces via exsolution engineering. Hence, product choice is set by parent material design rather than reaction condition requirements. Beyond performance, this establishes a design strategy connecting interface structure to product selectivity.

articles.title: Distributed acoustic sensing for marine mammal monitoring
articles.abstract: Marine mammal monitoring provides critical data to inform species management and sustainable industrial development. Passive acoustic monitoring, in particular, can provide continuous, long‐term and non‐observer‐biased data, with a subset of systems capable of delivering data in near‐real time. Acoustic monitoring is increasingly required around industrial activities to assess impacts on marine mammals. However, while effective, these systems can be costly and pose human safety risks during at sea field operations, hindering adaptive management efforts. Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) is an emerging technology that converts underwater fibre optic cables into dense listening arrays providing data with high spatio‐temporal resolution. It is usually implemented from a dry end (e.g. from shore, from a substation or a platform) enabling real‐time data processing and communications. DAS implemented on the extensive existing infrastructure of telecommunication and energy industries, can detect and localize low‐frequency baleen whale vocalizations, including blue (Balaenoptera musculus) and fin whales (B. Physalus). Ongoing research seeks to extend its capabilities to broader taxonomic groups, including through custom fibre installations. DAS is a promising economic alternative or supplemental method for marine mammal monitoring. DAS is increasingly used by offshore industries for infrastructure monitoring, presenting dual‐use opportunities for simultaneous infrastructure and environmental assessment. Given the growing recognition of submarine cables as critical infrastructure, DAS implementations are likely to accelerate. The broad adoption of dual‐use DAS that allows for marine mammal monitoring requires dialogue between marine researchers, technology developers, ocean industries and policymakers. Operational DAS‐based marine mammal monitoring requires systematic advances in two critical areas to reach their full potential: (1) characterizing DAS performance across species‐relevant frequency ranges and cable configurations and (2) developing robust automated methods to process the massive spatial–temporal datasets generated. This review provides a development framework addressing these priorities through standardized protocols and algorithm benchmarking. Our recommendations emphasize open science collaboration to enable real‐time processing and adaptive management applications.

articles.title: ggNetView: An R package for reproducible biological network analysis and visualization
articles.abstract: Biological network analysis has become an important approach for investigating interactions among microorganisms, genes, proteins, and environmental variables across ecology, microbiology, and molecular biology. In practice, however, turning an inferred network into a clear figure and a full set of downstream topology and module analyses remains laborious, because the required steps are spread across several packages and are often finished by hand in a graphics editor. In response to these challenges, we have developed ggNetView, an R package that provides a complete analytical workflow. Its upstream step constructs networks from a variety of data sources, and its downstream steps encompass topology analysis, module analysis, and network visualization. The package utilizes a unified graph object, offers functions for geometric layout construction and annotation, and enables different types of networks to share a consistent set of aesthetic mappings. Beyond visualization, ggNetView enables comparison of similar modules across multiple networks and supports association analysis of the entire network and its subnetworks with environmental variables to help identify candidate modules associated with environmental variables. ggNetView has been applied to microbiome co‐occurrence, WGCNA‐derived co‐expression, and protein–protein interaction networks. Across repeated runs with the same graph object and parameters, node coordinates are reproduced. The package is freely available at https://github.com/Jiawang1209/ggNetView. 摘要 生物网络分析已成为解析微生物、基因、蛋白质与环境变量之间相互作用的重要途径，在生态学、微生物学和分子生物学中广泛应用。但在实际操作中，从网络推断到一张清晰的网络图，再到完整的拓扑属性与模块分析，仍然十分繁琐，所需步骤分散在多个软件包中，不少环节还需要在图形编辑器里手工完成。 为此，我们开发了ggNetView。该R包提供了一套完整的工作流程:上游分析基于多种据源进行网络构建，下游分析覆盖拓扑分析、模块分析和网络可视化。该软件包采用统一的图对象，提供多种几何布局构建函数与注释功能，并支持不同类型的网络共享同一套美学映射。 除可视化外，ggNetView还能在多个网络之间比较相似的模块，并可对整个网络及其子网络与环境变量做关联分析，从而筛选出与环境因子相关的候选模块。 我们已将ggNetView应用于微生物组共现网络、WGCNA共表达网络和蛋白质相互作用网络。在相同图对象与参数下进行重复运行，节点坐标可完全复现。软件包可从https://github.com/Jiawang1209/ggNetView免费获取。

articles.title: Dot1 triggers a conserved ribophagy signal to govern ribosome quality and longevity by methylating Rpl12
articles.abstract: Chen et al. show Dot1-mediated Rpl12 methylation as a conserved autophagic “eat-me” signal that directs selective ribosome degradation. By coupling nutrient sensing to ribosome quality control, this mechanism promotes cellular adaptation to stress, maintains tissue homeostasis, and supports organismal longevity.

articles.title: Hierarchical buffering of cellular RNA polymerase II pools maintains transcriptional homeostasis
articles.abstract: Gillis et al. integrate quantitative single-cell imaging with genomic techniques to examine transcriptional homeostasis following acute perturbation of RNA polymerase II abundance. This work demonstrates that total mRNA production is buffered against altered polymerase abundance by the transcription cycle and further shows evidence for robustness in RNA polymerase holoenzyme assembly.

articles.title: Promoter-proximal pausing enables transcriptional buffering of RNA polymerase II availability
articles.abstract: Through titration of cellular RPB1 levels, Olthof et al. show that transcription is surprisingly sensitive to RNAPII dosage, but that genes vary widely in their sensitivity. Genes involved in transcriptional maintenance are typically dosage insensitive. Expression of these genes is buffered through decreased promoter-proximal pausing and increased mRNA stability.

articles.title: Comparative Phylogeography and Genetic Diversity Between Mainland and Island Populations of Common Ground Doves (Columbina passerina) and Their Parasitic Lice
articles.abstract: Island archipelagos are ideal natural laboratories for studying genetic variation in populations of organisms. However, relatively little attention has been given to parasites associated with hosts from oceanic islands. Here, we focus on Common Ground Doves (Columbina passerina) and two ecomorphs of parasitic lice, Physconelloides eurysema body lice and Columbicola passerinae wing lice. Both louse species parasitize C. passerina doves and their close relatives but differ in their dispersal abilities. The doves and lice are widespread across the Caribbean archipelago and adjacent continents. We were interested in two primary questions: (1) do doves and lice have congruent phylogeographic histories? and (2) do island populations of doves and lice have reduced genetic diversity compared to mainland populations? To address these questions, we used genomic data from doves and lice to reconstruct phylogenetic relationships, assess population genetic structure, and estimate measures of genetic diversity. We found that genetic structure was not consistently congruent among the doves and lice, suggesting movement of the doves that is not apparent from their genetic information. Doves and lice also have different phylogeographic histories. Doves likely originated in the Caribbean islands, whereas lice originated in the mainland or dispersed multiple times between the mainland and islands. We also did not find strong evidence that island populations of doves or lice have less genetic diversity compared to mainland populations. Our results highlight that hosts are the most immediate ‘island’ for their parasites, but varying dispersal abilities and island geography can lead to discordant phylogeographic patterns over time.

articles.title: Evidence of Putative Mitonuclear Incompatibilities in the Bullock's and Baltimore Oriole Hybrid Zone
articles.abstract: Mitonuclear incompatibilities are genetic mismatches between mitochondrial and nuclear genomes that initially arise through hybridization. Although these incompatibilities can reduce hybrid fitness and contribute to reproductive isolation, they remain poorly understood in most avian hybrid zones. To investigate mitonuclear discordance in the extensively studied hybrid zone between Bullock's (Icterus bullockii) and Baltimore Orioles (I. galbula), we used whole‐genome resequencing and mitochondrial haplotyping to assign mitochondrial ancestry to 136 individuals previously characterized for their levels of nuclear genomic admixture. We detected a narrow mitochondrial cline across the hybrid zone and strong asymmetry in mitochondrial inheritance, with 83% of putative F1 hybrids having I. galbula mitochondrial ancestry, a pattern consistent with predictions from Darwin's corollary to Haldane's rule involving uniparentally inherited loci. Genome‐wide association analyses revealed nonrandom associations between mitochondrial haplotype and autosomal nuclear loci, notably including candidate genes with mitochondrial functions. Population‐specific signals of positive selection at these loci further suggest differential selective pressures linked to mitochondrial ancestry. Together, our results provide evidence that mitonuclear interactions may contribute to asymmetric introgression and the maintenance of species boundaries in this classic avian hybrid zone.

Investigating Contact Electrification at Nanofluid-Solid Interface by Using Bulk Effect Triboelectric Probes
Atomically Precise Au14V1 Clusters Selectively Block the Neutrophil Elastase-NETosis Axis
articles.abstract: Neutrophil elastase (NE) is a key driver of neutrophil-mediated inflammation and tissue injury across diverse diseases. However, current NE inhibitors often lack sufficient target selectivity, limiting their therapeutic efficacy in suppressing inflammation and promoting organ repair. Here, we report that single-atom V doping programs atomically precise Au15 clusters into a relatively selective and potent NE inhibitor. The ultrasmall size of Au14V1 enables selective accommodation within the NE binding pocket. Multiscale mechanistic analyses demonstrated that Au14V1 inhibits NE through a reversible mixed inhibition mechanism with an inhibition rate of 87.6%, while exhibiting minimal activity toward closely related proteases, highlighting its preferential inhibition toward NE. In LPS- and CLP-induced systemic inflammatory injury models, Au14V1 reduced NE activity and NET formation, alleviated oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, mitigated tissue injury, and improved survival. These findings establish a single-atom engineering strategy for developing selective enzyme modulators and precise therapy targeting the NE-NETosis axis.

articles.title: Correction to “A Dual-Cascade Activatable Near-Infrared Fluorescent Probe for Precise Intraoperative Imaging of Tumor”
Operando Imaging of Battery Interfaces through Combined Analysis of Broadband Optical Backgrounds and Raman Features
articles.abstract: Solid-state batteries promise improved safety and energy density, but their performance is governed by buried interfaces where ion transport, chemical reactions, and stress evolution are strongly coupled. Resolving these processes during operation remains challenging. Here, we present an operando spectroscopic strategy that jointly analyzes broadband optical backgrounds and characteristic electrolyte Raman features within a single measurement. Asymmetric least-squares baseline (ALS) estimation extracts broadband optical contrast associated with lithium distribution, while Raman band intensities and peak positions provide complementary information on interfacial chemistry and local stress estimates. This capability provides a unified optical framework for visualizing structural, chemical, and mechanical evolution at battery interfaces and offers a broadly applicable route to interrogate buried interphases in diverse electrochemical systems. More generally, by enabling real-time, multimodal insight into interfacial dynamics, this method advances efforts toward safer, longer-lasting, and more predictable energy-storage technologies.

articles.title: Resolving Overlapping Signals in Quantum Relaxometry Enabled by Spectral Hole Burning
articles.abstract: Quantum relaxometry based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is an easy-to-use technique that detects magnetic noise by measuring the longitudinal relaxation of NV centers. It is favored in chemical and biological applications due to the robustness against imperfect spin control. By tuning the energy level, NV relaxometry can detect magnetic noise generated by other spins and obtain magnetic resonance spectra through cross relaxation. However, the spectral resolution is greatly limited by the inhomogeneous broadening of NV centers, especially for nanodiamond-based relaxometry. Here we demonstrate a hole-burning technique to remove the inhomogeneous broadening. We utilize a weak pump field to deplete specific NV centers during the relaxation measurement, which contribute a reverse signal in the cross-relaxation spectra with a much narrower line width. Our method retains the convenience and sensitivity of NV relaxometry, opening up new avenues for high-resolution magnetic resonance spectroscopy in complex scenarios.

articles.title: Reversible Electric-Field-Induced Changes in the Thermal Resistance of Hexagonal Boron Nitride
articles.abstract: Understanding the behavior of ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) materials under high electric fields is essential for advancing next-generation power electronics. While electrical degradation processes have been widely studied, the influence of high electric fields on thermal transport remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the first experimental measurements of changing thermal resistance under an applied electric field in a UWBG material, using single-crystalline hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) as a model system. We observe substantial, and sometimes reversible, changes in thermal resistance during prolonged exposure to a strong DC electric field. These results reveal a previously unrecognized sensitivity of phonon transport to high-field electrical stressing and show that thermal resistance can serve as a sensitive probe of electric-field-induced material evolution that remains undetected by conventional electrical characterization. More broadly, this work establishes thermal transport measurements as a powerful tool for investigating high-field phenomena in UWBG materials.

articles.title: Scintillation as an Extreme Exciton Density Regime in Colloidal Nanocrystals
articles.abstract: Colloidal semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs) have emerged as versatile light emitters for a broad range of applications, where they are typically operated in the dilute- or single-exciton regime. Scintillation under ionizing radiation, however, represents a fundamentally different mode of operation. A single absorbed X-ray photon can generate a large number of electron–hole pairs within a nanoscale interaction volume, driving individual NCs into extreme exciton occupancies. In this Perspective, we argue that scintillation in NCs should be viewed as an extreme exciton-density problem and show how simple occupancy considerations impose fundamental limits on achievable scintillation light yield. We further outline two complementary strategies to overcome these limitations: (i) engineering NCs for enhanced multiexciton radiative yields and (ii) designing NC composites that redistribute deposited energy across larger NC populations. We anticipate that exciton-density engineering will provide a unifying framework for designing the next generation of NC scintillators.

articles.title: Single-Reactor-Run Architecture of Cleaving Homoepitaxial GaN with Aperture-Driven Disordered BN Interlayers
articles.abstract: High-quality freestanding GaN membranes are fabricated using a single-reactor-run metal–organic chemical vapor deposition. The procedure begins with the growth of a single-crystalline GaN template, followed by the formation of a 20 nm-thick full-coverage disordered BN layer on GaN, which remains stable under high-temperature GaN growth conditions. We introduce a heat-treatment step to generate numerous nanoscale apertures in the BN layer, enabling aperture-mediated homoepitaxial regrowth. Meanwhile, the BN layer suppresses strong epitaxial bonding, where the regrown GaN is mechanically detachable from the GaN template. In addition, multiple disordered BN interlayer formations are established, enabling epitaxial lateral overgrowth (ELOG). Moreover, GaN Schottky diodes are fabricated to demonstrate minimal material degradation through the aperture-mediated lift-off process, enhanced device performance with BN-assisted ELOG, and the feasibility of ultralight wearable UV detectors. This approach eliminates the need for ex situ transfer or substrate-specific lift-off processes, providing a simple and thermally robust platform for manufacturing freestanding wide-bandgap semiconductor membranes.

articles.title: The Answer Lies within the Puzzle Piece: PET-Derived Defect-rich MOFs Boosting Ethylene Glycol Oxidation for Total-Product PET Upcycling
articles.abstract: Chemical recycling of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) is limited by harsh depolymerization conditions and the low-value utilization of terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG). Herein, we report a “one-stone-three-birds” strategy that couples PET depolymerization, TPA utilization, and EG upgrading for total-product upcycling. Waste PET serves as an in situ slow-release terephthalate precursor, whose gradual, incomplete hydrolysis dynamically perturbs metal–ligand stoichiometry, generating missing-linker defects and oxygen-deficient, coordinatively unsaturated environments in a bimetallic MOF (NiCo-PET). Relative to NiCo-MOF prepared from commercial TPA, NiCo-PET exhibits 67% higher spin concentration and enhanced EG oxidation, requiring only 1.29 V vs RHE at 50 mA cm–2 while achieving 93.6% formate Faradaic efficiency and stable operation for 24 h at 2 A cm–2. Operando analysis confirms favorable reconstruction into high-valence oxyhydroxides. This work valorizes both PET-derived products without additional purification or isolation, offering a sustainable route to total-product plastic upcycling.

articles.title: Theoretical Foundations of Goldene Plasmonics
articles.abstract: The recent experimental realization of goldene, an atomically thin form of gold, provides a unique platform to investigate collective electronic excitations in the ultimate two-dimensional (2D) limit of a noble metal. Here we reveal that goldene is a plasmonic material whose collective response is strongly shaped by its reduced dimensionality and underlying electronic structure. Using first-principles many-body calculations, we show that monolayer goldene supports intrinsic acoustic and optical plasmons arising from the interplay between the low-energy metallic response and dispersive s and more localized d states. As the number of layers increases, interlayer coupling and enhanced screening progressively quench this directional anisotropy, driving the system toward the isotropic response of bulk gold. In finite nanostructures, the plasmonic resonance follows the size scaling characteristic of confined 2D metallic systems. Our results establish the foundations of goldene plasmonics, with technological implications for nanophotonic sensing, photocatalysis, and atomically thin optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: Modular benzylamine synthesis through trifunctional zirconium catalysis
articles.abstract: Photocatalysis can expand the reactivity of transition-metal catalysts by enabling new reaction pathways under mild conditions. Now, a trifunctional zirconium catalytic system is developed that combines photochemical, redox and Lewis acid catalysis for the modular assembly of diverse benzylamines directly from aryl aldehydes, alkanes and nitriles under mild conditions.

articles.title: Pulling sugars off salt activation
articles.abstract: The chemical assembly of oligosaccharides hinges on the reactivity of the anomeric site. In 1980, the introduction of a Lewis acid-catalysed method for the activation of anomeric imidates marked an important step in carbohydrate synthesis, becoming the foundation of complex synthetic strategies to this day.

articles.title: Ru/rutile-TiO2 catalysts with coverage-independent particle size and shape enable isolation of particle density effects in polyolefin hydrogenolysis
articles.abstract: Particle density effects in heterogeneous catalysis are elusive because particle density usually changes simultaneously with particle size. Here we show that the size and shape of Ru particles, formed by reducing epitaxial rutile-RuO2 structures supported on rutile TiO2 with closely matched lattices, remain constant with 16-fold change in density. Using the Ru/rutile-TiO2 catalysts, we demonstrate that, in polyolefin hydrogenolysis, high Ru particle density enhances the multiparticle adsorption of polymer chains, leading to lower coverage of adsorbed H (*H), and thus higher selectivity towards CH4, with desorption being the rate-determining step. Short-chain alkanes accommodatable on a single Ru particle do not show such particle density effects, and C−H bond activation is the rate-determining step. This work provides a strategy to deconvolute particle density effects from size and shape effects in high-temperature thermal catalysis, while revealing how the large size of polymer substrates impacts catalytic mechanisms. Particle density effects in catalysis are difficult to disentangle from other factors. Now the synthesis of Ru/rutile-TiO2 catalysts with constant size and shape at varying densities enables the elucidation of particle density effects in polyolefin hydrogenolysis.

articles.title: Programming supramolecular polymer network topology via homochiral self-sorting
articles.abstract: Stereochemistry greatly influences polymer structure and assembly, yet its use in controlling polymer network topology remains underexplored. Now, homochiral self-sorting is used to suppress primary-loop formation in end-linked polymer networks, offering a strategy for controlling network topology.

articles.title: Data centres asymmetrically exacerbate energy burdens through wholesale price increases and regressive grid cost shifting
articles.abstract: As data centres increase pressure on power systems, the costs of accommodating their growth are becoming a concern. Here the researchers show that data centres raise wholesale prices and shift transmission costs onto households, with the largest burden increases in rural and low-income communities.
