Neural interface instructs layer 4-appropriate circuit reconstruction with engrafted human brain organoids and improves visually guided behavior
articles.abstract: Li and colleagues show that targeted neuromodulation guided by endogenous narrowband gamma rhythms instructs human brain organoid grafts to acquire layer 4-appropriate molecular and functional properties in the injured mouse visual cortex, enabling bidirectional host connectivity, direction-selective responses, and improved visually guided behavior.

articles.title: Cyclic tetracoordinate borons enable tetrasubstituted axially chiral alkenyl silanes
articles.abstract: A Pd-catalyzed atroposelective ring-opening coupling of cyclic tetracoordinate borons affords tetrasubstituted axially chiral alkenyl silanes while retaining the boron moiety. The reaction integrates boron and silicon within a configurationally stable chiral framework and exhibits broad functional-group tolerance. More broadly, this strategy expands the reactivity of tetracoordinate borons beyond conventional migration pathways and provides a distinct approach to tetrasubstituted axially chiral molecules.

articles.title: Two-Dimensional IR Spectroscopy: Mapping Structure and Dynamics in Complex Molecular Environments
articles.abstract: Complex, dynamically heterogeneous environments such as lipid membranes, electrocatalytic interfaces, soft polymer matrices, crowded biological media, and phase-separated assemblies are characterized by spatially distinct microenvironments, multiscale structural dynamics, and short-range interactions. Microscopic interactions are poorly captured by bulk descriptors. In this article, we review how ultrafast two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy and related vibrational methods provide direct access to these complex molecular landscapes by resolving inhomogeneous ensembles, picosecond environmental fluctuations, and exchange between local states. When combined with vibrational probes and modern molecular simulation, these spectroscopic observables reveal how local interactions, such as electrostatics, hydrogen bonding (H-bonding), and ion pairing and aggregation generate microscopic heterogeneity and govern multiscale dynamics. We organize discussions around representative classes of complex environments, including hydration and electrostatics in lipid membranes, molecular environments and dynamics in biomolecular condensates, confinement and crowding in self-assembled and interfacial systems, including electrochemical interfaces, polymers/gels and soft matter, electrolytes and ion-specific effects, and aqueous cosolvent mixtures relevant to solvation and cryopreservation. Looking ahead, ongoing advancements in vibrational probe design, multidimensional spectroscopy, and molecular simulation are expected to enable more quantitative and predictive analyses of heterogeneous molecular environments across chemistry, materials science, and biology.

articles.title: MOFs for photonics: bridging photocatalysis, optical wireless communication, and high-energy radiation sensing
articles.abstract: Light-conversion materials hold considerable promise for addressing global energy and environmental challenges, with applications spanning photocatalysis, optical wireless communication (OWC), and high-energy photon detection and imaging.

articles.title: Non-carbon-supported low-loading precious metals: from rational synthesis to mechanism insight for advanced electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: This review presents the recently developed non-carbon-supported low-loading precious metals for various key energy conversion reactions.

articles.title: Recent advances in multicolor inorganic persistent luminescent materials: mechanisms, properties, and applications
articles.abstract: We illustrate the physical pictures, performance evaluation criteria, and microscopic mechanisms of persistent luminescence, and further highlight the application-oriented multicolor design principles of inorganic persistent luminescent materials.

articles.title: Anion-Templated Cu14 Nanoclusters Reveal Ligand-Controlled Stability and Catalytic Evolution During Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
articles.abstract: Two atomically precise sulfide-templated Cu14 nanoclusters (NCs), [S@Cu14(4MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-4MBT) and [S@Cu14(3MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-3MBT), were synthesized and structurally characterized to investigate the influence of ligand engineering on the stability and electrocatalytic performance of Cu NCs during the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that both NCs possess a highly similar S@Cu14 core architecture stabilized by twelve positionally different methyl-substituted thiolate and six triphenylphosphine ligands, allowing direct evaluation of ligand effects without changes in core structure. Despite their structural similarity, positional variation of the methyl substituent generated distinct electronic environments, intermolecular interactions, and crystal-packing arrangements. The relatively electron-deficient Cu environment in S@Cu14-3MBT resulted in superior CO2RR performance, achieving highly selective Faradaic efficiencies of 52% for formate and 18% for CO at −1.4 V vs. RHE with suppressed hydrogen evolution, whereas S@Cu14-4MBT exhibited lower selectivity and stability. Theoretical calculations, together with comparison with structurally analogous metal NCs, reveal that precise modulation of the electronic configuration plays a critical role in promoting formate selectivity. Post-catalytic analyses revealed degradation and ligand loss in S@Cu14-4MBT, whereas S@Cu14-3MBT remained structurally intact. These results highlight ligand engineering and anion templation as key strategies for tuning the stability and CO2RR performance of atomically precise metal NCs.

articles.title: Reactive Decaborane Initiates Low-Temperature Polymer Decomposition and Drives Ceramic Formation
articles.abstract: Boron carbide (B4C) is a ceramic of considerable interest due to its high hardness, elevated melting point, excellent thermal stability, low density, and chemical inertness. Decaborane-functionalized preceramic polymers (PCPs) prepared from ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) are excellent single-source precursors of B4C, but the mechanistic details for the decomposition and ceramic conversion during pyrolysis have been overlooked, preventing advances in redesigning preceramic polymers that have high char yields and desirable chemical compositions. Herein, we reveal insights into the role of decaborane during the polymer-to-ceramic transition of poly(cyclooctenyldecaborane) (PCD) to boron carbide. ROMP of the cyclooctenyldecaborane monomer enabled controllable molecular weight and produced a series of polymers with molecular weights up to 35 kg/mol and dispersities (D̵) in the range of 1.3-1.6. Thermogravimetric analysis coupled with infrared spectroscopy and mass spectrometry (TGA-IR and TGA-MS, respectively) of PCD revealed the evolution of small hydrocarbon species following an initial release of hydrogen at low decomposition temperatures around 250 °C, which is in stark contrast to the decomposition profile of unfunctionalized poly(cyclooctadiene) (PCOD) that transitions into volatile hydrocarbon species at approximately 450 °C. ReaxFF molecular dynamics (MD) simulations support the experimental findings that hydrogen release from decaborane initiates the polymer-to-ceramic conversion. MD simulations indicate that the release of H2 results in the exothermic formation of boron clusters, which promote the thermal decomposition of the hydrocarbon polymer backbone. These findings indicate that decaborane plays an active role in the polymer-to-ceramic conversion rather than serving solely as a boron source, providing mechanistic insight that will enable the rational design of next-generation PCPs with enhanced ceramic yields and tunable compositions.

articles.title: Vapor−Liquid−Solid Growth of Unconventional Nanowires
articles.abstract: Vapor−liquid−solid (VLS) growth has delivered a level of synthetic control in group IV and III−V semiconductor nanowires that remains unmatched in any other class of one-dimensional materials. For Si, Ge, and GaAs, decades of mechanistic study have made diameter, growth direction, crystal phase, and axial composition into design parameters. For oxides, carbides, and chalcogenides, including emerging van der Waals materials, which we refer to collectively as non-conventional nanowires, one-dimensional structures have been reported in abundance, but comparable deterministic control has not been achieved despite their predicted functional properties and broad application potential. This review examines where and why the two groups diverge. We survey and categorize the literature on VLS and VLS-related synthesis of non-conventional nanowires, following the sequence of the growth process itself, namely, precursor creation and delivery, seed particle formation and evolution, and nucleation and growth of one-dimensional structures. Each step is compared against the group IV and III−V baseline to locate shared behavior and genuine differences. From this comparison, we identify seed particles, spanning the choice of seed material, the chemical composition of the seed during and after growth, and its dynamics, as the principal bottleneck restricting deterministic synthesis, with precursor creation and delivery acting as an upstream constraint that narrows the accessible seed design space. We discuss potential solutions, including new precursor chemistries, improved reactor designs, and in situ characterization of growth, that would deepen the mechanistic understanding of nanowires already demonstrated by VLS and extend seeded growth to emerging quantum and functional materials, ultimately paving the way for deterministic synthesis and integration of complex one-dimensional nanomaterials.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of Cannibalism in Austro‐Papuan Dragons (Lacertilia: Amphibolurinae), With a New Record of Cannibalism in the Peninsula Dragon (Ctenophorus fionni)
articles.abstract: In 2012, one of us observed an adult male peninsula dragon (Ctenophorus fionni) predate a juvenile conspecific. This was noteworthy as we understood peninsula dragons to be primarily insectivorous and it prompted us to investigate cannibalism more generally using a systematic, comprehensive review of the literature. Cannibalism has never been reported in any wild, natural‐living Australo‐Papuan (i.e., Amphibolurine) agamid, except in the peninsula dragon. There are now three records of cannibalism in the peninsula dragon, all from populations of the central form. This raises the possibility that peninsula dragons, or certain populations thereof, may be unusually predisposed to cannibalism. However, the current data available are too sparse to draw firm conclusions and we encourage anyone with observations of cannibalism to publish them.

articles.title: Do Leaf Temperatures Determine Endophyte Composition and Richness in Florida Native Plant Species?
articles.abstract: Microbiomes play crucial roles in ecosystems, largely through their interactions with plants. Fungal endophytes occur in nearly all plant tissues and can influence host physiology, stress tolerance, and productivity. Although previous studies have examined how air temperature shapes foliar endophyte communities, endophytes may respond more strongly to leaf temperatures, which are often decoupled from ambient air temperatures. Consequently, changes in leaf temperature (e.g., due to global warming) may alter endophyte diversity and composition. In this study, we experimentally tested whether elevated leaf temperatures affect fungal endophyte richness and community composition in six native subtropical plant species from South Florida. Using in situ localized heating of individual branches, we increased leaf temperatures by 1°C–3°C over a 2‐week period. Leaf thermal profiles were monitored with thermal imaging, and pre‐ and post‐treatment leaf samples were collected from warmed and control branches for fungal DNA extraction, ITS sequencing, and community analysis. Our results show that fungal leaf endophyte richness and composition were strongly determined by host plant identity, but were unaffected by warming. Linear mixed‐effects models and paired t‐tests showed no significant changes in ESV richness with heating across all hosts. Similarly, distance‐based redundancy analysis and PERMANOVA tests revealed no significant shifts in fungal community composition due to increased leaf temperatures. However, a random forest classification model identified a subset of fungal ESV that were predictive of temperature treatment. While overall endophyte communities were stable, specific taxa may be thermally responsive. Foliar fungal endophyte communities in subtropical woody plants may be resistant to short‐term warming. Such stability could buffer host plants against microbial disruption during temperature extremes, though it may also limit adaptive microbial turnover. This study advances understanding of plant–microbe thermal dynamics and underscores the need for further research on the functional resistance of endophyte communities under climate change.

articles.title: Experiences and Gender Demographics of Researchers in Long‐Term Individual‐Based Study Systems
articles.abstract: Long‐term individual‐based studies have invaluably advanced our understanding of animal ecology and evolution. Participants involved in the creation and/or maintenance of long‐term study systems benefit from synergistic collaborations, which can provide greater opportunities for co‐authorship. We conducted two surveys to collect anonymous data from current and former participants of long‐term individual‐based studies about leadership structure and authorship patterns as it is unclear whether all participants—regardless of their intersectional identity—derive the same benefits from participation in these systems. Our goal was to collect these data in a less harmful way through self‐reporting gender compared to gendering participants/authors by their first name. We found that gender representation was biased toward men historically and has recently become more equitable across genders. PI gender demographics were positively associated with the gender composition of project participants. Male PIs had higher numbers of publications compared to those of marginalized genders for overall authorship and as last author. Our results parallel similar patterns observed across other science disciplines. This research may serve as a first step in sparking broader reflection, discussion, and action on how gender data is collected and to ensure that the remarkable opportunities offered by long‐term individual‐based study systems are equitably accessible to all.

articles.title: Fertilisation Success in Acanthaster cf. solaris and Acanthaster brevispinus and Reciprocal Hybrid Crosses Across a Range of Sperm Concentrations and Development to the Hybrid Juvenile
articles.abstract: Novel species interactions between resident and range shifting species in response to warming are posing challenges for conservation and management. This is especially the case when major predatory species are involved, as seen in the appearance of a mixed species outbreak of coral‐eating crown‐of‐thorns sea stars Acanthaster cf. solaris (As) and the lesser‐known Acanthaster brevispinus (Ab) in the tropical to subtropical transition zone in eastern Australia. The outbreak consisted of reproductively mature animals, and we investigated the potential for cross‐species hybridisation in fertilisation experiments across a range of sperm concentrations to sperm limitation conditions (106–102 sperm mL−1). Fertilisation was successful in all combinations of parents (As ♂ × As ♀, Ab ♂ × Ab ♀, Ab ♀ × As ♂, As ♀ × Ab ♂) with successful hybrid crosses in sperm dilutions as low as 102 sperm ml−1. Development in conspecific and heterospecific crosses was similar through the bipinnaria and brachiolaria larval stages to the juvenile. Juvenile hybrids had typical juvenile Acanthaster spp. development with a stellate five‐armed profile post metamorphosis, gaining arms after ~78 days. At no stage did the juvenile hybrids develop the distinctive pink colour trait that is characteristic of Acanthaster cf. solaris juveniles. Our results indicate that hybridisation is not restricted by sperm limitation conditions, with subsequent development of hybrids to the advanced juvenile stage. Our results highlight the potential for hybridisation and species introgression when range shifting species overlap with sister taxa. This may facilitate further range expansion or development of resilient hybrid progeny as a risk to vulnerable high latitude coral communities.

articles.title: Genetic Diversity and Putative Origin of the Bait Polychaete, Diopatra aciculata Knox and Cameron (Annelida: Onuphidae), Occurring in South Africa
articles.abstract: The bait polychaete Diopatra aciculata is commercially farmed in Australia and is collected as bait in several South African estuaries. Despite its widespread use, the species' geographic origin remains uncertain, hindering management efforts within sensitive estuarine ecosystems. Mitochondrial Cytochrome Oxidase subunit I (mtCOI) data and ddRAD‐generated single‐nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were used to gain insight into the origin and genetic diversity of D. aciculata. A total of 204 individuals were collected from an aquaculture farm in Australia and the Knysna, Keurbooms, and Swartkops Estuaries in South Africa. The mtCOI analyses supported the monophyly of D. aciculata and revealed lower genetic diversity in the South African population compared to the Australian population. Both marker sets revealed significant genetic differentiation between the continental populations that are naturally isolated by the Indian Ocean basin. The SNP dataset revealed low intrapopulation genetic diversity for both the Australian and South African populations. The discordant genetic diversity findings between the mtCOI and SNP datasets may be attributed to the differences in the evolutionary rate of the two marker systems. In addition, the low genomic diversity observed in the SNP dataset is consistent with the effects of captive breeding in the Australian aquaculture population; consequently, the effect of sampling bias cannot be excluded. However, the mtCOI signal of reduced diversity in South Africa is consistent with an introduced population and both mtCOI and SNP‐based RASP analyses recovered Australian samples in a basal position, suggesting Australia as the plausible origin. This highlights the need for precautionary conservation efforts to prevent further spread.

A participatory framework involving trained citizen scientists and conservationists advances genetic understanding of an endangered carnivore
articles.abstract: Although citizen science is increasingly used in biodiversity monitoring, moving beyond passive observation toward the active collection of high-quality biological samples remains a major challenge. To address this, we present a participatory framework originating as a bottom-up initiative, designed to facilitate the active and structured collection of high-quality biological samples. This conceptual framework allows for the development of a genuine partnership where collective field expertise enriches scientific data interpretation to inform conservation policy. Designed to be adapted to a wide range of conservation projects, this participatory framework is particularly effective for monitoring threatened, low-density and cryptic species across large landscapes by combining robust biological sampling with strong social engagement. We illustrate the operational strength of this framework through an eight-year case study mobilizing a network of 274 volunteers trained to collect non-invasive samples from the Eurasian lynx (Lynx lynx) in France, 42 untrained volunteers and a scat-detection dog. The sampling expanded across 13 departments, with the network collecting 729 scats with a 45.8% genetic confirmation rate. An anonymous online survey evaluating the human dimensions of the framework showed that despite baseline knowledge, most respondents reported gaining new insights and naturalist skills. Direct contribution to conservation was the primary motivation, and participation strengthened trust in science and data governance. Relationships with project coordinators drove long-term engagement, resulting in high willingness to re-engage in future projects. By co-constructing the research project with civil society from the outset, this framework bridges scientific expertise and local knowledge, addresses critical gaps in our understanding of the genetic health of an elusive species, and strengthens public ownership, social acceptance and scientific credibility of the findings, all of which are essential for successful conservation.

articles.title: Temporal variation in multidimensional benthic macroinvertebrate diversity in Lake Chaohu, China, from 2018 to 2024
articles.abstract: Benthic macroinvertebrates are widely used as indicators of freshwater ecosystem changes due to their sensitivity to environmental disturbance and important ecological functions. However, long-term variations in multiple biodiversity dimensions of benthic communities under eutrophication and seasonal environmental stress remain poorly understood. In this study, quarterly surveys were conducted at eight sites in Lake Chaohu from 2018 to 2024 to investigate temporal dynamics of benthic macroinvertebrate communities and their environmental drivers. A total of 33 taxa were identified, with communities consistently dominated by oligochaetes and chironomids. Density and biomass varied significantly among years and quarters, whereas species richness showed significant quarterly variation and a Year × Quarter interaction but no significant main effect of Year. Community structure Mixed-effects models further identified associations between selected. The dbRDA model explained 11.59% of the variation in biodiversity indices (R2 = 0.116, P = 0.0007), with NH4+-N, CODCr, and TN identified as significant predictors among the measured water-column variables. Mixed-effects models revealed additional associations with composite biodiversity scores, although the statistical support for some relationships was sensitive to the omission of individual observations or sites. Temporal changes were reflected mainly in community composition, functional diversity, and taxonomic distinctness rather than interannual differences in species richness. These findings support integrating multiple biodiversity dimensions into the ecological assessment of eutrophic shallow lakes.

articles.title: Climate Warming Reduces Seed Mass in European Beech Through Altered Resource Dynamics and Drought
articles.abstract: Seed mass is a key life‐history trait that influences dispersal, seedling establishment, and plant fitness, yet its long‐term response to climate change remains poorly understood. We used two long‐term datasets of European beech (Fagus sylvatica) from the United Kingdom (1989–2024) and the Netherlands (1976–2024) to test whether seed mass has changed over time and whether any decline can be attributed to changing climate or altered resource dynamics. Seed mass declined by 13% over the study period, with a non‐linear decrease starting in the mid‐2000s. Models of year‐to‐year variation showed that seeds were smaller in years with lower reconstructed stored resources and in years that early summer was dry. Temporal contribution analysis indicated that the long‐term decline in seed mass was driven primarily by declining resource availability, with increasing drought making an additional contribution. Climate warming affects seed size in beech by direct effects of drought on seed development, and indirectly by altering reproductive dynamics and shortening the intervals available for resource recovery between reproductive events. Because seed mass influences dispersal and survival of seeds and seedlings, declines in seed mass are likely to reduce regeneration potential. Our findings identify an indirect pathway by which climate change may weaken forest regeneration.

articles.title: Microbial Life‐History Strategies Shape Biocrusts Soil Multifunctionality Responses to Multi‐Year Snow‐Cover Change
articles.abstract: Winter snowfall is a critical water source sustaining the survival and ecological functioning of biocrusts in desert ecosystems, yet how different biocrust types respond to altered snow‐depth conditions and maintain soil multifunctionality (SMF) through microbial community adjustments and life‐history strategies remains poorly understood. Based on a field snow‐manipulation experiment, we compared SMF responses in cyanobacterial and lichen crusts under snow removal, ambient snow, and double‐snow treatments across different treatment‐duration categories and further explored the underlying microbial regulatory mechanisms. Cyanobacterial and lichen crusts exhibited contrasting SMF responses to altered snow conditions. SMF significantly increased in cyanobacterial crusts in the short‐term treatment plots (1 year), whereas lichen crusts showed a significant decline only under short‐term snow removal. In the medium‐ and long‐term treatment plots (8 and 11 years), differences in SMF between altered‐snow and ambient‐snow conditions were reduced for both biocrust types. Lichen crusts mainly showed increases in bacterial and total microbial diversity under snow manipulation, whereas significant diversity responses in cyanobacterial crusts were primarily associated with fungi. Microbial life‐history strategies showed clear but biocrust‐type‐specific associations with SMF. Random forest and structural equation modeling (SEM) analyses indicated that SMF in cyanobacterial crusts was strongly constrained by the S strategy, while Y‐related metabolic pathways were positively associated with SMF; in contrast, SMF in lichen crusts was positively associated with the A strategy but negatively associated with the S strategy. Soil physicochemical properties also played an important role in regulating SMF, but their effects and interactions with microbial attributes differed between the two biocrust types. Overall, this study demonstrates that altered snow conditions regulate biocrust SMF through the coupling of soil environmental changes and microbial functional responses, with the underlying regulatory pathways strongly dependent on biocrust type.

articles.abstract: Transforming plastic waste into valuable organosulfur chemicals, this work presents a solar-driven, continuous-flow photoelectrochemical platform. Centered on a bismuth single-atom molecular catalyst with precision-engineered local coordination, the system uniquely enables selective carbon-sulfur bond formation via a controlled interface microenvironment, establishing an efficient and bias-free route for sustainable plastic upcycling.

articles.title: Optimising the performance of acoustic telemetry receiver arrays for tracking aquatic animals using the arrayplanR package
articles.abstract: Strategically deploying acoustic telemetry receiver arrays is vital for tracking the movements of aquatic animals. Nevertheless, there is a lack of tools that provide the capacity to evaluate how well arrays perform in their study area, as well as ways to optimise receiver configurations to best meet study goals. Receiver configurations vary based on the species or behaviours being studied, environmental conditions affecting detectability or the spatial resolution being targeted (e.g. fine‐scale positioning), among other factors. Therefore, optimising detectability of transmitters across receivers—relative to the diverse study objectives that often exist—should be a major priority in acoustic telemetry research. Here, we introduce a simple probabilistic approach through an R package (arrayplanR) to plan and evaluate the detection performances of acoustic telemetry arrays, when combined with user range detection data, specifically with the goal to optimise receiver locations depending on the needs of the study (e.g. transmissions detected on n receivers, largest area covered beyond a detection probability threshold, highest detection probability across entire study area). There are two distinct workflows associated with our approach: (1) ‘DE_array_quantify’ quantifies array performance for receivers at pre‐designated locations (e.g. an existing study); and (2) ‘DE_array_optimize_1overlap’ and ‘DE_array_optimize_3overlap’ enable users to iteratively identify optimal receiver locations based on animal transmissions being detected by one receiver (e.g. planning for a broad‐scale presence study) or detected by more than one receiver (e.g. planning for a fine‐scale positioning study), respectively. Each workflow incorporates several input parameters to allow customisation based on study goals (e.g. number of receivers, minimum distance between receivers, fixed receiver location(s), anticipated animal‐receiver depth differences, habitat‐specific receiver locations). Using a simple case study, we show how optimal receiver configurations vary based on study parameters and highlight how strategic receiver deployments across different habitats or areas can improve detection capacity for telemetry studies. Overall, this work can contribute to better research planning and study design across the global telemetry community and marine, estuarine and freshwater environments.

articles.title: Identification and regulation of an ACC1-associated lipogenic metabolon in liver
articles.abstract: Zhu et al. identify a nutrient-responsive ACC1-centered metabolon that organizes lipid-synthesis enzymes near lipid droplets and associates with intracellular trafficking proteins. ACC1-associated interactions increase in steatotic, insulin-resistant livers, revealing a potential target for modulating hepatic lipid production in MASLD.

articles.title: Nuclear TRiC states captured in situ
articles.abstract: Xing et al. visualize the duty cycle of nuclear TRiC using cryo-electron tomography and identify TRiC interactors in the nucleus. These findings indicate that TRiC may act on misfolded proteins in the nucleus.

articles.title: PARP1 hyperactivation uncouples transcription from protein expression through nuclear RNA retention
articles.abstract: Ortega et al. show that PARP1 hyperactivation suppresses translation by promoting nuclear RNA retention. APE1-dependent cleavage of abasic sites triggers PARP1 hyperactivation, increasing nuclear PAR, which competes with RNA for binding to RNA-binding proteins. This disrupts RNA splicing and export, limiting expression of DNA damage-induced stress-response proteins.

articles.title: SNPs in Copy Number Variants Play a Key Role in Local Adaptation to Climate in Lotus (Nelumbo nucifera)
articles.abstract: Copy number variation (CNV) constitutes a major source of adaptive genetic variation, yet its relative contribution to climate adaptation compared to non‐CNV (single‐copy) variants remains unresolved. Using whole‐genome sequencing of 125 Nelumbo nucifera (sacred lotus, a common aquatic vegetable) wild accessions spanning tropical‐temperate gradients, we distinguished 388,600 CNV‐derived SNPs from 485,982 SNPs of single‐copy regions. Latent factor mixed models (LFMM) revealed that CNV‐SNPs appear to drive adaptation to temperature extremes and precipitation seasonality, whereas non‐CNV SNPs dominate humid thermal adaptation. NnPAL2, a homologue of a drought‐related gene in Arabidopsis, shows a recent selective sweep in temperate N. nucifera, with reduced copy number and expression associated with lower precipitation in the warmest quarter. Our results suggest that CNV SNPs and non‐CNV SNPs contribute to distinct environmental axes, but the heterogeneous CNV effects across bioclimatic variables largely reflect ecotype‐specific copy number backgrounds rather than intrinsic differences in selective pressures. CNV therefore plays a disproportionate role in coping with abiotic extremes. Discriminating CNV‐derived SNPs from those derived from single‐copy genomic regions is essential for accurately understanding the genetic basis of climate adaptation, with potential applications for crop improvement.

articles.title: Species Identification in Drosophilids; the Utility of k‐mer Characters
articles.abstract: Over 14,900 COI DNA sequences of drosophilids were used to build a character‐based diagnostic system for the identification of genera and species in the group. This approach uses aligned COI sequence characters, k‐mer characters and applies a hybrid approach that combines the two. To assess the efficacy of the diagnostics, accuracy versus coverage plots were used and resulted in the observation that practical rules (allowing 5% leakage [misidentified assignments]) perform much better than strict rules (no leakage). In addition, k = 10 was determined as the optimal k value for k‐mer character analysis. Hybrid methods incorporating both k‐mer characters and aligned DNA sequence characters outperform the individual approaches. Finally, unnamed drosophilid accessions were compiled and tentatively assigned taxonomy based on the diagnostic system developed here.

Atomic-Scale Signatures of Structural Irreversibility during Oxygen Redox in Li-Rich Layered Oxide Cathodes
articles.abstract: Li-rich layered oxides access high capacity through transition-metal and oxygen redox, but oxygen loss and structural reconstruction cause large first-cycle irreversibility. Here, we examine Li1.2Ni0.13Co0.13Mn0.54O2 at four states of the first charge–discharge cycle using atomic-resolution STEM, nanobeam electron diffraction with electron pair distribution function (NBED-ePDF) analysis, electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS), image simulations, and DFT. Up to 4.3 V, Li extraction is dominated by interlayer sites and the slab framework remains largely preserved. At 4.8 V, changes in Li/O contrast and O K-edge features coincide with a short ePDF correlation near 1.57 Å. Seeded DFT relaxations stabilize short O–O pairs near vacancies in the transition-metal slab. After discharge, incomplete spectroscopic recovery accompanies near-surface reconstruction and oxygen-related contrast changes consistent with oxygen depletion. Together, the results implicate Li depletion from the transition-metal slab in high-voltage oxygen rearrangement and suggest that controlling this site occupancy may improve oxygen-redox reversibility.

articles.title: Chirality–Polarity-Regulated Magnetic Vortex Chains for Ternary Logic
articles.abstract: Spin-based multivalued logic offers compelling advantages for next-generation computing. Thus far, only binary systems─exploiting domain walls, skyrmions, and vortices─have been realized. These schemes rely solely on the manipulation of the chirality or polarity of magnetic carriers, precluding the implementation of multivalued logic operations. Here, we demonstrate the implementation of ternary logic operations using a one-dimensional vortex chain, via the co-manipulation of both the chirality and polarity of magnetic vortices. We show that ternary AND logic functionality can be achieved via dipole-mediated chirality modulation and domain-wall-assisted polarity reversal in the vortex chain, with operation times on the nanosecond scale. Our work establishes a viable and scalable platform for multivalue magnetic logic, thereby paving the way for next-generation spintronic logic applications.

articles.title: Continuous, Size-Based Purification of Virus-like Particles Using Electro-Viscoelastic Microfluidics
articles.abstract: The modular assembly of protein nanoparticles has enabled the design of highly immunogenic and cross-protective viral vaccines. However, downstream translation is hampered by labor-intensive purification methods that lack the resolution needed to efficiently sort molecular assemblies. Here, we report an affinity tag-free nanoparticle sorting platform that exploits electro-viscoelastic microfluidic (EVM) migration for the high-fidelity, continuous-flow isolation of virus-like particle (VLP) assemblies. This migration mechanism can overcome Brownian fluctuations, which are typically dominant on the nanoscale, confining the target assemblies to central streamlines for selective collection. In a single pass, the system segregates 40 nm VLPs from 6 nm excess antigen monomers, increasing the VLP purity by 20.2%. A sacrificial electrode outlet directs undesired electrohydrodynamic effects to the waste, preserving the VLP-rich product stream. Our results offer an alternative downstream framework for the rapid purification and quality control of complex bionanomaterials, establishing a scalable pathway for precision nanomedicine processing.

articles.title: Designing Strong and Broadband Nonreciprocal Thermal Radiation in Magnetic Topological Materials
articles.abstract: Breaking reciprocity in thermal radiation opens opportunities for energy harvesting, sensing, and thermal management. Traditional nonreciprocal radiative semiconductor devices need an external magnetic field. In this work, we predict a series of magnetic topological materials for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal thermal radiation in the infrared regime by combining first-principles calculations with Maxwell electrodynamics. We find strong and broadband nonreciprocity in magnetic Weyl semimetals (e.g., Co3Sn2S2), outperforming conventional semiconductor InAs. Furthermore, we propose material design recipes. Strong nonreciprocity requires a large anomalous Hall response relative to the optical loss, whereas the broadband response favors a large optical loss and small dielectric dispersion. Our work establishes a predictive material discovery framework and quantitative design rules for next-generation magnet-free nonreciprocal thermal devices.

articles.title: Direct Selenization Growth and Electronic Properties of Ultrathin Fe(Te,Se) on a van der Waals Ferromagnet
articles.abstract: Fe(Te,Se) is a prototypical iron-based superconductor and a promising platform for exploring topological superconductivity. However, growing high-quality ultrathin Fe(Te,Se) films on magnetic substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate epitaxial growth of monolayer-to-trilayer Fe(Te,Se) on the van der Waals itinerant ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) via direct selenization of the substrate, without external Fe or Te deposition. Combined scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS), low-energy electron diffraction (LEED), scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), and energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) characterizations reveal large-area, atomically flat tetragonal films with well-defined rotational alignment to the hexagonal FGT lattice. Cross-sectional STEM-EDS confirms Se incorporation and interfacial elemental redistribution. Thickness-dependent spectroscopy reveals evolving electronic structures and progressive decoupling from the ferromagnetic substrate. Measurements across lateral monolayer–bilayer interfaces further uncover asymmetric band bending and charge redistribution driven by Fermi-level equilibration. These findings establish substrate-mediated selenization as a versatile route to ultrathin superconducting heterostructures and magnetic quantum platforms.

articles.title: Electroelasticity-Regulated Vacancy Diffusion Enables Frequency-Adaptive Neuromorphic Perception and Control
articles.abstract: Emulating frequency-dependent synaptic plasticity requires artificial devices capable of integrating temporal inputs and adapting their responses. Here, we demonstrate electroelasticity-regulated vacancy diffusion in MoSe2 memristors as a physical mechanism for frequency-adaptive synaptic dynamics. An applied electric field induces lattice deformation that lowers the vacancy diffusion barrier, whereas poststimulus electroelastic relaxation progressively restores the barrier, creating a dynamically evolving diffusion landscape. This coupled electroelastic–ionic process gives rise to intrinsic second-order memristive dynamics and enables frequency- and history-dependent plasticity, including pair- and triplet-spike-timing-dependent plasticity and Bienenstock–Cooper–Munro-type learning with a sliding modification threshold. Leveraging these dynamics, memristor-based spiking neural networks realize adaptive neuromorphic functions spanning composite color–direction perception and autonomous drone control. These results establish electroelastic regulation of vacancy diffusion as a materials-level mechanism for translating temporal input statistics into adaptive synaptic responses, providing a pathway toward neuromorphic systems with frequency-adaptive perception and control.

articles.title: Agentic AI needs a science of interaction
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from stand-alone models towards systems of interacting agents. These systems do not merely classify, predict or generate: they plan, exchange messages, call tools, divide labour, adapt and coordinate action across tasks and time. This shift has made agentic AI one of the dominant frames for the next phase of the field. Understanding how these agents interact will therefore be as important as improving what each agent can do alone. Here, the authors argue that agentic AI requires a shift from evaluating individual agents alone to analyzing interaction architectures, proposing a framework that links agent interactions, collective configurations and time-dependent outcomes.

articles.abstract: Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella enterica serovars cause gastroenteritis and typhoid fever, respectively. Here, McKenna et al. show that the two types of serovars use opposing pre-invasion strategies to sense and invade human intestinal epithelium.

articles.abstract: Similar memories can be confused in different ways depending on how learning has progressed. This research shows the hippocampus responds by separating memories along the specific dimension of similarity, causing confusion at each stage of learning.

Here, the authors report a photoredox/cobalt-catalyzed method for regio- and stereoselective vinylation with internal alkynes, enabling efficient access to trisubstituted allylic amines without directing groups or oxidants.

articles.title: Banana fruit with nutritionally significant concentrations of iron and zinc: results from the field evaluation of genetically modified bananas (Musa spp.) in Australia
articles.abstract: Iron and zinc distribution in wild‐type and transgenic Cavendish banana (Musa spp.) lines. Summary Iron deficiency remains a major public health problem in East Africa, where banana is a staple food for > 30 million people. This study investigated whether genetic modification could produce banana fruit containing nutritionally significant concentrations of iron while maintaining agronomic performance under field conditions. Six transgenes associated with iron homeostasis were expressed singly or in combination in Cavendish and Lady Finger bananas. In total, 450 genetically modified plants were field evaluated in Australia and fruit mineral concentrations assessed in the first planting crop. Elevated fruit iron and zinc concentrations, reaching 45.5 and 51.9 mg kg−1 dry weight, respectively, were associated with increased nicotianamine (NA) accumulation following expression of OsNAS. Iron concentrations sufficient to meet 50% of the estimated average requirement for children were achieved in 28 lines, with elevated NA suggesting improved iron bioavailability. Increased mineral accumulation negatively correlated with yield; however, this effect was partly mitigated by co‐expression of OsVIT1. Early indicators of yield penalty included low corm iron, high leaf zinc concentrations and reduced photosynthetic efficiency. These findings demonstrate the potential of using genetic modification for the mineral biofortification of bananas in East Africa while highlighting factors that may assist in the early identification of high‐performing biofortified lines.

articles.title: PhYAB4 directly activates PhAGL6‐2 to regulate lip‐related organ curvature morphology in Paphiopedilum henryanum
articles.abstract: PhYAB4–PhAGL6‐2 regulatory module controls lip‐related organ curvature in Paphiopedilum henryanum. Summary The orchid lip is a highly specialized floral organ that contributes to floral architecture and pollinator interaction. However, the developmental and molecular mechanisms underlying lip‐related organ curvature in Paphiopedilum remain poorly understood. Using Paphiopedilum henryanum and its Type A peloric mutant, we found that visible divergence between wild‐type petals and mutant lip‐like petals begins at Stage 4. Curvature was associated with adaxial–abaxial epidermal cell number imbalance in the distal region, whereas average epidermal cell area remained largely unchanged. Transcriptome and expression analyses identified PhAGL6‐2 as a lip‐associated AGL6 homolog enriched in lips and lip‐like petals during Stages 4–5. PhAGL6‐2 was preferentially expressed on the abaxial side, particularly in regions associated with curvature. Virus‐induced gene silencing‐mediated silencing of PhAGL6‐2 in Dendrobium Chao Praya Smile and P. henryanum affected perianth organ curvature, suggesting a broader role in floral organ morphogenesis. The YABBY transcription factor PhYAB4 directly bound the AGTGTG motif in the PhAGL6‐2 promoter and activated its transcription. Silencing PhYAB4 reduced PhAGL6‐2 expression and caused stronger floral curvature, lip outgrowths, and partial disruption of floral symmetry. These findings identify a PhYAB4–PhAGL6‐2 pathway associated with epidermal cell number imbalance and lip‐related organ curvature.

articles.title: The CitRWP–CsWUS regulatory axis governs citrus plant regeneration in association with chromatin remodeling
articles.abstract: Working model of the CitRWP–CsWUS regulatory axis in association with chromatin remodeling in citrus. Summary Plant regeneration underpins crop genetic improvement, yet its regulatory mechanism remains poorly characterized in woody fruit trees. The RWP‐RK domain‐containing (RKD) transcription factor CitRWP acts as a pleiotropic regulator of nucellar polyembryony and somatic embryogenesis (SE) in citrus, but its downstream molecular network remains elusive. We demonstrate that CsWUS, a core stem cell regulator, is a direct downstream target of CitRWP. CitRWP binds to the CsWUS promoter to activate its transcription. Additionally, CitRWP interacts with the SWItch/Sucrose Non‐Fermentable (SWI/SNF) chromatin‐remodeling ATPase SPLAYED (SYD), synergistically enhancing CsWUS activation, while chromatin accessibility at the CsWUS locus is enhanced upon CitRWP overexpression. We further uncover that CsWUS negatively regulates CitRWP expression via a feedback loop. CsWUS overexpression promotes SE in recalcitrant citrus callus, but causes abnormal meristem proliferation and impairs shoot organogenesis from epicotyl segments. CsWUS greatly enhanced in planta transformation efficiency in the model citrus. This study establishes the CitRWP–CsWUS regulatory axis as a central module that coordinates multiple developmental fate transitions in association with chromatin remodeling, providing novel insights into the mechanisms of cellular totipotency and plant regeneration.

articles.title: Programming immunity in situ: A new frontier of in vivo cell engineering
articles.abstract: In vivo cell engineering enables the direct programming of immune cells inside patients. Instead of isolating, modifying, and reinfusing cells, therapeutic instructions are delivered directly to selected immune cells through lipid nanoparticles or viral vectors. This approach could facilitate rapid and scalable deployment of varied immune cell therapies across disease contexts. Early clinical studies in oncology and autoimmunity demonstrate increasing technical and clinical feasibility. The next challenge lies in enhancing precision to ensure that vectors reach the target cell type and tissue, deliver the appropriate payload, and produce desired transient or durable activity. Progress in targeting ligands, vector design, biodistribution control, and genome editing is beginning to address these barriers. Ensuring safety against immunogenicity, inflammatory toxicity, off-target editing, and uncontrolled persistence remains a central priority. By mastering these constraints, in vivo engineering could turn endogenous immune cells into therapeutic agents generated directly in the body, expanding cell therapy to diseases refractory to current modalities.

articles.title: The structural basis of IL-36R proinflammatory signaling mediated by IL-36γ and IL-37
articles.abstract: The interleukin-36 receptor (IL-36R) drives proinflammatory signaling and is therapeutically targeted by spesolimab in acute skin inflammation. Beyond its three canonical agonists (IL-36α, IL-36β, and IL-36γ), IL-36R was recently proposed to be activated by IL-37. Together with antagonism by IL-36R antagonist (IL-36RA) and IL-38, this creates a complex structure-function landscape that remains poorly understood. Here, we report the cryo–electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structure of human IL-36γ bound to IL-36R and the shared co-receptor IL-1R accessory protein (IL-1RAcP). IL-36γ engages IL-36R with low affinity, enabling high-affinity IL-1RAcP recruitment. IL-37 exhibits the opposite binding signature, binding IL-36R with high affinity but IL-1RAcP weakly. Functional comparison of IL-36R engagement by IL-36γ and IL-37 confirmed their common proinflammatory signature, with IL-36γ exhibiting markedly higher potency, consistent with its more stable signaling complex. Structural comparison of cytokine-bound versus antibody-antagonized IL-36R revealed that spesolimab acts as an allosteric antagonist. This study therefore provides a structural and mechanistic blueprint for IL-36R activation by distinct cytokines.

articles.title: A simplified high-pressure freezing workflow in Autogrids
articles.abstract: Weber et al. introduce a modular planchette system that simplifies high-pressure freezing of biological samples for cryo-electron microscopy. By reducing sample handling and accommodating diverse specimen types, the Autogrid planchette approach makes it easier to study complex biological structures in their near-native state, expanding opportunities for cellular and biomedical research.

articles.title: Covalent remodeling of CRBN creates a non-canonical neosubstrate interface with NTAQ1

This work reveals how site-specific chemical modification can reprogram E3 ligase specificity and expand the design space for molecular glue degraders.

articles.title: Lab leak disease outbreaks: the long, murky history
articles.abstract: In the heart of Russia, fear of plague is spreading. Unbeknown to the outside world, authorities have quietly commandeered the building where the first case emerged. Rifle wielding guards stand at the entrances. Inside, people are locked in quarantine rooms. There have already been deaths—pneumonic plague. And it came from a laboratory.This was the scene at a Moscow hospital in 1939, according to a handful of recollections written by scientists who lived through it. The microbiologist Abram Lvovich Berlin had travelled in from the outskirts of the capital to discuss his experiments with Yersinia pestis, the bacterium that causes plague. But he had inadvertently infected himself, becoming highly contagious. He would soon be dead.Sources differ on the details—was it two or three people who succumbed after coming into contact with Berlin? articles.abstract: A woman aged 35 years was evaluated for a 1-year history of recurrent, brief (approximately 15 min) episodes of non-positional vertigo described as a spinning sensation. Episodes were not accompanied by headache, tinnitus, hearing loss, visual symptoms, or other neurological complaints. Blood pressure was normal, and there was no orthostatic hypotension or tachycardia upon standing. Neurological and vestibular examinations, including audiometry and the Dix–Hallpike manoeuvre, were normal between episodes.

articles.title: [Comment] Preparing for dialysis when dialysis might never begin?
articles.abstract: For older people (aged ≥80 years) with frailty or multimorbidity living with kidney failure, choosing a care pathway could involve deciding whether to prepare for dialysis long before it is needed. Preparation involves education, appointments, investigations, and, for some people, surgery to create dialysis access. The alternative care pathway is conservative kidney management, which involves active care aimed at slowing kidney disease progression, managing symptoms, and preserving quality of life without planning for dialysis.
