Harnessing protein conformational dynamics for next-generation supramolecular materials
articles.abstract: Protein conformational dynamics govern how proteins assemble across distinct pathways. This review unifies native crystallization, amyloid fibrillization, and reduction-induced phase transitions, revealing how dynamic assembly routes can be harnessed to design adaptive, hierarchical protein materials with programmable functions.

articles.title: PARP1 directly disassembles nucleosomes to regulate DNA repair
articles.abstract: Verma, Zhu, et al. show that PARP1 promotes NAD+-dependent eviction of H2A-H2B dimers, generating oriented hexasomes with increased DNA accessibility. The H2A C-terminal tail supports this remodeling activity, linking PARP1-dependent nucleosome disassembly to cellular responses to DNA damage.

articles.title: An enriched methane D/H ratio in the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS
articles.abstract: JWST spectra of interstellar object 3I/ATLAS reveal an enhanced D/H ratio in methane compared with measurements of Solar System objects. The high value is comparable with that calculated for pre- and protostellar regions, indicating a primitive origin.

articles.title: An intertwined short and long γ-ray burst with a 4-minute separation
articles.abstract: GRB 160425A emitted two sub-bursts in short succession with differing properties, indicative of two distinct progenitor types: collapsar and stellar merger. This event raises questions about γ-ray burst progenitor scenarios.

articles.title: Apparent magnetic field decay in a solar flare from Zeeman splitting of the Mg I 12.32-µm line
articles.abstract: AIMS mid-infrared spectroscopy of the Mg I 12.32 µm line during an X1.5 flare reveals magnetic field weakening beneath impulsive-phase ribbons via Zeeman splitting. These changes may arise from an elevated line-formation height or local magnetic redistribution.

articles.title: Coherent manipulation of Zr(III) aryloxide qudits
articles.abstract: Paramagnetic molecules can serve as electron spin qubits for quantum information processing, provided that they preserve their spin coherence for a sufficient time to allow for computation and error correction. Here we report the rare isolation of stable Zr(III) aryloxide complexes, where Zr is an earth-abundant metal ion with a coherently manipulable electron spin. Density functional theory calculations reveal the trigonal planar d 1 geometry stabilizes a 4 d z 2 –5 s hybrid singly occupied molecular orbital with little ligand contribution and significant s character (25–27%), yielding large isotropic hyperfine coupling constants of 803–809 MHz. We observed long spin–lattice relaxation times ( T 1 ) up to 87 ms and dephasing times ( T m , T m CPMG ) up to 123 μs using isotope-selective pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy. Nutation experiments further showed coherent manipulation of several electronic and electronuclear transitions. This study introduces Zr(III) aryloxides as competitive molecular qudits and expands the scope of metal ions to more earth-abundant metals.

articles.title: Cytokine circuits in CNS homeostasis and disease
articles.abstract: In their Review, Becher et al. discuss how selected cytokine networks preserve, destabilize and restore central nervous system integrity.

articles.title: GutPath links immune archetypes and single-cell landscapes in the infected gut
articles.abstract: A single-cell gene expression atlas, spanning six phylogenetically diverse infections, reveals pathogen-specific reprogramming of the intestinal epithelium and a novel Yersinia-induced enterocyte state that is spatially linked to tissue pathology.

articles.title: Bispecific dual T cell agonist invikafusp alfa in solid tumors: the phase 1/2 START-001 trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology Congress 2026, in a phase 1/2 trial in participants with solid tumors, invika, a first-in-class bispecific agonistic antibody that selectively targets the prevalent Vβ6/Vβ10 T cell subsets, was well tolerated, enabling the selection of a recommended phase 2 dose for further testing, and showed a preliminary efficacy signal in both immunologically hot and cold tumors.

articles.title: Determinants of response to CAR T cell therapy in a multicenter, multi-trial cohort analysis of patients with lymphoma
articles.abstract: In patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) treated with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy, factors associated with efficacy overlap with prognostic biomarkers. Currently, there is no consensus on optimal product characteristics. We analyzed the phenotypic attributes of the anti-CD19 CAR T therapy axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) from 580 patients with NHL across multiple clinical trials with long-term follow-up (median, 41.9 months). A high proportion of naive-like (CCR7+CD45RA+) T cells was the most significant feature associated with prolonged progression-free survival (PFS; hazard ratio = 0.46, 95% confidence interval: 0.31−0.68, P = 9.8 × 10−5, high versus low naive-like T cell groups) without impacting safety. The relationship between naive-like T cells and efficacy was independent of tumor microenvironment characteristics (assessed in 112 patients). In multivariate models, the naive-like phenotype outperformed clinicopathologic features such as inflammatory markers and tumor burden, remaining significant after adjusting for product expansion. An inverse correlation was observed between prior lines of therapy and the proportion of naive-like T cells in both product and matched apheresis samples, suggesting a benefit of earlier intervention. The key findings were validated in an independent cohort of 203 patients treated with axi-cel-based therapy or brexucabtagene autoleucel. Mass cytometry by time-of-flight analysis of products from a subgroup of 116 patients confirmed an association between a CD8 naive-like T cell phenotype lacking expression of exhaustion markers, such as TIGIT, LAG-3 and PD-1, and PFS. The evidence generated by this study has the potential to advance the development of more effective cellular therapies. A large comprehensive analysis of clinical trial samples from patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma who were treated with anti-CD19 CAR T therapy shows that a high proportion of naive-like and stem cell memory-like CCR7+CD45RA+ T cells in the pre-infusion CAR T product correlates with improved and prolonged clinical benefit, which was validated in an independent external cohort including different products.

articles.title: Lymph node-targeted, mKRAS-specific amphiphile vaccine in pancreatic cancer: the randomized phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026, in a randomized phase 2 trial evaluating an off-the-shelf lymph node-targeting peptide vaccine in patients with mutated KRAS pancreatic cancer within 6 months of standard curative intent therapy, the primary endpoint of disease-free survival was not met, but prespecified subgroup analyses showed significant disease-free survival benefit in the vaccine arm for patients with circulating tumor DNA-negative disease and in those without prior radiation treatment.

articles.title: Putting conversational AI to the test in primary care
articles.abstract: A patient-facing conversational AI showed promising feasibility and safety in a single-center primary care setting, providing a basis for larger-scale evaluation.

articles.title: The human microbiome and chronic disease: ten strategic priorities for research and public health
articles.abstract: The human microbiome has emerged as one of the most consequential frontiers in biomedical science. An international group of leading microbiome scientists, convened by the US Department of Health and Human Services, presents a strategic vision for realizing its potential to transform public health.

articles.title: Benchmarking segmentation methods for spatial transcriptomics
articles.abstract: This Analysis benchmarks segmentation methods across different datasets and presents Nextflow, a pipeline for standardized method selection for spatial transcriptomics.

articles.title: NanostarDB: an interactive knowledgebase for standardized annotation, discovery and reuse of nucleic acid nanostructure designs
articles.abstract: The lack of standardized reporting and annotation of nucleic acid nanostructures limits reproducibility, interoperability and the efficient reuse of published designs. NanostarDB is a community-driven knowledgebase that standardizes nucleic acid nanostar designs through persistent identifiers, structural annotations, and integrated computational tools for design exploration, analysis and reuse, and is compliant with principles of findability, accessibility, interoprability and reusability (FAIR).

articles.title: Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles
articles.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are present in biofluids and may be useful biomarkers to non-invasively monitor brain cells, but isolating cell type-specific EVs remains challenging. Here we introduce an approach to immuno-isolate EVs from neurons and glia based on protein surface markers. We first selected transmembrane proteins suitable as cell type-specific EV markers based on gene expression and EV proteomic data. We developed a high-purity EV isolation method and cataloged the proteins present on EVs in human cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. We then computationally identified cell type-specific candidate markers for isolating EVs from neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and microglia. Using ultrasensitive immunoassays against several predicted neuron-specific proteins, we confirmed one marker, NRXN3, as present on EVs in cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. Finally, we developed efficient EV immuno-isolation methods and applied them to isolate NRXN3 + EVs. Our work provides a general methodology for the isolation of cell type-specific EVs, advancing the goal of using EVs to study brain diseases.

articles.title: Sustained antidepressant-like effects of psychedelics through 5-HT2AR–β-arrestin signaling
articles.abstract: This study shows that the sustained antidepressant-like effect of psychedelics is driven by 5-HT2A receptor–β-arrestin signaling. Repeated low-dose LSD preserves this effect in mice without inducing hallucinogenic-like behaviors in mice or monkeys.

articles.title: Beating the break-even point with autonomous quantum error correction
articles.abstract: Conventional quantum error correction requires repeated measurements and real-time feedback, which are technically complex. An autonomous implementation that eliminates these while beating the break-even point is demonstrated in a trapped-ion system.

articles.title: Maxwell’s demon with memory
articles.abstract: Maxwell’s demon may produce work using the information it obtains by measuring the system as fuel. Now, it is shown that the amount of produced work increases if the demon takes information about the dynamical correlations of the system into account.

articles.title: Particle collisions on a quantum computer
articles.abstract: Elementary particle physics rests on the discovery of particles produced in high-energy collider experiments. Now, a model collision above the threshold for particle production has been simulated on a quantum computer.

articles.title: The physical chemistry behind porous liquids
articles.abstract: Margarida Costa Gomes, CNRS Research Professor at École Normale Supérieure de Lyon, talks to Nature Synthesis about understanding the molecular behaviour of porous liquids and the challenges of translating that understanding into functional materials.

articles.title: Understanding porous liquids
articles.abstract: Becky Greenaway, Associate Professor (Reader) and Royal Society University Research Fellow at Imperial College London, talks to Nature Synthesis about developing automated high-throughput experimentation to design porous liquids as well as persistent challenges in the field.

articles.title: Quantum Advantage for Sensing Properties of Classical Fields
articles.abstract: Researchers demonstrate a quantum sensing protocol that uses entanglement and squeezing to learn diverse classical signal properties with subvacuum precision.

articles.title: Toward Complete Characterization of Topological Insulators and Superconductors: A Systematic Construction of Topological Invariants Based on Atiyah-Hirzebruch Spectral Sequence
articles.abstract: A framework based on the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space yields topological invariants that classify stable superconducting phases across 159 space groups.

articles.title: Physics for plays, not for work
articles.abstract: Nilanjan P. Choudhury left physics for a corporate software job, then returned to it for playwriting.

articles.title: An autonomous macrophage-nociceptor mechanosensory relay drives chronic visceral pain
articles.abstract: Visceral pain in ulcerative colitis is conventionally attributed to inflammatory cascades, though whether immune cells directly transduce mechanical cues into nociceptive signals remains unclear. Here, we show that the mechanosensitive channel Piezo1 in tissue-resident CX3CR1 + macrophages directly drives colitis-associated visceral hypersensitivity. Piezo1 triggered calcium influx and nuclear factor κB nuclear translocation that occupied the Ngf promoter to induce nerve growth factor (NGF) synthesis. This macrophage-derived NGF remodeled and sensitized the peripheral terminals of TRPV1 + nociceptive afferents in neuroimmune units. Using a minimally inflammatory intracolonic zymosan model, we found that this Piezo1-NGF-TrkA axis functions as a direct mechanosensory relay largely independent of cytokine cascades. Genetic deletion of Piezo1 or Ngf in resident macrophages, or Ntrk1 in TRPV1 + neurons, abolished visceral hyperalgesia in both inflammatory and noninflammatory models. These findings reveal tissue-resident macrophages as autonomous mechanical sensors that establish a direct, parallel pain transmission pathway to sensory nerves during disease.

articles.title: ILC2-derived IL-9 promotes eosinophil-mediated antitumor activity
articles.abstract: Innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) regulate tissue immunity, yet their roles in tumor control remain incompletely understood. Here, we combined analyses of human sequencing datasets with genetic ablation mouse models and adoptive transfer experiments to identify that glucocorticoid-induced tumor necrosis factor receptor (GITR) engagement on tumor-infiltrating group 2 ILCs (ILC2s) induced activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3) and robust interleukin-9 (IL-9) production, exceeding the modest coinduction of IL-5 and IL-13. ILC2-derived IL-9 promoted intratumoral eosinophil accumulation by enhancing survival, tissue retention, and cytotoxicity through tumor-induced IL-9 receptor expression. Eosinophil ablation abolished GITR-mediated tumor control, whereas adoptive eosinophil transfer restored it. This IL-9–eosinophil pathway suppressed tumor growth in the absence of adaptive lymphocytes. In human datasets, IL-9 and eosinophil signatures were associated with favorable prognosis in melanoma and lung adenocarcinoma. These findings define an innate pathway linking ILC2s to eosinophil-mediated tumor immunity and support GITR agonism as a therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: [Articles] Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials
articles.abstract: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis.

articles.title: The clinical relevance of multiple sclerosis genetics: from susceptibility to disease severity and progression
articles.abstract: Large-scale genome-wide association studies have identified hundreds of multiple sclerosis risk loci, most of which implicate immune pathways and establish multiple sclerosis as a highly polygenic, immune-mediated disease. These findings help explain why immune-modifying therapies suppress relapses and new lesion formation. However, susceptibility genetics does not adequately explain disability accumulation, variation in disease course, or treatment response. Evidence from rare-variant studies, genetic studies of disease severity and disability progression, epigenetic analyses, gene-environment studies, and Epstein-Barr virus research is beginning to extend this genetic framework from susceptibility to disease expression. Still, the direct clinical relevance of this research remains constrained by modest individual-level predictive value, underpowered studies of genetic determinants of disease severity and disability progression, complex regulatory mechanisms linking variants to function, and restricted generalisability across populations. At present, multiple sclerosis genetics is most useful for interpreting mechanisms, prioritising therapeutic targets, supporting causal inference, informing biomarker discovery, and enriching research cohorts. Future clinical value will likely depend on integrating genetic architecture with longitudinal clinical, imaging, biomarker, and multi-omic data to identify the contexts in which prevention or treatment is most likely to succeed.

articles.title: Perioperative chemotherapy and stereotactic body radiotherapy versus perioperative chemotherapy alone in patients with high-risk, localised pancreatic cancer (MASTERPLAN): an open-label, phase 2, multicentre, randomised trial of the Australasian Gastro-Intestinal Trials Group
articles.abstract: BackgroundPancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has poor outcomes and high rates of locoregional recurrence. MASTERPLAN evaluated whether stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) reduced locoregional recurrence in patients with high-risk, localised PDAC.MethodsMASTERPLAN was an open-label, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted across 14 hospitals in Australia and New Zealand. Eligible participants were aged 18 years or older with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1, and had previously untreated localised PDAC with at least one high-risk feature, including tumour size more than 4 cm, extrapancreatic extension, node-positive disease, borderline resectable disease, or locally advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (2:1) using the method of minimisation to investigator-choice chemotherapy, with or without SBRT, stratified by participant cohort (potentially operable vs inoperable), planned chemotherapy regimen, randomisation before or within the first 28 days of chemotherapy, and institution. Chemotherapy consisted of mFOLFIRINOX (day 1 oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, irinotecan 150 mg/m2, leucovorin 50 mg, and fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46 h every 14 days for six cycles; all intravenous) or gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 every 28 days for three cycles; both intravenous). SBRT was delivered as 40 Gy in five fractions, with two to four fractions delivered per week, with real-time radiotherapy quality assurance. Surgical resection was considered following induction therapy, followed by a planned further 12 weeks of adjuvant chemotherapy with either mFOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine plus capecitabine (28-day cycles of 1000 mg/m2 intravenous gemcitabine administered on days 1, 8, and 15 with 830 mg/m2 oral capecitabine twice daily administered on days 1-21). Participants deemed not suitable for surgery continued the same chemotherapy for an additional 12 weeks with reassessment for surgical suitability permitted, for a total planned duration of chemotherapy of 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was 12-month locoregional recurrence in the intention-to-treat population, with safety endpoints analysed by treatment received. The trial planned to recruit 120 patients but due to slow accrual closed to recruitment early on Jan 6, 2025. Trial closure and database lock occurred on July 21, 2026. This trial was registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trial Registry (ACTRN12619000409178) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04089150), and is complete.FindingsBetween Feb 26, 2020, and Jan 6, 2025, 74 participants (43 [58%] male, 31 [42%] female) were randomly assigned to chemotherapy and SBRT (n=49) or chemotherapy alone (n=25). After a median follow-up of 3·2 years (IQR 1·9-4·3), 12-month locoregional recurrence was 20·2% (95% CI 9·9-33·1) in the SBRT group and 52·0% (30·3-69·9) in the chemotherapy alone group (subdistribution hazard ratio 0·44 [95% CI 0·22-0·88]; p=0·022). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 33 (70%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group and 16 (64%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·27), with one (4%) treatment-related death secondary to biliary tract infection in the chemotherapy alone group. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were diarrhoea (seven [15%] in the SBRT group vs five [20%] in the chemotherapy alone group), and thromboembolic events (three [6%]) vs one [4%]). Overall grade 3 or higher serious adverse events occurred in 30 (64%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group, and 14 (56%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·24).…

Genome-wide human T cell screens: barriers and design

We discuss how context shapes perturbation effects, and how readouts guide prioritization, with implications for T cell engineering in solid tumors.

articles.title: Mesenchymal stem cells: towering ambitions, shaky foundations
articles.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have been a feature of stem cell research since the early 1990s. Despite long-standing questions concerning the identity, characteristics, physiological functions, and potential therapeutic uses of these cells, MSC studies are now published more frequently than those of any other stem cell type. Over the past decade, this increase in the MSC literature is attributable almost entirely to publications by scientists in China. Reviewing the history and present state of MSC research, we explore why this might be and propose steps that stakeholders in China and other countries might take to address what has become one of the more perplexing developments in contemporary stem cell research.

articles.title: Dependency grammar remains the simplest theory of grammar: a reply to Fujita
articles.abstract: In the original article [1], I claimed that dependency grammar is the simplest theory of grammar. All theories of grammar have rules for connecting words together to make larger units. In dependency grammar, these connections are directly between words. In phrase structure grammars, there is slightly more structure than in dependency grammar, consisting of nonterminal categories for the connected elements, such as the noun phrase and the verb phrase. I argued that these two alternatives are somewhat interchangeable.

articles.title: Evidence supports constituency-based syntax, movement, and unpronounced elements
articles.abstract: Gibson advocates dependency grammar [1], contrasting it with constituency-based accounts that posit movement and phonologically null (unpronounced) syntactic elements [2,3]. Dependency grammar represents sentence structure through word-to-word relations, whereas constituency-based accounts represent sentence structure by grouping words into larger hierarchical constituents. Movement accounts for cases in which a constituent appears in one position but is interpreted in another. For example, in ‘Who did you call?’, ‘Who’ appears sentence-initially but is interpreted as the object of ‘call’; this is analysed as movement from the object position to the sentence-initial position.

articles.abstract: Sulfur-assisted oxidative coupling of methane (SOCM) provides a direct route for methane conversion to ethylene over transition-metal sulfides (TMSs), with sulfur-rich surface environments involved in methane activation and ethylene formation....

articles.title: Lifestyle-induced regulatory T cell fragility primes adverse events after immune checkpoint blockade
articles.abstract: Dietary and microbial alterations increase susceptibility to irAEs by promoting IFN-γ-driven Treg fragility and cytotoxic tissue-resident T cell responses. Treg-specific disruption of IFN-γ signaling restores tissue homeostasis and reduces irAEs without compromising antitumor immunity, highlighting Treg stability as a potential therapeutic strategy for limiting checkpoint blockade toxicity.

articles.title: MCT6 is an intestinal Lac-Phe exporter required for metformin-associated weight loss
articles.abstract: The orphan transporter MCT6 is the route by which the meal- and exercise-associated metabolite Lac-Phe exits intestinal cells and enters the blood. Mice lacking gut MCT6 cannot maintain normal circulating Lac-Phe levels and exhibit resistance to metformin-associated weight loss, establishing metabolite export as a regulatory node for systemic action.

articles.title: Metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive
articles.abstract: Single-molecule imaging reveals that metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive, and it relies on the repeated recruitment of Pol α and Pol δ rather than their stable replisome association, thereby uncoupling leading- and lagging-strand synthesis.

articles.title: Genetic dissection of rapid proteolysis identifies TXNDC15 as a key factor of ERAD and lipid homeostasis
articles.abstract: ER-associated protein degradation is central to organelle homeostasis, yet many regulatory components remain unknown. Liu et al. exploit the rapid turnover of short-lived proteins to identify TXNDC15 as a noncanonical MARCHF6-dependent ERAD factor that links proteostasis to lipid homeostasis, illustrating how rapid proteolysis can uncover hidden metabolic regulatory circuits.

articles.title: Microbial inositol phosphates orchestrate host diurnal metabolism and energy homeostasis via HDAC3
articles.abstract: Zhang et al. show that gut microbial inositol phosphate metabolism transduces feeding cues into intestinal diurnal rhythms through histone deacetylase 3. This pathway activates PGC-1α and enhances nutrient absorption during feeding, promoting juvenile growth during undernutrition but exacerbating obesity during overnutrition.

Lactate depletion suppresses repair-associated lactylation and impairs MRN-mediated DNA repair, while Au-Pt catalysis amplifies radiation-induced damage. This metabolic remodeling simultaneously alleviates immunosuppression and promotes systemic antitumor immunity.

By selectively removing undesired cells during development via synthetic apoptosis circuits, this approach enhances tissue maturation and refines morphogenesis across organoid and embryoid models.

articles.abstract: Identical-location electron microscopy enables particle-resolved tracking of structural evolution, providing deep insights into catalyst stability and the structure–function relationship beyond what ensemble-averaged analysis can offer.

articles.abstract: Chemical stitching tailors the closed-pore mouth of hard carbon, forming a high-modulus, inorganic-rich intrapore solid electrolyte interphase that mechanically confines Na-cluster growth and enables fast sodium storage.

articles.abstract: TFSM constructs a bidirectional hydrogen-bonding bridge at the perovskite/C 60 interface, enabling efficient charge transfer and reduced energy loss, leading to 27.49% efficient inverted perovskite solar cells and 17.5% flexible modules.

articles.title: Hydromorphological Restoration of Streams Does Not Ensure the Recovery of Ecosystem Functioning
articles.abstract: Ecological restoration is widely expected to recover multiple ecosystem attributes, yet biological structure and ecosystem functioning may respond differently to hydromorphological restoration. Interpreting functional change is further complicated because higher or lower process rates do not inherently indicate recovery; their ecological meaning depends on how degraded and restored conditions compare with an appropriate reference state. We synthesised 582 effect sizes from 66 studies to quantify responses of nine ecosystem functions to hydromorphological restoration of streams and to assess whether changes in biological structure coincided with functional responses. Ecosystem‐function responses varied substantially among processes and baselines. Gross primary production was significantly higher in degraded than in reference streams, illustrating that elevated functional rates do not necessarily indicate reference‐like ecological conditions. Restoration did not consistently reverse degradation‐associated functional differences: denitrification was significantly lower in restored than in degraded streams, whereas nitrate uptake remained significantly lower in restored than in reference streams. Other restored–reference differences were generally weak or uncertain. Functional responses did not differ systematically among broad restoration‐measure categories. Restoration age was associated with changes in gross primary production and denitrification relative to degraded conditions, but none of the functions showed detectable convergence towards or divergence from reference conditions through time. In studies measuring both biological structure and ecosystem functioning, biological responses to restoration were generally positive relative to degraded conditions, whereas functional responses were more variable. However, the available evidence was too uncertain to conclude that biological and functional responses systematically differed. Our synthesis shows that functional recovery cannot be inferred either from restoration‐associated change alone or from concurrent biological recovery. Assessing restoration success therefore requires direct measurements of ecosystem processes and ecologically meaningful reference conditions that reveal whether functional change represents movement towards a process‐specific restoration target.

articles.title: Non‐Linear Increases of Soil Carbon Stocks and Turnover Along Alpine Greening Gradients on Different Bedrocks
articles.abstract: Alpine ecosystems are experiencing warming, leading to alpine greening—an upward migration and enhanced productivity of vegetation. Although soils represent the largest carbon (C) stocks in these ecosystems, impacts of greening on soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamics remain unknown, especially in the high alpine zone. We measured SOC stocks, quality and radiocarbon (14C) based turnover rates along elevation gradients from (sub)alpine forests to periglacial zones on three bedrock types, representing trajectories of changes in climate and vegetation and weathering regime. Data were linked to SOC stabilizing pedogenic oxides (PO) to assess the potential of soils to sequester C upon alpine greening. Results show pronounced decreases in SOC stocks (from 10 to 1 kg C m−2) and increases in 14C‐based turnover times (from decades to millennia) with increasing elevation. This pattern followed a non‐linear sigmoidal function with a threshold at the vegetation line where grassland transitions to the nival zone. High alpine soils showed low SOC:PO ratios, indicating low C saturation and a high capacity to stabilize SOC on reactive minerals. However, negligible 14C‐derived carbon inputs suggest that low vegetation productivity constrains SOC sequestration in these soils. In contrast, towards lower elevation with a warmer climate, grassland soils receive higher C inputs, but appear more C saturated, leading to greater SOC turnover but little SOC stock changes. Bedrock influenced SOC dynamics with approximately 50% smaller SOC stocks and faster turnover rates in dolomitic than in siliceous soils, due to slower weathering and lower SOC stabilization. Using elevation as a space‐for‐time substitution, we infer that SOC sequestration under alpine greening will be confined to areas around the vegetation line, with parent material influencing the magnitude of C uptake. Future projections of SOC dynamics should account for vegetation shifts and bedrock‐driven stabilization to constrain the role of alpine soils in land carbon‐climate feedbacks.

articles.title: INDITEK‐2.0: A Bayesian inverse modelling framework for mechanistic evolutionary processes
articles.abstract: Mechanistic eco‐evolutionary models are powerful tools for understanding how life diversified over geological timescales, yet estimating their parameters remains a key challenge. The high computational requirements of these models make probabilistic inversion methods unfeasible. We introduce INDITEK‐2.0, a novel Bayesian inverse modelling framework built upon the cost‐efficient and spatially explicit INDITEK diversification engine. To validate this framework, we conducted a proof‐of‐concept study. We first generated synthetic global distributions of current biodiversity of marine invertebrates using INDITEK with known parameter values. To mimic field data, some realistic random Gaussian errors were added. We then used our Bayesian inverse modelling framework to recover these original (true) parameter values from the dataset of current biodiversity distributions after 500 million years of diversification. We also conducted a suite of sensitivity analyses by disabling specific mechanisms of the model. Our solution is a probability distribution on the parameter space, and we show that the method successfully recovered the target parameter values with a relatively low degree of uncertainty. INDITEK‐2.0's ability to probabilistically infer underlying evolutionary processes provides a new, spatially explicit modelling tool for reconstructing the evolutionary history of biodiversity across Earth's ecosystems and taxonomic groups.

articles.title: HP1 can act independently of H3K9 methylation to promote heterochromatin focus formation, gene repression, and organogenesis
articles.abstract: Delaney et al. show that HP1HPL-2 can silence genes and restrict organogenesis independently of histone H3K9 methylation and the major H3K9 HMT SETDBMET-2. HP1HPL-2 and SETDB1MET-2 form heterochromatic foci by binding distinct cofactors, and these foci, not H3K9me3, track with gene silencing and developmental control of organogenesis.

articles.title: Cryptic Diversity and Patterns of Structure in Nine Species of North Pacific Rockfishes (Sebastes spp. and Sebastolobus spp.)
articles.abstract: Understanding how habitat and life history traits contribute to population genetic structure is critical for evaluating conservation risks and identifying optimal management of wild populations. Species derived from adaptive radiations can provide a useful model for studying such patterns because the presence of some consistent traits allows for closer examination of attributes which differ. Here, we examine population structure in rockfishes (genera Sebastes and Sebastolobus), a group of speciose, recently diverged marine fishes that exhibit a continuum of genetic structure, from cryptic species to putative genetic panmixia. In this study, we analyse low‐coverage whole genome resequencing data from nine rockfish species and identify four major types of genetic differentiation: cryptic diversity, isolation‐by‐distance (IBD), no detectable structure (putative panmixia) and no detectable structure with a single genomic region putatively underlying local adaptation. Two species, Dark (Sebastes ciliatus) and Northern (S. polyspinis) rockfishes, each exhibited cryptic diversity consisting of two sympatric groups differentiated at every chromosome throughout the genome. Black rockfish in Southeast Alaska also had two genetic groups, despite an overall signal of IBD from the West Coast of North America through the Gulf of Alaska (GOA). Five species showed evidence of genetic panmixia throughout the sampled range, while Yelloweye Rockfish exhibited high gene flow across ~4000 km, from southern California to the GOA, but had strong differentiation between the Salish Sea and the outer coast. Of the species in which no structure was detected, only Blackspotted Rockfish had one outlier region exhibiting signatures of potential local adaptation. Our results highlight how multiple mechanisms likely promote genetic structure in rockfishes, hinting at tentative links to depth distributions and offshore habitats that might influence patterns of differentiation in rockfishes more broadly. Further, this study provides genetic data for some of the most abundant rockfishes in commercial fisheries in the Northeast Pacific, enhancing the scientific information available for informing fisheries management.

articles.title: Temporal Community Assembly of Bacteria and Protists in Different Habitats of a Mountain Lake
articles.abstract: Whether microbial community assembly is primarily deterministic (selection‐driven) or stochastic (dispersal‐driven) remains a central debate in microbial ecology. We investigated community assembly of bacteria and protists and their driving ecological processes in mountain Lake Tovel using a 5‐year 16S and 18S rRNA metabarcoding dataset. The frequencies of assembly mechanisms and their processes depend on the considered temporal scale. We assessed the influence of temporal scale (years, seasons, temporal distances from 1 to 48 months across all years) and year‐pooling (a common strategy in the assessment of assembly patterns) on the inference of community assembly in the upper euphotic (0–3 m), lower euphotic (3–25 m) and deep hypolimnetic (30–35 m) layers. Focusing on single years, bacteria showed more often different assembly mechanisms (both deterministic and stochastic) across layers and years than protists. Year‐pooling hid the inter‐year differences and preserved the signal of the most frequent single‐year process. A lagged effect of water temperature on bacterial community assembly was found, while an immediate effect on protist assembly. Bacterial and protists' niche width was generally independent of year‐pooling and increased with depth. Our study showed that different temporal scales and depth layers should be considered to gain a comprehensive overview on community assembly.

articles.title: Transposable Element Activity Is Associated With the Rise of Termite Diversity
articles.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) have long been hypothesized as a driver of lineage diversification due to their mutagenic ability. However, the correlation between rates of TE activity and diversification has rarely been tested, since it is challenging to measure the rate of TE activity in the deep past. Here, we investigated TE activity during the last ~150 million years of termite evolution. First, we determined the timing of TE amplification events using the sequence divergence of TE copies and identified two waves of TE bursts that took place synchronously across termite lineages, coinciding with the two major phases of termite diversification. Furthermore, we built phylogenetic trees using the presence/absence of orthologous TE insertions in the flanking regions of Ultraconserved Elements (UCEs), in which the branch length provided a measure of the rate of TE insertion/deletion near UCEs along the termite phylogenetic tree. The rate of TE insertion/deletion near UCEs predicted up to 34.8% of the variation in the termite net diversification rate. Overall, these results supported TEs as an important contributor to species diversification. More broadly, this study provided a phylogenomic approach to quantify TE activity in the deep past.

articles.title: A self-shadowing black hole accretion disk at sub-Eddington luminosities
articles.abstract: A multiwavelength study reveals a vertically extended inner disk in a black hole X-ray binary at unexpectedly low luminosities, reshaping its emission and shielding the outer disk, with implications for its physical and observational properties.

articles.title: Human Argonaute 2 is a programmable targeting domain for RNA editing
articles.abstract: ALTER is a programmable RNA base editor built entirely from human proteins. By using human AGO2 instead of bacterial CRISPR–Cas proteins, ALTER mitigates a key risk factor for harmful immune responses in therapeutic applications while also proving generally more effective than dCas13-based editors.

articles.title: Recordanelles capture transient gene expression in single human cells
articles.abstract: RNA sequencing can capture high-resolution snapshots of a cell’s transcriptome, but transient changes in individual cells cannot be captured over long periods at a transcriptome-wide scale. Now, a synthetic organelle termed the ‘recordanelle’ can record cellular RNAs in cells for several days and be read with single-cell sensitivity.

articles.abstract: Author Correction: Multiomic analysis of familial adenomatous polyposis reveals molecular pathways associated with early tumorigenesis

articles.title: Inducing local heating fields in ferromagnetic high-entropy alloys to inhibit (bi)carbonate formation for durable CO2 electroreduction
articles.abstract: Carbonate precipitation at the cathode caused by local alkalinity during electrocatalytic CO2 reduction represents a major limitation to carbon efficiency and system durability. Now local heating induced in ferromagnetic high-entropy alloys by an alternating magnetic field reduces carbonate precipitation, extending durability in alkaline and neutral electrolytes.

articles.title: Water regulates interface access and reactivity in CO2 electrolysis
articles.abstract: Understanding interfacial processes is important for achieving efficient CO2 electrolysis at high current densities. Now, two-dimensional correlated operando Raman spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics provide insight into the relationship between interfacial species, water structure and product selectivity under application-relevant conditions, revealing the role of water in regulating CO2 availability at the electrode–electrolyte interface.

articles.title: Heatwave-induced capacity bottlenecks in European electricity grids
articles.abstract: This study models how heatwaves raise demand and reduce generation and transmission capacity across Western European power grids, showing how heatwaves can expose bottlenecks that simplified models may miss and providing a basis for resilience planning.

articles.title: Serine protease inhibitor A3 is a soluble SIRPα ligand that suppresses inflammation and antitumor immunity
articles.abstract: Here the authors show that SERPINA3 is a soluble SIRPα ligand with immunosuppressive and therapeutic activity against inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, whereas cancer cells overexpress SERPINA3 and blocking it can be protective.

articles.title: Strain turns carbon dioxide into circular polyesters
articles.abstract: The high ring strain of cyclic hydrocarbons enables alternating copolymerization with carbon dioxide to produce polyesters amenable to closed-loop recycling.

articles.title: Zero-field spin-wave networks with integrated non-volatile memory
articles.abstract: Ferrimagnetic nanostructures with low spin-wave damping are used to demonstrate the reprogrammable routing of spin-wave signals across a wide range of frequencies.

articles.title: CauTrigger: deciphering biological system state transitions by hierarchical causal decomposition
articles.abstract: CauTrigger is a hierarchical deep latent variable model that can identify potential causal triggers and predict outcomes of perturbation events.

articles.title: OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
articles.abstract: OpenDVP enables scalable and high-resolution proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods.

articles.title: Tracing causal cascades underlying biological state changes
articles.abstract: Maps constructed from omics data to identify the causal mechanisms underlying state transitions have not been established. We developed CauTrigger, which treats state transitions as layered causal cascades rather than isolated molecular changes, effectively separating causal signals from spurious variation. CauTrigger prioritizes potential upstream triggers, predicts perturbation responses and helps turn omics measurements into testable mechanistic hypotheses.

articles.title: Behavioral genomics identifies Creld1 as a cross-modal regulator of somatosensation
articles.abstract: Jiang et al. developed a robust postnatal knockout platform for somatosensory genomics and behavioral screening, identifying Creld1 as a cross-modal regulator of somatosensation through its control of sensory neuron excitability via voltage-gated sodium channels.

articles.title: Network geometry shapes the transformation of task representations across the human cortex
articles.abstract: The dimensionality of intrinsic brain connectivity systematically shapes how task representations compress and expand across the cortex, and activity flow modeling shows the active role of network geometry in generating the transformation.

articles.title: Teleportation transition of surface codes on a superconducting quantum processor
articles.abstract: Quantum teleportation is often discussed for individual quantum systems, but fault-tolerant quantum computers will encode information in multiqubit states. Now teleportation of surface code logical states has been demonstrated.

articles.title: Wigner crystals get dressed
articles.abstract: When repulsion overcomes their tendency to move freely, electrons can arrange into a crystal. Two experiments have now identified Wigner polarons, quasiparticles whose optical signatures reveal the collective response of the electron lattice.

articles.title: Cancer theranostics
articles.abstract: Theranostics integrates diagnostic imaging with targeted therapy to enhance cancer treatment. In this Review, Sofias et al. discuss recent advances in radiotheranostic strategies, advances in nanotheranostic and microtheranostic platforms, and image-guided therapeutic and surgical interventions in oncology.

articles.abstract: Edge-mediated nonlocal transport measurements in thin Fe(Te,Se) devices reveal a robust conductance plateau governed by spontaneous magnetic ordering.

articles.title: New strategies for enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones
articles.abstract: Enantiopure α-stereogenic ketones constitute prevalent scaffolds in numerous natural products and pharmaceuticals while also serving as versatile and valuable building blocks for diverse synthetic transformations. Conventional methods for constructing chiral α-stereogenic ketones typically rely on the reaction of ketone enolates or enamines with electrophiles. However, the need for strong bases to generate these intermediates often limits the substrate scope. Additionally, achieving stereo- and regioselective formation of enolates or enamines from unsymmetrical dialkyl ketones remains a significant challenge. This review provides an overview of recent advances in the enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones, highlighting emerging strategies beyond classical chemistry, such as radical reactions, nucleophilic reactions, acyl–nickel-enabled cross-coupling, and enzyme-catalyzed dehalogenation.

articles.title: Selection-for-prediction: rethinking early cognitive development
articles.abstract: For decades, core knowledge accounts have proposed that early cognition is organized by innate, domain-specific conceptual or concept-like representations of objects, physical events, number, and agents. I propose a different starting point: infants’ behaviors may arise from domain-general attentional priors—evolutionarily shaped selection biases—interacting with perceptual mechanisms that organize information and support perceptual prediction, rather than from abstract, postperceptual representations. Attentional priors favor ecologically consequential information, including continuity, contact, and synchrony. When such information is disrupted, perceptual prediction error—rather than conceptual contradiction—may produce violation-of-expectation effects. Grounded in constraints on visual input and neural processing, this framework accounts for early successes and systematic failures, suggesting that development begins with perceptual-attentional mechanisms that shape selection, organization, prediction, and learning.

articles.title: A bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor for ferroptosis induction in vivo and tumor suppression
articles.abstract: Selective pharmacological induction of ferroptosis in vivo has remained difficult. By developing the bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor KY0418, this work links systemic ferroptosis induction to tissue metabolic remodeling and demonstrates context-dependent suppression of tumor progression, including metastatic spread.

articles.title: Contrasting demographic impacts of Roman colonization and early medieval migrations in the Iberian Peninsula
articles.abstract: Roman and post-Roman Iberia was transformed by extensive mobility across the Mediterranean, with large-scale inputs from Eastern Mediterranean and North African populations reshaping its genetic landscape. During the migration period, Central-Northern European ancestry arrived largely through elite-associated groups that intermarried with local populations but did not replace the highly diverse population that had formed under Roman rule.

articles.title: In vivo Gene Writing with engineered retrotransposons
articles.abstract: Computational reconstruction, screening, and engineering of non-LTR retrotransposons uncovers elements, termed Gene Writers, that enable stable transgene integration in human cells using all-RNA delivery. After extensive characterization and optimization, Gene Writers is deployed to generate functional CAR-T cells in vivo in a humanized mouse model.

Proteomic atlas of T cell exhaustion defines proteostatic collapse
articles.abstract: A multi-omic atlas of human T cell exhaustion reveals that dysfunctional T cells undergo broad remodeling of protein turnover and ubiquitin regulation that is not captured by transcriptomic analysis. The E3 ubiquitin ligase RNF166 regulates T cell persistence and anti-tumor function, highlighting proteostasis as a targetable axis for improving immunotherapy.

Proteasome inhibition bidirectionally regulates ferroptosis sensitivity
articles.abstract: How proteasome function shapes ferroptosis sensitivity is poorly understood. Murray et al. demonstrate that proteasome inhibition enhances sensitivity to ferroptosis induced by direct inhibition of GPX4, while protecting against system xc− inhibitors. Sensitization to GPX4 inhibitors requires protein synthesis and is opposed by activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4).

articles.title: A phage-encoded small RNA that mimics chimeric guide to inhibit CRISPR-Cas9
articles.abstract: Chen et al. identify rAcrIIA1, a phage-encoded chimeric crRNA-tracrRNA mimic that competitively blocks Cas9 guide loading and DNA interference. This reprogrammable RNA guide enables efficient genome editing, gene silencing, and diagnostics, with enhanced trans-cleavage activity.

articles.title: CNS targeted AAV gene therapies: Recent advances and clinical insights
articles.abstract: Brown and colleagues review recent approaches to overcome limitations to AAV brain gene therapies from vector design through clinical implementation, highlighting how success and patient safety must consider routes of administration, target engagement, and dosing.

articles.title: Inhibition of the CTP synthase 1 prevents GVHD and delays skin graft rejection revealing distinct alloreactive T cell responses
articles.abstract: Allogeneic transplants can trigger graft-versus-host disease and graft rejection. Lopes Souza et al. demonstrate that deletion of Ctps1 in T cells prevents GVHD and reduces skin rejection. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of CTPS1 improves survival in acute GVHD, highlighting CTPS1 as a promising therapeutic target for alloreactive T cell responses.
