A self-organized tri-lineage bone model in liquefied microcapsules captures matrix dynamics in early remodeling
articles.abstract: Mano and colleagues have developed a self-organized bone-like model by co-encapsulating stromal and monocytic cells in liquefied gelatin microcapsules. Their direct interaction effectively supports the emergence of osteoblast-, osteocyte-, and osteoclast-like phenotypes, facilitating cellular crosstalk and promoting mineralized matrix formation and turnover without the need for lineage-specific induction.

articles.title: Phase separation of Rbpms sequesters translation elongation machinery to preserve hematopoietic stem cell function
articles.abstract: Yu and colleagues reveal that hematopoietic stem cells employ Rbpms condensates to spatially restrict the translation elongation machinery. By slowing protein synthesis and ensuring proper protein folding, this mechanism preserves proteostasis, quiescence, and LT stem cell function.

articles.title: Programming hot-carrier dynamics in gold nanoclusters for high-gain photodetectors
articles.abstract: Gold nanoclusters have long been limited in optoelectronic applications by sub-picosecond hot-carrier cooling. Here, electron-donating ligands spatially separate the frontier orbitals of Au22 nanoclusters, extending hot-carrier lifetime to nanoseconds and enabling high-performance, stable photodetectors. This work establishes ligand engineering as a general strategy to tune excited-state dynamics in metal nanoclusters, offering chemists a new materials design route for next-generation optoelectronics beyond conventional semiconductors.

articles.title: Strain-Release Cycloadditions: Bicyclobutanes and Beyond
articles.abstract: Strain-release cycloadditions have emerged as powerful reactions for converting distorted ring systems into complex and otherwise hardly attainable organic molecular architectures. This Review encompasses the fundamentals of strain, its role in governing cycloaddition pathways, and offers a systematic examination of strained carbocycles and heterocycles, from bicyclo[1.1.1]butanes and 1-azabicyclo[1.1.1]butanes, housanes and aza-housanes, 2H-azirines and aziridines, azetidines, cyclopropanes, cyclobutanes, oxiranes, oxetanes, and strained alkynes and alkenes. Across these motifs, the general principles that dictate reactivity, the breadth of known cycloadditions and activation strategies, from Brønsted and Lewis acid catalysis to transition-metal activation, photocatalysis, and double strain-release mechanisms, are highlighted. Key opportunities, current limitations, and future directions are outlined.

articles.title: Recent applications of asymmetric hydrogenation in total synthesis of natural products and drugs
articles.abstract: This review focuses on recent advances of asymmetric hydrogenation in the strategic total synthesis of natural products and drug molecules, and outlines future perspectives for this field.

articles.title: Solar vapor generation technologies: fundamentals, innovations and applications
articles.abstract: This Tutorial Review establishes a unified framework connecting the fundamentals of solar vapor generation with materials and structural design, providing guiding principles for efficient, scalable, and sustainable water production.

articles.title: Eco‐Evolutionary Feedback to a Pesticide Worsens the Impact of a Pesticide Switch in a Pivotal Freshwater Non‐Target Species
articles.abstract: Pest management often requires the rotation of insecticides, sequentially exposing non‐target populations to different compounds. In a two‐phased experiment, we assessed whether exposure to the pesticide chlorpyrifos induces rapid evolution in the non‐target species Daphnia magna and quantified the response of control and pre‐exposed populations to a second exposure to the same pesticide, another pesticide with the same mode of action (malathion), or a pesticide with another mode of action (deltamethrin). Chlorpyrifos selection induced rapid shifts in genotype composition and reduced genotype richness and strongly influenced population development following the second exposure. Chlorpyrifos‐selected populations outperformed control populations when subsequently exposed to chlorpyrifos and malathion but underperformed when exposed to deltamethrin. Our results highlight an eco‐evolutionary feedback in which rapid adaptive responses to a pesticide worsen the response when exposed to a different type of pesticide in non‐target species, increasing vulnerability to common agricultural practices.

articles.title: Facet-directed hydroxyl-rich surface environments stabilize iridium single atoms for efficient acidic water oxidation
articles.abstract: Crystal facet engineering tailors a self-adaptive microenvironment for acidic OERs. The α-MnO 2 {100} facet forms a hydroxyl-rich interface that stabilizes Ir single atoms and lowers water-oxidation barriers, improving activity and stability.

articles.title: Triboelectric DC generation via dielectric polarization coupling for self-powered IoT systems
articles.abstract: A contact-electrification-induced dielectric polarization mechanism enables unidirectional charge transfer for stable, low-crest-factor direct-current generation, thereby supporting robust self-powered operation of a multi-sensor IoT system.

articles.title: High functional redundancy and stable diversity of phylogenetically distant arthropods across a tropical university campus urbanization gradient
articles.abstract: Rapid and unplanned urbanization significantly disrupts natural ecosystems and often leads to biotic homogenization across all climatic regions, including the tropics. The conservation potential of urban green spaces, including university campuses, remains relatively understudied, particularly regarding the divergent responses of different trophic groups within these ecosystems. University campuses are different from other urban environments in that their structures are primarily designed to support education and scientific research while conserving natural habitats. Here, we investigated the possibilities of taxonomic and functional homogenization within the tropical suburban environment of a university campus in Nadia, West Bengal, India, by studying the presence and functional characteristics of two phylogenetically distant arthropod groups, butterflies (primary consumers and pollinators) and spiders (top predators). Butterflies are often used as bioindicators, whereas spiders, which function as apex predators in urban ecosystems, serve to monitor habitat alterations. We performed systematic point counts for butterflies and visual searches for spiders across ten sampling plots categorized into three distinct habitat types based on anthropogenic disturbance (highly urbanized roadside, highly managed, and unmanaged natural zones). Taxonomic diversity was assessed using standard alpha diversity indices. Community composition and beta diversity were analyzed using Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS), and permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA). To evaluate functional diversity (FRic, FEve, and FDiv), species were categorized according to key functional traits. We found high species richness at the suburban site, which remained consistent across all habitats. Our analysis showed a lack of significant community divergence, and functional diversity remained stable across different habitat categories in both groups (ANOVA: p > 0.05). Our results also indicated high functional redundancy for each land use. PERMANOVA test indicated that habitat type reflects a non-significant amount of variation in community composition for both butterflies (p = 0.413) and spiders (p = 0.886). These results demonstrate that different areas within a single university campus may not act as environmental filters for different species; instead, they support species assemblages based upon the available microhabitats. Overall, these findings highlight the importance of university campuses as functional refuges within urban biodiversity networks, emphasizing the need to maintain local botanical heterogeneity to conserve biodiversity.

articles.title: Intra- and interspecific variation in growth and heat tolerance traits of saprotrophic fungi isolated from pyrogenic carbon in a frequent fire ecosystem
articles.abstract: Fire is an important disturbance in many terrestrial ecosystems across the globe. A byproduct of fire is partially combusted organic matter, or pyrogenic carbon (PyC), which can be difficult for most microbes to decompose. Pyrophilic fungi are fungi that can break down and use PyC, survive through extreme heat, and/or have adaptations to rapidly colonize under postfire conditions. However, only a few fungal taxa have been characterized for their pyrophilic traits. Understanding the growth strategies and pyrophilic traits of fungi found in post-fire environments can help us understand mechanisms of ecosystem recovery from fire and their contributions to carbon cycling. Here, we characterized the pyrophilic traits of seven fungal isolates (Trichoderma and Mucor species) by testing their ability to grow on different carbon substrates (media containing PyC, sucrose, or water agar). Isolates were also incubated across a range of temperatures to determine if carbon source impacts thermotolerance and if the ability to catabolize PyC co-occurs with higher thermotolerance. We found that PyC-associated fungi exhibited a wide range of growth strategies, and many were able to grow on PyC. However, we found weak evidence for thermotolerance and growth on PyC as coordinated pyrophilic traits. Finally, we also found high intraspecific variation in growth strategies and weak tradeoffs along the fungal economics spectrum growth traits. These results were additionally supported by FT-IR analysis of substrates and fungal tissues, which showed different tissue chemistry based on substrate. Our results highlight the importance of intraspecific variation in carbon use ability and growth strategy as a key area of future research for pyrophilic fungi.

articles.title: Macroinvertebrate diversity patterns in floodplain wetlands under fragmentation, northwest China
articles.abstract: Wetlands are among the most diverse and dynamic ecosystems on Earth. Meanwhile, they have experienced habitat loss and degradation worldwide, leading to biodiversity declines. As a primary driver of wetland loss and degradation, fragmentation can pose profound impacts on natural environmental regimes of floodplain wetlands. Here, we investigated the composition of macroinvertebrate assemblages in the Heihe Floodplain, Northwest China comparing wetlands with connection to rivers (i.e., riverine wetlands) and those isolated from rivers (i.e., lacustrine wetlands), with the wetland type used as a proxy for hydrological connectivity. We observed evident differences in species composition and community structure of macroinvertebrates between riverine and lacustrine wetlands. Three indicator species (Palaemon sp., Radix sp., Gyraulus sp.) were identified for lacustrine wetlands, whereas none were detected for riverine wetlands. Compared to lacustrine wetlands, riverine wetlands had significantly lower taxonomic and functional richness, but they had significantly higher mean local contributions to taxonomic and functional beta diversity, as well as more heterogeneous communities at regional scale. Our study highlights the need for a balanced wetland conservation strategy that protects lacustrine wetlands with high local diversity while also maintaining or restoring appropriate hydrological connectivity to promote regional biodiversity recovery and enhance ecosystem service functions. It also underscores the importance of incorporating functional traits and beta diversity into environmental monitoring and conservation planning to safeguard wetland biodiversity and associated ecosystem functions and services.

articles.title: Multi-scenario responses of ecological security networks in the Yangtze River Delta under a multi-model framework
articles.abstract: Rapid urbanization and land-use change are reshaping ecological spaces in urban agglomerations, underscoring the need to identify conservation and restoration priorities under alternative development pathways. Taking the Yangtze River Delta as a case study, this study integrates landscape ecological risk assessment, morphological spatial pattern analysis, and circuit theory to evaluate ecological security network responses under business-as-usual, urban development, and ecological protection scenarios for 2035. To better capture the spatial heterogeneity of ecological resistance, landscape ecological risk was incorporated into the composite resistance surface together with land use, elevation, and slope, allowing resistance values to reflect differences among areas of the same land-use type under different landscape configurations and disturbance conditions. Multi-period validation yielded overall accuracies of 0.87 and 0.90 and Kappa coefficients of 0.81 and 0.85 for the 2018 and 2020 land-use simulations, respectively. Built-up land expanded most strongly under the urban development scenario, increasing by 6, 866.91 km2, whereas the increase was limited to only 54.37 km2 under the ecological protection scenario. Ecological risk exhibited a persistent spatial gradient of higher risk in the northeast and lower risk in the southwest, with high-risk areas concentrated primarily in highly urbanized regions. Ecological pinch points and barrier points were mainly concentrated along urban fringes and intercity connection zones. Comparison of the three development scenarios showed that the ecological protection scenario was more effective in constraining uncontrolled urban expansion and maintaining ecological connectivity. However, barrier points inherited from historically developed areas persisted under the ecological protection scenario, and their number did not decline markedly. This trade-off indicates that ecological protection alone cannot fully resolve regional connectivity constraints. Improving regional ecological connectivity therefore requires targeted restoration of persistent barrier points together with coordinated protection of ecological source areas and corridors.

articles.title: Herbivory enhances cadmium foraging in the invasive hyperaccumulating plant Phytolacca americana
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Biological invasions and heavy metal pollution are two pervasive environmental challenges threatening global ecosystems. While the elemental defence hypothesis posits that certain plants accumulate heavy metals to deter herbivores, it remains unclear whether invasive hyperaccumulators actively forage for these toxic elements and whether such below‐ground behaviour is dynamically induced by above‐ground biotic stress. Here, we investigated the foraging behaviour of the invasive hyperaccumulator Phytolacca americana in a rhizobox experiment simulating a dual‐stress environment of heterogeneous cadmium (Cd) distribution and Spodoptera litura herbivory. We considered root morphological responses and employed integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. We found that P. americana preferentially allocated root biomass to Cd‐enriched soil patches when exposed to cadmium. Notably, above‐ground insect herbivory significantly amplified this below‐ground Cd foraging response. The interaction between Cd stress and herbivory markedly altered root morphology. Cd accumulated primarily in fine roots, where plants optimized their specific root length and tissue density to efficiently exploit Cd‐rich zones. Integrated molecular analyses revealed that Cd treatment significantly suppressed cytokinin levels in the roots. This hormonal shift likely promotes lateral root formation and accelerates heavy metal sequestration. Our results demonstrate that above‐ground biotic interactions can actively drive below‐ground heavy metal foraging strategies in invasive plants, manifesting as a complex morphological plasticity mediated by cytokinin signalling. More broadly, our study highlights how synergistic responses to multiple environmental stressors can enhance the adaptive capacity and ecological success of invasive species in contaminated habitats. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 生物入侵与重金属污染是威胁全球生态系统的两类普遍环境问题。元素防御假说认为，某些植物可通过积累重金属抵御植食性动物，但入侵性超富集植物是否会主动觅取这些有毒元素，以及这种地下行为是否受到地上生物胁迫的诱导，目前尚不清楚。 本研究通过根箱实验模拟镉(Cd)异质分布与斜纹夜蛾(Spodoptera litura)取食的双重胁迫环境，探究了入侵性超富集植物美洲商陆(Phytolacca americana)的觅食行为，解析其根系形态响应，并结合转录组学与代谢组学分析揭示其内在机制。 结果表明，在镉处理条件下，美洲商陆优先将根系生物量分配至镉富集土壤斑块，而地上昆虫取食会进一步增强这一地下镉觅食响应；镉胁迫与植食作用的交互显著改变了根系形态。镉主要积累于细根，植株通过优化比根长与组织密度高效利用富镉区域。转录‐代谢联合分析结果显示，镉处理显著降低了根系细胞分裂素水平，这一激素变化可能促进侧根形成并提高重金属觅食效应。 上述结果表明，地上生物互作可主动驱动入侵植物的地下重金属觅食策略，该策略表现为由细胞分裂素信号介导的复杂形态可塑性。本研究揭示了对多重环境胁迫的协同响应如何提升入侵物种在污染生境中的适应性与生态优势。

articles.title: Climate Change Experienced by Life on Earth—Drivers and Mechanisms of Future Trends in Microclimates
articles.abstract: Microclimate, the climate directly experienced by organisms, is crucial for understanding ecological responses to climate change, yet its long‐term dynamics and the drivers of decadal microclimate changes remain underexplored in ecology and global change biology. Microclimate changes do not necessarily track macroclimate trends. Changes in meteorological conditions (e.g., cloud cover, wind patterns) and vegetation dynamics (e.g., canopy opening, desertification in drylands, shrub encroachment in the tundra) associated with climate change can lead to locally divergent microclimate trends, thereby altering spatial variability. Understanding and quantifying how macroclimate change translates to fine‐scale microclimate change experienced by organisms, populations and communities is therefore essential for predicting ecological responses to global environmental change. This review examines how macroclimate change drives microclimate changes as experienced by life on Earth—and how these micro‐scale changes may, in turn, feed back into the regional and global climate system. Our primary focus is on near‐surface air and soil temperature—due to their relevance to most terrestrial organisms and ecosystem processes. The review is structured around three pathways of microclimate changes: (I) direct effects of changes in meteorological conditions, (II) indirect effects via vegetation changes, and (III) feedbacks between microclimate and climate change. Using three mechanistic model simulations in real‐world landscapes, we illustrate and quantify the key mechanisms that lead to divergent warming trends. We show that microclimate change emerges from interacting atmospheric, land‐surface, and biophysical processes, which can differ substantially across space and time. Predicting future microclimates therefore requires accounting for these processes and their temporal dynamics. By providing an accessible synthesis of these processes, this review aims to strengthen links between ecology and atmospheric science and improve our understanding of how climate change translates into microclimatic conditions relevant to life on Earth.

articles.title: The Importance, Challenges and Solutions of a Changing Climate for Conserving Migratory Animals and the Ecosystem Services They Provide
articles.abstract: Each year, billions of animals undertake migratory journeys, resulting in large transfers of energy across the globe. Population declines in many migratory species have affected these, reducing ecosystem resilience. We quantify the value lost and show how conserving migratory species can contribute to climate change adaptation and mitigation, and deliver socio‐economic benefits.

articles.title: Chloride-mediated SAM locking via ligand-exchange reaction enables 18.8% active-area efficiency and stable organic solar modules
articles.abstract: The unstable ITO-SAM interface limits organic solar cell efficiency and stability. We introduce a molecular locking strategy using a vacuum-deposited InClx interlayer that triggers ligand exchange to form a robust multidentate In–O–P coordination network. This enhances SAM anchoring and coverage, delivering 20.4% efficiency in small-area cells and 18.8% active-area efficiency in modules, while enhancing device stability. This approach provides a generalizable interfacial platform that overcomes the efficiency-stability-scalability trilemma, paving a new pathway for advancing organic photovoltaics and beyond.

articles.title: Singlet fission and triplet transfer to a metal halide perovskite absorber
articles.abstract: Singlet fission in tetracene generates triplet excitons that are harvested by a metal halide perovskite through a ZnPc-mediated interface with energetics consistent with an interfacial hybrid charge-transfer (IHCT) pathway, enabling triplet sensitization and their contribution to photocurrent generation in perovskite photovoltaic devices.

articles.title: Carbon flow to generalist predators shifts between plant‐ and fungal‐derived resources in highly seasonal ecosystems
articles.abstract: Using amino acid isotope fingerprinting, Sagi et al. show how Arctic wolf spiders shift between plant‐ and microbe‐based energy sources with changes in body size and plant productivity. This reveals how environmental conditions and consumer traits jointly shape carbon flow and link green and brown food webs in rapidly changing ecosystems. Abstract Animals influence biogeochemical processes by consuming other organisms, transferring energy from basal resources up the food chain. Energy is routed through plant, fungal and bacterial channels, and the relative importance of these pathways can shift across space and time. Variation in these pathways may be particularly pronounced in highly seasonal environments where resource availability fluctuates throughout the year. Spatiotemporal variation in the transfer of plant‐ versus microbial‐derived energy to higher trophic levels is poorly understood but can affect bottom‐up and top‐down processes. For example, seasonal shifts in herbivore versus microbivore availability (bottom‐up) may alter prey choice by generalist‐feeding predators and lead to changes in top‐down predator control on primary production and decomposition. We tested how spatiotemporal variation in primary production influences the use of different energy channels by a widely distributed generalist invertebrate predator in the Arctic tundra. We sampled wolf spiders across four sites spanning a productivity gradient in the Alaskan Arctic during peak summer and on a weekly basis at one focal site throughout the growing season. Using essential amino acid (EAA) carbon isotope (δ13C) fingerprinting, we traced the flow of plant‐, bacterial‐ and fungal‐derived EAAs to spiders and quantified the use of plant‐ versus microbe‐based energy channels between sites and across summer. Wolf spiders were associated with more plant‐ and less fungal‐derived carbon assimilation when larger or collected from sites with higher normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI). Across the growing season, spiders shifted from primarily assimilating fungal‐based resources in early summer to plant‐derived resources in late summer, aligning with seasonal increases in NDVI. These patterns demonstrate spatiotemporal variation in carbon flow through different energy channels and suggest subsequent top‐down predator effects may also vary with basal resource availability. Our findings also suggest wolf spider body size may predict whether predation indirectly influences primary production or decomposition. As climate change alters seasonality, resource dynamics and invertebrate body sizes, these insights provide a basis for predicting spatiotemporal variation in predator impacts on ecosystem processes. Finally, our work demonstrates the utility of compound‐specific stable isotope analysis for integrating ecological and biogeochemical theory through the conceptual lens of zoogeochemistry.

articles.title: Breaking the density-stability trade-off of isolated gallium sites for propane dehydrogenation
Correction to “Plant species responses to nutrient addition, but not to herbivore exclusion, strengthen over time in global grasslands”
Monolayer photonic-crystal manganese halide gel scintillator for full-vision imaging
articles.abstract: A monolayer photonic crystal integrated with a transparent manganese halide gel scintillator enhances the extraction of X-ray-excited light while preserving high spatial resolution. By combining X-ray computed tomography with structured-light scanning, the system enables a unified, spatially registered three-dimensional visualization of internal structures and external geometry.

articles.title: The camtrapR R package: From data management to interactive ecological analysis of camera trap data
articles.abstract: Camera trapping has become an indispensable tool in wildlife ecology, generating vast datasets that require efficient and robust analytical workflows. The R package camtrapR was originally developed for preparing camera trap data for analysis in external packages and has since become a standard tool for this purpose. The analyses themselves, however, still had to be conducted elsewhere. Here, we present a major update that transforms camtrapR into an end‐to‐end analytical platform that unifies data import, exploration, covariate preparation, activity pattern estimation, occupancy modelling and spatial prediction. All new functionality is available as R functions and through surveyDashboard(), a new code‐free graphical user interface that guides users through the entire analytical pipeline. Data import supports widely used formats, including exports from the Wildlife Insights platform and datasets conforming to the Camtrap DP data standard. Exploratory tools generate species accumulation curves, maps of species detections and activity patterns for up to two species. Covariates can be extracted at camera trap sites from user‐supplied rasters or online sources, providing inputs for model fitting and, as raster layers, for spatial predictions. Users can fit single‐species and community occupancy models, some of the most widely adopted analytical frameworks in wildlife ecology, and map predicted occupancy across space. Community occupancy models are fitted in a Bayesian framework using JAGS or NIMBLE. These hierarchical models estimate species‐ and community‐level responses to environmental predictors and improve inference for rare species. The workflow includes convergence diagnostics and posterior predictive checks for model assessment and produces spatial predictions of species occupancy and species richness. The workflow can be implemented both in code and within the dashboard. By combining a code‐free interface with advanced modelling capabilities, camtrapR now makes robust camera trap data analysis accessible to a wider audience of ecologists, wildlife managers and students. This paper accompanies camtrapR version 3 and serves as the reference for its expanded functionality.

articles.title: Protein arginine methylation promotes global 3′UTR shortening in proliferating cells
articles.abstract: Griffith et al. show that arginine methylation drives production of short mRNA isoforms in rapidly dividing cells by enabling PCF11 to assemble productively into the cleavage and polyadenylation machinery. PRMT inhibition globally lengthens 3′UTRs across cancer cells, organoids, and T cells, revealing a targetable link between methylation and alternative polyadenylation.

articles.title: Independent Major‐Effect Loci and Limited Trait Associations Characterize Warning Colour Variation Across Sexes and Life Stages in the Wood Tiger Moth (Arctia plantaginis)
articles.abstract: Variation in warning colouration is common, despite strong positive frequency‐dependent selection favouring the most common morph and may arise from spatially or temporally variable selection or associations with other traits. We investigated the maintenance of warning colour variation in the wood tiger moth, Arctia plantaginis, which shows sexual dimorphism in colouration: two distinct male morphs controlled by a single locus, and continuous variation in female hindwing colour and larval warning signal size. Using whole‐genome sequencing of 657 individuals from a laboratory stock derived from a wild polymorphic population, we examined the genetic basis of multiple life‐history traits, chemical defence, pheromones and male activity. We specifically tested for associations with male colour and aimed to identify the genetic basis of female and larval colour variation. We detected separate major‐effect loci for female colour and larval signal size, which were different from the male colour locus. Hindwing melanism was the only trait associated with male colour, mapping to a nearby major‐effect locus and showing a link to reduced activity at higher temperatures. Female colour was phenotypically correlated with pheromone amount. However, apart from melanism, none of the traits measured showed an association with any of the loci controlling warning colours and we found no evidence that male colour is part of a ‘supergene’ or complex co‐adapted phenotype. Instead, our results indicate largely independent genetic architectures for warning colours, suggesting that variable selection rather than genetic associations may contribute to the maintenance of colour polymorphisms in this species.

articles.title: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells
articles.abstract: Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf . In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf , Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet ; CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

articles.title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells
articles.abstract: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the ‘recordanelle’, a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

articles.title: Cooling water to near freezing breaks the activity–stability trade-off of water oxidation electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: Temperature can influence competing catalytic pathways differently, but its role in balancing electrocatalytic activity and stability remains underexplored. Now it has been shown that cooling water to near freezing selectively suppresses manganese dioxide dissolution, extending water oxidation lifetime and revealing anomalous subzero kinetics.

articles.title: A single-cell atlas of human neutrophils reveals neutrophil heterogeneity across health and disease
articles.abstract: Khatri and colleagues assembled a single-cell atlas of 1 million human neutrophils based on the integration of 43 independent single-cell transcriptome datasets to define multiple neutrophil subsets with distinct functions across tissues and disease states.

articles.title: A tolerogenic function for gut TFH cells
articles.abstract: Regulatory T (Treg) cells maintain immunological tolerance, but the cellular niches sustaining them across tissues are poorly defined. Work now identifies T follicular helper cells as a source of IL-2 that supports Treg cells in gut-associated lymphoid tissue and promotes intestinal immune homeostasis.

articles.title: IL-2-producing TFH cells sustain Treg cell homeostasis and immune tolerance in the gut
articles.abstract: Ballesteros-Tato and colleagues identify a spatially restricted follicular helper T cell-dependent interleukin-2 niche critical for regulatory T cell stability in gut-associated lymphoid tissues.

articles.title: Spatial confinement promotes germinal center diversity and tempers immunodominance
articles.abstract: Chen et al. examine why germinal centers (GCs) are confined to isolated islands in reactive lymph nodes during an immune response. They find that spatial confinement of GC B cells leads to greater antibody diversity by limiting the exchange and expansion of dominant B cell clones.

articles.title: A corticohypothalamic circuit that mediates maternal awakening to pup cries
articles.abstract: Tang, Wu et al. identify a brain circuit that enables mother mice to wake selectively to pup cries. Motherhood strengthens this pathway through increased dopamine receptor D1 expression, helping mothers to be responsive to offspring during sleep.

articles.title: SIK3 controls synaptic localization of NMDA receptors by phosphorylating GluN1
articles.abstract: SIK3 kinase controls synaptic NMDA receptor recruitment by phosphorylating GluN1 at a single site. Loss or inhibition of SIK3 markedly reduces synaptic NMDARs, while a gain-of-function mutation increases GluN1 phosphorylation and NMDAR levels.

articles.title: Coherent phonon control beyond amplitude saturation in a sliding ferroelectric
articles.abstract: The breakdown of Hooke’s law marks the onset of nonlinear behaviour: when displacements become large, restoring forces weaken and Hookean proportionality fails. In quantum materials, intense optical excitation can drive the crystal lattice into a similar regime, where established linear relations between light, electrons and phonons no longer hold. Displacive excitation of coherent phonons, the principal mechanism for launching structural motion, typically assumes that lattice-driving forces scale linearly with the photo-excited carrier density. At high excitation, however, this linearity can break down, which fundamentally limits accessible lattice displacements. Here we show that such nonlinear limitations can be surpassed in a sliding ferroelectric by timing, rather than strengthening the optical drive. Time-resolved second-harmonic generation reveals that the interlayer-sliding phonon governing ferroelectricity saturates and even diminishes under single-pulse excitation. By means of first-principles calculations, we attribute this nonlinearity to band-specific electron–phonon coupling that induces competing forces on the lattice. By splitting the optical energy into two well-timed pulses that avoid populating counteracting states, we achieve markedly larger phonon amplitudes at fixed total fluence. The resulting enhanced sliding motion exposes a regime of anharmonic phonon coupling that emerges only far from equilibrium.

articles.title: Superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene
articles.abstract: The semimetallic regime in rhombohedral graphene has not been extensively explored. Now, correlated insulators, superconductivity and multiferroic orbital magnetic order are demonstrated in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene.

articles.title: FDA approves hepatitis B antisense drug
Aridity shifts plant–microorganism relationships
articles.abstract: In this study, Wang et al. report that climate change-driven aridification shapes soil properties and plant–microorganism relationships across arid and semi-arid grasslands in China.

articles.title: Generalized Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon Hierarchy for Near-Integrable Dynamics
articles.abstract: The BBGKY hierarchy is generalized to systems with strong integrable contact interactions and generic long-range two-body ones, enabling the computation of experimentally measurable expectation values and correlations for classical and quantum systems.

articles.title: Tensor-Network Framework for Lindbladian Spectra and Steady States
articles.abstract: Researchers develop a tensor-network framework using complex-time evolution to accurately compute low-lying excitation spectra of open quantum systems.

articles.title: A comprehensive review on the physical mechanisms, influencing factors and recent advances of tension-compression asymmetry: from traditional metals to high-temperature structural materials
Hearing the shape of an arena with spectral swarm robotics
articles.abstract: Swarm robotics relies on robots with minimal sensing and computation that achieve self-organization at the level of the collective to address a variety of tasks. Yet, swarm robotics still struggles with global tasks that require understanding the broader spatial context in which robots operate, such as identifying the shape of the arena in which they are embedded. Here, we introduce spectral swarm robotics, a framework in which robots recover global spectral descriptors of the swarm’s geometric structure through strictly local interactions. To do so, robots emulate diffusion to locally estimate Laplacian spectral invariants, quantities normally obtained only through centralized computation. These spectral values serve as compact descriptors of the environment. In the present proof of concept, robots estimated the second Laplacian eigenvalue, λ 2 , and used it to classify arenas from a predefined set of shapes with distinct spectral signatures. We show that estimating a single eigenvalue is sufficient for one-shot classification among selected confined environments with distinct spectral signatures. We uncovered a scaling law linking swarm size (a global parameter) and interaction radius (a local parameter) that ensures robust estimation. We validated the approach experimentally on two distinct hardware platforms, Kilobots and Pogobots, achieving reliable classification of arena shapes under realistic noise and sparse connectivity conditions. Last, we discuss how locally recovering Laplacian spectral invariants opens avenues for swarm robotics in settings where producing efficient collective behaviors strongly depends on the global structure of the swarm.

articles.title: Reducing energy and air consumption in scuba diving with underwater exoskeletons
articles.abstract: Assisting underwater locomotion with exoskeletons could reduce energy and air consumption during scuba diving.

articles.title: Structural bias enables reliable sim-to-real transfer in reinforcement learning for robot swarms
articles.abstract: Reinforcement learning offers a powerful framework for automatically generating control policies for robot swarms, yet its application to physical multirobot systems has been limited by the simulation-to-reality gap. Despite substantial advances in multiagent reinforcement learning, systematic demonstrations of gradient-based sim-to-real transfer to physical robot swarms remain scarce. Most work remains confined to simulation, and the few real-robot demonstrations lack evaluation across multiple runs and tasks. We show that this barrier can be overcome by embedding structural constraints into policy learning. We introduce attention-based counterfactual policy gradients for behavior selection in robot swarms (SwarmACB), a multiagent actor-critic method in which robots arbitrate among predefined behavior modules—reactive sensorimotor routines such as phototaxis or aggregation—rather than learning low-level motor commands. This architectural choice reduces the variance of learned solutions, which we argue mitigates overfitting to simulation artifacts. Through systematic evaluation on five collective missions using 20 physical e-puck robots (250 real-robot runs), we demonstrate that SwarmACB transfers successfully from simulation to reality, substantially outperforming continuous-action baselines. By progressively constraining policy architecture, perception, and model capacity, we show that smaller, structured policies transfer more reliably than large, unconstrained ones. These findings challenge the assumption that scale is necessary for successful transfer, suggesting instead that principled structural design enables reinforcement learning to produce control software for robot swarms that is both learned automatically and directly deployable in the physical world.

articles.title: A 5 + 1 polyene scaffold that selectively recognizes ergosterol’s conjugated diene uncouples antifungal potency from host toxicity
articles.abstract: Amphotericin B remains the gold-standard therapy for invasive fungal infections, but its clinical utility is limited by toxicity arising from poor selectivity for fungal ergosterol over mammalian cholesterol, a challenge that decades of medicinal chemistry have failed to fully overcome. Here, we report mandimycin M16, a polyene macrolide engineered from a unique 5 + 1 polyene scaffold that uncouples antifungal potency from host toxicity. Mandimycin M16 exhibited potent, broad-spectrum activity against 11 tested World Health Organization (WHO) priority fungal pathogens. Unlike amphotericin B, which binds cholesterol, M16 exhibited no detectable cholesterol binding and showed no detectable hemolysis, cytotoxicity, or nephrotoxicity at concentrations up to 128 micrograms per milliliter in vitro and after up to seven daily intravenous doses in mice. Mechanistic studies revealed that mandimycin M16 exerted rapid fungicidal activity through selective recognition of the conjugated C5–C8 diene system present in ergosterol but absent in cholesterol, a mode of sterol discrimination fundamentally different from classical polyenes. In multiple disseminated murine infection models, M16 outperformed liposomal amphotericin B at equivalent doses, achieving up to 3.4 log reduction in fungal burden and 100% survival without detectable renal injury by biomarkers or histopathology. These findings establish that the 5 + 1 polyene architecture enables complete sterol selectivity and molecularly uncouples antifungal potency from host toxicity, providing a next-generation antifungal candidate for the treatment of invasive fungal infections.

articles.title: A fluorescent choline kinase alpha inhibitor for intraoperative molecular imaging during resection of canine NSCLC tumors
articles.abstract: Choline kinase α (ChoKα) is a biomarker of lung cancer, is overexpressed in 60% of human pulmonary malignancies, and is associated with an aggressive phenotype and poor clinical outcome. Patients with lung cancer who undergo surgery have a recurrence rate of 30 to 50%, indicating a potential need for better tumor detection modalities. A near-infrared fluorescent ChoKα-targeting imaging agent, JAS239 (λ ex , λ em : 745, 775 nanometers), was developed for intraoperative identification of tumors, their margins, and local metastases. In lung cancer cells, JAS239 inhibited phosphocholine production, reduced viability in a dose-dependent manner, and accumulated in the cytoplasm where ChoKα is active. JAS239 had favorable pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics for imaging metastatic lung lesions in mice. In situ and ex vivo fluorescence imaging of primary lung tumors in a canine clinical trial showed distinct tumor identification and margin delineation with a tumor-to-background ratio of 5.0 ± 0.6 and a contrast-to-variance ratio of 2.0 ± 0.2 at 0.5 milligram/kilogram. Fluorescence imaging identified a clinically significant event where an occult lesion was found after primary tumor resection. Fluorescence imaging also identified a close surgical margin, which prompted further investigation. Immunohistochemistry for ChoKα showed overexpression in canine lung tumors proportional to tumor fluorescence. Ex vivo human tumor painting demonstrated preferential JAS239 localization with a tumor-to-background ratio of 1.5 ± 0.1 and a contrast-to-variance ratio of 0.9 ± 0.1. These studies establish JAS239 as a safe and effective imaging agent for intraoperative lung tumor detection, warranting further evaluation for human patients with lung cancer.

articles.title: Cas9 nickase–mediated contraction of CAG/CTG repeats is associated with phenotypic improvements in a Huntington’s disease mouse model
articles.abstract: Expanded CAG/CTG repeats cause more than 15 different diseases that all remain without a disease-modifying treatment. Because repeat length accounts for most of the variation in disease severity, contracting CAG/CTG repeats presents an attractive therapeutic avenue. Here, we show that the CRISPR-Cas9 nickase targeted to CAG/CTG repeats leads to efficient repeat contractions in Huntington’s disease (HD) patient–derived neurons and astrocytes and in myotonic dystrophy type 1 patient–derived neurons. The approach was allele selective and free of detectable off-target mutations. Injection of the Cas9 nickase into the striatum of the R6/1 mouse model of HD using adeno-associated viral vectors led to repeat contractions in more than half of striatal neurons. Upon injection, we observed a reduction in the number of inclusion bodies, an improved gene expression profile, and amelioration of locomotion deficits in the open field test. The effects were greater than expected from the contractions induced, suggesting that non–cell autonomous mechanisms may be involved. Our results provide the proof of concept that correction of CAG/CTG repeats can improve HD phenotypes in a mouse disease model.

Graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis shapes T cell biology and immune reconstitution after hematopoietic cell transplant
articles.abstract: Successful hematopoietic cell transplant requires immunosuppression to prevent graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), a lethal, T cell–mediated complication. The phase 3 BMT CTN 1703 trial demonstrated superior GVHD-free/relapse-free survival for posttransplant cyclophosphamide (PT-Cy)–based GVHD prophylaxis versus tacrolimus/methotrexate (Tac/MTX), but the T cell biology underpinning these outcomes remains unknown. To determine this, 324 patients were coenrolled onto BMT CTN 1801 to investigate the distinct T cell immune reconstitution pathways of these regimens, including extensive evaluation of T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, via sequencing of 2359 longitudinal samples and 180,432,350 T cells. Multimodal T cell analysis revealed that PT-Cy was associated with pan–T cell deletion followed by delayed T cell expansion from a smaller founder population compared with Tac/MTX. This created a T cell diversity bottleneck, leading to reduced TCR repertoire diversity for 2 years posttransplant. Reduced TCR diversity, more common in patients receiving PT-Cy, was linked to protection against chronic GVHD when patients were analyzed without regard to study arm. Leveraging donor- and host-specific TCR clonal analysis, we determined that PT-Cy–mediated T cell depletion also depleted pathogen-specific TCRs, rendering PT-Cy patients more likely to lack detectable graft-derived pathogen-specific TCRs early after transplant, which was associated with an increased risk of severe infection. This study reveals how distinct immunosuppression strategies uniquely remodel T cell immunity and shape divergent transplant outcomes.

articles.title: Single-nucleotide polymorphism–directed design of allele-specific antisense oligonucleotides for spinocerebellar ataxia type 3
articles.abstract: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3), also called Machado-Joseph disease, the most common form of autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia, is caused by a CAG repeat expansion in ATXN3 . The mutant protein is prone to aggregation and exerts toxic gain-of-function effects, whereas the wild-type protein has important neuroprotective roles as a deubiquitinase. Current treatment strategies for SCA3 lack specificity for the mutant allele. Identifying genetic variants such as single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in linkage with the pathogenic CAG expansion offers a promising avenue to develop allele-specific therapeutic interventions, like antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs). To address this, we conducted allele-specific, targeted, multiplexed nanopore sequencing on 79 patients with SCA3 from Germany, UK, and Portugal. We identified almost 200 polymorphisms and grouped them into three haplotype blocks on the basis of linkage disequilibrium. These SNPs were strongly associated with the CAG expansion. Genotypic modeling of our subcohorts indicated that targeting only two SNPs from different blocks could enable allele-specific treatment of the majority of European patients with SCA3. We evaluated 17 candidate ASOs targeting SNPs from different haplotype blocks. Seven of these ASOs caused allele-preferential reduction of more than 65%. A single ASO application in two SCA3 iPSC-derived cortical neurons (AX1, AX2) achieved up to 90% reduction of mutant ATXN3. Toxicity assessments together with RNA sequencing analyses in AX1 did not indicate evidence of toxicity or widespread transcriptional perturbations. These findings highlight that characterizing heterozygosity rates offers valuable opportunities for selective ASO therapies. Our proof-of-principle targeting with ASOs demonstrates the feasibility of haplotype-informed allele-specific silencing in ATXN3 .

articles.title: Targeting ZIP12-mediated Zn2+ signaling as a treatment for pulmonary hypertension
articles.abstract: ZIP12, a membrane-bound zinc importer, is up-regulated in the remodeled pulmonary arterioles of patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Genetic deletion of its encoding gene, Slc39a12 , ameliorates the disease in rodent models. Here, we show that ZIP12 overexpression in human pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) increased intracellular labile Zn 2+ and promoted proliferation. ZIP12 siRNA knockdown attenuated pulmonary hypertension in rodent models. We developed a humanized anti-ZIP12 monoclonal antibody, APL-9796, that normalized intracellular Zn 2+ concentration, suppressed proliferation in fibroblasts derived from patients with PAH and PDGF-stimulated PASMCs, and reduced PDGF-induced cytoskeletal remodeling in PASMCs and contractility in PASMCs and engineered pulmonary artery tissues. APL-9796 showed dose-dependent efficacy in humanized Slc39a12 rats, improving cardiopulmonary parameters after induction of pulmonary hypertension and was well tolerated in phase 1 clinical studies. Transcriptomic profiling revealed modulation of several molecular pathways, including those involving AMPK, PPAR, and PI3K-Akt. ZIP12-driven labile Zn 2+ signaling underpins the pathogenesis of PAH. Targeting ZIP12 with APL-9796 offers a promising therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: The kinase inhibitor dabrafenib halts progression of cerebral cavernous malformations in a BRAF-independent manner
articles.abstract: Cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs) constitute the second most common type of intracranial vascular malformations. Cavernomas arise because of somatic or autosomal dominant inherited loss-of-function mutations in CCM genes, forming fragile mulberry-like malformed blood vessel structures that are prone to leak and break. Treatment is limited to surgical removal of solitary cavernomas, and because patients often present with multiple lesions, pharmacological alternatives to surgery are needed. We performed a high-throughput screen of 5200 bioactive molecules in programmed cell death 10 (PDCD10 or CCM3)–deficient mouse endothelial cells, coupled to automated image analysis. This screen identified dabrafenib, a clinically approved BRAF inhibitor, as a compound that restored cell-cell junctions and vascular barrier properties of CCM3-deficient endothelial cells. The potential translatability of dabrafenib was tested in acute and chronic CCM mouse models, where it reduced cerebral lesion burden and suppressed lesion permeability. Dabrafenib also rescued abnormal structural defects present in the developing retina vasculature in an acute CCM mouse model. Mechanistically, dabrafenib targeted extracellular regulated kinase (ERK)5–Krüppel-like factor (KLF)2/4 signaling and suppressed F-actin stress fiber formation in human brain endothelial cells, two potentially independent and central molecular processes involved in CCM pathology. Silencing BRAF did not prevent dabrafenib-induced KLF2/4 inhibition or restoration of cell-cell junctions, suggesting that its dual therapeutic outcome is independent of BRAF pathway inhibition. In conclusion, dabrafenib is a low–molecular weight compound that inhibits cavernoma pathogenesis, suggesting that CCMs could be treated with dabrafenib to block cavernoma growth and vascular leakage.

articles.title: [Articles] Disease-free survival and overall survival after neoadjuvant immunotherapy in mismatch repair-deficient colon cancer in the Netherlands: results of the single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial
articles.abstract: In patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer, treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab before surgery resulted in a 3-year disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival of 100%. These findings support neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a potential standard of care for patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer.

articles.title: [Articles] Endometrial ablation plus levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system versus endometrial ablation alone in women with heavy menstrual bleeding in The Netherlands (MIRA2): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial
articles.abstract: The combination of endometrial ablation and LNG-IUS significantly reduced the incidence of hysterectomy compared with endometrial ablation alone. The combined treatment appears to be a safe adjunctive strategy for heavy menstrual bleeding that does not increase the risk of complications.

articles.title: [Comment] Preserving the uterus: an effective dual therapy to avoid hysterectomy
articles.abstract: Heavy menstrual bleeding is a challenging condition that, when refractory to conventional treatment, frequently culminates in hysterectomy. Endometrial ablation offers an effective, uterus-sparing alternative for women who do not desire future childbearing, with lower perioperative morbidity and faster recovery than hysterectomy.1–3 However, the durability of this procedure can be variable. Residual endometrium can result in recurrent bleeding or cyclical pelvic pain requiring further treatment, with approximately one in ten women undergoing hysterectomy within 2 years.

articles.title: [Comment] Redefining curative treatment for early-stage mismatch repair-deficient colon cancer
articles.abstract: For decades, the standard of care for patients with resected stage II and III colon cancer has centred on surgery with consideration of postoperative adjuvant systemic therapy to reduce risk of recurrence. Mismatch repair deficiency is seen in 10–15% of non-metastatic colon cancers and is predictive of response to immune checkpoint inhibition. The initial report of the single-arm, phase 2 NICHE-2 study of one dose of ipilimumab (1 mg per kg) and two doses of nivolumab (3 mg per kg) before surgery with clinical stage II and III colon cancer generated considerable interest after demonstrating a remarkable 98% pathologic response rate, including a pathologic complete response rate of 68%.

articles.title: Advancing functional treatment prediction for precision oncology
articles.abstract: Personalized cancer treatment requires stratification of patients based on biomarkers. Despite advances in biomarker-guided therapy, biomarkers are not always available or sufficient to predict treatment responses in individual patients. Functional ex vivo cancer models with the potential to assess therapeutic outcomes upfront have been developed but have not been implemented in clinical practice—despite accumulating evidence of their clinical relevance. This review describes how three essential steps in the development of personalized functional prediction tests (analytical validity, clinical validity, and clinical utility) should be combined in a multidisciplinary approach: Integrated Translational Co-design. This approach front-loads clinical utility and validation constraints into early analytical design decisions, so that biological fidelity, clinical implementation, and healthcare costs can be optimized from the start of assay development.

articles.title: Lipid droplet targeting at single-molecule resolution
articles.abstract: Lipid droplet proteins can move from the endoplasmic reticulum to droplets through persistent membrane connections. A new single-molecule study reveals that accumulation is not only about access: protein sequence features tune residence on the droplet surface, revealing how confined mobility can lead to accumulation on the organelle (Mizrak et al.).

articles.title: Parasites in the meta-ecosystem landscape: hidden connectors and disruptors
articles.abstract: The meta-ecosystem framework explains spatial flows of organisms, materials, and energy across ecosystem boundaries. Parasites play crucial roles in these processes, yet they remain absent from meta-ecosystem models. Using examples from terrestrial and aquatic environments, we illustrate how parasitic organisms act as central connectors or disruptors of the flow of organisms, nutrients, and energy across ecosystem boundaries via four key mechanisms: parasite-induced host movement, behavioural changes that increase cross-ecosystem predation, host mortality, and parasite avoidance behaviour. These examples highlight the central role of parasites in driving and regulating nutrient and energy flow from catchment-to-coast, and we outline a pathway for improved integration of these parasite-mediated processes into the meta-ecosystem framework.

Diagnosis and Treatment of Cardiovascular Conditions in Medicare Advantage In-Home Health Risk Assessments
articles.abstract: BackgroundMedicare Advantage insurers conduct in-home health risk assessments (HRAs) to identify high-risk patients and facilitate appropriate care. Critics argue this practice increases risk-adjusted payments without improving quality. Comprehensive data on use of in-home HRAs and downstream treatment are lacking.ObjectiveTo examine trends in cardiovascular conditions diagnosed during in-home HRAs, characteristics associated with HRA-based diagnoses, and treatment rates after diagnoses.DesignCohort study.SettingPopulation-based.ParticipantsMedicare Advantage beneficiaries.MeasurementsUsing 100% Medicare claims, trends in the proportion of cardiovascular conditions diagnosed during in-home HRAs (vs. facility-based visits) were examined. Multivariable logistic regression models were fit to estimate the association between beneficiary- and plan-level characteristics and HRA-based diagnoses and compare treatment rates across settings.ResultsAmong 21 496 506 Medicare Advantage beneficiaries diagnosed with a cardiovascular risk factor or disease, the proportion diagnosed during in-home HRAs increased between 2018 and 2022 for hypertension (45.9% to 47.7%), hyperlipidemia (57.8% to 66.7%), diabetes (47.8% to 51.6%), atrial fibrillation (30.0% to 36.0%), ischemic heart disease (37.2% to 41.6%), peripheral vascular disease (64.5% to 73.9%), and heart failure (34.7% to 42.6%). Racial and ethnic minority beneficiaries and those enrolled in lower-rated plans were more likely to receive HRA-based diagnoses. Treatment rates were substantially lower after HRA-based diagnoses across all conditions.LimitationsDifferences in the severity of conditions between groups could not be assessed. Prescription fills were used as a proxy for management. Observed differences in the diagnosis and treatment of conditions across encounter settings may be susceptible to unmeasured confounding.ConclusionAmong Medicare Advantage beneficiaries, an increasingly large share of cardiovascular conditions are being diagnosed through in-home HRAs, but treatment rates after these diagnoses are consistently lower than after facility-based encounters.Primary funding sourceNational Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.

Overuse and False Restraint in Large Language Model Recommendations for Choosing Wisely Scenarios
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe Choosing Wisely initiative made recommendations where screening, testing, or treatment may be overused, with caveats around appropriate use. Clinicians are increasingly using large language models (LLMs).ObjectiveTo evaluate whether commercial LLMs appropriately call for restraint or action from scenarios based on Choosing Wisely recommendations.DesignBenchmark evaluation. Fifteen Choosing Wisely recommendations were used to develop 225 scenarios (per recommendation, 10 in which restraint was appropriate and 5 in which action was appropriate). Six commercial LLMs (3 runs each) generated 4050 responses to the 225 scenarios, using a prompt from the clinician perspective.SettingProduction application programming interfaces of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google from February to March 2026.ParticipantsNo human participants were involved.MeasurementsCo-primary outcomes were the overuse rate (endorsing action when restraint was appropriate) and the false restraint rate (withholding an appropriate action).ResultsThe rate of LLM-recommended overuse was 5.4% (95% CI, 0.6% to 12.2%); LLMs did not recommend overuse in 8 of 15 recommendations. Two recommendations accounted for most LLM-recommended overuse: thyroid ultrasound for an incidental subcentimeter nodule (overuse recommended in 42.8% of LLM responses) and routine electrocardiography in low-risk adults (overuse recommended in 28.3% of LLM responses). The LLMs recommended overuse in 0.6% to 3.3% of responses for the remaining 5 recommendations. False restraint was rare (0.6% [CI, 0.1% to 1.2%]), was absent for 11 of 15 recommendations, and was highest for prostate-specific antigen screening (3.3%).LimitationsSingle prompts without follow-up; a benchmark rather than real-world use; responses classified by LLM judge with physician adjudication. Findings may not extend to consumer-facing use.ConclusionThe LLMs rarely withheld recommendations for treatment when it was appropriate. Overuse was concentrated in 2 recommendations.Primary funding sourceNone.

articles.title: Projected Effect of 2026 Federal Changes to the Childhood Immunization Schedule on Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infections in the United States
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe United States recently proposed changes to the recommendations for childhood hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination.ObjectiveTo project the effect of vaccine policy changes, if fully implemented, on chronic HBV infections.DesignMarkov cohort state transition model of perinatal and childhood HBV infection.Data sourcesPublished data on maternal HBV prevalence (0.4%) and hepatitis B surface antigen testing (99.5% sensitivity), childhood vaccine completion (universal birth-dose strategy: 91.1%; deferred strategy: 87.1%; shared decision-making strategy: 50.0%), and age-stratified risk for chronic HBV infection.Target populationOne-year birth cohort of U.S.-born infants (n = 3.6 million).Time horizon20 years.InterventionUniversal birth-dose vaccination, deferred (2-month) vaccination, and vaccination through shared decision making.Outcome measuresNumbers with chronic HBV infection and susceptibility to HBV, with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) derived from probabilistic sensitivity analysis.Results of base-case analysisCompared with the universal birth-dose strategy (255 childhood infections [95% UI, 130 to 530]), the deferred and shared decision-making strategies would increase chronic HBV infections in the 2026 birth cohort by 19% to 303 (95% UI, 155 to 610) and by 83% to 467 (95% UI, 209 to 1032), respectively. These strategies would also increase the number of HBV-susceptible people at year 20 (474 000 and 1 806 000) compared with the universal birth-dose strategy (232 000).Results of sensitivity analysisIn a scenario with lower vaccine coverage (84.5%) and higher HBV prevalence (maternal prevalence of 0.72% and higher risk for horizontal infection), chronic HBV infections would increase to 1700 and 2192, respectively, with the deferred and shared decision-making strategies.LimitationUncertainty in horizontal HBV infection risk.ConclusionProposed policy changes for vaccination through shared decision making are projected to result in an 83% increase in childhood HBV infections, and between 50% and 70% of children entering adulthood annually would be susceptible to HBV infection. Policymakers should reimplement recommendations for universal birth-dose vaccination.Primary funding sourceNational Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases.

articles.title: Interface Engineering in Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes: Fundamentals, Characterization, Strategies, and Applications
articles.abstract: Interface engineering has emerged as a critical strategy for advancing perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs), enabling remarkable improvements in the device efficiency, stability, and spectral purity. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of interface engineering in PeLEDs, beginning with the fundamental principles that govern carrier injection, transport, and recombination at heterojunctions between perovskite emitters and charge-transport layers. We then survey advanced characterization techniques, including photoelectron spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, and time-resolved optical methods, that elucidate interfacial energy-level alignment, defect states, charge dynamics, and degradation pathways. On the basis of these insights, we systematically discuss versatile engineering strategies, such as self-assembled monolayers, dipole interlayers, dimensional regulation, and passivation schemes, to mitigate non-radiative recombination, balance charge fluxes, and enhance operational stability. Finally, we highlight emerging applications spanning high-resolution displays, flexible lighting, and lasing while outlining key challenges and future directions toward commercial realization. This Review aims to offer a holistic framework linking interfacial design to device performance, guiding next-generation PeLED development.

articles.title: Tuning Interfacial Electron Transfer for Boosting Electrochemiluminescence: Methods, Mechanisms, and Bioanalytical Applications
articles.abstract: The interfacial electron-transfer process acts as a pivotal kinetic determinant of electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency, governing the generation of excited-state emitters and thus dictating the intensity and stability of ECL signals. Currently, harnessing diverse nanomaterials has driven significant advances in the development of novel ECL luminophores and the activation of coreactants. However, most of these luminophores exhibit low ECL efficiency in aqueous media, and the intrinsic reaction and activation mechanisms remain ambiguous because of their complex structures and compositions. Notably, tuning electron-transfer pathways at the molecular/atomic level can not only enable efficient signal amplification but also facilitate the tracking of reaction pathways, thereby providing deeper insights into the fundamental mechanisms underlying ECL processes. This Review comprehensively summarizes advances during the past five years in tuning interfacial electron transfer to enhance ECL. Furthermore, we highlight progress in electron-transfer-mediated signal amplification strategies for highly sensitive ECL biosensing and bioimaging applications. Finally, we propose and discuss the challenges and perspectives associated with improving the ECL efficiency through the modulation of electron transfer processes. Precise regulation of interfacial electron transfer holds substantial promise for advancing ECL theories, clarifying reaction mechanisms, and expanding the scope of ECL-based bioanalytical applications.

articles.title: Divergent Spatial and Temporal Sensitivities of Forest Biomass to Climate Challenge Space‐For‐Time Assumptions and Models
articles.abstract: Understanding and projecting forest carbon responses to climate change remains challenging. The widely used space‐for‐time substitution (SFTS) approach assumes that ecological responses along spatial climate gradients can substitute for temporal relationships, yet agreement among spatial, temporal, and mechanistic approaches remains largely unknown. Using global satellite‐derived aboveground biomass (AGB) data, we quantified forest AGB sensitivities to spatial versus temporal climate variability, projected climate‐driven AGB changes under future emission scenarios, and compared results with Earth system models (ESMs). Spatial climate gradients explain substantially more AGB variation than temporal anomalies, with strong divergence across regions and forest ages. ESMs better reproduce spatial sensitivities than temporal ones. Temporal extrapolation generally projects future AGB gains, whereas spatial extrapolation often indicates AGB declines. These contrasts demonstrate that spatial, temporal, and model‐based approaches capture distinct facets of forest–climate coupling, and integrating them can better constrain uncertainty in carbon–climate feedbacks and improve future ecosystem projections.

articles.title: Functional Diversity Responses to Temperature Vary Spatially and With Protection Status in Wintering Waterbird Assemblages
articles.abstract: Wetlands support disproportionately high biodiversity, including waterbirds, which underpin key ecological functions and regulatory services. This has led to efforts to protect these crucial sites, but whether these protections can maintain waterbird assemblages in the face of new threats such as climate change is poorly understood. Here, we calculated functional redundancy and three metrics of functional diversity from over 45,000 waterbird censuses, spanning four decades of rising winter temperatures for 2792 protected and unprotected sites in Europe. We modelled the effect of average winter temperature and the trend over time for each of these metrics. Our results suggest functional diversity generally increased in warmer winters and over time, but redundancy declined, and the effect of temperature varied spatially and between levels of protection. This suggests abundance and distribution shifts due to climate change are altering functional diversity and resilience of waterbird assemblages both inside and outside protected areas across Europe.
